Philip leaves them in love, he says, for there is nothing else. It is a short session. It did not need to be longer. One truth, said plainly, is enough work for a lifetime.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Blank Mind
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the blank mind.

February twenty-seventh, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn spends the whole evening on one subject: how the contact actually works. Not the philosophy this time. The mechanics. How does a human being become a channel? And the answer, repeated patiently through several new instruments who stumble and stall in real time, is simpler than anyone in the room wants it to be.

Think of nothing. That is the whole technique. The instrument Don, Hatonn says, has cleared his mind of other thoughts and is allowing me to speak through him rapidly, using his mind simply as a relay station. A relay station. Not a translator, not an interpreter. A relay. The thoughts arrive and the mouth repeats them, with nothing in between.

Here is the part that surprised me. We do not use words, Hatonn says. Your language is composed of words. I am using concepts. The concepts are impressed upon the mind of the instrument, which immediately transfers them into language. So what the room hears is Don's vocabulary carrying Hatonn's concepts. The meaning is the cargo. The words are just the truck.

And this is why the new instruments struggle so visibly in this session. One of them gets stuck repeating, I am Hatonn, I am Hatonn, I am having a hard time. Another stalls out entirely. Hatonn is gentle about it. The problem is never the contact. The problem is the analysis. The moment the instrument starts examining the thought, arranging the sentences to sound better, wondering whether it is real, the flow chokes. Do not analyze the source of the thought, he says. It is only necessary to speak it.

To make the point land, Hatonn tells a small story. A child listens to its parents, and before listening it could not speak, and after listening it could speak quite fluently. The child was totally unaware of the process. It simply learned. If you were as a little child, Hatonn says, we could speak through you with no difficulty. The problem is that you are not as a little child. You question everything. You have been trained to interrogate every impression before you let it through. The training that makes you competent in the world makes you deaf to the contact.

I love the honesty of the evening's second half, where the teaching turns from technique to motive. Why channels at all? Because the people of Earth are waking up, Hatonn says, and soon many will want to hear. And here is the line I want you to keep. Truth must be realized from within. It cannot be impressed from without. If the voices landed their craft on the lawn and announced the truth, people would accept it on authority, and authority is just another trance. So they speak through ordinary people in ordinary rooms, so that each listener has to weigh the words and decide for themselves.

And then, almost as an aside, the most moving sentence of the night. We are seeking too, Hatonn says. We are attempting to help those of the planet Earth who desire to seek truth to seek it also, and in doing this we find that we grow in our understanding of truth. They are not above the process. They are inside it. The teacher is also a student. The relay station works in both directions.

Near the end he tells them what the Confederation actually wants from the people of Earth, and it is not obedience or belief. Give us the only thing that we ask of your peoples, he says. Give us understanding. You can do this through meditation. That is the whole transaction. Not worship. Not following. Understanding. Given freely, in the quiet, by people who owe them nothing.

So the practice is the same as it ever was. Sit down. Clear the mind. Think of nothing. Say what comes. The infinite, it turns out, is not impressed by your vocabulary. It is waiting for your silence.

Thank you for listening.

title: As a Little Child
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: as a little child.

Later that same evening, second meditation, and Hatonn picks up the story he started earlier. He is speaking, he tells the room, from a craft hovering above the house. And he wants to talk about the craft, and about desire, and about why the brothers of the Confederation do not simply land and say hello.

First, the rule. Our craft would be visible to this group upon request, he says. Desire is the necessary element in any communication with us, be it thought, visual, or any physical medium. Nothing is shown to the curious. Everything is shown to the desiring. It is the same law as the channeling. Ask, and the channel opens. Do not ask, and it stays closed.

Then the question everyone asks, the one the group has clearly been asking all week. Why do you not meet us face to face? Why not bring a craft down where we can get a close look? Hatonn's answer is disarmingly practical. The problem, he says, is overreaction. Either fear or worship. Neither attitude is necessary or even desirable.

Listen to how he puts the alternative. When you have reached a maturity that will allow you to meet us casually, as an equal, I should say, as a friend, then face-to-face contact will be more possible. As a friend. Not as a savior. Not as a threat. The day you can shake hands without flinching or kneeling, that is the day the handshake happens.

The rest of the evening returns to the new instruments, and it is rough going. The contact keeps dropping. Instruments stall mid-sentence. Hatonn keeps coaxing. Do not be afraid of making an error, he says. Relax and let it happen. And then he tells the story of the child again, the one from earlier, and this time it lands harder because the room has just watched grown adults fail at the simplest thing a toddler does without thinking.

A small child listens to its parents, and though it understood nothing of the process, it learned to speak fluently. That is the whole method. The child has no knowledge of what it is supposed to do. It simply speaks. If you were as a little child, Hatonn says, we could speak through you with no difficulty. The problem is that you are not as a little child.

Think about what stands between the adults in that room and the child they once were. It is not intelligence. It is the habit of questioning everything before it is allowed through. A technological society, Hatonn says, trains people to interrogate every presentation. That training is useful for buying a car. It is fatal to receiving a thought. If you do not question what we are attempting to do, but simply relax and let it happen, it will happen.

There is a quiet mercy in the closing lines. We are aware continually of the activities of your group, as we are aware of all such groups on your planet. We are here to be of service. They are not grading the performance. They are watching people learn to be empty, and calling that service.

And the promise underneath it all is democratic to the point of scandal. All of you in this room are capable of thought transfer, he tells them. All that is required is that you desire it. Not talent. Not training. Not a special sensitivity. Desire, plus the willingness to be as a little child. The door was never locked. It only looked that way from the thinking side.

So tonight, the invitation is the oldest one in the book. Become as a little child. Not naive. Not foolish. Just unguarded enough to let something true arrive without demanding its credentials first.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Possibilities
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: two possibilities.

March second, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn opens with a sentence that sounds like the beginning of a logic proof, and then spends the evening showing it is the beginning of a whole way of life. There are two possibilities, he says. One is to be in the service of the infinite Creator. One is to be otherwise.

That is the entire teaching, really. Everything after is commentary. But what commentary. The definition he gives is so plain it almost slips past. To be in the service of the Creator is to go forth with a purpose that you understand to be desired by your Creator, a purpose determined through an understanding of the principles which govern this creation. In other words, service is not busyness. It is alignment. It is knowing what you are doing and why.

And here is his diagnosis of the planet. Upon your planet at this time there are many individuals performing many services. Very few of these services, however, are services we would consider to be in the service of our infinite Creator. For man is primarily concerned with serving himself. He does not say this cruelly. He says it the way a doctor reads a chart.

Then comes the sentence I want to underline twice. We have said to you many times that it is necessary to meditate. This is the most important truth that we bring to you, for if one practices meditation, then one has no questions about service. Read that again slowly. Not meditation will answer your questions about service. Meditation removes the questions. When you sit in the silence long enough, the fretful calculating about how to help, whom to help, whether you are helping enough, simply stops. What remains is obvious.

Each of you here desires to serve, he tells the room, and each of you is serving. But to serve efficiently, prepare with daily meditation. The order matters. Preparation first, then service. The voices never ask anyone to pour from an empty cup.

He is honest about the difficulty. Man on this planet has lost sight of reality almost entirely. He has built a myriad of illusions, and these illusions are so very strong that he is locked within them and cannot be served. I find that phrase haunting. Cannot be served. Not will not. Cannot. The illusion is a locked room, and the person inside does not know there is a door.

And because the room is locked from the inside, the way out cannot be a rescue. It has to be a catalyst. It will be necessary, Hatonn says, for man to experience the strong catalytic action of his physical environment, in order to break his self-made illusion. Life itself will do the breaking. The hard events, the losses, the shocks, are not punishments. They are the walls cracking. The kindest thing the universe can do for someone locked inside is to shake the building.

So the teaching stays simple, deliberately simple. We have attempted to maintain a simple message, Hatonn says, for man on Earth has confused himself for many generations with complexities. It is not necessary to get lost in the complex web of intellectual seeking that man seems so fond of. It is only necessary to avail yourself to an understanding that is not of an intellectual nature. And this you may do in daily meditation.

The closing is a promise and a warning together. When the seeker is ready to join the work directly, he will know it, for it will be apparent to him in his meditations. You do not have to audition. You do not have to be recruited. Sit still long enough, and the readiness announces itself.

Two possibilities. That is all there ever were. Tonight, in the quiet, you might ask which one today belonged to.

Thank you for listening.

title: Because You Called
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: because you called.

March fourth, nineteen seventy-four. The shortest session in the early archive, and maybe the tenderest. A new instrument, D, is channeling, and Hatonn comes through for only a few minutes. The group has asked for reassurance. Something personal. Something to hold onto. And he gives it to them straight.

I am come because you have called me, he says, and I desire to be of service to you.

That is the whole theology of the archive in one sentence. He does not come because they are worthy. He does not come because the stars are aligned. He comes because they called. The entire machinery of heaven, it turns out, runs on invitation.

The group wants to feel the presence, to know it is real. And Hatonn explains what the conditioning is actually for. It is not a parlor trick. Conditioning is to make you more aware of our presence. When you feel the conditioning, you know that we are with you. The strange sensations the new instruments have been reporting all week, the pressure, the involuntary movements, are not the message. They are the knock on the door.

And then the quietest line of the session. Conditioning also helps to reassure you.

I love that. Not convince. Reassure. The voices understand something about human beings that human beings forget about themselves. We do not only need truth. We need to be steadied. We need to feel, in the body, that we are not alone in the room. So the conditioning is given the way you would put a hand on someone's shoulder. Not to prove anything. To calm.

The session ends almost as soon as it begins. A fragment of contact, a pause, an inaudible stretch, and it is over. But it does not need to be longer. Some nights the teaching is a whole cosmology. Some nights it is just this. You called. I came. I am here.

Thank you for listening.

title: Flowers and Thorns
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: flowers and thorns.

March sixth, nineteen seventy-four. Carla is channeling for the first time in the archive, and Hatonn speaks through her to a room of people who keep showing up, week after week, trying to wake up. What he tells them is not comfortable. It is not meant to be.

We come across the deeps of dimensions you know not to speak with you, he says, and yet you are asleep. And though you hear us you do not hear us.

I want to stay with that image for a moment. People sitting in a circle, listening intently, taking it all in, and being told they are asleep. Not because they are insincere. Because hearing is not the same as hearing. The ears receive. Something deeper has to open.

What you hear is truth and yet not truth, he goes on. What you take in with your physical senses is only true for the illusion, and this illusion is a very small part of the creation. The senses are not lying, exactly. They are reporting accurately on a very small room, while the house goes on around them unnoticed.

Then the sentence the whole session is built around. Meditation, my friends, is the great bridge to the total creation of the Father. It is your birthright. Not a technique for the gifted. Not a hobby for the spiritual. A birthright. Something you were born owning and forgot to claim.

And notice who the bridge is for. All of us together are the Creation, Hatonn says. Through meditation we can begin to become more aware of it. This is true of us, also. The voices are not handing down something they have finished with. They meditate too. The bridge carries traffic in both directions, and the ones speaking have not reached the far side either. They are walking it alongside you.

And he gives them a practice, one of the most practical in the early sessions. Stop yourself at each point in the illusion at which you think a thought, and ask yourself how much of the truth of that thought applies to the real creation. Every thought, held up to the light for a second. How much of you is real? How much is the dream talking?

The contact shifts to another instrument, and the tone sharpens. You must be careful, Hatonn says, for the traps of the illusion are hidden. And unless you are careful where you are stepping you will fall. Many of them are hidden. Many of them appear as flowers. But beware, my friends, for below the flower is the thorn, always.

Below the flower is the thorn, always. That is a line to carry in your pocket. The illusion does not trap you with obvious ugliness. It traps you with beauty that has a barb in it. The compliment that needs something back. The pleasure that costs your peace. The flower is real. The thorn is real too. Wisdom is knowing both are there before you reach.

The instrument tires, and Hatonn leaves them with the practice. Observe your actions, he says. Watch how they fall. Whether the things you participate in are adding to the illusion or erasing it. That is the whole examination of conscience, reduced to one question. Is this making the dream thicker, or thinner?

Tonight, pick one thought, one action, and ask it. Flower or thorn? Adding or erasing? The bridge is yours by birthright. You only have to walk it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Voice of the Creator
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the voice of the Creator.

March eighth, nineteen seventy-four. Three voices speak this evening. Hatonn, then Oxal, then Laitos. And between them they cover the whole arc, from the seeking, to the finding, to the simple recognition that what you were seeking was speaking to you all along.

Hatonn begins where he always begins. It has been written in your holy works that if you seek, you shall find. We are here to help those who seek. We are here to help them find. And what shall we help you find? Life, he says. Life as it was intended. Life as you desire it.

He is clear that this is not the life on display. There is what man on Earth presumes to be life abundant, he says. However, this life is not acting in a manner ever intended by our Creator. Abundance of things is not abundance of life. The distinction matters, because so much seeking on this planet is aimed at the wrong abundance.

Then he names the objective, and it is one thing with many names. There is only one thing worth seeking. There are many ways of defining it. There are many pathways to it, and many names for it. But no matter how you name it, no matter how you reach it, there is only one objective, and it is the same for each of us. It is simply a return to the awareness of the thinking of our Creator.

I love how undramatic that is. Not a prize. Not a revelation. A return. Like remembering something you always knew.

The contact passes to Carla, and Hatonn gives the image of the seed. Like a seed being planted, he says, in darkness. There is darkness also in the conscious and waking reality of those who are beginning to seek, for they feel that they are awake, yet they are asleep and in darkness. The seed does not know it is growing. It only knows the dark. If you are in the dark right now, that may be the planting, not the failure.

He is honest about the odds, too. We realize, he says, that we will be successful with only a relatively small percentage of those whom we contact. However, this will be sufficient for the time being. For from these seeds will grow a wider understanding of the truth for those who desire it. The work is not measured in crowds. A few seeds, properly planted, are enough. The garden does the rest.

And then the line about uniqueness that I keep turning over. Consider that each man has a handprint uniquely his own. No one else's handprint in the whole world can match it. Consider each leaf or snowflake, and realize that there has never been a duplicated entity. The way from the illusion to reality cannot be measured, he says, and is as individual as your handprint. Your road will not look like anyone else's. It was never supposed to.

Then Oxal speaks, and the evening lifts into something else entirely. I am the Creator, he says. Yes, my friends, you are listening to the voice of the Creator. You hear the voice of the Creator each day, as you go about your daily activities. It is only necessary to recognize it.

Listen to how he puts it, because this is the heart of the whole night. As you meet your fellow man in your daily activities, as he speaks, then you hear the voice of your Creator. Birds singing in the trees speak with the voice of the Creator. The very winds that blow through these trees speak to you. This noise that you hear is the voice of the Creator, for His expressions are infinite.

It is only necessary, he says, that you hear and see these expressions, and then understand that these are the Creator. This knowledge is self-evident. It does not require a complex analysis. Truth speaks to you. It is all about you. It is the Creator.

Laitos closes the evening briefly. Join us, my friends, he says. Join us in light. It is all about you.

So tonight, on your walk, at your window, in the next voice you hear, try the recognition. Not as a belief. As an experiment. What if it is all the same voice?

Thank you for listening.

title: Holy Ground
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: holy ground.

March ninth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn speaks on the subject of seeking, and he calls it perhaps the most important of all subjects that could be spoken about. Not the most interesting. The most important. And then Oxal follows him, and together they say something so simple that the mind wants to rush past it.

Seeking, Hatonn says, is a way of growing. It is, in truth, for the people of this planet at this time their only way of truly rapidly growing, growing in a sense that is spiritual. The people of Earth are almost all children in a spiritual sense, he says. Most are not seeking spiritual growth at all. And yet all of us throughout all of space are growing. The difference between the fast growers and the slow ones is one thing only. The fast ones are seeking.

Why must it be sought, rather than given? Because it cannot be given. It is something that each individual must find for himself. It is not a difficult thing to find. It is a very simple thing to find. It is only necessary that the individual go about seeking in a proper way.

And here is the great simplification. We will not attempt to confuse those whom we wish to aid with complex lectures on various problems and concepts. We will simply give to them the simplest of the Creator's ideas. For His ideas are not complex. It is man, especially man on Earth, who has made a complex set of rules and conditions for spirituality.

I love that reversal. We assume the truth is complicated and our confusion is simple. Hatonn says it is the other way around. The truth is simple. The confusion is our elaborate construction.

The contact moves to Carla, and the teaching takes its strangest, most beautiful turn. There is the complication in your vision of the concept of time, Hatonn says. And the complication in your vision of the concept of space. You ask, where and when may I seek? In what place may I find holy ground? And at what time may I seek the Creator?

And then the answer, which undoes the question. My friends, you are the Creator. For the Creator is you. And as it is written in your holy works, the place whereon you stand is holy ground. There is no complication in time, for all time is here and now. There is no complication in place, for all place is here and now.

Wherever you are standing, while you listen to this, is holy ground. Not metaphorically. The ground does not become holy when you arrive at the right temple. You are the temple, arriving at the ground.

It is not necessary to have the most perfect meditation, he adds, or the most proficient spiritual moments, in order to be seeking. It is necessary only to turn your will. Your will to seek is as important as the source. I find that deeply merciful. The stumbling meditator with the turned will is seeking. The perfect posture with a wandering allegiance is not.

And he does not ask them to despise the world they live in, either. It is good, he says, that you appreciate those things in your illusion that you wish to appreciate. All of these things are here for your experience. The teaching was never to reject the world. It is to stop mistaking it for the whole of reality. Enjoy the scenery. Just remember you are traveling through it.

Then Oxal speaks, and gives the evening its closing vision. When you meet your fellow man in your daily activities, you will recognize him for what he really is, a part of the creation, just as you are. And the creation is the Creator. And then, as you look at Him and He looks at you, the Creator looks at Himself, through each pair of eyes.

The Creator looks at Himself, through each pair of eyes. Every glance you have ever exchanged was that. Every stranger on the train. Every tired cashier. Every friend across the table. The universe, looking at itself.

And His thought in all these manifestations, Oxal says, is a thought of love. For this was the thought that created all that there is.

Tonight, try it once. Look at one person, anyone, and let the thought arrive. That is the Creator, looking at the Creator. The ground under both of you is holy.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seeking Is Serving
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seeking is serving.

March tenth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn takes two words that seem to point in opposite directions and shows the room they are the same word. I and my brothers are here only to serve you, he says. And it is a very great pleasure to be here. We offer conditioning to those of you who desire this. We serve you, and we seek. Serving is seeking.

Listen to how carefully he unfolds the paradox. The two words seem different. To seek and to serve. One suggests that you need something, and one suggests that you have something. For those who seek must need, and those who serve must have, to give away. It is a paradox, he says, as are all intellectual things. And yet it is the simple truth, that they are one thing.

Here is what I think he means. In the illusion, people seek the way beggars seek, from a position of poverty. They go on pilgrimage for physical security, or for spiritual experience, as though they were supplicants, poor and needful and ever lacking. Hatonn calls this dealing from a position of weakness. It is possible, he says, to seek a treasure that can be held and shown and counted. But that is the small seeking.

The large seeking starts from the opposite end. When we seek reality, he says, we turn either very far inward or very far outward, into the light. And we find that we are not dealing from a position of poverty, but that we have all that we have been seeking. We are dealing from a position of complete strength. Because we are infinite. You, my friends, are infinite. You do not need help. You only need realization.

You do not need help. You only need realization. That sentence rearranges the whole spiritual economy. The seeker is not a beggar approaching a full table. The seeker is the owner of the table who forgot where the dining room was.

All I can tell you, Hatonn says, all you can learn, all that is possible in this infinite creation, is abiding eternally within you. For you are one with all that there is. The illusion suggests otherwise. The illusion is as evanescent as a bubble, he says. Pop, and it will be gone. It is as fleeting as a dream. Soon you will awaken.

And then the turn toward service, which is where the paradox resolves. This is our technique of seeking, he says of the Confederation. It may seem strange that we would seek through service, but this is our understanding of seeking. It is stated in your holy works that it is necessary to seek in order to find. We have found many ways of seeking. One of these is to serve your fellow man.

For in serving others, we serve ourselves. It is a law of this creation, he says, that only through service may one be served. This was the original idea that generated the entire infinite creation. The idea of mutual service. The idea of mutual understanding. The idea of mutual love.

He is honest that most of the planet has missed this. Man has become lost in a complex creation of his own, with many thoughts of a trivial nature that keep him very busy, in an effort to reach that which is of no value. A minor creation that will last only the shortest period of time. Which has no value once it is attained, for he will lose it.

But the way back is not complicated. The man known to you as Jesus made the simple realization, Hatonn says, and then demonstrated it by his activities. It was not necessary that he be understood. It is impossible to force this understanding upon another from without. It is only possible that it be attained from within. He simply pointed at the path, like a guidepost, so others could find their own way from darkness to light.

For light, my friends, is eternal and infinite and real. The rest is illusion. Go within. Become aware of reality. It is within each of you.

So the paradox stands, and it is not a riddle to solve but a practice to live. Seek by serving. Serve by seeking. They were never two words.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Original Thought
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the original thought.

March eleventh, nineteen seventy-four. This is one of the great cosmological sessions of the early archive. Hatonn lays out, as plainly as language allows, what the creation is made of, how it got here, and what a human being is supposed to do about it. It is a long evening. Stay with it. It repays the attention.

He begins with the diagnosis. Man on Earth has very little understanding of his life. The life of an individual is not what he thinks it is. Man is concerned with a life limited by his waking hours, during a present physical lifetime. His plans and desires are governed by this extremely limited portion of experience. And so, from the perspective of those who see further, his activities are, in Hatonn's startling word, ridiculous.

Not cruel. Just true. We plan for decades and call it long-term thinking, while standing inside an existence that has no term.

Then the cosmology, and it is breathtaking in its economy. Life is composed of two materials, Hatonn says. One of them is what you might call consciousness. The other is light. But consciousness is love, and light is its physical manifestation. All that you experience as a physical universe is composed of one ingredient. Light.

Originally, the Creator expressed a desire. This desire was expressed in a state of consciousness best described by the word love. The Creator, expressing desire through love, caused the creation of all matter. He caused the creation of light. This light was then formed in its infinite configurations to produce all of the forms that are experienced. For this reason, Hatonn says, we greet you each evening in His love and His light. For this encompasses all that there is. The consciousness that creates, and the fabric that is love and light.

And then the part about you. The love that produces the configuration of light occurs in various vibrations. These vibrations are the result of free will. When the Creator produced the original concept, the concept included the gift of freedom of choice to all of the parts He created. Those parts are then totally free to change the original Thought. Each of you here this evening has a vibration. This vibration is yours, and you have control over it.

I want to pause on that, because it is the hinge of the whole evening. Your vibration is yours, and you have control over it. Not your circumstances. Not your past. Your vibration. The one instrument you can actually tune.

This, Hatonn says, is perhaps the most important principle in this creation. That each of the Creator's parts be able, throughout eternity, to select for themselves what they desire. Nothing is forced. The straying is allowed. The return is allowed. The whole infinite experiment runs on permission.

The man known as Jesus, he says, simply matched his vibration to the original Thought more closely than those around him. For this reason he was able to work what were called miracles. But the original Thought was that all of the parts should be able to generate by thought what they desired. The miracles were not exceptions to the rules. They were demonstrations of the rules.

And then, near the end of the night, the parable. Picture if you will, Hatonn says, a prison, deep in the ground. Old metal, and many rusty keys. Inside the cells there are many ghosts, barely visible, and yet trapped. My friends, you are holding yourselves prisoner.

Listen to the way out. Meditation allies you with the truth of freedom. Unlock your own spirits from these dungeons by simply realizing that each intellectual thought process is a mere shade, only a ghost, and cannot harm or hurt you or cause you pain. As these shades disappear, you rise from this earthly, rusty frame of mind. And once you are up in the sunlight, and the sun is warming you, you have found an avenue from meditation to demonstration.

From meditation to demonstration. The sitting is not the point. The walking out of the cell is the point.

He leaves them with two questions to ask when the illusion presses hardest. Does this problem have to do with my spiritual growth? Does it have to do with a service to aid another in spiritual growth? If the answer is yes, he says, this problem is in the area I have described as the dungeon. It need only be let go.

So tonight, the practice is one question. What am I holding that is only a shade? Name it, and watch it thin in the sunlight.

Thank you for listening.

title: All Roads Lead Inward
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: all roads lead inward.

March seventeenth, nineteen seventy-four. The contact is difficult this evening. The instrument struggles, the channel keeps dropping, and Hatonn has to work to get through at all. And maybe that is fitting, because the session is about exactly this problem. The noise in the head, and how to get past it.

He begins with the mechanics of a clear mind. In order for a good contact to be made, he says, the thoughts of daily activities must be erased from consciousness for the period of the contact. It is necessary to maintain as close to a totally clear mind as possible. This may be practiced in meditation, and an individual may learn to think of nothing.

Some find it harder than others, and Hatonn names the culprit without apology. Those who are involved in activities that require the use of the intellectual mind sometimes find it much more difficult to clear the mind than those who are not so encumbered. The analyst, the planner, the professional thinker, has the hardest time stopping the thinking. The mind that earns your living is the mind that blocks the contact.

But it can be overcome, he insists. It is quite possible for those involved in these activities to learn to shut off these thoughts and become aware of the thoughts impressed upon them as a result of their desire. The amount of practice required varies widely. Some require little or no practice. Others require an extensive amount. There is no shame in either. There is only the practice.

I love the mercy in that. No hierarchy of the gifted. Just practice, and patience with the kind of mind you happen to have.

He adds something the group needs to hear. It is not necessary for an individual to be able to directly channel our thoughts, as does this instrument, in order to be an effective channel of our Confederation. There is more than one type of channel. We are impressing these thoughts on all who desire them, he says, not only on the ones who can speak them aloud. Daily meditation, and a natural progression in seeking, is enough. You do not have to speak for the voices to carry them.

Then the contact shifts, and the second half of the evening gives us the saying. There is a saying on your planet, Hatonn says, that goes, all roads lead to Rome. This is a very true saying, if you consider the road of life which lies before each of you.

There are many questions about which road to choose, he goes on, and many considerations about what action seems appropriate. What does it mean? Where shall I go? What shall I do? And here is the answer, and it dissolves the whole anxious apparatus of life planning. There are lessons in every road, and it is not what you encounter which marks the rate of your spiritual progress. It is rather the quality of your awareness of what you encounter.

Not what you encounter. The quality of your awareness of what you encounter. The road does not matter the way you think it does. The job, the city, the relationship, the choice you are agonizing over tonight, none of them is the test. The test is the attention you bring to whichever one you are on.

Daily meditation, he says, encourages the shifting of the attention from the exterior illusion to the infinity within. When you have questions such as I described, remember that the answers lie within you, waiting to be unfolded through daily meditation.

All roads lead to Rome. Every path you could take is a path, and every path has its lessons, and the lessons are not in the scenery. They are in the seeing. So the frantic question, did I choose the right road, gets a gentle answer. You are on a road. Bring your awareness to it. That was always the assignment.

Tonight, whatever road you are on, try the shift. Not a different road. A different attention.

Thank you for listening.

title: Exactly What You Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: exactly what you desire.

March eighteenth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn speaks at length this evening about desire, and he means it in the deepest sense. Not wishes. Not cravings. The fundamental orientation of the being. And what he says about it will either offend you or free you, depending on how you hear it.

It is the wish of our Creator, he says, that man throughout the universe get what he desires in all instances. Each of the individuals upon the surface of your planet are obtaining exactly what they desire.

Exactly what they desire. He repeats it, because he knows how it lands. It is sometimes difficult to understand, he admits, that each individual within the illusion is obtaining exactly what he desires. It is difficult for an individual who is in a position he considers undesirable to accept that he is being rewarded with exactly what he does desire.

I want to be careful with this one, because it is easy to hear as blame. Hatonn is not saying your suffering is your fault. He is describing a law, the way you would describe gravity. The mechanism is infallible, he says. It was designed by a Creator who expressed nothing but total love. The plan was infallible and is infallible. What looks like the world ignoring your desires is, from a larger vantage, the world answering them precisely, including the desires you do not know you hold.

This is why the teaching matters practically. It is only necessary for man on Earth to learn how to change his desires, Hatonn says, in order to experience the truth of desire. You cannot change the law. You can change the signal you are sending into it. It is only necessary for him to desire love, and therefore express and experience it in all of his activities.

Desire love, and the machinery of the universe, which cannot help but deliver exactly what is desired, begins delivering love. That is the whole technology. There is no more to it, and there is nothing less.

This we bring to the people of the planet Earth, he says. Our understanding of the true workings of this creation. It is much simpler than you might expect. And yet it is much different than you might expect. Simple, because the law has one moving part. Different, because it puts the responsibility exactly where we least want it. On the desirer.

Earlier in the evening, through Carla, he gave the instruction that makes the larger teaching possible. In meditation, do not bring your intellect, my friends. Drop it. Put it down. It will not serve you. It will only beguile you. The light that you see during the day is in fact beauty and power, he says. You and your brothers share this reality. Relax, meditate, and if you wish us to serve you, it is our greatest pleasure to be with you.

The intellect wants to argue with the law of desire. It wants to list the exceptions, the injustices, the evidence. Hatonn's advice is to put it down at the door, the way you would set down a heavy bag before entering a quiet room. You can pick it up later. For now, just sit.

He closes with faith, and with a promise. There will be difficulties in the awakening, he says. But the only requirement is faith. For each individual will awaken. Perhaps not immediately. Perhaps in what you would consider the farthest regions. However, he will awaken. And we will serve him, for that is our desire. For in serving him we serve ourselves, as we do in serving you.

So tonight, the question is not what you want. It is what you desire, underneath the wanting. The universe is already delivering it. Make sure it is love.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are Already Channels
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are already channels.

March nineteenth, nineteen seventy-four, first meditation. The room is full of people learning to channel, and Hatonn says something that quietly redefines the whole project. My friends, he says, are we not all channels? Always, in all our aspects, do we not demonstrate something? What, my friends, do you demonstrate?

Sit with that. The question is not whether you are a channel. The question is what you are broadcasting. Every person in every room is transmitting something, all day, with their face, their tone, their attention. The only choice is whether it is conscious.

To make the point, he reaches for the natural world, and the passage is one of the loveliest in the early archive. Look about you, he says. Look at the water as it rides along the shore, flowing freely, not choosing, but going infinitely, equally, from place to place. See the rain as it falls upon the sea. It does not choose to fall over here or over there, but it spreads equally.

Consider the atmosphere, he goes on. It ever flows, it equalizes itself, not selecting this or that course, but choosing them all. The Earth does not choose. It gives what service it has to give to those who ask. Consider that you are channels, my friends, every day, in all that you do and say. You reflect something.

The rain does not audition its recipients. The shore does not interview the water. Nature gives without choosing, and Hatonn holds that up as the model. Take the potential that you have raised, he tells them, and demonstrate it as best you can. Your meditations, he says, are like a storing up of energy, a charging, a raising of your potential forces. The sitting still is the charging. The living is the broadcast.

He is also frank about why the Confederation bothers with any of this. The time of the great harvest is at hand, he says. Soon there will be more opportunities for you to be of service to your fellow man than you can presently offer them. The channels are being trained because the audience is about to arrive. People will start seeking, and when they do, someone needs to be able to answer.

And this, he says, is the greatest thing one can do for another. To aid another in his or her spiritual evolution. Greater than comfort. Greater than rescue. To stimulate another to seek truth, and thereby aid their progression. That is the service.

One voice in the session states the offer in its simplest form. I and my brothers are always available to help you, Hatonn says. This is our purpose. All that is needed is that you desire it and avail yourself. No application. No worthiness test. No waiting list. The help is standing by, permanently, and the only switch is desire. It has always been the only switch.

There is a passage about the craft as well. Hatonn speaks from a small craft high above the dwelling, and he says the sightings are deliberate. It is our purpose that our craft be seen to some extent. Not to prove anything. To produce seeking. A light in the sky is a question mark. And a question mark is the beginning of a seeker.

But he draws the line carefully. Many have sought the truth of the craft, he says, but they have not been rewarded, because their seeking was of a nature that results in no real gain. Curiosity about the ships is not the same as seeking the truth. One wants a spectacle. The other wants a transformation.

So the evening ends where it began, with the redefinition. You are already channels. The training is not to become something new. It is to become conscious of what you have been doing all along, and to choose, deliberately, what you demonstrate.

Tonight, notice your own broadcast. Walking into a room, you change its weather. What weather are you bringing?

Thank you for listening.

title: The Walls You Built
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the walls you built.

March nineteenth, nineteen seventy-four, second meditation. Hatonn returns to his great theme, seeking, and this time he gives it a mechanism. He describes seeking as a projector, and the image is worth taking apart slowly.

Your seeking, he says, may be thought of as a projector, of which there are two components. The aimed direction of the projector, and the force which impels the seeking. The seeking itself is largely the directional portion. The energy which impels it is the function of the unity between you and the creation.

Two parts. The aim, which is yours to choose. And the power, which is not yours at all, but the universe's, flowing through the fact of your unity with it. There is an infinite amount of energy available to all entities at all times, he says. When properly directed and fully realized, there is no limit to how far one may seek. The electricity is free and unlimited. You only supply the direction.

But the degree of realization of unity varies from person to person, and it is through meditation that a closer realization is obtained. With the seeking carefully centered, aimed, and prepared, and with the energy channel opened, you embark upon your seeking. The practice tunes the projector. The aim sharpens. The current flows.

Then he names what blocks the current, and it is one of the most human passages in the early sessions. We are aware, he says, that it is not always as simple in the doing as in the telling, and we do not wish to infer that we are not aware of the difficulties of working within the illusion that you now enjoy. I love that admission. The voices know the projector is cleaner than the living of it. They are not selling ease. They are describing the mechanism and trusting you with the difficulty.

What you seek is all about you, he goes on. You have walled yourself away from what you seek because, within the illusion, it seems to be a safety-making factor to have walls. Physical walls. Mental walls of defense. Emotional limits beyond which each individual does not go. For he wishes to be safe within his walls, and within his illusion, these walls make him safe.

The walls make him safe. Within the illusion. That qualification is everything. The walls work, in the way a child's nightlight works. They make the dark feel manageable. But they also make the room small. And what you walled out was not only the danger. It was the thing you were seeking.

But, my friends, this is the illusion, Hatonn says. The reality is that you are part of the unity. There is none other than you. That which you seek is that which you are. You need only come into full realization of this unity, and that which you seek will be yours. This, my friends, is your birthright.

That which you seek is that which you are. Every wall you built to protect yourself from the world was built between you and yourself. The treasure was never across the moat. You were the treasure, and the moat was the only thing in the way.

Earlier in the evening he gave the proof, in the form of a life. The man known as Jesus, he said, displayed reactions to his environment quite different than those about him. His reactions were due to his own state of evolved consciousness. He was able to realize the truth of all that he experienced, and being able to do this, to truly react with intelligence and to serve his fellow man. Same world. Same events. Different walls. Different reactions.

It is necessary that an individual initiate his own seeking, Hatonn says. Once initiated, carry it through to realization. Many on the planet have reached the point where they need but little enticement to move that short distance onward. Perhaps you are one of them. Perhaps the wall is thinner than you think, and the distance shorter than you fear.

Tonight, find one wall. One defended place, one subject you do not go near, one feeling with a fence around it. You do not have to tear it down. Just notice it. Notice who built it, and what it was meant to keep out. The birthright is on both sides.

Thank you for listening.

title: Graduation at Hand
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: graduation at hand.

March twenty-third, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn speaks through Carla this evening, and the session has a strange, quiet gravity to it. He is talking about the end of something. Not the end of the world. The end of a set of lessons.

He begins with a disclaimer that I wish more teachers would make. We are still seeking, he says. We are not of the ultimate authority. Nor would we ever insist upon anyone listening to what we have to say, if another mode of thinking seemed more profitable. Understanding is possible only for one person at one time. Each person is completely free at any time to choose. This is why we are indirect. We may say things to you that you may consider in the privacy of your own thoughts, and what you choose to do is completely your own idea.

This is as it should be, he says. And I love the confidence in that. No sales pitch. No urgency. The truth does not need your agreement to remain true, so it can afford to wait for you.

Then the cosmology of the evening. Our understanding of this illusion, which is taken for physical life, he says, is that it consists of a path, of a road, to be followed, and of lessons to be learned. There are as many paths as there are people, and there are no set lessons.

No set lessons. Your curriculum was never published. There is no syllabus you are behind on. There are only the lessons that arrive, in the order they arrive, on the road you happen to be walking.

But after a great many lessons have been met, he goes on, there comes a time when all of the lessons change to a different set. And those who are ready for the change go on to a new set of lessons. It is our understanding that the planet known as Earth approaches the end of one set of these lessons. And thus graduation is at hand for some, and not at hand for others. And there are many people balanced very delicately between going on and repeating these lessons for another cycle.

Graduation is at hand for some. Read that without the apocalyptic reflex. He is not describing destruction. He is describing a school. Some students are finishing the coursework. Some will repeat the year. Many are balanced delicately between the two, and it is those in-between ones the Confederation most wants to reach. It is our desire, he says, to aid those who are almost ready to graduate.

And why do they care? Because in our service to you lies our service to ourselves. It is by our serving you that we are able to progress upon our spiritual path. The teachers need the students as much as the students need the teachers. The graduation, if it happens, graduates everyone involved.

He adds, quietly, that this has worked before. In their graduating, he says, we have had some success in the past in giving this service to other peoples, in other places and times. This is not their first school. Other planets, other cycles, other groups balanced delicately between going on and repeating. Some made it. The precedent exists, which means the hope is not theoretical.

He closes with the practice, and with the example. Seek understanding, my friends. Seek through meditation. And seek to know there was a reason that the master teacher known as Jesus retreated from time to time to a place where there was silence. There was something he was seeking. Seek for the silence where there is much understanding awaiting you.

Even Jesus needed the quiet. The busiest teacher in the tradition kept slipping away to be alone. If he needed the silence, with everything he knew, then the silence is not a luxury for beginners. It is the classroom itself.

So tonight, the invitation is simple. Find a place where there is silence, even a small one, even for a few minutes. The lessons are ending, or beginning, or repeating. The silence knows which. Go and listen.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Wise Man's Gift
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the wise man's gift.

March twenty-fourth, nineteen seventy-four. The contact is difficult all evening. The instrument keeps losing the thread, and Hatonn keeps patiently picking it back up. And somewhere in the middle of the static, he tells a story. A parable, really. The archive does not have many of them, which is why this one shines.

But first, a strange and lovely aside about identity. I am Hatonn, he says. I identify myself to you as the one that you know as Hatonn. However, this is for purposes of establishing a contact between you and us. This identification is more of an address than it is an identification of a separate part of the creation. We do not recognize a separation in this creation. We only recognize unity. It is, however, convenient to have an address.

An address, not a name. Like a house number on a street where all the houses are one house. I think about that every time one of the voices introduces itself now. The name is for us, not for them. They do not need it.

Then the story. Upon your planet there once lived a man, Hatonn says. This man had great material wealth, and this gave him what he considered to be power. For many of his fellow men would eagerly do his bidding for a part of this wealth. And so he acquired more, believing that in wealth there was power, and in power, happiness, and in happiness, security for the rest of his days.

What is not understood by those men, Hatonn says, is that in acquiring this wealth, and in attempting to possess much power through this wealth, they are giving up an infinite amount of power for that which is in actuality no power at all. An infinite amount of power, traded for no power at all. That is the exchange rate of the illusion, stated plainly.

The rich man had everything he desired, and great status. But he lacked one thing. He lacked love. For it was not given to him by those about him, and this he did not understand. So he set out to find it the way he found everything else. He went to a wise man, and offered to pay him much of his wealth if he would but tell him how to obtain love.

And here the story turns strange. The wise man gave unto the rich man all that he possessed, which was but a pitiful small amount. And the rich man accepted it, for he had long ago resolved never to turn down a gift. And he left the wise man penniless. For he had not paid the wise man. For the wise man had not told him how to find love.

Days passed, and the rich man returned, baffled. Why had the wise man given him everything? And the wise man answered. It is because I have a great love for you, and you desire wealth. Therefore I give you that which I have, to add to your riches, for this is what you desire.

The wise man did not lecture him about the emptiness of riches. He did not refuse him. He loved him, and gave him what he asked for. And in that moment, something broke open. The rich man looked at the wise man and said, and for the first time, know love. And he gave to the wise man great wealth. And in doing so, he felt an even greater love. For, for the first time, he had learned the truth of the Creator's gifts to His children.

Do you see the mechanism? Love was not purchased. It was not taught. It was demonstrated, and in the demonstration, it was transmitted. The wise man loved first, without guarantee, and the rich man caught it like a fire catches. Giving, it turns out, is not the price of love. Giving is what love looks like from the outside.

Hatonn closes the parable with the diagnosis. Man on Earth continues to seek within his material illusion that which is of no real value, for he lacks faith. He stands upon the surface of this planet and experiences all of the gifts of his Creator. He breathes the air and smells the fragrance of the flowers and is in the company of his fellow man. And yet he does not understand. He does not have faith that within this creation, he has supply.

He has supply. The warehouse was never empty. The rich man was never poor. He was only looking at the wrong ledger.

Tonight, the question from the parable. What are you trying to buy that can only be given? And what could you give, right now, that would teach you how?

Thank you for listening.

title: The Fabric of Nothingness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the fabric of nothingness.

March twenty-eighth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn speaks from a craft in the atmosphere, and he gives the evening to a single subject. The illusion. What it is, why it exists, and how to see through it without leaving the world. It is one of the most practical sessions in the early archive.

He begins with communication itself. Telepathy, he says, is the normal technique for communication. The method used by the people of your planet is not at all normal. The Tower of Babel referred to in your Bible refers to the loss of ability of the people at that time to communicate with each other using what you call telepathy.

I love the inversion. We think of telepathy as the miracle and speech as the baseline. Hatonn says it is the reverse. Direct mind-to-mind knowing is the factory setting. Grunting through air with sound waves is the workaround we invented after we forgot. The isolation you feel is not the human condition. It is a recent malfunction.

It is necessary to be in tune with the intended expression of love that created this universe, he says, to use telepathy as it was intended. The tuner is not technique. The tuner is love. Which is why the whole archive keeps circling back to the same two practices. Meditate. Love. Everything else is commentary.

Then he defines reality, and the definition is worth memorizing. Reality, he says, is the original concept of our Creator, rather than its extension through the experiments of His children. The world you argue with every day is not the creation. It is the creation plus everyone's renovations. The original blueprint is still underneath.

The separation between your consciousness and other consciousness is the illusion, he says. The separation is illusion and is not reality. It is possible through meditation to totally reduce this illusory separation to what it actually is. A total illusion.

And here is the practice, stated with unusual force. It is extremely important that every thought generated by an individual who wishes to make progress be analyzed immediately upon generation. If this thought is generated by the false illusion, then this thought should be immediately rejected. Every thought. Immediately. Checked at the door.

That sounds exhausting until you hear the reason. The illusion, he says, is useful. It was generated out of desire, and it is useful for those who would wish to evolve at a very rapid rate by experiencing it and then overcoming it while within it. Many of us who are now circling your planet, he says, would desire to have the opportunity that you have. The opportunity to be within the illusion and, through understanding, overcome its potentials.

The beings in the craft envy the beings on the ground. Let that land. The confusion you resent is the classroom they wish they could attend.

And then the image that gives this episode its title. Think backwards in what you consider time, Hatonn says. Say, one year. Consider all the potentials within the illusion that you experienced in that time, and how they affect you now. Think backwards five years, or ten, or fifteen. The illusion has no lasting effects, my friends. It dissolves. It is a fabric of nothingness.

A fabric of nothingness. Try the experiment tonight. Take the worry that consumed you a year ago, the one that felt permanent, and notice how little of it remains. The illusion does not need to be defeated. It needs to be outlasted. It dissolves on its own. It was always dissolving.

Who are you today, he asks, and why are you you, today? It is because of your thinking. It is because of your reactions to the illusion. Wherein lies truth, my friends? It lies in you. In your ability to express it lies your ability to serve. In your reaction to the illusion lies your ability to demonstrate your awareness.

The teacher known as Jesus, he says, recognized the illusion, understood the reason for the potentials within it, and his reactions expressed the Thought of the Creator. A Thought of love. Same world. Same provocations. Different reactions. That was the whole miracle.

So the practice stands. Guard the door of the mind. Reject what is generated by the nothingness. Express what is generated by love. And when the noise gets loud, think backwards, and watch it dissolve.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Choice Before Us
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the choice before us.

April of nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn is speaking through Don, and he has come with news. More of their craft will be seen in your skies, he says, and soon. They mean to advertise their presence. Not to prove anything. Not to frighten anyone. Simply to alert those who have heard of them but never considered them of any importance. A choice is coming, he says, and everyone on this planet will make it, whether they understand it or not.

Listen to how plainly he lays it out. There will be those who choose to follow the path of love and light, and those who choose otherwise. This is all that is necessary. No middle area. And here is the part I keep returning to: this choice will not be made by saying the words. The verbal choice will mean nothing. The choice will be measured by demonstration. Not by what you claim. By what you show.

He gives the mechanism a name that sounds technical but is really quite simple. The vibratory rate of the individual. It is necessary, he says, if an individual is to join those who choose love and understanding, for his rate of vibration to be above a certain minimal level. And he is honest about where things stand. Many are close to that level. But the erroneous thought prevailing on the surface keeps them fluctuating around it, or even drifting away. And there are many whose vibration is already high enough to move, with no difficulty, into the density this planet is about to experience.

So what is the task of a group like this one, a small circle of meditators in a living room, while the Confederation begins to make itself visible? Hatonn says their work is to bring understanding, to those who desire it, of their alternatives. That is it. And he names what is coming in a phrase you will hear again and again across these years: the harvest. A harvest of souls. He does not soften it. We are the harvesters, he says. Our mission is to extract the greatest possible harvest from this planet.

And here is the mystery of their method, which I find beautiful and a little strange. They are trying first to create a state of seeking among those close to the acceptable level. Those above it, he says, have already made the grade. Those far below it cannot be helped at this time. And even a small percentage of this planet's people is a vast number. But the offering must be truth without proof. No concrete evidence, as he puts it. They will offer truth and nothing else. Because if proof were given, if belief were forced, it would have no usable effect on anyone's vibratory rate. The motivation, he says, must come from within the individual.

Think about what that means. He is telling you that your freedom matters more to them than your agreement. They could show you. They will not. Because being convinced is not the same as being changed, and only what rises from inside you raises you.

And so groups like this one become, in his words, the second stage of the approach. He uses a metaphor from your own world, and it makes me smile every time: they are the advertising display in your atmosphere, and the small meditation groups are the commercial that follows it. But the truth they carry must be exact, he says. Nothing else will do. And only in meditation can they avail themselves of the precise truth, and only in meditation can they learn to speak it in the language of their peoples.

He does not pretend it will be easy. He says plainly that it will be a great task, and that they will not be entirely successful. They have seen harvests before. The dissemination will fall short. But the harvest itself, he says, will be complete. There will be a complete success in the harvest of which we speak. What will be done for each person is up to the individual, and his desire to understand, and his desire to seek this truth, to create his vibratory change, even though it may necessarily only be slight.

I love that last line. Even though it may necessarily only be slight. Hatonn is not asking for saints. He is asking for a small movement in the right direction, made from within, by people too busy and too confused to know a choice is being made at all.

And the choice, remember, is not spoken. It is demonstrated. In every act of love, in every turning toward light, the choice is made. The skies may change. The advertising may appear. But the choosing happens quietly, inside, one demonstration at a time.

Thank you for listening.

title: Peace, Be Still
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: peace, be still.

April third, nineteen seventy-four, the evening after. Hatonn is speaking through a different instrument tonight, and the contact is difficult. There are gaps, pauses, inaudible stretches. But what comes through clearly is worth the trouble. He has come, in part, to talk about the people in the room who are beginning to become channels themselves. And he begins somewhere unexpected: with a storm on a lake, two thousand years ago.

You may remember, he says, reading the holy work you call the Bible, that the master known as Jesus had a simple reaction to the upsetting type of illusion which he faced. His reaction was to inform it that it was an illusion. When he was confronted with a very stormy sea, he said, Peace. Be still. And by understanding that the difficulty was an illusion, that vision caused his own reality to become peaceful and still.

Listen to how they put it. The ability to look at the illusion upon your planet and say to it, Peace. Be still, is very dearly earned. He does not pretend otherwise. They are aware, he says, of the great efforts which a person living upon the surface of your planet must make to accomplish the detachment of which they speak. And yet, he says, once this is accomplished, you may find it to have been worth the effort, and more than worth the effort. For reality, my friends, is a freedom that is a great joy to those who have never known what lies beyond the illusion of storm.

I love that phrase: the illusion of storm. Not the storm itself. The illusion of storm. As if the trouble is real enough to your senses, and yet, at the level that matters, it is weather passing through something larger.

Then he turns to the practical matter at hand. The group is learning to channel. This gives their hearts great gladness, he says. But he offers one caution, and it is the heart of the evening: there is a Peace, be still, to be inserted before any information is passed. Before the channel opens her mouth, let her still the waters. The reason is simple and strict. So that you do not say that which has not been asked. And that you say what you say in such a way that it does not infringe.

That is the whole ethic of channeling in three clauses. Do not speak what was not asked for. Do not impose. Still yourself first. Because this service, he says, needs the purity of that Peace, be still. It needs the detachment to listen to what is answered. It needs the ability to allow oneself to be linked to the higher, infinite mind that will answer truth. Incorrect information, or information given at the wrong time, may not be of service. And then, with great gentleness: they rejoice that these people are becoming channels, and may they offer their service always, at any time, to help in any way they can.

Later in the evening, speaking through another instrument, Hatonn returns to the same theme from a different angle. Be grateful, he says, whenever you are asked to be of aid. Service is the only means of evolving into realms or ways. And be cautious not to create any negative train of thought. There is nothing in all of creation to be alarmed at, he says, if you are in a constant state of consciousness.

Nothing in all of creation to be alarmed at. I have to sit with that one. It is easy to read as comfort. But I think it is instruction. Alarm is what the storm wants from you. Stillness is what answers it.

And there is a promise tucked into this session that I want you to hear. They cannot contact all of the peoples of your planet at this time, he admits, because many have not yet awakened. But the time will be short. And when those people begin to seek, they will need information through channels such as the ones in this room. In order to gain a strong grip on the light, they will be able to evolve rapidly once making the decision. Once making the decision. The decision does the work. Everything after is momentum.

So the evening's teaching comes down to two sentences, really. Say to the storm: Peace. Be still. And when you are asked to serve, be grateful, for it is a gift from the Creator. Everything else in the session, the difficult contact, the arriving group members, the tape running out, is just the weather around those two sentences.

Find a storm in your own day, however small, and try it. Look at it and say, in whatever words are yours: Peace. Be still. See if your reality answers.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Ship Overhead
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the ship overhead.

April eighth, nineteen seventy-four. A Monday. And tonight the voice is not Hatonn's. It is Oxal. The contact is rough. The instrument struggles. Sentences start and restart. Whole passages fall into inaudibility. But through the static, Oxal tells them something extraordinary, and he tells it plainly, as if it were the most natural thing in the world.

I am at this time, he says, in a craft above your house.

Let me say that again, slowly, the way he must have wanted it heard. He is speaking to them, right now, from a craft hovering above the house they are sitting in. A small vehicle, he says, used for short reconnaissance. He cannot meet them in a direct physical way. He realizes they would wish to meet, and he wishes for the same. But at this time, he says, it is not possible.

I find this session deeply moving, precisely because it is so broken. Here is a being from somewhere else, close enough to be overhead, reaching down through a struggling instrument, through pauses and static and repeated I am Oxal, I am with this instrument, just to say: we are here. We wish we could be with you the way you wish. We cannot. Not yet.

And then he turns from the fact of his presence to its purpose. We of the Confederation, he says, have primarily attempted to serve you in arousing the interest in seeking. That has been the program so far: to wake up the question. But shortly, he says, we must serve you in an additional way. More direct. And this is the turn the whole evening rests on: it will be necessary, if they are to do this, that you prepare yourselves. And the preparation is one thing only. Meditation.

We will not be able to communicate with you, he says, unless you are able to avail yourself to our thoughts in meditation. We cannot contact you in the manner you are accustomed to using upon the surface of your planet. This would be of no avail. We do not have concepts in your language that we wish to convey. We have concepts that are not within your language.

Read that twice. The limitation is not theirs. It is ours. Their thoughts do not fit in our words. The only bridge is a quieted mind. If you will avail yourself in meditation to us, he says, we will prepare for our meeting. But this is essential.

There is a moment in the session, half lost to the tape, where Oxal seems to do something to them. We are going to at this time prepare each of you in a certain way, he says. It will be obvious to you. Please be patient for a few moments. Then a pause. Then: feel the rhythm, the rhythm of your breath, as it slowly becomes one with all that surrounds you. This realization is important. It is a major step towards reaching a new level of consciousness for the peoples of your planet.

All the peoples of your planet have this potential, he says, if they so desire it. There are no rules that omit any one of you.

And then, near the end, the sentence the whole broken evening was building toward. For love is all there is, my friends. This is the mainstay of all creation. We offer it to you. You must learn to offer it to all of those around you.

He closes with a warning and a promise braided together. Your planet, he says, is in the midst of many changes. These changes will affect your lives in many ways. I know it is hard for you to understand, but you must trust, for we do bring love.

So tonight's teaching is simple enough to carry in one hand. There is a craft above the house. There will be no landing, no handshake, no proof. There is only the invitation, repeated through the static: quiet your mind, and we will meet you there. The meeting was never going to happen on the lawn. It was always going to happen in the silence.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Inner Garden
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the inner garden.

April tenth, nineteen seventy-four. Two voices tonight. Laitos opens, briefly, speaking of conditioning, of silence as a medium. We will be using the next few moments, he says, in order to communicate to you through the medium of silence. Silence, not as an absence of message, but as the message itself. Then Hatonn takes the instrument, and what follows is one of the most beautiful passages in this stretch of the archive.

He speaks of conditioning first, the invisible work they do on the group. The conditioning wave, he says, is sent in a blanket wave. Some feel it immediately as energy. Others feel nothing at all, and yet they are receiving it just the same. I love this image. A blanket wave. It falls on everyone in the room equally. What you feel depends on how you are tuned. The work is happening whether you notice it or not.

And then he says: we do not wish to bore you with speeches. And offers, instead, a place.

You are in a garden at this point, my friends. In your holy works it is called the Garden of Eden, and in the garden there is perfection, there is safety, there is protection, against all, against each, against every possible evil, for indeed, my friends, within the Garden of Eden there is no evil. You are in this place as you meditate, my friends, for this place is reality. This perfect garden is truly your home.

Listen to how they put it. Not the garden was your home, long ago, before the fall. The garden is your home. Now. When you meditate, you are not visiting a memory. You are returning to reality. The life you live outside of it, with its noise and its threat, is the temporary address.

And then comes the instruction, and it is not what you might expect. He does not say: visit this garden when you are tired. He says: take this high place, this garden, this home, and live in it in your mind. Not just in meditation, but always. Keep it close. Reach for it. Move into it. Keep it by you. Use it. Live in it. Become one with the garden, for this is your true identity, and in this realization your shining beauty will give grace and happiness to many.

I have read that passage many times, and what strikes me is the verbs. Keep. Reach. Move. Use. Live. Become. This is not contemplation as escape. It is contemplation as residence. He is asking them to carry the garden with them into the grocery store, into the argument, into the ordinary Tuesday. Your true identity, he says, is not the worried person walking through the world. It is the garden itself. And when you know that, your shining beauty gives grace and happiness to many. Notice: you do not have to do anything with the beauty. You do not have to aim it. Shining is enough. Being the garden is the service.

There is a second half to the evening, quieter, about practice. Hatonn notes that the instrument known as R is having difficulty receiving, and he is gentle about it. It is only necessary to practice, he says, and to maintain a relaxation and a lack of analysis that produces a good contact. The good channel is not the clever one. It is the relaxed one. The one who has stopped analyzing.

And he closes with a line that stays with me. I leave your physical awareness at this time, he says, though I stand sentinel above you, far above you, waiting and watching for any way in which I may be of service. Only seek our aid and we will surely be there, within the silence and within your service.

Within the silence and within your service. As if those were the same place. As if the garden and the work were one address.

So tonight, one image to carry. A garden with no fence around it that anyone can build, because it is inside you. No one may pass there. No one may distract. No one may say you nay. It is yours. Live in it, he says. Not just when you close your eyes. Always.

Thank you for listening.

title: Desire Like Fire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: desire like fire.

April twelfth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn has come to talk about a single word, and he begins by telling you the word is wrong. Desire, he says, is a somewhat misunderstood phenomenon upon planet Earth. The misunderstanding lies in the feeling that one has desires about only certain sorts of objects. The truth, my friends, is much closer to the intensity of fire. There is, however, no such word as what we are looking for, and we use the word desire.

Sit with that for a moment. The entities who speak through this archive are always reaching past our vocabulary. They take the nearest word and then apologize for it. Desire is not wanting a thing. Desire is fire. It is the intensity itself, before it has chosen an object.

And then Hatonn says something that rearranges the whole of your biography. Each incident that you experience in your present activities is a result of one thing, my friends: desire. The work of past desire is brought to fruition in the present. And your desire at this time shapes your future. You were given complete freedom of choice by an infinitely loving Creator. Give back to Him the highest desire you can be aware of.

Your life, in other words, is not happening to you. It is the harvest of what you have wanted, and the seed of what you are wanting now. This is not blame. It is authorship. The fire has been burning all along. The only question is what you feed it.

Be aware, he says, that there is much to transcend. The earthly desires can be passed fairly rapidly by those who seek. Even the esoteric, intellectual desires, the sophisticated ones, the spiritual ambitions, can soon be passed by. And then he asks a question that I find startling and wonderful.
