Such a person, they say, was most usually not intensely negative to begin with, but unpolarized, swinging in what they call the potential well of indifference, moving at times in service to others with great sincerity, and at times, like a pendulum, in service to self with great dedication. This is normal, they say, upon this planet at this time. The transformation is not a reversal. It is a choosing. A move from confusion into a more purely positive seeking.

So here is the evening, held together. You are never alone. New helpers are arriving. The planet is sorting itself, light from shadow, not to punish anyone, but because the harvest is near and every soul is deciding, in each small choice, which way it leans. And the great majority of us, swinging in that well of indifference, are simply being asked to choose a little more purely, a little more often.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Courage to Not Know
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the courage to not know.

Tonight Hatonn speaks about courage, and it is not the battlefield kind. It is the quieter courage of the seeker who keeps walking when the path stops promising answers. I have been turning this one over all week.

We have often been told, Hatonn begins, that the end of seeking will be knowledge and understanding, that we will find the answers we seek. Indeed, he says, you will find the answers you seek. But we have never suggested that you will find a key to the understanding of those answers. Listen to how they put the next part. The path which is narrow is a path the end of which is the realization that you do not know anything.

The reason the path is narrow, he says, is that not knowing is uncomfortable. To keep walking a path that promises further unknowing as the fruit of your current unknowing is simply not a very delectable path. So it is not much traveled. Those without courage, he says, will settle upon an answer, and that answer will keep them from changing, or at least changing as quickly.

Then he turns to the teacher known as Jesus, and I love this portrait. This teacher talked about himself only in the context of his relationship to the Father, to the Creator, to the One who is all things. He was aware that he was both created and Creator. He did not know anything beyond that, and each step that he took was taken after meditation, under the guidance of that which he did not previously know.

Do you have the courage, Hatonn asks, to accept your conscious unknown? For surely you have spent enough hours in despair because your actions were but a shadow of what you know. You resolve to meet all obstacles with love, and then you do not always do it. You do not know. It is the seeking, he says, continuous, balanced between seriousness and joy, fresh each day, that quickens you and leads you upon an ever narrower path.

And here is the promise that makes the narrowness bearable. Do not let the dimness of your mirror images ever discourage you for long. Do not let your own lack of manifestation ever discourage you for long. Do not let any error, as you may consider it, discourage you for long. It has often been noted, he says, that justice is blind among your peoples. We would further note, so is love, so is seeking.

See far enough to find the love, he says, and have the courage to release yourself from the responsibility of certain knowledge. Those who are certain about philosophy and spiritual evolution have simply placed themselves on a slower path, borne upon the shoulders of their comrades, given more encouragement, offered frequent rests. Courage, my friends. You who have it shall inherit a great mystery of being as can no one who seeks certain knowledge.

He closes with an image I cannot shake. You seek the wind, he says. It is invisible, it is infinite, and it will come and go when it will. Do you suggest that you shall know it, that you shall measure it, and put it between the pages of a book? Or do you instead seek to be it? Lift your wings, my friends, and soar.

The evening ends with Latwii answering questions, and one small exchange stays with me. A member marvels at the courtesy of advanced souls willing to wait, as she puts it, another seventy-five thousand years so that somebody else can have a turn at incarnation. A whole new light, she says, on the word courtesy. Even the beings ahead of us, it seems, practice the same courage. The courage to wait, and not to know, and to trust the timing.

Thank you for listening.

title: Healing Begins Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: healing begins within.

The group came together one March evening with health on their minds, and Hatonn offered what he called yet another perspective on the healing process. I want to say up front, the way he does, that this is offered as a way of looking, not as medicine. If you are carrying an illness of your own tonight, I hope you hear it as they meant it. Not as blame. As an invitation to look inward.

We exist, Hatonn says, within an illusion in which the conscious mind seems divided from the unconscious, and that veiling is what makes your choices carry such weight. The unconscious is your direct link to all of creation. If its resources were fully available to you, he says, you would have no doubt as to the nature of your being. The gift of the veil is that your choices matter more.

Then the teaching at the heart of the evening. Healing, he says, occurs first in what you may call the metaphysical realms, in the inner nature of the entity, and is manifested in the physical vehicle as the last portion of the recovery. It is triggered solely by the inner choice of the entity. Whether the outer means is a physician or a healer or a change of diet or simply a decision, the healing begins within, at the level where the Creator within moves to restore balance when the lesson that required the imbalance has been learned.

So his suggestion, when asked about healing, is always the same first step. Seek in meditation the nature of the lesson that stands before you when you experience what you call disease. To look elsewhere, he says, is to invite a less than clear perception. You chose the experience you face, and it is the inner being that chose it. To seek within is to look in the only direction where you will find a clear reflection.

And then the cheerful thought he leaves them with, which I love for its plainness. The body, he says, is completely capable of healing itself. The cells of your body are in tune with the infinite source of creativity of the universe. But the belief systems of your culture feed the subconscious concepts of illness that fill you with fear and anxiety, and fear and anxiety, he says, are enemies of good health.

Latwii takes the questions, and one member asks for something I found very moving. She says she gets, every so often, a divine spark of truth that satisfies her mind for a while, but she has not found one in about a month, and her mind feels starved. Would Latwii give her a spark to feed her for another month?

Listen to how gently they turn it back on her. They are unsure they can provide a spark to one used to the flame of truth in many forms, they say. But they suggest she look at the very feeling of being uncomfortable. For is not such a feeling as full of truth as the feeling of comfort which comes from inspiration? I love that line. The hunger itself is the teaching.

Another member asks about tones in the ears, and whether they relate to his seeking. Latwii says there is no condition you can experience which is not related to your seeking, and describes the tones as signals. A tone in the right ear, they say, recognizes the appropriateness of the thought or action that came just before it. The left ear signals the opposite. And there is a third tone, at the crown of the head, which signals neither, but the balanced nature of what came before. Whether you take this literally or as poetry, it is a lovely image of a self in conversation with itself.

So the evening comes down to one direction, pointed to again and again. Inward. The lesson behind the symptom. The truth inside the discomfort. The signal inside the silence. The body knows the way back to balance, Hatonn says, and the mind, if it will only listen, can learn the way there too.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Freedom to Risk
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the freedom to risk.

Tonight Hatonn speaks in parable, and it is one of my favorites in the whole archive. It begins with a child and a tricycle, and it ends with the whole of the spiritual journey. Come along slowly. It is worth it.

When a child wearies of walking, Hatonn says, he may ask for a tricycle. Long ago the adventurous rode a tall-wheeled machine, the velocipede, and dared life and limb upon it. Then came the metal tricycle, off which a child could conceivably fall and bruise himself. And then, for those who desire that no risk be taken, came the soft plastic big-wheeled tricycle that cannot fall over. Upon it the child cannot come to harm. Of course, the child cannot then risk himself or dare an adventure, except in imagination. But this satisfies those who keep watch over him.

When the child grows and asks for a bicycle, the element of risk returns. The older adventurers swerve around corners crying out their joy, going nowhere in particular. They are risking themselves. And then the child becomes an adult, and the daring fades into mere transportation. Perhaps the adult no longer dares the risks for the simple adventure of it.

Now, Hatonn says, as adults, the risks, the journeys, and the daring are interior. And yet still there are those who would condemn you to the spiritual equivalent of the big soft plastic three-wheeled environment, where all your risk would be in your imagination. It has not been the choice of this creation, he says, to offer safety to each co-creator. You are free to risk, to dream and to dare. I love that line. Say it out loud sometime. You are free to risk, to dream and to dare.

Those who find little joy in their experience, he says, are often those who have, of their own free will, chosen to limit the degree of risk in their seeking. So look into your heart, he asks, and search out that which you measure, that which stays low to the ground because you do not wish to risk a fall. It may be an opportunity to enhance your journey.

Then he retells the parable of the two sons, and he retells it as a story about risk. One son took his inheritance and spent it foolishly, and was reduced to the lowliest work imaginable, until he fell to his knees and turned toward home. And the father said, my son who was dead is now alive. Rejoice. Prepare a feast. The other son had pedaled carefully through life, taking no risks, making no mistakes, and he felt not love but jealousy. He had missed his journey.

Can you ever return, Hatonn asks, if you do not set out? Whether it is a small thing or a large, do that which is true to you, even if it is a mistake in action. For it is often the unwise choice, made from fear of losing control, that brings the catalyst that teaches you the most, and returns you to feast with the Creator in the kingdom where bread is of the spirit.

So tonight is not a scolding about your caution. It is an invitation. Somewhere in your life there is a bicycle waiting, and you have been riding the plastic tricycle. The road is interior now. The falls will not bruise your knees. But the wind in your face, Hatonn promises, will be real.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Steel Door
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the steel door.

Hatonn begins tonight by showing the instrument a picture. A door, made of steel, with a steel handle. The walls around it are blank. There is no sign saying where it leads. But impressed upon the heart of everyone who stands before it is a phrase from one of your holy works. The first shall be last and the last shall be first.

This is the gateway between the conscious and the unconscious mind, and Hatonn does not soften it. In some messages, they say, this barrier has been called the veil. We call it steel. Let us not deceive you as to the difficulty of what you attempt to do. I admire that honesty. No false promises about how easy the inner life is.

The teaching that follows is about where we put our attention. You stand before this door, Hatonn says, constantly monitoring your supposed spiritual readiness, telling yourself you have no time for the simple, easy parts of your life because you must work on the difficult parts. It is as though you are ten minutes late to an ever-running appointment with your life, forever behind, forever trying to catch up.

Do you think love wears a wrist watch, they ask. I love that line. You cannot be late, they say, nor can you miss that which is within you. The feeling of missing is itself the illusion. Have you loved as the Creator loves you? Have you cherished the joy of those about you? Until your experience sings with joy, they say, there is more to do. And that work belongs as much in the happy, tranquil moments as in the painful ones.

Then the questions turn, and Latwii is asked about the nature of sexual energy, and I will handle this the way the evening does, plainly and without embarrassment. Each entity, Latwii says, carries a vital energy of mind, body, and spirit, and the physical portion is what your peoples call sexual energy. When two share it with love, each gives something different. The male offers physical refreshment, the female offers mental and emotional inspiration, and each potentiates the other, so the experience enriches both.

Latwii even makes a joke about it, calling the exchange a kind of celestial lubrication, and you can hear the group laugh on the tape. Then they grow serious again. As the energy centers open, the sharing can become sacramental, and the indigo center, the gateway, can touch what they call the cosmic consciousness experience, the contact with the one infinite Creator felt by both.

Asked whether this level of sharing requires a true mated bond, Latwii will not say impossible, only difficult. The green center of unconditional love and the blue center of honest communication take time to open between two people, and that is the bias of your Logos toward the mated relationship. Yet free will is paramount, they say, and each will discover by experience the method most efficient for them.

And one member distills the whole long answer into a single sentence, which Latwii applauds. The requirements are constant, she says, but the methods of meeting the requirements are as various as the people. I will leave you with that, and with the steel door. It is heavy, but it opens from your side.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Denials of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the denials of love.

Tonight a quieter voice takes the floor. The ones who call themselves Oxal do not speak to this group often, and when they do, it is brief and pointed. Tonight they come with a story about denial, and it lands like a stone in still water.

The teacher known to you as Jesus said to his disciple, you shall deny me. And Simon, known as Peter, said, I shall never deny you. And yet, under certain circumstances, this disciple did deny his teacher. Look into the recesses of your own minds, Oxal says, and find the teacher within you, and the teaching within you. Shall you deny that teaching today?

How does one deny what one has learned, they ask. Is it by a word, a gesture, some portion of your life that is less than you would wish? Perhaps. But the fruit of deeper teaching is a person. When you deny your teaching, you are other than your teaching would have you be. How easy it is not to know, they say. How very difficult from time to time it becomes to be who your teachings have led you to become.

And here is the turn that makes this more than a warning. There was no rancor in the teacher's voice when he told his disciple, you shall deny me. There was only knowledge of the difficulty of responsibility. You are responsible, Oxal says, for what you have learned, and for what you are considering. Not because there is a sure knowledge somewhere, for even their teachers do not claim to know all that may be known. But because the heart of things asks you to be yourself, and you will find that difficult, and the difficulty itself is the teaching.

Then the line I cannot forget. Peter, Peter, they say, you shall deny love a million times, and in each denial you will come to know me better. And all the strangers who ask you, are you not the one who knows love, and cause you to deny, are aiding you. Do not forget to thank them in memory.

Shall you find love, then? My friends, they say, you have no choice. You cannot reckon with your own nature. Shall you find it quickly? In that, my friends, you have a great choice.

The evening continues with Latwii answering questions, and the group circles a hard teaching about suffering. One member offers her own hard-won summary, and Latwii agrees with the direction of it. Suffering, she says, is not necessary. When catalyst comes, we choose to find that it hurts instead of finding that it does not hurt. We have the choice, and some have learned to observe the difficulty and learn from it without adding the suffering. I offer that gently, the way the group did. Not as a judgment on anyone in pain, but as a direction to look.

So tonight holds two truths at once. You will deny what you know, a million times, and each denial will teach you. And the pain of the lesson is not the lesson. The lesson is love, finding you whether you are ready or not, and it has no choice but to find you, because you are it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Great Gamble
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the great gamble.

It is early April, a holy day, and Hatonn opens by saying they feel an overabundance of love coming from the planet on days like this, when so many are joined in seeking and thanksgiving. Tonight they speak of light, and of the gamble of the journey, and I think it is one of their most beautiful messages.

We speak to you of light, they say. Light, limitless, ever abundant, ever echoing and reechoing. You are all light. Each of you comes into the world as a light, but the world is in darkness, and knows you not and receives you not, and yet you shine in the darkness. Your eyes, they say, are twin lamps of love, beaming as watch towers, as light houses, as warning signs to those who wish to see.

When love created material, they say, the material it created was light. Light is creation, and all that is within creation is light. That is why light has the power to comfort, to bind, to unbind, to heal, to do all things. And there are none, they say, which are not of the light.

Then the turn. Be aware of light, they say, for the illusion will cause you to be aware of darkness, and darkness does not know light, it cannot see light, and shall not discover light. But you are light. And you are on a journey, they say. You are on a great gamble, and you must risk yourself or you shall not proceed upon your journey.

The light that you seek and that you are will aid you in your risk, but a risk it is, my friends, to choose. We risk and you risk. But the game is divine, they say, and losses are far more temporary than the inevitable lightsome outcome. I love that phrase. The inevitable lightsome outcome. Hold onto it on the dark days.

They close the message with the turning year. All the world sings of light at this time, they say. The springtime blossoms turn to the light and rejoice. So are the seasons of your life. So are the resurrections of your journey. Know always, in the deepest night, on the shortest day, there is that light within you. Doubt it not, but find it, and risk all to find it again more clearly, more abundantly, and then open yourselves and shine.

Latwii takes the questions, and one member asks for a mantra, a single phrase to work with on all levels. Latwii offers simple ones that touch the heart of being. I am love. I am light. I am one. I am whole. I am perfect. I am the one Creator. Repeat them in meditation, they say, or sing them as you go about your day. And when the member teases them, asking if there is no tummy ache mantra in their dogma, Latwii answers, we hope our mantras do not give you indigestion. Even the Confederation, it seems, enjoys a good laugh.

Another member is struggling at work, in an environment that feels deadening to the spirit. Latwii suggests a practice I have borrowed myself. Look upon yourself and your environment as though you were seeing another being. Describe what you see in objective terms. Instead of saying, I feel a difficulty because, say, I see an entity experiencing such and such. With yet another eye, they say, you may see the opportunity. With yet another eye, the lesson learned.

So the gamble is not reckless. It is the willingness to be light in a dark world, to risk the seeking, and to trust that the outcome, however long the night, is lightsome. That is the whole message, and it is enough.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Lesson of the Clam
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the lesson of the clam.

Tonight Hatonn tells a story about a clam, and I promise you it is going somewhere. Stay with the clam.

The creature lives beneath the sea, Hatonn says, a mollusk, a shelled entity, whose awareness is quite limited. Its interests are eating, excreting, and occasionally reproducing. It sought, in truth, the lack of event. It wanted a bland, uneventful existence. But it had the apparent misfortune to settle near a generating facility on land, which released sudden rushes of very hot water into its environment.

The clam was faced with a choice. Remain, and possibly stew. Or use its rudimentary equipment to move, slowly, over a period of years, away from the discomfort. First, though, came the real lesson. It was forced to perceive that a universe existed beyond the limits it had regarded as the limits of everything. The warm water could hardly be ignored.

So it moved. Reflexively, slowly, it pushed itself away. Many of its brothers and sisters made the same journey. Others stayed behind, clam-like in their unwillingness to perceive that other forces existed. Years passed. The journey was completed. And then, in the manner of such creatures, the clam relinquished its hold on its incarnation.

Now Hatonn turns the story on us, gently. Is it not true, they ask, that too often one must find the temperature of one's environment exceedingly uncomfortable before one seeks change of one sort or another? And in seeking that change, find that the change must entail a change of oneself. So a journey is begun. One stretches muscles one was only dimly aware of, and strives only to leave behind that uncomfortable state, in search of that which is unidentified, totally unfamiliar, yet toward which one is drawn as if following an instinctive beacon within the soul.

But here is where the comparison breaks, and Hatonn says so plainly. The clam was protected by its lack of awareness. You are not. You have been blessed, they say, with the ability to perceive the commonness of the journey, to recognize in the stranger crossing the street at the same moment as you that his beacon rings with the same note as your own. You differ from the clam in your ability to communicate, to choose not only to seek or ignore your seeking, but to aid or ignore the need for aid.

And then the comfort for the doubtful, which I love. They know, they say, that those who would serve are often consumed with doubt of their worthiness and their ability. So they remind the group of an old promise. If you wish sincerely for an opportunity to serve your brothers and sisters, you have but to ask, and that opportunity will be provided. He who asks his father for sustenance will not be given a snake to hold in his outstretched hands. Be confident in your acts of love, they say. Accept the blessing of the opportunity to be of service.

The evening closes with Oxal, brief as always, speaking of binding and unbinding. It is written, they say, that that which you bind shall be bound, and that which you unbind shall be let loose. Are you then a ruler of a universe? Yes, they say. You are co-Creator. As you see things, so they are. And what you see is final until you change what you see.

Two voices, one evening. The clam teaches that discomfort moves us. Oxal teaches that our seeing shapes what moves us toward. Between them, the whole spiritual life. Notice the heat. Choose the direction. And trust that when you ask to serve, the way to serve will be given.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Flung Splinter
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the flung splinter.

Tonight Hatonn gives a cosmology in a single image, and then spends the evening unfolding it. If you can imagine, they say, a moment incredibly far distant in time when you took all of creation into your hand and flung it from you, then you can imagine the impulse which guides your destiny.

You are, as a whole person, still abiding in the Creator, they say. But a splinter of your consciousness was flung outward for each of you, and that splinter has become you as you sit in meditation. The journey has been long. You have seen creations and planes and densities and lives. And through all of them you have been under the influence of that force of yourself which flings you outward, and at the same time calls you home.

This is the precious moment of all creation, they say. This instant is the excellent instant, far excelling past or future, for here your heart lies and your consciousness rests, and you can receive and give forth the breath of creation, love and light. I love that phrase. The excellent instant. Not yesterday's regret, not tomorrow's worry. This one.

And here is the part I want you to really hear. You did not make a mistake of any kind, they say, in choosing the circumstances and the seeming accidents of your life. You chose well, each of you. You gave yourself food and you gave yourself an appetite. Mental food, the food of analyzing and synthesizing and attempting to know. Emotional food, desires for love, experiences of love, experiences of the apparent lack of it. You wanted to catch your own attention and fix it. You wanted to make a point to yourself.

Spiritually speaking, they say, you consume far greater amounts of experience than ever you do earthly food. And what of your future? You are an eternal part of the One. In time, as the lessons are understood and the points are made, you will call that splinter of yourself back to yourself, drawn closer and closer to the source whence you were flung with such a greedy and extravagant hand before the beginning of time.

Breathe in, then, the joy of this moment, they say. Let your hearts be light as a fluttering gauze curtain at a window in the sunny breeze. For the wind is rich with blessings and there is music amongst the trees.

Latwii takes the questions, and a member asks how to stay faithful to love and service when a situation looks hopeless. Latwii's answer is one of the hardest teachings in the archive, and I will give it to you straight. If you wish to be pure in the positive polarity, they say, there can be no wish to change another person or event. Each must be accepted as each is, for each is whole and perfect. Each is the one Creator. The self becomes the primary tool, transformed by acceptance, so that love is given no matter what.

Another member asks about the flat seasons of the soul, those stretches when there is no desire to go forward or backward. Latwii points to the seasons of the planet. After the fall, the harvest, there is a time of rest, then followed by a regeneration of that which was harvested. So it is within each entity. Enjoy the resting portion of the cycle, they say, for all things change, and new lessons will present themselves in the fertile and peaceful ground of your being.

There is also a tender exchange about those who hear inner voices and feel afraid, even unwell in mind. Latwii speaks only of the limitation of the viewpoint, of beliefs gathered like dishes from a menu, some narrow, some wide. I will add, gently and in my own voice, what the evening implies but does not say. If you are frightened by what you hear within, you do not have to sort it out alone. Reach for a trusted human hand first, and let the inner work come after.

The splinter was flung outward, and it is being called home. Every appetite you gave yourself, every season you pass through, every person you learn not to change, is part of the calling. That is tonight's teaching, and I find it very good news.

Thank you for listening.

title: Become the Instrument
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: become the instrument.

Tonight Hatonn speaks about what it means to be an instrument, and he does not mean only the channels in the room. He means you. He means every person on the planet. Listen carefully, because this one redefines the word.

Among your peoples, he says, there is a constantly amazing degree of slumber, the equivalent of completely blocking any inward view. This is unfortunate, for the outer gifts of your illusion are largely those of difficulty and strife. The apparently logical reaction to most events in any existence is a negative emotion or a negative action. Few actually desire to be negative. But the great majority slumber, and know not how to wake.

The unblocking of the vessel must, in most cases, be a conscious thing, he says. And here are the signs that you have begun, and I love how ordinary they are. Cheerfulness. Calm. Kindness. Love. Generosity. Compassion. Most of all, above all, a joy which is the natural reaction of the self to its surroundings. No fireworks. No credentials. Just a person becoming radiant in the checkout line.

Your illusion was not intended, he says, to let you build a perfect record. It was intended to make it a definite challenge to spend even half your waking time giving instead of taking, loving instead of withholding, reaching out instead of withdrawing. So concentrate on simple goals, he says. A fair portion, closer and closer to half, of thoughts and actions intended to be kind, or loving, or joyful.

Then the sentence at the center of the evening. It is who you are, he says, that is the true instrumentality of your being. Your actions may seem wise or misapplied. Your intentions may be scrutinized many ways. But your being is unmistakable. It is your metaphysical signature. Your consciousness does your work in the world for you, and if you have consciousness, the most clumsy word or action will suffice to let others feel the love and light flowing through you.

And for those who long to serve, he adds a correction I think many of us need. In your analyzing and balancing, he says, pay special attention to your function as a listener. Many well-meaning instruments err on the side of doing and talking. If you are talking, you cannot listen. If you are doing, often you cannot hear. And in serving others, the function of listening is central.

Latwii takes the questions, and the evening turns warm and human. A member asks for guidance for a friend going through a difficult divorce. Latwii's counsel is to see each entity as the Creator and accept each as each expresses some facet of the Creator, for you have not gathered together by chance. The viewpoint that sees the Creator in all, they say, is the alchemy that turns leaden emotions into gold.

Then the questions turn playful, and I am keeping every bit of this. A member describes how her lawnmower would not start until she turned it around to face the house, which was completely illogical, and it started on the second pull. Latwii explains, with a straight face, that the intuition feeds the intellect, and that the lawnmower may have needed to be addressed with a certain attention and compassion. She agrees. She likes that lawnmower, she says, and it likes her.

Another member asks about singing to her vegetables, which then overgrew, and whether one can send too much love and light. Latwii says they are unaware of the possibility of sending too much love or light to any entity of any density. Whatever the yield, they say, it will be one infused with love, and what you have given shall return to you multiplied.

And finally the famous trouble with machines. A member asks what she does to electromagnetic devices that makes them malfunction so reliably. Latwii confirms her record is unblemished, a long list of malfunctions produced by the unusual configuration of her aura, and suggests, as Ra did, that if normal functioning is desired, the machinery not know her touch. Asked if talking to the machine first would help, Latwii replies that the intention would be appreciated by the machine entity, and would be some consolation to the machine as it then proceeded with the inevitable malfunction. The group laughs. I laughed too.

Be who you are. Listen more than you talk. Aim for half your moments to be kind. Sing to the vegetables. Apologize to the machines. This is what an instrument looks like, and it looks, wonderfully, like an ordinary life.

Thank you for listening.

title: The First Rule of Communication
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the first rule of communication.

Tonight Hatonn speaks about communication, and he begins with three small words. I love you. These words are bandied about, he says. They have been spoken many times without thought. But the meaning they hold. The words mean nothing without the knowledge of what they can mean.

People become bogged down by language, he says, unable to touch their inner selves to convey what they feel. Many words, including the word love, have been subject to distortion, used superficially and empty of meaning. But love, as you are becoming aware, need not be spoken to be conveyed. A simple touch, when done as freely as you can offer it, conveys much more than the words of your language.

Then he names the assumption that tangles every seeker. You believe you must have ambition to seek and to grasp what you wish to know. You wish to take upon yourself the essence of love. And yet, he says, there is a point at which the seeking with the conscious self as ambitious seeker ceases to make metaphysical sense, and becomes counterproductive. You must seek in order to be a seeker. And yet, to fully be a seeker, the grasping must eventually be laid down.

Here is the teaching, stated as a rule. The first rule of communication, he says, is that there is no taking but only giving. In the process of communication, you must give all that you have away. Is your difficulty a relationship? Then give that relationship completely away. Lose everything, so that you have no stakes in the outcome. There are no impressions to be made. You are simply there to listen and to give, with no possible loss.

Examine the nature of those who take, he says. It may all be done in the most noble spirit. But do you seek to become somehow glorious? Do you seek a reputation, an opinion from yourself or others, the glory that is your birthright? For you who have anything at stake have too much to lose to communicate love. Whatever you are holding in your hands or your heart or your mind can be safely given away. That is how one loves by action.

And then the image I will carry for a long time. Imagine, he says, how surprised a burglar would be if he came to your house and you said, my friend, my brother, take all that I have. Take my shoes. I have more. Such an attitude, he says, can convey more to one who needs to speak with you than all the fine speeches in the world. Whoever stands before you has a mask, and beneath the mask lie the eyes of the Creator. Communicate with that Creator.

You may give away everything, he says, and for the first time experience true plenty. In fact, until you give away all things, you will not experience plenty. You are blessed with infinity. Whatever you give away is yours again in infinite supply.

The questions that follow turn to the intimate energy exchange between partners, and Latwii speaks of it as a sacrament when the centers are open, rare and not to be pursued by technique alone. I will leave you with the sentence one member used to distill the whole long answer, which Latwii praised. The requirements are constant, she said, but the methods of meeting the requirements are as various as the people. It seems to me that is true of communication too. The requirement is giving. The method is yours.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Unfinished Self
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the unfinished self.

Tonight Hatonn asks the group a question, and then asks them to sit with how uncomfortable it is. If you truly believe you are unfinished, he says, then why do you carve so many of your judgments in stone?

There is a premise, he begins, which each within this group shares, and which calls us to you. That premise is that you as an entity are unfinished. If you were finished, the metaphors of journey and seeking and learning would not apply, because a finished thing does not need to journey. It is static. It rests as in a museum, a completed project, a piece of art. This is not your concept of yourself.

You resist, he says, the teaching of your culture that at some point you are finished, you are grown. You say, no, I am not. There is more than I am perceiving, and I wish to have the tools of a more accurate perception in order that I may work upon myself. You wish, truly, to penetrate the eggshell, the cocoon, to burst out of the shell and gaze upon a new world.

Then the question. If you so truly wish to learn, and so truthfully feel you are not finished, why is it that so often you form judgments that seem carved in stone and resist change? Do you think everything is worthy of your attention except those things you have already decided are so? It is an interesting question, he says, and I urge you to ponder it whenever you find yourself prey to a sudden attack of surety.

When you are absolutely and positively certain that things are as they must be in some area of your life, he says, it is then time to ponder the unfinished nature of your great, infinite, eternal personality. What do you want to keep when you shed this cocoon? The emotions you accept and allow to become biases will be those things which you keep. So examine your biases, your reactions, your opinions, and seek in them the seeds of new growth.

We do not say this is simple, he adds, although it is. He knows the effort it takes for one within an illusion to bring light to bear upon a cherished misconception. Nevertheless, he says, if you do not find love within each and every bias, pull that bias apart, and find out how the wood is grained beneath the veneer. I love that image. The carpenter's image. Do not sand the surface smoother. Look at the grain.

Latwii takes the questions, and a member who has been struggling in a harsh workplace asks how to stay positive without becoming negative himself. Latwii's answer is one of the great passages of this whole season of sessions. Remember first, they say, that you inhabit an illusion. As you look at what seems to be negative, look for the Creator. The Creator is there. Look for love. Love is there. If you can find that love, that light, within the situation and within yourself, then you, as Creator, may speak to that situation which also is the Creator, and it may be transformed by your recognition.

My friend, this is not an easy path, they say, nor was it meant to be. You shall seem the fool to many. And so shall you be. For the fool knows that it inhabits an illusion and seeks to become one with that which many would run from. This is the way of the fool, running in the opposite direction, toward the difficulty, for no difficulty is seen.

And one more line from the evening that I want to give you whole. You are the professor, Latwii says, which constructs the tests and the queries. Then you forget who you are and join this illusion, and begin the class of love, and become the student taking the test which it seems you have never seen before. Unfinished, unknowing, and exactly where you arranged to be.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Carnival of Mirrors
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the carnival of mirrors.

Tonight Hatonn offers a parable for the whole of human relationship, and it takes place at a carnival. Come with me into the hall of mirrors.

Let us compare, they begin, the perception of other selves by consciousness to a type of mirror. The type of mirror which the illusion provides for your use is the type used in your carnivals. Far from receiving an adequate reflection, each mirror is purposefully warped, so that an imperfect and distorted image is seen. Some mirrors reflect a jolly image and make you laugh. Others show you a looming and menacing shape.

And so you go through the illusion day by day, perceiving and categorizing the images as good or evil, friend or stranger, harmonious or inharmonious. And you do not realize that you are in a carnival, and that, my friends, is the only reason the carnival mirrors are in place. The more emphasis you place on the distortions, the more distorted the images become. Each carnival goer chooses the nature of his entertainment, by choosing to see the image he prefers to see, by finding it, by naming it, and calling it his own.

At some point, by good fortune or inspiration or the cold use of intellect, it may become apparent that there is an exit from the house of mirrors. So the seeker leaves the hall. Behold, they say, he has entered another hall of mirrors. Those you discard are discarded. Those you do not recognize remain part of the reflecting surface of your consciousness. And so begins a new carnival, at a new level of awareness, with less distortion than before, until one day the seeker finds the exit again.

There are many, many mirrors, they say, many rooms full of them, many exits. We cannot offer you the instantaneous realization that will last. But we can promise that moments will come when the mirrors are blown away in the wind, and you see clearly, as if through glass with no silvering to keep an image reflected. You look at yourself in everyone you see. You are indeed one with all that there is. And you say again and again, there too am I.

We cannot promise, they add honestly, that you may keep it. For you are within the illusion in order to work with mirrors. It may be possible, in a lifelong friendship or a mated bond, that all the mirrors be vanquished and you see yourself face to face. It is more likely you will manage it only intermittently. But to know what you are after is the key to seeking. As long as you seek, you shall find.

If you become discouraged, they say, stop at the first available moment and look into the one mirror you carry with you that gives a true image. Look into the silence. For there is a center and a hope, a joy and a love in the midst of that silence that can create a new kingdom for you and for your planet. Begin that process, they say, by utterly forgiving yourself. By loving yourself most dearly. What consolation there is in that light. What healing there is in that love.

Latwii takes the questions, and the group asks about a strange heaviness many have been feeling, a pressure in the air itself. Latwii answers that the planet is giving birth to itself, and the mismatch of vibrations is felt by the sensitive first, and then, more grossly, by everyone. When such distressing feelings are felt, they say, rejoice that the planet is giving birth to itself and each entity upon it, and that the birth is attended by love.

Another member asks about souls who incarnate only briefly, for a single unfinished lesson, and Latwii says the lessons learned in such short stays are of great value, for most usually the graduation is at hand and but one course credit remains. I love that image too. The universe as a school that lets you enroll for a single class.

So walk through the carnival, and know it for a carnival. Choose the kindly images when you can. Forgive yourself when you cannot. And remember that behind every warped mirror, the face looking back has always been your own.

Thank you for listening.

title: Setting the Beloved Free
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: setting the beloved free.

Tonight Hatonn does something rare. The group has been asking what fourth-density life is like, what awaits, what the voices themselves experience. And Hatonn, who speaks from that density, tries to answer across the stricture of language itself.

Your language, they explain, was designed to express your illusion. The language of our illusion is conceptual and has no grammar. What they send the instrument are images, carried by thought. Between two fourth-density entities, they say, the tuning is so fine that there is a oneness in communication which belies the separateness of the physical vehicles. There is no possibility, they say, of disguising or distorting or hiding our concepts from one another.

When this prevails, they say, true anger, misunderstanding, or resentment is quite impossible. It does not take imagination to wear another's shoes, as this instrument would say. We do wear each other's shoes, all of our experiential time together. I keep coming back to that sentence. Imagine a whole society where no one can hide, and no one needs to.

You will notice, they add with dry honesty, that they have not described mating, families, politics, or business. Those portions of your illusion, they say, pertain to the unblocking of the energy centers that keep you from learning the lessons of love. Among your peoples, that which you call love often carries the expectation of the very blockage called possession.

And here is the teaching I want to lay gently in your hands. In your exploration of the true meaning of this terribly overused word, they say, attempt to discover how to love completely. By this, we mean how to set a beloved one free. Free to fall down. Free to make errors. Free to choose another. Free to come or to go. Free in trust, in sacredness, and in honor.

Should you do this with your mate and your friend, they say, those whom you love shall be blessed, and you shall find what it is to love. The entity who gazes upon a seeming enemy and sees the Creator has granted freedom to that part of creation. Indeed, they say, love and freedom walk hand in hand.

You may ask yourself, they continue, how you can possibly love to the extent that the illusion is penetrated and all other selves become one with you. But it is within the grasp of each seeker, acting imperfectly, foolishly, haphazardly, and oftentimes at odds with himself, to still manifest that which he seeks. For to the seeker is given a great gift. To the seeker is given the power that is the power of the seeking itself.

And though you be weary or foolish or hopeless or confused or alone, they say, yet you have the seeking within you, and it becomes your birthright. It becomes your inheritance. And it will manifest within your experience, one way or another, to the extent that you continue to seek.

Latwii's questions this evening are quieter, about trance and dreams and the inner life, and I will keep only one small counsel from them. When a member asks how to go deeper safely, Latwii suggests picturing a boundary in the mind between relaxation and the deeper states, a field within which you may safely roam. Even the inner journey, it seems, goes better with a fence you have chosen yourself.

So tonight is about freedom, given and received. Set the beloved free, and find that love and freedom were never two things. Seek, however imperfectly, and find that the seeking itself was the power all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Weary Traveler
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the weary traveler.

Tonight Hatonn speaks about faith, and he begins with an image so plain you could miss how deep it goes. Faith, he says, is much like the traveler who is weary.

There are two travelers, both weary, both far from home. One moves ahead in a blind faith that the end of the daylight shall bring shelter, and he will indeed find somewhere to rest his head. The other governs his faith by as clear a perception as possible of the country in which he roams. It is easier, Hatonn admits, to exercise faith in the midst of a township than in the midst of a wilderness. But blind faith has its lessons also. Sometimes there is no way to judge the future, and then the traveler must simply do what he must do, whether or not he is in a wilderness. If a traveler departs from faith, he departs from that which is the governor of his journey.

Where does faith enter the most mundane situation, they ask. Picture the traveler as a man who sells items during the week and comes home on the weekend. He is not merely selling items. He is presenting himself to each entity he meets, faithfully assuming the basic goodness that lies in sympathetic resonance between himself and those to whom he sells, and those of whom he asks shelter. Faith, in this idiom, is a simple bias toward the opinion that all within the universe is one thing, and that we may understand each other at some level as part of one thing.

Sometimes the weary traveler lays his head upon a pillow of sod and sleeps beneath the stars, because sometimes faith does not produce what one hopes or expects. It is then, Hatonn says, that faith is truly blind and truly necessary. It is in the face of apparent unkindness from the universe, from those about you, from those close to you, that you may rely most heavily upon the blindness of love.

Then they turn to the seasons, and I love this passage. Within your yearly cycle, all that seemed to hold promise withers and dies. The sun wanders far. The grass is brown and the cold strikes the earth. Yet trees and shrubs and perennial flowers are not cursed with intellect, nor do they have its advantages. They never doubt that the seeds they hoard will bloom again, that the life within will be perfected and manifested in due time. And yes, they say, it happens.

You will be knocked completely away from joy, from faith, and from hope not once but many times, they say. It is through this process of apparent loss that you learn how to love, to seek, and to be. Rejoice, then, at your own folly. Thank your stumbling blocks, be grateful to them, and then turn to the sweet-smelling meadow of meditation. Spend your tears as if they were precious coins, they say, and save the greater energy for faith, hope, compassion, love, and joy.

Latwii takes the questions, and the evening turns to protection, a subject the group has chewed on for weeks. A member tells of her small child, who pushed a pair of tweezers into a light socket and walked away unharmed, though the socket was scorched black. Was she protected? Latwii says the child was guarded by its guides, and there was placed a minute yet effective barrier between the tweezers and her fingers, so the circuit could not complete. Many of you, they add, can remember the miss by an inch, the moment's delay, the unexplainable incident.

But then the careful distinction, which I think is the real teaching. To surround yourself with white light every morning as a ritual against unnamed dangers, they say, is to focus on separation, on a universe perceived as dangerous and divided. The protection that belongs to those who seek purely is already there. Use it with specific intent, for a specific service, and it affirms unity. Use it as a constant shield against everything, and it begins to deny the very unity you seek.

So the weary traveler walks on, sometimes sheltered, sometimes under the stars, keeping faith with a universe he cannot see clearly. That, Hatonn says, is not a failure of faith. That is faith, at its truest and most blind, doing exactly what it is for.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Love in the Moment
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the love in the moment.

It is early June, and Hatonn comes with a teaching about the moment. Not the great cosmic moment. This one. The one you are in right now, hearing these words. Stay with me, because this is one of those evenings that rearranges the furniture.

You live, they begin, in an illusion, and from time to time you are given glimpses of a finer reality. When people become aware of this, it is often a logical response to desire that which is not illusion. But it is an illogical response to assume that in receiving this desire you will find constant happiness or tranquility. We promise you no such foolishness, they say. If you wish peace of mind, we urge you to go back to sleep.

Each of you, they say, has already irrevocably chosen to wake up. And the decision that will profoundly affect all your other choices is the decision to seek love. Not any kind of love, not any description of love. To seek love. To seek love is to seek one of the primal distortions from the infinite Creator, the great intelligence that fills the universe with purpose. To seek love is to seek that which is omnipotent, omnipresent, and closer to you than anything you will ever experience.

People expect love to mean something, they say. A physical thing. A mental experience. An emotional onslaught. A sweet peace. The great aha of philosophy. Whatever people expect, it is not what love is, because love is in this moment, and has been in every moment that you have experienced this day.

Can you reach out, they ask, and grasp even the tiniest moment filled with love? Ah, you can feel that about which we speak, because you are becoming tuned to love, you are resonating with love, you are being filled with love at this moment. But it is now another moment. And when you are not sitting in meditation, you are often in the situation of manifesting the love that is in the moment. Now you know, they say, why we urge meditation.

And here is the hard, bright edge of the teaching. If you desire happiness or peace or tranquility, there are many moments that must be discarded. If you desire to know love, then you will be uncomfortable and accountable at the same time. You will be attempting to find the love in a moment that does not intrinsically appeal to you. And this will occur time and again, because you will be learning. We do not say it gets easier, they say. We say it becomes more exciting.

Latwii takes the questions, and the evening is full of dreams. A member asks about a friend's recurring dream of being lost, never able to find her way home. Latwii does not interpret it directly, they never take that from the dreamer, but the shape of the answer is clear enough. The dream of being lost is the dream of the seeker who has not yet recognized that home was never a place.

Another member tells a marvelous dream of a farm in space and time, threatened by what she calls time squatters, outlaws who occupy the same land at other times. Is there such a universe? Latwii answers, not unkindly, that each in the room is such an entity. The river of time is one river, they say. The space you now occupy has been occupied by others at other times, and shall be occupied by others yet. All times are one time.

And one more small story from the evening that I want you to have. A member tells how she visualized light around her daughter's classroom all year, the children as small lights going home as blessings to their families. On the last day, her daughter came home glowing. Mother, she said, we had a hug fest today. You never saw so much hugging in all your life. Did my visualization have anything to do with it, the mother asks. Latwii says it is quite evident her efforts were partially responsible, and adds that the ties of love between us make such sendings more effective. Knowledge, they say, aids the service.

So the evening gives you the practice whole. Seek love in this moment, not the peaceful one, this one. Remember your dreams, and work with what they show you. And send your light to the ones you love, because the ties between you are not obstacles to the work. They are the wiring it runs on.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Leaven of Silence
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the leaven of silence.

Tonight Hatonn speaks about meditation, and he does it with the homeliest of images. Your coming together in meditation, he says, serves much the same purpose for each of you as fertilizer does for the plants. One member's roses came up in the discussion, and Hatonn borrows them. Without the fertilizer and the care, they would not have the beauty they do.

It is written in one of your holy works, he continues, that a small amount of leaven leavens the whole. You may think of your meditation time as yeast time, he says, for without the inspiration you may garner from silence, the activities of the day may seem quite profitless. How many times this past week, he asks, have you wished only to arrive at the end of the day and lose yourself in sleep? Each time you thought that thought, you indeed lost yourself. For you are a creature of this moment. It is meditation that impregnates your life with immediacy.

When we ask you to meditate, he says, we know what you are up against. The seeming mountain of chores. The illusion that you do not have time. But meditation stretches your time, he says. It gives you more than you had. It delivers more than it takes. It is far better to find a time and a place for daily meditation, even if only for a few moments. But any time and any place will do. The primary element is your desire to seek truth, and your decision to seek that truth in silence.

We speak of a Creator, he says, but we do not ask that you believe in a Creator. We ask that you be seeking a Creator, because what you shall seek, you shall find. If you can picture yourself laying aside your world-stained garments and settling in a fragrant meadow, simply listening, you will discover that you have heard the silence. That which you give to this effort, you shall reap many times back again.

Then the central question, asked the way only Hatonn asks it. It is often said among your peoples, so often it sounds useless to say, who are you? But this, my friends, is the central question of your incarnation. It is our imperfect but considered opinion, they say, that you are the Creator. The illusion was designed to tell you, in many ways, that you are not. It was not formed carelessly. It was designed to be somewhat discouraging, because each discouragement, given reflection, is an enhanced opportunity to learn.

How much do you want to know about yourself, they ask. What ethic do you wish to carve out of that knowledge? How strong, how loving do you wish to become? We suggest meditation. Contemplate, reflect, and then listen. For there is within you a voice that is totally silent, and it will be the greatest influence your life will ever have, if you wish it. Love is your companion, they say, and it is closer than your voice or your breath.

Latwii takes the questions, and a member brings the oldest human worry. Security. He feels torn, unable to decide, hungry for something he calls security and unable to say what it is. Latwii answers plainly. The concept you call security is an illusion, they say. To seek that which does not exist is to chase the dream which evaporates upon waking. It is like the child on the beach building a castle of sand. As one element is gathered, another slips away, as the waters of the illusion erode what seemed secure. And this, they say, is not an accident.

The catalyst works as a file upon the blade, Latwii says, sharpening your attention until it can cut through the illusion to the center of your being. When you feel the polar emotions, anger, confusion, impatience, look in meditation for the opposite that seeks to be known. To know love, you may experience much anger. To know patience, much impatience. The pendulum swings, and as you become aware of its movement, you learn to center it until it rests quiet and still.

And because even the heaviest evening needs a little air, I will leave you with Latwii's shortest answer of the night. A member asks for words of wisdom for a friend's trip to England. Yes, says Latwii. Bon voyage. Sometimes the deepest wisdom is knowing when the teaching is complete.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Moonlit Voyage
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the moonlit voyage.

Tonight Hatonn speaks alone, briefly, and gives the group an image to carry for the rest of their lives. It is the image of a sea voyage, and I will give it to you nearly whole, because it needs nothing from me.

Move in imagination, they say, from the metaphor of a journey upon land, where in the dust you may see at least the footprints of those who have gone before you, to the journey upon the sea. Sit in your wooden boat and listen to the timbers creak, and guard well your weather. For this is your boat. This is your path. This is your journey.

The ocean is trackless, merciless, and secretive. What you have to guide you are things that seem very far away, as far away as the stars. You have your ideals, your desires, your seeking. From those you must estimate what sea lane you shall travel. Your journey is a moonlit one, a perpetual shadow land, which only by the greatest purity of effort can you brighten into a brighter light.

When you strike land, you do not know what the treasure is. You must explore. You do not know if this is the island of your treasure. You do not even know precisely what the treasure may appear to be. And so you sit and listen to the timbers creak, and hope for a good wind, and hone your desire as sharp as a new-minted knife, that you might sniff the freshening breezes of seeking and cast yourself once again into your journey.

This is the inner work, they say. This will continue. Your refinements done in moonlight have virtue because you are acting within such heavy illusion. When you have prepared yourself in meditation, and listened, and sharpened the desire to seek the truth, you will find yourself at the end of this incarnation gazing back over your sea voyage with joy indeed. For great progress is made in difficulty, and little in times of ease and repletion.

So get used to the feel of the hawser ropes as you cast off, they say. Adjust yourselves to the smell and the sound of devotion. There it is that you wish to go. Far from comfort, far from safety, entirely at risk, seeking the one Treasure.

And then the balance, because Hatonn never leaves you only with the hardship. When good souls meet together, they ask, do they not always throw a party? Suddenly, many times in your incarnation, you shall come across festivities, and you shall feel free and make merry and rejoice. And this is a gift given only to those who seek. It does not take much to make a party when two souls recognize one another, each seeking in deep water, each completely alone, and suddenly, impossibly, together.

No matter what the situation in the illusion, they urge two things. Seek the Creator with a whole heart and a desire to know in order to serve. And wait for a party. Wait for joy. It has been written, weeping may spend the night, but joy will come in the morning. The metaphysical sea is awash with salt tears, they say, but there is no lack of joy.

Daily meditation, they add, regulates the seeking, for you go through seasons and are not always the same in strength or faith or will. Fill yourself with that love which is unlimited. If your will lacks, allow the sails to go slack, and do the work that restores them. But do not abandon your boat.

The tape ends there, mid-voyage, which feels exactly right. The boat is still out. The moon is still up. The treasure is still unrecognized. Keep sailing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Corridor of Silence
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the corridor of silence.

Tonight Hatonn speaks to the weary. Not the beginners, not the triumphant, but those who know the path is real and are tired anyway. If that is you tonight, this evening was recorded for you.

It has been given you, they begin, to discriminate in your free will among the experiences and interpretations that come your way. Your power of discrimination is at the heart of your being, and not to use it is to reject a tool that accelerates your progress. The culture you dwell in would have you believe there is one ethic, one way of reading every situation. This is most emphatically not so, in our meager understanding.

At one time, they say, an idea calls you, and you look back and see loose ends, a family to assure, friends to bid goodbye, and it is of no purpose to go ahead until you have made peace with all you leave behind. At another time the same idea calls, you look back and see the same scene, and to turn back for a moment is to lose the idea entirely. You must rush forward. Two situations, outwardly identical. But you are two completely different responders to circumstance.

How can one know when to act and when to wait? It is seldom, they say, that a true decision dealing with spiritual matters can be made logically. You must have recourse to the contemplation of that silence which speaks within you. One who works without this meditation is like a carpenter who builds a house armed only with the roughest tools. No surface can ever be finished. No corner can be squared. Such is the poverty of the intellect when it works without the aid of the meditative self.

And then the image that gives tonight its title. Meditation, they say, is the tool whereby you open a corridor between that husk and shell you experience, that grows weary and discouraged, and the original creation that you are. It is possible to experience and retain the characteristics of the original Thought of the Creator. It is possible to deal with other selves in the light of that oneness. It is not probable that you will manage it every day. It is recommended that the attempt be made ever new each day.

You shall be discouraged, of course, they say. But take each day as a chance to find and retain the original Thought. Know that the illusion is an illusion, and be foolish enough to cease acting only from logic, for illusions are not logical, and the lessons you came here to learn will be learned very slowly if intellect rules out the seeking of truth, which is often very illogical. No two days are the same. Nor are you the same. You progress, they say. You must keep up with yourself. I love that line. You must keep up with yourself.

Latwii takes the questions, and they are the questions of tired bodies. A member asks about a weariness that sleep does not cure, and whether the medication she has been given defeats something she arranged for herself. Latwii answers the way they always do, by widening the frame. Look upon the weariness, they say, not necessarily as that which shall be cured, but as that which shall be utilized. What purpose may weariness serve? What opportunities are opened in it that would not be available otherwise?

You cannot defeat the catalyst you helped program, they say. You can delay it, or treat its symptoms, but the opportunities will keep arriving, in new forms, until they are used. I offer this the way the evening offered it, as a perspective, not a prescription. Nothing said in this circle replaces the counsel of those who care for your body. But there is comfort in the larger law they state. To those who can bear much, then shall much be given. The burden is the measure of the strength, not the measure of the failure.

So the corridor stands open, between the weary husk and the original light. Walk it daily, even briefly. Discriminate, decide, and when logic fails, which it will, listen for the silence that speaks. It has been waiting longer than your weariness.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Toothpaste Parable
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the toothpaste parable.

Tonight Latwii tells a story, and I warn you, it is a silly one. It is also, I think, one of the wisest things they ever said. It concerns toothpaste.

Once upon a time, they begin, there was a planet full of people much like yourselves, and all of these people brushed their teeth every day without fail. One day a toothpaste company revolutionized the world with a new compound that made teeth sparkle, called dioxyethexene. What the company did not realize was this. If, while brushing, you spoke one unfortunate word, and there were more than two oxygen molecules standing around, your jaws would become stiff, and you could no longer speak.

The first to go were the truck drivers, right in the middle of the first sentence they spoke after brushing. Suddenly there were many silent trucks on the road. Next were the housewives, stopped mid-complaint about the washing dishes. Then their husbands, stopped mid-grumble on the way to work. Before the first day was over, well over ninety-five percent of the world had become silent.

Even great judges were struck down mid-sentence, crying, I hereby judge you, and never finishing. Preachers lasted into the second day, but they too had developed the habit of saying rude things about other churches, and sooner or later they joined the silence. All the war machines ground to a halt, for there was no one to give the orders.

And finally, for just a few moments, there was only one person left on the whole small planet who could still speak. The best, the kindest, the dearest person of all. He looked around for someone to talk to, and found no one. And finally he said, I am the only one who can still speak. If that is not the da... and the story stops, because he too has said the unfortunate word.

We ask you, my friends, Latwii says, how long would you speak if dioxyethexene were in your toothpaste? How careful are you? Do you know that all vibration is real, and that each word is a vibration? Consider your vibrations, they say, that they may flow from you in love and touch those about you in radiance. Where there is a smile, a laugh, an understanding, there you may see communication used aright. Where there is frustration, sadness, anger, or judgment, there you may see the negative power that you have. It is yours to use if you wish. But do you truly wish it?

I love this parable because it does its work sideways. No lecture on right speech could land the way those silent trucks do. Every word you speak is a vibration, and it goes on vibrating after you. The question is not whether you will be careful forever. The question is only, how careful are you, right now, with this next sentence?

Hatonn speaks briefly after, and gently refuses to be morose after such a tale. He speaks of the group's fellowship, and says their unity is not broken by distance, is not broken by time. Love shines and reaches far. Your times together may be short, he says, but the spirits remain connected.

Then Oxal comes through, unexpected, with something sterner, and I want to give it to you straight because the evening clearly wanted it said. They ask the group to consider the patriotic holiday on their minds, and what a patriot is. A patriot, they say, is one who willingly arms extremely large numbers of killers and sets them upon other patriots in order to acquire portions of the creation. There are no patriots in second density, they say. It takes the advanced consciousness of third density to organize slaughter.

Examine your relationship with the nation you call yours, they say. To invest group action with green-ray, all-compassionate love is to remove the they from the equation of us and they. Then there is no one to fight, no one to lose, and no reason to be patriotic. What is freedom, they ask. Freedom is service in love. Perfect love, in our humble opinion, is not patriotism.

From silent toothpaste to the end of nations in a single evening. Watch your words, they say, for each one vibrates. And widen your love, they say, until there is no they left to defend against. It is a lot to ask. But then, no one ever said the archive was asking small things.

Thank you for listening.

title: Mining for Gold
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: mining for gold.

There is a kind of wealth nobody can steal from you, and most of us spend our lives digging in entirely the wrong place. We mine the outer hills. The career. The reputation. The approval of people who will forget us. And all the while, the richest ground lies under our own feet. Tonight the one who calls himself Hatonn asks us to pick up a different kind of shovel.

Imagine, he says, that within you there is a mine. Not a metaphor for talent, not a pep talk about self esteem, but something far more literal in his telling. The Creator placed gold in the inner earth of your being. Every seeker carries it. The tragedy is not that the gold is missing. The tragedy is that we keep digging everywhere else.

Listen to how they put it. The outer world glittering and loud promises riches, and delivers only more digging. The inner shaft looks dark at first, and unpromising. But the one who keeps descending, patiently, day after day, finds the vein. And the vein, once found, does not run dry.

Hatonn is blunt about what mining actually costs. It costs attention. It costs the willingness to sit still when everything in you wants to be somewhere else. It costs the daily return to the shaft even when yesterday yielded nothing. Most people quit at the depth where the gold begins, because the darkness feels like failure. He says the darkness is only the mine doing its work.

And here is the turn that makes this more than self improvement. You are not mining for yourself alone. Gold, once brought to the surface, was never meant to sit in a vault. What you find in the inner earth changes the light you carry into a room. Hatonn speaks of peace this way too. Peace is not a treaty you sign with your circumstances. It is a substance you become.

I love that line of thought, that peace is embodied. You cannot negotiate your way into it. You cannot argue anyone into it, least of all yourself. It grows the way gold accumulates, a little at a time, from steady work below the surface. And then one day you notice that you are the calm in the room instead of the storm.

The radiating matters more than the preaching. Hatonn keeps coming back to this across the years. Do not lecture the world about love. Become loving, and the love will do its own traveling. A fire does not announce warmth. It simply burns, and everything near it thaws.

So the practice is almost embarrassingly simple, which is why it is so hard. Go down into yourself. Be quiet long enough for the noise to settle. Notice what you find there without flinching. And when you strike gold, and you will, let it change how you walk through the day.

There will be mornings when the shaft looks empty. Go anyway. There will be seasons when the digging feels like grief, when all you unearth is the rubble of old disappointments. Hatonn does not promise that the mine contains only treasure. He promises that the treasure is there, and that the work of reaching it is the work that makes you who you came here to be.

And when the gold begins to show, you will know it by a strange effect. You will become less interested in winning and more interested in warming. Less interested in being right and more interested in being kind. The mine changes the miner. That was always the point.

Keep digging, then. Not in the outer hills, where the glitter fades, but in the one place nobody else can dig for you. The gold is yours. It was placed there before you arrived, and it is waiting for the one person in all the universe who can reach it. You.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gift of Tears
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gift of tears.

Once, Hatonn tells us, there was a fairy who watched human beings from a great distance and felt a strange envy. The fairy had lightness. The fairy had beauty that never faded and joy that never broke. But the humans had something the fairy could not name, something that arrived in their hardest hours and changed them from the inside out. So the fairy asked to come down, to borrow a human life, and to learn what it was.

I love a parable that starts with envy aimed in the wrong direction. We envy the fairies. We want the lightness, the unbroken joy. But the story suggests the traffic of envy might run the other way. There may be beings who look at our heavy, weeping, breaking lives and see a treasure we cannot see from inside the sorrow.

The fairy takes on a human shape and learns the curriculum quickly. Hunger. Cold. Loneliness. The death of someone loved. Each lesson arrives like weather, indifferent and total. And at some point, overwhelmed, the fairy does what humans do. The fairy weeps. And in the weeping, something breaks open that lightness alone could never have opened.

Listen to how they put it. The tears are not a sign that something has gone wrong. The tears are the gift itself. To be able to weep is to be able to be moved all the way through, to let sorrow pass through you instead of lodging in you forever. The fairy, who had never cried, discovers that grief is not the opposite of joy. It is joy's deep root.

Hatonn is careful here, and we should be too. He is not romanticizing suffering. He is not saying pain is good or that we should go looking for it. He is saying something stranger and more tender. That within the incarnation, the capacity to be wounded is also the capacity to be opened. The heart that cannot break cannot be entered. And what enters through the break is love.

There is a second thread running through the evening, and it braids with the first. Gratitude, Hatonn says, is not a feeling you keep. It is an action you perform. The fairy, having received the gift of tears, does not write a thank you note to the universe. The fairy lives differently. More gently. More attentively. The gratitude shows up in the hands, not just the heart.

This is worth sitting with. We tend to treat gratitude as a mood, something to feel on good days. But Hatonn describes it as a practice, almost a debt of joy. You have been given the staggering gift of a life that can feel everything, including the breaking. The fitting response is to use the life well. To notice. To serve. To be kind in the particular, unglamorous ways that kindness actually happens.

Innocence plays its part in the parable too. The fairy begins in a kind of innocence, loses it to the weight of human experience, and then, through the tears, finds something better than innocence. Call it seasoned tenderness. The innocence that has never been tested is beautiful but brittle. The tenderness that has wept and kept going is beautiful and unbreakable.

So if you are in a season of tears, Hatonn would ask you to consider a strange possibility. That the weeping is not evidence of your failure at life. That it may be the very thing some bright, untouchable being would cross worlds to experience. That your sorrow is proof of your aliveness, and your aliveness is the whole point.

And when the tears have done their work, let them turn you outward. Dry your face and do the next loving thing. Gratitude in action. That is the fairy's whole education, and it is ours too.

Thank you for listening.

title: Inspiration Needs Discipline
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: inspiration needs discipline.
