And persevere with a light heart. Knowing that all is truly well. That all things move in love. That you are an infinitely valuable portion of that love, and that you cannot err in your seeking of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Wisdom of Waiting
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the wisdom of waiting.

The ones who call themselves L/Leema speak tonight of the positive, the negative, and the neutral. And they begin, of all places, with the atom.

Positive, in metaphysical terms, is that which radiates, gives, emits, shares. Negative is that which attracts, takes, enslaves. But then they ask you to look at the neutron, which makes up the vast majority of the actual matter of an atom. And they say something I want you to sit with. The neutron is that which is lost in love. It is the thought which is uncreated, neither positive nor negative, remaining at rest within the unmanifested mystery of the one infinite Creator.

Now carry the analogy inward, because that is where they are taking you. Far more of your own life, and far more of your seeking, is likewise lost in the Creator, safe within the kingdom, than you can realize while bound in the illusion. The vast majority of the essential you has never left the creation of the Father. It dwells unmanifest and unpotentiated, full of energy, full of life, but without any need for outer expression.

From its infinite regions, they say, you yourself will require only some small portion for each lesson you accept. And here is the teaching that gives this evening its title. Sometimes it is time to wait. For that which is unmanifest cannot be pushed or pulled or bullied. The rhythm of the Father is such that only in the Creator's time, which is your inner time, shall your lesson emerge from timelessness and act out its drama upon your world's stage. And then you shall learn, and know, and go on. And again you will wait.

So their counsel is simple, and I think strangely tender. Wait happily. Know that what you must do is single. Ask. For is it not written, ask and it shall be answered. And therefore, they caution, be careful what you ask, for in good time that which is asked will be received.

They know what the seeker objects to. Where are the visible fruits? Look at Gautama Siddhartha, they say. A king among men, who gave his fruits most productively when, after many adventures, he ferried people from one side of a river to another. Look at Jesus of Nazareth, a carpenter's son, walking in the dust and heat, dying beside two petty criminals. Put yourself in either of their places and try to say when your life became spiritually productive. The secret these two shared, L/Leema says, was the secret of waiting. Of metaphysical neutrality. Meeting each circumstance with spiritual freshness, with a vivacious love that dissolved positive and negative, so that all was light and love.

The eyes to see, the ears to hear, the hearts to understand, they say, lie in that part of yourself that has never left the Logos, waiting to be potentiated by your free will as co-creator. For you are in God, and the Creator is in you.

We shall wait with you, my friends, they say, in joy and without anticipation. So that we may, as you, be surprised by the even greater joy of action within the love and the light of the One Who Is All.

Thank you for listening.

title: Nearer Than Breathing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: nearer than breathing.

Hatonn speaks this evening of something almost too simple to grasp. The kingdom within you.

He begins with the body, and how little astonishes us that should. Could you, without seeing a form, develop the intricate system of your own body? The universe of man, he says, is a universe in which the true mysteries are often those things most taken for granted and unexplored, while the mind turns to distractions, recreations, and the creation of artifacts of man's own making.

And yet the numbness of daily life can be removed. Meditation, he says, is the most efficient path toward the removing of that numbness which keeps one from perpetual astonishment and transformational joy from moment to moment. There is a kingdom within you which religious leaders have located far away from you. Within you is the kingdom of the Father, and yet within you is the Father. Father and kingdom being one.

This concept is too simple to easily grasp, he says. It is just as difficult to grasp the concept of dwelling within the present moment. Everything in your illusion has a process. The aging of bodies, of gems, of planets in their courses. And in none of these processes does there indwell, to the casual observer, the present moment, because there is always the feeling of time passing. But the metaphysical present moment is not at all the same as the physical present on your clocks.

I want to read you the passage where he tries to describe entering it, because it is one of the strangest and most beautiful things in the archive. How beautiful and how fair, how full of glory is the face of creation. How limitless is the light. Motion and motionless, these things are one. All things are one. Oh, greet each other, my friends, and know each other as one. Know each other as the Creator.

And then the return. Let bliss drift like the waves of the sea, moving back and forth, and find yourselves seated within the illusion, within physical bodies, within all those things which may seem to separate you. This, he says, is travel without time. This is a kind of talking that attempts to describe that which is meditation, and which is found in meditation.

The closing thought is the one I want you to keep. Your worth is as infinite as the Creator. And that which you do shall always be an imperfect trace of the energy pathway of limitlessness. The creation of love, he says, is nearer to you than your breathing. Closer to you than your thinking. More dear to you than your body.

Thank you for listening.

title: Dare to Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: dare to love.

Hatonn speaks tonight to those who feel like strangers here. And he begins with a simple observation about difference. There are many ways separation can be apparently seen. Differences of race. Of male and female. Of young and old. Of personality. But one difference has been the subject of much pondering. The different dimensions from which wanderers come.

Those of fourth, fifth, and sixth densities all have some representation among your peoples at this time, he says. Because there is a great call, a call which cannot be ignored, coming from this planet in travail which you call Earth. And wanderers, being far different in their internal modes of thinking from those native to third density, feel a kind of loneliness. The loneliness of the stranger in a strange land.

I love how specific he gets about this. Fourth density is the density of love and compassion, and its native way of living is the banding together in groups. Many fourth-density wanderers moved through the Earth during what this instrument calls the baby boom years. Those young people known as hippies, dwelling not in couples but in communities, were yearning through memory to reproduce the love and compassion of a larger reality. Sixth-density wanderers are fewer, dwelling in large families related not by blood but by commonality of thought. And fifth density, the density of wisdom, seeks solitude. For the essence of wisdom, Hatonn says, is the knowledge that that which is to be sought is a grasp of the unity of all things. And that part of the journey must needs be a solitary one.

And here is why your communities keep failing to agree, he says. It is the mixture of fifth-density entities with those of fourth and those few of sixth. Each half-remembers a different depth of friendship and companionship. Those of fifth density must needs seek solitude within community. Those of fourth, loving and generous, have hospitality to offer like children at play. Those of sixth carry the half-remembered memory of the larger family. The chief reason for the failure of larger communities, he says, is the inability to bring these disparate memories into alignment, and the inability to stop confusing the love of the Creator with what your peoples call romantic love.

But then he says the thing that reframes everything. My friends, there are no failures. It is the attempt about which you shall be concerned. The attempt to share love is far greater than any manifestation which may seem to fall short of the ideal. And the journey home is not a journey backwards, for you cannot go backwards. Each time you visit that home, you have been transformed. You have been dead, but again you live, and your spirit begins to soar once again.

So he closes with an appeal, and it is the title of this evening. Have you white skin and another black? Are you male and another female? Are you old and another young? Are you solitary and another sociable? My friends, this is all illusion. Cease pondering your differences. You are all one, my friends. Please dare to love each other. We assure you that though you shall fall, you shall always be helped up again, if only you keep your heart and your mind in the belief, in the faith, and in the hope of unity with the one great original thought of love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Discipline of Joy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the discipline of joy.

This is a short evening with a long teaching. The ones who call themselves Oxal speak of joy. Not the passing kind. The kind that is a discipline.

They begin with a warning that might surprise you. If you wish a specific remedy against joy, they say, it would be history that would take first place among the active distractions of those who seek. History. The past that did not work out. The future that is being planned. Success and failure, they say, belong to that outward portion of yourselves which belongs to history.

The discipline of joy, then, is the discipline of remaining outside of time. Or more precisely, within that womb from which time issues, and toward which it shall once again be drawn in the great rhythm of the cosmos. I love that image. The womb of time. A place you can reserve within yourself, centered there, while the processes of daily living go on around you. The telephone rings. The doorbell rings. The visitor knocks. The information comes through the post. And still, a portion of you remains seated within love and its expression. Joy and laughter. Regardless of outward circumstances.

Oxal is honest about how hard this is. The more one throws the whole self into the petty, the more one worries over seeming failures, the more one robs oneself of the opportunities for transformation. And yet transformation is what you have come to choose. It seems that that which is new becomes old. But consider, they say, whether it is not one's interest that becomes old. When one perceives things from the standpoint of joy, nothing can escape the illumination which love brings.

Later in the evening, the ones who call themselves Q'uo speak briefly on meditation, and their few sentences belong here. They speak of the great sacrifice the Creator made in causing a portion of its being to have mind and become independent. And you yourself, they say, are a sacrifice to your own mind. Without mind you would constantly be in a state of meditation, and all things would be whole and entire unto themselves. Yet you have sacrificed that awareness to come into incarnation, to be limited by your separation from those things about you.

And separation runs deep, they say. How easy it is to feel separate from life that indwells all things. To forget that the stones sing, that the earth shouts with rejoicing, and that the trees skip in the springtime. The only road from separation into unity, they say, is keyed with meditation. There is no set time. There is no set method. There is one thing they must emphasize, and that is the fidelity to the practice.

So the evening leaves you with two disciplines that are really one. Reserve a portion of yourself in the womb of time, where joy holds sway. And return to the silence, faithfully, that you may remember what you are.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Bitter Cup
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the bitter cup.

This session was recorded in the season when many celebrate the memory of Jesus, and the ones who call themselves Laitos open with it. But they do not speak of history. They speak of you.

Consider the significance of the resurrection, they say. The one you call Jesus led a life of quiet contemplation, of study, of experience, and reached the point where he found the core of his existence lay not within the physical shell, but within his own source. And in reuniting himself with his Creator, he was sustained through his period of hardship to the extent that he was capable, quite literally, of rising above that which is called death.

In his words, I am the way, he left a clue for those who would hear to follow. That those who desire may follow a similar journey. May turn within, in the face of any difficulty, and find that which truly sustains. To rise again, Laitos says, is simply to return to the illusion with this awareness. And to take up the cross again, that others may be reached, that others may see, and in seeing, find the opportunity to wonder and to seek.

And then Hatonn takes up the same thread from the other side. The side of the suffering itself. And this is the passage that names our evening.

The Creator, Hatonn says, seems to offer a great deal that is bitter. It is as if the Creator were handing you a cup full of bitter wine. And yet, because the hand holding the cup is the Creator's, in faith we drink it, and it is bitter. The faith in which you take the most bitter drink within this illusion is, in essence, the faith that the Creator, being in right relationship with you, shall give you that which shall seem bitter, but which is in the end sweet and rich.

I want you to hear the honesty in what follows. You shall spend a very large portion of this creation's time dwelling upon the fruits of the bitter cup you take in faith now. For this is the heaviest illusion for those beings which have become conscious of the self. This is the illusion in which we choose whom to serve. So Hatonn asks you not to flinch. Gaze without regret at all which seems bitter and difficult, he says, for this has been given you with the greatest love and wisdom.

To transcend that which grinds the soul into numbness, he says, is to shake off all suppositions of the unfairness of the creation. You may picture the greatest and most terrible torture. The limits of your imagination are all that limit the possibilities of difficulty. And yet it is the Creator's hand which has dealt you these bitter things, and has asked you to taste them, and accept them, and see through them toward the transformation and purification of the self. Until finally the paradox of separation between Creator and created is at an end, and the hand that serves the cup is your own.

So rejoice, Laitos says, not only in the resurrection of one who has gone before, but in your own. For you have truly learned to go within, and to bring back that which you found. Give freely, and give without fear. For there is no way in which one who does so can fail to find the way safely home.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Art of Hope
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the art of hope.

The evening opens with a brief visitation from one who calls itself Amira, and it is worth hearing in full. How I yearn to touch your hearts, Amira says. Why are your heads turned to the burnt offerings which you insist upon offering to the Most High? Have I not said that the sacrifice of blood is to be offered no longer? And yet within your nations, instead of spreading the unity of the children of God and taking comfort in each other, you offer your firstborn again and again. I came to you as a servant, and you have called me a king. When shall your burnt offerings cease, and when shall you turn toward each other, nation to nation, people to people, in love?

Then Hatonn takes the floor, and the subject is hope. And he begins by separating it from faith, because the two are easy to confuse. Faith is blind, he says. Faith does not have eyes that see, nor does it need them. Faith is an inner sureness, and an invaluable ally. But there are situations in which a focused vision has its place, and is far more effective than blind faith. That faculty is hope. Hope is the development of faith upon a specific area of intent, so that a vision is developed which affirms all that is best in a situation, all that is requisite in an outcome.

And then the image that carries the whole teaching. Hope is that which, while the eagle soars, gazes toward its prey. Faith is that which causes the eagle to leap into the air. The eagle has wings, yet it does not cogitate upon its flying. It hopes for its prey, and in its inner eye sees it long before the outer vision finds that which it seeks.

I love how practical he makes this. Refine your inner vision, he says, for hope is a means whereby you may use your deeper intuitions to envision that which is sought. This does not mean attempting to predetermine an outcome. It means perceiving a situation in such a way that the good can be seen, and the rest can be seen to fall away. Just as in the eagle's eye, all that is not the prey is seen, but is not registered as important. Hope has a way of clearing the mind, of strengthening inner vision, of pulling the cobwebs out of situations, of focusing that incredible strength within each of you which is will.

Do you think you know what you desire? Is that desire intangible? Then sharpen that faculty of hope until within you, you can almost taste and feel and see that which is hoped for. Then allow faith to set you winging upon the air, and open your inner eyes wide as you fly. Your faith shall carry you, he says. But where shall it carry you?

And here is the line I want you to keep for the dark days. Sad indeed is the soul which is hopeless, for faith alone cannot turn the mind to the goal of love. Faith has no direction. It is a faculty which strengthens the spirit so that it may go forth and seek. Hope is the result of having found a direction in which to point the faithful self.

Hatonn does not ask you to hope for a trouble-free existence. In your density, confusion and difficulty are to be expected, by the very nature of the lessons you set yourself. To put an end to these confusions would be to limit your ability to learn. And yet, he says, we hope with you that you may penetrate the outer shell of experience, and aim unerringly for the transformations which lie just the other side of understanding.

Thank you for listening.

title: Heart to Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: heart to heart.

Hatonn opens this evening with an observation about something the group was doing before the session began. They were talking, he says, about topics of little spiritual concern. And yet the desire behind the talk, the wish to share what could be helpful and increase the enjoyment of the group, allowed the work of blending vibrations together in a harmonious manner to occur.

From this small beginning he builds a teaching about your daily round. You know these interactions. Conversations that seem tedious, confusing, inane, pointless. The endless rituals and regulations of daily life. And yet, he says, these tedious interactions bring together people such as yourselves. People who have hopes, dreams, fears, feelings, family, friends. Just as you do.

And here is the turn. When you are able, through these activities, to find the heart of the situation, and share in an honest and loving fashion your point of view with those who share the situation with you, then the tedium of the moment may be forgotten. Even the most minute and mundane of activities takes on the communication of heart to heart.

I want to linger on what he says next, because it reframes an entire life. Look at the activities that filled your week, he says. How many were of more than a routine nature? The routine, the mundane, the seemingly trivial, is the fabric of the illusion in which each of your peoples move. The illusion is well constructed to hide the unity of all people and events. And so entities move about in a seemingly endless array of irrelevant matters, and have countless opportunities to interact with others in any fashion which those involved may choose to fathom.

You may concentrate only on the surface of appearances, and pass each moment off as one more item completed upon the list that shall comprise your day. In this way, days and years and eventually a life may be measured by an unending string of check marks. Activities dutifully completed, but without a harvest which gives meaning to the life.

Or you may, with desire and persistence, look beneath the surface, and see what was hidden from lack of desire to find it, or lack of knowing that more is available in each moment. For each entity brings to each moment the entirety of its being. And when you consider that each entity is a facet of the same Creator, moving within this illusion with you, with the purpose of finding that which was hidden with you, those about you become more than functionaries of the day. They are those who travel this illusion with you in search of the one Creator, disguised as difficulty, as confusion, as jealousy, as ignorance, and so forth.

And notice, he says, as you share the heartfelt feelings and the honest communication with a true concern for those about you, that the response is so overwhelmingly accepting and loving that the joy you cast upon the waters of the moment returns to you manifold. Though it was your intention to give it away.

Later, Latwii answers a question about soul mates, and the answer belongs in this evening. The term is reserved, they say, for those entities who have from incarnation to incarnation journeyed together, and found the seeking of truth enhanced by joining in repeated incarnations, so that lessons begun at one time may be completed at another. Those of the nature of soul mates may be many in number, not just two. And twin flames, they say, are more specific still. Entities whose individualized consciousness sprang from the same root, like the upper levels of the second-density pool of consciousness dividing in two.

Whether the other is a soul of many lifetimes or a stranger in the line at the store, the teaching is the same. Bring your heart to the moment. And the moment will answer.

Thank you for listening.

title: Stewards of the Ordinary
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: stewards of the ordinary.

Latwii speaks tonight of something philosophy usually neglects. Expenditures. Money. Time. The ordinary stuff of a Tuesday.

The questions that bring you to a metaphysical group are basic, they say. Who are you? Why are you here? Where are you going? And somehow philosophy neglects that which may be called daily or ordinary life, expecting that the seeker will become closer and closer to the infinite mystery, and that ordinary life will fall away. And yet each of you does live a daily life. That ordinary life, they say, is grist for your mill. It is the material from which you extract the answers to the most basic metaphysical questions.

One of the things each entity must consider is the expenditure of money and time. And here Latwii refuses to generalize, which I appreciate. You do not each have the same time to spend. You do not each have the same money to spend. What you have in common is the ability to look inward and discover consciously within yourself that about which you feel most strongly.

Some of you have incarnated with a special love for the second density of your planet, they say. The beauties of the outdoors. And this may be a suggestion, made through the roots of mind, to aid the environment in which you find yourselves. Some have a special feeling for the plight of those who are hungry. One may give thanksgiving that one has fed one's family, but more than that, one may discover the suggestion that stewardship regarding the feeding of strangers in need might be appropriated. Some have no strong interest in the world's problems, but a strong interest in seeking the presence of the Creator. For that entity, stewardship may be not the expenditure of money, but the expenditure of time.

I love the sentence that follows, because it turns the whole evening outward. It is important, they say, that the awareness of unity with all things, and co-responsibility for all that there is, be sharpened. Your talents and gifts are for you to discover, but the environment which you enjoy hungers for your touch. For your caring. For your presence. And for your expenditure of yourself.

And then the question they ask you to ask yourself. What portion of the creation disturbs you? Draws you? Concerns you? Are you spending enough of your riches on impersonal giving? And they do not mean only money, for time is often far more of a sacrifice than your money. For those who feel the call to no particular part of daily life, they urge this. Consider how active you are in your beingness. If what you have to offer is a determination to become closer to the Creator, how often and how freely is that companionship given to the world? And not an exclusive world of people who already think as you do, but a world of people whose faces are blank and whose names are unknown.

Your incarnation is not your own, they say. Your incarnation is the Creator's gift to itself. And the Creator is in all things.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Journey Is Home
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the journey is home.

Hatonn begins with an image that undoes the most common picture of the spiritual path. There is within the heart of each of you, he says, a pathway. There is within the heart of each of you a home. These are one and the same.

Very often, because of the illusion, the seeker believes the journey leaves him homeless. The road that stretches ever onward. The straight and narrow path. The craggy mountain trail. The endless desert. And so some feel homeless, while others, who find themselves in an oasis, comfortable, surrounded by support and love, almost feel as if they have left the path.

But the first steps are the wrenching ones, he says. Preparing the mind for a journey. Deciding what baggage to carry, what to leave behind. And once the decision is made, once you are out of sight of the starting point, the journey changes its character. How upsetting this is to many seekers. It seems too easy sometimes. One step, then another, then another. All so logical. Problems become challenges, and challenges become things to enjoy. Hardship becomes that which is not so bad, and then that to which one is used. And the seeker begins to wonder if he is still on the path.

It is impossible, Hatonn says, to go back to the you that you were before you began your conscious journey. Were you to go back, you would find yourself doing the equivalent of what people do who have been on hard treks. They cannot sleep on hard beds, but seek the floor. And yet, when one is on the trail, such behavior is normal, has become comfortable. And one begins to think, how can I be comfortable and be a pure and sincere seeker?

And then the oasis. There are no stones. There is no desert. You seat yourself upon the greensward under trees and drink of the cool spring, and you say, how can I be a serious seeker and be so very, very happy? Am I not supposed to suffer?

Listen to his answer, because it is the heart of the evening. My friends, you are supposed to seek. Not only is that your responsibility, it is your inevitability, for the choice, once made, is irrevocable. In your illusion, suffering is almost inevitable. But so is joy. You must learn to accept the gifts that are given you. Whether they seem too hard or too easy, they are yours. No one else can quite grasp your dilemmas or your joys. No one else can lift your next foot, or tell you when to leave the waving palms of the oasis.

So he suggests you toss concern about your own sincerity to the wind. Sing the songs of joy that are in your heart at this moment. Or turn your face to the wind and moan and cry, if that be your lot. Accept joy and sorrow as if they were the same thing. Accept the rocky place and the oasis as if they were equal gifts. For these are your home.

Later, Latwii is asked about coping and conquering, and the answer completes the picture. In your cultures, they say, the product of an effort is given much value, and the process is overlooked completely. But the situation you call coping has much more to it than keeping your head above water. There is much work upon the inner levels accomplished at that time, which may be likened to the tempering of an instrument, that it may probe yet further without bending or breaking.

Whether you are in the desert or the oasis, coping or conquering, the teaching is one. You are creatures of the moment, and the journey lies within.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Same Living Water
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the same living water.

The question before the ones who call themselves L/Leema this evening is one the instrument believes she is asking. Am I a Christian? And they approach the answer in a way, they warn, that will be unexpected.

First, they speak of death, and I want to handle this part gently, as they do. To be alive within a chemical body in third density is to be concerned with death, they say, for that which begins shall also end. And they observe, without judgment, a love of death that distorts many among your peoples. Some have been uncomfortable in their bodies as long as they can remember, and yearn for a period to be put to the sentence. Some have been devastated enough to contemplate removing the self. Some, of a warlike nature, seek risk, and welcome the possibility of death in order to live more finely tuned moments.

However one comes at a fascination with death, they say, it is as though one were making war upon oneself. For each of you came into this incarnation not to die, but to live. And to live, thinking greatly of death, is to live less well. While to live absorbed in, rejoicing in, and giving thanksgiving for each moment of beauty and love and glory, for glory there is, all about you and within you, that is the other choice, and it is always before you.

If you find yourself sitting with thoughts of death more often than you would like, please hear this as invitation rather than instruction. There are people in the world, kind ones, trained to sit with exactly those thoughts alongside you, and reaching for them is a way of choosing the life this teaching points toward.

Then they turn to the question itself, and to the gift, as they call it, of congruency with an established religion. Many who would wish to be Christians, they say, cannot accept the wordings and seemingly limited viewpoints of others who also call themselves Christians. In many cases, Christians are more vitriolic and judgmental of other Christians than of those they consider heathen. And so one who has been given the gift of congruency feels she does not fit in, that she cannot possibly be Christian.

And here is their answer, which I find quietly radical. If it is pleasurable and instructive and nourishing to study the teachings and to live the life of the Christ, then do not listen to those whose Christianity bears a different mark. For this word is a word and no more. The point in any approach to divinity is to discover and dwell in the presence of love, the one original and creative thought.

They go further. You have many idols, they say. Money, power, lust, gross eating, excess. Those your world recognizes. But there are less recognizable idols. One is the man known as Jesus. Another is Gautama Buddha. Another Lao Tsu, another Confucius, another Mohammed. None of these men hollowed themselves out to be worshipped, they say, but rather to become messengers, channels, wayfarers, sharing a consciousness. The consciousness of the Creator.

So they are not interested in semantics. They are interested in giving you the freedom to pursue the presence of Christ consciousness. That which was channeled through the Christ of Jesus, the Christ of the Buddha, the Christ of Lao Tsu, the Christ of Confucius, the Christ of Mohammed. Whatever your choice, they say, acknowledge it and do not look back. Follow it not only with energy, but with discrimination. Yet all these structures yield the same living water. All are channels through which this water may flow.

The evening also holds a tender exchange on love itself. Asked whether everyone gets the chance to fall in love, L/Leema says that romantic love is an approximation of the more universal compassion, and indeed few experience even the approximation. And the degree to which pain accompanies the experience, they suggest, is the degree to which the mind has formed boundaries within which love is allowed to express. For if there are no conditions or boundaries to the expression of love, there can be no pain accompanying the loss of such love. For there will be no loss.

And on the old teaching that you must love yourself before you can love others, they agree, with a reason worth hearing. As the entity moves into this illusion, the first awareness is the awareness of self, and this becomes the foundation upon which all experience is built. Since for the self all begins within the self, there first must love be found.

Thank you for listening.

title: Already Meaningful
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: already meaningful.

The question put to the ones who call themselves L/Leema this evening is not an inconsiderable one, as they say. What is the meaning of life?

They begin by drawing a distinction. Meaning has to do with the nature of something. Purpose has to do with its function. And they shall address themselves, they say, to the nature of life.

It is a glorious and mysterious thing, they say, that there is nothing in the infinite creation which is not full of life. The air is full of life. The earth beneath your feet. The stones, the rivers, the fires that heat you in winter, the breezes that cool you in summer. All the animals that delight your senses. All of these entities are full of life. But those of you in third density are not only full of life. You know that you are alive. And so, unlike rocks and fire and air and water and trees and small animals, it is within you to ask, what is the meaning of my being alive?

In essence, they say, that which has meaning in life is consciousness. That is the essence of life. All consciousness comes from the Father, the Creator of all things. Through those portions of himself, thrown out into the vastness of the starry heavens, this infinite and invisible Creator offered the incredible opportunity for the Creator to be conscious of the Creator.

And here is the turn that makes this evening worth your time. It is impossible not to be a meaningful person, they say. For as you experience, record, and change through catalyst, you are becoming aware, in a unique way, in a brand new way, in a way valuable to the creation, of some part of the creation. When you think a thought, you think it not only for yourself, but for all that lives. When you meditate and wish someone well, that wish has meaning and power. When you decide to seek to find love, all that you do has meaning. For as you experience, and as you record what you experience within yourself, you are adding to the store of knowledge of that which is.

It may be difficult to accept, they say, that you need do nothing, you need accomplish nothing, you need have no worldly ambition, in order to have meaning. Yet you as consciousness are meaning. And each entity that you see is the essence of creation. Creation is cut of one whole cloth. There is no division in meaning or in unity. As all are one, so each of you is a holograph of all that there is, containing within yourself the great circle and heart of the universe.

The meaning of life is an essence, they say. And that essence is the one original thought of the Creator. That creative love which through light has created us all.

Thank you for listening.

title: Speaking and Listening
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: speaking and listening.

The question put to the ones who call themselves L/Leema this evening is one every seeker has asked. What is the place of analytical thought upon the spiritual path?

And they answer with an image I want you to hold. The intellectual mind and the intuitive mind are two sides of one coin. Analysis is a form of speaking. Intuition is a form of listening. And yet, when one is speaking, does one not also have ears? And when one listens intuitively, does one not hear the voice of silence?

They will not overgeneralize, they say. It may be possible to reach a significant degree of enlightenment through the singular pursuit of either course. But total dependence upon either the intellect or the intuition leaves one open to imbalance. Like standing upon one foot.

Listen to how they put the case against the intellect first. This is perhaps the greatest single difficulty with an overdependence upon the intellect, they say. For the presence of the Creator is an experience, not a knowledge. The Creator is always the same, is the singular, is the simple, and is not to be learned by degree, by method, or by rote.

And then the case against intuition, which is the braver passage. Total dependence upon intuition, they say, is a total dependence upon a portion of your deep self which is unreliable. Much comes through the intuition which is of extreme merit. But much occurs by seeming intuition which is in fact a product of deep fears, of experiences from previous incarnations not yet worked out, and of static, as if you were between radio stations, picking up no clear signal, but a babble of varying messages. So the mind is to be taken as a whole thing, and not split. For the intellect and the intuition are both portions of the mind.

And then the line that steadies the whole teaching. You are not your mind. Your mind is a kind of information processor which works for you as a tool. It is well to balance your seeking, they say. Do not shut out the loud voice of intellect when it offers new ideas, new questions, new waves of skepticism. Many a baseless fear has been removed by the work of the analytical portion of the mind. And it is wise to listen to your intuition, to quiet yourself, so that you may feel and be in a more whole and entire sense. For the heart of yourself is being. Not thinking. Not feeling. Being.

But neither analysis nor intuition, they say, can offer the heart of seeking. For the heart of your seeking is found in that fathomless portion of yourself which seeks, and wills to know, and has the faith that there is something to know. These things are gifts. The mind has been earned. It is a product of many incarnations, and it reflects your biases. Neither intellect nor intuition often reach deep enough to uncover faith and will.

So turn, they say, from the consideration of clear minds and clear intuition, long enough to gaze at the mystery. You have the will to seek. And what do you seek? Many would say truth. Many would say love. Many would say the Creator. They say to you, there are no words. For the Creator is mystery infinite and invisible. It cannot be reached by analysis. It cannot be sounded through intuition. It is closer to you than that. For you are that which the Creator is. The one original thought. You are what you seek, and you seek what you are.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Dance in Darkness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a dance in darkness.

The ones who call themselves Q'uo speak this evening of two selves that live in you. And they do not flatter either one. They simply describe them.

The first is the biological self. And Q'uo is blunt about it. It is well to know one's biological handicaps, they say, for there is no deep instinctual yearning in your biological makeup toward truth, or the betterment of others, or cooperation between peoples, or any kind of redemptive grace. That body which you inhabit will say to you, time and time again, that mysteries will come to nothing. That meditation and seeking are games you play to distract yourself from the certainty of your own death. That ethics are the luxury of those who have no unmet needs.

This is the material, they say, that will be thrown up before your vision, time and again, as long as you inhabit the dwelling place of your fragile physical vehicle. It is a wondrous machine, full of delights and folly. It is well to know it, and its limitations. And even to acknowledge, before the magnificent rationality of the brain, that intense skepticism concerning the spiritual seeking is the logical stance.

And then the turn. Let us plunge, then, into darkness. Let us become blind and deaf. Let us become aware of the something within us that is other. Other than what, you may ask? Perhaps a good adjective would be otherworldly. And yet we do not mean absentminded. We mean something more basic.

The body with which you are so familiar seeks and loves light, they say. It basks in the summer. It delights in the fire. But that within you which is other, that which is spirit, delights in the darkness which frightens the biological shell. It is the darkness of the seeker. For we do not seek in light, or we should most surely have a short journey to the end of our seeking. We seek in the shadowland, where the only light is that of hope, the only star that of faith, the only flickering candle that of blessed will, the only electricity that of inspiration.

I love how they refuse to make this abstract. Your logical, rational, measurable shell is itself mutable, they say. Indeed, your environmentalists will be pleased that it is also biodegradable. But that within you which seeks is immutable and unchangeable in its essence. It is eternal, and coeternal with the Father. It is your source, and it is your goal. You are the full circle of that which you seek. And yet seek it you must, and in some length, for an entire creation shall be spent with the seeking of one self for the self.

And you do not need to make the journey at once, they say. For your journey is this step. This moment. This situation. The entities about you at this time. The emotions you feel at this juncture. The rational mind loves to stretch back into the past and into the future. But the heart of your seeking lies with that portion of yourself that is other. And that otherness dwells in an eternal present moment.

So their blessing for the evening is a strange and beautiful one. May your dance in the darkness, they say, be all that you hope and all that you seek.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Other River
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the other river.

The request put to the ones who call themselves L/Leema this evening is a layman's discussion of the concept of three-dimensional time. And they begin, as they often do, by apologizing in advance for the inadequacy of language.

You dwell, they say, in a domicile rich in time. It has stood still in space through many seasons, and is full of years. Each of you sitting in this circle has ceased to grow in the physical sense. The space you occupy is the space you shall occupy. But as you dwell within your physical bodies in space and time, you dwell also in time and space. And as you grow more full in years, so you grow rich in time.

Then the simple picture. In space and time, you think little of setting out for another city. When the trip is done, you think little of the next journey. You travel geographically, to and fro in space. Now imagine the reverse. A sensitive enough student would not think a great deal of moving back in time, and experiencing, in the stream of space, the movement in time. Your year nineteen twenty-nine would be as Cincinnati to Louisville. The year six hundred before the common era, perhaps Australia or Madagascar. Just as you do not notice, moving in space, that time is anything but a flowing river, so in moving through time, space is seen as a simply flowing river. One place is as easily arrived at as another.

It is the simplicity of the concept that confuses the mind, they say, rather than its complexity.

And here is why it matters to the seeker. Meditation, they say, is as far as they know the single most efficient controllable method of achieving conscious experience of time and space. For within time and space dwells much of that which you call the mind. Much of what you experience goes unnoticed by the conscious mind dwelling in space and time. When you dream clearly, the portion of your mind dwelling in time speaks to you of that which you have not yet become aware of in space.

I love the analogy they reach for. Think of experience as putting the ball in the basket. One's conscious experiences in space are such that one may learn lessons without recourse to the deeper mind only by extremely accurate observation. That would equal the action of the ball thrown so that it moved through the hoop without touching the rim or the backboard. It is seldom that a player develops skill without recourse to the rim and the backboard. It would be an inefficient use of the tools given for the game. It is equally unlikely, they say, that an entity will move through an incarnation without the use, conscious or unconscious, of the backboard of the deeper mind.

Now the river. If you consider time to be the river, as one in your illusion is almost forced to do, in the illusion called time and space it is equally incongruous to suppose that the river of space will cease. The river is a foreverness, whether the river in space or the river of time. You were in time and space before you came into incarnation, and to that river you shall return. And time then, as before, shall become static. It is the stasis of time which enables the spirit to do so much with that tool in seeking. For within the body, you are bound by the river of time. In time and space, that river ceases to flow, and you may remain in an eternal present moment, and dwell what may seem long upon the most brief moment. For that moment may hold a key for you.

So they encourage the movement inward. For the goal of your consciousness is to seek out experience, and to process it in such a way that you add to the Creator's knowledge of itself. Thus it is necessary, they say, that space and time be mismatched.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Crystalline Self
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the crystalline self.

The ones who call themselves Yom speak this evening of light. Not as metaphor. As mechanics. As the stuff of everything.

Light itself, they say, being alive and being the first creature created of love, forms all that there is. It furthermore, in its creative freedom, surrounds and interpenetrates in original form the structures created by the influence of free will upon light. So all that there is is not only made, mechanically speaking, of articulated light, but is also interpenetrated by limitless light, which some among your students of metaphysics call prana.

And from this they build a picture of crystalline structures. You may term each atom an inchoate crystalline structure, they say. Galaxies, stars, and planets have a time and space crystalline structure. Your own planet has such a structure. You yourselves are time and space crystalline structures. Those among you who learn to heal are manifesting in space and time that crystalline structure which is the essence of regularized light.

I want to pause on what they say about astrology, because it is the driest and most surprising passage of the evening. The nearer stars and the planets of your sun system, they say, have regularized time and space properties which result in instreaming from planet to planet, which in turn affect the crystalline entities of third density. It has often been questioned whether the art you call astrology has a basis. The basis, in fact, they say, is most dry and scientific. Astrology is the science of the crystalline properties of light in time and space, and the influence of this upon the planet. The orientation of your being at the time of conception affects the physical parameters of the vehicle, and the orientation of this sphere at entry into incarnation has an effect over the mental, emotional, and to some small extent the spiritual nature of the entity.

But lest you believe in a mechanistic universe, they hasten to add this. Each cell within the physical vehicle has a great portion of its nature hidden in time and space, and is in that portion in a crystalline structure open to influences from other crystalline structures. The greatest of these influences is that of the third-density entity which has achieved, to some degree, the manifestation in space and time of its crystalline nature. Such entities are often teachers, healers, and leaders. Those which serve as the watershed over which many entities will move, and thereby be transformed, or in many cases, healed.

And then the teaching turns practical, and gently funny. This instrument, Yom notes, has made light of writers who advocate the use of affirmations. But they suggest that if one is not satisfied with any portion of the being, it is well to use an affirmation repeatedly, as a way of moving from conscious thought to concept to light, to the sending of that light to the cells of the body, or the brain, or the subtle bodies, in order that healing at the cellular level may take place. Most affirmations find their benefit in the mental and emotional areas, they say, but physical healing is also quite available through affirmations which, indistinct or poetic, prosaic or wondrously beautiful, nevertheless have the intent of focusing the light of the infinite Creator so that it interpenetrates and enlivens each cell.

A gentle note as you listen. These are teachings about attention, intention, and the inner life. If you are carrying a real illness or ailment, the kindest thing you can do for yourself is to seek the care of people trained in healing bodies, alongside whatever inner practices you keep.

And they close with a play on the word that I want to leave you with. Light is used in your language as the opposite of heavy. To be full of light, they say, is to be light. That is, cheerful, joyful, and resilient. When you discover heaviness within the heart, you have a choice. It is acceptable to the Creator if you wish to experience the heaviness. But you may also choose to turn to some affirmation, one of your jokes, or any inspiration which yields realization of light. It is without you and within you, interpenetrating each cell, and it is a tool for your use.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Green Ray
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the green ray.

The ones who call themselves L/Leema speak tonight of healing energy. And they begin by correcting the question itself, which I admire. One is not using healing energy as such, they say. This must be emphasized, for it tells much about healing.

What they describe instead is the heart energy center, the green ray. In the meditative state, when an entity turns purely to the heart chakra and moves the brain wave energy in concentration to that locus, there enters a very pure love vibratory emanation. The crystallized being acts as a catalyst in the connection between two green rays, the auric shell of the one to be healed is pierced, the green ray opened, and the energy is sent forth. And then, they say, the one to be healed may choose healing at that time.

Listen to how they describe love itself, because the whole evening rests on it. Love, my friends, is a creative, fiery, intelligent, and ever present source, concentrated at the heart chakra of your beings, and sent forth to nurture, to help, to encourage, to grow, and to transform.

And then the passage I cannot leave out. Many healings, they say, are wrought by one who listens with a wide open heart. The listener may never speak. But the talker will feel the healing of green ray, which is love. The babe at the breast seeks green-ray nurturance. Milk is the second-density reason for the suckling. The green-ray exchange between mother and child is the metaphysical reason for the nurturing that takes place. Indeed, there is so much healing associated with the green-ray center that when your very planet is looked at in a nurturing sense, it is described in terms of a breast. Putting one's head upon the breast of mother nature, as one lays one's head upon the mother's breast.

Asked how one may enhance this energy, their answer is almost disappointingly simple, and I think that is the point. The discipline of silence, they say. Not easily begun, and not easily maintained. But all-important to the eventual and continued contact with intelligent infinity. This is the simplest and most important method of enhancing green-ray intensification.

And they return, again and again, to intention. Each word spoken to mate or colleague, friend, stranger, or seeming foe, vibrates with intention. If the intentions are persistently compassionate, so you shall enhance the development of green-ray crystallization and power.

A gentle note as you listen. The teachings this evening are about presence and compassion between people. If you or someone you love is unwell, please do not mistake a loving presence for a substitute for medical care. The two belong together.

The evening closes with an unexpected visitor, the one who calls itself Yadda, who speaks in a very different voice, and I want you to hear it. You think you are vivid, sitting there, Yadda says. But you are nothing but shadow. What you build in this incarnation, you build behind the shadow world. First, you build something called you. What will you look like when you enter the larger life? The face you see in the mirror is not what you are doing here. Second, if you have a mate, you build a person that is not you, not me. It is called relationship. You cannot control what your mate builds. You control what you build. Forget the shadows of your mirror. Forget what you can see, and move to what you are building. You architects of the spirit.

Thank you for listening.

title: Perfect Freedom
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: perfect freedom.

Hatonn speaks this evening of freedom. And given that the Fourth of July approaches, he begins where his listeners are. Amongst you who call yourselves Americans, you celebrate your independence, your freedom, defined as the pursuit of happiness. Indeed, he says, the nature of freedom in third density is in large part social.

But the deeper nature of freedom, he suggests, is no such personal thing. You have heard countless times that the Creator manifested itself as love. But what is love? Love chooses between love of self and love of other self. And he offers an equation to ponder, not once but many times. If service to others' self is love manifested toward other selves, strike out all the selves, and what you have left is this. Service to others is love.

And what does this have to do with freedom? You are given freedom in totality, he says. There is no holding back on the part of the Creator. No hidden loopholes or clauses. You are free. Free to do nothing. Free to work diligently upon a personal agenda with no contact with other selves. Free to throw yourself into service of other selves at every opportunity, whether service is requested or not. And finally, free to leave yourself open to the potential for the opportunity of being of service whenever that opportunity is offered. He finds the more virtue, he says, in the latter course.

And here is the paradox that names our evening. What he is suggesting may seem upon the surface to smack not of freedom, but of slavery. Let us observe slavery among your peoples, he says. There is no time in the history you know in which humans have not been slaves. And there is a reason. To some, happiness, that happiness which is the manifestation of freedom, lies in seeing a loved one happy. In tending a loved one's hurts. In tending and encouraging a loved one in distress.

He is careful to say what he does not mean. He does not speak of those who are slaves against their will. He speaks of those who love their masters and are loved in return, and who therefore find happiness in service. Were slavery uniformly disagreeable to all, it would be attempted unceasingly, but found counterproductive. It is those happy combinations which ensure that slavery, whether traditional or untraditional, as in some marriage relationships, endures.

But he is not suggesting you choose a master and become a slave. The scope, he says, is somewhat small in that suggestion. Rather, he suggests that freedom lies in the concept of oneself as a manifester of servanthood to any and all who cross the path. Think of service, in this context, in terms of slavery. For one of the great paradoxes of the spiritual search is that freedom, and that service which approaches what you call slavery, are both paradoxical and synonymous. When the opportunity to help is perceived, the seeker offers itself in service, not condescendingly or patronizingly, but as servant to all. And if all are servants to all, then where shall be contention? And if all serve all, where is slavery?

Service by itself, he says, shall always be a duty, and shall not feel like freedom at all. It is the willing openness to the finding of peace and joy in the concept of the self as a servant which opens one to a freedom beyond human freedom. For in human freedom, you attempt to please yourself and gain happiness, and yet the happiness is caught up entirely in the pursuit, and the goal is never truly attained.

So he asks you to look back over your life, at the fruits of seeking personal happiness as master of your fate and captain of your ship. Some of these fruits, he suggests, may include anger, frustration, jealousy, quarrelsomeness, and dejection. And then to remember the times you sacrificed the self, seemingly as servant of another in need. Remember doing all that you could and more, and feel again the peace that comes from knowing you have done all you can, and the joy that comes when in any small thing another self turns to you and says, truly I have asked you, and truly you have served.

He closes as he began, with an offer. We are, if you will, your slaves for the moment, he says. And we are filled with great joy at the thought that we could have been of some service to you. Love one another. Serve one another. And find your freedom, your joy, and your peace.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Law of Finished Beginnings
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the law of finished beginnings.

The group gathered on the evening after Independence Day, and the phrase all men are created equal was still in the air. Q'uo took it up — not to argue with it, but to add something to it. Yes, they said, each of you is the Creator, each carrying the whole godhead in potential. And yet, in the illusion of personality, all are manifestly unequal. Each life is unrepeatably itself. And that inequality, they said, is not a flaw in the design. It is the design.

Within that design, they said, two great influences shape a life. The first they called, beautifully, the law of finished beginnings. That which was left unfinished in another lifetime comes back around, asking to be finished in this one. Many difficult relationships are made of this material.

I love the image they use for it. Such a relationship, they say, is like produce that seems fresh from the grocery — sweet and fresh to every physical sense — and yet, taken home, seems somehow aging and putrefying. There is something ancient in it, something you cannot put your finger on, something that smacks of déjà vu. That ancient flavor is the unfinished beginning, asking for your attention.

Their advice is twofold, and both parts matter. Take such influences seriously, they say — give them careful and persistent consideration. But also use the light touch. The laughter. The seeking of joy. Find the love hidden inside each difficulty, and the challenge will loosen its grip.

Then the second influence, the one they say is rarely spoken of and even less rarely grasped. Alongside everything you have called to yourself, there comes what you never called at all — the brand-new circumstance, the experience for which you have no previous tools, no memory to guide you. You come to it, they say, as a virgin comes to her first love.

Why would the Creator arrange such a thing? Because the way to transformation is the way of balance. If you have sought and sought only the good and the perfect, then it is a just balance that the painful shall also occur to you — not because you deserve it, they are careful to say, but because balance is how transformation happens. And the reverse is just as true. If your life has been one half-remembered nightmare after another, wearily endured, then something utterly, unexpectedly marvelous shall occur. Not because you deserve it either. Because a balance needs to be brought.

And here they give it a name. Grace, they say. There is such a thing as grace. There is that which rains when there is drought, and which shines to brighten an interior dim landscape. It arrives not when you expect it, but always as a gift. And whether it comes as happiness or as sorrow, it carries lessons that are more simply learned, because you have already been learning their opposite.

Be meticulous, they urge, in acknowledging each gift. The easy lessons are easy to waste. Watch for the ones that arrive unasked, and receive them with gratitude — for they are the balancing of your own becoming, and no one else's.

Later in the evening, the conversation turned to infatuation, and whether it has anything to do with love. Q'uo's answer is tender and precise. Infatuation, they say, is like the magnet and the iron filing — no thinking required to bring the two together. And in one sense, they say, it is a pure form of love, for it accepts the other totally, without condition.

Pure, however, in the sense that it has not been tested. It lacks the depth of experience. When two people stay, and the inevitable catalyst of shared life begins its work, there come the moments of non-acceptance — and the need to accept what was not acceptable, to forgive what felt unforgivable. That is how love gains its strength and depth and richness. The love that results is tested love, and it is stronger for the testing.

Someone asked, then, for a simple yes or no: is the fastest way to learn love simply to work on accepting others, and yourself, as you are? Basically correct, Q'uo said. For each entity and event is the Creator, knowing itself in a mysterious way. Find the joy and the light of the Creator within that person, that moment, that event — and you have moved yourself further along your chosen path.

Two influences, then: the unfinished business that returns, and the grace that arrives unasked. Between them, a whole life. Thank you for listening.

title: The Riverbed Healer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the riverbed healer.

The evening opened with a visitor — Yadda, a contact with a comedian's timing and a teacher's heart, who greeted the group by calling them, affectionately, bozos. Beneath the jokes, the question was the one every seeker carries: how do I love? What is love? What has love to do with me?

I love how Yadda frames it. You do not want an answer, they say, as much as you want a clear understanding of the question. And the question — how do I love — has two great stumbling blocks in front of it. The first is the habit of thinking in the head without ever having observed anything worth thinking about. Your culture is fast and shallow, they say, like a stream that has no depth but moves very quickly. You cannot think until you have observed. To think right off the bat is putting the cart before the horse.

The second stumbling block is your opinion of yourself. You were born into illusion, and if you look in the mirror and see only an age, a weight, a salary, a list of degrees — you are falling flat on your face. Lose those provincial ideas, they say, and look again. See perfection. Not the perfection of achievement, but the perfection of what you are: a collection of well-arranged atoms housing self-aware consciousness. Love yourself not for what you do, but for what you are — and the gate opens.

There is a third block too, born of the shortness of the physical vehicle: impatience. You want to know everything now. But everything is in this moment, they say, and the work is to seek only to know this moment. Your best ally is meditation — not done well, for no one meditates well, but done daily, in faith. The discipline of returning, day after day, opens the birthright: that you are an heir to all of the truth, because you are the truth, walking around in a body.

Yadda leaves the group three requests. Discount your conclusions and gather data instead — be a witness. Love not your mask but yourself, and not the tasks about you but the selves about you. And meditate, opening to the silence without judging the stray thoughts.

Then Latwii took up a question from a healer — a woman who could feel the pain of everyone she tried to help, and was being drained by it. How, she asked, can I tune in to another's suffering without absorbing it?

Listen to how they put it. See yourself, they say, as a portion of a river. Let the feelings brought to you by the one seeking healing move through your being the way water moves through a riverbed. You are the bed and the banks and the air above the water. Notice where there is blockage, where there are deeps, where the water eddies and whirls — work with what you notice — and then let it all continue downstream. Nothing needs to be absorbed.

It is, at heart, the discipline of the observer rather than the experiencer. The healer stays in the body, concentrates, and watches — the way a person under hypnosis might watch a frightening memory without being pulled inside it. The pain is seen clearly precisely because it is not claimed.

The last question of the evening came from a woman overwhelmed by a sudden, terrible depression. She could not tell whether it was a cleansing or a weakness, and she could not think past it. Latwii's counsel was gentle and practical: follow the feeling. Let it lead you to the anxieties and fears underneath it — the beliefs that may not be true, the guilts that may yield to a wider point of view. To sit inside the depression without moving with it is to stay stuck; to follow it is to let it point the arrow toward what can be transformed.

A gentle note from me, not from the archive: Latwii speaks here as a spiritual counselor, and their counsel is beautiful. But if the heavy days keep coming, please reach out — to someone you trust, or to a professional who can walk with you. The teaching and the care belong together.

The riverbed does not drink the river. It only gives the water somewhere to go. Thank you for listening.

title: The One Original Thought
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the one original thought.

Hatonn's opening words were lost — the tape gives out, and only the greeting survives. So the evening belongs to Q'uo, who took up the largest subject in the archive: the one original Thought upon which all creation was founded. That Thought, they say, is love. Love is not only a feeling. It is a thought, a principle, a logos — the material of everything.

You, by your very consciousness, are that Thought in holographic form. Your field of energy is completely unique, they say, and completely precious to the Creator — for by your mirroring of your perceptions, the Creator learns of itself. There is no one else who can do your particular piece of the mirroring.

This incarnation, Q'uo says, is an incarnation of choice — the choice of how you will manifest that original Thought. There are two basic ways. Service to others, or love for others. And service to self, or love for self. The first demands that you love yourself first, so that you may love each other self as the self. It offers the vaster range of experience. The second is narrower, more intense, and, they say plainly, the more difficult path.

Then comes the passage I keep returning to. To open yourself in love to those who are disharmonious seems an act of folly. But look at the flowers, they say. They open their faces in love to the sun — and yet they do not withhold their perfume from any being. There is no judgment on the part of a flower as to who shall receive its gifts of beauty.

You yourself are crystalline, they say, and many-petaled, and capable of a great radiance. But do not depend on the limited supply of love your personality can offer. Open as a channel for the Creator's love instead — especially toward those who seem to wish you quarrelsomeness. Your own love will fail you, they say, with a kind of tenderness. The channel will not.

I love that line: the nature of service to others is such that you will find again and again that you have nothing to offer except your very being. Your consciousness, your attention, your sympathy, your attempt to understand — that is the most precious service there is. You are not preordained to do or be anything. All choices are yours, to make and remake, softening and firming, again and again.

And here is the turn that steadies everything: do not demand the outcome. It is a good thing to desire peace and to serve in love, and yet they encourage you to remain detached from solutions. When you think you have the right answer, you are pulled away from love and cannot allow others to choose their own. It does not matter, spiritually speaking, what the result of your service is. What matters is that your desire to serve was pure.

Latwii said the same thing that evening, answering a question about a great peace march that had seemed, by outer measures, to fail. What is seen and registered, they said, is not the result but the intention — the intention that survives the struggles and does not die with seeming defeat. That intention radiates outward in ways no eye can trace, and lightens hearts inside the mystery.

So the teaching rests on a single sentence, and I will leave it with you the way Q'uo left it: the core of choice is love. There is nothing lukewarm about it. Thank you for listening.

title: The Pattern of Prayer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the pattern of prayer.

A question had come in from the group's written correspondence: L/Leema had once said that the critical mass for the harvest was nearly reached — and the group wanted to know what, exactly, that meant. What follows is one of the most carefully reasoned answers in the archive, and I want to walk through it slowly.

First, they untangle two things people keep tying together: the harvest of souls, and planetary cataclysm. The Earth's fever — the venting of long-accumulated human anger — is real, they say, but it does not cause the harvest, and the harvest does not cause it. They are concomitant, not cause and effect. The harvest is the quieter event, and the more important one.

What is it, then? The critical mass is the point at which roughly one in ten of a planet's people can hold fourth-density vibration within themselves — and, more than that, can offer themselves to a group identity, a larger self. That nucleus, they say, becomes the beginning of a social memory complex: the shared mind of a planet waking up together.

They will not give hard numbers — free will makes all counting approximate — but they suggest somewhere around eight or nine in every hundred may already be at harvestable levels. And they note something beautiful about the children being born now: many are old souls, strong and willful, come for one more attempt at graduation. It should be, they say, an interesting generation.

The time frame? They refuse to pin it down, and they tell you why: they cannot quantize what happens in time and space the way you count hours, and they cannot predict what free beings will do. Perhaps as short as three decades, perhaps as long as fifteen, for those in third-density bodies attempting to graduate. Their advice, though, is unambiguous. Behave as if this were the last chance to achieve a harvestable vibration — for in that way, you give your effort all that it deserves.

And then, at the heart of the session, something I did not expect: a commentary on the Lord's Prayer, offered as a pattern for meditation itself. Five movements. First, praise — the Creator hallowed, which is the highest self-acceptance, since you are the Creator too. Second, the request that the greater self be given authority: thy will be done — the little self listening to the greater. Third, the daily bread — and notice, they say, how minimal the request is, and how shameless the asking may be. They retell the parable of the man knocking at his neighbor's door at midnight, demanding bread for a guest — and receiving everything, because he would not stop knocking. Bring your real troubles to meditation, they say. Speak plainly. Expect to be answered.

Fourth, forgiveness given as forgiveness is asked — the simple, staggering recognition that you are the judge of everyone you meet, and that holding them guilty binds you both. Fifth, the honest acknowledgment of temptation, and of the errors you do not even know you have made, affirmed as forgiven in advance.

Then silence. In the silence you do not pose questions; you listen for inspiration. Sometimes, they say, the greatest fruit of meditation is not an answer at all, but the refining of the question.

One more thing, for those already walking the path: learn to be solitary happily first — and then seek with at least one other. Two who seek together, they say, are always more balanced than one who seeks alone. That is why the call to community runs so deep right now. It is the nascent art of becoming one larger self.

The harvest, in the end, is not an event you wait for. It is a vibration you practice. Thank you for listening.

title: Weights Upon the Bar
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: weights upon the bar.

Hatonn's message this evening is for anyone who has ever looked at their own worst moments and despaired of them. The seeker, they say, draws to himself exactly the experiences he needs — and then, very often, mistakes the difficult ones for evidence of failure. They are the opposite. They are the laboratory.

Here is the practice they describe. Watch your own spontaneous, unrehearsed responses to the events of an ordinary day. Notice the biases and attitudes you are armed with — the flash of anger when the world will not bend to your design, the impatience, the need to control people and events. Do not judge what you see. Just look, the way a naturalist looks.

And then consider the possibility that changes everything: that you arranged this before you came. That the anger you keep tripping over was programmed in — the seeming opposite of what you actually came to learn. If you wished to learn compassion, acceptance, forgiveness, what better classroom than a personality that defaults to none of them? Each release of anger, looked at without judgment, reveals the potential hidden inside it: the chance, in that exact moment, to generate the loving acceptance that was the original intention.

I love how plainly they say it: within even the darkest and most dimly lit moments of your experience, great treasures potentially await. The seeker is quick to credit the joyful times with all the growth. But it is in the moments of difficulty that the fiber of your being is truly tested — and given the greatest opportunity to grow stronger.

They offer an image for the times when life seems to be actively opposing you. See it, they say, as placing more weights upon the bar. The bar is heavier, yes — but it is the heaviness that builds the strength to lift it. Welcome the intensive opportunity. It is how you progress at a quicker pace.

Latwii, answering questions later, added something I find myself using as a diagnostic. When you hit a wall, they said, the message is not always the same. Sometimes it says: proceed with greater intention and vigor. Sometimes it says: take another path, more appropriate to you. Sometimes it says: this path is yours if you want it — learn what it has to teach.

How do you tell which? Take the confusion itself into meditation. Study it with the mind as far as the mind can go — and then release the intellectual description, and let only the desire to know what is most appropriate remain. That desire will draw to you the hunch, the intuition, the still small voice that speaks when spoken to and listened to. Listen always to that voice within.

The wall is not always telling you to stop. Sometimes it is telling you to get stronger. Thank you for listening.

title: Desire and Surrender
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: desire and surrender.

Latwii opened the evening unusually — not with answers, but with an invitation to review what little any of us actually knows. That which is seen is transient. There is more than chance to the universe. And the most important force in a life, they said, has been love — the love that creates and the love that destroys, the love that gives and the love that takes.

Then, with the gentleness this group is known for, they took up the pressure so many seekers put on themselves: the urgency to choose faster, seek harder, get it right. Step back from that urgency, they said. In choosing to meditate, in choosing to seek, you have sown seeds — and seeds take time. Rely on the purity of your intention, and pray for its continuation. As you desire, so shall you have.

The first question cut straight to the tension every seeker feels: should I desire the things I want, or should I simply wake up each day and say, thy will be done? Latwii's answer holds both. Desire is helpful — but let it be general, they say. Build on the simplest desire of all: to be made aware of what is appropriate for you. And then surrender the outcome completely.

For here is the trap: when you dedicate yourself to a particular result, that very dedication can block the more appropriate pattern of experience from arriving. Desire opens the door; clinging to the outcome bars it. Let the desire be wide, the surrender total, and what is appropriate will find an easier entry into your life.

The second question was about feelings — whether true knowledge comes through the emotions rather than the intellect. Latwii's answer is one of the most useful in the archive. The emotions, they say, are a direct line to your preincarnative choices — the lessons you chose before this life began. When someone pushes your button and you react, that reaction shows you what you actually believe, underneath what you wish you believed.

So the emotions are a barometer — or, as they put it, a temperature gauge. They point to exactly what is in need of balancing.
