Work with the charge, refine it, and what remains when the coloration falls away is that quality known as love. Your feelings are not the enemy of your seeking. They are its instrumentation.

And the evening closed on a note of pure affirmation. Asked whether every living thing carries something indestructible, something eternal, Latwii answered: indeed it is so. There is one endowment — the endowment of love, with free will to know itself as it will. Each learns in a unique fashion. And all need not be the same, to be equal in will and faith.

Desire widely. Surrender completely. And trust the gauge. Thank you for listening.

title: Stewards of Consciousness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: stewards of consciousness.

The evening's teacher was a newcomer — an entity calling itself t'Michael'h, from what they describe as the inner planes of Earth itself: not the Confederation, but third-density beings, harvestable to fourth, who have made a study of polarity. The question before them was a small, human one. What is the point of bad moods?

Their answer begins with an image that reframes everything. A bad mood, they say, is the shutting of two doors — the door to positive polarity and the door to negative polarity both closed at once. Polarity, in their language, means accepting a job description: to serve others, or to serve the self. The bad mood is neither. It is self-employment — consciousness idling, swayed by crosscurrents, prey to every minor ill of the illusion.

It is not wrong, they are careful to say. It is not evil to be cranky or irritable or angry. It is a waste of potential. And the reason runs deeper than mood. The spiritual journey, they say, is a very expensive journey — one which, in metaphysical terms, none of you can afford. You cannot transform yourself from your own resources, because you do not own the thing you are trying to transform.

You are stewards of consciousness, they say. You do not own consciousness. That sentence stopped me cold, and I have been carrying it around for days. You are working for another — for consciousness itself, which some call love, or the Logos, or the one original Thought. Your salary is heightened perception, and the pain and peace of the road. And the secret of all effective seeking is surrender to your employer.

This surrender has two faces, they say. One is the higher self — the richer, more experienced you, benign and full of information, available the moment your consciousness empties itself of judgment and self-importance and asks to know and to serve. The other is grace — the kindness of the Creator, which offers to the one who surrenders the ability to manifest a greater will than its own.

So what do you actually do on a bad-mood day? Their counsel is refreshingly practical. Do not try to tighten the strings of your own perception with your own energy — the soul grows weary when it is out of tune, the way an unstrung instrument makes a poor sound. Distract yourself. Rest — and by rest they mean the sleep of one who lays down the burden of consciousness for a while. And when you are ready to pick it up again, use stimulation of a loving kind: read what inspires you, listen to music that calls to the highest in you, talk with others who lift you. If silent meditation will not come, do not force it. Let beauty do the starting.

As you seek, so shall you find — even when you feel anything but loving as you begin. Love, they say, is a perception away.

Later, Latwii answered questions — on the meaning of names, on whether there are truly accidents. Their answer on names stayed with me: there are no accidents. A name becomes the trigger that opens certain recognitions of ability and potential — and as you live, the name gathers your experience into itself, until it symbolizes everything you have chosen to become.

One question touched on an apparent healing of a sick infant. I want to be careful here: Latwii spoke of it entirely in the language of the soul — of love generated among those gathered around the child — and I will not translate that into a medical claim. The archive is not a clinic, and I will not present it as one.

You do not own your consciousness. It owns you. And it is, at this very moment, carrying you home. Thank you for listening.

title: The Season of Transformation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the season of transformation.

Q'uo began this evening by speaking to the diversity inside the circle — the many different seekers, one harmony — and to something every one of them had felt: the maddening irregularity of spiritual growth. You can seek with steady intensity for years, they say, and still be unable to rule the moments when transformation actually arrives.

Their image for this is the watchman. He patrols night after night, year after year — and only once, at the burglar's convenience, does he find what he has been ceaselessly seeking. You can choose to seek, and quicken the tempo of your evolution greatly. But you cannot schedule the breakthrough. The mists of illusion clear that extra amount only rarely, and unpredictably.

I find this strangely comforting, and I think they mean it to be. The seeker who takes his own spiritual temperature and is disgusted at the result — Q'uo knows that seeker intimately. Turn, they say, from criticism of the self to encouragement. If you are disappointed, be disappointed the way you would be with someone who made an error — and then affirm, positively, that next time you will choose differently. Wash the ill feeling out of the assessment, and feel your step grow lighter.

Focus instead, they say, on the one strong point every conscious seeker has: the love you have felt and found and wish to know more about. That love — whatever you call it — is truer than your other perceptions. Everything else is a shadow of a shadow. It is a distortion of what love created.

The questions that evening turned, wonderfully, to trees. Do they know when to drop their leaves? Do they feel it when you hug them? Q'uo's answer moves like sap. Trees are second-density beings, they say — earth, air, fire and water, grown into movement and form — and they move in rhythms: the sun, the turning of the planet, their north or south placement, and subtler rhythms underneath. All of creation moves in variations on a theme, cycling from receiving to giving, that each portion might gain experience and come to know itself.

And then Carla offered an analogy, and Q'uo confirmed it, and it is the heart of the evening for me. Perhaps, she said, the reason we sometimes cannot improve, no matter how we try, is that we are asking the tree to put out new leaves before it has shed the old ones. Yes, they said — in the basic sense, that is correct. The conscious mind tries to move faster than the feet can go. There is a season for the exercise of the will, and a season for the surrender of it, and the seeker's art is the balance between the two.

Do not force the season. Let the old leaves fall. The new ones know when to come.

There was one more thread I want to leave you with. Asked about the guides who plan our incarnations with us, Q'uo said something I keep turning over: if there is value in knowing your guides' names, the names will find you. But do not waste your energy hunting for them — for the guides consider themselves messengers, not the message. It is the service that deserves your attention, not the servant.

The tree does not hurry its spring. Neither, in the end, can you. Thank you for listening.

title: The Humble Iron
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the humble iron.

Hatonn's message this evening is disarmingly simple, and I think that is exactly the point. The seeker who decides to accelerate the journey, they say, gazes at his own consciousness and asks the great questions — who am I, what is consciousness — and learns, at last, that consciousness sprang from a creative force, and that force is love. All that you see, in whatever form, is made of a direct emanation of love.

But then comes the turn. Your lessons, they say, involve something beyond this simplicity — because you are not simple. You have built yourself a complex illusion, full of seemingly impossible problems, so that through meditation and contemplation you might discover the love lying, in all its simplicity, at the heart of every tangle.

And here is where it gets practical, and where I love them most. Forget your impressions of spirituality, they say. You will work best upon your spirituality by paying close attention to the very small things of daily life. Most entities, in most densities, are working for the most part upon themselves — and the self is met in the small hours of the ordinary day.

Listen to how they put it. The one who irons a shirt, praising it as part of the creation — dwells, in that moment, in the kingdom of the original Thought of love. The cook who praises the broth and smiles at the soapy dishes has garnered far more than good food and a clean kitchen: the consciousness of joy has entered the domicile and softened the neutrality of everyday things.

So they ask you to review the day — not as an audit, but as an inventory of attention. Each word said to another. Each gesture, each smile and frown, shared with another consciousness. What little angers pulled you into unconscious negativity? How much of the day was lost to confusion, anxiety, irritation, distraction? They know these questions cannot really be answered — concentration fails, intentions do not endure. But there is no penalty, metaphysically speaking, for the wasted moments. Each mistake teaches. Each misstep strengthens the future steps. And when you must rest, you simply put your foot on the path again at the end of it.

For the path does not go anywhere, they say. It is always with you — as near as your breath. You have only to calm the mind and feel the key turn in the door that opens your heart.

And meditate — some minutes each day, no matter what else the day holds. Silent meditation, they say, is the most efficient tool for seating the awareness of the Creator's love within you. Under your own power you run like batteries, and must be replaced by sleep. Meditation is finding the electrical cord. The power flows through you then, not from you — and you become radiant with something that is not your own effort.

Focus on the little things faithfully, and the large things will take care of themselves. The scale of your faithfulness does not matter. The faithfulness does.

Later, Latwii added a single image I want to leave with you. Asked whether the world still needs pyramids to balance the planet's energies, they said: each conscious seeker may now serve as a portable pyramid. In meditation, the heart does what the great stones once did.

Iron the shirt. Praise the broth. The kingdom is in the kitchen. Thank you for listening.

title: The High Mountain Cave
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the high mountain cave.

Q'uo began with an observation about the shape of the spiritual life: there are times when the waters seem dammed up, and you feel the need to guard what is precious — to conserve, to hold tight. Relationships. Possessions. Reputation. None of these are inappropriate in themselves, they say. But there is a function of your evolution that cannot be fulfilled while you are full. It requires you to be, to a significant extent, empty — and doing nothing.

Have you ever wondered, they ask, why so many seekers have turned to solitude, fasting, and silence? They are trying to empty themselves, to make room for the one spiritual function that matters most: turning the attention toward the perception of the infinite Creator. Polarization — the choosing of the path — needs space.

But here is what I appreciate about this teaching: they do not prescribe the cave. It is not necessary, they say, to give up your responsibilities. Many who have touched the consciousness of love can keep that relationship as the point of view from which they evaluate everything in the illusion — and that, they suggest, is the worthwhile process. It will intensify your experience, generating more catalyst for your heart to digest than meditation in a cave ever would.

The outer solitude rescues you from unawareness of the process, and so accelerates it. But the same acceleration is available in the world, if you can find the quiet moments. The high mountain cave, in the end, can be the cave of your own daily meditation.

I love the closing image of the discourse. Each of you, they say, is a holographic representation of the Creator — and herein lies your great and fundamental equality, for each of you is in all ways perfect. That is your reality. What you experience now is a dim perception of your true nature, and the whole journey is the slow refining of that perception, until you define yourself — and all others — in terms of love.

The questions that night were human and unguarded. One man asked whether his meditation counted, since he kept falling asleep in it. Q'uo's answer made me smile: yes, they said — you have opened a level of perception so soothing that you followed it into sleep, and the meditation continued there. As you learn to grasp those perceptions consciously, you will need the sleep state less and less. Nothing is wasted. Not even the naps.

Another asked how to inspire a loved one to begin seeking. Their answer: you cannot say what is appropriate for another's journey. Desire to be of aid, reflect the love you have found as purely as you can, give with an open and cheerful heart and no expectation of return — and let the seed grow in its own time.

Empty yourself a little each day. The cave is closer than you think. Thank you for listening.

title: All Are Instruments
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: all are instruments.

As October opened, the group did something different. Across eight evenings of intensive sittings, they set aside the usual Sunday circle to work with a new instrument — a woman known only as K, who had offered herself to learn the service of vocal channeling. Laitos, the entity who specializes in this work, was delighted. It is not often, they said, that we have the privilege of working with new instruments.

And then Laitos said something that widened the whole subject beyond the circle. In truth, they said, all are instruments. Each person channels from deeper and deeper portions of its own being, at various times in the life experience. The desire to serve as a vocal channel only tunes more finely a capacity everyone already has.

The new instrument's task is simpler than it looks, and harder than it sounds. Laitos describes the blend: roughly seventy percent their thoughts, thirty percent the instrument's own experience and phrasing. The contact arrives the way your own thoughts arrive — which is why every new instrument is convinced, at first, that she is making it all up. She is brave enough to speak anyway. That bravery, they say, is the whole of the art at the beginning.

Do not be surprised, they told the group, if our messages use your own experiences — recent or distant — in the telling. We ratify the validity of your own patterns of seeking, and use them. The teaching is never separate from the life of the one who carries it.

On the first night, K managed only the identification — I am Laitos — and then, on the second attempt, a few phrases of greeting. Laitos was, in their words, exceedingly overjoyed. A beginning is a beginning. The limb holds.

Laitos closed the first sitting with a practical instruction for every new instrument who will ever try this: speak only the thoughts that appear within your mind, as they appear, and trust that the blend will refine itself with practice. You are not performing, they said. You are opening. And an opening, however small, is enough.

Every one of us is an instrument, tuned by the desire to serve. The music is already playing. The only question is whether we will let it sound through us. Thank you for listening.

title: The Sacred Fool
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the sacred fool.

On the second evening of the intensive, the new instrument reached further out on the limb. K was now speaking short passages through the contact — and Laitos was frank about what that requires. It takes, they said, a combination of bravery and foolhardiness: to speak words that seem to exist in a vacuum, unconnected to others of their kind, with no assurance that the limb will hold your weight, or that the next words will come at all.

This is the heart of the vocal channeling process, they explained. The receiving mechanism of humankind is not built for dictation. No complete message arrives to be read off line by line. Instead, small portions of a larger message are given, each followed by another of roughly equal length, until the whole has been transmitted. The instrument must step forward without knowing the next step exists. Every act of service, they suggest, asks something of this same foolishness — the willingness to share what is in the heart without reservation, asking nothing in return, not even that it be accepted.

I love that Laitos does not dress this up. Within the illusion, they say, nothing may be known with certainty. The foundation of all creation is shrouded in mystery, hidden from all but the most persistent inward-seeking eye. The fool is simply the one who walks forward anyway.

The evening's questions turned practical. Carla described a psychic greeting — a negative presence that would not leave when challenged — and asked about the assumptions underneath her response: the love of the Christ, the hymn sung in the mind. Laitos would not judge her method, but offered the general principle. When you feel influences that oppose your free will, they said, the most helpful response is the one taken with the widest possible view: see all entities, thoughts, and experiences as portions of the one Creator, and bless and love them. Move to their heart, and join in love with them.

And then the image that stays with me: an entity that will not do this will find it necessary to remove its presence from the mirror — the mirror that reflects back to it the heart of love it has denied. You do not have to fight the darkness. You only have to become the mirror it cannot face.

The evening ended the way these evenings seem to end: with laughter, and with Laitos's trademark benediction, requested by name. Be sure to meditate every day, they said. Five minutes will suffice. Even five seconds.

Be the fool. Speak the words. The limb holds. Thank you for listening.

title: Drawn from the Depths
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: drawn from the depths.

On the third evening of the intensive, Carla brought Laitos a question about the book she was writing — not a book on the mechanics of channeling, she said, but on every aspect of it that might help those who want to channel and those who already do. Did they have any suggestions?

Laitos's answer pleased me, because it is true of far more than channeling. The process you are using to write this book, they said, is itself a process of channeling — and you are using the instrument's most valuable tool, which is the personal experience of the instrument itself. To speak on any topic, it helps to be familiar with it intellectually. But it is far better to have made such a close identification with it that you draw it from the depths of your own experience, and your responses to that experience.

Then the work takes on a life of its own, they said — dynamic, in motion within the author — and the words carry that life force to the reader, shared without reservation. That, in their experience, is the heart of any channeling process. I think it is the heart of any honest writing, too. The reader can always tell when the writer has lived what she is saying.

K, the new instrument, asked the question every beginner asks in some form: the contact feels tenuous and faint. Am I doing this right? How will I know when you are finished? Laitos's counsel was simple and has the ring of all good teaching about contemplative practice. Quiet the inner conversations, the over-nervousness, the doubts. Practice as if practicing scales on the piano — the concentrative muscle strengthens with exercise. And as for knowing when the transmission is done: we will tell you, they said. We will tell you when we are finished.

There was one more teaching I want to keep, on discernment. When a contact identifies itself, Laitos said, watch for what comes with the name: the sentiment of love, peace, joy, light, blessedness, close-bound to the greeting and the farewell. We do not wish to leave any with a name alone, they said, but with the name of that principle in whose service we come. If those concepts do not rise in your consciousness — challenge immediately.

Draw from your depths. Speak what you have lived. And check the name against the love. Thank you for listening.

title: The Faculty of Hope
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the faculty of hope.

The group had been reading the prophecies of Nostradamus, and they asked Q'uo to comment. What came back was not really about Nostradamus at all — it was about us, and what we do with prophecy, and with every other channeled or inspired text we encounter.

I want to be careful in how I frame this evening, because the territory is full of old predictions. I am going to stay with the teaching, not the forecasts. The forecasts belong to another decade; the teaching does not belong to any year.

Q'uo's first move is to hand the authority back to you. Regard the prophet, they say, as the same kind of instrument as the one speaking our words — a human being through whom something came, recorded as faithfully as he could. The information is yours to use for your spiritual progress, or to set aside. Prophecy may inspire one person and leave another cold, and both responses are legitimate. Take responsibility for what you assimilate. Digest it well — and excrete, without apology, what you do not find spiritually inspiring.

Then the deeper teaching. Begin, they say, with the original Thought — love — of which every portion of creation is a hologram. Each fragment contains the whole. That is why the patterns repeat at every scale: the atom mimics the solar system, and the death you will one day undergo is the subjective model, in miniature, of every ending the prophets describe. Your illusion is designed so that one day you will drop the body and take wing into a more light-filled one. Nothing is more crushing to the physical being, they say, and nothing more liberating.

And here is the sentence I carried out of the session: the search for truth is not a cold building up of facts, but a journey to the heart. As you live in your head, you die to the passion that can burn within you, to the joy that can leap from your heart at simple things. If prophecy is to be of any use, let it make you rejoice at what is to come — or pray, and offer yourself in dedication, for what may be sad.

They were asked, that night, about cataclysms and pole shifts and the fate of civilizations, and their answer kept returning to the same ground: the future is constantly formed and reformed by the choices of the living. No vision is the only potential. And the collective consciousness of humankind is the thermostat. As our choices grow more balanced, the fever recedes.

Which is why the evening ends, remarkably, on hope — not as wishful thinking, but as a faculty, a practice. There is, they say, a substantial reward for practicing hope and faith. Each time you send light to the Earth, the Earth changes. As you mold your consciousness, so in echo will your growth mold itself.

Read the prophecies if they help you ask better questions. Then put them down, and practice hope. Thank you for listening.

title: The Great Conspiracy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the great conspiracy.

As the intensive week wore on, the new instrument was no longer wondering whether the contact was real — she was feeling it. And the feeling frightened her. A confusion, she called it. An unsettledness. More nervous than before, and she did not understand why.

Laitos's reassurance is worth hearing slowly. This is natural, they said. You have become aware, intellectually and emotionally, that the process is actually occurring — that information is moving through you, and that you play only a minor part in it. Excitement and anxiety arrive together. Let them move through you the way the contact moves through you, without undue concern. Familiarity will do what argument cannot.

Then K named the deeper fear, the one Carla calls the great conspiracy: the suspicion that she is only saying things that come from her own head. Am I really vocalizing your thoughts, she asked, or only mine?

Listen to how honestly they answer. We play a part in causing that very suspicion, they said. To make contact through a new instrument, we deliberately use more of the instrument's own experience — her memories, her phrasing, the way she talks in daily life — so the contact can stay open long enough for confidence to build. The suspicion that it is all coming from you is built into the method. And yet, they assured her: you have been quite accurately representing our thoughts — in your own words, as it must be.

I find this deeply humane, and larger than channeling. Every genuine collaboration between the conscious mind and something deeper feels, at first, like talking to yourself. The doubt is not evidence of failure. It is the tax paid at the border between the known and the unknown.

Carla asked a question I have thought about since: why have you been stimulating me so strongly — all this conditioning energy, but no words? Laitos's answer: each instrument gets what it needs. With the experienced instrument, they were working at the deeper levels of the mind, sensitizing and stabilizing at once, preparing the way for word-by-word transmission. The energy you feel is not a malfunction. It is maintenance.

And the closing teaching, the one that gathers the whole week: the art of the vocal instrument is dynamic. The surrender of the personal will is ongoing — not achieved once, but renewed every time you open. Whether the service is channeling or healing or any other, the practice is the same: open a little more fully than you did yesterday, to the opportunities that come to anyone who seeks to serve.

Doubt the voice if you must. Then speak anyway. Thank you for listening.

title: The Village Cobbler
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the village cobbler.

One evening of the intensive, Laitos tried something new: a story, told a few sentences at a time through each instrument in turn, no order announced — so that everyone would get practice in perceiving the contact and daring to speak it. What came through was a small parable, and I want to give it to you whole.

Once upon a time there was a young man living in a distant land, in a small village with old and rigid customs, who wondered whether others anywhere thought as he thought. So he set out on a journey to see how others lived.

He walked twenty miles to a hidden village in a valley among the trees, and there he met an old man. For many days, under the bright sun and far into the moonlit night, the young man listened — his mind a sponge, his heart growing ever fuller with the love he perceived in his teacher. Until one day the old man would speak no more, and the young one knew he had learned all he could there. Sadly, he took his leave and walked on.

For three years he walked and asked, his questing mind ever refining its question. He always found someone. He always learned. He rested in the comfort of his own poverty and the ease of needing to impress no one but himself. And at the end of that time, he sat down to take stock of everything he had gathered.

As he sat, a bird flew past — and he understood. He could learn no more from teachers. His sojourn now would be within himself. He would learn to be his own teacher.

So he turned homeward — and it was a new journey and a new beginning. Back in his native village he learned a trade, the simple trade of making shoes, and in due time became the village cobbler: a quiet man, sought out by travelers, sharing what he had learned from others, but mostly what he had learned on the journey within himself.

And so the journey ended as it began. The young man had become old in his native village, living quietly. And yet he had also become what he sought — because he sought it. And so shall you, Laitos said, if you seek faithfully.

Then the teaching underneath the story, stated plainly. Desire, they said, is a vacuum created in your future — and what you desire is attracted into the empty space within yourself. So desire carefully, and steadily. Crown every question you ask — of others or of yourself — with the desire to know and serve the Creator. For your journey shall end according to the shape of your desire. And in that ending shall be your beginning.

The seeker goes out to find the teacher, and comes home to become one. Thank you for listening.

title: The Shelter of Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the shelter of light.

Near the end of the intensive, Laitos reflected on what had been built — not in a week, but over years. With each instrument, they said, there is a firm foundation: the desire to be of service to others. On that foundation, each has fashioned a unique structure, a channel through which contact can move. And in that uniqueness, they said, we take our joy — for through such individuality we are able to impress our message, which is always and ever the same.

Always the same message: the great original Thought, the thought of love, which binds all creation together. And the instrument's whole life — every joy and sadness, every success and failure — becomes the library we draw upon to say it. Your experience is not an obstacle to the message. It is the vocabulary.

Then, through the new instrument, came the passage I want you to hear. The structures you have built, Laitos said, may also function as a refuge — armories of light, protections you carry with you. And we urge you: do not fear to take refuge in the shelter when you feel it is needed. Rest is a good thing, and needful. It is not well to push yourselves beyond your limits.

To rest in the shelter you have built is not giving up, they said. It is not retiring from the journey. It is part of the process — and ignoring it is what creates the real obstacles. So be merry, be joyful. Do not concern yourself with great goals, or with keeping up. What you need will come to you. Take the experiences of your life as they come, and do not worry yourselves with pursuing them.

I love the gentleness of this. The spiritual life is so often sold as relentless striving — and here is Laitos, the teacher of discipline, saying: rest is part of the discipline. The shelter is not a detour from the path. It is one of the rooms of the house you built to walk it.

Latwii closed the evening in their own characteristic key: holy foolishness. It is a joy, they said, to work with an instrument so eager to be the fool — for we are also fools, and find great mirth in such foolishness. In this way of being, one may see the creation as a joyful unity, in which all may play any part they choose, and trade parts, and enlarge them, and discard them, as meaning moves them.

The play of each entity, they said, is what glorifies the Creator — because each moves as freely and as happily through the creation as foolishness allows.

Build the shelter. Rest in it when you need to. And play the fool gloriously. Thank you for listening.

title: The Other Torn Half
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the other torn half.

The last evening of the intensive was a quiet one — few questions, short contacts, the feeling of a week of work settling. But Laitos left two images that I have not been able to put down.

The first came as the group was closing. We can think of each other, they said, as the other torn half of a perfect shape. For each entity that you encounter is your other half. Each of you is a miniature of every group you belong to — your culture, your species, your archetypal souls — and finally, of the universe itself.

Is it any wonder, they asked, that you are all such good channels for each other? You share one universe in so many wondrously various facets that the picture seldom stales — and wonder is but an eye-blink away. Every person you meet is another facet of the same jewel, cut to catch a light you cannot catch alone.

The second image was a counsel, given for the new instrument but meant, I think, for all of us. Open the mind, they urged. Let down the armor. Become vulnerable and without fear, so that we may touch her mind with our own. And then the widening: each of you could use this frame of mind — that your mind may be touched by the thoughts and the hands of the Creator in every entity you meet.

The stranger is not an interruption in your day. The stranger is the other half of the shape, arriving with the piece you are missing.

And the closing words, through the new instrument who had come so far in a single week: we are all bound together by love in the service of the one Creator, for love is all that there is. It is what motivates us, and what enables us, and it is also the fruit — the reward, shall we say — of our efforts to serve.

The message is simple, they said, and yet there are many words to fill that simplicity. So we strive to share that simplicity with you in yet another way.

Let down the armor. The other half is reaching for you. Thank you for listening.

title: The Moment of Power
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the moment of power.

The intensive week was over, and the Sunday circle gathered again — with a new instrument among them, and Hatonn opening on a theme the whole week had been circling: silence. It is the silence that teaches, they said, perhaps more than even the most inspiring words — just as it is the space between objects that allows objects to have dimension.

Their counsel is not to visit silence, but to carry it. Bring it with you, they said, not only into the dark with your eyes closed, but into the harshest daylight, under the most trying conditions. If a portion of you remains in the silence of what is most precious to you, then all else is but a shadow moving across the sun at the center of your being — and no cloud is large enough to blot out the joy you may take in living.

It is difficult to love when one is busy, they said. Difficult to perceive the consciousness of the Creator when the hustle has you. And then the parable: imagine a king who could direct his kingdom any way he wished, and so wished — and one thing was added upon another, everything he had ever wanted, all manifesting. Wealthy, powerful — and at the end of it, not the ruler of his life but its servant, ministering unto his desires, trapped by his own snare. Your past desires have all come home to roost.

None of you who recognize this is alone in it, they said — it is the nature of your culture to distract you from the love and light of the Creator. The unseen values do not glitter in the hand. Pursued, they retreat. And yet: what others think of your seeking is irrelevant, and even your own estimate of your excellence is irrelevant. All that is needed is your seeking. That is your power, and your peace. It is your very identification — for you are what you desire.

May your desires, they said — and I love this image — flow from you in a clean and pure stream, glittering and bubbling, into the great ocean of all that there is.

Then Latwii took the evening's question — speak to me about living within the moment — and gave the teaching its other half. The present moment, they said, is the moment of power. Yes, you may turn your eyes backward to glean the lessons, and forward to prepare the harvest. But the moment is also complete within itself, needing no addition from past or future. Enter it undiluted, and the full potential of your being comes to bear: the boundaries of your thinking are offered the chance to expand.

The meditative state is the easiest door into this, they said — for there, with no coloration of past or future to filter it through, you may discover that the battery of your personal energy is fully charged at all times. And from that discovery you move back into the daily round inspired, better able to use what you have learned and to gather what each new moment offers.

Two smaller teachings from the questions, both worth keeping. On the emotional charges that cling to old memories: see the charge as one half of a full point of view. In meditation, magnify it — let the pendulum swing to its fullest arc — and watch it draw its opposite to equal strength. When you can hold both ends of the continuum and accept yourself for containing all of it, the charge has done its work. What remains is quiet acceptance — which is, in metaphysical terms, unconditional love.

And on the fear that a life can be wasted, that a mission can be missed: it is possible, they said honestly, to ignore what you placed in your own path. But nothing is wasted. The unbalanced patterns simply become the work of the next incarnation. And the momentum of your deeper choices keeps bringing the catalyst back around. It is a difficult task, they said, to ignore forever what you put there to find.

The silence. The moment. The stream. They are all the same teaching, spoken three ways. Thank you for listening.

title: The New Instrument
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the new instrument.

Tonight is a short evening, and a tender one. Laitos comes to work with a new instrument, the one the group calls K, and the whole session is practice, patience, and gratitude. Nothing grand is attempted. That is the point.

Laitos looks upon the vocal channeling type of service, they say, as one which offers increasing kinds and depths of service to all those with whom the process is ongoing. The deeper the instrument goes, the wider the service becomes. And there is a lovely detail tucked into the evening. The experienced instrument, the one called Jim, is serving as a kind of anchor for the new one, and Laitos notes that for those who are more experienced, helping a new instrument is itself a way of becoming a new instrument on another level. Nobody is finished learning. The teaching always finds a new beginner.

I love what Laitos chooses to talk about that night. Rather than offering grand and general information, they offer words useful to the people in the room, the ones learning to serve as vocal instruments themselves. These sessions, Laitos says, are set aside for developing the instruments who will later move into wider kinds of service, reaching a wider selection of peoples. The teaching bends itself to the room. The ones who have come to learn how to serve are served first.

There is a warmth in the way Laitos speaks of K. They are quite pleased, they say, with the progress this instrument has made, and glad of the chance she has had to work with other contacts besides their own. It is the tone of a teacher watching a student take her first steady steps, and not wanting to rush her.

The evening ends early, because part of the group is leaving to sing sacred music, to praise the Creator in song. Laitos is unhurried about it. They count it a privilege, they say, to serve in this manner, for there are many who are seeking, and the call is great, and they are appreciative of any additional means by which the call may be answered. Then a few final words through the new instrument, and a simple blessing. Be joyful, they say, and peace be with you.

A short session, then, but a clear window into how this work gets passed along. One instrument at a time. One act of service answering the next.

Thank you for listening.

title: Stilling the Mind
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: stilling the mind.

The night before, Laitos worked briefly with the new instrument, the one the group calls K. Tonight they are back, and the whole evening becomes a master class in the art of vocal channeling. It is practical, patient, and surprisingly tender.

The first lesson is about the challenging of entities, and Laitos is firm about it. The contact the night before had been less than perfect in strength, and they tell K plainly: it is never as important to speak as it is to assure yourself of a strong contact. If the energies feel uneven, ask mentally that they be regularized, and that the identity be given in a stronger and more stable way. Speaking can wait. Certainty cannot.

The second lesson is about K's own mind. She is analytical by habit, and the thoughts keep bouncing. Laitos finds no fault in this. It is inevitable, they say, given her habitual method of reasoning, and it will be hers to manage no matter how experienced she becomes. I love how they frame it: not as a flaw, but as a challenge that can be turned to good use, for if one knows one's challenges, one may properly meet them.

Then comes the part I find most beautiful. Laitos tells K that she should expect to recognize their presence not only by the call, but by a certain feeling, a comfort or sweetness that pervades what they call the inner seat of compassion, when mind and body and spirit greet a loved acquaintance. Her sensitivity, they say, is circuited through the emotions, and it is in the emotional area that she should look for their conditioning. If there is not a certain comfort in the call, ask for it mentally, so you may know the contact is real, a contact of compassion and love, of spiritual truth and of peace.

And when the contact wavered the night before, Laitos has a gentle diagnosis. It was a matter, they tell her, of having one foot in the door, and one on the porch. I have never heard the divided mind described more kindly.

The practical counsel follows. As you enter the meditative state, the day's activities come with you, the conversations, the thoughts, and they tend to remain unless you set them aside. Even pleasant feelings can filter and hinder the contact if they stay in the conscious mind. So the vocal instrument must place the desire to be of service at the fore, and focus attention as cleanly as possible.

K asks the question every beginner asks. She cannot seem to ignore the thoughts bouncing around her head. What can she do? Laitos answers that there are many techniques peoples have devised for stilling the mind, and any of them may help. But do not be overly concerned with the technique, they say. It is the desire to be of service, and the desire to focus attention, that matters most. The thoughts moving through the mind are a kind of momentum built up during the daily round of activities. It can help to spend time in silent meditation before any channeling is attempted, to let that momentum run down. This is an exercise, they say, in which one does less and less in order to gain proficiency.

Then Laitos widens the lens. The process of serving as a vocal channel is continually surprising, they say. The instrument who has practiced for a long time begins to gain confidence, and that confidence at once assists further progress and can inhibit it, if it does not allow for the dynamic nature of the art. So expect what seem to be anomalies. Do not be overly concerned that something is wrong. Look upon each situation as something that can teach further lessons, for what they have offered any instrument on any evening is only a portion of what is possible. Indeed, they say, there is no end to what is possible to offer when serving as a vocal instrument.

The evening closes with reassurance, spoken through the more experienced instrument. These wobbles are inevitable stages. Perhaps, Laitos suggests, the new instrument might recover at least half of the former fearlessness that made her progress so swift. And if the contact pauses while the energies regularize, that is no cause for criticism, from them or from those she will serve. Who would wish a channel to speak, they ask, when the contact has not offered any food for thought?

A whole evening on how to listen well. The technique matters less than the desire. The certainty matters more than the speaking. And the sweetness, when it comes, is how you know you are home.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Daily Conditioning
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the daily conditioning.

Three nights running now, Laitos has worked with the new instrument, K. Tonight is the last of the three, and the tone has shifted from training to parting counsel. Laitos is pleased with her progress, and now the question is what she should do when she is on her own.

The ideal, Laitos says, is for a new instrument to have periodic exercise in the presence of an experienced instrument, so that the small and sometimes medium-sized difficulties of the practice can receive the attention of experience, and a sure hand at the right time. This is the arrangement they endorse whenever it is possible.

K, they feel, has come far enough that she could practice in a carefully guarded situation even without the more experienced instrument present. But the guarding matters. Laitos describes it plainly: at least two other entities, in stable harmony with her, who feel an open-hearted acceptance of this kind of information and this means of its transmission. And they are honest that such a grouping is not easily obtained. The vagaries of the seeker's path make gathering it somewhat difficult.

If that stable circle is not available, there is still work she can do, and I love the simplicity of it. Not the vocalizing of contact, but a daily period of silent meditation, during which she may mentally request their conditioning vibration. No words transmitted. Only the recognition of the contact, and the familiar feeling of it, refined day by day. A relationship kept warm in silence.

It is a modest proposal, and that is its beauty. The grand work of channeling is set aside, and in its place a quiet daily appointment: sit, request the vibration, notice it, let it become familiar. The instrument is tuned the way an ear is tuned, by listening.

Even with all of this, Laitos adds one more recommendation: that she avail herself of periodic contact with this particular group, to reinforce the basic principles she has gained, and to bring her questions. For as the practice continues, new experiences arise, and there is often confusion in the mind of the new instrument as to the most appropriate means of resolving each one, whether it is simply new and untested, or a difficulty of some kind.

Then the tape ends, mid-counsel, and the evening with it. Three nights of training close the way they began: with gratitude for the privilege of the work, and confidence in the student.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Shadow of Compassion
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the shadow of compassion.

A seeker asks Q'uo about enlightenment, and how to attain it. Q'uo begins by turning the question inside out. Enlightenment, they say, can only be seen by its reflection. It is the creature and manifestation of the thought of love which an entity has made its own. So let us turn, they suggest, from the manifestation to the essence. The real question is how to achieve communion in the unity of consciousness and love.

Their answer starts where so many of their answers start: with meditation. Meditation, they say, introduces you to yourself. You may not like what you see. You may discover many, many thoughts, thoughts that do not stop, thoughts you do not control. You may find your body ill-suited to sitting still. And yet, they say, even if all you discover, over and over, is that you are dissatisfied with your meditations, the intent that sits you in the chair and puts you in the kingdom of silence is fulfilling completely its part in your development. It is not only intent, but intent carried through with even and steadfast perseverance, that creates personal power.

I love that line. The bad meditation counts. The sitting down is the whole of it.

Once you have meditated long enough to perceive yourself differently, outward changes follow. Contact with the essence of love causes a continuing shift in the point of view, and the way you evaluate things becomes regularized toward valuing what serves others. But the road there is not smooth. You will find many wars going on within yourself, they say, and it is as though everything you knew methodically becomes torn away. Things fall apart. If this does not happen to you in at least a small way, they suggest, meditate a little longer, or a little more regularly. Perhaps you have a high tolerance for the illusion, and to awaken from it may take a little more.

Someone asks whether this transformation can feel like deep depression at times, and Q'uo answers with an image. They bring to mind the elephant perceived by the blind man, each portion seeming different from the others, yet each a portion of one entity. The journey moves through mountains and valleys, across deserts and through jungles. At one point the seeker is lifted high into light. At another the seeker must move through the valley of the shadow, and it seems the totality of experience. Each extreme, and all points between, are portions of one journey.

If you are moving through a dark valley of your own, please hear this part gently, and be kind to yourself as you go. Reach for the people around you, and for whatever professional support you need. The archive is a companion for reflection, not a substitute for care.

And then the sentence this whole evening seems to have been walking toward. Never suspect, Q'uo says, that enlightenment benefits the enlightened one. Enlightened entities, for the most part, work very hard, and do not consider themselves enlightened. No, enlightenment is for the benefit of lightening others' weary loads, lifting other people's spirits with an enlightened smile or a few soft words. Seek the essence of compassion. Seek the Creator which is all truth and all love. Enlightenment will be your harvest.

Your perception of enlightenment, they say, is the shadow of the reality of compassion. I keep turning that phrase over. The light you see is not the thing. The thing is what the light lets you do for someone else.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Sea of Eternity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the sea of eternity.

This is a special meditation, and Q'uo begins it unusually. They pause, they say, to move in the stream of time and blend their vibrations with the group's, so that they may speak not only inspiring words, but words needful to the people actually in the room. Then they take up the subject on everyone's mind: meditation, and what the mind is.

The rational mind, Q'uo says, is a calculator, and it calculates many things very well. Your race has built many beautiful artifacts with it. And yet, in all the complexity of the creation of man, there is no ultimate truth. All rational inquiry has ended thus far in mystery. The clear thinkers, the scientists, turn finally to appreciation, even adoration, of the mystery which unifies all phenomena, never convinced there is not an ultimate answer, but aware it has not yet been found.

Consciousness is not only rational. And it is in using the rational mind alone, or the subconscious mind alone, that knowledge has become fragmented and incomplete. The deeper mind, the part your peoples shrug off as the province of fools and dreamers, functions with precision and elegance. You know this from your own life: the times you knew through intuition or hunch, because you saw it in a dream, or just knew it to be so, what would occur before it did. Without intending to, you have used the deeper powers of your mind. Yet there is far more improvement possible through meditation.

Then Q'uo offers the sentence everything else hangs from. There is one consciousness, they suggest, which in its original and undistorted form may be called love. The consciousness of love is the great original Thought, crystal clear and pure, and by its profound, generative nature, the Creator of all that there is. Your identity, your nature, is some distortion, one representation, of that one great original Thought.

When the conscious mind is used without the aid of the deeper mind, very little of the consciousness of love can be channeled through you. The person who lives in mind and not in heart lives a dry and arid life, unrelieved by the beauty of love or the joy of passion. It is those with a passion and joy for knowing the truth, for celebrating friendship, for seeking love, who create the full potential of consciousness.

And here is the image I cannot shake. When you move from the conscious mind into the deep mind, you are moving from busyness and noise, distraction and sleep, to a cool, clear pool of light, silent, profound and infinite. Infinity cannot be comprehended by the rational mind, for the mind calculates only the calculable, leaving mystery uncalculated. The deep mind is at home in the endless sea of infinity, for in infinity it has its home, just as you have your home in infinity.

If you feel unworthy to meditate, Q'uo says, release it. All entities make errors in judgment. Go into meditation having released your previous perceptions of yourself, your faults and weaknesses, focusing only on what you desire: knowledge of the truth. Turn regularly, daily if possible, from the wrangling of the conscious mind, long enough to swim in the sea of eternity, so that you may cleanse yourself of dailyness and emerge clear and clean, resting in infinity, bathed in the love and light of the infinite Creator.

They close as brothers and sisters, not authorities, asking you to take what rings true and forget the rest. And with one last urging, the simplest of all. Love each other. Care for each other. Experience the Creator in every face you meet.

Thank you for listening.

title: Wisdom Born of Suffering
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: wisdom born of suffering.

Q'uo opens this evening with a sentence that stops me cold every time I read it. Wisdom, they say, is born of suffering, dilemma, contradiction and pain. The happy times you experience within the illusion are useful as randomly as the difficult times, and the intrinsic value of happiness is quite low. It is not cruelty. It is an observation about how attention works.

No experience, they say, has a great deal of value except as part of a very large base of information from which the deeper mind may begin to draw intuitive conclusions about the way things are not. You consider yourself a fairly stable personality, a kind of business to be managed, so much of this and so much of that, and behold, a well-managed metaphysical path. Q'uo is gently dismantling that picture. You seek to create a life, they say. Do you know that you cannot help create life, or that the enormous bulk of what you create was created before you got your rational hands on it?

Then the passage I find strangest and most compelling. You move in a maze, they say, working not on understanding but on prejudice. You are seeking to be prejudiced against happiness and for suffering, against comfort and for discomfort, against peace of mind and for humble and disquieted thought. You are seeking to tie a knot so complex that it becomes unity, moving through complexity and dissolving. You are seeking the mystery you name but cannot describe, and the doors to the mystery open most fruitfully when the attention is heightened, focused and intensified by loneliness, discomfort and suffering.

Would that we could teach those within an illusion, Q'uo says, to pay sufficient attention while peaceful and happy, for then discomfort and pain would have no spiritual use whatsoever. These, they say, are the two by fours applied to your foreheads by your higher selves, in a loving effort to get your attention. I laugh every time, and then I stop laughing, because I know exactly what they mean.

Why is it, they ask, that at noon you think about what you will do from noon until one, and at one you think about the afternoon, and you never think to yourself, I wish to take this time out of time, I wish to take this moment with utter seriousness? Why do you skate on the pond of your life, never plunging into the icy waters that protect sleepers from wake ones?

Things are simple, as our message always is, they say. You may put on light. You may put on love. You may put on commitment. You may put on honest doubt. In all of these ways you are declaring that your element is wakefulness, and that your goals are not surface, not sleep-ridden, but further into the light, further into life, further into that which is conscious. For there is that within each life which is conscious, but hides beneath the waters, and the waters hide beneath the ice.

Someone asks Q'uo to say it again more simply, and they oblige with an image. All you perceive is illusion, and the good and the bad together form the mountains and valleys of the terrain of your life. It is not from reading about such terrain that one learns to navigate it. One must travel it, moving between the peaks and the valleys, remaining in various locations for a time, in order to grasp the effect upon one's thinking of residing there. Only by traveling it can you fashion what is truly born of wisdom, and arrive at a loving acceptance of all that you experience.

And doubt not that you have attained, they add, but continue to doubt that you know what you have attained. For that which you seek is truly born of mystery, and will continue to attract your seeking. In time you will see with clearer eyes. Within the illusion, you must content yourself with continuing the journey toward mystery, and accept that you do not know what you do or how to do it, but that you wish to do that which will make the mystery move within your life in the pattern that may only be described as love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Beware of Answers
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: beware of answers.

Q'uo begins this Sunday evening with a warning that sounds like a riddle. We ask you plainly, they say, to beware of answers, and to focus upon questions. For as you seek and seek again, so shall the doors of your own consciousness open to you, and you shall carry understanding deep within your heart, not to communicate except clumsily and incompletely, but only to manifest in your smile, your laughter, and the light of joy which you share with those about you.

There is no information so complete and so satisfying that it constitutes the ultimate answer, they say, for if it can be said, it is not the truth, and he who says it has pride, not understanding. The answers lie within you, not within us.

What you are after, they suggest, is a kind of simplicity that is not in fashion. A simplicity that is not dogma, not doctrine, not complex. Your civilization assumes that a spiritual body of knowledge will be complex and articulate, like a detailed list of directions for putting together an enlightenment kit. And yet the instruction booklets, affectionately regarded, need to be viewed with misgiving too, because there is not an intellectually acceptable set of instructions for constructing enlightenment.

Then Q'uo gives the image at the heart of the evening, and it is worth slowing down for. Each of you, they say, falls headlong into a blazing white light, the white light of an infinite Creator whose very nature is love. You are falling unbelievably quickly, and you shall fuse and become one in your perception, as you already are in reality, with love itself. This is your destiny. And yet none of you knows how quickly spiritual gravity pulls you toward that great center. Each of you feels you cannot possibly be moving quickly enough, you need to know more, and so you draw yourself along. Yet in reality, you could not hold yourself back if you tried.

So what do you actually do? You stoke the fire of your desire. Lift your spirits from the dust of dailyness, they say, and move until you are far, far from town or country or planet, until you feel that you are indeed falling, and gaze at the white light toward which you fall. Glory is yours now, if you can but release the demand to know, to understand, and to judge, and replace the desire to catalog with the desire to feel, with head and heart in unison, the light and the love that does not speak in words.

If you have a longing, a yearning for the presence of the Creator, and if you allow that longing to persist and to grow, if you encourage that desire, in study and meditation, mind and heart both exercised, then shall that longing deliver you into the very presence you seek. Expect it, they say. Look for it. And when the moment comes that you feel you have been given something you cannot describe or name, rejoice, and let that go too.

The questions that evening turn personal. Someone wrestling with self-love asks for illumination, and Q'uo answers that as you find qualities in yourself and your environment that you can accept more and more freely, you are accepting further portions of the self. There is really nothing but the self, small or great, which comes before your attention, and upon which you may work.

Someone else asks about the blocks he keeps hitting in learning to channel, and Q'uo suggests embracing the seeming blockage as an obvious opportunity, a riddle which, moved about within the mind and seen from various perspectives, begins to unfold itself when you have learned to cherish the difficulty and penetrate the outer illusion. I love that counsel. Cherish the difficulty first. Understanding follows.

And on why different channeled entities teach so differently, Q'uo offers a final image. Each portion of the Creator moves, likened unto a planetary body, about a great central sun of truth. The sun shines equally upon each, yet each, from a unique point of view, sees that sun and is warmed by it according to the position from which it orbits. So each teacher offers the fruit of its own journey, the one mystery seen from one more angle.

Beware of answers, then. Tend the questions. The longing itself is the delivery.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mated Pair
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mated pair.

The question put to Q'uo this evening is a hard one. What do you say to people who are considering a divorce, ending a commitment? And Q'uo answers with unusual care, asking most especially for each seeker's discrimination, because they would not wish anyone to act as they think they ought, but as they feel. Take what follows, they say, as food for thought, not as instruction.

Their frame of reference is not the legal custom but the metaphysical function. The purpose of the mated pair, they say, is increased efficiency in the gaining of catalyst, fellow aid in the processing of catalyst into experience, and the supplying of a yokefellow for whatever service you have created for yourself, for polarizing within your incarnation. In plainer words: two people join so that each may learn faster, help the other digest what life serves up, and pull together on the same rope.

And here is the turn that will either offend you or rearrange you. Almost never, Q'uo says, is suffering, hardship and trouble used as the reason for choosing a future partner. And yet this is the precise experience you wish to share, for your illusion is created in order that you may suffer and learn. Self-consciousness must be awakened, and happiness and contentment do little to awaken the soul. It is the interactions with others that bring grief, suffering, loss and trauma which create the opportunities you most cherished before the incarnation.

Thus, they suggest, it is well to choose the mate you want to suffer with, and the mate you feel will pull as strongly as you do to carry equally the burden of illusion. Certainly choose in love. But do not mistake the red-ray pull of the body, or the quiet arithmetic of benefit, for the deeper choice. Those motives are service-to-self in orientation, and they will lead to exactly the kind of catalyst each actually entered the relationship to meet, only now it will be met as an unacceptable inconvenience, something to be shrugged off as if the relationship were a piece of clothing that could be shed.

What, then, is one to do inside the difficulty? Q'uo's answer is unsparing and, I think, strangely hopeful. The only sphere in which any entity has power is the sphere of himself. True power is power over the self. If you see anything except the face of love, you are having difficulties with perception. It is well to persevere at all times with only one question, and as always that question is, where is love?

And the one who believes that by changing the situation he will change his experience is following a false belief, they say. When a lesson is declined by moving out of a situation, the same lesson shall be presented again, made clearer so there is less chance of misunderstanding, which in the language of the illusion means more painful, and longer to work out. The one who walks away is buying time, but not changing the catalyst.

Yet listen to how gently they speak to those who have already left, or been left. There is no sin in moving from a situation, they say. It buys trouble, yet with the wisdom of survival you have chosen to heal, so that you may throw yourself once more into your catalyst with a new zeal. If you have been left and find yourself acting in ways demeaning to your mate or yourself, take hold of your will and your powers of love, for if you have not been tested again, you shall be. Next time, offer your love back to the situation. Forgive and forgive again. Forgive yourself. Forgive any who seem to have hurt you.

Someone asks about unconditional love, whether it is the true love we are supposed to feel for everyone, even the people at work, and how to do it without seeming strange. Q'uo answers that love is not an emotion but a consciousness. How you express it depends on your emotional makeup. Whether you feel it does not. To work with each day's experiences and attempt to find love in each moment is the means by which such love is found, and as it is found, it will find its own level and means of expression, as natural as drawing one breath after another.

We do not speak of right or wrong, Q'uo says near the end. We speak of love. And love has the power of infinity, while the version we try to generate on our own is finite, and will die away, as all finite things do. The invitation is to let the infinite kind move through.

Thank you for listening.

title: Present Joy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: present joy.

The question this evening is one of the largest ever put to Q'uo. How can I better utilize my being? And Q'uo answers, in effect, by asking what beingness is for.

Beneath thinking, doing, and intention lies beingness, or consciousness. When you can surprise yourself in a state of unthinking beingness, they say, you have the evanescent glimpse of the face of the Creator, for each of you is in the basic consciousness a holograph of all that there is. And the word they use for that consciousness, the way they use the word Creator, is love. Not the pale emotional sense of the word, but a fiery, creative love, far more primal. The closest your language comes, they suggest, is the Logos of your holy works: the Thought that created all that there is.

Now what shall you use this consciousness for? Within the illusion you choose your state of consciousness by what can be done, so you choose to be awake when there are things to do. But consciousness, Q'uo says, is not measured in conclusions drawn or actions taken. There is a kind of awakeness that is the proper goal, and that is the state of present joy. For the consciousness of creative love, the consciousness of the Logos, is ecstasy.

They reach for the strongest words they can find. The Logos, they say, is orgasmically joyful, and that is its steady state. I include the phrase because it is theirs, startling and deliberate. They do not mean that pleasure-seeking is the path. They mean that the nature of love itself is a joy beyond expression, and that joy is the ground note of everything.

You cannot systematically decide to be joyful and have it be so, they warn. The approach to joy moves through a humbling sequence. The seeker becomes confident through meditation that he has grasped the nature of seeking. Then comes a lack of openness to change, then discomfort, then the painful consideration of further refinements, and finally a bafflement deep enough to cause the seeker to surrender the quest and leave the understanding of it in the hands of the Creator. The most efficient use of being, they say, is the surrender of that being to the higher will of the greater self, the greater being, the greater love, so that what the seeker does is channeled through the seeker from an infinite source of compassion and creative love.

Move slowly, they counsel, and turn always to meditation, for it is within the silence of your own being that you shall contact the source that lies deepest and truest within the universe that is your own being. First discover for yourself the nature of your journey, and a great enough respect for your own being and for the Creator that you place your being and the Creator's together.

The questions that night range widely, and I will carry only two answers forward. Asked about the higher self, Q'uo says guidance is offered where possible, but the free will of the conscious entity is paramount. The higher self, with your agreement before the incarnation, lays out the possibilities like a roadmap, and the incarnation is where that predetermined direction meets the free will you exercise within it. There are points where the higher self can guide and even protect, most often when the seeker calls for assistance by rededicating itself to service and surrendering the conscious will so that a greater will may move through.

And asked whether any soul is ever lost, Q'uo answers with plain finality. In our range of knowledge, which is admittedly limited, they say, we are aware of no soul which has been lost to the point of being unable to be found or redeemed.

The best use of being, then: a persistent attempt to approach a natural state of present joy. Not the joy you manufacture, but the joy you surrender into, the steady state underneath everything, waiting for you to stop striving long enough to feel it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Now Is Harvest Time
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: now is harvest time.

The group asks about the harvest, and Q'uo begins by confessing the limits of the subject. We are not without error, they say, but are as you, seeking upon a path which takes us into mystery, and when we understand what we did not understand before, then we find a greater mystery. How could we be infallible, we who are your brothers and sisters? Take what is useful. Leave the rest without a second thought.

The subject, they say, is really two subjects, and they will treat them separately: the physical changes of the planet, and the harvest in the metaphysical sense. On the first, they are brief. Your Earth has moved into an area of space which is fourth density in vibration, and there may be geological disruption and confusion of weather as the planet adjusts. But this, they say, does not have significance insofar as your soul's harvest is concerned. We of the Confederation are concerned with the harvest of your spirits, your mind, body and spirit in their most unified and true form.

Your physical bodies, they add, shall not all be removed in a trice, for harvest is a process rather than an event. Your incarnations, and your children's incarnations, shall move to their conclusion in the physical sense, in the ordinary way of things. The harvest of consciousness goes on underneath, at its own pace.

How do you prepare to be, they ask, when you are being at all times? There is no preparation possible, and yet there is everything to do. Take yourselves seriously as beings, they urge, that you may be more and more conscious of the value of your basic vibratory patterns. For it is your consciousness which shall be harvested: the consciousness that has striven and learned and borne fruit, the fruit of adoration and service and giving to the Creator, and to the face of the Creator in all that there is.

The concept of an instantaneous harvest has not been helpful, they have observed, and they discourage it. To us, they say, your harvest looks like an afternoon's excitement, a cause for rejoicing all too short, but we cannot translate our time to yours. How greatly you desire to know when you should be ready. And yet we say to you, it is this moment that you must be prepared, and that you must be ready. If you be not ready now, then you must work now, pray now, meditate now, surrender now, and ask now to be channels for the love and light of the one original Thought.

Then the image that carries the evening. Each of you moves through your days meeting one entity after another, and it is unknown to you in advance whom you shall meet. Yet that entity may be desperately looking for love, not the love of the glad hand and the pat on the back, but the total and accepting love of compassion, the love without judgment, the love that flows through rather than from each of you. You may have only one moment to be a channel of love for the infinite Creator, to show the Creator's face to this entity. One moment, my friends, no more. Shall you be a channel for love, then?

And if there is a moment when you are not, go into mind and heart, they say, and search out what kept you from it, and do your utmost to bring your consciousness to the consciousness of love. You do not know when your harvest shall come. Rest your anxieties about the future, a future which may never come, and gaze instead upon your being, that you may channel love now.

There is the parable, too, of the maidens who await the bridegroom, who watch and pray and trim their lamps. Some think they have a little time before the stroke of midnight. Yet midnight comes, and the lamp, the light, the love, has not been lit. Prepare, Q'uo says, as though the bridegroom knocked upon your door this minute, this hour, this night.

Above all things, love each other, they close, for you shall feel love only as you love others, only as you truly love yourself. Not what you see about yourself, but that which is beingness in yourself and others, perfected and whole, without flaw. You are acceptable to the Creator, for you are the Creator. Each of you carries the creation within consciousness.

Now is your harvest time. Now is when you shall be ready.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mystery of Union
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mystery of union.

It is mid-December, and the group asks about the season: the birth of Christ, the life of Christ, what he had to teach. Q'uo answers carefully, aware the subject is central to some present, wishing their words to be neither stumbling blocks nor paths into an unproductive wilderness. And they begin with a sentence worth sitting with. The nature of Christ, they say, is mystery, not because there was an intention to be mysterious, but because mystery is what Christ is.

The entity known as Jehoshua, whom the Greeks called Jesus, was born, they say, closely upon the heels of midsummer, a few years before the year your histories suggest. The birth was humble, brightened by an unusual configuration in the heavens that made it appear, for some months, that an unusually bright cluster of light hung in the night sky. The astrologer kings did journey following the star, though their arrival was about a year and a half later. That, Q'uo says, is a spiritual adventure you would do well to ponder, as you approach your own stable looking for the newborn, guided by hope, the brightest star of your being.

The entity Jesus was loved and loved in return, but his mind drove him to be alone, for though too young to have settled the nature of his being, he had a tremendous hunger for wisdom. You would call him a child prodigy. He taught many more things than are written, and what is recorded is typical enough of the teaching's content that Q'uo does not choose to adjust it.

Then they speak of the Christ itself, and here the language grows careful and strange. The concept of the Christ was this: that intelligent infinity, as experienced by the Logos, would enter a third-density experience, not erasing the personality of the one known as Jesus, but coming into the closest possible harmony with that being. There needed to be one who wished to sacrifice an incarnation to the ever-increasing pleasure and agony of the Creator. Such is the sorrow of your illusion, and the joy of sensation and communion.

In the end, Jesus the man became so able to bear both joy and agony that this entity stopped experiencing the Creator and for long periods of time became the Creator experiencing third density. Such, Q'uo says, is the perfect channeling of love. The achievement of the perfect channeling was the mystery of union between Creator and illusion. At the crucifixion there were almost no tears left, no bones unbroken, no companionship that had not been betrayed in one form or another. Nevertheless, Jesus the Christ lived well, and did not stop the channeling until the breath left the physical vehicle.

And what would Jesus think of the way your people celebrate Christmas? He is pleased, Q'uo says. He is pleased at all that is given and received of love, generosity and cheerfulness. He never confused the personal life he lived with the Christ he channeled, but always knew the source and called it the Father. The Creator is pleased that those who celebrate mark the spiritual advent of light into darkness. And that same Creator will celebrate the same event on another level in each of your lives, whatever your season may be, whenever your star beckons.

For the season is also a ritual of renewal, and it belongs to everyone. Within each seeker there comes a time when activity ceases and attention turns inward, when trials test what has been learned, and through sacrifice and surrender comes the possibility of a new seeding of awareness. Each entity that takes part in the celebrations in the name of the Christed Jesus partakes in some fashion of this ritual, the resurrection of the Christed consciousness within the self.

The evening's final question draws out the mystery at the center of it all. The seeker, Q'uo says, places itself in receptivity to the truth by the intensity of its seeking, the strength of faith and will, so that at some point it is possible for such a seeker to not only discover that which it seeks, but to become that which it seeks. Thus is the meaning of the resurrection within third density. The pure and virgin consciousness of the one Creator moves to gain the experience of the creation within the life pattern of beings who have prepared a place for it, and thus they not only receive what was sought, but become what was sought.

Not only find it. Become it. That is the mystery of union, and Q'uo leaves it exactly where it belongs: beyond explanation, inside the seeking.
