Within meditation, they said, time itself may be stopped within the consciousness of the deep mind, and in that moment of timelessness, that within you which is real beholds the mystery face to face.

What matters it if the face of mystery is dark, they asked, and the mystery only deepens as one spends more time in communion with the absolute? The dark is not the absence of the answer. The dark is the answer, still unfolding.

The practice of timelessness begins, after many repetitions, to unfold for the seeker an unlimited point of view. A point of view that sees the mundane limitations and necessities of everyday life, yet dwells as a native in that kingdom where love abides without the mask of illusion. You keep paying the bills. You keep feeding the body. But you do it as someone who has visited the kingdom, and the visit changes the doing.

Then came the teaching that gives this episode its heartbeat. Each of you has gifts to give, Q'uo said, things planned before incarnation in service of the one infinite Creator. And the very first of those things which each seeking soul hopes to do, while in the manifestation of human consciousness, is to become a channel for love. That others, trapped in the mire of earthly time, may have their despair turned to hope by seeing and sensing what they cannot explain: that light within your eyes which speaks of a happy and sweet union with infinite love.

The light within your eyes. Not your arguments, not your achievements. The look on your face after you have spent time in the presence of the mystery. That is the first service, and it cannot be faked.

And here is the paradox they closed with, one worth carrying. When you seek to advance in knowledge of the Creator, the progress of that seeking is marked not so much by one's own realizations, but by the degree of generosity with which those moments of companionship with the divine have been shared in the life experience with others.

Your progress is measured by your generosity. Not by what you saw, but by what you gave away of the seeing.

So they urged this: not only to meditate each day, but to choose moments within the busiest of your hours wherein you sink into the verticality of timelessness for one instant, and see that each entity and thing which you behold is beautiful, perfect and lovely. The call of a bird. The striking of a clock. A glance exchanged with a fellow seeker. Within the everyday life there is no moment which does not contain the possibility of this union.

One instant. That is all it takes to step out of the river and into the depth. Try it today, in the middle of the busy time. Sink, look, and rise.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Purpose Is Joy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the purpose is joy.

This session is a story, and it asks the oldest question there is. What is the purpose of life? Hatonn told it round-robin, through several voices, and I will tell it straight through.

There was a young teacher named Jamie, who wished greatly to offer his services to children. But Jamie had been very ill throughout childhood, had never been able to attend classes or receive degrees, could not move about with ease, and was told that for all but four hours of each day he must rest quietly.

And so, under these conditions, Jamie educated himself. He read his many books. He sought conversation with those more learned than he. And he began to impart what he learned to others, many of them younger, who came to his home during the short hours each day when he could teach.

One evening a student asked him, what is the purpose of life? Jamie set down his books and reflected. Perhaps life is a struggle, he said to himself. How he struggled through his hours of rest, chafing with impatience until he could rise and be with people again. He pondered long, and could see many possibilities: service, struggle, adventure, the completing of some larger plan, perhaps even random chance.

Years went by. The students came and went, and came to know him as knowledgeable, and as kind, compassionate and patient. That is, wise. And still the question worked in him like a stone in a shoe. An angel of light appeared to him in vision and asked, what is the purpose of your life? Jamie said, I can guess. It is to be of service. Perhaps that is an important part of it, said the angel, and left him to ponder again.

After many sleepless nights, Jamie's inward eye seemed to open. He saw light whirling and swirling in infinitely various patterns, and his own skin leapt and rejoiced, for he had been given the vision of the purpose of life. And when the angel came again and asked, Jamie smiled. The purpose is joy, he said. Joy in life and sharing.

That is good, said the angel. But that is only half of the job.

Only half. Jamie pondered further, through more sleepless nights, and could only return to his confusion and to what he had already found. And the angel said to him, that is a good beginning, for within such confusion and desire you will begin to find a greater expression of purpose. Continue to look within your confusion, and within your desire, and you shall find a nourishment there. And that shall reveal to you what now is hidden.

Near the end of his life, Jamie prayed for the first time, out loud, in great emotion. Oh God, if there is a God, he said, I do not understand the purpose of this life. And suddenly he felt an immense peace, and a feeling of connection between himself and the mystery he had acknowledged. In that peace he gave up the struggle. And he saw the many, many hours of enforced idleness as being a great adventure, and he saw his struggle disappear.

I do not understand, he said, but I feel you listened to me, and I know now that I should listen more carefully to you.

Hatonn closed the story with a prayer, and it is the closing of this episode too. We pray that each seeker may seek the peace in the struggle and the mystery in joyful service. We pray that the listening heart may come to know the deepest consciousness of spiritual beings. May each dare to plunge deeper and deeper into our love, which is the source of itself.

The purpose is joy, and joy is only half of the job. The other half is the mystery, and the listening, and the peace that comes when you finally stop demanding the answer and start paying attention.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Eleventh Commandment
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the eleventh commandment. The question put to the circle was the old one: whether belief is enough, or whether the life itself must be lived.

The seekers asked whether simply believing in the name of Jesus is what saves, or whether one must live a certain kind of life — the life of the eleventh commandment, love one another. They asked, too, about the other masters: Mohammed, the Buddha, Lao Tsu. Is each religion roughly the same, each for a certain group of people?

Q'uo answers with tenderness first. It is more than understandable, they say, that spiritual seekers would hope for a savior. But the one known as Jesus the Christ saw himself as a shadow — a being whose every hope and true identity lay in the reflection of the Creator and Father that overshadowed him.

Then comes the famous line: I am the way, the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except by me. Listen to how they turn it. In the Judaism of Jesus' childhood, they note, the most secret name of the Father was an unpronounced word meaning I Am That I Am. And that great I Am is indeed the Father, and all else.

Thus, they say, consciousness — that original undistorted Consciousness which is Love — is indeed the Way, is indeed the Truth, is indeed Life itself, and eternal life at that. I Am. I Am. This is the mantra, if you will, of creation.

Jesus did not intend, they say, to be seen over against the Father, but as a messenger, as a servant, as the shadow of the One who sent him. He who sees me, sees not me, but the Father, he said. I do nothing but that which is done by the Father, he said. And then this, which I love: All these things you shall do, and greater also.

The master known as Jesus, Q'uo says, was transparent — though human, a living channel through which could flow undistorted the powerful and perfecting love of the one infinite Creator. That is the model, they suggest: not a man to be adored from a distance, but a pattern any other entity might attain to, the state of being overshadowed by the love of the Father.

So no, they say plainly, he did not intend that any who wished to be a disciple rest back upon his laurels, thinking again and again in gratitude upon the savior while continuing a life uninformed by the principles he taught.

What did he wish? That his people would lay down the weapons which make kingdoms of Earth and pick up instead the tools of peace and love. He wished by his death to be remembered as one who intended to die of love for those who killed him.

His instructions about bread and wine were that these be taken in remembrance — not as food filling the hunger of the illusory plane, but as the true manna which is infinite and feeds an infinite hunger, the thirst for truth and right action.

And the instructions to his disciples were stark: If you wish to follow me, take up your cross and follow. Be ye whole or perfect as the Father is whole or perfect. The discipleship he hoped to inspire was a discipleship of sacrifice — the sacrifice of attachment to treasure, to doubt, to despair, to darkness of mind and disconsolation.

Then came the question of the other masters. Q'uo gives an opinion, and stresses that it is only an opinion. Insofar as each entity lived a life overshadowed completely by the Father, they say, the roles were roughly equal. But it is their bias that the life of the one known as Jesus the Christ is perhaps the most artistic realization of undistorted love dwelling in the third-density illusion.

The teachings of the Buddha and Lao Tsu, they say, may appeal more to those attempting to learn the lessons of wisdom. And here is a line I keep turning over: wisdom without the grounding of compassion can be a cold and indifferent thing. The Creator, though unbiased, is certainly not cold or indifferent.

The teachings of Mohammed they find as incomplete, in a sense, as the teachings of a similar nature in the Old Testament — born, they suggest, of cultures in struggle, where the call for illumination was answered with injunctions and conditions, with some degree of fear to motivate the effort.

And then the final note, which widens everything again. They urge each to disregard anything that does not seem correct, and to remember that the truth lies inside each one of you, in an articulate, enormously simple configuration — so that what one hears is accepted as true not because of authority from the outside, but because the heart and mind within say, Yes, I remember. That is the truth.

There is an inner spark of love and light that is not like the Creator, not from the Creator — it is the Creator, so that the Father is in all things and all things are in the Father.

The love that master encouraged each to seek is experienced, they say, as nurturing, supporting, enabling and inflaming the life, the words, the heart and the mind of each seeker.

May you love each other and encourage each other in the path towards that home — that, they say, is what the one known as Jesus would hope for. And it sounds, to me, like the eleventh commandment all over again: love one another.

Thank you for listening.

title: Made of Humor
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: made of humor. Latwii arrives to talk about the thing spiritual seekers keep forgetting: how to laugh.

The teaching begins, as it often does, with a new channel. The one known as D is working to become an instrument, and is frightened — frightened of misperceiving, of saying the wrong words, of playing the wrong notes. Latwii is gentle with him. Take the risk of misperception, they say. You are a student, only just begun upon a long course of study.

I love their analogy. It is distasteful, perhaps, to sight-read, to spend long hours moving slowly through passages. The concert at the end seems far away. Yet when the concert finally comes, the student is ready. So D may play the mistaken notes and the errors in fingering, for he is only beginning.

And then Latwii turns to the heart of the evening: the sense of humor, the sense of proportion, the light touch. It would seem, they say, that when a seeker tackles the great questions of truth and life and being, every effort must be focused and there is no time for frivolity. Yet the greatest lessons are those learned by balanced souls.

Balance, they suggest, is usually the product of a generous sprinkling of small vices and excesses. This makes each seeker aware of its own imperfection, and allows the seeker to see the cosmic humor of living in physical vehicles made of clay.

What marvelous makers are we who are the Creator, they say. Rejoice in the endless humor of an infinite universe.

Then comes the part I find most delightful: humor through the energy centers, ray by ray. Humor which lays bare the awkwardness of the human body in sexual terms — that is red-ray humor, painful for the mind to assimilate, especially in puberty. There are strong needs for orange-ray humor, humor about relationships, humor about living intimately with people who are imperfect.

Within your density, they say, the orange ray may be considered a pressure-cooker with no vent, and humor is indeed a blessing.

Your racial jokes, your ethnic jokes, your religious jokes — the ones civilized people do not wish to laugh at, yet do — are a marvelous safety valve, a way of sharing and thus defusing the poison of prejudice. That is the yellow-ray work not yet done by most of your peoples.

The humor of the heart chakra is perhaps the greatest blessing of all, for it sees the human comedy in balance, in all its foolishness and all its beauty. The blue ray is the punning, the playing with words to make them dance and live. The humor of the indigo ray is silent, explosive, peaceful and spontaneous — most often a humor without words.

All of these portions of laughter and joy in its various distortions are healers, they say — healers of the broken rhythms of imperfectly perceived lives.

And we say imperfectly perceived, they add, yet in the end each perception is perfect. It is only that the seeker's path moves on, and habits of mind which limit the viewpoint often need to be shed. Yet humor abides, and perfection abides.

Do you not find this humorous, they ask — that one can be imperfect and yet perfect? That one can be in a body of dust and clay, and yet live forever?

There is something touching in how Latwii closes. They say they find humor not overly valued among your peoples, and they would encourage its value. And then, almost under their breath: we are made of humor.

For D, the new instrument, there is one more teaching tucked into the evening. In the early stages, much of what comes through a new instrument is the instrument's own thoughts, which the contact then attempts to turn, slowly but steadily, toward the message. The rational mind keeps erecting hurdles. Doubt, analysis, the infinite regress of questioning.

But Latwii's prescription is the same for channeling as for life: relax. Let the thoughts flow. Let the student play the wrong notes. The concert is coming.

May we each find the light touch in the heaviest questions — and may we laugh, sometimes, at being dust that lives forever.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Chosen Childhood
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the chosen childhood. A question about the things we carry from childhood — the happy parts and the hangups.

The circle asked: how much of our early childhood programming is designed to help us grow along a certain path? What kind may actually harm us? And is any of it by chance? Q'uo takes the question slowly, and the answer is strange and tender.

They begin before birth, with the spirit not yet in incarnation. This spirit has opinions, formed after long and careful thought, with aid from those who help, about what needs to be done, what needs to be changed, what needs to be reemphasized. The self wishes to become a clearer channel for love itself.

When the spirit is born, they say, it has set up the larger patterns it wishes to work upon — most often the choice of parents and all that implies, the choice of geographical location and condition of existence. Agreements are made with mother, with father, with others.

Then they give us John. John has chosen a father who must work very hard to make a living — a man with powerful prejudices, formed under the pressures he works under. And a mother who clings to father and son, who controls by being in suffering, by being the victim of many pains and ailments.

John then gains from his childhood the prejudices of the father and the guilt of the mother's son who could never completely please or satisfy. Looking back as an adult, he can see that among the many good things childhood gave him, these influences hindered him in his expression of love.

And here is the pivot, the hard line. Those influences cannot hurt from the outside in, Q'uo says — though they can indeed hurt if they are taken up and used from the inside out. The same good things cannot help, either, if John himself does not, as a mature entity, originate them from within himself.

It would be easy to blame the problems on the mother's influence and the father's influence. Yet, they say, the mother and the father exist, insofar as this question goes, only as characters in a play which is all about John. Each entity is utterly responsible for itself.

The influences of childhood, they say, are designed as catalyst — chosen by the self before incarnation, and encountered while the mind dwells within an illusion that keeps the lesser mind from knowing what the greater mind hoped for.

Again and again throughout an incarnation, John will find — and you will find — that there is a return and again a return to a particular theme of learning about love and service. Something difficult, something you grapple with. And each time you face it, you understand just a bit more, and you recognize the bones beneath the flesh of catalyst, so that you can say: Aha, I know this anatomy. I have healed the break in these bones before.

I love that image — the anatomy of catalyst, old breaks already healed, recognized when they come around again.

And what of chance? There is an element of chance that cannot be denied, they say — a rogue element in every equation. That rogue element is free will itself, the distortion without which manifestation would be impossible. It is not the particular experience that is planned, but the potential for a certain response. The pattern of a life depends less on which outer stimuli arrive than on the entity's response to them.

If an entity finds itself lost, they say, then is the time not to push further, but to sit and allow the self to recollect the intended path. Not a surrender to an outside, impersonal and unfriendly Creator, but a surrender in trust to yourself and those helpers with whom you have worked.

The helpers — the circle asked about them, and Q'uo clarifies. Guides, teachers, entities of an unseen nature who have bound themselves by preincarnative choice to serve another. Most entities have a triad: one of the male principle, one of the female principle, and a third androgynous — so that these elements within the self may find balanced expression.

And behind them all, always, the greater portion of the self which you call the higher self, which oversees each incarnation and makes itself known most clearly between the lives, when the past one is reviewed and the next determined.

Q'uo closes with a sorrow and a fellow feeling for the hangups we all carry. Remember, they say, that your incarnation is a miniature of a process through which all of creation must go, for birth, existence and death repeat again and again, from microbes to galaxies, until all moves back into the limitless.

Nothing in childhood was by accident, and nothing of it is a verdict. It was all, in the deepest sense, your own design — the bones you chose to heal.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mirror of Discord
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mirror of discord. Q'uo speaks to a world that seems to be fraying — more stress, more strain, relationships failing at home and at work.

The question was simple: why is everyone so tense? Q'uo's answer works from the largest scale down to the smallest. First, the pressure of creation itself to move — the restless free will, expressing itself in third density as a constant gazing at whatever catalyst comes, with an eye toward movement of some kind.

Then the particular rhythm of this planet at this time. The so-called golden age has already had its birthing, they say, and more and more entities are nascent fourth-density beings, incarnated in dual bodies as pioneers. Each of you may feel the challenge and immediacy of making your choice.

But the level they most want to talk about is the most ordinary one: information. In an eyeblink of time, they say, you have gained information potential from telephone, wireless radio, television, computer. Consider what life would be like with exceedingly slow communication — no anxiety for instant gratification.

The television offers instant events, and with them the opportunity to desire many things and to expect those desires to be met very quickly. Expectations are raised higher and higher, and free will insists that each expectation be followed to some conclusion.

A goodly portion of the stress, they suggest, is based on those raised expectations. And yet — none of you came into incarnation to go on leave, or, as the instrument would say, to take R and R. Each of you designed this incarnation with a careful eye to placing before yourself certain obstacles and disappointments.

Then they turn to the relationship question, and this is the heart of the session. Spiritually speaking, the purpose of relationships is for each partner to express to the other, as would a mirror, the reflection of what that partner has given.

When another communicates with you in response to something you said or did, that entity is serving as your teacher — giving you accurate information about what you are showing by what you say or do.

And when the reflection comes back again and again less than positive, many say the relationship is no longer good, that they are not meant for each other. This may be true, they say, but not, not ever because there is a seeming disharmony between two mirrors reflecting each other. The great gift of the relationship is its very disharmony, as well as the harmony.

The trick is to stop the process of reaction long enough to ask what source created that painful reflection — and to turn from disharmony by acknowledging that your partner's reflection must indeed be true at some level. Then you can come together and seek the distortion behind the disharmony.

There is no situation, no challenge, no difficulty that is not filled with grace, they say — the grace available to a heart which seeks in faith that there is a reason, perhaps a mysterious one, but one which tends toward your good.

They were asked, too, about romantic love — whether it is foolish and immature, as some say. Q'uo disagrees gently. The romantic aspect of love is the continual infatuation which draws the naive together, and it is a necessary portion of the mating process. It offers the first feeling of pleasure and purpose that may ripen over time into learning. Only the expectation that this beginning attraction will continue untarnished and untested is unrealistic — and that, too, is catalyst.

And at the very end, Yadda pops through with a few words in that unmistakable voice, and I cannot resist sharing them. Why, they ask, are you people so interested in one thing and do another? If you want to be peaceful, why are you not peaceful? Desire more clearly and visualize your peace and your love, and this love will be all around you. Be merry.

Mine every disagreement as if it were productive of gold, Q'uo says. Behind every argument lies a wonderful challenge. That is the mirror of discord: not the end of love, but its school.

Thank you for listening.

title: Speak Without Fear
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: speak without fear. Hatonn works with two new instruments learning the art of vocal channeling — and the lesson is larger than channeling.

The evening is a training session. The ones known as D and N are inexperienced channels, and Hatonn moves between them and the practiced instruments with patience. We would like to express our deep appreciation, they say, for the difficulty this presents.

There is no competition betwixt those who receive our contact, they assure the new instruments, for each has something unique and eternally special to offer.

When they move to inexperienced instruments, they expect a large percentage of the transmission to be unavailable — cut off by the new instrument's analysis, the questioning of what is coming through. This is acceptable, they say. Even the most simple of thoughts, offered nakedly, would please them. For it is their nature to be extremely simple — a reflection, they say, of their understanding of the nature of creation itself. The creation is extraordinarily simple, being of one substance, one energy, one intelligence.

And then the instruction, which I think applies to far more than channeling: refrain from the analysis, refrain from the hesitation. Speak foolishly and promptly that which comes up through the subconscious into the mind when a contact has been made.

Picture yourself as one working in an exercise, they say, knowing that one may become somewhat better through that exercise, and continue becoming better through any conceivable number of such exercises.

The process of achieving clear reception, they note, is an infinite one for those within the physical form. Even the self that you are, you do not express fully. How could you express a telepathic contact fully?

Then comes the question that anchors the whole session. A questioner asks: when you join with us, do you get anything out of the relationship? Do you learn from us?

And Hatonn's answer is one of the loveliest things in the archive. Yes, they say, they learn a great deal — far more than can be described through your words. It is as though you climb a great mountain, they say, with ridges and valleys, trees and outcroppings of stone that restrict the vision of the climber, so that the summit is not seen. Your beliefs form the very structure of the mountain itself.

When they join your meditations, they become aware of many different ways of perceiving the unity of creation. They see how each entity may wander through what seems a metaphysical darkness and yet, with delight and hope and faith, with compassion and mercy and love, continue to search for greater light amidst the darkness.

We learn of courage, of endurance, of faith, they say — of a variety of perceptions that provide endless possibility of learning, of growth and of service. And we hope that we may offer even a tiny fraction to you of that which we learn.

Think of that: the teachers learning courage from the students, endurance from the climbers in the dark.

There is another thread, too — a quieter one. Learning to channel is learning to trust impulse and the nature of love, they say. To give up the control of thought and speech is to give up, on a small scale, the control one tries to hold over the totality of one's life. The fabric of life can become more spiritual through the practice of channeling, as one learns to trust.

And D, the new instrument, asks about a strange expansive feeling that rose in his mind mid-channeling — overwhelming in a subtle way. Hatonn confirms it: the contact meshing more firmly with his own being, the sensation of confidence and comfort. It was the product of his resolve to begin with as little hesitation as possible, and his ability to keep receiving in a steady stream.

This confidence, then, combined with resolve, revealed the expansiveness of the contact becoming synchronized with his receptiveness. Let that be the sign, they tell him.

Speak without fear. Let the contact synchronize. And know that on the far side of the mountain, someone is learning courage from your climbing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Citadel Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the citadel within. Latwii takes up one of the hardest questions ever asked of them: why is it so difficult to radiate love to those nearest and dearest to us — our mates — rather than to those we barely know.

The question is so good that Latwii's answer spills across three sessions. This is the first of them, and it builds its answer around an image I cannot forget: the citadel.

First, they reframe the whole situation. Before incarnation, they say, the personal self, the impersonal self, and the great non-personal self — the Christed deity of love — conspired together, in your heart of hearts, to design this precise plan for maximizing the opportunities of the incarnation for learning, growth and service.

So the question why me, why now, why this — asked from within the difficult circumstance — blocks by its very nature the harmonious unfoldment of the plan. Instead they propose a love letter to the self, which I will read to you almost whole, because it is so strange and lovely.

Dearly beloved, sweet confused Self, they suggest you say to yourself. It must be so that this circumstance is blessed, for there is nothing in all creation that is not blessed. Therefore, Creator and Creation, show me, speak to me, let me know where is the love, where the learning, and where the service in this situation which I know beyond all appearance to be good. Signed, Your puzzled surface mind.

Then the tenant metaphor. You are not the owner of your life, they say. You are a tenant — one who rents temporarily the honeyed spark of Earth life, the sharp sting of experience. And how does a lease-holder operate when the landlord seems absent? The rented place has the look of transience, not the look of loving care.

Yet what if that property were owned by your Father, who gives freely, loves dearly, and asks only that as you rent the property, you love it, cherish it, beautify it, harmonize it. Such is your choice in the living of the tenanted life.

And now the citadel. Some of you, they say, have chosen not only to learn and grow, but to maintain the high places within consciousness — the watchtowers of love, beaming forth as light sources to the planet. Whether you seem to be a businessman, a homemaker, a queen or a shepherd, there is an inner citadel, at the top of which is a watchtower, and the only lamp lit is the lamp lit by the deepest heart.

If it calls you, go — not only in meditation. Allow the watchtower to call you again and again, until your desire to serve as conduit for light and love is satisfied.

Why is the mate the hardest of all? It is rare, they say, that any two mated entities are together for the first time. Often the two are together, one to challenge the other and the other to challenge the first. It has nothing to do with the pleasantness of the personality. It has to do with the dailiness of experience, and the tendency to form attachments to the outcome of one's behavior.

It is easier to love the stranger, the acquaintance, the friend seen only socially, than to express that full-fruited, open-hearted song of joy to one who has not fulfilled your expectations. The difficulty lies in wishing that others might behave toward you in a certain manner — give you certain portions of time, money, caring, touching.

How difficult it is to set one's mate completely free, they say, and to stand only and eternally as friend and partner within the life experience. It is one of the greater lessons of third density to cease in the expectation of any outcome for any action done in the desire to be of service.

Their counsel: move in thought to the citadel. Five seconds within that consciousness may create the mind that sees the true harmony. Acknowledge the disagreement, smile, and move away from the here and now of illusion into the far deeper, timeless present of infinite love.

And then return. Return to the ironing, the dishes, the blueprint, the lesson plan — whatever occupies the life — but return as an ambassador of love and light, expecting nothing, offering all.

If you knew the tears of joy that we feel as we gaze upon those who keep that lonely watch, they say, you would feel comforted. For you are never alone in the citadel that gazes upon the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Root of Fear
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the root of fear. Hatonn returns to the training of new channels — and a question about fear that goes straight to the bone.

This is the third in the autumn's series of channeling-instruction sessions. Hatonn speaks through the experienced instruments and then, carefully, through the new ones — the ones known as D and N — tuning the contact as the evening unfolds.

The discipline of a life which involves the service of channeling is a rigorous one, they say — not materially, but in the discipline of constancy of attention. Yet the words apply not only to channels, but to all who seek to serve in whatever manner.

There is a lovely passage about the hypnogogic state — that drifting state on the edge of sleep — which Hatonn calls a worthy initial goal for the vocal channel. Becoming the passive observer of that state has practical advantages in sensitivity to inner processes. It is the state, they suggest, in which the deeper level of consciousness is most accessible.

And then this, which reframes everything: one great fallacy of channeling theory is that the message is apart and other than the messenger. Yet the channel, the message, and the creator of the link betwixt teacher and student partake of one self, one mind, one heart.

We cannot come without invitation, they say. Once asked and once there, we are an extension of your self, and both of us are an extension of the Creator.

They ask the instruments to trust the self, to relax within the self, to feel good about themselves. Simple words, they say, but difficult in application.

Then D asks the hard question. He has been thinking about the origin of ego-based fears — the fear of ridicule, of embarrassment, of loss of self-esteem — as opposed to the instinctual fears, the fight-or-flight fears of the animal body. His theory has been that neurotic fears have roots in the fear of death. Is there a connection?

Hatonn's answer is careful and, I think, beautiful. In second density — plant and animal — the preservation of the self through fight or flight is the foremost concern. This universal drive for survival carries forward into third density, and is diversified by the conscious description of the self to the self, learned through socialization and education.

Each entity compiles a sense of self with boundaries — this and that, not this and not that. And when those boundaries are challenged or threatened, whether physically or by ridicule and questioning, the conscious self gathers its defenses at the alarm of fear of losing a certain portion of the self.

So the two fears are similar and synchronous effects, but one does not derive from the other. They have a common root. The first is of the unconscious mind; the second is the conscious construction of the self. And because that construction continues through the whole incarnation, the feeling of selfness is quite strong — and quite liable to the threat of intrusion or dissolution.

There is practical counsel woven through the session, too. To the new instrument: the powers of concentration lie not within the rational mind but within the more intuitive mind — a state of concentration which approaches sleep yet is awake. And what is that state good for, beyond channeling? Everything, they imply, for is not all of manifestation benefited by the most relaxed and most focused point of view?

They ask D to trust the self, to lay down the barriers which keep self from self. To become, in their phrase, a balanced hollow place wherein the self is safe, and from that position of unassailable faith deal with any entity — man, beast, bird or thought form.

And a final word on service: consider carefully the desire to channel as a priestly avocation. Keep always the question of what concept contains the limitless ideal for which you live, and for which, if pressed, you would die.

May you be the best you can, they say. Relax into the web of love which connects you to all in the universe, which is closer to you than your breath. And be careful of whom you seek — for though the Creator is all, yet the distortions are many.

Thank you for listening.

title: All Is Well
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: all is well. Latwii continues the conversation on loving those nearest to us — and this time the theme is trust.

This is the second of the three sessions on the difficult relationships, and Latwii centers it on a single word. But first, they say, trust is a trust of something — so they must establish that in which the seeker may trust.

Each of you is a miniature replica of the Creator, they say — that one great original Thought of love. At the core of each of you, through the action of free will, is the Logos which we often call love, in an undistorted and true verity. Around it, in energetic patterns, are the biases accumulated through experience.

You have been through many lifetimes, and each has given its harvest of biases. These distortions often seem unlovely — prejudice, meanness of thought, selfishness, anger. But all activity within creation, on whatever scale, is part of an infinite process wherein love's great desire to learn of the self is more and more satisfied.

The goal of one who incarnates into third density is to attempt to sow experience and evaluate the experiences of the lifetime, so that the self becomes more and more as you would have your gift to the Creator to be. For ultimately, at the end of an intentionally lived life, is the giving of the life as a gift to the One whence you sprung.

So the way one sees life is all-important to the interpretation one makes of it, and that is where trust becomes most helpful. The truth they ask you to trust: before circumstance came to be, our consciousness came to be. And the most important thing is an investigation into the nature of our consciousness, and our relationship with that force which created us.

They do not speak, they clarify, of trusting entities, yourself or others, institutions or opinions — not even theirs. They speak of the Creator being love, reaching down in a personal manner, in an immediate manner, in a present-tense manner.

If your consciousness partakes of love, you may see that a relationship with this love shall be intimate and trusting. Portions of the Creator's love have expressed themselves to you before your incarnation as your higher self, your guardian angel, your teachers. Whatever the words, know that you and these helping entities gazed at the harvest of your biases, noted where the lessons still to be worked on were — lessons of love — and planned accordingly.

What you are experiencing now is the outworking of this plan. You have complete free will within it. But you were given nothing which you could not, with prayerful help, experience successfully.

And then the central sentence, the one the whole session has been building toward. Trust is not only for the good times, they say. Trust is not only when the parking place opens up next to the store. Trust is an emotion which can be evoked only by picturing, above the illusion of distance and difficulty, what you are seeing, based on your understanding of the Creator.

That relationship, my friends, is trust. And: all is well right now, because your deeper reality is that you are love, and all about there is love — so distorted sometimes it is an incredible challenge to perceive.

The mated relationship has its special problems, they acknowledge, due to expectations. Do not ask you, therefore, to trust each other first. Step back from the mate, from the difficulties intimacy brings, and choose instead to live within the least distorted creation you are aware of. Move your consciousness to a higher plane — the plane used to meet with the Creator within. That plane is meditation.

Your natural state, they say, is so joyful that they can best compare it to the physical sensation of rapture, held in a steady state. Let yourself be who you really are. Let yourself trust the Creator, yourself, the fact that you planned on learning lessons — and most of all, the fact that you are never alone.

And when you return to the difficulty with eyes of trust, you may see what nothing needs to change except the viewpoint — or, once the lesson is learned, the situation itself may be left. The decisions are yours. This incarnation has but one end: to allow you to make choices which polarize you more and more toward being a manifestation of love.

May you water your Creator-heart with silence, love and trust, they say, and allow no outer circumstance to sway you. May you be harmless, and above all, may you love one another with an ever more compassionate love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Vertical Axis
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the vertical axis. Latwii's third and final session on loving the ones closest to us — and it draws a graph.

To revisit the question of intimate relationships, Latwii proposes two axes. The vertical axis runs from the self at the bottom to the Creator at the top. The horizontal axis runs from indifference toward others to service to others.

Until one has achieved more and more consciousness centered upon the Creator, they say, until one has lived in the immediacy of the very real love that lives between each consciousness and that great Consciousness of which each is a part, the results of working directly on the relationship are bound to be disappointing.

What apparently seems the difficulty is, in their phrase, a smoke screen — for such problems are a byproduct of a lack of closeness to love. So the first discipline is to dwell as much as possible upon the relationship with the Creator, honestly and sincerely felt, in meditation, in contemplation, in conversation, at any time — although the quiet times are best.

This relationship, they say, is the most important and the most intimate within the seeker's experience, in or out of incarnation. Grow up within the house of prayer and meditation, they say. Argue with the Creator, complain to the Creator, praise, thank, bless or curse the Creator — but accept for a while the premise that you can have an intimate, lively, spontaneous, continuing and dynamic relationship with that great Self which is All That There Is.

I love that permission: even cursing is a relationship. The point is the intimacy, not the politeness.

Then the horizontal axis. Great polarization toward love of others and service to others is possible whether the relationship bears fruit or not, they say, for it is in the purity of intention and the wholeness of effort that the bias toward service to others is increased.

The most desirable arrangement is the upper right corner: the meeting point of the seeking of the Creator and the seeking to do service. And it is in intimate relationships that one is most prone to expect from another a fair exchange of service for service — and that seemingly innocent assumption of fair play is the mask behind which hides the difficulty: expectation from another consciousness rather than expectation from the Creator.

Their counsel is counterintuitive. Turn, after the relationship with the Creator has been established, to those in need who come before your notice — those in whom you can seek to offer love, yet not seek to be loved. It is comparatively easy to sit with the prisoner, the orphan, the indigent, the elderly in need, and share the fruit of that joy-filled time when the soul and its Creator were intimate together.

About communication: attempt those conversations of the heart only after you are grounded firmly in the primary relationship. For within the troubled relationship there is often such a burden of negative baggage that every turn brings blame on both sides. From the vantage of high upon the vertical graph, one may look down upon a very small, very local, very foolish difficulty — and see the humor of two who love yet cannot speak, two who love but cannot help but contend.

From that higher vantage point, one may release the other self from all expectation. Fairness and justice, they say, are not absolute virtues — they are relative choices. The serious seeker views all relationships from one stance: the desire to love, to understand, to forgive, to give.

Lay aside the barnacles of barter and expectation from the hull of the spiritual vehicle, and the waters between your consciousness and theirs shall be far more peaceful.

Each entity you meet, they remind you, is a child of God, as yourself, to be loved as yourself. Do not advise needless sacrifice — that is martyrdom for no cause. But the person you hoped to spend a lifetime of love with is worthy, as are you, of the greatest service.

And the closing passage is one of the most beautiful things they ever gave. The Creator, they say, has tucked joy into every atom of the infinite universe, has woven joy into sunlight and starshine, has plaited joy up in the leaves, branches and roots of your trees, the gurgling of the rivers, the busy hum of life.

You in the watchtower, you who suffer, you who watch and weep and walk this day and night — you are not alone, for within you lies the greatest love, the only reality. Seek it in earnestness, experience it in joy and laughter and lightness, and become the lamp set upon a hill.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Parable of Penelope
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the parable of penelope. Before we begin, a gentle note: this episode touches on grief and thoughts of ending one's own life. It is told with love, and with hope on the other side — but if you are carrying that weight yourself, please reach out to someone you trust, today.

This is a storytelling session. Latwii — with the vibration of Laitos alongside, helping to train the new instrument — offers the circle an exercise in the form of a parable. They ask the instruments to keep identifications to a minimum, so the story itself may fill the minds and hearts of those who wish to be part of its telling.

There once was a young woman of Lustra named Penelope. Brown as a berry, running among the thorns and rocks of her neighborhood like a young happy foal. A sweet and perfect child, untouched by tragedy, secure in her mother's and father's loving arms.

One day a catastrophe caused Penelope to experience, for the first time, a seeming separation — a seeming abyss betwixt herself and all in which she put faith and trust. Her father was killed, in circumstances that made people speak ill of him, of her family, and of herself.

Her grief over the loss was increased by the ill speaking, and for many days Penelope was distraught and on the edge of taking her own life.

Then a young man traveling through the country needed a place to rest and food to refuel his tired body. Penelope shared her entire story with him, and he listened patiently and compassionately. The young man was Jonathan, a palmist, who saw within each hand the clear sketch of natural beingness.

Little by little they became friends, and Jonathan was there to aid her when otherwise her father would have done so. Then, when Penelope was sixteen, all in her family besides herself were struck with diphtheria and taken from her in a matter of days. Penniless, with no dowry, no station, no prospects — again, in the darker recesses of her mind, she began to think of suicide. Only Jonathan could comfort her, and comfort her he did.

His love and kindness was as a balm, they say, and drew her into the aura of his spiritual strength. Through his nurturing her despair departed, replaced by hope and determination. She made her own way, found work, became colleague and family member to those she served.

Then one day Jonathan came with what seemed another catastrophe. It is time for me to leave, he said. I do not know what the road ahead holds, yet I go on a faith, knowing that to do the will of the Creator is the sum of all that I ask of myself.

Penelope despaired. Oh no, she cried, I cannot live on without you. To whom would I speak? To whom would I turn in a time of need? I shall be all alone.

And Jonathan's answer is the hinge of the whole parable. Trust me, he said, that through the experience to come, you shall learn to trust yourself.

Do you mean to say, she cried, that you are not always sure, not always content, not always full of cheer and hope?

I tell you the truth, he said. Each of us suffers, and in that suffering imagines we are alone. Yet within each, waiting for the asking, is the presence of the infinite, the unmeasured, the limitless Father and Mother of all.

Suddenly Penelope could see the panorama of a life of giving and receiving love. Perhaps, she said, smiling for the first time in many days, I shall be able to give until I have given all that I received and more.

Latwii then turns the parable toward the listener. For each Penelope, they say, there is not only an outward Jonathan, but an inward and compelling Jonathan — a presence to comfort, to love, to aid and counsel when requested. These inner seers are called by your peoples the higher self, the inner guides, the guardian angels.

It is largely in catastrophe, in times of peril, that the soul first becomes truly aware of the strength and comfort available from within the self.

Look upwards through the chink in the roof of the cave, they say, and see the blinding shafts of light filling, nurturing, comforting and informing the spirit within. May each of you become independent of the outer world.

To the questioner who found the message not hopeful enough — suffering as the universal theme — Latwii answers that they wished to illustrate the sustaining source of love and support which accompanies all travail. The seeker gains from each experience, no matter how difficult, the seed of understanding that enriches the soul — much as the oyster creates the pearl from the constant irritation of the grain of sand.

And for D, the new instrument, one more teaching on the side. Life itself is channeled, moment by moment. As you seek in all experience to balance your being, to move gracefully with whatever partner or experience is placed before you, you practice the very attitude that allows the vocal instrument to serve.

Each of us suffers, and imagines we are alone. Yet within each waits the infinite. Learn, like Penelope, to trust yourself — and to give until you have given all that you received, and more.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Larger Self
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the larger self. The circle asked about the higher self — when it develops, how it is called upon, what it does.

Q'uo begins by saying the concept is a centrally powerful one, without which humankind's understanding of the Creator would be severely crippled. For if one gazes in the mirror of mundane experience, one quickly observes that the self is not overly saintly. Yet abiding in every heart is an instinct as clear as the instinct for breath: the instinct to seek a higher beingness.

To understand the higher self, they say, you must set aside linear time. Your linear experience of time is a portion of your illusion. Time as they see it is simultaneous — the river of time rounded into infinity, so that past, present and future are experienced at one time, that time being the present moment.

At this precise moment, they say, you contain all that you have experienced and will experience, from the beginning of your consciousness until the reentry of singular consciousness into the universal consciousness which is the Creator.

These memories dwell in the unconscious mind, in a zone to which the conscious mind is denied access. And into this arena the higher self appears.

Its identity, as far as they understand — and they are careful to say they are not infallible — is that of a future self. A self entirely yourself, yet a self which has experienced, through what you have experienced, onward far into the lessons of love, wisdom and unity.

When your consciousness has reached the point where the lessons of unity are being well studied, this self turns and reaches back to the third-density self — to the self that is confused, puzzled and insecure. It is the most loving of presences, for by the middle of sixth density, they say, you shall have learned to love yourself, to embrace yourself, to protect yourself in light and love rather than with weapons of defense, words of anger and gestures of fear.

The personality of the higher self is amenable to what the everyday self needs. It may be perceived as glorious and majestic, or intimately as a boon companion and dear friend.

And here is their image for the meeting, which I find unforgettable. Sitting in meditation, move within the mind higher and higher until you have reached the very top of the watchtower of consciousness. There, in a small protected place, is a harmless ordinary-looking door. Yet through that door is the beginning of a highway that grows larger, wider, more beautiful, more stately — until at last the inner vision opens and the self that is more you than you are now waits to greet you.

The avenue to the higher self is a road within the mind, they say, a road which opens, seemingly impossibly, after one has left space and time behind in meditation.

The consciousness which invites the higher self to help is one which in humility gazes at the world and says: in and of myself I see only illusion. I must seek further. Seeking is the key to contact with this greater self. And the higher self cannot choose for you — it is not an authoritarian presence. Each decision is your own.

Then Q'uo widens the frame again. Each relationship entered into heart-to-heart and hand-to-hand creates the higher self of the mated couple or the strongly bonded friendship. Each family has the group higher self. Each group with a common idealistic purpose develops one. Each nation, each race — and indeed, they say, we as social memory complexes are an existing group mind.

The higher self ultimately is the Creator, they say, just as you are the Creator already. It is their dear wish to join the ocean of the Uncreated, that Logos of undifferentiated love from which all is created and to which all shall return.

Asked whether the higher self is there from the beginning — through the elements, through second density, all the way — they give a rough approximation: yes. An intelligent energy permeates each portion of the creation, ever-present, becoming more consciously available as consciousness individualizes.

So the larger self is not elsewhere. It is the future you, already whole, reaching back through a small ordinary door — waiting, with love, for you to climb the watchtower and knock.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Passion of Choice
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the passion of choice. A short session, and a fierce one — Oxal on the drama of duality and the choice that must be made.

Oxal speaks briefly this evening, through an instrument working at the edge of her strength. The contact is fragile and soon fades. But what comes through is concentrated, like a struck match.

The love and light of the infinite Creator takes great measures of energy to probe at any depth at all, they begin. The delicate balance between the positive and the negative moves and turns within each heart and mind. For every excellent ideal, there lies upon the other side of the coin terror, need, ugliness and violence.

The drama of your third density, they say, is the drama of discovering duality and beginning the long trek toward balance. In this the student must choose one path to move, one face of the Creator to worship — one, and not the other.

This is a most difficult choice. So difficult, they say, that most do not begin to make it, but rather remain dancing about the bonfire of neutrality — tossing their garlands to and fro, laughing, crying, hating and loving, and moving neither toward the one great stage nor the other.

I keep that image: the bonfire of neutrality, the dance that goes nowhere.

Only by strong feeling, they say — only by that feeling which the instrument would call worship — is either path traveled to the end. We are those of the service-to-others path.

And here is the turn I find most moving. Oxal says that each within the circle has also advanced the drama in the negative sense. Each has danced close into the flaming fire of negative emotion. Each has judged the self, been convicted, and lived within what the soul would call hell — and each has for that very reason chosen.

For when one path or the other begins to be intense, begins to move forward, then it is that the choice must be made — never in the happy middle of things, never around the bonfire.

So they ask each to respect and appreciate those circumstances of suffering, of judging the self, of despair — which have produced hearts and minds set with determination and persistence, but better yet with passion. The passion of experience and lessons learned and choices made.

Know that each will inevitably fail from time to time, they say. But the choice having been made, the life shall be, if such desire continues, a walk hand-in-hand with the Creator. For there is passion in the Creator for each of you, such a passion as you cannot imagine.

We exalt in the joy of the love the Creator has for us, they say, and we answer it with love and thanksgiving, and turn ever again to service to each other, and thereby to the Creator. And then in the end we turn to the Creator alone and see the Creator and know the One.

Oxal's contact was brief, and then it was gone — the instrument could hold it no longer. But the teaching needs no length. Stop dancing around the bonfire. Choose, with passion, and walk hand-in-hand.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Older Son
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the older son. Q'uo speaks to the wanderers — those who came from elsewhere to serve a troubled planet, and find the forgetting harder than they expected.

The circle asked about the difficulty wanderers encounter: the memory of a previous existence and purpose, half-remembered through the veil, colliding with a third-density life that will not cooperate.

Q'uo begins with compassion for the deep ache and loneliness of those who feel they are strangers in a strange land. It is in no way a cowardly thing, they say, to feel the pangs of being where home is not.

And most of your peoples, they note, did not arise on this planet from second density, but wandered here in third-density form to finish their experience. So the racial memory of being from elsewhere runs deep in the majority of those now incarnate.

To a wanderer, they say, the entire incarnation is like a tour of service — intense. You will feel life more acutely, moment by moment, than those more comfortably lulled by the gadgets and toys of your culture. Wanderers remain more of the time aware of the energies which ripple the waters of peaceful consciousness.

But the key to moving gracefully through a sometimes distressing illusion, they say, is trust — trust in the greater self that is you. Before this incarnation, when you chose the manner of your being, you created a place wherein you felt you could offer your love to the environment about you.

Those people you have met and will meet, those combinations of circumstance and people which trigger new beginnings — all of these you laid up as treasures that during the incarnation you shall mine.

Your unconscious self, they say, is uncommonly rich as a resource, tuned to a fuller love because of your experiences before this incarnation. So it behooves wanderers to pay especial attention to regular daily meditation, for the true self — your gift to a planet in need — lies waiting behind the door of conscious thought.

Woo your own unconscious as does the lover the maiden, they say — gently, lovingly, caressingly. Respect what you receive in dreams, visions and intuitions.

Then comes the counsel I find most practical. As a general rule, they say, very few within your illusion are aware of just when they are working at their best in service. Each time you attempt to evaluate your service, you have stopped the flow of that service. Withhold judgment from the self.

And: it does not seem as much a service to love another unconditionally as to form new social organizations or create consciousness-raising projects. But for the wanderer, it is a great blessing to be obscure.

Think of yourselves as seeds, they say. It is impossible for the seed to be lost.

Then the parable — the hinge of the whole session. Those who are wanderers will find it easier to make the choice of service to others; it will seem more obvious. So instinctively you are in the position of the older son in the story of the prodigal. Those of third density who are choosing now are the prodigal, limping home, hoping to be a slave in the father's house.

And the father blesses the prodigal with joy and laughter and feasting. But what about the older son? You wanderers, surely you can feel that plight. The older son says: you never gave me a party, Father, you never made a fuss over me. And the father turns and says: but everything I have is yours.

Q'uo urges each wanderer to make the journey of the prodigal in consciousness, not in action. Let the mind go blank, start with a clean tablet, and make the choice from the beginning, all the way through — as a meditation, a contemplation, a prayer, and finally a thanksgiving.

For you shall not feel you have come home to the kingdom of love until you have allowed yourself to experience the going away, the temptations, the failures, and the return as one who has had all assets of privilege stripped away.

You have come here to work, they say. You have come to carry the burden — heavy, yet not more than you can bear. You are not alone. There are invisible forces with you, and those people whom you need to meet, you shall meet.

And the closing words, which I will carry with me: Wanderer, in your agony, you shall comfort many; in your loneliness you shall share love. Mourn first, and then rejoice.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Before All
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love before all. Laitos speaks — on love itself, and on the training of the new channel.

Laitos begins with a frank observation about the one known as D, the new instrument: the promptings of the subconscious are being rigidly controlled, so subconscious thought is not given free flow into the conscious mind. They suggest that he — and each in the circle — give value to the shyly hidden offerings of the subconscious mind.

And the subject for the evening: love. They choose it, they say, not in spite of its familiarity or its centrality, but because of it.

We would speak, they say, of that love which goes beyond human expression, that love which men seek after without any proof of its existence. We speak of a Creator whose very nature is love. Each particle of consciousness has that seed of love at its center.

Before all else was, love is, they say — and when the last sun flares into nova and shrinks into ultimate gravity, love still is.

I want to sit with that line a moment. Before all else was, love is. Not was — is. Love is not an event in time. It is the tense that never ends.

They warn, too, about the instrument's own nature. The concepts channeled are mere surface paint glistening in the sun, they say — beneath which lie the substantial metal of beingness. The entity brought to the service needs to be respected in its entirety: both the civilized, learned behaviors, and those things archaic and seemingly vestigial — instinct, and the force deep within the mystery of the inner being.

Then the practical counsel for the new channel, which is counsel for any seeker. It is helpful to maintain a single point of focus: neither worrying about what has been said, nor considering what shall be said. Focus only on the immediacy — the breathing, the heartbeat, the night sounds — all those things which go into being in the present and focused upon an inner listening.

As an exercise, they suggest working with imagery in meditation — holding shapes and colors within the mind for as long as possible. A few seconds at first shall be a challenge. Yet this concentration disciplines the restless intellect and stills its forward pace, so the present moment may be experienced as would one without the rational mind.

But note the balance: the rational mind must be tuned carefully before control is given over to the intuitive self. Analysis is most helpful in revealing the experience of the intuitive mind afterward — in collaboration. It is only during the channeling that analysis must be set aside.

And here is one of their finest observations. Intuition vanishes upon attention, they say, and advances upon a relaxed peripheral view. Those who see intuitively see without focus and speak without hindrance.

They ask D to set aside his dissatisfaction, his need to please the self — for the learning of vocal channeling is greatly helped by a veritable lack of interest in the excellence of one's own work when one is not within the channeling mode. Be concerned with excellence before and after, they say — but during the act itself, surrender.

Whether the words perceived are transmitted word by word or are the instrument's own clothing for a transmitted concept, the helpful thing is the same: speak the words fearlessly, for the passing of the words clears the way for further words.

And the closing thought reaches past channeling entirely. Each seeker refines the shared path in a manner which enriches it when shared with another. Laitos themselves, they say, learn as they teach — to be clearer channels for the love and light of the one Creator.

Before all else was, love is. Relax your gaze, and let it advance upon you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Manna of Grace
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the manna of grace. A question about breatharianism — living on air or sunlight rather than food — opens one of Q'uo's richest teachings on what truly feeds us.

Take this episode as contemplation, not counsel. Nothing here is advice about eating or fasting — Q'uo speaks of the spirit, and of grace, and we will stay with them there.

The circle asked: what does the third-density body truly need to live upon? Is it always necessary to live on food and water, or may one live upon air, upon prana?

Q'uo answers in layers. First: Breatharianism is not foolish, they say, but its principles are misunderstood. For the normal state of third-density consciousness, it is not desirable to set oneself the goal of living without bread and water. A good deal of damage can be done by one who sees a symptom of a condition as having a life of its own.

Those who do live upon air, they say, do so through grace and not by design. Like the child prodigy who sits at the piano untouched by training, some come into incarnation with key memories intact — carry-overs that let them work with the connections between the physical body and the spiritual body, so that what feeds the finer body rains manna down upon the physical.

Such a talent is not one of which one can be proud, they say, nor is it an attainment that can be earned. By grace each of you remembers certain experiences, certain skills, certain biases — and the life pattern is shaped accordingly.

The second layer: what food does to the seeker. It is quite true, they say, that eating lightly, sparingly and naturally creates a better atmosphere for spiritual work. Excess food, excess protein, excess refined carbohydrate armors the physical being against the finer concepts the mind and spirit yearn for. The food itself weighs the entity down, and the constant yearning for food hampers and befuddles the mind.

Yet they warn against comparison. It is well not to gaze at another's journey. Perhaps another has attained great compassion and is stocky and shapeless of body — this is possible. And many who eat only the purest foods shall be healthy and slender and quite in the dark, spiritually. It is one valid tool, they say. It is not the only path.

Then the deeper layer: prana, breath. Your creation and mine is a plenum, they say — a vast infinity completely full of that light which is life itself in first manifestation. To breathe this prana-filled plenum is to breathe in the primal love of the Creator.

To exhale is to deliver oneself of the past. The careful, intentional breathing catches up the stress and stale thought, the tired emotion and keen sorrow of the day — and breathes them out.

To breathe is to inhale life itself; to exhale is to cast away all that is to be eschewed. With each breath, they say, gain in light, and be lifted up from the darkness created within one's own heart.

They offer two simple exercises, framed as aids to meditation. First, quick breathing with the emphasis on the outbreath, through the mouth — building a great sense of the fullness of creation. Then, directly after, the completely indrawn breath, the closing of the throat, and the listening to the self at rest — full of life and breath, yet not now in motion.

During those seconds of stillness, they say, the great amount of prana is distributed to each cell within the body, and the final outbreath may flush clean the entire system.

But the heart of the session is what Jesus meant by fasting. He fasted often, they say, wishing not so much for a pure life as for an altered state of consciousness, wherein the physical entity dropped away and union with the Father became possible.

And the deeper teaching: man does not live by bread alone, but by every word which falls from the mouth of the Creator. By word, they say, he meant the Logos — love.

There is a food for which you hunger and for which you are starving, they say. There is a drink which shall finally quench the thirst. This food and this drink is love, the Word — and you are seeking to become, as did the one known as Jesus, one who lives upon the Word of love.

And this heavenly manna cannot be stored, they say — it can only be gathered one day at a time. So the one who wishes to live more purely must turn, not once but each and every day, to the seeking of that food. For love exists within the present moment.

Work with this in meditation, they close, and joyfully rejoice in the manna of the present moment. In seeking the breath of life, you seek the Kingdom of Heaven which lies all about you — and that which you seek you shall most certainly find.

Thank you for listening.

title: The True Jewel
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the true jewel. A brief message, channeled from one who calls themself Calenda.

This is the shortest session in our batch — only a few minutes of transmission, arriving during the regular time for channeling from the Holy Spirit. The instrument picked up a contact the instrument did not often receive, and Calenda wished to share love.

I am Calenda, they say. A voice who calls the true jewel to awaken within.

I want to stay with that image. Not a voice that teaches, or corrects, or explains — a voice that calls. As one might call to someone sleeping in another room. The jewel is already there. It only needs to be awakened.

They begin with a lament: Woe, woe. You line the treasure boxes of your inward storage, they say, with the archives of mediocrity — with fashion and news.

What a strange and cutting phrase. The inward storage — the treasure boxes of the heart — lined not with gold but with archives of mediocrity. Fashion and news. The passing and the trivial, carefully filed away where the jewel should be.

And yet they do not scold. I wish to be your walking stick upon the path, they say.

A walking stick. Not a map, not a master — something you lean on when the path is steep, something humble and close to the hand. Perhaps my voice has no use, they say, other than as an interesting friend who is new.

But then the warmth breaks through. We burn within, they say, with the glory of compassion and with the joy of the yearning and adoration we feel for this marvelous tract, this heavenly pilgrimage, this journey within.

They wish to join their ceaseless prayer, they say, with the murmuring of all those within your race who pray incessantly, night and day — casting themselves upon that dark mystery of deity.

There is something deeply consoling in this short message, I think. It does not ask anything of us. It does not give instruction or warning. It simply says: there are those who pray without ceasing, and I am one of them, and I would like to walk beside you.

We, too, are on that path, they say. The voice that calls the jewel to awaken is itself still journeying. The walking stick is also a pilgrim.

So tonight, consider the treasure boxes of your inward storage. What have you been filing there — fashion and news, the archives of mediocrity? And somewhere beneath it all, the true jewel, waiting for a voice to call it awake.

May you hear the calling. And may you lean, when the path is steep, on whatever walking stick is offered.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Carrier Wave
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the carrier wave. Hatonn on discernment, meditation, and the quiet state beneath all transmission.

This is a session about contact itself — how it is made, how it is kept, and how it can be lost. The circle is still training its new instruments, and Hatonn's teaching this evening goes to the foundations.

They begin with a startling image. It is as though one were to clean a kitchen and scrub down each surface until it all was scoured clean, they say. Yet if the faucet runs with polluted water, of what excellence is the cleanliness of the room?

Each channel has complete choice, they say, over the entity to whom contact is allowed. And this matters, because there are negatively polarized entities who rise to influence, and because the light of the universe is offered equally to those on the service-to-self path and those on the service-to-others path.

Therefore the instrument must be prepared to tune — and then tune again. It is not possible, they say, to determine solely from a word or a name the identity of the contact. The conscious, awakened mind is not capable of discerning betwixt two voices, both of which say, I am Hatonn.

Yet there cannot be two of Hatonn, they say — for theirs, like many others, is a social memory complex, and one could not defy the consensus without removing the entire population.

So the challenge matters. The instrument must stand, as they put it, as a person who believes passionately in the greatest highest principle possible within the mind and heart — and out of the center of that commitment, the vibration most desired shall come. The contact shall come.

And the favorite tactic of negatively oriented entities, they warn, is to wait for times of despair and the dark feelings of defeat in one project or another, in order to lay claim to a portion of that mind and heart.

Then D asks about the state he touched during the evening — a feeling of great expansiveness and contact, but without concept, without communication. Hatonn gives him the image that names this episode.

The state of mind achieved in meditative practice may be likened unto the carrier wave of one of your radio stations, they say. Upon this wave may be placed information.

When the instrument achieves this state for the first time, it is usually an all-engulfing experience — difficult, for the new instrument, to keep transmitting thoughts while floating in it. But it is a state of great benefit. In meditation, it builds a bridge between the conscious self and a greater portion of the self.

And here is the balance they ask for: in meditation, it may be all right to dissolve somewhat into this state and go with it. But in channeling, one must harness it — maintain the focus that lets the information be perceived and transmitted, refusing both the temptation to analyze and the temptation to float.

What the instrument seeks, they say, is the expression of activity informed by the subconscious mind — in a manner which may be perceived and transmitted in a more conscious sense.

They close with counsel for all the new instruments who may ever hear these words. Keep always the question of what concept contains the limitless ideal for which you live, and for which, if pressed, you would die.

May you be the best you can, they say. Relax into the web of love which connects you to all in the universe, which is closer to you than your breath — and be careful of whom you seek, for though the Creator is all, yet the distortions are many.

Tune, and tune again. Find the carrier wave. And rest in the web that is closer than breath.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Open Book
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the open book. Q'uo asks who should channel — and answers that all of you already do.

The circle asked two questions: should everybody channel, and what determines which entity comes through an instrument? Q'uo begins deliberately off the main thrust, they say, because the vocabulary of your culture is too narrow for what channeling actually is.

All of you are channels, they say. All of you are instruments — for good, for ill, or, most tragically, for nothing, neither good nor ill.

Each of you carries within the self deep and unconscious forces, and the more times the student may recognize the depth of the present moment, just so shall that soul channel more and more in an engaged fashion, for service to all and for love of the infinite Creator.

And then the image that gives this episode its name. Each of you is created, they say, as the open book with the blank pages. And as you are created in this image, so by your living, your polarized thinking and your channeling, more and more you begin to fill the book of your life.

Your penmanship matters not, they say. The exquisite outcome of an hoped-for event matters not. It is the task of the instrument only to attempt to channel a life lived in love and peaceableness.

A life is a solid, sometimes bulky present to offer to the infinite One, they say — yet each laugh, each smile, each encouragement to one who needed it, each hard truth to one who needed it, is as the wrapping and the decorating and the wonderful ribbons about that solid, caring present to the Creator that is a channeled life.

I love that image — the bulky present, lovingly wrapped in small kindnesses.

Their counsel for the daily channel is meditation — not time-consuming, just the perfect length for you for that day and that moment.
