There is a beautiful passage about what mathematics reveals, when it is approached as a spiritual discipline. In the relationships of number, they say, you can see the fingerprints of the Creator. The harmonies, the symmetries, the impossible elegance of certain proofs, these are not accidents. They are reflections, in the realm of pure form, of the underlying unity of all things. The mathematician who contemplates these harmonies with an open heart is doing the same work as the mystic in meditation. Both are gazing at the infinite through a finite window.

I want to linger on what they say about the limits, because it is the quiet revolution of this session. There comes a point, they say, in every system, where the symbols break down. In language, it is the place where words fail and only silence speaks truly. In mathematics, it is the place where the equations point beyond themselves, to a reality that cannot be calculated, only contemplated. This is not the end of the inquiry. It is the beginning of wisdom. To know where your system ends is to know where the mystery begins.

The voices speak, too, about the temptation to worship the system. It is so easy, they say, to fall in love with the precision, the certainty, the clean lines of a proof, and to mistake that love for love of the truth. But the truth is larger than any proof. The truth is the living reality that the proof points toward. Hold the mathematics lightly, they say. Use it as a ladder. But do not mistake the ladder for the destination. The destination is the direct experience of the unity that the numbers can only suggest.

The closing thought gathers the whole session into a single image. Words end. Numbers end. All systems of notation end, at the shore of an ocean they cannot cross. But the ocean is there. It has always been there. And the purpose of every language, every mathematics, every art, is not to contain the ocean, but to bring you to its shore, so that you can stand at the edge of what you know, and gaze out at what you cannot know, and feel, in the salt air on your face, the presence of the infinite.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are Warriors
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are warriors.

This session begins with a question about the children, and it becomes one of the most searing passages in the archive. The group asks about the young ones incarnating now, the ones who seem to carry so much pain, so much anger, so much confusion. What is happening with them? What do they need? The voice that answers is Latwii, and they do not offer comfort first. They offer truth, and the truth is about the nature of the battlefield every soul has chosen.

You are warriors, they say. Not in the sense of violence, but in the sense of courage. Each entity who incarnates into this density has volunteered for the hardest assignment in the creation. To forget who you are. To walk in darkness. To learn love in a place where love is hard to find. This takes a warrior's heart. And the children coming now, they say, are the bravest of all, for they have chosen to incarnate into a world on the edge of transformation, where the old structures are crumbling and the new ones are not yet built.

I want to be honest about what follows, because it is not easy listening. Latwii speaks of the pain these young ones carry, the abandonment, the neglect, the violence done to their spirits before they are old enough to understand it. They speak of the anger that rises in response, the rage at a world that promised love and delivered indifference. And they do not pathologize it. They honor it. The anger, they say, is the warrior's response to injustice. It is the soul refusing to accept that this is all there is.

Before I go further, let me say one thing in my own voice. This session touches abandonment, despair, and deep suffering. If these words stir something painful in you, please be gentle with yourself, and if the weight feels like too much to carry alone, reach out to someone you trust, a friend, a counselor, someone who can sit with you in the dark.

The teaching turns on the question of what these warriors need. Not pity, they say. Not rescue. Not the condescension of those who believe they have figured it out. What they need is recognition. To be seen as the brave souls they are. To be told the truth, which is that their pain is real, their anger is justified, and their courage in continuing is the very definition of heroism. The world calls them troubled. The voices call them warriors.

There is a beautiful passage about the nature of the healing, when it comes. It does not come from fixing the past, they say. The past cannot be unfixed. It comes from the discovery, in the present, of a love that does not abandon. A love that stays. A love that sees the warrior beneath the wounds and speaks to that warrior directly. One moment of true recognition, they say, can do what years of therapy cannot. Not because therapy is without value, but because the wound is not psychological. It is spiritual. It is the wound of forgetting who you are.

Latwii speaks, too, about the role of those who would help. You cannot save the warriors, they say. You can only stand beside them. You can be the steady presence that proves love is real, not by preaching it, but by embodying it. Show up. Keep showing up. Let your life be the evidence that the darkness is not the whole story. This is the service. Not grand. Not dramatic. Just the daily, unglamorous choice to be a light that does not go out.

I want to linger on the closing image, because it gathers the whole session into a single breath. The warriors are not broken, they say. They are in process. The pain they carry is the price of the courage they showed in coming here. And one day, they say, when the remembering comes, when the veil lifts and they see what they volunteered for and why, they will understand that every wound was a teacher, every abandonment a lesson in self-reliance, every dark night a preparation for the dawn. Until then, they fight. And we who love them, we stand witness to their courage, and we do not look away.

Thank you for listening.

title: Faith and Rage
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: faith and rage.

This session begins with a question that has no easy answer, asked by someone living inside it. How does one hold faith when the body is failing, when the pain is relentless, when the prayers seem to go unanswered? What is the spiritual response to illness, not in theory, but in the middle of the night, when the rage at the unfairness of it all rises up like a tide? The voices answer with a honesty that I find breathtaking, and they begin by refusing to spiritualize the suffering away.

The rage is real, they say. The grief is real. The feeling of betrayal, the sense that the universe has broken its promises, these are not failures of faith. They are the human response to unbearable circumstances, and they deserve to be honored, not suppressed. You do not have to be grateful for the pain. You do not have to find the blessing in it. You are allowed to be angry. You are allowed to grieve. The Creator is large enough to hold your rage.

Before I go further, let me say one thing in my own voice. This session speaks of serious illness and the emotional storm that comes with it. If you are walking through something like this, please be gentle with yourself, and lean on the real supports in your life, the people who love you, the caregivers and counselors who can help carry what feels uncarryable.

The teaching turns on the nature of faith itself, and here the voices offer a redefinition that I want you to hear slowly. Faith, they say, is not the belief that everything will be all right. It is not the confidence that the pain will end, or the illness will lift, or the prayers will be answered in the way you hope. Faith is something smaller, and something vastly larger. It is the willingness to remain in relationship with the mystery, even when the mystery does not explain itself. It is the choice to keep the heart open, even when the heart is breaking.

I love the image they give for this kind of faith. It is not the faith of the mountaintop, they say. It is the faith of the valley. The faith that whispers, in the dark, I do not understand, but I am still here. I am still reaching. I have not let go. This faith does not require you to feel peaceful. It does not require you to feel grateful. It requires only that you do not close the door. That you leave it open, even a crack, for the love that is trying to reach you.

There is a beautiful passage about the relationship between the rage and the faith, and it is the heart of this session. They are not opposites, they say. The rage is the measure of the love. You rage because you love life, because you love the people you may leave, because you love the future you imagined and now grieve. The rage is love, turned inside out by pain. And the faith is the container that holds them both. It does not resolve the tension. It sanctifies it.

The voices speak, too, about the loneliness of the suffering, the way illness separates you from the world of the well, the way even loving people cannot follow you into the place where the pain lives. And they offer a truth for that loneliness. You are not alone in the aloneness, they say. The Creator is in the pain with you. Not watching from a distance. Not waiting for you to get through it. In it. The divine does not exempt itself from suffering. It enters it, fully, with you.

I want to linger on the closing counsel, because it is practical in a way that honors the reality. Do not try to feel what you do not feel, they say. If you feel rage, feel rage. If you feel grief, grieve. The spiritual path is not the suppression of the human. It is the holding of the human in a larger love. And on the days when you cannot hold it yourself, let others hold it for you. Let yourself be carried. This, too, is faith. The faith that receives.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Sacred Spot
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the sacred spot.

This session is unlike any other in this group of episodes, because it is not a teaching delivered from above. It is a story, built collaboratively, in the moment, by the channel and the voice together. The voice is Laitos, and the occasion is a small intensive gathering, a few days of deep work. What emerges is a parable, and like all true parables, it is simple on the surface and bottomless underneath.

The story begins with a family. A mother, a father, and two children, a brother and a sister. They live in a place of great beauty, a garden, a sacred spot, where everything they need is provided. The children play. The parents watch with love. It is, in the telling, an Eden, though the word is never used. The sacred spot is not a location. It is a state of belonging.

Then comes the rupture, as it always does in such stories. The brother and sister quarrel. It is the ancient quarrel, over nothing and over everything. Words are said that cannot be unsaid. And in the heat of it, they leave. They walk away from the sacred spot, from the garden, from the parents who love them. They go out into the world, and the world, as the world does, teaches them its lessons.

I love the patience of the telling here. Laitos does not rush the wandering. The siblings experience poverty. They experience loss. They know hunger, and cold, and the particular loneliness of those who have chosen their exile. They meet others who are also wandering, and they learn, slowly, painfully, what it means to be separate. The sacred spot recedes into memory, and memory, as memory does, gilds it. Was it ever that beautiful? Did they imagine it? The doubt is part of the exile.

Then, in the way of parables, comes the turning. It is not dramatic. There is no thunderclap. There is simply a moment, in the midst of the hardship, when the brother looks at the sister, and the sister looks at the brother, and they remember. Not the garden as it was, but the love that made it a garden. They remember that they belong to each other. And in that remembering, the sacred spot is not behind them. It is within them. It was never a place they left. It was a love they carried.

The return, when it comes, is quiet. They walk back, not as the children who left, but as those who have learned what the leaving was for. The parents receive them, not with reproach, but with the joy of those who never stopped watching the road. And the sacred spot is restored, not as it was, but as something deeper. A belonging that has been tested by exile and chosen again, freely.

I want to linger on what Laitos says this story means, because the interpretation is the teaching. The sacred spot, they say, is the open heart. The garden is the state of love before the learning begins. The quarrel is the inevitable friction of incarnation, the moment the soul chooses separation in order to learn what unity means. The wandering is the life you are living now, with its poverty and loss and loneliness. And the return is not a place you go. It is a recognition you make, that the love you have been seeking in exile was within you the entire time.

There is a gentleness in the closing of this session that feels earned by the story. You have never left the sacred spot, they say. You have only dreamed that you left. And every moment of remembering, every act of love, every forgiveness offered and received, is a step on the road home. The road is not long. It was never long. It is the distance between forgetting and remembering, and it can be crossed in a single breath.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Protection of Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the protection of light.

This session comes from a small intensive gathering, a few days of concentrated work, and it is focused on something the archive returns to again and again. Protection. Not protection from the world, but the kind of spiritual protection a seeker builds from the inside, through visualization, through intention, through the deliberate claiming of identity. The voice is Laitos, and the teaching is practical from the first sentence.

They begin with the energy centers, the chakras, and they describe them not as abstract concepts but as living realities. Each center, they say, is a gateway. Each one processes a different quality of the infinite energy that flows through you. The lower centers handle the basic business of incarnation, survival, relationship, power. The heart is the great transformer, turning the personal into the universal. The upper centers open onto communication, vision, and finally, the gateway to intelligent infinity itself.

I love the way they make this intimate rather than technical. You do not need to master the system, they say. You need to befriend it. Sit with each center. Breathe into it. Feel where it is open and where it is guarded. The body knows what the mind has forgotten. And as you attend to each gateway in turn, you are doing something the voices consider essential. You are declaring, in the language the deeper self understands, that you are ready to be a conscious participant in your own transformation.

Then comes the visualization at the heart of the session, and it is worth doing as you listen. See yourself, they say, surrounded by white light. Not as a metaphor. As a reality. The light is the love of the Creator, made visible to the inner eye. Draw it close. Let it fill the space around you, above you, below you. Feel it as a warmth, a presence, a shield. This is not imagination, they say. Imagination is the faculty by which the spiritual senses perceive what is real.

The teaching deepens with the question of identity. Who is it that stands within this light? And here Laitos offers the declaration that gives this episode its weight. You are a child of the infinite Creator, they say. This is not a metaphor. It is not a religious formula. It is the literal truth of what you are. And to declare it, consciously, deliberately, in the face of doubt and fear and the noise of the world, is an act of spiritual power. Say it, they say. I am a child of the infinite Creator. Feel the truth of it settle into the bones.

There is a beautiful passage about what this declaration does. It aligns you, they say. Like a compass needle finding north, the self, when it remembers what it is, orients itself toward the light automatically. The fears do not vanish. The challenges do not disappear. But they are met from a different place now. Not from the small self, scrambling for safety, but from the true self, resting in its identity. This is the protection. Not a wall against the world, but a rootedness so deep that the storms cannot move it.

I want to linger on what they say about the daily practice, because the session is insistent that this is not a one-time working. Each morning, they say, renew the declaration. Each evening, give thanks for the protection. Make it as regular as the rising of the sun. The spiritual life, they remind us, is not built in moments of ecstasy. It is built in the quiet repetition of small acts of remembrance, until the remembrance becomes the ground you walk on.

The closing thought is simple, and it is the whole teaching. You are loved, they say. You are protected. Not because you have earned it, but because it is the nature of the Creator to love and protect its own. Rest in this. Declare it. Live from it. And let the white light you have visualized be the visible sign of an invisible truth. You were never alone. You were never unguarded. You are a child of the light, walking in the light, protected by the light.

Thank you for listening.

title: Loving Intensely
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: loving intensely.

The last session in this group of episodes comes from another small intensive gathering, and it is about the bravest thing a group of seekers can do. Tell the truth about themselves, to each other, out loud. The voice is Latwii, and the teaching is about the relationship between self-revelation and love, between the masks we wear and the intimacy we crave.

They begin with the paradox of the group. You have gathered, they say, because you want to know and be known. And yet each of you arrives wearing the careful constructions of a lifetime, the personas, the defenses, the polished surfaces. This is not dishonesty. It is habit. The self learned early that some parts are welcome and some are not, and it arranged itself accordingly. But the arrangement, however necessary it once was, is now the barrier between you and the love you seek.

I love the directness of the counsel. Tell the truth, they say. Not the polished truth. Not the spiritualized truth. The real one. Speak of your fears. Speak of your failures. Speak of the places where you feel unlovable. For it is precisely in the speaking of the unlovable that the love becomes real. As long as you present only the acceptable self, the love you receive will feel, to the deeper heart, unearned. It is loving the mask, not the face.

There is a beautiful passage about what happens when one person goes first. Courage, they say, is contagious. When one member of the group risks the truth, the others feel the permission to do the same. The room changes. The air gets thinner, clearer. What was performance becomes presence. And in that presence, something the voices consider sacred occurs. You see each other, actually see, and you discover that the feared unlovability was a fiction. The others do not recoil. They lean in. They recognize themselves in your confession.

Latwii speaks, too, about the intensity of this kind of love, and it is the intensity that gives the episode its title. This is not the mild, polite affection of acquaintances, they say. This is loving intensely. Loving with the whole heart, without the hedges and qualifications. It is risky, they admit. To love intensely is to make yourself vulnerable to loss, to disappointment, to the pain of caring deeply in a world where everything changes. But the alternative, they say, is a far greater pain. The pain of never having loved at all.

I want to linger on what they say about the relationship between this love and the spiritual path itself, because it reframes the whole endeavor. The path is not solitary, they say. It was never meant to be. The lone mystic on the mountaintop is a beautiful image, but it is incomplete. You learn love by loving. You learn it in the friction of real relationship, in the daily practice of seeing the other clearly and choosing them anyway. The group is not a distraction from the work. The group is the work.

The closing counsel is for the moments when the truth-telling feels like too much, when the vulnerability threatens to overwhelm. Go slowly, they say. You do not have to reveal everything at once. Trust is built in layers, and each layer of truth offered and received makes the next one possible. But do not stop. Keep moving toward the center, toward the real. For at the center, beneath all the constructions, is the self you have been seeking. And that self, they say, is love, waiting to be known.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hollowed Channel
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hollowed channel.

It is a summer evening in nineteen ninety, and Latwii has come to speak to a small circle of meditators about the energy centers of the body, one by one, from the root to the brow. What follows is a journey upward through the self, ending somewhere neither the speakers nor the listeners quite expected.

They begin where the body begins, in the red ray. The full and open heart, Latwii says, is one that accepts all the energies of life as beautiful. It embraces its own physical vehicle, sending light to every cell. Listen to this image, because it is one of the loveliest of the whole evening. Wherever there is any darkness in the body, picture light moving there, oceans and oceans of bubbles of light, refreshing, easing, comforting, cleansing, renewing each cell.

I love that they do not stop at imagery. In the full acceptance of this body that is yours within the illusion, they say, is the full healing of this body. Find the way in your heart to love all aspects of it, never to begrudge it. And then they move on, because the road goes up from there.

In the orange ray there is the dance of one relationship at a time, the first movement outward from the self, a trading of energies between you and one other person. Where the exchange is blocked by imperfect communication, they say, balance it, so the energy can move freely without distortion. Then comes the yellow ray, the center of groups and institutions, where the work is done on attitudes, and the only way through is to accept that the illusion is as it should be. Then the green ray, the heart itself, where the keynote is love and compassion, and where something is born that they call the most important endowment an aspirant to truth may find. A sense of purpose, born in the heart center.

From there the road turns creative. The blue ray is the power of expression, the joy of creation as it occurs, the first center that may act creatively. And the indigo ray, between the brows, is the center of insight, where concepts do not stand alone but join like small streams into larger ones, flowing together toward a single source. And here they tell us what they call the most basic secret known and knowable in indigo ray. That if you ask, you will indeed receive, for in truth the asking is the receiving. The seeking is the finding.

But the evening takes a turn when Latwii returns to talk about channeling itself. Here is where the title of tonight's episode comes from. The new instrument, they say, keeps trying to look ahead, to know what is coming next, to teach. And teaching is exactly what a channel must surrender. Channeling, they say, is a teaching in which one surrenders all desires to teach, to make sense, or to do anything except to listen, to feel, to be, to float in that highest tuning which may be held in a stable manner.

The image they offer is one I want to hold onto. In this surrender, each thought opens like a flower, and bloom and beauty and lightness enhance the communication. To be a good instrument, they say, is to become a completely hollowed channel, with neither the preconceived idea nor the desire to know what is next, simply offering itself as an open instrument. The crutches that help at the beginning, the looking ahead, the rush of energy, all of these must eventually be laid down.

And then this, which feels like the real heart of the whole evening. Let yourself be a channel of wonder and mystery and astonishment to yourself. Allow this. It cannot be wanted. It cannot be desired and therefore gotten. It must be desired and then released. The true courage, they say, lies in that sweet surrender to the unknown which guides you and all, in infinite love, in the full and open heart.

All of it comes back to the daily work, done quietly. The effect of consistent daily meditation, they say, is not felt suddenly, but it is the surest and only safe approach to spiritual growth that one may take. So take heart, and in a quiet joy go about your daily routine, knowing that nothing you do will put you so far from the love and the light of the one Creator that you are beyond redemption. All is acceptable. You are of the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: Cut the Bond
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: cut the bond.

Hatonn comes on a summer evening in nineteen ninety with one of the most practical teachings in the whole archive. The question is simple and hard. How do you deal with a person who drains you dry, someone whose presence feels like a leech on your very life? Listen for what Hatonn does not do. He does not scold. He does not simplify. He starts by telling you that you have free will, and that no one can take it from you.

First, he says, understand how the hold works. It is usually long habit or love. You have let this person into your private inner space because you loved them, and they have used that access to drain you. The first step is to take back, in your mind's eye, the right to that intimacy. He is wonderfully concrete about it. It is as though, he says, you take the scissors and you cut the bond. Some people press their fingers across the area just above the navel, where the attachment tends to fasten, and imagine cutting it, sealing it, and standing protected in the full armor of the love and the light of the infinite Creator.

The second step is the silence. Do not listen to the sense of what the draining person is saying. Let it be, he says, like a bubbling brook, or a news show coming from a television in the house next door. You may hear, but you do not have to attend. A vampiric nature, as he calls it, feeds on fear and demands control. Where there is no fear and no control, it cannot feed.

The third step is the walking away. Move to the room with the lock and lock it. Leave the dwelling if you must, and find peace in a place known only to yourself. And here I want to pause and say something plainly, as your friend. If you are living with someone who hurts you, you deserve real help, not just a teaching. Reach out to someone you trust, or to a local line or service that helps people in your situation. You are allowed to protect yourself in the outer world too, not only in meditation.

But Hatonn does not stop at protection. Underneath all of it, he says, there is slower work, and it is the lesson of love held herein. Pray for those who despitefully use you. Pray for your enemies. For what good is it to pray for those you already love? As you grow strong inside, pray to forgive, and then pray to forgive the you that was weak enough to fall for such nonsense as that of a vampire who wished to make you a prey. Forgiveness, he says, stops the karmic tie that binds you to this person. In forgiveness is personal freedom.

I love the tenderness of what comes next. When you are discouraged and at your weakest, he says, picture yourself in the arms of the Creator, nurtured and cradled and loved, infinitely, infinitely loved. Let that female, divine principle rock you and hold you until your pain is quieted and your faith reawakened. Nurture yourself again and again, as many times as it takes, until you may rest in bliss and quietness and renew your strength of spirit.

And here is the strangest and most beautiful turn of the evening. Hatonn tells the group that the channel herself needed these words too, for she too faces the vampire, the impersonal one called pain. Your pain has eyes, a face, a form, and a seeming reality, he says. Yet pain, of heart or soul or mind or body, is of one and the same nature. It is the vampire which must be faced, loved, forgiven, realized as part of the self, taken into the self, and made so much a part of the self that there is no longer any fear, no longer any adversity, no longer any struggle. Such, he says, is the power of your own faith in love.

So claim your birthright, he says, as loving children of a loving Creator. Do the work of forgiveness, no matter how long it takes. Pray the prayers that cut the bonds. And know this. You are, as all are, equal spirits. Each of you is the warrior self, completely calm at the center, completely relaxed, and able to respond in compassion and courage and in effectiveness to those attacks which are perceived.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Martyr and the Mystic
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the martyr and the mystic.

In June of nineteen ninety, the group asked Q'uo about two words that are often tangled together. The martyr and the mystic. What are they, how are they alike, and how are they different? What follows is one of the clearest things Q'uo ever said about both, and it ends with a piece of advice I think about often.

A mystic, they say, is not one thing. The word covers any number of things, but at bottom it means someone who chooses a non-literal way of seeing the world. There are no two mystics whose paths are the same. The mystic is one who says, I do not need an objective referent to believe that something is there. The mystic believes that which it does not see, and has faith in that which cannot be touched, or felt, or measured.

I love how they put the value of it. The mystic looks through the bars of the prison of third density and sees that there is more. Whether these entities are called philosophers, or fools, or poets, or men of god, they have a vision of the way the world is, to which those who hear it resonate. And the planet itself is enriched by the mystical view, by the love of mystery and the withholding of judgment that accompanies the mystic grasp that we do not, nor can we, know anything for certain.

The martyr is a more specific word. It means the entity which chooses to allow itself to be used, even unto death, in service to something it holds greater than itself. And here Q'uo makes a distinction worth sitting with. There are those who martyr themselves for ideals, and there are those who martyr themselves for idols. Many are martyrs to idols, they say. The mother who abandons all personal hope and dreams to serve the demands of the family. The student who worships the teacher instead of seeing through the teacher to the Creator. Excessive and unnecessary self-sacrifice, they say, binds you karmically to the one idolized, just as surely as cruelty would.

So when is it wise to lay yourself down? Q'uo is gentle and firm about this. If the situation of martyrdom is not placed in front of you, they say, it is never necessary to create a martyr's path. Do not go looking for the cross. They remind us of Jesus in the garden, praying the night before he accepted his martyrdom. I know my time has come, he prayed. I see the cup I am to drink in front of me. I am afraid of the pain. If it is possible, move this cup away from my lips. And when the cup stayed, he said, not my will, but Thine be done.

The great error, they say, of those with mystical leanings, is to choose self-sacrifice when it is not at all necessary, and when it may actually make another entity's road longer, because the other never has to take responsibility for itself. Martyrdom for an idol is a kind of idolatry. There is but one Creator. Unless your self-sacrifice is a clear communication of an ideal to others, it has a karmic element, which then must be balanced.

And then comes the part I keep returning to, the true wisdom of martyrdom. Do not offer your body on any cross. Offer up, instead, the stale and unhealthy parts of yourself, the self-perceived sicknesses of mind and body and spirit, on the cross of change and transformation, so that the rest of you may live, and be renewed, and be more and more who you truly are. Your own dualism is the cross you bear. Drag it to its hill, and crucify it there.

So which are you, mystic or martyr? Perhaps, Q'uo suggests, you are a little of both. Believe what you cannot see. Serve what you love. But do not make yourself the sacrifice unless life itself places the cup in front of you. And remember that you are always dealing with your colleagues, each entity an imperishable and perfect light being, neither higher nor lower than you. There is no possibility of being a martyr, they say, as long as you remember that.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Currency of Forgiveness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the currency of forgiveness.

On a June day in nineteen ninety, the group asked Latwii about forgiveness. What is its purpose, what is its method, and who needs it in any situation? The answer that came back is one of the longest and most passionate discourses in the archive, and its central claim is startling in its simplicity. Forgiveness begins with the self.

They start with karma, which they describe in a way I have never forgotten. Karma, they say, is that energy held in dynamic tension with another entity where the intransigent desires of the self live. When someone wrongs you and you cannot let it go, the inertia of karma goes merrily along singing a repetitive song of, I got you, I got you, and the other person, admitting guilt, says, he has got me, he has got me. And so the wheel turns, lifetime after lifetime. Only one thing stops the wheel of karma, they say, and that is total forgiveness.

But here is the part most of us get backwards. The key to forgiveness of others, they say, is the forgiveness of the self. There is always a lack of forgiveness of the self, they say, that seems to be held more tightly than the forgiveness of others. You gaze too closely into the mirror of this illusion and your manifestation within it. So they ask you to gaze at yourself as a most loving mother would. Forgive yourself, accept yourself, allow yourself to be yourself. Release, release, release, they say, give back to the forces of the universe those energies which are easily absorbed in infinity, and let forgiveness flow as a sweet river under the surface of all that you do and say.

I love the practical turn they take next. When you have not forgiven the difficult things, you will be speaking with a hard heart, and your judgment will be unfair. Only self-forgiven, they say, can you enter into the forgiveness of others. And this is not about pretending everything is fine. Do not abandon your biases, they say. You have earned them. Do not simply say that all things are acceptable. You are miles and miles away from that elevation. First you must learn to love, and you must learn to have wisdom, and you must learn to have compassionate wisdom.

And what if someone is truly abusive, truly dangerous? Latwii is clear about this, and I want to be clear too. Forgiving a person, they say, does not mean you must keep accepting acts that put you or your children in danger, in mind or body. If you see that union is impossible, do what you must do, with love and compassion and peace, staying within the forgiveness. Leave if you must. Forgiveness is an inner release, not a requirement to stay. If you are in a situation like that now, please seek real help from people you trust, as well as these words.

Then they give us the image I will carry from this session. Be the Johnny Appleseed of forgiveness, they say. For forgiveness is the essence of what they call the Kingdom of Heaven, and the seeds of forgiveness are like leaven, that lighten and lift and make delicious the whole loaf of life. And then they offer this beautiful thought. Forgiveness is a universal currency, a kind of money, since your people are so interested in the power that money has. Spend that currency with a whole heart.

They close with the story of the two thieves on the cross beside Jesus. One did not ask for forgiveness, and remained in karma and imbalance. The other turned and asked, will you remember me, please, when you come into your kingdom? And the broken and dying lover of mankind replied, this day you shall be with me in paradise. May you turn from error when it is perceived, they say, without being discouraged that you have made an error, and ask forgiveness. Deep within yourself there is the redemptive and forgiving self. Allow it to flood you, allow it to make you thankful, and know that you are self-forgiven.

So tonight, whatever you are carrying, whatever old song of I got you is still playing in your head, consider this an invitation to put it down. You are, as Latwii says, a treasure, a child of the infinite One. And all of it, every dish you wash, every floor you sweep, is alive to the light within you, if it is done in utter and complete love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Laughter Quotient
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the laughter quotient.

In June of nineteen ninety, the group asked Q'uo a question many of us have asked in private. How do we make our way through the illusion when the catalyst, the difficulties and confusions and challenges, feels overwhelming and never ending? Q'uo answered with three resources. The first is yourself. The second is service. And the third, which gives tonight's episode its name, is laughter.

The first resource is the way you handle yourself. Do you handle yourself, they ask, as if you were a precious Chinese vase? May we say that no, you do not. And yet how much more precious are you than such a man-made artifact. How little you value yourselves. You cannot cope with a life, they say, for a life is an illusion. The only real thing in it is each imperishable spirit. It is not circumstances which overwhelm you, but your choice of reaction to circumstance.

So the first resource is self-love, and they mean it in the most practical sense. When you are hurt, they say, you cannot run to your mother anymore and hide your head upon her lap. You must be that nurturing mother-self to yourself. You must treat yourself well. This is not service to self. For if you cannot treat yourself well, out of a pure and unconditional love for yourself, with all of your imperfections and errors, then how can you love and serve those about you?

The second resource is service, but not the kind you might picture. The service-to-others path seems simple, they say. One pictures oneself as a kind of celestial waitress, bussing the tables of humanity, splitting the great sea so friends may cross dry shod. That is not it. Each entity needs room to learn for itself. Sometimes the greatest service is to allow a being that depends on you to make it safe, to make mistakes. What you offer instead is an atmosphere in which learning is safe, a relaxed and welcoming aura which invites entities to feel safety and peace when they are around you.

And then the third resource, which they admit the instrument thought they were taking too long to reach. Humor. People who are extremely serious about accelerating their spiritual evolution, they say, have a tendency to sound like boatmen putting their poles in the deep rivers and pushing slowly to make the great barge move. This is not the true nature of spiritual evolution. The laughter quotient, they say, of your days should be gradually moving upward. More things should be transparent to you, and therefore deeply humorous in that humor that goes beyond the smile and warms the heart.

For this life that you experience, they say, is the joke without the punch line. You play the second banana to yourself. As you gain perspective and see yourself as a soap opera character, a cartoon character, a creature that may be ridiculous and still be safe, secure, and undaunted, so will you lose the many layers of fear which cause you to armor against the delightfulness of life. They are not being flippant. They know the world is full of injustice. But they ask, shall you be the cynic, who is usually correct for the moment? Or the idealist, who suffers for the ideal now, but finds in a millennium or so that the ideal still holds true?

They close with two small assignments, and I pass them on to you. First, sit quietly and watch your grass grow. You will be delighted by the life teeming all around you. The glory of the sky, the beauty of the foliage, the music of the laughter of children. How funny and beautiful is your illusion, if you can but slow down and look at it? And second, laugh. Not a giggle, not a chuckle. Lose yourself. Find that one thing that, for you, takes you out of yourself. All of you are in need of healing, they say, and laughter is the medicament.

So love and nurture and honor yourself, love and nurture and honor others who are all yourselves, and be merry in your love. Give to your life the light touch. You are not working on the world, they say. You are working upon yourself.

Thank you for listening.

title: Chopping Wood
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: chopping wood.

This evening is different from most in the archive. It is an intensive session in June of nineteen ninety, devoted not to a teaching but to practice. Latwii moves from channel to channel, tuning three instruments, teaching them the art of channeling itself. And the phrase that holds the whole evening together is this one. Chopping wood.

By chopping wood they mean the preparation, the unglamorous work before the words ever come. The tuning, the challenging, the centering, done scrupulously every time, naming who you are as the contact comes and as it leaves. Whatever we have to say, they tell the group, can be summed up in two words, and you know what they are. Love and light. That is the thought and the material that is all that there is in this creation.

What I love most about this session is how honest it is about the difficulty of the work. The mind of the channel is never completely pure, they say. Stray thoughts will come. Side thoughts will come. And here is their advice, which I think applies far beyond channeling, to meditation, to prayer, to any attempt to listen deeply. Regard the stray thoughts, they say, with as little significance as one would regard the wind rustling through the branches of your trees as you converse with a friend below. If you fix your attention on the wind, the contact is lost. Let it rustle. Keep listening.

They speak to the new instrument, the one called K, who is frightened by the pauses, who panics when the flow stops and tries to fill the silence with patter. And they give her an image I will not forget. They show her a cat, the household cat, who frequently frightens itself so that it jumps at its own movement, and then jumps again at the jump. This, they say gently, is the activity within your mind. The remedy is simple and takes much practice. Relax the worry, the analysis, the panic, as the surface of a pond is moved by the wind. Move below the surface activity and sink more and more deeply to the bottom of the pond, to the bottom of the mind, so that you may perceive that which is given.

And then this permission, which feels like the heart of the teaching. Rest within the pause, they say, confident that there shall be a continuation. If you need time, say so. Say, I need to take a minute here, do not go away. They are quite happy, they say, to work within whatever format lets the instrument mount again the horse which has thrown it. They applaud, they say, this dedication and perseverance.

Near the end of the evening they offer something for all of us, not just channels. Set aside a time of meditation each day, they say, and within it build yourself a symbol that holds the feeling of comfort. A cup that is full. A landscape. A fragrance. A piece of music. Fill that symbol with the peace you find in meditation. Then, in the busier portions of the day, when there is a chance for a small breather, whether for seconds or minutes, return to the symbol, and let the peace transfer.

Chopping wood. The daily, humble, repeated work. Review what has been set in place by conscious design, they say, so that you might more fully and freely exercise your instrument in service to others. Do not judge yourself because the work is imperfect. A perfect instrument, they say, is a useful concept for making goals, but not at all necessary in expectation.

Thank you for listening.

title: Choose the Comedy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: choose the comedy.

In July of nineteen ninety, the group brought Q'uo a question born of fear. People were reporting frightening encounters with strange entities, and rumors were spreading of coming enslavement, and many sincere seekers felt helpless, as though their free will were about to be taken from them. What would Q'uo say to people who feel that afraid?

What I admire about the answer is where it begins. Not with the phenomena, but with you. You yourself, they say, are not either a good person or a bad person. You are, if you consider good and bad as the full circle of being, a three hundred and sixty degree being. It is by your choices that you define who you are. And the single most important thing they want you to hear is this. There is nothing to fear.

They explain, in their way, that there are those who serve others and those who serve the self, and that both paths are real, and that the negative path, too, is a path that leads to the Creator, though it is a difficult and long one. The drama of your density, they say, is weighted to seem sometimes on the side of the negative. This is necessary. It is the background against which each of you shall make a choice so important that the remainder of millions of your years will depend upon it.

But here is the turn. Those gray figures, or any entity or situation whatsoever which attempts to make you feel helpless and out of control, they say, are completely malleable and transformable by love, love unhindered by any fear. Positive entities can gaze at one of the loyal opposition, as they playfully call them, and find in the contact an opportunity to realize that this entity too is a part of the self, and is to be loved, and blessed, and prayed for, and taken into the heart.

I want to be careful here, as your friend. If you have had an experience that frightened you, in the night sky or anywhere else, your fear is real and deserves respect. What Q'uo is offering is not a dismissal of your experience, but a way to stand inside it without being ruled by it. Whatever frightens you loses its power to steer you, they suggest, the moment you meet it with steady love instead of panic.

And then they make their two requests, which I find wonderfully down to earth for such a cosmic evening. First, find a path that includes love of the infinite One shown as worship, adoration, or simple attention, on a daily basis. Daily time spent in silence, listening for the voice that is silent but speaks so loudly. Second, be lighthearted and merry. Find every chance to be joyful. For the most serious choices of millions of years are being made by you now, they say, and you would be crushed by your own solemnity did you not have the saving grace of a sense of humor.

See the illusion, they say, not only as the life and death choices that they are, but also as part of the unimaginably funny human comedy of the soap opera that is called third-density experience. Oh, how high your emotions run, and how important everything seems. Step back whenever you feel too intensely disturbed. Step back, and see the thousands of years that lie before and after this moment. If you are upset with someone, be ridiculous with them mentally. Take the clown's bat and harmlessly bat them about with it, while the circus audience laughs. Do whatever is necessary to break the spell of the illusion, and then gaze up at the stars, and know that you are a player upon a stage.

You may make it a comedy or a tragedy, they say, of this fifth act of the play. It is not anyone's choice but your own. So choose the comedy. Choose love without fear. And remember that you create your life. You do not merely react to it.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are Made of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are made of love.

This is one of the shortest and sweetest sessions in the archive, a potluck evening in July of nineteen ninety. Hatonn comes through with a message he calls quite simple, so simple as to be unbelievable by most of your people. Here it is, in his words. You are made of love because love wished to know itself.

The Creator loves you, he says, as a mother and a father and as a student of itself. All the conversations you have are conversations of gripping interest you created, for it is listening with gripping interest, the self speaking about the self. And it was courageous, he says, in this creation, giving each of its children free will. Each may choose to love or not to love the true Creator of its spirit.

Then he offers an image for the whole spiritual path. You are on a climb, ever upward, and beyond each crest you reach there is another range, and another beyond that. The choice, he says, is what you give your attention to. The soreness of your lungs, the tediousness of the journey, the pain of stepping on rocks. Or the sky and the clouds above you, the trees, the wildflowers, the small creatures that join you along the way, the companions who walk beside you for a little distance or all the way to the top. Shall you focus on the irritations of your traveling companions, or look for what joy and merriment may be made together? The choice, he says, is yours as to what type of journey you will experience. He urges you, his children, to make it a merry one.

And then the teaching turns inward, to the question of identity that was on everyone's mind that evening. He speaks of the channel herself, who loves others so much and yet is so upset with herself. This, he says, is the mark of a service-to-others entity who has left out but one very important step. The realization that before one can love one's neighbor as oneself, one must love oneself.

This instrument has yearned for nurturing from others, he says, and nurturing lies within the self. The gentle rocking in the cradle is the rocking in the arms of the Creator. Why is it, he asks, that she forgives others instantly, yet begrudges herself her own humanity? Each seeking entity, he says, finds everyone easier to love than the self, because the self knows each thought, each self-perceived error. Where it would forgive instantly such behavior in others, it begrudges itself its own humanity.

So here is his assignment, and I give it to you as he gave it to them. Spend time each day to fall in love with yourself, for you are a child of God. The Creator loves you with a love so passionate no words could express it. The Creator loves just precisely who and what you are. And in meditation, in the deepest part of yourself, say to yourself, I love you with my whole heart. That love, he says, that thought, is the lesson of this density.

Each of you needs someone's help in loving yourself, he says. That is why we ask each of you to love each other. The companions reach out the hand of the Creator to you and call out, I love you. These are the words of the Creator. So be that voice for someone today. And let someone be that voice for you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Deep Memories
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the deep memories.

In July of nineteen ninety, Q'uo spoke to the group about meditation, and about what meditation opens. Not calm, exactly, though calm comes. Something stranger. The deep memories that lie within, nibbling at the edges of consciousness.

In meditation, they say, you begin to expand your awareness of half-buried recognitions. Thoughts not running through your mind as in a daydream, but thoughts with which you are deeply familiar, to which you turn your conscious attention for further pondering and integration. Things that seem half remembered. Entities that seem so familiar, yet with no conscious link in this incarnation. Each of you, they say, is aware of the deeper self, the metaphysical entity, the imperishable light being, and the connection on that level of all the entities of this planet.

And there are moments when the illusion is penetrated, when the connection with some other self is made, and the awareness of the other self as Creator brings a momentary dispelling of the illusory bonds of flesh and societal structure. What comfort there is in such connections, they say. The response is often one of joy, of remembered community. Peace and love and ease of being.

They speak too of the wanderers among us, those whose tasks feel even more arduous because the heaviness of this illusion weighs more on those accustomed to greater degrees of light. To them, and to all of us, Q'uo offers this encouragement. Allow yourselves to be encouraged by the glimpses of the deeper reality behind the illusion. Know that you exist in truth in that deeper reality, that you may contact it at any time in meditation. Within the shell of third-density flesh that surrounds you, they say, your beingness shines with a radiance so bright that were you fully aware of it, your joy could not be contained.

There is a thread of pain running through this evening, the channel's own pain, which she asks about with heartbreaking honesty. And I want to say this gently, as your friend. There is nothing noble required of you in suffering. If you live with pain, please be tender with yourself, and lean on whatever care and comfort is available to you, in body and in spirit. What Q'uo offers her is not a cure but a companionship. They tell her that though the price is great, the reward is greater, and that her feet, though the steps are painful, are ever planted on the trail, and the progress steady.

And for all of us they leave this simple charge. Look for the joy in all things, they say. Savor it. Choose the light touch, the merry twinkle in the eye, the smile when none was expected. These things mean more than you think. For on the metaphysical level, those things of greatest value lie in the areas of intention and in the state of being. So be who you are, my friends. Be light, be love, be joy.

Love is long, they say, and time is fleeting. The days are short. Make them light-filled.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Life in Faith
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a life in faith.

In July of nineteen ninety, the group asked Q'uo how we drop old patterns and find new ones, how we release the behaviors that have supported us for so long but no longer serve, and how we know the new pattern is truly ours. Q'uo answered with a long meditation on faith, and on the difference between faith and belief.

Faith, they say, is not belief. It has seemed to them, watching your peoples, that rigid belief systems kill faith and destroy being, giving the person instead the choice of behaving instead of being, and holding on dependently to a set of rules. They suggest that all belief systems be examined, and none taken up blindly. A life in faith, they say, is a life without words, for there are no words to express faith. Faith is a basic attitude that one finds because one wills it, and because as a result of willing to know the truth, it comes to you.

And what is faith, in practice? It is the willingness to keep choosing. Choice is change, they say, make no mistake. Each choice that you make will change you, and you will feel pain and discomfort, because it is painful to change. Some truths will remain the same forever for you. Some truths will be outgrown, and must be let go.

I love the tenderness with which they speak of our mistakes. Instead of saying, oh, two plus two does not equal five, say, oh, I have learned something, two plus two equals four. That is the nature of mistakes, of all errors. Like an error in arithmetic, simply seen, and slowly and carefully replaced by the truth. Should you chastise yourself when you err? Please, my friends, they say, if you wish to attain your goal, never chastise the self, but form all internal dialogue positively.

Because the voices that chastise you are rarely your own. The voices of childhood parents and authority figures still ring in the heart's ear, they say, with negative expressions and warnings and judgments. Many of the most difficult portions of your lives are difficult because you are still listening to these voices. When you hear them, they say, answer with the positive affirmation of that old criticism. When you were small you could not defend yourself, but you can defend yourself now. You can live a life of faith in which no voice on the Earth, over or under the Earth, no discarnate voice, none whatsoever, need have power over you.

There is none better than you, they say, and there is none worse. You are made of precisely the same infinite intelligence and free will as every spirit in the infinite universe. You are a portion of the Creator, which is everything. And so the choices are yours. They do not have to be handed to you by society, by friends, or parents, or spouses, or the ubiquitous they. Remove them, they say, from the voices you wish to grow with.

They give two tools for the work of changing patterns. The first is forgiveness, always forgiveness, beginning with the self. How can you love your neighbor in utter and open forgiveness if you have not forgiven yourself? The second is companionship. Tell those you trust what you wish to accomplish, and ask them to be mirrors for you. Good friends, they say, will not please you by ignoring what you asked their help with. They will choose to seem harsh, because you asked for a mirror you could count on. Rich indeed, they say, is the pilgrim who has many companions along the way.

So may you love yourself infinitely, for you are a child of God. Your mother, your father, is the universe, love itself. Rest, and have peace and confidence in who you really are. And when you fail and fail and fail again, as you will inevitably think that you do, never chide yourself, but with patience and care and love grasp once again your desire, your hope, your dreams and your ideals, and go forward on this path of mystery.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Tempered Lens
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the tempered lens.

This is a short session from July of nineteen ninety, an intensive evening devoted to practice. But before the practice, Q'uo speaks about the one thing every channel must understand first, and it begins with a sentence I want to read to you twice. There is no virtue in pain. No virtue in guiltiness. No virtue in judgment. No virtue in any negative or separating condition, thought, or awareness.

The channel had been working through pain for many hours, refusing medication out of discipline, and Q'uo gently chastises this. Tend to the body, they say. Care for it. Show it the love you show all others. If medication must be taken, anything lost to its side effects may be gained in the strength of the contact. You are stewards of a treasure, they say. The treasure is yourself. How shall you spend yourself? And I will add this plainly, as your friend. Be as kind to your body as you can, rest when you need to, and accept the care that is offered to you. Discipline is a fine thing, but it should never be a cruelty.

Then they turn to the real subject, which is love. Not the love you know, they say. The love of which we speak is beyond that of mother for child, of lover for mate, of friend for friend. It is beyond any concept of love with which you are familiar. The word they want kept foremost is unconditional. This love has no condition tied to it. It is given without any consideration of the entity, the situation, the time, or any other consideration that might qualify the object of the love to be loved.

And how is such love made? By tempering, they say, like steel in fire. The heat of your experience as you live your incarnation, and your ability to process this heat into a light-filled consciousness, allows you to express the product of the processing, which is love. All situations, all entities, all thoughts and experiences become the food, the fuel for this process. As you work with the heat, there is a slow smoothing of the rough places, the distortions within the lens of your ability to see, so that you see more and more clearly, until you do not see that which is other than the self, other than the Creator.

I love the patience in this teaching. From our vantage point, they say, without your veils, this process occurs very rapidly. That is the great virtue of your illusion. Within each incarnation, no matter how slowly it seems to proceed, much work is accomplished, much polishing of the lens. Do not be discouraged by the length of the process. In each lifetime, progress is indeed made, though you are largely unaware of it within the illusion.

So here is the practice they leave you, simple enough to begin tonight. As you greet each entity you meet, whether for a moment or for a lifetime, attempt to see the face of the Creator in the face of this entity. Attempt to view each second-density creature about you, the animals, the trees, as the Creator too. At first it will take a courageous effort, they say. But as the awareness grows, there will be less and less need for the effort, because you will simply know what was always true. That the love of the Creator is all pervasive, and your task is but to become aware of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Comforter Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the comforter within.

In July of nineteen ninety, the group asked about guides, the unseen companions that oversee our progress. What is their purpose, how do they function, and how can we become aware of their work? Q'uo's answer is one of the warmest in the archive, and it begins with a sentence that stops me every time. You are not here to learn how to be loved. You are here to learn to love.

The reason you have guides, they say, is quite simply that you need guides. Only in third density is there a veil between your conscious thinking and the memory of all those with whom you share this world. Everywhere else, beings know they are one. Here, you are purposely made unaware that you are all one, and you see the world as very challenging, if not nearly hopeless. This is no mistake. You asked for the veil so that you could learn to choose.

And who are these guides? They answer twice, they say, because the mathematics of it has significance. First, your guides are portions of your deep self. The self you identify as the nurturer. The self you identify as the provider. The self you identify with spirit. Second, they are also independent personalities, which you call angels, in congruity with ourselves in nature. Do you think we would appeal to you as angels? they ask, with a laugh. Angels are passe. We learned long ago to lose our wings and gain a planetary identity. We speak still the truth, and yet not all of the truth.

What do the guides do? It is not their purpose to change you, they say. It is their purpose to offer comfort, and the wisdom that is part of your own deeper and hidden self. When you habitually act in a negative way toward yourself, and you do not feel worthy, you call upon the nurturer, and the comforter is there to hold you and to keep you and to love you just the way you are. When you are caught in a habit that intellectually offends you, you may call instead upon the sterner principle, the one that kicks and shakes you out of yourself, that you may see the damage and cease to do it.

And at last, they say, there comes the third guide, the androgynous one, the spirit-filled entity with no bias, a portion of oneness itself. You come to this comforter when at last you see that of yourself you cannot free yourself from your own free will. You are ready, they say, to surrender your willfulness to the higher self within, that self which is of love, which is of the Creator, connected with the heart of yourself and of all others. Then you discipline your will and become passionate in your path of service, serving the Creator in every moment, in every thought, in every humble chore.

I love what they say about how the guidance actually arrives. You ask questions too deep for words, they say, and in a number of days you have your dream, your vision, your answer. The longer you pay attention to what occurs to you and how you react to it, the more you know yourself and your biases. And as you honestly ask yourself, why am I angry, why am I happy, why was I irritated by what just happened, doors will open to you. Because you have asked. And what you ask, you will receive.

They speak too, that evening, of the mated pair, two people bound in intimacy, as the most efficient mirror of all. To honor your mate, they say, is to honor yourself, is to honor your teacher. Few of us use the opportunity well. But when two people truly communicate, each becomes the other's teacher, and the differences in their thinking become challenges that improve them both. It is well, they say simply, to find someone to whom you can speak.

So tonight, if you feel alone in the work, remember this. You are free to discipline your own free will, they say, for yours is the freedom and yours is the will. And you do not do it alone. The comforter is there, the nurturer is there, the guides are there, portions of your own deep self, waiting for you to ask. Never argue or criticize yourself, they say. But when you feel you have acted inappropriately, begin again.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Light Too Small
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no light too small.

On an August evening in nineteen ninety, Q'uo spoke to the group about service, and said something that dissolves a whole lifetime of worry in a single image. It is about the sun.

The group had been wondering, as we all do, whether they were truly being of service, whether their small daily efforts mattered at all. And Q'uo answered with the simplicity they are so good at. What is of importance on the metaphysical level, they say, is the desire to be of service, and the purity of the intent in the offering of the self. Not the size of the act. The desire.

The services you perform are many, they say, and yet they are one. A smile given to a stranger on the street. A look of love exchanged with one who is close. The more obvious forms of teaching. All these seemingly various services are but one thing, and that is the radiation of the love of the Creator, which pervades you and your illusion, have you but the ability to perceive it.

And here is the image. When we speak of the love of the Creator, they say, the metaphor most analogous is the radiance of your sun. The sun does not necessarily do anything. The sun is. It radiates the essence of its being. It radiates heat and light and gives life by its radiance. This is the nature of the Creator's love, giving, simply and freely, as part of the nature of its being. And this, they say, is the love that you may also radiate to those about you. All you have to do in order to be of service is not to rush about finding services to perform, but to look to the heart of yourself, to perceive your true nature, and to let that perception so pervade you that it becomes clear to those about you.

There are those that say the small lights surely will not make any difference in the vast darkness, they say. We know the great beacons of your history. And the individual may become discouraged, feeling it has but a small light to offer. We say to you, they answer, that no light is so small it makes no difference. No matter the size of the light, it still shines. And as you band together in your efforts, the effects of the light you project are multiplied.

That evening the channel asked a question I want to hold gently. She said, I know everything you have said about life being worthwhile is true, but how can you tell that to yourself when you are feeling really down? If you are in that place now, please hear this as a friend. You do not have to argue yourself into hope tonight. It is enough to rest, to be kind to yourself, and to reach for whatever support is near you, a person, a counselor, a quiet hour. What Q'uo told her was this. The very asking of the question offers the self the opportunity for gradual transformation. The intensive effort to continue, to choose again to go on, tempers the will, and the product of such a test is simple. The entity has persevered long enough to give itself the opportunity to do so once again.

So tonight, do not rush about. Be the sun. Know yourself, let the true nature of the self radiate through the transparent self, and shine out as a beacon into the thick darkness. You are lightening the consciousness of your planet, they say, simply by being who you are.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Is the Way
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love is the way.

In August of nineteen ninety, the group asked Q'uo about some of the most famous words ever attributed to Jesus. I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life. No one comes to the Father but by me. How are we to understand this, they asked, when each person walks a unique spiritual path? Q'uo answered in two ways, and both are worth hearing slowly.

The first way is a kind of rescue of the sentence from the damage it has caused. Jesus, they say, was a mystic, attempting to express the nature of redemption to simple people in the language they knew. The name of the Creator in his religion was never spoken aloud. It meant, I am that I am. I am because I am. So when he said, I am the Way, those who heard him in his own time heard something different than we hear. Identification with the Creator, the Way. I am, the Creator, the Truth. I am, the Creator, the Life. Stand up and be counted, for until you know I am, you shall not come to I am. To think he meant himself as a human doorway, they say, is a potentially wholly destructive distortion of what he meant.

And then they say it, the sentence I want to give you tonight as plainly as they gave it. Let us call it love. Let us say love is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. No one comes to the Father but by love. This, they say, is the change Jesus himself would have accepted, for to him his experience of his beloved Father was love given and love received.

The second way of understanding the words is about intensity. They show the devotion, the worship, the surrender, the love, and the desire to serve the Creator by serving each other, that a life in faith requires. All paths of service, they say, if they be positive, full of love and light, and harmless to all, are helpful to those who are comfortable with that particular story. The path you walk matters less than the intensity with which you walk it. But it cannot be a once-a-week affair. Religion, they say, works as a tool to polarize and discipline the seeker not one day a week, but every day.

Better still, they say, is the path the entity creates for itself, alive in faith and service and worship, that includes the forgiveness of self, the forgiveness of all others, an adoration of the Creator, and a surrender to the Creator-self within. How do you reach that deep realization? By faith that comes from persistent, daily attempts at meditation. No judgment of the meditations. No taking the spiritual temperature. Only looking always for ways to see the Creator.

I love what they say about where the Creator lives. The Creator did not need houses built for it, they say, for the house of the Creator is your heart, that room into which you may go and shut the door behind you. The most personal and intimate part of yourself is the part that has faith. If you do not have faith, you do not have a way, you do not know a truth, and you do not know how to live your life.

And they are honest that it is not easy. It is not easy to live a life in faith. The more intense your faith becomes, the more it is tested in the fire of experience. For faith is not rigid, they say. It is flexible, adaptable, accepting. It allows people their own paths. It allows people not to find a way to eternity. It allows people to be where they are without regrets for them, because of the sure knowledge that one day they will awaken to their true self, to the I am.

So here is their closing word to you, and I will leave it unadorned. Eternity lies in each present moment. Work as you will with those things which keep you from your awareness of who you are. Do not be discouraged if the rest of your life is taken up in the first step, self-forgiveness and forgiveness of others. You have all the time in the world to become your own I am. Courage, my children.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Crystallized Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a crystallized being.

In August of nineteen ninety, the group asked Q'uo about a region of the Earth that has known turmoil for thousands of years, a place many call holy, and why the energies there seem to play out in confrontation again and again. Q'uo chose not to speak of the politics of the moment. Instead they spoke of something larger, something about you.

There are places on the Earth, they say, which magnify whatever is upon an entity's heart. They call such a place a trigger point, a place of power. The power itself is neutral. It belongs to the land no more than to anywhere else, for that power is understood to be in all things. But generations of prayers, of cries, of yearning, have charged such places, and those who live there find their inner states magnified. The same, they suggest, is true in smaller ways of every place where human beings have loved and suffered for a long time.

And then they turn the teaching inward, which is what they always do. You, they say, are potentially a crystallized being. The greater portion of yourself is a kind of crystal, though most of the time it is not charged. Each time you decide to do that which indicates love for someone else, and unselfishness of yourself, they say, you are crystallizing your own being, and lightening the consciousness of your planet. The crystalline shape offers space, they say, a spaciousness in which any sort of light which you wish may arrive.

I love the honesty of what follows. We will always fall down, they say. We will always make mistakes. We will forget to meditate. We will not think upon our own personal power or our deepest ideals. Do not scold yourself, they say, or feel that you have in any way failed because of these things. Were you able to do all that we say, you would be running out of lessons, not learning. Simply begin again. Persist, endure, and love.

What can one person do about the quarrels of nations, the ancient angers of a holy land? You cannot alter them, they say, not immediately. But you are part of the solution. As you meditate, know that your consciousness is the most important thing about you. Your consciousness is light if your thoughts are joyful, if you find cause for giving thanks and offering praise. You can, by your smiles and your unjudging ear, share that light with people. The world will change, they say, not because you are persuasive, but because you are sincere, passionate, and persistent in opening yourself.

And then they answer the question so many ask. What is my service? What is my path? What did I come here for? And they say to any and all, the first and foremost thing you came here to do was to be loving in the face of a cold and unloving environment. That is it. That is the whole assignment. Not money, not fixing, not persuading. Loving, where love is scarce.

So take yourself seriously, they say, not denying yourself laughter or fun or joy. For you are indeed children of love, and there you are, by yourself seemingly little, yet together you have the power to become transformed into that crystallized being which has no sense of smallness or largeness, but only of being love. And that love, they say, can transform the face of this Earth which you love so dearly.

Thank you for listening.

title: Accept the Unacceptable
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: accept the unacceptable.

In September of nineteen ninety, the group asked Q'uo about the hardest thing in human life. How do you deal with a person or a situation you find truly unacceptable, when you have tried everything you know, and nothing changes? How do you balance doing what you can with accepting what is? The answer fills one of the longest sessions in the archive, and its heart can be said in a single sentence. You did not come here to learn how to be loved. You came here to love.

When you find someone unacceptable, they say, you are usually gazing at a lesson you arranged for yourself before this life began. Those things you find unacceptable, they suggest, were intended by you for your own spiritual work, because you saw in yourself the limits of your love and wished to stretch them. It is even possible, they say, that there is no old karma between you at all, but a mutual agreement, made in love, to give each other the very catalyst you each needed.

So what do you do? First, they say, remember who you are dealing with. Think of the pure and beautiful spirit that you are, and that the other entity is, who fearlessly and courageously made these agreements to walk a path that involved the ordeal of not being understood, and in many cases, not being loved. And then, each time you see the unacceptable one, say to yourself, I came here to love and serve. I do not have to be loved. I do not have to be understood. I do not have to be consoled. For all of these resources are within me.

I love the image they give for the work itself. You cannot push a flower out of the ground, they say. You must wait, nourish it, feed it, water it, let the sun shine upon it, and give all credit for the bloom to the Creator of that bloom. Your work is not to fix the other person. The only entity in the universe you can work on, they remind you, is yourself. The faults you see in others are a mirror image of your own unfinished work. If you did not have work to do in that area, you would not react with such difficulty.

And then the practice, stated as simply as a prayer. When the thought rises, this is unacceptable, correct it. Say to yourself, I am here to serve, I am here to love, I am here to forgive, to heal. All of these are possible, they say, through surrender to the self in its higher forms, which in the end becomes the God self. If you can take the few seconds to remember who you are, what sort of being you are, you are most likely to make great progress.
