What the conscious work does is quicken the pace. And they add something worth remembering: the transformations of third density almost always come from an oblique angle. They do not telegraph the punch.

The first technique is the trigger. Find the small automatic moments in your daily routine and invest them with meaning. The bell that strikes the hour. A doorway you pass through often, which you turn, in your mind, into a magical doorway. Each time you pass, you get a moment to center yourself and reorient to love and service. The world is full of reminders if you appoint them.

The second is the turning around. Mentally seat yourself in the part of you that does the work in consciousness, and look at your life from there. Your primary environment is a spiritual one, and it must be named and expected before it can be seen. Once it is seen, the busy humming day gets recreated around it, and you keep vibrating with the original thought even in the thick of things.

The third is the balancing of the day. In meditation, let the mind ripple back through the day's experiences and find what distracted or attracted you. Replay the memory. Let the emotion intensify, then lay it down and sit with it. Then let the opposite emotion arise and be honored. Hold both side by side, and see that you are both, which means you are neither. Then drop them. You have arrived back at the fundamental spiritual environment.

The fourth is reduction, and it is the most practical of the five. When you are facing more than you can do, reduce the field of attention until only what is in front of you gets noticed. Clear the desk until one project remains. It is easier, materially and mentally, to do one thing well. And keep the daily meditation going, because without that silent listening time the energy to focus will flag.

The fifth is the one I love best. Q'uo calls it holy silliness. When a situation has you by the emotions, see it as a cartoon and write the caption underneath. Let yourself make fun of the whole gestalt. At first the captions will be sarcastic and bitter. Keep going, and they turn gentler and sweeter, as the light of the original thought begins to align the whole scene. Laughter, they say, is the fire's communication with the earth, as mercy is the rain's. Laughter burns away pain, and then it builds golden castles.

All five rest on one perception: there is a country within that is native to you. You are at home in this spiritual country, and only visiting in the foreign land of incarnation. Once you have truly sensed it, you can reenter it in the split second it takes to think.

And the key to focus, they say, is the present moment. Do not look back or forward except as needed to inform this perfect now. If the attention strays, bring it back. If you do it a million times in a day and still forget, then when you remember, bring it back. No judgment, no scolding, just realign. The habit is hard to make, but once made it is even harder to break.

One more thread from the questions, for the makers among us. K wonders how a creative artisan can gain more focus, and Q'uo points to music. Music is a great teacher, they say, because its energy lives entirely in the present moment, expressing emotion and then releasing it. To express the emotions with love, in whatever medium you use, lets the mind become empty and free. The work that comes from that emptiness carries the quality of love in it. So make things. It is a spiritual practice with its own kind of focus.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Road to Chicago
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the road to Chicago. The question is about destiny. Is it fixed, or can we change it? Q'uo answers with a road trip.

Before incarnation, they say, each of you chose the lessons to be learned. That choice sets up one axis of your destiny. The other axis is made of the agreements you made with the key people of your life: the parents, the siblings, the mate, the children, the friends. Two axes, and between them the long trail of a personal history.

But free will is kept all the way. Picture three seekers traveling from Louisville to Chicago. All three are destined to arrive in Chicago. But one may go by one road and one by another, fast or slow, by car or by train. What is destined is the arrival. Within that, free will chooses the manner of conveyance and the speed.

Destiny, more deeply, is what captures the heart. Even with many options open, there is a lane that simply feels more appealing, more right. You cannot fully know your destiny, Q'uo warns, but you can learn to feel for it: the feeling of rightness, of clarity, of fitting well into one particular option. Follow that feeling, and life begins to move with less effort, like a well oiled rifle sending the bullet straight to the target.

The image matters. The spirit can live like the bullet: swift, straight, accurate, with substantial force. And the closer you get to the hub of your destiny, the narrower the options become. At the start of a lesson, leaving Louisville, you have money for many routes. Nearing Chicago, there is less room to maneuver, less latitude before the punch line of the lesson.

Then they turn to what happens when two destinies join, as mates join. The tracks of two become fused, two paths traveled as one. And here is the hard part: when a relationship splits before the lesson is done, you cannot go back. Louisville, once left, no longer exists. The lesson does not simply repeat; it returns more pointed, the difficulties more pronounced, the options fewer. That is why so many people find themselves in what feels like an empty existence. They walked away from the hard work, and the rhythm of the dance was lost.

But free will never leaves. After a split, each traveler continues on a separate track, and may even rejoin the old companion later, if enough repair has been made. Nothing is final until the lessons are learned.

One seeker asks about the advantage of walking with a mate, and Q'uo answers with a paraphrase: two heads are better than one. What one misses, the other may find. Those who seek together, of like mind, shall far more surely find.

There is one more practical thread. How do you cooperate with destiny? Surrender the intellectual and logical modes, they say, and adopt a willing, flowing attitude. Feel your way until you find what feels right within. It is not the cleverest plan that aligns you with destiny. It is the willingness to move forward without resistance when change is needed, trusting the feeling of rightness over the noise of the mind.

And what of death, the final destination? Q'uo says the time of it is not fixed. There is at least one moment in each incarnation when the lesson could end, and often more than one, because most of us carry more than one lesson. After a certain minimum has been reached, there is the choice to let this be the last or to take up another. So the ending is not set, but the shape of it is inevitable. You will arrive. The only question is how you travel.

I want to linger on the bullet and the rifle, because the image has a second half. The bullet is the spirit, swift and straight. But the rifle itself, the part of you that carries you through the physical, mental, and spiritual vehicles, must be kept oiled and in trim. Destiny gives you the target and the momentum. Free will gives you the maintenance. Neglect the weapon and it corrodes; the best aimed bullet in the world cannot save a rusted barrel. So care for the vehicle, and the travel takes care of itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: Doubt and the Channel
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: doubt and the channel. The question is the one every new instrument asks: how do I know I am not just making this up. There is an honest answer.

Oxal answers with unusual directness. Each seeker walks a path balanced between doubt and the rational mind on one side and overzealous faith and an irrational mind on the other. The intellect wants small correctnesses. The zealot wants feeling without discipline. And neither knows the truth. There are no shortcuts. Truth blooms within each seeker like the desert flower, and the best you can do is treasure it when a glimpse appears.

There is, they say plainly, no provable way to know that a contact is genuine. The experience of receiving a channeled message is very like the process of ordinary thinking: a concept rises from the subconscious, crosses into consciousness, and gets clothed in words. There is no bright line between the two. So the channel can never prove, even to itself, that the words came from elsewhere.

What the channel can do is watch the results of tuning. As experience mounts, certain ways of preparing will show themselves to be the most efficient for you personally. Note them. Repeat them. Build a ritual. And the deep mind, recognizing the ritual, will open more reliably and more correctly each time. Every instrument must develop its own protected way of opening, because every path is unique.

Oxal also passes on a practical word from Latwii. When a contact is left open, there is no simple way for a discarnate entity to refrain from speaking. So when practicing, after the greeting, it is wise to ask politely to move straight to the closing. A few stray sentences of other thoughts are nothing to worry about, but the channel should guard its conscious mind neatly.

Then Oxal turns to what they most love to talk about: love. It is always at the heart of their message, they say. Love is. That little word is expresses its nature in all that there is, and each of us can quicken our evolution by matching our vibration more closely to that original love. The message is almost too simple to hold the mind, so they tell it in endless ways.

The word love itself has gone weak in our language, they admit, because so many things are called love. But the creative and sometimes terrible love of the infinite One is strong. All that you see was brought into manifestation by it. When you walk down a summer lane and see the sun warming the leaves, you are looking at a primary manifestation of love. All beauty is wrought with the light that love created.

The session becomes a round, the contact passed from instrument to instrument, each adding a piece. One thread I want to keep: that the original gift any of us can give another is uncompromising, unstinted love. How hard it is to move from all our judgments and cautions to relating to others as one who loves unconditionally. And yet those who receive the gift recognize it, no matter how stumbling the attempt.

And the companion thread: that the love of the self matters as much. To judge the self is to bar the door to loving anyone else, because all selves are one. The seeker must discover that the parts of the self felt to be unacceptable are as acceptable as any other, all of them distortions of the one Creator. When the small self is accepted, that acceptance ripples outward, from friends to strangers to everything, until all is accepted as the one great Self.

One more thread from the round, the one that stays with me longest. After all the careful instruction on ritual and opening, the instruments keep circling back to the same small word. Love is, they say. Love is the key to the door. Love is the original gift. It is the kind of message that sounds too simple to be useful, until you try to live it. Uncompromising, unstinted love, given to the self first so it can be given to everyone. When the contact is genuine, they tell us, that is what it carries. Nothing else is needed.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Unforced Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the unforced life. The question is about non dedication to outcome, about how to stop measuring everything by the result and judging yourself by the measure.

Q'uo begins with a tree in early spring. Bare all winter, it thaws, and the living sap rises from the roots, feeding every limb. Each bud opens in its turn. Does any leaf consider what it shall do? No. Being of second density, the tree has a full unconscious awareness of the perfection of the process, and the process happens perfectly.

We had that once. Third density gave us the gift of self consciousness, and with it a veil dropped between the conscious and unconscious mind. We no longer feel the perfection of the process from the inside. And into that gap rush the ambitions: to read, to do, to learn, to gather, to become more aware. Life grows enormously complex, and even the attempt to simplify becomes complicated, because the mind creates what it desires by desiring it.

So how do you get back to the tree's way? Q'uo suggests you begin by questioning your own perception. Your senses send millions of bits of information to the brain every moment, and the brain uses perhaps one or two percent of it, programmed before you were even born. If you want to change your attitude, ask which data gets priority. And you can talk to the part of you that decides. The beginning of that conversation is silent meditation.

It is not one method for everyone. Each path is good for the one who walks it. The point is faithfulness, the repeated knocking at the door of the deeper mind: I am ready. I am here with these emotions and attitudes, questing. And the deep mind hears, and one more small step moves the seat of living from the brain, with its justifications, to the heart, with its purity of feeling. True wisdom lies in the emotions, progressively purified by focus.

Once you have felt that flowing, centered life a few times, you do not have to create it again. You only have to access it, with practice, calling to your perception: I want information about love in this moment. Where is it? And you will be disappointed with yourself many times along the way. That disappointment, Q'uo says, is itself a lovely part of the process, the old falling away as the heart changes its habits.

Then the session turns, and Oxal comes to close with something I did not expect and will not forget. Put value in the self without reservation, they say. The infinite love can only shine through an entity comfortable enough to open a channel to it. If you can, picture your inner self as a child who needs a hug. Those who try to do service before they have fallen in love with the self burn out and exhaust themselves spiritually.

You are loved, each of you, Oxal says, and it is in that love that you truly reside. The thinking, deciding, functioning self is not the end of you. There is also the unlimited Self, young and newly conscious and hungry, and it must be nurtured like a child. Turn to the sun which is love, and bloom gloriously.

In the questions, someone asks how grace comes into our lives. Q'uo answers that grace is nurtured as you open to the perfection of all creation. Fling your expectations to the wind, become hollow as a pipe, and let the water of the spirit move through. Then your experience is the perfect reflection of the one Creator smiling through your face.

There is one more encouragement I want to lift from the transcript. Q'uo urges each seeker to find within the attitude a growing awareness of how love felt within is a channel, a way for the infinite love of the Creator to flow through to others. Let the light within be, they say. Let the self open and flow consciously. Sometimes it is nothing more than a supportive smile to a stranger that makes the difference for that stranger in that moment. The unforced life is not only unforced for you. It becomes a current others can drink from.

Thank you for listening.

title: Dressed in Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: dressed in light. Oxal teaches a small group how to protect themselves in the work of channeling, and the teaching turns out to be about much more than channeling.

They begin with a warning against fear based protection. To protect yourself in the spirit of fear would be poor advice, they say. There is nothing to fear in terms of negativity. But there is something to respect. When you stand very close to the light, you cast a very sharp shadow. Oxal calls it the loyal opposition: the energies of service to self, delighted to sway a channeled message until the original intention to serve others is quietly undone.

The danger is subtle. A positive channel is compromised not by drama but by appetite: the hunger for more and more specific answers. The negative source simply keeps supplying specifics, less and less accurate, until the whole attempt to serve the light has been foiled. So some form of protecting effort is wise, alongside the inner cleansing they call tuning.

Then comes the practice, and it is beautifully concrete. Picture the spine, and see the seven energy centers as colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. Ask to see them as they are right now. If an energy is sluggish, ask it to spin and brighten until it is clear. Do this for each center in turn, until the chakras spin together like a roll of bright candies.

When they are open and working together, swirl the violet down to the red and back, until you have a red violet color, and picture yourself drenched in it, inside and outside every cell. This is the body's own protection. Then picture the limitless white light and drench yourself in that too, breathing it in, feeling it move into every sense. If you do not feel brightened by this, Oxal says, find another image that does the work. The form is less important than the effect.

I love the humility with which they speak of themselves. They are of fifth density, they say, and are not often contacted. They feel their way here, new to this pleasant task of opening a channel. They ask the new instrument to share any discomfort, and they listen. It is a reminder that even the teachers are learning.

There is a practical instruction for the new channel on knowing when to begin. After tuning and challenging, let some part of your awareness record how the shared energy feels, and store the memory as high priority. Next time that sensation comes, you will recognize it sooner and more keenly. Each instrument has its own equivalent of a sense of rightness, and that is what to watch for.

When someone asks how to tell whether the inner voices they hear should be challenged, Oxal gives a simple rule. Offer each voice the challenge that asks if it comes in the name of what you live for most passionately and would die for most willingly. It need not be long or effortful, but it must be pure in intention. And it is enough to challenge at the beginning of each contact; the answer can be trusted for the rest of it.

Underneath all the technique is the simplest message Oxal knows. There is one great original thought, and it is love. It created all that is, beginning with the photon, the first light. All of it, your world and everything you can imagine, is light that is the manifestation of love. When they greet you in love and in light, that is all they mean, and it is everything.

Near the end, Oxal looks at the circle and tells them what they see. Each of you, they say, is a ball of light, and this group is a very bright and cheerful one. There is little shadow here. I include this because it is easy to hear a teaching on protection and imagine danger everywhere. Oxal's view is the opposite. The protection is real, the discernment is real, and underneath it all, the room is already full of light. Most of what we fear is already handled by the brightness we bring.

Thank you for listening.

title: Money as Energy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: money as energy. The group asks what the endless chase for enough money does to the spiritual life, and whether there is a better attitude.

Q'uo starts with the brain, the biocomputer. It is very good at problems inside the illusion, and one of the problems it perceives is supply. Not just enough for today, but enough for some possible future need, with extra beyond that. As cultures grow more sophisticated, the perception grows with them, until there is a universal feeling that whatever is coming in is probably not enough, because there is not enough extra.

The spiritual view is not reached through the brain. It is reached through consciousness. And the consciousness of the One is a consciousness of infinite plenty. The creation is full. Every need has that which can meet it. To place your financial worries inside that holy of holies is to let a different light fall on them.

They offer a small linguistic trick. Replace the word money with the word energy. Energy does not need to be hoarded; its nature is to be used, spent, potentiated. Do what you must to gain enough energy to survive and be comfortable. And notice how many impossible things happen through the trading of goods and services, when people stop insisting on a single form of energy.

Then the deeper cut. Why do we worry beyond today? Because when we touch that worry we are gazing at a temporal being, ourselves, in fear that it may cease to exist, or exist less comfortably. Even those who amass great quantities are moved at heart by fear. There is no ceiling on the need for more, all in the name of being more secure. But where is your security? In the bank that may fall? The job that may end? Feel the footsteps wander off the path.

The daily practice they suggest is simple and hard. When you catch yourself turning to that grasping concern for more than enough, say to yourself: let go of fear. Then reorient, consciously, into the awareness that there is enough, because consciousness is infinite.

Someone asks the honest question: what about the person who works from sunrise to sunset and has no time left to seek? Q'uo answers without flinching. For some, the life agenda is exactly that: the single pointed dedication to survival, the honing of desire on one concept, until perhaps one day the awareness lifts to a higher goal. For those with more margin, there is the luxury of pursuing the finer ramifications. Each life gives the opportunity that matters most to that soul's pattern.

Money, they say, is a perfect symbol of the whole illusion. It is polarized: more and less, and underneath that, all and nothing. To the prudent there is more money and less money. To most of us there are only two states: I have money, and I do not have enough. Such is the radicalizing effect of fear.

And here is the turn I want to leave you with. Your job in incarnation is to let the programming of consciousness replace the programming of the mind. See the concern for money as the challenge it is, and let consciousness lend it the awareness that there is enough. Celebrate your problems, they say. Every discomfort that makes you seek and seek and seek again is bringing you to the point of desiring a higher truth.

The session opens with a small, warm detail I almost skipped. Q'uo notes that the sun is streaming into the room, touching the channel's body with warmth, and says they feel the metaphysical warmth of the group's welcome in return. It sits beside the hard teaching on money like a window left open. Even in a session about fear and scarcity, the light is coming in. The consciousness of infinite plenty is not an idea to believe. It is already touching your skin, if you let yourself feel it.

The practice they offer is almost embarrassingly simple. Catch the grasping thought, the one that says there will not be enough, and say to yourself: let go of fear. Then turn, on purpose, toward the awareness that consciousness is infinite. Not once, as a philosophy, but every time the worry comes back. That is the whole exercise. The fear will come back. The turning is the work.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Spiritual Desert
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the spiritual desert. The question is about those wasteland times when the spirit seems gone, when you feel isolated, abandoned, unconnected to everything you are doing.

Q'uo begins with a small observation about meditation. As you sit, there is a sensation of deceleration, as though the racing mind were being slowed by stillness. That is why they recommend it so often. Incarnation is all action, but without stillness the fundamental nature of the pure self can never be felt. And without self knowledge, how can you move back into action skillfully?

The feeling of not being present is deadening, they admit. Your human essence is the intense experience of perceiving choices and making them. When life hurries you, you start numbing your own creative perception, because it hurts to spend your days doing things that feel unimportant. Even a meditation that feels like a failure, full of inner noise, resensitizes you. The attempt itself opens the inner door.

Then the practical heart of the teaching. Put into each day moments whose only goal is to sit with the inner reality and be present with all that there is. Touch that gate to eternal things, and the meditation grows larger and larger until the starry heavens dwell within the tiniest point of silence, and you are all that there is.

When the desert comes in earnest, the first rule is: do not fling away your identity. The desert seems to invalidate everything you believed, and the temptation is to discard the whole self and start over. But your nationality, your character, the homely facts of who you are, these are not things you outgrow. They are the building blocks of the milieu you came to learn in. The commonplaces of your life do not stay common when you sit with them in faith.

There is a beautiful passage about why poetry and music move us so. In music, tones create words that carry more feeling than explanation could. In poetry, words are twisted together until they make a rope stronger in evocative truth than the words that made the rope. The common things of life are freighted with more than they can bear, and that freight is the immanence of love.

Do not walk away from the world of too much to do, they say. Not for long. This is the world you came to learn the lessons of love in. Respect the incarnation, the celebrations and the sufferings both. When you feel most trivial and dry and disconnected, do not fill the time with distraction. Sit with the feelings and honor them. You are not here to feel good all the time. You are here to know the truth of each thing and honor it.

Cultivate not indifference but fearlessness about your state of mind. If discomfort can be seen without fear, the groundwork is done for the present moment to touch the heart anew, and suddenly the self feels itself in green pastures again, strengthened and strong.

In the questions, someone asks how to refocus quickly when the mind is really bothered. Q'uo suggests keeping a small treasury: the passages, the music, the images that have focused you before. Recall them deliberately when the center will not hold. They are crystallized moments of your own seeking, and they still work.

And I will add this in my own voice. Desert times can feel like depression, and sometimes they are depression wearing a spiritual costume. If the dryness does not lift, if you feel abandoned in a way that frightens you, please talk to someone you trust, a counselor, a helpline in your country. Sitting with your feelings is holy work, and so is asking for help.

The closing blessing of this session is one of the loveliest in the whole batch. Q'uo blesses each seeker for their very being, and then says: rest, enjoy the illusion, make every mistake, and know that you are loved. It is the perfect word for the desert. You do not have to earn your way out of the dry times. You do not have to perform your way back into the green pastures. Rest. The green comes back on its own schedule, and the love never left.

Thank you for listening.

title: Stuck in the Tar
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: stuck in the tar. The first evening of a weekend of dialogues with Aaron and Q'uo, asking the oldest question: what is the spiritual path, and how do we live it. Aaron's answer is worth hearing.

Aaron's answer begins with a shock of simplicity. You have been on the spiritual path since the moment you first sensed a separation from God, illusory but seeming real. There is nothing you can do that is not part of it. There are only more skillful and less skillful ways to walk. And by skillful they do not mean good or evil. They mean the ways that bring pain to yourself or others, and the ways that free all beings from pain.

Each of you, they say, is like a pebble tossed into a still and infinite sea. Every splash sends out waves that touch all the other pebbles. When you send out loving energy, your interrelationship with the world is utterly different than when you send out fear. And yet, as long as you are human, the emotions will keep arising. Fear, anger, greed, jealousy. You cannot stop their arising. You can change your relationship to what arises.

Here is the difference they want you to see. One being feels fear turn into anger, and either acts on it or hates itself for feeling it. Another being sees the fear arising, sees the anger growing out of it, and simply smiles. Oh, they say, you again. Here is jealousy. Here is desire. Here is rage. The difference is ownership.

To make it vivid they tell the story of Brer Rabbit and the Tar Baby. The rabbit thinks the tar baby is mocking him, so he punches it, and his hand sticks. Let me go, he says, and punches with the other hand. Two hands stuck. Then the feet. Here is one very stuck rabbit. That is what we do with our emotions. We grasp at them or punch at them to get rid of them, and the moment we decide somebody owns this feeling, we are stuck in the concept of the owner.

It is never too late to come back, they say. At any moment you can cut through the ownership and smile at yourself. Here I am, stuck in it again. Take a breath and remember: this is not who I am, but I am human, and as long as I am human this will keep arising. It is not given to me to fight with. It is given to me to learn from. Just relax and be with it.

Aaron speaks of a practice from the Dzogchen tradition, Rigpa, the luminous great perfection: finding the space of the divine in yourself and resting in it, over and over. This, they say, is the essence of the spiritual path in every religion they have known in their many lifetimes. Some had it distorted, some had it clear, but all of them aimed at the same thing: coming back, again and again, to pure being.

First you must recognize that space within you. Most of you are in it far more often than you know, but without recognition it comes and goes unnoticed. Then you work to stabilize it, learning to relate to the world more and more from that clarity and connection.

They give one image for the multiple motivations tangled in every act. You have an apple in your pocket, red and juicy, and you are about to bite when a thin hungry child holds out a hand. Your heart opens and you give the apple. And alongside the pure giving comes a small thought: did I not do well? Did anyone see? The giving is pure love. The thought grows out of fear and the wish to be the good one. We never act wholly out of love or wholly out of fear, they say. The work is to get acquainted with the mixture, so the choices can grow more skillful and more loving.

They end the evening by raising the questions the weekend will explore, and they are the real ones. When we act from love and the results boomerang into pain, did we act from hidden fear, or do we need deeper faith? Is pain always a sign we did something wrong, or is pain sometimes simply inevitable? Can you try so hard to be harmless that the trying itself becomes a kind of harm? They offer no answers yet. Only the questions, held in love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Center of the Cross
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the center of the cross. The second day of the dialogues, and Aaron takes up the question of service to self and service to others, and what it really means to choose.

Q'uo lays the foundation first. This density is the density of choice: the choice between radiant service and grasping service, service to others and service to self. To discern that choice in each moment is much of what you incarnated to learn. The other part is simpler: keep offering praise and thanks. That is the music that gladdens your walking.

Aaron adds that there is no such thing as absolute evil. Beings on the negative path are also motivated by a form of love, however distorted: love of the separate self. It can carry them very high, but it cannot carry them all the way home, because the delusion of separation remains. It becomes a dead end, and eventually the polarity must reverse.

Then they return to the apple. Last night the apple holder gave the whole apple to the hungry child. But what if the apple was the only food the holder had, and the holder had not eaten for days? Is the thought, I am hungry too, an evil thought? No. You chop the apple in half and trust that more will come. The self is also an other. To become a martyr with no respect for your own needs is needless sacrifice.

The skill is in telling which needs grow out of love and healthy respect and which grow out of fear. The voice that says, what if I need it, is old mind speaking, old habit from past hunger. In this present moment, you are not hungry and the child is. You can give freely. But you do not scorn yourself for the habit arising. You see it as human fear, touch it with compassion, and come back to the bare perception of now.

This is what Aaron calls the horizontal practice: living skillfully and lovingly, moment by moment, in relative reality. And there is also the vertical practice, which cuts through the illusion of the self entirely. In the vertical, you ask of each arising thought: whose thought is this? From where did it arise? And you see that it arose from old mind habit, that you do not own it. Pop, goes the balloon of thought, and for a second there is only pure awareness, no somebody doing anything.

The goal is the intersection, the center of the cross, where compassion and wisdom meet. Horizontal without vertical becomes a doer helping a receiver, and the ego solidifies. Vertical without horizontal becomes sterile wisdom that disassociates from human life. Christ consciousness, Buddha consciousness: awareness aware of its divine nature, and at the same time aware of the tools of the incarnation.

Aaron also speaks of the light body, and I want to keep this image. Picture the heart as a ball of radiant light, and within it small dark flecks: the emotions and thoughts that block the light going out and coming in. The work of consciousness slowly dissolves the shadow. A being like himself, sixth density, held before the perfect light, would still show a distinction. A Christ or a Buddha would be almost invisible. The distortions of the physical body are reflections of the higher bodies, which is why clarifying the higher often brings healing below.

And a warning for the sincere. Do not try to cling to being the higher self without doing the work to dissolve the shadow of the emotional and physical bodies. The strings of the instrument must be in harmony. If the high strings are in tune and the low strings are not, the music is discordant. You do not get rid of the emotions. You find space for them, let go of fear of them, and become a harmonious whole.

The questions turn to faith, and Aaron gives it a definition I want to keep. Faith, they say, is the willingness to allow whatever will arise. To say, I do not know, and to rest in the not knowing. Most of us treat faith as a kind of certainty, a harder grip on the answer. Aaron turns it around. The more you can practice resting in the open question, the more space there is for what they call miracles, the outcomes that cleverness could never have planned. Faith without proof is not a lesser faith. In this density, it is the whole glory of the thing.

Thank you for listening.

title: Angels in Earthsuits
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: angels in earthsuits. The second afternoon of the dialogues, and Aaron moves from theory to the practical question everyone actually asks: how do I know whether I am following love or following fear. Aaron gives a practical answer.

They begin with an image. I call you angels in earthsuits, they say. Your angelness is undeniable; it is who you truly are. But you have pulled on a suit of armor for this incarnation, and closed the visor in front so you cannot see clearly. The suit is a burden and also a necessary tool. The earth is your schoolroom, and the body and emotions are the embodiments of the lessons you came to learn.

The trick is balance. Live the angelness fully without discarding the suit. You are like actors in a play. If you look at the audience and say, this is only a play, it does not matter, the audience learns nothing. If you forget it is a play entirely, you turn your back and mumble your lines. The good actor lives the lines convincingly while knowing, all along, that offstage she is someone else. That is how you are to live: one foot in relative reality, one foot in ultimate reality, with no wall between them.

Then the practical teaching on motivation. In every human situation there is multiple motivation. They return to the apple: ninety five percent of the giving may be pure generosity, and five percent the voice of fear, either the fear that says what if I need it, or the fear that wants to be somebody good. If you deny the fearful part, it grows stronger. If you acknowledge it and smile at it and turn back to the loving part, you deny power to your fear. They call this not getting into a dialogue with fear.

They tell a story to ask the hardest version of the question. A woman, call her partner A, shares her possessions with her partner B out of love and trust. Soon after, B betrays her, and A is left heartbroken and in a drastic financial situation. What did I do wrong, she asks. I followed my heart.

Aaron offers possibilities, all hypothetical. Perhaps A is being invited to let go of needing things to come out a certain way, to trust not only the good but the bad. Perhaps it is karmic, an old debt being balanced. They tell of a Zen priest falsely accused who served six years in prison without fighting, because in meditation he saw he had committed that crime in a past life and gone free. I have paid in my own way, the priest said, and I am free. Perhaps A's suffering, borne without hatred, is itself a service to B, opening a door.

And perhaps, they say gently, there was denial in A as well: a reluctance to admit that B was not trustworthy, a clinging to the love offered rather than the faith to say no. So many of you, they say, interpret kindness as never saying no, and become a doormat. Then rage builds, and you erupt, and then you call yourself bad and go back to the doormat. But there is a place in between. To say no can be done with love. It does not have to be done with hate. In fact, allowing another to use you as a doormat harms them too.

So how do you know whether to stay in the painful job or the rocky relationship, or to leave? Their answer: there is never a right or wrong decision, only more or less skillful ones. Ask whether you are still learning there, or whether the pain has contracted your energy so far that learning has stopped. If it has, forgive yourself for the humanness of it, and let go with the intention to understand the fear later, when you are no longer stuck in it.

They close with two practices. The all encompassing one: whatever you do, do it with awareness. Awareness is the key to all learning. The specific one: find your own stumbling block and design a practice for it. If greed is the block, practice letting others go first and watch the old fear prove itself wrong. If jealousy, practice gladness at others' good fortune until it becomes real. If holding on, practice giving in small things until you learn that you lose nothing when you give.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Two Wings
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the two wings. The third morning of the dialogues, and Aaron takes up mercy and wisdom, the two great streams of the spiritual life.

They begin with religion itself. Your religious persuasions, they say, are not the spiritual path. They are tools for walking it. And they simplify the great traditions into two qualities. The Christ embodies mercy. The Buddha embodies wisdom. Mercy is one wing of the bird, wisdom the other. The bird cannot fly with one wing, though one wing will always be stronger. Through faith alone, liberation is possible. Through awakened wisdom alone, liberation is possible. But the bird flies best with both.

What is your own bias? That is the question they put to the room. Where there is only wisdom with no mercy, is there a fear of letting the heart speak? Where there is only heart with no wisdom, is there a fear of the conceptual mind? Know your strengths and build on them, they say, but do not be afraid to strengthen the weak muscles too.

Then two stories. The first is their own memory, from a lifetime in which they were a poor shepherd and knew Jesus in the flesh. After their wife died, Aaron was injured on the road with a broken leg, and went to the teacher expecting healing. The teacher kept them there for months, tended and fed, and would not heal the leg. Aaron was angry, thinking the healing was withheld. Only later did he understand: the leg was not what needed healing. The heart was. The teacher's mercy was not maudlin. It was tempered with wisdom, and he would not let Aaron leave until the grief itself was healed.

The second is a story of the Buddha. A woman's only son died, and she begged the Buddha to revive him. He agreed, on one condition: she must bring him a pinch of a certain spice from a household that had not known death. Door after door she knocked, and door after door the answer was the same. An uncle last month. A daughter last week. A father last year. By dusk she understood: death is part of the continuum of life, and she returned with dry tears and an open heart. Was that less merciful than a miracle? Aaron asks. The child was helped into the ground, and the mother was helped into wisdom.

The path of mercy contains wisdom, and the path of wisdom contains mercy. Each predominates in one direction. Those drawn to the Christ are drawn to loving kindness and forgiveness. Those drawn to the Buddha are drawn to wisdom tempered by mercy. Your work is to find your own balance, and to notice where fear blocks it.

Aaron then turns to the emotions that most distort our seeing, and to one in particular: unworthiness. Is it genetic, someone asks. No, they say, but it is hereditary in another way: it is culturally conditioned, and you chose this culture for the learning it offers. They tell of a gathering of western Buddhist teachers with the Dalai Lama, where one teacher asked about people who truly despise themselves. The Dalai Lama was puzzled. Do you mean people in mental hospitals? No, said the teacher. Those sitting around this table.

Where does the story come from? You are divine, Aaron says. How could you ever be unworthy? Unskillful, afraid, dull at times, yes. But unworthy? On the ultimate plane there is no worthy or unworthy. There is only God. On the relative plane, the pain of feeling unworthy can become the very tool that teaches you your worth.

They trace how it forms. A child who feels rage toward a parent learns quickly that rage threatens the bond it depends on. So the child buries the rage and tells itself: I deserved this. Unworthiness becomes armor over the rage. Even the baby greeted at three in the morning by an exhausted, irritated parent feels the difference, and begins the same lesson. The way through is not to deny the rage but to admit it with compassion. It is not unspiritual to feel rage. It is just feeling rage. And when the feeling is allowed, it can pass like a cloud instead of hardening into an identity.

I want to speak to this gently, in my own voice. If what Aaron describes touches something real in you, especially experiences of abuse or neglect from childhood, you deserve support in working with it, not just meditation. A trusted counselor or therapist can walk with you through what unworthiness has been covering. There is no shame in that. It is one more way of refusing to wage war on yourself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Masked Ball
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the masked ball. The closing session of the weekend of dialogues, and Q'uo comes to say farewell.

They begin with gratitude, and with a name for themselves I had not heard: the brothers and sisters of sorrow. They were drawn to this planet, they say, by the great cry of pain and sorrow rising from it, especially in the last two hundred years, and most especially the last fifty.

They have watched our factories and technology give us something precious: leisure, time beyond the making of a living. And they have watched the same system fill that time with distraction and triviality. They do not condemn it. They only remind us that we have free will in all matters, and urge us to make judicious use of our time, our space, our relationships, leavening all earnestness with high spirits.

Be reckless with your laughter, they say, and generous with your sarcastic comments. The seemingly trivial moments of self parody are like yeast, lightening the whole texture of your living. I love this permission. The spiritual life, in their telling, has room for puns and bad jokes.

Then the teaching on vocation. Whatever you do to create the energy of money may or may not look like a spiritual task, and it does not matter. The spiritual vocation is not a job description. It is the heart's eye, seeing every experience in the context of the consciousness you are nurturing into vigorous life. Do not try to haul yourself into some discipline where you will be spiritual. Simply be yourself in each present moment, and look within for where the love is.

The Creator lies before your face and in your face, they say. You open your eyes and see the creation. You gaze into your fellow human's eyes and see the Creator. It is a wonderful masked ball. Enjoy the many dances of life.

And the last promise: they are with those who call to them, not to channel through you, for that would be an impingement, but as a carrier wave of love, so that you need never be completely alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: Children of the Sun
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: children of the sun. The group asks Q'uo to comment on some teachings of Ra about the sun, and the answer is stranger and more beautiful than I expected.

Ra begins with the levels. In relation to intelligent infinity, the sun is simply part of infinity, like everything else. In relation to intelligent energy, it is the offspring of the logos for a vast family of sub logoi, using its free will to co create the nuances of the densities. Physically, it is a great body of gas undergoing fusion, radiating heat and light. Metaphysically, it means more and more as entities grow able to grasp it, until by sixth density the sun can be visited and inhabited, and even partially created from moment to moment by the entities evolving there.

Q'uo takes up the thread. Let us go to the beginning, they say: intelligent energy, created by free will, creates unpotentiated love, and love articulates one thing, the photon. This light is timeless and spaceless. It is solid, limitless, a perfect creature of love containing infinite intelligence without distortion. All that there is dwells within that one original thought.

They draw a distinction I want to keep. There is the limitless light, and there is the radiation of light as we experience it. The first is the background of everything, the environment in which the infinite Creator has being. When you go into meditation and call for the limitless light and rest in it, basking, you are tabernacling with the one infinite Creator.

All things are made of light, they remind us: the instrument, the microphone at her neck, the clothes, the furniture, the earth, the sky. We cannot easily see it, because light operating in our density appears as magnetism, as fields, as form and color and size. But the shape of every object is the result of a field of energy holding it together, and this is worth remembering whenever we think about healing.

Light is inherently intelligent, they say. Any amount of infinite light can grasp, as though it were an entity, the heartfelt communications made to it. When the sun's radiation touches your skin and you praise the light and the love of the infinite One, you have communicated with the infinite Creator. This is why sun worship runs through all of human history. There is real conversation available there, with what they call the Lord of light.

Then the teaching that stopped me. Some entities of sixth density choose to reproduce by fusion, and some choose to do it as part of the beingness of the sun. Portions of the light you receive, Q'uo says, are the offspring of the generative expression of sixth density love. The immediate offspring is more a quality than a thing, more a tiny being than a measurable substance. And not all the sun's rays are these children, but the healing quality in sunlight is greatly aided by them.

It is a sacrifice, they say. These beings cannot enjoy the company of their offspring or live alongside them. But the offspring, only halfway aware of free will, can choose intelligently to drench the sun's radiation so that the maximum healing energy reaches the places where prayer or pain has announced a need. Think of that the next time sunlight finds you: some of it is love, deliberately aimed.

Someone asks whether our own fusion experiments involve sixth density beings, and Q'uo is dryly practical. No. And you would not want it. The operations of beings living within fusion amount to a kind of perpetual motion, ever enlarging. In a power plant, that would blow up. But there are other children of light present, the elementals, enlivening and particularizing the light wherever it falls.

One more question in the session, and a dry answer. Someone asks whether sun worship through history came from the practical gifts of sunlight, the crops and the rain, or from a real awareness of the sun's metaphysical qualities. Q'uo says: mostly the practical reasons. But in a few instances, some metaphysical material concerning the sun was known, in much distorted form, as during the ancient Egyptian civilizations. The rest of us, it seems, worshiped the sun because it warmed us, and only later learned what the warmth was made of.

Thank you for listening.

title: First I Will Be Here
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: first I will be here.

The question on the table, on the last evening of October, nineteen ninety three, is one most of us have asked in some form. The seeker works all week, rushes from task to task, feels pressed for time, and wonders where in all that busyness there is room to touch the spiritual self at all. How does a person with a full life find the unity that sustains the rest of the week?

Q'uo answers with what they call a wry smile, and I love this opening because it turns the whole question around. They say they frankly envy you the confusion and the struggle. From their side of things there is no need to gather assets, no world to go out into, and so no context in which to put truth into vibrant action. Your thick, confusing illusion forces the soul into direct confrontation with time and space. What you experience as a crowded schedule, they see as the opportunity for great witnessing.

The first answer they offer is the simplest one. Gather. Since the beginning of your time as a species, humans have come together to express spiritual feeling, as if by instinct. And Q'uo says the instinct is true. One alone who meditates is tremendously powerful. Two together are far more than their addition. And three or more become the universe. I love that line. Not three are powerful, but three become the universe.

They describe what happens when a small group sets aside time and place for common worship. Entities you cannot see, those you might call angels, flock to the site. The simple room becomes the holy place. The empty church fills with invisible energy. And the channeling that evening was happening not in a church at all but in a small home, which Q'uo says might as well be a cathedral, for it hosts a mighty company. Any small group can do this. Dedicate the treasure of time and position, and the charmed circle becomes a tower stretching to the heavens, lifting every spirit within it.

But a weekly gathering is not enough to carry the whole week, and Q'uo knows it. Normally, they say, the morning light does not call the seeker to the Creator. It calls the seeker to more mundane questions. What is to be done? What to wear? Where to go? How then to insert into this running program of activities a time for stillness?

Their answer is discipline, though not of the harsh kind. They suggest you study your own states of mind across a normal, hectic day. Gently but accurately, notice which moments you visit most often. Then find a comfortable place within that moving context to insert what they call the centering identification of self, a little marker in time and space that says, it is time to seek and know the infinite One. And then practice it. Repetitively. Listen to how they put it: practice assiduously. This is the second way to move in mind into the seeking of the Creator in all ways, in all things, which they call the key to living the busy, hectic, confusing life of one who is active in the world and yet able to remain within a spiritual context regardless of location.

The evening's questions take a personal turn. Carla asks whether becoming busier will hurt her ability to be what she calls a moving, walking-around home for the people who depend on her. Q'uo answers that those connections will show themselves most clearly in the quiet of the beginning and ending of days, like a communications center that switches on when the mind is still. And on whether she and Jim should trade channeling back and forth, Q'uo refuses to take sides and gives her this image instead: it would be as though one message were spoken in two different languages. The choice, they say, is yours.

They close with what they opened with. You cannot see how successful you are. You go on trust and faith and hope, and that inspires them. You are making the great choices between loving and risking, being loved and not risking, and each choice made unfolds yet one more petal of what blooms within. Please know, they say, that we are always with you, willing to meditate and pray with you, not in words but simply by our presence.

And there is one sentence I want to leave you with, because it might be the whole evening in seven words. The blessing of humankind is humankind. The blessing of love is love.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Brownie Points
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no brownie points.

The question in mid November, nineteen ninety three, is a delicate one. We are all engaged in some great effort, earning money, doing a life's work, completing a task. How much motivation can we draw from appreciating our own efforts? And where does honest appreciation tip over into spiritual pride?

Q'uo begins with the teacher known as Jesus and the parable of the stewards who were given money to keep for their master. One received five coins and made five more. One received two and made two more. Both were judged equal, because what mattered was not the amount of the gift but the energy put into using it. Only the one who buried his gift and did nothing lost even what he had. Listen to how they put it: the positive acceptance of spiritual responsibility is not only that which seems good but that which has great value.

The currency of the spiritual life, they say, is not money but energy, the energy the seeker is willing to spend in the attempt to do what their unique gifts suggest. One entity may have a dramatic gift, like healing. Another may have the modest gift of nurturing, and spend the life dwelling with children and family. The excellence lies equally with both, so long as each offers heart and flesh in the attempt to give what they have. Whether you wash the dishes or found a nation, it is the equal desire to serve that has equal value.

So how does one find one's gift? Meditation, over time, familiarizes the self with the deeper levels of the self. The flow of subconscious material through the threshold of consciousness increases, and more and more the meditator becomes aware of deeper gifts within. And then, having found the direction, open the consciousness to its fullest with the spoken desire to serve, not as I will but as the Creator wills. That posture of keen desire and open willingness will, in time, produce not one but often several ways of moving into more service. It helps greatly, they say, to know consciously that you are looking for it.

Then comes the heart of the question. Suppose you have found your service. Should you be satisfied? Q'uo says there is no proper answer to that query. Those who pat the back after accomplishing spiritual works are not harming the work. The harm has nothing to do with whether the work was good. The harm comes when the servant allows the work to be subjected to the reasoning process, to be weighed and measured. Yes, it is incorrect and unhelpful for a seeker to be proud of accomplishments. More than that, it is irrelevant. Whenever one attempts to quantify the value of spiritual work, one has missed the point.

There are no Brownie points, as the instrument puts it. Strip all from the mind that would suggest otherwise. Naked are you. You cannot be clothed with righteousness. You are clothed, each of you, they say, by the light of your desire to abandon all except the desire to serve.

Then how do you know when you have gotten it right? Not by patting the self on the back, but by turning to give thanks. The moment when you are one with the work, when there is a feeling of complete freedom in doing it, that liberty is the sign of service well done.

The evening's questions wander into lovely corners. Carla asks whether encouraging the self is permitted, since encouraging others surely is. Q'uo answers with the ideal: focus the encouragement on the Creator as fully as you can, seeing the effort and the entities involved as the Creator, and giving praise and thanksgiving for both. And a seeker who struggles to stay in meditation gets this spare, beautiful counsel: the most important portion of meditation is cultivating the desire to meditate. That can be done in an instant. All other effort is built on that foundation.

So the answer to the evening's question is not a formula for balancing pride against humility. It is a direction. Stop trying to measure. Keep asking one question: how may I serve?

Thank you for listening.

title: The Secret Mansion
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the secret mansion.

Late November, nineteen ninety three, and the question is one of the oldest in the archive. Ra has suggested that lessons learned with the forgetting process in place carry far more weight than lessons learned when we remember our total nature. So how does the forgetting work? How is it put into place, and how does the remembering happen?

Q'uo asks us to picture a large mansion with many rooms, built in the grand style of centuries past. In this dwelling there are secret passageways and staircases, secret rooms and tunnels. A visitor could live there a long time without ever knowing the secret portion of the house exists. Yet the rooms would continue to exist on the other side of that secret door, whether the visitor knew or not. It is in this kind of way, they say, that the forgetting process occurs.

Picture a newborn infant, a tiny bundle of raw need and pure, innocent life. Yet that infant contains all the space for its memories that it has ever had and ever will have. Some of those memories are from many, many incarnations. But some of the content is older than that: memory given as a portion of essential beingness, from the original Thought, which is divine love. The truth, they say, is ineluctably placed within each entity as part of the basic consciousness. The secret door is there. The visitor simply does not know it.

They speak of birth itself as a true marriage of Earth and heaven. Before the first breath, the consciousness may hover near the forming body rather than take its seat within it. When the time comes, the entity must go into the physical vehicle and bind the lighter bodies to the physical one, until the body is laid down. That which has not been born nor shall die joins itself to that which lives and dies. That which is forever the Mystery takes up residence.

It may seem a cruel joke, they admit, that such pure infants must be taken from the consciousness of truth. But to the conscious mind there is given only a shadow of the stored memories. What remains is something like a bare instinct for the right, a flag or a token suggesting that there is a more ethical way to live. And this is the point. The deeper truth is protected from quick and easy access on purpose, because there is extreme power released when the truth is claimed, and it is a worthy goal to seek it, to persevere in asking and desiring.

To the one who watches and pays close attention, every situation can hold revelation. But know, they say, that the doors open only insofar as one continues to apply the truths already learned. And many seekers try to speed up the process far beyond the rate at which they can reasonably learn and retain. Better to allow the waiting, to let the growing perceptions seat themselves in the stable connection between newly opened subconscious material and its emergence into the fully conscious mind.

There is a mythological image they offer. These secret places within the mansion of your being are the treasure trove, and the dragon guards the treasure. The dragon is that portion of the universal Self which helps the self stay whole, because the original Truth you seek is powerful enough to have created all that there is, and powerful enough to end it. Contact with this energy is best allowed to occur naturally, with no heightened expectations. In quietness and in peace shall truth be yours.

And what is the key to the secret door? When asked directly for the best way to aid the remembering, Q'uo gives the shortest answer of the evening. Meditation. Contemplation. Prayer. Whatever the name, the intention to seek the Mystery triggers an instinct within the conscious portion of the deep mind, focusing energy around that mountaintop which has poked up from the subconscious, that little peak which says there must be a Creator. You carry the blueprint of all things within, and the potential to activate any or all of this knowledge.

The evening ends with a surprise guest. After Q'uo takes their leave, a new voice comes through the instrument, brief and bright, calling itself Yadda. Let no one discourage you, it says. If someone seems to have authority yet discourages your efforts, then you must say, he is not what he seems. Stand on your two feet and encourage yourself. Be never faint of heart.

Thank you for listening.

title: Sharpening the Intellect
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: sharpening the intellect.

Late November, nineteen ninety three, and the evening's discussion is astrology. The tape begins in the middle of a question, so we drop straight into Q'uo's thoughts, offered with the usual disclaimer: hear these as the thoughts of a friend, not an all-wise teacher. They make errors too.

Q'uo gives the instrument a picture first. A world in darkness, but a waiting darkness, like the eve of a great holiday. There is among your peoples, they say, a growing consciousness that some great event seems to be in the offing, so that the coming of the night is more acceptable. The end, they say, is truly near, not physically, but mentally and spiritually. It is a great time to be watchful, and a good time to celebrate whatever might aid the development of that sharply tuned hunger for the truth revealed in the present moment.

Into this frame they bring astrology, which they describe as a complex, detail-driven system of ephemeral mathematical constructs having to do with the configurations of heavenly bodies. For the student who wishes to probe more deeply within the self, it offers one way of learning more about the deeper mind. Not the personal predictions so much as the archetypical level: the relationships of star to star and star to your home system, and how those relationships explicate the archetypical mind.

There is a personal level too. Keeping up with the progression of one's own chart can develop an instinct for influence and a relatively authentic feeling of control over life experience. But Q'uo is careful here. To one entity such study would be work, a difficult chore. To such a one they suggest investigating other avenues, better attuned to their environment. Astrology is that for which some entities are well suited, and others not.

Then they widen the lens, and I love this passage because it is not really about astrology at all. Insofar as any system is internally valid in its logic, that system may become, for the entity who plumbs its depths, a crutch or aid which acts as a collector for the abilities of the seeker. Astrology, numerology, the study of the hand or the head, the systems of myth, science, philosophy or ethics, pick whichever one you are drawn to. What avails the seeker is the systematic nature itself, because the mind within incarnation has the instinct for the pattern.

The mind, they say, is always working to place the present moment into a context that yields the maximum amount of information. That information is usually biased toward comfort and well-being. But the mind can be trained to retain catalyst which has little survival use and yet aids in spiritual learning. And the way to do that work in consciousness is to persist in experiencing one system, whatever system you are personally drawn to, so deeply that it sharpens the intellect.

Listen to how they put the payoff. Astrology is the hors d'oeuvre which encourages an entity to fit the intellect to accept an increasing number of inferences. This ability to loosen the self from the physical and move into an abstract system of gazing at the self is key. It softens the mind to accept increasing numbers of inferences, so that the gifts called psychic may express themselves intelligibly. For that which you seek cannot be deduced or received. Discuss what you will. You cannot bring instrumentation to bear on the original Thought of the one infinite Creator.

And the deeper purpose of all this sharpening is one they return to again and again. Dwell in the present moment. Marinate the complete entity in it. It may seem odd that the entrance to the present is often roundabout, moving not through the invisible door but completely around the structure of living to surprise the present moment, only after the long walk has sharpened the appetite.

The evening's questions then turn to a seeker who wants to know whether logical reasoning has any use when examining his own reactions to giving aid. Q'uo applauds the care. To look at the experience after it is completed, and review one's reactions, thoughts and emotions, is the archetypical path of the seeker. The illusion exists for your seeking and your learning. Spend time daily reflecting upon the day as it has passed, they say. Note those experiences where there was movement in your own consciousness, those that left behind a strength and a mark upon your memory.

And one caution about that giving. To have a preconceived idea of the outcome of any event is to confuse the perception of the event when it occurs. It is not inappropriate to have these preconceptions, they say, only inconvenient.

Thank you for listening.

title: Keep Walking
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: keep walking.

Mid December, nineteen ninety three, and the group has a sheepish question for Q'uo. The Confederation contacts hear basically the same sorts of questions from us, again and again. Being and doing. Controlling and allowing. The lessons of love. We orbit in small circles, asking for the same things. What does that look like from their side?

Q'uo's answer is gracious and a little funny. We were unaware, they say, that we ever do any other thing but iterate and reiterate the one simple truth: that all that there is is one thing, and that thing is a mystery which recedes before us as we move. They have a very favorable opinion of your repetitive queries.

They point to the teacher known as Jesus, who told his followers to be perfect as the Father is perfect, and then spent his ministry bestowing love on a rogues' gallery of the imperfect: the tax collector, the prostitute, the halt and the lame. We too, say Q'uo, encourage you to fight the good fight, gazing on each moment as the ever unfolding opportunity to become perfect. And we predict the odds are great that you shall not perceive yourselves as being anywhere near it.

There is a tender observation here. Earlier that day Carla had been in despair, looking at her own actions and thoughts and asking herself, is this the way you live in the Creator's presence? Q'uo points out gently that in each instance she was thinking of the Creator, with the relationship of the self to the Creator inevitably characterized within the heart. There was no chance of being away from the Creator's presence. When you criticize yourself, gaze at who is criticizing and who is criticized. These are both the self. And that dialogue with self would not be possible were the self not composed of voices which include the voice that calls to remembrance.

Then comes the heart of the evening, and it is an image I will not forget. The early days of seeking bring rapid, noticeable change. Meditation becomes routine. The world of nature is seen with brand new eyes. But as the desire for spiritual evolution is satisfied, the unfamiliar sets in. The self is transforming and is no longer a set character. The path moves onward, yet the seeker wishes for some structure within which to seek, and that structure is constantly being torn down by the very progression that was desired. So the odds are good that the seeker will again and again perceive the self as out of balance. And their greatest message in this regard is this: keep walking.

They illustrate with ice on a pond. The sheet of ice is solid to the touch, one shape only, changed only by breaking. Yet below the ice is living water, the habitat of beings, and fish and plant life thrive beneath the solid sheet. This is you in incarnation. The solid entity that greets you in the mirror is crystalline and marvelously wrought. But it is merely the surface of your form. Within are deep and living waters, in which the flora and fauna of archetypical images may thrive and bloom. Does the physical form change because of this life moving within? Usually not. Yet this is your self, mostly unknown by you, except that you can feel that pressure of vitality coming from the depths within.

The crystalline form needs to be battered with that blunt instrument called repetition, a hundred or a thousand times before the dent is made. The work is slow, and you feel pokey and petty and tired of not quite getting it yet. So they encourage each to consciously irrigate the self in these living waters of the deep mind, and then allow that consciousness to fade, and take up the attempt again, daily, hourly, moment by moment, to live the life of faith as witness.

And there is a last comfort for everyone who has ever asked the same question twice. With each repetition, the total of Love does not expand but simply intensifies, so that as each lesson is repeated, new and deeper graspings are found. The entity has not been dealt, they say, that can do the same thing twice, not in the world of spirit.

So do not be disappointed in the repetition. It simply indicates where the rubber is hitting the road. Keep walking. Keep irrigating. And in that witness, whether by expression or aura or any word or deed, may you celebrate that imperfection which is the perfect outworking of a life lived in faith and service.

Thank you for listening.

title: Spirit Mother, Spirit Fathers
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: spirit mother, spirit fathers.

Late December, nineteen ninety three, and the whole evening is given to a single dream. A seeker has had what he felt was an extremely enlightening dream, and he asks Q'uo to help him understand it in five parts. We join the interpretation already underway, because the dream state, Q'uo says, is marvelously equipped to handle complex and shifting values, the concerns a seeker is considering on many levels, most of them subconscious.

The first teaching is a key to all dream work. The denizens of dreams have various identities, but in one of the most important senses, all figures within a dream are the self. This seems confusing at first. If all the figures are the self, where is the dynamic that carries instruction? Yet the self is an entity of a level of complexity difficult to express. Within each self exist the foreshadowings of all possible states of mind, all feelings and emotions, indeed, all situations. So the interpreter looks at each character hoping to penetrate the symbol it represents. Familiarity with the archetypical mind helps, through disciplines like the tarot, which attempt to capture the many-layered colors of the tapestry of the self.

The seeker's dream holds a spirit mother and three spirit fathers. Q'uo lingers on the mother. To gaze at a mother in a dream is to look for the archetype of the female. The female, they say, is the doorway through which all life essences stream. Those incarnated in female vehicles contain the world within them, for through their wombs all must come who come into manifestation. Before that door, that gateway, all give homage. Toward the female is felt an irresistible love, often experienced as a darker, more convoluted love bearing in its folds the pain of that within the male which is not alive as is the female.

The three images of father, the rough, the strong, the wily, are not mutually exclusive, but Q'uo suggests considering them as the mind, the physical vehicle, and the spiritual self, moving always back from the detail to the essence, from complexity toward unity of wedded understanding.

The second question concerns the spirit mother's answer about the constancy of the seeker's being. Q'uo offers a startling image. When the tadpole becomes a frog, the change is obvious. When a seeker has unwittingly fulfilled an archetypical task, the transformation is not obvious at all. It takes place at two levels. In the subconscious there is no veil, and clarity of color and detail is seen. But the conscious self is like the tip of the iceberg, tempted to think the mirror image is the whole self, while most of what makes the seeker unique lies forever hidden. Great magnitudes of change are seen below the threshold of consciousness, rainbows of color detailing the melodrama of the evolving self, while above the threshold the changes are muted.

It is well, then, to accept on faith alone that the work done faithfully is creating new selfhood below the veil, even when conscious experience lacks brilliance. And do not try to take the spiritual temperature. The least among your peoples can judge the self, but the greatest among you cannot judge wisely. The running of the race is in itself that satisfaction which truly endures.

The third question touches the archetype of the Choice, from the tarot: a male figure with hands crossed across the breast, holding in each hand one of two women, one of positive polarity and one of negative. The moment of choice between them configures the way that opens before the one who chooses. The seeker's question itself, in its energy, constrained the form the spirit mother's answer took.

The fourth asks why this happened in a dream rather than in waking life. Q'uo encourages the seeker to rejoice, because the subconscious is always far more fully conscious than the waking entity. Were this material given with such clarity in waking life, the consensus reality the self depends upon would be greatly shaken. The dream is skillfully knitted up for the self by the self, in a way that lets the self remain within its incarnational biases. Such brightness would blind the physical eye.

The last question is how best to honor such an experience. Q'uo suggests the skill that moves forward from such a dream-vision. To stay with the lesson of today, tomorrow and tomorrow is to baffle the natural flow of ongoing experience. It is well for the mind to open the hand, metaphorically, to release from any bondage that great gift which has been given to the self by the self. Have faith that what has been harvested within is safe and cannot be denied or stolen.

They close with the ground of it all. This frustrating, confusing, chaotic experience you rush through is where lessons are learned, love is taken in and given out, and all of worth is collected. Respect the incarnational self. Respect and offer homage to the intransigent, often negatively seeming face of everyday life. And always, the steady, persistent, daily meditative times, be they short or long, for these seat and stabilize learning and open the door into the silence which births the creation.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Center of the Constellations
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the center of the constellations.

The first Sunday of the new year, nineteen ninety four, and the question comes from N. Since as above, so below, can we understand the whole by finding correlations between cosmic cycles and the workings of the human body, down to cells and molecules and the etheric body? And what about the great cycles of time: the minor harvest cycle of twenty five thousand years, the master cycle of seventy five thousand?

Q'uo's first move is to say that the attempt to match these hierarchies is made non-useful by a simple fact. Neither your physical vehicles nor your consciousness are equipped with receptors capable of assimilating the amount of data that exists. That which is above is indeed reflected in that which is below, but that which is above is other than can be conjured or figured out. It is difficult to express how this perfectly logical-seeming set of correspondences actually has an effect, because the archetypical mind is most deep, and for that reason most difficult to penetrate.

They do not dismiss the study entirely. To work on the influences of heavenly objects is subtle work in the area of the archetypical mind, and the study of these correspondences yields a wealth of detailed information for each individual who undertakes it. But they are clear that it touches healing only tangentially. What aids healing is not a map of cycles but an understanding of fields, of the amount of saturation, the fullness of love in the fields. The more saturated the awareness of love, they say, the more fullness of health there is.

As for the great cycles themselves, the timing is not fixed in the stars.
