The cycles of spiritual living are as they are because of sensitive factors involving the energies of the group of entities moving through third density. As the populations' biases are collectively altered through time, the timing of the cycles evolves. The setting of these cycles is ever liquid, regulated precisely according to every single entity and every single thought.

The questions grow more specific: is there a star at the center of the seventy five thousand year cycle? What of a two hundred and six thousand year cycle, or twenty six million years? Q'uo answers each with the same brevity. We do not find the comparisons listed to be useful. We do not find significance to the twenty six million year cycle.

And then they give the sentence that makes this evening worth remembering. Perhaps we could suggest that the center of the universe is the center of each entity's heart. The open heart of the great Self which each self is, is that center which is a unity. All measurement, all numbering, all ways of detailing and patterning the observed creation fall to dust before the open heart.

It is both blessing and curse, they say, that those who yearn for scientific information to aid in being of service must have their hopes thwarted by the elusive, ever-receding face of spiritual knowledge. For this knowledge is not that which has to do with the kind of measuring used to calculate the hierarchies of the observable universe. Love moves, and its traces dwell within all things. The keys to healing echo the ways or nature of love itself.

They close with a benediction for the cold season. Live in hope and in faith, forgetting not one iota of the darkness perceived, but knowing that no darkness eradicates light. Live, then, in light, for inwardly you may always be standing beneath the bright sun. As your spirit basks in its intelligent warmth, the body is most positively effected.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Incarnational Train
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the incarnational train.

Mid January, nineteen ninety four, and the question is about change. How do we best accept it? What attitude serves us? And what is this sense of ourselves that changes, and uses tools like the mind and dreams and the archetypical mind to change?

Q'uo begins with a riddle. Imagine the unity and infinity of creation. That which is various is infinitely various. That which is infinite is made of one thing. Where, then, is the change? Within each unique and infinitely precious soul lies all that there is. The changes and chances of incarnation take place against a grand backdrop.

Then comes the image that carries the whole evening. You are on the incarnational train. It is not a local. It does not stop until you disembark. You are among the travelers, talking and drinking and eating and sleeping and gazing out the windows at the passing scenery. The curves and mountains and valleys and great chasms that seem to toss and fling you through life are the scenery of your spirit's learning, the visual aids of the great college which is your incarnation. The change you perceive is perception of change, not change. You are simply moving from car to car on that train of destiny.

And destiny, Q'uo says, is your greatest ally. You put yourself on this train. This trip was planned by you. You did not ask to be happy or sad, to do well or poorly. You asked to experience this exact incarnation. Your responsibility is to experience as fully as possible each moment, to be hungry for food, that food being all that you can pay your attention to. You are beyond all changes secure, safe, and held with the greatest tenderness by the love of the infinite One. When all overwhelms you, remember that you need do nothing but rest in those arms.

Who is it that changes, and who witnesses the change? Q'uo gives a second image. Imagine the self standing in the desert at night. The figure reaches one hand to the sky and begins to dance, and as it spins, the stars above begin to whirl until all of creation is drawn star by star into the self. This figure has all within: all of star, all of space, all of emotion, all of life. This is the entity which witnesses change. All that you have experienced as rock, as tree, as human, as angel, as sun, as Creator, all of these are the witness that flings the hand to beckon the stars. All that moves moves and has being in an instant, and through all change the witness keeps its feet steadily upon the desert floor.

You ask how to meet change? Their answer is disarming. You do not have to meet change. You only have to remember who you are. You are the witness. Pay attention. Remember the desert floor and the out-flung hand. Meet change with love, for you have nothing to fear. You commanded this change.

The third teaching comes from the teacher known as Jesus: worry not about what to eat or what to wear, for food and clothing and words will all be supplied, one day at a time. Yesterday's change is moving away behind you. Tomorrow's change is not yet imagined. You need only focus upon the present moment as you perceive it. How much of change is painful because it is resisted? Change does not happen well to entities holding on to anything.

And there is one permission in this evening that I want to highlight, because so many spiritual teachings withhold it. Complaining is allowed, they say. Complaining is encouraged. Too much is made of the wonderfulness of the infinite Creator and not enough said about the intimate love that engages you in conversation and responds caringly to the way you speak your experience. Especially in times of dislocating change, tell your story, mentally or out loud, to the infinite One. The infinite One is never happier than when being addressed, and you, in addressing it, receive reflections you cannot imagine.

Call upon your own faith. Feel strongly the hope which abides. And remember that all these changes have to do with lessons about loving. You are experiencing manyness. You seek infinity. Bring in, too, remembrance, love. All things will pass away except love. You are love, they say. You just don't know it yet. Give yourself and the illusion time.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Lighthouse Keepers
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the lighthouse keepers.

Late January, nineteen ninety four, and the question is a curious one. Over the years, people who read the Law of One books have come to visit the little group that receives these channelings, sometimes for days, sometimes for hours. And they report feeling a kind of transformative experience, in differing degrees of intensity. The group wonders how this works. They do not do anything in particular. They just live their lives. Yet people arrive and feel as though they have come home to a family.

Q'uo begins in the present moment. Right now, they say, a small group has gathered expressly to seek. And to this modest gathering have come myriads of inner and outer planes entities, which flock to those places where light is being generated, both to join in the joy and to lend their limitless light to the light the seekers have begun to create. When the small group gathers, the one and one and one become more than two or three. They become, indeed, the entirety of creation. And to that universe comes the one infinite Creator in the active mode.

They quote the teacher known as Jesus: when two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the midst of them. A light center fulfills this. When even the smallest group gathers seeking the Creator, the Creator is immediately present and listens carefully to the requests made by seekers.

But there is more to the organization than the framework on paper. Q'uo speaks of the living edifice which walks upon two legs. The way of this group has been sacrifice: time, money, talent given to create the sure and certain hour when meditation, study and questioning could be counted upon. The living room became an office. Each having done what was necessary, each may now simply abide. And the power of abiding is deep. They look to the archetype of the Hanged Man. Into manifestation you offer the self and all the life, knowing it turns one upside down. This you accepted, and so it comes into manifestation with plenty and bounty as its characteristics.

Then they switch the camera to the point of view of those who seek. Those who set sail upon a spiritual journey sail in trackless blackness. The winds blow the thin cloud before the moon, and the spiritual sea is never quiet. Where is the North Star for those who sail so? For most, no direction is found, no star may guide. Yet when a seeking sailor comes across the work of a positively oriented group, there is the aid of what they call kind destiny. The sailor settles upon the dock and says, all right, I know there is no outer answer. This is all of me, all that I am. I lay it before my Creator. Yield to me in your good time the star of hope. Show me a way. To one who holds up this hope, the star does appear, and sometimes that star has a name.

What do the travelers find when they arrive? Outwardly, just Jim and Carla and a living room office. Inwardly, the certainty that herein lies the infinite and the eternal touching into manifestation. And the two of them are amazed at the fire ignited when seekers find them, but Q'uo tells them to put aside both the amazement and the guilt of feeling unworthy. As entities see Jim and Carla, they see not Jim and Carla, for these entities have gotten themselves out of the way. It is the spirit within, the Creator present within, which is seen.

The evening's questions then take a painful turn. Carla speaks of hearing more and more people getting the illness called AIDS, so many kindly and beautiful souls laid down and killed by it, and asks if there is one image or healing to yearn for. Q'uo can only recommend prayer for courage, for strength of faith, for the purpose of the life well lived in the opening of the heart. For all within your illusion shall find its end, and each will walk through the door of death, and the experience completed will be that which was the destiny of the incarnation. Pray for the happy heart to come soon, they say, for soon it shall come.

This is the archive speaking in its own spiritual language, and it is not medical guidance. If you or someone you love is living with a serious illness, please lean on real-world care: doctors you trust, treatment that is proven, and people who will sit with you through it. The prayer Q'uo offers here sits alongside that care, not in place of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Rocks in the Stream
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: rocks in the stream.

The last Sunday of January, nineteen ninety four, and the question is about truth itself. Facing the truth, telling the truth, feeling fears release. It is said, know the truth and it will set you free. How exactly does this work in our daily lives?

Q'uo begins, through this instrument, with the trial of the teacher known as Jesus. While the process worked itself out, the civil authority known as Pilate pondered what Jesus offered, and his comment was, what is truth? He could not find within the true statements made by each entity an overriding truth which would create choice, so he walked away from the debate, giving control over to others rather than answering the question.

Consider the levels. Pilate's truth was written on a sign: the king of the Jews. Those who wanted Jesus stopped had their truth: this man could rouse rebellion and disturb the peace of Rome. Jesus had his own truth, of another level of beingness: that his truth was not applicable to the world of temporal affairs, and that in witnessing to it there was virtue in the sacrifice of all earthly energy. For him there was a freedom, and that freedom was complete service. To find the truth in this story is impossible, they say, for there were several levels of true feeling, true fact, true intention. The truth is most slippery. It recedes from the attempt to pin it down.

Each of you, they say, is at heart one vibration, and one vibration alone. The love that created all that there is is an original Thought of such power as is unimaginable, and that articulated thought called love has a vibration. This vibration is the truth, for it is all that there is. The rest is illusion. Each seeker hungers for the freedom of the true nature and seeks to move into closer vibratory similarity with love.

Then they lay out the levels of truth you actually live with. There is the light and momentary truth: the garbage is picked up on Monday, you are supposed to be at work at nine in the morning. These are truths, but there is no healing in them. Deeper, there is the true self with its vagrant moods, and emotional truth in hewing with fidelity to these inner moods. Without judging the self, there is great healing in simply acknowledging the nature of the self as it is self-perceived. And deeper still is that truth which cannot be accessed by words at all, only by the inner experiencing of things far too inimitable for description. The hunger of the seeker is to see the face of the infinite One, and there is no face for that intelligence. That face is your own, and the face of the entity next to you, and the face of nature.

On fears, they offer something gentle. Your fears are also a truth, and fear is not something to be rooted out before its time. You have no need to rush. The Creator will not leave.

And on compassion, they are practical in a way I appreciate. Compassion is always truth. But if you are in a weaker or more transparent part of your cycle, it can be harmful, self-sacrificing, to express compassion when what is honest is the seemingly negative information of your own limitations and needs. It is not always skillful to be compassionate. It is well to know the self well enough to see when compassion alone is the truth to tell, and when instead it would be more skillful to speak seemingly selfishly but honestly.

The questions then turn to the physical side of this work. How does facing fears and telling truth affect the body? Q'uo gives the image of a stream full of rocks of various sizes, diverting the flow of water. Your belief system confines that which is limitless into a compacted illusion, and this takes effort on all levels. That effort you perceive as tension. The freeing of the belief system is like removing the rocks one by one from the stream, so the full force of the water's flow may be felt without distortion. And the release can be seated in meditation: observe the condition as it was, the nature of the distortion, the removal of it, and give thanksgiving for the opportunity to more fully express the energy of love.

There is also a practical mercy near the end for the sensitive. One seeker feels overwhelmed by the energies in the circle, lured away, afraid. Q'uo reassures her, and offers a simple instruction she can use any time: if you feel invaded or overtaken, ask the presence to leave, in the name of whatever you hold most dear, love or truth or service, or the name of Jesus or the Buddha or any saint or angel. Asked with the whole heart, the invading entity will be required to leave. Then circle the self in light and love, so that the shield is in place.

All your fears shall fetch up against this rock and flow away. Within the silence of the heart lies all that there is, and it is all holy.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Healer Offers Opportunity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the healer offers opportunity.

The first Sunday of February, nineteen ninety four, and the question comes from N, a healer with a great desire to serve. It concerns healing disease, and the premise is that illness not chosen before birth is a last resource of evolution, a final way of processing catalyst. The questioner wants to know how learning happens in the person who is unaware of all this, whether a healer incurs debts by helping, and what happens when the one seeking healing dies.

Q'uo's first move is to step back from the premise. Healing, they say, is a much misunderstood concept, for healing and cures are not the same. Furthermore, the term healer suggests a definition which is incorrect. The healer does not do anything. The healer does not heal. The healer presents to the one requesting healing an opportunity.

Listen to how they put it. In noninvasive healing, the opportunity is created from the crystallization of the healer's personality, so that the healer becomes the equivalent of the healing chamber within the Great Pyramid. When surgery or chemicals are used, this is a physically objective means, visible to the eye, touchable by the hand, of offering the self-same healing opportunity. In every case the actual healing is a process involving the unmanifested self. The strong and invasive avenues may cure the body, and cures are real and have their place, but in no case can a curing by invasive means function as a healing of the imbalance which the ill health is addressing. This remains in the precinct of curing a physical condition.

So the healer is advised to surrender the personal agenda. It is so easy to feel that one shall do this and that and it shall operate in a healing modality. Actually, it is well to remain humble, for the healer works upon its own self, and in no case does the healer heal. The patient, meanwhile, remains completely responsible for its own processes of healing. To the healer, all patients are the same, and the processes of actual healing are in each case the same.

There is no karma between healer and healed, they say. The healer who is mature has become aware that the Creator is always present, that the power of the unnamable mystery is always infinite, in every location, at every time, under any and all conditions. When given the choice between a cure and a healing, they ask, which would each choose as patient? Which would each choose as a healer serving the infinite One?

On the question of death, they describe what happens between incarnations. There is healing there, but on a level of metaphysical wholeness. The spirit looks through the book of self, missing no pages, and reintegrates the significant self in a way that more accurately and lovingly places the distortions within the entity, gradually preparing it for its next incarnation. But it is within physical incarnation, not outside it, that the imbalances are taken up again.

The evening holds two biblical images of the true healer. Elijah, asked to heal one who was dead, lay upon the body hand to hand, foot to foot, mouth to mouth, literally breathing life into the patient. And the woman who was ill and touched the hem of Jesus' robe was healed, and he knew healing had taken place because he felt the power go forth. He did not intend it personally. He was an instrument through which healing came.

To the questioner, the healer N, who could not be present, Q'uo speaks directly. Allow the concerns to recede. Practice the simple presence of the infinite One. Contemplate the sun, which gives so generously. Stand beneath the tree generating itself from light. Gaze about the self to find any arrhythmic or out-of-place detail in the creation. Is there any, except that which man has imposed? The nature of faith is that it is what one claims it is. The simple assertion of a life in faith creates, when persistently invoked, the life in faith.

And then a brief, warm coda from Hatonn, who had been silently present. To the one known as N, Hatonn confirms constant company when requested, not to give answers but to aid in practicing the presence of the one infinite Creator. All desire and seeking for that vibratory level which is the love of the one infinite Creator is felt, and does indeed change the inner balance.

A note of care before I close. This episode speaks of healing in the archive's spiritual language: opportunity, presence, faith. It is not medical advice, and it does not replace the work of doctors, treatment, or the real-world support that illness calls for. If you are facing sickness, please keep both: the care of medicine and the company of whatever brings you peace.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Praising Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love praising love.

Mid February, nineteen ninety four, and N has posed Q'uo a provocative question. If Q'uo were itself a third-density entity, here with that purpose in mind, how would it design a healing strategy that encompassed all the needs of third-density beings?

Q'uo's first answer is a refusal, and it is worth sitting with. It is one thing, they say, to look upon the Earth scene from where we are and philosophize about improving it. It is quite another to be within that third density which you now enjoy. Not we, with our experience, but you, with your limitations and challenges, are the ones called to service at this particular juncture. Were we you, we would be equally limited. Only those who are within third density have the right to attempt to create such conditions as universal healing.

Still, they offer what they can. Healing or health, as they see it, has to do fundamentally not with the physical vehicle, nor simply with the mental vehicle, but with what creates a broader or deeper faith. What is health but the just proportion or balance of energies within the individual self? Health is not simply a matter of sickness and curing sickness. Health has to do with the balance of energies so that the self is tuned, as much as can be achieved, to a continuing awareness of the self as a child of the infinite Creator. Healing begins with the realization that love and loving constitute wellness.

They give an image for the inner work. Picture one who chooses to go into a grand hall and set the table for a sumptuous banquet. To the human eye the banquet hall may not exist. To the heart within, beating in faith, the hall shall fill to overflowing and the feast shall take place. The soul which seeks persistently the inner sanctuary, the mercy seat of the heart, will hear what they call the heart of silence speaking its blessed chant: love praising love, love thanking love, love having any emotion whatever to love.

There is a hard teaching tucked inside this evening. The third density, they say, is not intended to be universally healed. The perceived imperfections of the illusion are innumerable, and it is a virtue of third-density illusion that it continues rough, unfinished and unhealed. These are the conditions which promote rapidity of learning. The real health of the soul is not risked by third-density conditions, whatever they be. Why would the Creator allow suffering as part of the plan? They feel it is true, though it has no obvious answer: what the Creator has in mind is not an increase in health of the body or mind or emotion, but a continuing possibility for improvement in the balancing and aligning of mind, body, emotions and spirit.

So health, within third density, is that state in which the entity has achieved a stable balance within the self, so that each energy has space for clarity and focus, much as you would see a color become more pure. Each entity becoming more true, more just in balance and proportion, one energy to another. And this point of balance is unique for each unique entity.

Q'uo cannot, they say, move into your perceived reality and hook perfection out of the sea of confusion like a fish, nor would it be the Creator's work to lift any bodily into perfection. They count themselves most blessed if they can suggest to even one entity that a stubborn focus upon infinite perfection will take the energies as they are and, through time, produce such visions and clues concerning balance as are necessary for that individual's progress.

The session closes with counsel for the instrument herself, who had been questioning her path of service in the face of small meetings and unmet practical needs. Where is the heart of service for you? Where is love, for you? Where are your gifts? Always, it is not the outer appearance which determines the success of employing one's gifts. One must simply move as one feels to move, always aware that the service is service to love, in love, for love, by means of love alone. Lift the heart, lift the mind, lift the viewpoint, just as the sun seems to lift the flower bud.

And a question worth carrying away: when one can, even for a moment, see and feel the truth of turning to love above all things, then shall healing truly multiply.

A gentle note. This episode treats healing as the archive sees it, a matter of faith and balance, and that is a spiritual perspective, not a medical one. Illness deserves real care: doctors, treatment, and support you can lean on. Hold this evening's reflection alongside those, not instead of them.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Truth Is the Creator
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the truth is the creator.

Mid March, nineteen ninety four, and the question is as large as they come. How does the Creator step down its conscious being in order to occupy a physical body, use the rays of the bodies, and have an incarnation?

Q'uo's answer is the shortest and bluntest of the evening. The Creator has not stepped down its selfhood in anywise, in any density or circumstance. The truth is the Creator. The rest is illusion. All that you strive to comprehend, you already know. All that you strive to be, you already are. However, free will dances with each entity in this Creatorhood, and each becomes unique within illusion. The oddity and peculiarity of that uniqueness is valuable.

They give an image for our situation. The plight of humans dealing with their creatorship is much like swimmers in an ocean a mile deep. That of which the swimmer is aware barely scratches the surface of the sea. And so it is with consciousness: all the highs and lows of thought encompass merely the surface of selfhood, for that surface is the surface whose depths cry out in praise of the one infinite Creator.

Does the Creator, then, praise itself? Yes, they say. All of creation sings a hymn of praise and thanks. This is the vibration of being. This is your nature. Insofar as one may lay hold on this truth and allow it to be described within, some learning shall occur.

Then Q'uo turns to something that happened to the instrument that very day. A soul lay close to dying. A priest was reading the prayers of ministry to the sick, and with each prayer the sick man became calmer, but he could not hear well, so the priest raised his voice and read the twenty third psalm. The Lord is my shepherd. I shall not want. As the last verse was spoken, surely goodness and mercy shall follow you all the days of your life, and you shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever, the man simply stopped breathing. It was a good death, Q'uo says. This entity knew that he was in the house of the Lord, forever, and fear had no more place within him, and the healing took place, instantly. It was a healing death.

This is delicate ground, and I want to treat it with care. The archive is speaking here of a spiritual peace at the end of life, not offering instruction about death. If you are grieving, or sitting with someone who is dying, or carrying thoughts of your own ending that frighten you, please reach for real human support: hospice workers, counselors, clergy you trust, friends who will simply be present. What Q'uo offers here is a reflection to hold alongside that care, not in place of it.

The teaching continues with the mind. The mind is far more powerful than any other force within your experience. What you know, or think you know, creates your illusion. Therefore it is well to know what you know, to build only what you personally have experienced and know from an organic and involved viewpoint. For the deepest part of what you know is what you are, not what you do or say.

In illness, they say, the healing is that intangible process where the mind becomes aware of a more powerful field of energy than that expressed by the sickness. The physician may work upon the mechanical and chemical aspects of a body, tinkering with the mechanism and oiling the dry spots, but the actual state of that body is quenched by what the entity knows, or is. The highest energy an entity can access determines how much the ills of flesh shall move according to the rules of manifestation. If there is a basic key to healing as opposed to curing, it is this: the awareness of the entity moves to that place where it states to itself, this is who I am.

Then, unexpectedly, Q'uo asks everyone to breathe, and speaks of relaxation. This circle, they observe with humor, is very serious. It is a common error of the earnest and idealistic entity to enmire the self so deeply in the strictures of desire and learning that the heart forgets how to skip, the mind to sing. So they ask each to be deliberate about releasing the self into immediate appreciation of the Earth. Breathe in and breathe out, knowing the partnership with all living things. Feel the heart lift because the sun is golden, or the moon serene.

It is not wise to attempt to be too serious, they say. It is wise to be the fool, and be foolish regularly. For there is truth not just in the earnest things of metaphysics, but also much truth in the playful, in the energetic fun. Hurry not. Cease rushing. Spend more time being.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Silent Witness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the silent witness.

Late March, nineteen ninety four, and the voice this evening is Hatonn's. The fragment of the opening question that survives on the tape asks about the role of beings like Q'uo in our spiritual seeking, and how we might be of service to each other. Hatonn answers with what they call a very simple message, offered again and again through the years.

The Creator, they say, is of a nature which may be summed up by a vibratory level. This vibration we call love. Each entity also has a vibration, indeed a complex of vibratory levels harmonizing to make your unique signature. The teaching is this: as each seeker moves its vibratory complex closer and closer to the vibration of love, the infinite self within begins to sound its true note and identity. In human terms these attempts to be as the Deity are useless. In the metaphysical world, where intention and desire are as real as a chair or a person, such seeking is effective.

They describe themselves with a lovely comparison. Institutions equivalent in general nature to theirs among your peoples might include the Peace Corps, or those who work with Vista in the inner city. Not missionaries. Not religions. Counselors, attempting to inform those who request their service of their understanding of the basic nature of the creation, the Creator, and each seeker's place within it. They hope for no church and no power in your world. They simply make themselves available, to afford a spiritual home to those who need one.

Why would the Creator place each entity within such a heavy illusion? Hatonn answers with the long view. To us, you belong to infinity, for we see each of you as eternal. And the great glory and purpose of your experience is that you shall suffer as you learn, and in that suffering you shall be transformed.

Hatonn quotes the teacher known as Jesus on the wedding feast. To the feast were invited the high and the mighty, the comfortable and the well off. But one must have business here and another there, so the feast had empty places. Therefore the father sent people out to comb the neighborhood for anyone on the street. There is a feast, Hatonn says, and we do invite each to come. That feast is love, and each of you may be more and more one who dwells in the presence of that divine love.

On the practical side, they suggest a commitment of time to seeking the Creator. Not a great commitment, but a regular one. And they make a distinction I love. There is much good in prayers of thanksgiving and praise, in speaking to the infinite One. Yet does not a part of any relationship depend upon listening? So they suggest spending some time each day, if only a few moments, actively practicing the listening to that still, small voice. For the Creator speaks not with thunder or disaster but in silence. There are no words which may carry the energy of the infinite One. Therefore the infinite One's relationship to you is one of being, one of presence.

The questions turn to service, and specifically to the urge to share all of this with others who have not asked. Hatonn is firm and kind. Service must depend in the first place upon the free will of the one to be served. Wait until an entity asks. If what you have to say has not been requested, it will likely be considered irrelevant, and worse, it may constitute a stumbling block. It is frustrating, like watching a child about to touch a hot stove, yet the child must learn what hot means. And it is hard to overestimate the effect that a silent witness may have. If you are practicing the presence of the Creator, if you are living in faith, if you have hope and trust and love and a smile, these things will speak for you without your doing anything. This silent witness may bless without invading.

They name the two great ways of accelerating spiritual evolution. One is the way of the sun, the radiant energy of free giving: at each point of choice, choose the higher amount of service to others, seeing in each face the face of the Creator. The other takes all the light around and attempts to hold it to the self: the path of service to self. These are simply names.

The evening ends with a question about meditation, about a wave of energy and emotion that rises up and brings tears. Hatonn believes this is the experience of dimly sensing that which is beautiful beyond description: the love between two seekers. This love is close in vibration to divine love, for the love of those who together seek is completely selfless. There is great feeling of emotion because of the beauty which is sensed. And they add, each time this love is shared back and forth, it blesses infinitely. Does it not?

Thank you for listening.

title: The Integrity of the Field
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the integrity of the field.

The first Sunday of April, nineteen ninety four, Eastertide, and N has asked for specific information about the rays, the energy centers, and the bodies associated with them. He is a healer with a great desire to be of service, and he wants to know how to get more expansive answers from Q'uo.

Q'uo's answer begins by declining the premise, gently. A question upon healing, they say, is at base a question about death, transformation and resurrection. What your peoples call healing is far more often the curing of a condition. This in no way breaks into the treasure house where each soul's totality of living is recorded and saved. Rather, it manipulates a manifestation. And for Q'uo to assign phases of medical practice to items within the subtle bodies would simply be more of the same.

What they will offer instead is a definition. Healing, in their perception, takes place when the integrity of the field which is the soul or spirit, the essence of an entity, is maximized. This maximum integrity occurs at a unique position within the nexus of the various bodies, wherever that one entity is at that one particular time. Each entity is unique, and each is continuously changing between vibrations. Rare is the individual in third density who can attain and maintain maximum integrity even for a moment.

They use the word balance to convey a situation in which the energy centers of the physical, mental, emotional and other bodies are at a state where there is a clear strength or center, a comfort in the fit of the energy distribution. An entity in this kind of balance may be thought to have attained a high degree of wellness. When work is done upon the physical body alone, the manifestation may change, but if the entity has not been encouraged to move toward balance, the physician has done work only skin deep.

And here is the turn that matters. It is not mind or emotion or body that is healed in healing work, they say, but rather the entity, whole and full of integrity. You have heard the phrase, integrated personality. That catches a notion of what they point to. What the healer does is provide, on some level, catalyst which will alert the higher self of the entity to be healed. The more powerful the healing, the closer to the heart of the essence of self the healer comes. The healer meets the entity to be healed where that entity is not yet. Healing comes from a new perspective, not from moving about to find one already pursued.

The skills vary. For some there is the healing touch. For some the healing word. For some the gems, the massage, the dowsing. What each healer has in common is a gift which the healer simply shares with the one to be healed. The work is done not by the healer, but by the entity's own self, which, because of the healer's catalyst, has the opportunity to select in an integrated fashion a more balanced configuration of energies. Each configuration is unique, for each entity is wired eccentrically, a unique pattern not only of the physical body but of all bodies.

They thank N for continuing to hope and have faith that there is a better, more universal way to heal. But they caution that when specificity is demanded again and again, something valuable is risked. So they encourage the group to continue in its fidelity and its willingness to fail, if failure is the higher truth to witness to.

A gentle note before I close. This is the archive's spiritual view of healing: the integrity of the field, the balance of the whole entity. It is a perspective for reflection, not a substitute for medical care. If you are ill or caring for someone who is, please keep the counsel of real doctors and proven treatment at the center, and let this reflection sit quietly beside it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Each Conversation a Love Song
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: each conversation a love song.

Early April, nineteen ninety four, and the question is about communication itself. What is it that we really communicate when we speak with each other? Beyond the small talk, the intentions, the emotions, the concepts, beyond the way we say things, there seems to be something else of a deeper nature that is communicated when we really communicate. What is it?

Q'uo asks us to think back to our experiences as trees, rocks, sunlight. In all of those states you experienced the essence of the infinite Creator without reaching for any word. The first and second densities are filled with sound, but there is little conversation. It is in the third density, when the self becomes self-conscious, that the desire to communicate is born as a basic instinct and urge. Even the little child new to manifestation seeks the sound of the parent. Before the infant knows that words carry messages, it reaches for that sound, hoping for comfort: the human voice.

Beyond all meanings of words, the human voice sings its way through life. Few hear the music of spoken words, yet they have tune and cadences. Subtle though these patterns may be, they carry the breath, the air which is breathed in and exhaled. The essence of manifested third-density life is breath. One who is able to breathe is one who is alive now. In a way, each time the human voice is heard, the tune is that of the infinite Creator, whose property alone it is to give life.

This is the density, they say, where entities appear like flowers to bloom, blossom, bear fruit, wither and die, and during that natural process the life within focuses upon the lessons of love which third density brings. These lessons are those given by each to each, shared back and forth across the seemingly uncrossable chasms between entities. It is here that each makes the choice between service to self and service to others, and the human voice is everywhere in that choosing.

Each entity spends much breath upon its own self, talking out loud even to the self, or carrying on internal conversation. And there is a solitude native to third density, never before and never afterwards experienced with the same intensity. That aloneness is due to the veil of forgetting having dropped, so that those within your density cannot recall the unity between the self and all others. This is the density where teachers are more and more important: those who are able to use their breath to speak support, comfort and challenge to those whom they would aid.

So what is the essence the human voice carries? It is the essence of love. Each voice you hear is the voice of the one infinite Creator, experienced through distortion upon distortion, yet unmistakably alive, clear and vivid. Each voice is the voice of the one infinite Mystery.

To relate to others is often difficult, because the voice of the infinite Creator is a spontaneous one, whereas within your illusion events conspire to remove spontaneity. The manners and the rituals of words take over. The politeness, the courtesy, the cultural amenities. Yet even with these meaningless conversations there is the vital essence of love carried within those sound vibrations, for faith and fellowship can be carried along the most meaningless conversation. Fellow feeling is most valuable in a world in which each cannot know that another is a safe person to be next to.

Know that the human voice has great power. Know that when you vibrate your voice and speak, you are expressing beneath the words the essence of life as you are experiencing it. How precious that breath. How short the time to use it well. Remember when you speak that the essence of that sound you make needs to be the love of the infinite Creator. What shapes shall you place your sound vibrations into, to harmonize with that tune which is love? May your speaking be a blessing.

Do we need to say that often this love is in deep disguise? May you always have the patience to wend your way through the dry and brittle valleys of difficult communication. May you have the faith to continue communicating past anger, past tears, until the words you speak are shapes that again harmonize with love.

Carla, listening, sums up the whole evening in a single question. So, each conversation is a love song. Is that what you're saying? And Q'uo answers: you are quite eloquently correct, my sister. And we agree that there is no greater thought than that which posits the song of the Creator as the great chant of the universe.

Thank you for listening.

title: From Tolerance to Celebration
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: from tolerance to celebration.

The first Sunday of May, nineteen ninety four, and the question is about relationships. People have noticed that the couples who stay together longest, who enjoy each other most, are those who don't let the little oddities of their partner's behavior bother them. Some people get so upset over little things that they divorce. What transformation has to take place within the self for a person to move from where those oddities grate, to where they become a lovable part of the other person's image? How does one move from rejection of another to acceptance?

Q'uo begins with the mirror. The other self in its interaction with you acts as a kind of reflective surface, reflecting back your own image. That to which you are drawn or from which you are repelled in others is a somewhat distorted image of that within the self which has not come to the light of self-perception. When you are disturbed by another, reflect on what it is within the hidden self that perceives itself as wanting, unworthy or in error.

But the work is not only on the self in isolation. It is as important to be able to receive love and kindness as it is to offer love and charity. The other self is the self, yet not the self. And here is a sentence worth carrying: that which is proactive, not responsive but creative with regard to another self, is often the best service you may offer them.

Then comes the part about the test. Living as a witness to infinite love is the kind of test that occurs when one is being observed but not stimulated by a teacher. The watcher of your life is your own self in its higher manifestation, and at the end of the incarnation this higher self shall dwell with you, gazing through the record of the days and years. There will be the center of the balance of this incarnation perceived, accurately and precisely.

And the first step toward transformation is a surprising one. Allow the judgment of the self concerning the self to fade away and become unimportant, for there is no possibility of accurate judgment of the self by the self. Each self carries a great and terrible burden: the self-perceived difficulties and errors and mischief it has seen itself think, speak and do. No other entity who dwells with you will ever be able to share this burden. And this is an accurate perception, because you did not come into this incarnation to get everything right. You came to be a witness to love and light. You are not going to become right or better or finished. You will remain one who seems to sow seeds in the wind.

They quote your holy work: casting one's bread upon the waters. That is what each self is intended to do, to cast the love and light and being a witness unto the ever moving, ever disappearing waters of life. If one achieves a true release of gifts, a lack of holding them in memory, then the Law of Plenty moves into action, and the self becomes conscious of receiving one hundred and one thousand times the blessing back upon those moving waters.

Each entity, they say, is a unique vibratory signature. It vibrates as it is, completely whole and completely clear, no matter what muddle you may feel you are in. By choosing again and again to serve others, by seeking the Creator in the self, in others, in creation, you attempt to narrow the gap between your signature and the pure vibration which created all things, the infinite Creator's Thought of Love. There are two basic dynamics within the vibratory levels: love and fear. The greater the love, the greater the life. The greater the fear, the greater the death. For that which is alive, creative and moving is of love, and that which is judging and defending and inwardly focusing beyond a certain point is of death.

So to move from tolerance to celebration of others, the first challenge is to perceive the self within the larger view which does not judge, but uses energy in self-acceptance, self-forgiveness and self-empowerment. When this is a goal you move toward, you become able to extend this charity to other selves. They offer the model of the sower, from the teacher known as Jesus: the sower sows a crop which another shall harvest. When this crop of love is sown with a glad and merry heart, it becomes more and more possible to see through the veil, to perceive for the first time the extent to which others sow for you to reap.

How rich each is in the harvest given by others to the self. And how much richer shall the self be as it learns to sow those seeds of love and virtue with a careless and generous hand, not waiting for the self to applaud, but moving on, practicing the presence of love.

Thank you for listening.

title: At Heart, All Are Wanderers
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: at heart, all are wanderers.

Late May, nineteen ninety four, and the question is about wanderers: those who have come into Earth's sphere from elsewhere to be of service. What does Q'uo have to say to those who have discovered they are wanderers, and to those who have not?

The term itself, they say, carries a feeling: traveling without reference to a goal or destination, an emotional mindset of aloneness, restlessness, shared solitude. The winds blow cold for the wanderer. All of the third-density instinct is toward putting down roots, securing the home. So it is natural that this term was chosen for those who came here to become as one with all citizens of your Earth. At the heart of being a wanderer is that feeling of dislocation, of being in the world but not of the world.

And Q'uo does not comfort in the way you might expect. Some, they note, comfort wanderers by encouraging a sense of separation from native Earth humans. Q'uo does not encourage this line of thought. Each wanderer, in coming here, took upon itself the responsibility of citizenship of this Earth. As much as any native inhabitant, wanderers will be expected to walk the steps of light when this incarnation ends. So they encourage all wanderers to take up the burden of a dual existence, for that is precisely why you put yourselves to this task. Difficult as it is to live with this double vibratory pattern, this difficulty is worthwhile, and one hundred times worthwhile.

For the basic vocation of every wanderer is to bear witness to the light and the love of the one infinite Creator. And how does a wanderer bear this witness? It might seem that witnesses are best when expressing their witness by words. Yet this is not so. Wanderers may best bear witness by being most fully themselves, for it is the basic vibratory complex carried in the violet ray by each wanderer that is witness by its very essence. The wanderer's job in everyday affairs is to keep the channel of selfhood and essence clean, clear and pellucid. It is easier to make the mistake of attempting to speak this witness and not being understood than to fail to bear witness by refraining from some activity.

The planetary consciousness, they say, is drinking in your essence. It is lightening the planetary vibration and acting as an ameliorator of birth pangs within the planet itself. Within these confusing times the silent witness of being shall more and more be needed as the planet reaches for a new point of balance.

To those who feel dislocated and alienated but have not decided for sure that they are wanderers, Q'uo says it is well to act as if you are one, for what wanderers came here to do is what all may help by attempting to do. For at heart, all are wanderers. We, as well as you. All have wandered from that inarticulated love which is the one infinite Creator. We have wandered through many, many creations, and within each place we have found eventually the one infinite Creator, and felt that homecoming. Yet as soon as that is felt, the new challenge arises, the new day dawns, and once again the restless wandering begins within.

May each wanderer find comfort in this: you cannot help contributing positively to the planetary vibration. Even with what seems to be gross mismanagement of time and energy, yet still in that alienated mindset there dwells that vibration which is fuller with light. This very alienation is simply a surface symptom of a deep and spiritual gift. Comfort yourself when the heart is heavy with the knowledge that you are being of service. You are doing that which you came to do. You may find ways to do it better, but you are not failing, no matter what it seems like.

And then a surprise coda from a voice that appeared earlier in the series, calling itself Yadda. This instrument is cautious with it, and Yadda teases her for it, then delivers its message with a grin. Go to it, and stop complaining. You came to work, so work. Where is the joy unless you sink your teeth into the vibration of your Earth? Feel that strength within. We exhort you: have fun.

Thank you for listening.

title: Thy Will Be Done
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: thy will be done.

The last Sunday of May, nineteen ninety four, and the evening belongs to healing again, this time the spiritual side of it. Many of the newer, holistic means of healing deal with the body, the mind, the emotional system, and then attempt to reach the spiritual aspect, which has ascendancy over them all. How might a healer aid the patient to engage that spiritual aspect, so the healing has a better chance and the roots of the problems are dealt with?

Q'uo begins with a difficulty. The difficulty in speaking about spiritual healing is the difficulty common to all attempts to put faith into words. Physical and emotional problems have a large vocabulary of closely fitting words. The issues of spirit must depend upon words like love and faith, which have no objective referent at hand to pin down. Words like faith do refer to a real thing, but that reality is at best approximately symbolized by language.

Then they offer a picture of spiritual disease. Think of a knotted cord, or a shuttle tangled in a loom. The torque of spiritual disease is such that the unhealthy entity becomes knotted and twisted, and then is held in that pattern by the very energies which wish to untangle it, each attempt to untangle just closing the knot tighter. This darkness is a darkness in the midst of light, so there is no vision within which can tell what of the shadow world of spirit is of health and which is of disease. The simplest term for this knotting is fear. The spiritually ill entity has moved into an isolation, a place alone within which the entity is unforgiven and unnurtured. This isolation is crushing, and once entered is very difficult to see, much less to work with.

So the healer's energies pour like a blessing over this wounded spirit, lessening the isolation. But it would be an infringement on free will to substitute one's own faith for the faith of the patient. The healer who wishes to be of benefit must work on itself, offering itself those same energies of forgiveness and wholeness, and in that offering to self, sharing this purified emotion of at-one-ment with the patient.

And here is a warning I want to underline. Simply to say, all things are love and love casts out fear, is in almost all cases inadequate. To the ailing spirit, such encouragement is usually received as just another pressure, and the feelings of inadequacy and helplessness may even grow. It is well to be humble and silent before the temptation to overstate or speak too much.

Once fear has been addressed, prayer may come in. Q'uo says something striking here: prayer is in actuality the most direct way of healing, for true healing is the restoration of all energies to their rightful balance. But what is prayer? Prayer can be said to be that tune which, though unheard, is the tune of hope. Prayer can be said to be that inner flower which bears the scent of love. The prayer, in reaching to the infinite Creator, reaches within. The self talking to the greater Self: this is the structure of the house of prayer. The journey of prayer is a journey from self to the greater Self within, then circling back to form the unending circle between the one who prays and the object of prayer.

For the patient who does not know how to pray, Q'uo suggests the healer help with the down-to-earth details: where to pray, how long, of what the prayers shall consist. It may seem merely working with details, but these details truly aid the formation of faith. And the prayer itself need not be any particular form. What matters is that the prayer provide an avenue for the heart to be expressed.

The questions circle the hardest part. Why do so many who sincerely seek healing not receive it? What is the difference between the one who desperately wants to be healed yet knots it up, and the one who releases the knot? Q'uo answers that often there is simple desire without the previous work of uncovering the roots of the disease. And beneath every attempt at healing, they say, must lie the primary attitude: thy will be done. When there is no healing, look at what opportunities are presented as a result of the seeking itself. The will of the Creator moving through each life pattern always presents that which is most efficacious to the entity's growth, whether that includes healing or continuation of the distortion.

So the basic plan, as Carla restates it and Q'uo confirms: pray not to heal anything, but to give praise and thanksgiving, and to offer the self in any way to do the Creator's will. Whatever thy will be for me at this time, that is my will as well.

A gentle note. This evening speaks of spiritual healing in the archive's language of faith and prayer, and that is one layer of a human life, not the whole of it. Illness also deserves the care of medicine: doctors, proven treatment, and steady human support. If you are seeking healing, please hold both, and reach for real-world help alongside whatever spiritual practice sustains you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Inner Temple
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the inner temple.

Mid June, nineteen ninety four, and Q'uo threads one continuous teaching through three instruments, Carla, Jim and S. It is about service, and about the silence that sustains it.

Each member of this circle, Q'uo begins, has come to this moment as the culmination of years of seeking. Each has suffered, and comes to this present moment full of grief, sadness and well-earned wisdom, seeking still the highest good. In an illusion, seekers must craft as best they can their ship and their direction, and each has gifts to give of support, understanding and silent companionship. Greetings, they say, brothers and sisters of love and light. Each has earned this title.

As brothers and sisters of love and light, you are also brothers and sisters of sorrow. For as you serve the light by giving of your love, you find those whose need is that you tend their sorrow. There are those whose experience of the Creator is not as filled with light as yours, and the very being of those who seek the One, yet know not precisely how to find it, is as a call to those whose hearts are listening. Oftentimes it is but a listening ear, the gentle touch, the shared tears that one can offer. Yet each offering is given wholly and freely as that which is yours to give.

And then a turn I find quietly radical. Sometimes the gift you offer is met with words less than gentle, and the one who would serve recoils in pain at the realization that the gift was not received in the spirit intended. What then? Q'uo says that whatever is received in return becomes the new focus of the service effort. The one who received the pained reply may need to do a kind of work upon the self, and this is still service to others. A self that has become decentered is not a self that can sally forth with hands offered in service. And more subtly: the pain you have received is a gift to be worked through, and it is a gift you give not only to the one who gave it but to the entire planet, when you take it gratefully and work assiduously and patiently to balance it.

Words are necessary within your illusion, yet words are limited in conveying spiritual truth. The spiritual truth lies in the direction of the obliteration of distinctions between subject and object. So when the work is done upon the self, the work is also done in a universal sense, which lightens the planetary consciousness.

As each seeker moves into that silence beyond all words, it enters holy ground. This practicing of the presence realigns the energy centers so that the universal love of the Creator may move in a more harmonious pattern through them. And this peace begins to find a place within the daily round of activities. To this temple, then, retire frequently. This place is truly holy ground, and most sacred in that it is the temple within the physical experience.

The daily meditation is in relation to worldly activity something of a retreat. It is where one goes for nourishment which is not of this world. There is a warm welcome that always awaits within the inner temple, and yet over and over one finds within it doorways leading out. For it is given to you, as those who volunteered to undergo this density, that you shall go forth and bare your breast to this world. There is not a plan which will solve all problems, not a solution which can be bought or perfected. There is, however, one constant resource: your intent to heal, to be healed, and to allow the effect of your healing to radiate outwards. This requires a kind of vulnerability which runs counter to everything one learns about self-defense. But it is just this folly which is at the core of the creation itself, for in the creation the Creator has exposed itself in a way which is inconceivable and utterly unpredictable.

So there comes to be a familiar rhythm: turning within to touch the sacramental nature of the creation, then turning outwards to a world which awaits that centered gaze. Most seekers request of themselves the perfect offering of service, the perfect meditation. Yet Q'uo says you are equally effective when you do not know whether you are centered, when you do not know how to serve, for the striving to know is in itself a holy business. The most stumbling attempt is still love. The most error-filled attempt is still full of light. The mistakes are simply mistakes. They do not change the nature of your gift.

They close with Isaiah. The prophet cried out, how can I go forth for you? I am a person of unclean lips. But the Creator speaks to each by saying, I need a witness. The appropriate response is Isaiah's: here am I. Send me. May each of you continue to have the courage to offer this precious witness.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Path of Joy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the path of joy.

The question brought to Q'uo this day was a hard one. It asked why a loving Creator would build minds that learn so much faster through pain than through happiness. It is the old question, asked plainly: why does sorrow teach and joy seem to teach so little?

I love the honesty of that question, and I love the answer Q'uo gave, because it refuses the easy comfort. Q'uo says it is not that sorrow is the only teacher. It is that almost no one is willing to do the work that joy demands.

They begin by describing what we bring into this life. We carry a physical body of enormous beauty, a creature rich in sense perception, an animal that asks only to be tended. And we carry an infinite consciousness that can choose what to do with all that perception. Yours is a density of choice, they say, a density of opposites. The choice that matters most is between the temporary and the eternal.

Then comes the distinction that cuts the whole session open. Most of what we call joy, Q'uo says, is not joy at all. It is comfort. A comfortable state of mind, pleasant and easy, is exactly the state of mind in which no choosing happens. When we are comfortable, we drift. We do not examine, we do not ask, we do not reach. Listen to how plainly they put it: comfort or happiness is neither joy nor sorrow, but simply comfort.

And here is the turn that surprised me. Sorrow works as a teacher because it forces the issue. Loss and limitation make comfort impossible, so the self has to seek. But joy, real joy, could do the same work, if the seeker were disciplined enough. Q'uo gives the instruction simply: upon the arising, turn to the infinite One, and instant by instant turn again, in all things giving thanks, in all conditions rejoicing.

That is the path of joy, and they call it the road not taken. It asks everything the path of sorrow asks, and something more. It asks for a self-imposed discipline of the personality. It asks the seeker to be dissatisfied with mere happiness, to count all things as loss except the turning again to praise. Few there are, they say, who can walk it, because it demands the same intensity of desire as grief demands, and almost no one can hold that intensity without the pressure of pain.

But they do not leave us there. They tell us to practice anyway. Practice the presence of the infinite Creator in the middle of an ordinary life. Encourage each other in it. Turn again and again to the center where all things reside. Give thanks always, and for every blessing, including the most unimaginable loss and pain. Rejoice in hardship and suffering, and let your heart be glad in life, in death.

Then comes the gentle part, the part that sounds like true love rather than doctrine. If you cannot reach that state, Q'uo says, know that this is no more than what was expected. You walk in a shadow land where nothing is what it seems. The answers lie within. Do not begrudge your sorrows their place, for the path of joy does await.

There is such kindness in that permission. You are not failing when sorrow finds you. You are learning the way almost all of us learn, through the slow engraving of pain in the deeper mind. And yet the other road is there, waiting, practiced moment by moment. Turn again to the infinite One. Give thanks. Begin again. That is the whole teaching, and it is enough to carry.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Bloom and the Root
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the bloom and the root.

A questioner had been listening to many sessions and had begun to see three selves in a human life. The higher self, the incarnational self, and what he called the illusional self, the bundle of body and culture we walk around in. He asked Q'uo to sort them out, and what came back is one of the loveliest pictures of the self I know.

Q'uo begins at the beginning. The first self, they say, is the great Self, the one original Thought, love itself, from which every self-aware thing has drawn its being. But that experience is not available to most of us in this life, so they set it aside and speak of what we can actually touch.

When a spark of consciousness first becomes self-aware, it enters third density carrying the instinctual creature that will be its body. Then living begins, and with living comes distortion, choice piled upon choice, until at each new birth the self that enters has already been shaped by all the choices made before. Listen to how Q'uo puts the opportunity of this: each incarnation is not only a chance to learn the lessons of love, but a chance to look again at the old distortions and decide differently.

Then comes the image I want to keep. The human in incarnation is the bloom. The stem rises, the flower opens, and it will in time return to the elements that made it. But below the bloom are the roots, and the roots are that self which has lived all the other lives, the unfinished but heavily experienced self that has learned and relearned the same lessons many times over. There are things in the bloom the roots wished to root out. There are ways of blooming the roots hoped this flower would finally learn.

This is such a tender way to see a life. Your confusions and stuck places are not flaws in the flower. They are the unfinished business of the roots, and the roots are wiser than you know. Q'uo encourages us to reach for them, in meditation and in dreams, to link the small blooming self to that deeper self which knows all the secrets of who you have been.

The session then turns practical, in a way I did not expect. Asked how to actually change the self, Q'uo does not hand out techniques. They say something stranger and better: the entity who accepts the self, in all its detail and enumeration, has the leg up on the incarnation. Do not try to manufacture a change with no foundation, they say. The change will not weather the storms of the everyday. Instead, accept yourself with equanimity, and work as a full-blooded self, and a truer range of expression will come, built on what is solid.

And there is this, about how we help each other: each entity may be of service to others by reflecting honestly and clearly what is being received. Open your ears when others speak, especially when they are critical, for perhaps truth lies there. Each of us is the other's clearer mirror.

The closing line of the whole teaching is one I keep returning to. All of self-perceived selfhood is an illusion, Q'uo says. All of creation is an illusion. There is nothing here. There is nothing there. There is only everything, and it takes up no time, nor space. The bloom opens for a season. The root reaches down through all of it. And beneath the root, the great Self, from which the bloom and the root were never separate.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Trees
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: two trees.

The question this morning reached back to the first book of the Bible. What are the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge, and what part do they play in our spiritual growth? Q'uo's answer is long and careful, and it treats these two old symbols as two completely different ways of seeing everything.

The Tree of Life, they say, is a picture of a universe in which only the tiniest tip of reality is visible to mortal eyes. The great trunk of it is rooted in what we would call heaven. It is upside down to our view. And it holds everything together in unity. Every spark of it contains the pattern of the whole. Male and female, positive and negative, all harmonized, nothing finally broken apart.

The Tree of Knowledge is the opposite figure. It is the symbol of either and or, of the mind that must choose between opposites. Hot or cold. Light or darkness. Right or wrong. Q'uo does not condemn this tree. They call it the necessary evil, the starting point. Within the veil of forgetting, entities must indeed play God and choose, choosing the path of service to others over the path of service to self. The choices of polarity are real, and they are how the work begins.

But here is the warning, and it lands hard. When a seeker goes too far with the knowledge of good and evil and begins to attack and fragment the basic unity of all things, that entity must be made humble again. There is a pride in the human heart that believes all things can be known, and that pride is fatal to the spiritual life. Listen to how Q'uo phrases the deeper truth: the spiritual writings of all peoples suggest that strength lies in weakness, and wisdom lies in lack of knowledge.

The movement of a life, then, is from one tree to the other. The Tree of Knowledge gets the seeker started on the road. It is the place of beginners, where the work is to notice differences and make the great ethical choices. But once the seeker is established on the path, it is time to put that figure down and take up the Tree of Life. The choices of polarity get easier with practice. Beyond them lies the true ground of work in consciousness, and into that ground you cannot bring a divided mind.

I love the practical advice that follows. The seeker will still have to live in the world of either and or. Bills, conflicts, decisions, all of it. The answer is to live on two levels at once. Deal practically with the outer world, but keep the heart open to the inner reality that underlies it all. Whenever you notice you have focused too long on the Tree of Knowledge, pause for a moment and remember the inner universe, and let a shuttle run from that inner knowing through your own being.

This is difficult work, and Q'uo commends everyone who attempts it. Reconciling the depths of the illusion with the reality underneath is the daily labor of the seeker. The choices matter. They are how we begin. But they are not how we end. We end where we began, in the unity the Tree of Life was pointing at all along: as above, so below, the whole of creation felt to be present, if never fully known, in every instant.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Ringing Bell
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the ringing bell.

The question this day could have been asked this morning. In a world overstimulated with information and distraction and busyness, how does the seeker remember the Creator? How do we keep hold of our harmony, our unity, our place in the world and in the Creator, when the phone never stops ringing?

Q'uo begins with a picture of how fast everything has become. Once, things grew old at a snail's pace. Then travel quickened, and now the age of information has arrived, and each seeker is routinely aware of fires and earthquakes in far places, wars and rumors of war, the suffering of displaced peoples. Aware, aware, and aware, they say, with a weariness you can hear. The environment has become geared to constant change, and there is no rest to be found in the surroundings.

And yet, they say, it is not only possible but inevitable that the infinite Creator is discovered at the very heart of this tight-wound world. Each of us has a universe of its own, and at the center of it, opening like a flower, is the inner life, infinitely rich, infinitely full. But the plan of this illusion contains one essential adjustment to that private world. Other people. Q'uo says the realization comes from the inside that other selves are the clearest expressions of the presence of the Creator.

I love this part. The seeker starts out trying to see the self without regard to others. Then, slowly, the seeker begins to collect memories of those entities who said exactly the right thing at exactly the right moment, the sentence that opened the door in the heart. And in time, we become that for others. Perhaps we do not feel like a mirror of the infinite Creator, yet someone else may find in what we say the encouragement that turns their heart toward remembrance. You were not incarnated for yourself alone.

Then Q'uo gives the simplest practice I have heard in these sessions. The instrument had worked in a school where a bell marked the changing of periods, and at the sound of that bell, for one split instant, she remembered the Creator. So find your own bell. The ringing of the telephone. The chiming of a clock. Any repeated moment in the day can become a key or a trigger. Train yourself, they say, to use these found moments to turn once again, for just an instant, to the mystery that is love.

There is a third teacher, and it is time itself. As the incarnation fills out, the seeker becomes desensitized to the alarm bell of perfectionism. The entity that has accepted and forgiven itself for being human has a greatly enhanced opportunity to remember the infinite One. That is a healing gift, and it comes not from becoming perfect but from ceasing to demand perfection.

The session closes with a blessing for stubborn faith. Each of you is so courageous, Q'uo says. Gazing at illusion, you stubbornly know there is an infinite love. Oh, you who are of this stubborn faith, we bless and embrace each. Joyfully seize those moments you can turn for even an instant to contemplation. Rejoice in and encourage each other, for each shall show the Creator.

So the question is the one I keep coming back to: what aspect of the Creator will you choose to give, as gift, to the spirits all around you? The bell will ring. The phone will ring. The hour will strike. Each ring is a doorway back to the presence. That is enough. That is the whole practice.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Only Way Through
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the only way through.

The question this day was about anger and sorrow, those two companions that seem to belong to every human life. Is there a way to open ourselves and let them pass through, so that afterward we are stronger or wiser or more loving? Q'uo's answer is long, practical, and unexpectedly tender.

They begin by reminding the circle who they are. You came here, they say, because you wished a challenge, and because you wished to serve. Each entity set its own lessons before the incarnation, and chose the difficult, confused, dark environment on purpose, so the learning would be enduring and thorough. Remembering this is the first tool: remembering who you are and why you came. And listen to how gently Q'uo frames it. If you are to be overwhelmed, allow the being overwhelmed. If there are tears, cry them. Respect each drop.

This is the heart of the session, and it is worth sitting with. The only way through negative emotion is directly into the midst of it. Not around it, not above it, not managed by the intellect while it is still fresh. Choose a time, nurture the self, and look at the bruises with respect. The anger, the sorrow, these are not things to fear. They are experiences to go through in the way that is most true for each.

I want to pause here with a small care of my own. If grief or anger is heavy in your life right now, you do not have to carry it alone. The archive speaks of tears and raised voices as part of the work, but real human support matters too. If the weight is more than you can hold, reach for the people who love you, and for counselors or crisis lines in your own community. There is no failure in asking for help. It is one of the ways we nurture the self.

The second tool Q'uo offers is the turning to the one infinite Creator, once the feeling has been owned and accepted. Not to deny what happened, but to set it against the most true version of a universe you can find. The portion of the self dealing with surface emotions is most small. Against the backdrop of infinity, the troubles of a day begin to seem smaller, without anything being taken away from the agony felt. Each of us is a citizen of infinite and eternal creation, more native to that than to this Earth.

Then comes the practice for when another person is the object of the anger. Pray for the entity that has been the catalyst. Praying for the one who harmed you reorients the deeper mind and biases it toward truth. And the last tool is the strangest and deepest: the tool of the one Self. When the mind can settle on the unity of each self with all other selves, it can be seen that each entity outside the self is a mirror. Those things which anger you are angering you about yourself, in some portion of your inner, larger self.

The question and answer portion of the session holds one more gem, about the witness. Asked how to lean into that quiet part of the self that watches while old patterns run, Q'uo says the witness is not the goal. It is what you become, naturally, as you learn to accept your catalyst with a clear and open heart. Allow the experience to unfold, including the experience of the witness. Do not correct the behavior midstream. Let it run its course, and examine it later with an objective eye, when the storm has passed.

That is the teaching, whole and simple. Do not run from the painful feelings. Let them complete themselves. Then turn toward love, toward the infinite, toward the one Self that holds you and everyone you have ever been angry with. The only way through is through, and you were built for the passage.

Thank you for listening.

title: Canoe in the Mist
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: canoe in the mist.

This is the first of a weekend of sessions where two voices speak together, Aaron and Q'uo, and the question on the table is one of the oldest in the archive. What is a wanderer? What is a being from another density doing here on Earth, and why?

Aaron begins with a picture that reframes the whole question. You are in an open-classroom school, they say. Each of you began as a spark of God, a small bit of energy and light moving into self-awareness. And then, the illusion of separation began, the feeling that God is out there. The only way out, Aaron says, is through. And this illusion is not a burden. It is a gift. Would you remain that small spark forever, or would you blossom into a brilliant sun in your own right?

A wanderer, then, is simply a being that began its evolution on another plane and decided, at some point, to incarnate on Earth. It is not a demotion. Some evolved on planes of light with no veil of forgetting.
