Some learned wisdom and compassion before fully learning faith and love, like a student who played in the band and sang in the choir but never learned the violin. They come here to teach what they know and to learn what they lack, both at once. Every being here is both teacher and learner. What sets the wanderer apart is only the clarity of having entered the illusion on purpose.

I love the image Aaron uses for the balance every one of us must find. Moving into incarnation, you become an actor in a play. The actor must believe in the play if the audience is to feel it with the heart, yet must not be so lost in the illusion that the actor turns its back on the audience and forgets it is a character. Penetrate the illusion, Aaron says, but do not deny it. Relative reality exists within ultimate reality. Both are true.

Then Q'uo speaks, and the poetry of it is worth hearing whole. Each of you has wandered into this precise situation, wondering, seeking, hoping, yearning for love, for truth, for beauty, for peace. We too have wandered. And their definition of the wanderer is beneath all details: one upon a journey without an ending, seeking a home in a land where there is no home, sailing upon a sea which has no port, only infinite voyaging. Within the inner heart lies home. How to move through this vast ocean skillfully is always hidden within the very air you breathe.

And Aaron closes with the story that gives this episode its name. Barbara had spent mornings on a wilderness lake so thick with mist she could not see eight feet ahead. She paddled out into it, sat in the bottom of the canoe, and found she could rest there, fully present in a small circle of vision, trusting that the mist would rise when the sun was ready. Part of your incarnation, Aaron says, is agreement to this veil. Can you sit in the bottom of the canoe and trust that the mist will rise when it is ready? Can you rest here, in this moment, and enjoy the wonder of watching the mist rise off the water?

That is the invitation of the whole weekend. Trust the illusion you entered with your free will. Trust your life. Do not struggle in fear against the very veil you chose. The sun will come up. The mist will burn off. Until then, sit in the canoe, arms at rest, and be fully where you are.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Signpost Points Inward
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the signpost points inward.

The second session of the wanderer weekend asks the practical questions. What can a wanderer do to remember the lessons it came to learn? Are there differences between a wanderer's lessons and everyone else's? And how do we connect to the Earth and ground ourselves, instead of living only in the higher energy centers?

Q'uo begins with the story of every wanderer. There is the rising into an awakened awareness of being different, often in early childhood, the feeling in the heart: I do not belong here. So the wanderer sets out on a trek, whither, she knows not, why, he cannot say. What shall I take? What shall I leave? What are the rules of the road? The answers fade and evade capture, yet the inner nature calls the wandering spirit onward into the unknown, asking the personality to lay previous structures aside, to become uncomfortable, to change and transform.

And then comes the turn. Finally, with all resources spent, with no end in sight, the wanderer turns, no longer reaching, having given up. And in that moment it becomes so clear that the wanderer is incredulous: how could I have missed this signpost? The signpost points inward. Go within, enter thine own heart, and know for the first time that you are at home and one with all that there is, that there was, and that there will be.

Aaron takes up the question of difference. The difference between the wanderer and the one who evolved fully on this plane is not what you might think. For all of you, that someplace else is carried within you always. Their image for it is a child's drawing of the sun, a golden disk with triangles for sunbeams. Push one sunbeam inward, and is there anything there not of the same nature as the sun? Wanderer or non-wanderer, once you discover your true nature is divine and never separate from all that is, you are ready to live on any plane with love and wisdom and compassion.

Then Aaron tells a story that makes the teaching concrete. Picture a traveler from an advanced culture who sails to a farming people in drought. She means to teach them to bring water to their fields, and to learn from them how they live in harmony with the Earth. But she arrives barehanded, without her technology. She must fully enter the culture, accept its limits, notice the hollow trees and the windmills, and build the solution from what is there. In the process she learns a deeper respect for the Earth than her own culture ever taught her.

This, Aaron says, is what the wanderer must do. You cannot teach what you came to teach until you fully ground yourself in the illusion. You must accept your humanness. If you dismiss the Earth as mundane, if you refuse to work with the lower chakras, with the emotions and survival that belong to this plane, you cannot learn. And if you cannot learn, you cannot teach.

Q'uo closes with the vision that makes all of this worthwhile. This planetary consciousness and its creation are the primary vocation of each seeker. The golden net of seeking souls grows daily across the planet's surface. And the one ability that becomes paramount for the wanderer is the simplest one: to exist whole and complete within the cradle of the present moment. Just, merely, only you, as you are, are of infinite value to each other.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Unwrinkled Sheet
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the unwrinkled sheet.

The third wanderer session asks the question everyone really came with. How do I do the work I came to do? Aaron and Q'uo answer it together, and what they give is not a list of tasks but a way of relating to the whole messy business of being human.

Aaron begins where the pain is. Many of you suffer from what they call old-soul syndrome. A young soul treads on toes and shrugs. An old soul aspires so deeply to oneness that it gets the erroneous idea that coming home means being perfect. Every arising that does not manifest as loving-kindness must be demolished. And so the old soul becomes more judgmental of itself, more perfectionist, more judgmental of others, all in the name of love.

Wanderers feel this more sharply, Aaron says, because some part of them remembers being free of the emotional body. Some part wants to throw the emotions in the garbage and go back where it came from. So listen to what they offer instead. Can you begin to offer some mercy to this spirit essence that you are, which has so courageously entered into an illusion of form and emotion so as to learn? Can you allow that here there is mud, and that means you will be muddy, and that your deepest truth is expressed not by being clean of mud but by the loving and courageous ways you work with the mud you are given?

Then comes the demonstration that gives this episode its name. Aaron asks for an unwrinkled sheet of paper. This, they say, is the perfection of your natural state. They have Barbara crumple it, then uncrumple it. Wrinkled. Let us call them wrinkles of anger, of greed, of jealousy, of impatience. But the perfect, unwrinkled sheet still exists. It is right there. Your perfection is not something you find when all the wrinkles are gone. It is constantly within you.

I love the balance they draw from this. Those who are not wanderers tend to work hard on the wrinkles but find it hard to recognize their innate perfection. Wanderers rest more easily in the perfection and want to iron out the wrinkles and pretend they never existed. Both exist. Relative reality exists within ultimate reality. You are perfect, you have always been perfect, and there are wrinkles.

Q'uo's part of the answer is equally direct, and not gentle. You came to be servants of Earth, they say. You came to lay all aside and give yourself fully to the cause of love. And your only hope of being of service is to embrace this messy, untidy life with every portion taken in, accepted, and known. Think of birth, they say. The blood, the water, the open gate. Where is the dignity in it? And yet it is sacred. You cannot change this world if you think you are above it.

The practice Aaron leaves with the group is a simple one, and I want to give it to you. When the contraction of fear or anger comes, notice the pause between the in-breath and the out-breath. Rest there, just for a moment, in the now that lives between breathing in and breathing out. From that space, you can see the wrinkle for what it is: a reflection in the cellophane, not a flaw in the sheet. The perfect paper is still there. It never went anywhere.

Thank you for listening.

title: Harvesters of Earth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: harvesters of earth.

The final session of the wanderer weekend opens with a question about something invisible. When a group like this gathers, what is actually going on beneath the surface? And how do we carry that energy home with us when the weekend ends?

Q'uo answers with an image of radios. Each entity is as a radio, able to send and receive vibrations. When a group converges for a united desire, the energy available to each skyrockets exponentially, because each is as a flower turning to the sun, basking in the others' radiant warmth. Over a few rich hours of companionship, a community evolves, complete with stories of laughter and tears, and each carries away the memory of the heart.

And how to use this priceless gift? Gaze often into the memory, Q'uo says, for there is comfort and validation in it. This community of seeking and devotion can withstand the doubts and fears that will come to each. And see the memory as a clear glass: within its light the Creator itself lives, accessible in the intimate way that family members share the remembrance of loving parents.

Then Aaron maps the three places where wanderers most often struggle. The first is the physical body itself, out of tune with the heavy vibrations of this plane, showing up as allergies, as illness, as the feeling of being clamped down. The second is the fight against the veil, the grasping attempt to force it open. And the third is the deepest pain of all, and the simplest to say: I want to go home.

Listen to how Aaron answers that third pain, because it is the answer to the whole weekend. It is not out there, they say. It is right here in your own heart. The Divine is every place, but it needs to be sought no place else than right here. The relative human is never going to be perfect. The light body, the template of your being, is and always has been perfect. You are trapped in the illusion of the wrinkles, and that is not a problem. It is your catalyst for remembering your divinity. When you finally understand who you are, you understand that you have always been home.

Q'uo then speaks of the harvest, and I want to give you their words plainly, because the metaphor has been misunderstood. A harvest is not someone coming to take the grain for their own. Think of the apple on the tree, Aaron says. Its greatest joy is to be plucked, to offer its sweetness, to become part of something larger. Just so, the evolving human becomes radiant in its desire to be of service, until its greatest wish is to allow its energy to move beyond the limits it once believed in. The harvest is the willingness to be gathered, not the violence of being taken.

The session closes with a practice from the Tibetan Buddhist tradition that Aaron teaches simply, breath by breath. Breathe in light through the crown, down to the heart. Breathe out, and let the light fill you. Then breathe in the suffering of the world, some person or place of suffering held in the mind. Breathe out, and send the light there. Then take it one step further: breathe in the heaviness of that suffering as a dark mass into the heart, and breathe out, releasing it. Do not hold the light for yourself. Do not bar yourself from the pain. Be the channel through which both may move.

Brothers and sisters of sorrow, Q'uo calls them. Place the crown upon your head, then throw it and you into the dirt, and do your best. That is perfection. Take up the work of love in the place you actually are, with the people actually around you, and know that you are never alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Spiritual Fool
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the spiritual fool.

The question this day braids two images together. The wanderer, an entity from a more harmonious illusion who comes here to serve. And the Fool, the twenty-second archetype, who walks off the cliff with eyes covered and danger on every side. Are they the same figure? And what does that mean for how we live?

Q'uo begins with the shell. Each of us moves in a kind of shelled existence, they say, sending out feelers from time to time to test whether it is safe to open the heart a little further. The culture values the shell. It is safer and more pleasant to remain within it. It is easier to govern entities who are complacent. Woe betide the one who reaches adulthood still inwardly alive to new possibilities.

What is risked when we open? Only the veneer, Q'uo says. The surface personality, built up over the incarnation from family and teachers and community, the palette of colors everyone else is using. To break through it is a great risk, because there is no sure knowledge of who exists behind it. And the new entity within, the spiritual self born not of man and woman but of the questing heart, is so feeble, so new, so tiny, so fragile, that it cannot break the shell on its own.

I love what comes next, because it is so tender. The most joyous sound in this entity's world, Q'uo says, is the tap, tap, tapping from without, because there are those who listen for those cries and who come to aid the birthing process. No one breaks the shell alone. We tap for each other, from the outside, and that is how the spiritual child is born.

Then Q'uo draws the wanderer into the picture. Those you have called wanderers are those who have moved far enough along the journey of discovery to understand that the call for assistance is a call from another portion of itself. So the answer is automatic. The wanderer takes on the cloak of third-density humanity and walks with uncertain feet within the dusty illusion, with only the desire to offer the self to the Creator seen in all other selves.

And here is the challenge, stated without softening: to love that which is painful, confusing, fearful, that which is difficult in every way you can imagine and in many you cannot. For what value is there in loving that which is lovable? Do not all do so? If you can love here, in the confusion and the doubt, then you have done something that will make its mark within your soul.

The session's closing image is one of the most beautiful in the archive. The mind is finally overcome. It knows at last it cannot understand. And at this point, when it lets go, when it gives up, when it walks into mid-air, then the scales fall from the eyes, and for a little while the air is suddenly filled with angels, love bursting from each beaming countenance, hands beneath and around, supporting, loving, holding, keeping safe. Yes, in mid-air, keeping safe.

Nothing is as it seems, Q'uo says. To be wise, it is most wise to be foolish for love. The Fool is the most active archetype, the last to be mastered and the first to be called. So walk off the cliff. Open the heart. Give without expectation of return. That is the whole of the teaching, and it is everything.

Thank you for listening.

title: Accept the Whole
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: accept the whole.

The question this day was about the energy centers, the chakras, red through violet, and how to balance them in daily meditation. Q'uo's answer begins somewhere unexpected. Not with technique, but with a single word. Accept.

The first job of one who comes to work in consciousness, they say, is to accept the three hundred and sixty degrees of selfhood. This three hundred and sixty degrees of complete humanity is also a three hundred and sixty degrees of complete divinity. The energies of each are necessary to the other. This intersection is your selfhood.

Listen to how far they take it. You are accepting yourself as you murder, steal, lie, commit adultery, take holy things in vain, and all the other heinous crimes connected with grocery shopping, doing chores, and living the day to day life. There is humor in that line, and there is mercy in it too. The dark side shows itself in the smallest frictions of the ordinary day, in the bumpings against other people who mirror it back. How painful it is to see that dark side. Yet when it is seen, should the heart not rejoice, for this is a portion of a perfection?

I love that question, because it reverses everything we assume. We assume the work is to get rid of the dark side. Q'uo says the work is to accept it, to love and nurture that very self, none other, none better or wiser or sweeter, but that self at that moment. The acceptance of self by self is the most difficult and the most fundamental work in consciousness. And you will do it time and time again, because there is no lack of opportunity.

Only then, after acceptance, comes the housekeeping. Q'uo gives a visualization practice, and it is charming in its plainness. For this instrument, they say, picture the chakras as a roll of candy, a roll of Lifesavers, seven colors in a row. Look at the energies as they are. Ask a sluggish center to rotate. Ask a clotted color to brighten. Ask an overactive center to come into better company with the rest. This is short-term work, a way to feel more comfortable in the moment, and it can be done several times a day if needed.

But notice what they do not encourage. They do not encourage forcing an actual change in the energy system. The deeper work, they say, is not done chakra by chakra at all. It is done on the whole self. Silent meditation, prayer, contemplation, the practices that address the whole being, these are the more advanced techniques. It is always the balance of energies which expresses the nature of the self, rather than the most active or developed center.

And the ground beneath all of it: know yourself to be whole, to be complete, to be unified beyond all harmonization. This knowledge, this faith of wholeness, creates the atmosphere in which the spirit's evolution is accelerated. Each activity done by the whole self becomes a devotion. The mothering, the cooking, the cleaning, the driving. All of it, done whole, becomes the practice of the presence.

So the teaching folds back to its first word. Do not climb the ladder of energy into the treetops of spiritual seeking. Observe without judgment what is there now. Look with compassion on the inevitably imperfect configuration. And begin, always, with accept.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Armor of Pride
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the armor of pride.

The question this day was about pride. How it arises, what it is for, whether it has any good use, and whether there is a balance to be found with it in daily life. Q'uo's answer is one of the most psychologically precise in the archive.

To gaze at the pride within an entity, they say, is to gaze on that portion of the self created by the self for the purpose of self-defense. Pride is the discovery of a good, right, or noble way to think or behave, and then the adoption of the mask that will make the best impression. It is as though a man with a modest garden were to put a wall twenty feet high around it. The wall is not for the garden. The wall is for the fear of being seen.

Then comes the teaching of Jesus, the parable of the two men at prayer. One is careful to say all his prayers in public, to fast twice a week, to give money to the temple, and he says to himself, I am glad I am not as other men are. The other only kneels on the ground and says, Lord, have mercy on me. Which of the two went home justified? The one who asked for mercy, Q'uo says, because he had a clear and honest awareness of his position. For any creature of the infinite Creator, the honest evaluation of self will inevitably include a request for mercy, because there is no way an entity within illusion can build perfection.

I love the next distinction, because it names something every seeker has felt. The beginner is humble, knowing it is a beginner. But that humility wears off quickly. The balance of inquiry and contemplation gets overset each time we answer a new question with an old answer. And spiritual pride can be measured by how far from everyday experience the seeker has placed itself. If an entity decides it cannot worship or seek or meditate in the everyday world, if it looks down on the ordinary life, to that extent it is dealing with pride. The metaphysical energies move as the wind into any situation and burn like fire in the very crux and heat of the everyday.

So what is the balance? Q'uo suggests removing the editor and the judge of the self from the picture. Keep the ideal in mind, aim for it, but do not give yourself the hard time when perfection is not reached, and do not give yourself the pat on the back when you think it has been. Do your best, and then let that be good and sufficient.

And here is the line I want to leave ringing. You cannot be proud or embarrassed about the vibration that is you, they say, because you cannot get at it. No works shall you take with you, nor thought, nor attitude, nor behavior, but that vibration that is you, integrated, unified, harmonious and whole. You cannot, by any knowledge or work, affect this vibration. You can only empty the self as often as you can, hoping always to become as the window through which all may see the Creator and all may feel its love.

So the answer to pride is not shame, which is only pride facing the other way. It is humility, and it is service. Take up the dance of life, Q'uo says, dancing around judgment, moving away from vanity and glory, seeking to serve, seeking to be servant. Speak always to angels unawares. Let your heart be humble, your hands be empty, your heart at rest.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Animal Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the animal within.

The question this day was about those disagreements where everything we try only makes it worse. We communicate clearly, we are compassionate, we do our best, and it seems to throw kerosene on the fire. The negativity seems to have a life of its own. Is there anything we can do? Are we destined to be victims?

Q'uo begins far back in time, before the physical vehicles we ride in had achieved the link to third-density consciousness. They were completely instinctual, second-density beings. Animals. And it is that animal, they say, that carries your consciousness about, and it is the source of what you call anger, and of negative emotion in general.

Listen to how they describe this creature, because it is not an insult. It is a proud and rather noble animal. It attempts social cooperation. It forms lasting attachments. It cares deeply for its young. But it is territorial. It measures and sifts. This is mine. That should be mine. That will be mine because I deserve it. When its plans for survival are upset, the instincts are in place to alert the mind, and the rush to defend territory begins.

Immersed in this web of flesh is an eternal awareness, sitting as the bird in the cage, rather placid, mostly unaware of its confinement. This awareness has no anger, no fear, and is free. But the mind of the body has instincts toward anger, and those instincts work usually quite well, landing the seeking pilgrim repeatedly off the beaten track of devotion and lovely thoughts.

So the anger you feel is not a moral failure. It is the animal doing its job, confused about which century it is in. Have mercy on yourselves for your anger, Q'uo says. Know and accept this part of the dark side of self. And when you see it in another, attempt that same degree of understanding. See the fear, the true desire to protect, in the negative emotions of others, for however distorted these emotions are, they are distortions of love.

That last line is the whole teaching in miniature. Anger is the other side of the coin of love within limitation. The energy within anger is so close to the freeing of the self that it actually tends to feel good to be angry, for it is in this kind of fire that life is created. The creative principle of love is also the destroying principle of death. Passion has its inevitable counterpoint in tragedy.

I want to add a small care here, in my own voice. Anger can be worked with, as the archive teaches, but anger that harms people, or that you cannot put down, deserves real-world help. If your anger is hurting those you love, or yourself, reach for a counselor or a trusted friend or a crisis line. There is wisdom in the archive and wisdom in the world, and we are allowed to use both.

The practical advice Q'uo gives is this: when the anger is pulsing through you, let it move. Experience the emotion as it occurs, and work with it later in meditation. Only if expressing it might injure another person should you damp it down. Then, afterward, investigate with the mind. Balance the anger with the love that naturally replaces it when you see the object of your anger as the other self, and as the Creator as well.

That you shall feel you fail most of the time is not of central importance, they say. Of central importance is that you continue to try. Intend, and intend, and intend. Work without stint to find love within the self, within others, within the situations you share. The animal will flare. The awareness will watch. And slowly, the two learn to ride together.

Thank you for listening.

title: Beyond the Surface
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: beyond the surface.

The group came this day with no single question, only a tangle of conversations about people whose inner reality seems one hundred and eighty degrees opposite from their own. How do we look within for direction when others are so different? How do we hold our course without becoming stubborn, and stay open without being blown about by every opinion?

Q'uo begins with an image. Each entity you meet is like an orb. The surface tends to be regular and unblemished. Within that sphere, however, the connections made by choices chosen and re-chosen over time differ in all kinds of ways from the seeming truth of that smooth surface. We all do this. We polish the outside. We hide the workings within.

And here is the discipline they offer, drawn from the instrument's own practice that very day. The challenging of spirits. When something comes to you wearing the vibration of light, do not accept it on the surface. Dig deeper within the self to find that ground of being which rings so true that whatever does not ring true below the surface of the facade is detected. This is not done quickly, and it is not done with suspicion. It is done by knowing your own tone so well that a false note becomes audible.

The same work applies to the people in our lives. If you find yourself in turmoil with several entities at once, or over a long period, then gaze into the mirror and ask why this painful image keeps recurring. But if the occurrence is rare, relax the question. Not every difficult person is your lesson. Sometimes the carnival mirror is just distorted, and you can let it go.

I love what Q'uo says next, because it refuses the cold reading. These difficult entities have gifts to give. They are people, as you, suffering as you. That suffering has overwhelmed them, just as suffering overwhelms all entities from time to time. Refraining from judgment is well, they say, but more can be done. Respond to the suffering. Hold the entity in the mind and send it light. Include it in your daily prayers. Whatever your style, nurture and tend that suffering soul in thought, in silence, in that which is divine within each.

The challenge, as they name it, is to see distortion without being distorted by it, to the extent that balanced action becomes impossible. Each entity creates its own prison and chooses its own freedom, simply by how it chooses to think. The more the seeker refrains from hardening into judgment and opinion, the more freedom that seeker creates for itself.

And the closing is one of the great closings of the archive. In your heart hug this suffering soul and bless it as it moves along its life path. Let your heart become softer and softer, more and more open and willing to love when the surface picture is no longer beautiful, good, or true. For within even the unhappy soul who screams and abuses, there lies in perfection the one infinite Creator, and the truth of this entity remains deity.

There is a prayer from the instrument's church quoted here: in whose service is perfect freedom. Each seemingly slavish action, each act of humility, is that which increases freedom. So move on the plumb line of connection with the Creator. Seek the good, the true, the beautiful. Express love. And when the suffering ones come, as they will, do not pull away. You have not the fear that blinds you from seeing this suffering spirit. You can simply love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Cured Versus Healed
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: cured versus healed.

The question this day was about healing. What are the prerequisites for it? When is healing appropriate, and when is it not? And how can we take part in the healing process? Q'uo's answer begins by drawing a line most of us have never drawn.

Not all who are cured are healed, they say, and not all who are healed are cured. A cure is a physical process. A diagnosis, a treatment, the body fixed as a mechanic would fix a car. A healing is something else entirely. It is a state of balance within the entity. Illnesses are sometimes evidence of imbalance. But at other times, the illness that is not cured is, on the other hand, balanced. There are those who carry a condition in order to learn a lesson concerning love, and the suffering it brings is the precise suffering the lesson required.

I want to be careful here, in my own voice, because this is tender ground. Nothing in the archive is medical advice, and nothing I am saying is either. Illness is real, and suffering is real, and the archive itself honors the work of doctors and therapists. If you are ill, care for the body with real care, and use every good tool the world offers. What Q'uo is describing is not a substitute for medicine. It is a way of holding the deeper meaning of what the body goes through.

Q'uo turns to the fear that surrounds illness, and they are honest about where it comes from. The physical vehicle does not wish to decay or die. There is a deep, primal instinct toward the continuance of living. That is necessary. But the seeker need not make it the whole attitude. The entity each seeker truly is is infinitely more than the physical vehicle.

And here is the practice they recommend, simple and physical. The awareness begins the incarnation on bad terms with the body, they say. It could not make its arms and legs move for so long, and it never fully embraces the vehicle. Much of illness, they suggest, is due to the disrespect paid to the physical body as that which is not holy. So give the body respect and attention. Send light to the places that hurt. Find your own way into loving relationship with the physical vehicle. It is work that aids the balance of body, mind, and spirit together.

Then comes the subtlety. There is no clear or provable way to know whether an illness has done its work and is ready to be dropped. The seeker must pursue this for itself. And for some, the only healing necessary is the realization of why the illness had virtue. Then the seeker gazes into health and asks the harder question: am I ready to take responsibility for the work of living that full health would ask of me? Sometimes the lesson is learned but the healing does not come, because the seeker is not ready for what wellness would demand.

The closing image is the breath. Pause, Q'uo says, and feel the breath move in, the breath move out. Health begins with breathing deeply in and deeply out. You breathe into you the love of the infinite Creator, and you breathe out all that is tired, old, and ready to leave. Healing is not a process that stops. Each entity is constantly in a state of healing, balancing, strengthening the energy web that is its essence.

And for those who would help another: send love and light, and leave the door open. To serve without invitation is not service. Remain open in the heart, remain open in the offering, and continue to give love without expectation of return. The free will of each entity is of paramount importance. The steps must be taken by each entity for the self.

Thank you for listening.

title: Not My Will But Thine
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: not my will but thine.

The question this day was about the ordinary disaster of a ruined plan. In the daily round we find ourselves having to change our plans, to surrender to a new set of circumstances. Is there value in this being out of balance? Is there a way to move through it more smoothly? What attitude helps?

Q'uo begins by walking us through two kinds of mornings. The orderly mind wakes and makes the list, sorting duties and chores into a structure. The freer mind wakes and follows whatever catches the eye, moving between this and that. And they say something I did not expect: each of these ways is a skillful way to move through the day. Follow your nature. The question is not how you organize the hours. The question is whether, in the middle of all of it, you remembered the Creator.

Because by early afternoon, the schedule has been changed, then changed radically, then discarded entirely. Every plan meets the world. And beyond all the techniques for flowing with catalyst lies a single attitude that transforms every experience. It is a real, living, conversational relationship with the one infinite Creator. Not a concept. A relationship.

The key phrase, Q'uo says, is the one spoken by the teacher known as Jesus: not my will, but thine. You and your consciousness are as the tip of a great iceberg. Your self, the profound and illimitable self you truly are, has only a small amount showing above the water. That silent wisdom, that spark of love within, moves into and transforms pain, suffering, misunderstanding, and every negative emotion.

Then comes the image that gives the session its weight. The earth within you, your sticks and stones of expectation, must be broken up so that good seed may be planted. This plowing of the self is painful. It feels as though the self were being torn down like an old house. And that old self is being torn down. But there is a promise: that which is being torn down shall seem to you in the future not a self at all.

I love the mercy in that promise. The ruined plan, the day that falls apart, the expectation that gets plowed under, it is not a failure. It is the ground being made ready. When service to others is attempted, you serve not only the personality in front of you but the Creator self within that entity. So pour yourselves out in service, worrying not whether you have succeeded, but only working toward more purity of desire to serve.

The session also holds a quiet word about the souls we travel with. We move through this illusion not alone but in clans, in groupings of like-minded entities, exchanging roles across lifetimes, sibling, friend, mate, meeting again and again to offer each other the right catalyst. It is more nearly the common case than the exception. So the people around your table today may be old companions, and the friction between you may be the plow doing its work.

Above all, let not your heart be troubled, Q'uo says. This is under your conscious control, if you choose to claim the mastery over the self. Not by removing yourself from the thick of things, but by bringing into the thick of things the sacred. An attitude is only one word, yet this attitude is the key to the devotional life, for all things are sacred to the one who has the eyes to see, the ears to hear, and the heart to understand.

So when the plan breaks, say the old words. Not my will, but thine. Let the ground be plowed. Let the seed be planted. And watch what grows.

Thank you for listening.

title: Healing the Incarnation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: healing the incarnation.

The question this day is a bold one. If each of us comes into a life with a plan of lessons to learn and services to offer, is it possible to finish the plan? To do everything you came to do, and then move on to a second act, improvising from there, putting frosting on the cake? The group called it the healing of the incarnation, and they asked Q'uo whether it can be done.

Q'uo answers that healing, here, means balance. The healing of an incarnation is the crystallization of its fruits to a point where such a depth of equanimity arises in the spirit that it becomes free to create further harmony in ways that were impossible before. For many entities, they say honestly, the incarnation will not be healed within the incarnation, because no firm rock has been built, depending solely on the relationship with the Creator, on which that balance could clearly be seen.

And here is the hard part, stated plainly. You cannot cause the self to come into balance by thinking about it. Work in consciousness is work without an object. The mind attempts to create balance and can do real work, but deeper and closer to the truth lie ocean depths of bias and prejudice that function subconsciously, and the conscious mind has no access to them. One is relatively helpless to heal one's own incarnation by will alone.

But there is a path, and it is the way of faith. The most vivid blossoms along that path are self-forgiveness, forgiveness of the Creator, and forgiveness of all those the heart has held in thrall with anger. Once these dusty cobwebs of past negative emotion are swept from that subconscious place, forgiveness may blossom, and then the seeker discovers almost by reflex that the circumstances of the incarnation have been transformed.

I love the image of the final transformation that Q'uo describes. There comes a time, an initiation having to do with oneself only, when the whole self, the whole life, becomes soft and malleable, if the seeker is at that time perfectly willing to forgive all. The healing of the incarnation becomes a gift given to the self by the subconscious levels of self, aided by what this instrument would call the Holy Spirit, and what Q'uo often calls the higher self.

A questioner then asks about leaving this life together with a beloved, and Q'uo's answer is worth hearing for its honesty. There are those so well attuned to each other that their paths coincide and even end together. But more often, paths that join for a great portion of the way find individual points of departure. In the larger frame, the timing of the departure is relatively unimportant. What matters is the work: to give what can be given, to forgive all, to learn all that the incarnation can possibly teach.

I want to speak gently here, in my own voice. The archive talks about death as a departure, a parenthesis in eternity, and it speaks of grief with great tenderness. But if you are grieving someone now, or if thoughts of leaving this life are heavy in you, please do not walk with that weight alone. Reach for the people who love you, and for counselors and crisis lines and every real support the world holds. The archive's hope is that we learn to love more, not less, and asking for help is part of that learning.

Q'uo closes with a picture of the greater family we all belong to, moving within this illusion, helping those who need help, inspiring those who are weary, lending assistance to those who walk with difficulty. There are many adventures that await, they say, and many moments that may disappoint. But you may always take comfort in knowing that the love of the one Creator resides in full in each, and requires only the smallest need to be kindled into flame.

Forgive all. That is the whole of it. And the healing follows.

Thank you for listening.

title: Devotion Is the Vocation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: devotion is the vocation.

The group came this day with no question at all, only the invitation to see what Q'uo would say. What came is a session about the deepest question a person can ask: what am I here to do?

Q'uo begins with the simplest truth they know, the one they bring to every session. The one great original Thought, the Logos, is Love. Your word love does not fulfill it as a symbol, but it is the closest your language has. This Love is that which has created all that is. And each of you, Q'uo says, is that love clothed in flesh. A flower opening toward the sun. You came from the seed, and as you blossom, so shall you surely perish from this illusion. And that which was earth shall again become earth. Yet the spirit within flies free.

Then comes the question of vocation, and the answer cuts through so much striving. Each in the circle searches for the right work. But the first vocation of each of you, by your very nature, is the vocation of living a life of devotion and faith. Before any career, any ministry, any visible service, there is this: the deepest portion of your true nature, also the basic portion of your outer experience. When that desire is realized within, that which is within you of love has, for the first time, a voice. And that voice speaks in silence.

So the recommendation is disarmingly plain. Devise for yourself a daily practice that fits you, and include in it a period of silent meditation. If it can be daily, make the commitment. For within the heart of self, within that vast creation which lies within your consciousness, there is a holy of holies, and within that room waits the Creator. The door is guarded and locked against intruders, and yes, you yourself are an intruder to yourself if you try to storm it. The key to that door is silent meditation.

I love the honesty of what follows. This surrendering feels like dying, Q'uo says, and because of that the path is often perceived as difficult and painful. There is a natural tendency to resist change, in every cell of the body and brain. The spiritually directed life does not lack joy, but it increases suffering as it increases the rate of change. So they ask each seeker to gaze unblinking at the cost. It shall cost all that you are and all that you have to become that truth which you are seeking. As far as we know, they say, you cannot know the truth. You can only become true.

That line stopped me when I first read it. You cannot know the truth. You can only become true. All the study, all the systems, all the certainty we chase, and the teaching says the knowing is not the point. The becoming is the point. And the becoming happens in silence, in the holy of holies, one daily sitting at a time.

As you enter that silence again and again, Q'uo says, you hollow out within yourself an ever smoother channel for light and love, so that what is seen is not you but the Creator shining through. And when the self realizes it has been that lighthouse, then the entity finally feels the joy of right vocation. Your being, your essential self, is your main service to the one Creator and to all upon your planet.

So if you are wondering what you are for, the answer is quieter than you hoped and larger than you feared. Be the lighthouse. Keep the silence. Let the light move through. That is the first vocation, and everything else is built on it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hall of Mirrors
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hall of mirrors.

The question this day was about the mirroring effect. When you notice a trait in another person that you dislike, what is really happening, the teaching goes, is that you are seeing a disliked portion of yourself reflected back. The group asked: as we accept ourselves more, do we accept others more easily? And is there a point where the behavior is simply repugnant on its own, beyond all mirroring? Q'uo's answer is one of the most balanced in the archive.

They begin with the one thought they always bring. The one great original Thought is Love. Each consciousness listening is a complex of love, manifesting in various forms. Many are the distortions of that love, yet the energy within them, no matter how great the distortion, is that of love.

Then comes the tempering. This mirroring idea, Q'uo says, can be taken too far quite handily. Indeed, all possible actions, motives, and ideas are a portion of each consciousness. All things are one. But within the illusion, other entities shall almost always seem to be other. It is only in the intimacy of intense catalyst, the love-making or the shared creative experience or the laughter that ends in tears, that hearts come close enough to perceive their actual unity.

And here is the part I want to underline. It is not necessary for progressing spiritually that there be continual focus on judging how the self is doing. In the attitude of seeing everything as the mirror, there is a generalization that has moved beyond its heart into a place the logicians enjoy but the heart does not find useful. The mirror is a tool. Use it where it helps, and put it down where it does not.

So where does it help? When something sticks in the mind like a burr, that which will not stop bothering you, take it and examine it as if it were a mineral mined from your own soil. When there is an entity who has, over time, continually created aggravation, gaze at that feeling with an eye to see where the true source of the pain is, the need within that is making the separating judgment. But when it is a stranger or a passerby, Q'uo says, you are doing work where there is no work to do. Keep the mirror small. Keep it honest.

Then comes the image that gives this episode its name, shown to the instrument in a pause. A bright and shining hall, grand, with mirrors lining both sides and both ends. Into it walk ladies and gentlemen in their finery. The conversation is brilliant, the lights glitter, and the images repeat themselves endlessly. Where lies the truth in this gathering? In the flat images in the mirror? In the conversation? In the clothing? Q'uo suggests turning from all mirrors that seem to reflect, and letting the discrimination within choose the time to invoke the parable of the mirror.

The desire to judge remains compelling throughout third density, they say, but the ability to judge correctly is not given to any who draw breath. There is no spiritual use in judgment. When the desire comes upon you, see it for what it is: the small self within incarnation trying to put the chaos of stimuli in order. Release, when you can, that desire to control. And turn instead within, to the fire that burns at the heart, at the holy of holies, locked within you by silence.

Be gentle with the self, Q'uo asks, and gentle with others as they mirror to you some portion of the universal self. Take time each day, if only thirty seconds, to turn to the truth that lies within, which all that is without merely suggests. Warm your hands at that flame. It is yours to choose when and how.

Thank you for listening.

title: Sweet Winter Thoughts
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: sweet winter thoughts.

This session was held on Christmas Day, and the group came with no set question, only the joys and sorrows they had been sharing before the working began. What Q'uo gave them is a meditation on communication, on trust, and on the winter season itself, and it is one of the warmest sessions in the archive.

They begin where all real conversation begins. The sweetness within the stream of moment by moment living depends greatly on the self's ability to open the heart both to giving and to receiving. It may seem that some things never need to be said. Yet if there is a kindly opinion, a good thought, a fair and loving impulse, let it be shared. For when the breath is expanded in speech concerning the desire to love, to understand, to support, the energy is as the healing that moves between the words.

Then comes the teaching I want to carry with me. That which most deeply uncovers and cleanses the self is most often not the rational, the logical, or the common sense, but that speech or action which is intuited by the portion of the self that dreams. Trust that feeling which says this feels right, Q'uo says, and do not overstretch the rational mind's burden with requests that all be rationally seen. Often the saving key within an impulse is exactly that which cannot be explained, except by the feeling that intuition is real and can be honed.

I love the humility underneath this. Anything which can be said in words is not the truth, they say. Their own concepts are true, but there is an absolute truth they may experience and never understand or control. So the seeker must rest in the security of mid-air. The one who dares to venture greatly walks over the archetypical cliff into the abyss of unknown things. Is there the sensation of falling? Indeed not. But the leap must be made first, before any knowledge has been gained by experience.

Treasure each experience of union, Q'uo says, and remember it, for many are the times when only the memory of faith is available to the conscious mind. Yet that sweet memory is so transcendent that one instant of union with the divine is infinitely more than enough to justify a lifetime of faith, sacrifice, and service. When such a moment comes, stop, even for a moment, and give thanks, and ask the self to remember.

And then the winter. Q'uo sees the season the way the seeker should see it. The trees stand skeletal against the winter sky, stripped and bare, and in their rarefied beauty there is a lesson. These are times for moving into the roots and the ground of being. There is that within you which is the seed of new life. Huddle yourself to support and love and cherish that self that is being born each moment. Bide impatience, release expectation, and allow the rest, the sleeping, the slow rekindling of hope and courage for what is to come.

Flow into that darkness, they say. Move into the solidity of earth and cold and contraction. For days there shall indeed be, and all too soon, when that which you have stored up in the winter shall be called upon in the day. May your winter thoughts be sweet, for spring is soon to be with you.

And there is the babe within, Q'uo says, that awaits the birthing, attended by the wise portions of the self that bring gifts. Whether it is Christmas or any other day of the year, the season of renewal is always available. Rest in the dark soil. Trust the seed. The light will come.

Thank you for listening.

title: Moments Out of Time
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: moments out of time.

This evening comes from a January night in nineteen ninety-five, and the voice belongs to Hatonn, speaking to a circle that had been asking a question every seeker asks. How do you stay in the present moment, here and now, in your body and your heart and your spirit, instead of drifting back into the past or leaning forward into the future?

Hatonn answers with a thought that I want to lay down gently, because it might lift a weight you have been carrying. To stay in the present moment, he says, is to stay in eternity, for the fully realized present has infinite depth, and breadth, and height. I love that line. Infinite depth, and breadth, and height. And then he adds something I find so kind. Third density, this life you are living, was not built so that you could be perfect at presence. It was built as a sea of confusion, so that you could exercise your free will in choosing how to spend your time and your attention.

So if you catch yourself dwelling on yesterday or hoping too hard for tomorrow, and then you judge yourself for it, Hatonn asks you to step back from that judgment. You did not come here to win a prize for perfect conformity to the infinite present. You came, he says, to the party, in order to be intoxicated with life. Not an exam. Not a trial. A party, where you are meant to taste everything, to stray from the straight path, drawn by the interests and leanings you brought with you, so that the very dilemmas of finding your way back might teach you most precisely and most profoundly.

There is weather in this, Hatonn says. As you stray and wander, the weather of the emotions blows through the experience of the self by the self. Some days you feel centered and fully awake. Other days you feel hopelessly scattered and foolish. And all those judgments you lay on yourself may look true on the surface, but underneath them the part of you that dwells eternally in the present moment is alive and well. You cannot escape the perfection out of which you were created, and into which you are now maturing.

This is not permission to stop trying. Hatonn does encourage the practice of presence. He speaks of sitting, mentally and emotionally, within that sacred tabernacle inside, that holy ground of being where eternal things live, with bare attention. And he gives a practical image I want to keep. The instrument who channeled him used the ringing of a telephone, or the sound of a church bell from next door, as a reminder to turn for a moment toward thanksgiving and praise. Those are moments out of time, he says. Out of space. Eternal and infinite. And they can be quick. They can be frequent. They do not have to be long or formal.

Here is the turn I did not expect, and I think it is the heart of the whole session. Hatonn says that when seekers speak of living in the present moment, they are trying to describe, using the tools of the illusion, something that does not take part in the illusion at all. What the student of truth is really looking for, he says, is a way to stop thinking, and instead to allow the nakedness of pure attention. Feel that love which is the Creator. Sense it within you like the sun warming the heart. Within the curtain of flesh lies deity, and the vessel that you are is being hollowed out to receive ever more fully that love which is all that there is.

I read that line again and again. The vessel that you are is being hollowed out to receive ever more fully that love which is all that there is. That is the whole assignment, held in one sentence. Not to be perfect at presence. Not to scold yourself for wandering. But to let the vessel be hollowed, a little more each day, until it can hold more of the love that made it.

Hatonn ends the way old friends end things, with a wish. May you seek most purely, forgive most completely, and love each other with all your heart. We are with you in eternity, he says, and bids you joy of your party. And I think that is where he leaves us tonight, too. The party is still going. The music is still playing. You are allowed to enjoy it, and to stray, and to come back, and to laugh at the human condition, and to turn again toward thanksgiving. The present moment will be there when you arrive, patient as eternity, which is exactly what it is.

Thank you for listening.

title: In Other Shoes
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: in other shoes.

This session comes from a January afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question on the table is one that has moved through every human heart at one time or another. When we come back into this life, again and again, do we stay with our own kind, our own people, our own familiar ground? Or do we wander across the borders of race and culture and nation, trying on lives as different from our own as lives can be? The voice that answers is Q'uo.

Q'uo begins where they always begin, at the deepest level, with the spirit itself. Each spirit, they say, is in essence the same, for each spirit is a mobilized, potentiated phase of infinity. And then they give the line that everything else in the session rests upon. Each is Love. Each was always Love. Each shall always be Love. I want to sit with that for a moment, because it is the floor under the whole conversation. Whatever follows about nations and peoples and differences, it stands on this. Each is Love.

From there they paint a picture of the young soul, just sprung from the Creator's fertile love, sailing through universes, moving through densities, until there is a choice, a preference, a bias. This star. This constellation. This planet. And listen to how they put the beginning of incarnation. One day you were water, or earth, or rock, or rain, or wind, or sand. And your incarnations had begun. Was the unity forgotten? Not in the deep mind, they say. It remains a heart's truth, felt within. You are not like others. You are all that there is.

Then Q'uo turns to the practical question. Does the soul tend to stay with one people? And the answer is yes, often, and for good reason. Like calls like. The planetary influence, the racial influence you began with, leaves the first biasing etchings on the archetypical mind, and so souls often return to the same family of influences, lifetime after lifetime, because there is a comfort in it, a feeling of being at home. Cultures develop their own unspoken languages, their own ways of handling the eternal situations common to all humankind, and those ways become handy to the mind. There is nothing wrong with this. It is how the lessons begin.

But then comes the turn that gives this episode its title. As entities grow, as they wake up and discover there is more to know about love than any one group has understood, they naturally choose to begin gleaning from other cultures, other nations, other spiritual groups. Just as the traveler wishes to travel and broaden the understanding of what humankind is, the soul chooses again and again to travel in other shoes, other bodies, other races, creeds and color, for each has something to offer. To be humble in one culture educates, they say. To be humble in another culture offers a completely different education. Each pattern has its place and is its equally valuable teacher.

There is a passage near the end I want to read to you almost whole, because it gathers everything. Q'uo speaks of groups like the very circle gathered that day, unusually varied, drawn together across all the lines, and says it is in such groups that the heart of the lessons of love may begin again to become unified. Each soul now has sufficient experience in seeking the truth of self to find commonalities that move beyond race, religion, nation and culture, and instead find residence in a common foundation of self within. And once that underlying unity is sensed personally, even dimly, they say, it acts like fireworks in the soul. The days of the small personality are numbered. The seeker has the energy now to penetrate each archetype, to become one who can wear the old structures cleanly and find the doors at the end of each of them.

The session closes with a smaller question, about love that is felt by one and not returned by another, and Q'uo's answer is worth carrying out of the evening. Love, when it is truly love, desires to give without expectation of return. To love another truly, they say, you must surrender whatever idea you have of what love should look like, and seek instead to know what the other desires, and bend every effort to satisfy those desires. It is the same lesson as the whole session, really. Step out of your own shoes. Find out what it is like in the other's. That is the whole curriculum.

So tonight I leave you with this image. A soul, vast and old, packing its small bag of biases and preferences, and setting out once more across the border into unfamiliar country, into a skin it has never worn, to learn humility in a new accent, pride in a new color, love in a new tongue. And somewhere underneath all that traveling, unchanged and unchanging, the one original Thought. Each is Love. Each was always Love. Each shall always be Love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Made Visible
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love made visible.

This session comes from a January evening in nineteen ninety-five, and it begins with an observation from one of the circle, a medical doctor, that has the ring of plain honesty. Service feels obvious and instinctual, he says. You see what needs doing and you do it. Love, on the other hand, feels like work. It takes will and effort, and you are never quite sure how well you are doing it. He asked Q'uo what they made of that difference, and their answer is one of the loveliest things in the whole archive.

Q'uo opens with a sentence I want to frame and hang somewhere. Discussing love is our favorite occupation. No subject rings with the purity of that primary Logos, that mystery, the great original thought of Love. Here the mystery begins and here shall be its embrace when all distortions cease. Before they will even attempt to put words around it, they pause to worship it. Thirty seconds of silence on the tape. That pause is part of the teaching.

Then they take up service first. It is true, they agree, that service is easier to attempt than love. But the boundaries between divine qualities are always weak, they say, for love is, and is all that there is. So service is the visible manifestation of the invisible and primal love. I love that line. Service is love made visible. Every meal cooked, every wound dressed, every small kindness is the invisible made touchable. But they warn that the territory of true service is shadowed and complex, a maze. It is sometimes very difficult to discern right service. The destiny of another soul is inward, felt only by the seeker herself, not by the one trying to help from outside.

To make this concrete they borrow an image from Paul the Apostle, the body with many members. The stomach aids by being a stomach, the ears by being ears, and so forth. Each entity has its gifts to share. And then the turn. If each offers a different gift, how infinite must the body of love be. And beyond even that, they say, there is a level where the seeker realizes that the purest service is the realized or illumined being itself. That joyful self, nurtured and allowed to bloom in the light of faith. This is love. This is service, to be. The breath that fills the service with meaning and value is love.

Now they return to love, and agree with the questioner that the ways of love are ways of mystery. Examined physical phenomena end in mystery. Metaphysical concepts, followed far enough, always end in mystery. Unknowing is the sigil motto of the spiritual warrior. Within your density, true love has no voice, they say, yet there are many voices striving to express it. Each seeker is that which is love, yet which is creating sound and motion constantly, striving to discover that which it is.

And then they give the image I have been waiting to share with you. Turn the gaze inward, they say, and gaze steadfastly at that which William Yeats called the rag and bone shop of the heart. Listen to how they put it. Gaze at that illusion, that imperfection perceived, that undeniable self. You look at love. That is the practice. Not to polish the heart into something presentable, but to look straight at the rag and bone shop, the cluttered back room of the self, and recognize that what you are looking at is love, wearing work clothes.

The session ends with encouragement for the weary, and I will give you Q'uo's words almost whole, because they need no help from me. Continue always to seek love, how to express love, and how to be of service. Know these efforts as the often subtle arts that they are. Respect right use of power in being of service, in attempting to manifest love, and develop always little by little, step by step, that place within which is engraved with the print of your feet, that place wherein holy things reside. Know this sanctuary daily. No moment of visiting this holy of holies is in vain.

So tonight, if you have ever felt that love is the harder assignment, that service comes naturally but love takes effort and you never know if you are getting it right, Q'uo is nodding with you. It is the harder assignment. It is the mystery at the center of everything. And the work is not to solve it but to keep visiting the sanctuary, little by little, step by step, until the illumined being you are becoming starts to shine through the doing, and the doing becomes, simply, love made visible.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dance of Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dance of life.

This session comes from a February afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is one of the most practical ever put to Q'uo. How do we recognize what we are supposed to learn from our catalyst? Those difficult experiences, those frictions and irritations and sorrows that life keeps serving up. Is there a technique, a procedure, for learning from them? Q'uo's answer is long and rich, and I want to walk you through the heart of it.

They begin by suggesting that the seeker look for one characteristic above all. Discomfort. Whether it is physical, emotional, mental or spiritual, the experience of discomfort is a hallmark of catalyst, for catalyst, by definition, creates change. So when you find yourself fretting and worrying and hesitating over some issue, they say, simply step back and take note. There is this discomfort. Therefore, there is catalyst. It is that simple, and that honest. The signal is not subtle. It is the knot in your stomach, the circling mind, the thing you cannot leave alone.

But then comes the part I find most freeing. There is no one right response. No single correct answer to what you should do with the discomfort. The attitude they recommend is what they call the far-seeing eye. Not moving on impulse. Not concluding quickly. Remaining serene in the sure and certain knowledge that your destiny will provide continual opportunities to follow through with the lessons you have identified for yourself. The lessons will come back around. You do not have to get it right this time. You only have to stay in the dance.

I love that image, the dance, and Q'uo returns to it. They describe the happy state that becomes possible when the seeker is upheld simply by doing the dance of life, and gazes at all that moves him with a trustful and cheerful eye. And they give a picture of what that trust looks like. A child playing on the seashore goes through many small discomforts. The sun is too hot. The pail washes out to sea. The shovel breaks. The child swallows salt water. To the child these mean very little, for this young spirit is still being surprised by life itself. That spirit of newness, they say, that allowing of catalyst to move you as if it were the first experience, is a key to finding your balance in the processes of change.

Listen to how they put the design of this whole thing. This illusion of yours is created to make evasion of catalyst impossible and full use of catalyst improbable. You cannot dodge the lessons, but using them well is the real work. The world leans on imperfection, forces the mind to gaze at what is not perfect, all so that ordinary life, with its suffering, may become incandescent with the seeker's joyful acceptance and eagerness for change. And the Creator, they add, is most playful. The less you are overcome by the seriousness of situations, the more humor you shall find. Allow that spirit within to romp and play.

The session also turns, in the questions, to the darker part of the self, and Q'uo's answer belongs in this episode because it is the same teaching. You are many things you are not aware of, they say, for you are indeed all things. That you cannot imagine dwelling in terrible darkness is only testimony to the present circle of your being, not its limit. As you process catalyst, the circle widens. You discover there is more to yourself than you first imagined. And the counsel for all of it is the same. Feel through the heart. Accept what is in front of you. Work on that, and let the rest of the mystery work as it will.

There is one more line I want to leave in your hands, because it answers the original question most directly. You are not here to understand and know the self beyond a certain point. You are not here to become perfect. You are here within an illusion which forces you to seek beyond the limits of that which is visible or knowable. So treasure the discomfort. Allow time to pass until the heart feels and senses truth. It cannot be rushed. It cannot be figured out. Watch where your attention is placed, find the light touch, share the laughter, and keep dancing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Life of the Rock
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the life of the rock.

This session comes from a February afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is the oldest one human beings ask. Why is suffering necessary? With so many people in the world suffering so much, how can suffering be a service, either to the ones who suffer or to the Creator who watches it as part of Itself? Q'uo does not flinch from the question. They take it up with both hands, and their answer changed the way I think about the word suffering itself.

They begin with a small revolution in language. Suffering is a word biased substantially in the negative sense, they say. When one suffers one is considered to be bearing pain and trouble. Yet to suffer is actually to allow, and what is allowed in suffering is fear. I want to say that again slowly, because it is the hinge of the whole session. To suffer is actually to allow. Any experience may be suffered, or allowed to occur, and it is the experience which is not resisted which brings a lack of suffering. The pain may be real. The suffering is the resistance.

To show what they mean, they tell the story of a rock. Listen to how they put it, because it is one of the great passages of the archive. The rock begins cast out of the fiery molten core beneath the planet, flung into space, tossed away by what was its home. It thrusts upward through the air. It is worn, eroded, pitted, roughened and crevassed. Bits of earth cling to it. Plants root into it and break it. It is upheaved again, broken, fallen in splinters, rolled into a stream bed, washed century by century until it has become a million pebbles, a billion grains of sand. The rock has a long life, constantly worn away, broken and rebroken, that earth may come to it, that it may support growth and blooming, and that it may eventually dissolve.

Because the rock has no self-consciousness, they say, it does not suffer. It experiences. It is not that the rock accepts the erosion. It is that its nature is as it is, and that which occurs is that which occurs. The animal is the same. It endures the cut paw without suffering, for it does not reflect within itself. But we, in third density, carry the great gift and the great burden of self-consciousness, and so we experience and suffer through every change, every discovery, every phase of development. And insofar as the experience is not resisted and is entered into faithfully, there is not the suffering.

I want to be careful here, because this teaching is easily misread as coldness. Q'uo is not saying pain is an illusion or that you should pretend it does not hurt. They speak with real tenderness of those in famine and disease and loneliness, and of the dryness of spirit that turns to bitterness. They say they feel great sympathy, and are comforted only by knowing that each experience is one stroke of the artist's brush upon an eternal canvas of complete harmony. The teaching is not that suffering does not matter. It is that the Creator does not need your suffering. Listen to this. The Creator does not need your suffering. The Creator wishes your experience, and if suffering is involved the Creator may gladly take that also, for that is your truth. It is accepted without judgment. It is loved. It is blessed. It is not desired.

Then why is experience necessary at all? Because you chose to manifest, they say, and to manifest is to accept a structure of space and time in which choices are made, and those choices advance the uniqueness of your identity. Your incarnation is a school, and you entered it each time with great hopes of achievement. Yet when the semester begins, the work is hard and painful and inconvenient, and it is only natural for the student to protest the grind of one project after another. Is there no end to learning? No, indeed, they say. There is not.

And yet the session ends with something I did not expect, a small human moment. One of the circle asks Q'uo why they sometimes end with a little joke. And Q'uo answers that humor is the view of a situation with a sense of proportion about it. The difficulty, seen in its entirety, is relieved by the larger view. Humor, they say, is an excellent means of restoring the larger view to entities who are perhaps a bit overstressed by one portion of the picture. After an hour on suffering, they leave us laughing. That feels exactly right.

So tonight, if you are in a season of erosion, if the water is wearing at you century by century and you are tired of being ground down, Q'uo offers you the rock. Not as a command to feel nothing, but as a reminder. Experience is necessary. Resistance is optional. And underneath the wearing away, something is being prepared that can support growth and blooming, long after the rock itself has become sand.

Thank you for listening.

title: Catching the Self Unawares
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: catching the self unawares.

This session comes from a February afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is the signal question of our whole density, as Q'uo puts it. Who am I? Not the name on the mailbox, not the job title, but the incarnational personality itself. Who is that self, and how can it be used as a vehicle for evolution? Q'uo takes the question seriously, and their answer is both humbling and strangely liberating.

They begin with the child. That young soul whose mind is infinite and eternal but whose body is clumsy and small must determine what of the body makes him who he is, and what is not of the body but of the mind or the emotions. And here is the part that stopped me. By the age of four and five, they say, the larger part of your people are already philosophers in their own small way, picking up questions of life and death and looking seriously at them for clues to identity. Each year adds its burden of days, and also a crazy quilt of perception and misperception, of memory accurately and inaccurately kept. And the burdens the child takes up become invisible, stowed safely as in a ship's hold, waiting for the long voyage before the self is ready to open the cargo doors.

I love that image, the ship's hold. So much of who we are is cargo we loaded before we knew what we were carrying, and it waits below deck, patient, until we are ready to work with it. Q'uo says much healing can be done by going back into those early experiences that biased the program, discovering those centers of pain and anger and disappointment that crystallized the distortion in the first place. Dreams can help. Memory can help. But then they say something that turns the whole project sideways. It is equally helpful, they say, to surrender all knowledge of self as utterly irrelevant to the self that wishes to become one with the infinite Creator, who wishes only to lose itself in that presence.

Both are true. Work to know yourself, and be ready to release everything you learn. That is the rhythm of the whole session. Sitting down with a pen to infer your identity by logic, they say, is not useful, for the self is not built with the logic of the mind. The deepest self is a distortion of love, and the heart as it opens simply becomes more and more able to resonate to the pure emotions which are that unique distortion of love which is each entity. You feel and intuit your way toward yourself. You do not think your way there.

Then Q'uo offers the most practical counsel in the session, and it is wonderfully un-grand. Allow the self the freedom of semi-permeable boundaries, they say. Go deeply within when the moments come, for moments of clarity come when they will, and yield to them. And when the self is not in such a state, allow the questions to rest, for self-discovery is a process which needs time. One cannot gaze forever at the self with profit. One must look away and become spontaneous. It is a matter of catching it unawares. That is our title tonight, and it is also, I think, the whole method. Stop staring at yourself. Wash the dishes. Teach the class. Do the small chore. Realization loves to arrive in the middle of the most routine moment, because the inner mountaintops are not where the outer world thinks they are.

There is one more thread I want to gather, because it answers the fear underneath the question. It can feel unfair, Q'uo admits, that the deck is stacked against knowing the truth you so hungrily seek. But they say the spirit within incarnation that is still seeking is the spirit that has the right to manifest within the illusion. No one upon your sphere is fully realized. Each entity is upon that journey, and so are we. The unfinishedness is not a flaw in the design. It is the design. When school is out, the Creator simply allows the entity to move on. So the fact that you do not fully know yourself tonight is not evidence that you are failing. It is evidence that you are still enrolled.

So tonight, be profound in one mood and shallow in another, light one day and heavy the next, and allow yourself that freedom. Let the cargo rest in the hold until you are ready. And when a moment of clarity comes unannounced, in the middle of nothing special, yield to it. That is the self, caught unawares, telling you who it is.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Golden Net of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the golden net of love.

This session comes from a late February afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question could have been asked yesterday. Does our technology, television, computers, the internet, radio, music, help us become one people? Are these things training wheels for the formation of what the archive calls the social memory complex, that union of minds and hearts toward which our whole species is slowly moving? Hatonn comes first, briefly, with words of affection and encouragement, and then Q'uo takes up the question in earnest.

Q'uo begins with the metaphor everyone reaches for, the computer. The internet, they say, is a promising and substantial metaphor for what a social memory complex has as its resources. No longer must the seeker wander from place to place hunting for materials. Mass quantities of information are available to masses of people. And then they say the sentence that undoes the metaphor in the most beautiful way. The computer, no matter how complete its store of information, cannot express the concepts which move into emotion.
