There is no logic to emotion. The social memory complex is not a bigger hard drive. It is, in their phrase, a golden net of love.

I want to stay with that image, because Q'uo clearly loves it too. A net, as alive as those who have contributed to it, an infinitely great network of connections from person to person to person. When a member wishes to know something, the information is accessed, but it is accessed through the heart, through a knowing which is like instinct once it has been awakened within. Intuition, they say, is the way of knowing that no computer, no matter how sophisticated, can replicate. The machine has no heart. The net is made of heart.

Now here is the part that feels prophetic. Q'uo sees a two-way dynamic in your media and your networks. On the one hand, the mass media focuses on what carries a heavy negative charge, the war, the murder, the violence, and this builds fear and raises walls between entities. On the other hand, the same media carries much that is yeasty with hope for those who are looking for some place to belong, some place that does not feel alien. And with the greatly enhanced capacity to make connections that the age of information brings, these media become the harbingers, even the parents, of the social memory complex. The tools are neutral. The reaching is everything.

And then the counsel, which I think is the true heart of the session. The social memory complex shall be builded one relationship at a time, they say. Just as nations seeking peace must first seek peace within the self. The great desire to see the global self emerge is most productive when it does not lead to impersonally conceived campaigns to contact everyone, but to trust. Trust that the connections that need to be made shall be made as they come to ripeness and readiness. No outcome held in thought. No limitation placed on the possibilities of any connection.

There is a warning folded into this, and it is a gentle one. Those who most wish to help the world are sometimes drawn into rigid structures, great plans conceived irrespective of the connections actually made. Q'uo encourages instead the intuition and sense of the heart, the spontaneous connection, the relationship that ripens on its own. The deepest desires of the human heart cannot be shoved. They cannot be hurried. They arrive the way fruit ripens, in their season.

There is a quiet reassurance tucked into all of this that I do not want you to miss. You do not have to build the net. You only have to be one true thread in it. Every honest conversation, every act of reaching across a difference, every time you choose connection over comfort, the net grows stronger by exactly one thread. And no thread is wasted, because the net remembers every one.

So tonight, think of every message you have ever sent that mattered, every call that came at the right hour, every stranger who became a friend across impossible distance. That is the net being woven, one thread at a time, by hands like yours. The technology is only the loom. The thread is the reaching. And the pattern it is making, if Q'uo is right, is nothing less than a golden net of love, slowly drawing the whole human family into one.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Seed and the Sun
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the seed and the sun.

This session comes from a March afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is a hard one, asked plainly. When a minority is different from the majority, in sex or race or color or creed or dress or ideas, it gets pushed out. Is this built into us? Is it instinct, in humans, in mammals, in animals? And is there a way of seeing it that could help us live with each other? Q'uo answers at length, and with unusual tenderness, and I want to give you the whole arc.

They begin with the sun. Q'uo says they can feel, through the instrument's senses, the warmth of the afternoon sun, and it makes them nostalgic for their own third-density days, that wonderful feeling of life stirring out of winter's sleep. And then they turn that image on you. Each of you, they say, is a seed which has lain in the dark ground through times contracted and forlorn. Each of you is a seed of infinite love and infinite light, yet your blossoming shall be long in coming, and you shall have many bodies before that blossom is finally perfect, and in that perfection is lost into the All.

Now to the question. Is the pushing-out instinctive? Q'uo says no, not in the way we fear. The animal vehicle does have instincts about threat, taught by parents and the herd, but those responses are simple. Avoid what is dangerous. Ignore the rest. There is no instinct in the body for separating self from other self. What happens instead is something closer to an instinct gone wild. The real instinct, they say, is the hunger to know the self. Who am I? But in answering it, the young entity begins defining itself over against others who are different. The first prejudice, they say, is the very young child's discovery of the word no. That impulse to negation, innocent in itself, becomes the crux of a process that has given your world one destructive conflict after another.

Listen to how they trace it. The child accretes a list of natural enemies. Your people have no natural enemies except each other, yet one upon another the young soul piles up those to fear, those to avoid, those to distrust, generalizing from one or two particulars into theories about whole peoples. By the teenage years the basic floor of the prejudicial system is nailed together, ready to build upon. And underneath it all is a primal anxiety, a hunger to know the self, which gets projected outward. Entire sections of the human family are judged not as good, not as smart, not as wise as the self, because the self cannot bear its own unanswered question.

So what is to be done? Q'uo's answer is interior, and it is demanding. Bring the judgment back inside. Those who seek peace among peoples must first go into the cave of the self and take the fight to the place where the arena is prepared, for the heart within is wise. Whatever you perceive as characteristic of others is a dim reflection of disagreements within yourself. The business of humankind, they say, is the self. And the practice is to move within and see the self against the backdrop, not of others, but of the one infinite Creator.

And then the turn toward hope, which is why I chose this title. The great genius of humankind, Q'uo says, the great gift of self-awareness, is the endowment of the Creator for connection. The desire to connect, to communicate, to enter into communion with others, this is the instinct, the true instinct of humankind. It has been trampled and tossed in a corner while we played games of masks and sides. But it is still there. And as each entity wakes from winter's sleep and decides to disagree with the self rather than with others, then person by person consciousness shall be raised, and the group that is waiting to form shall begin connecting in a golden net of commonality and communion.

They close with a line I want to leave you holding. You bloom not for mankind, they say, but for the one infinite Creator. As the sun shines upon you, know that your greatest relationship is between the self that is individualized in you and that great Self which is the one original Thought, Love. You are lovely blossoms, even as seeds. Your nature is written clearly within, and you have but to free yourself to grow.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Onion Skin
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the onion skin.

This session comes from a March evening in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is about reality itself. What is real, and what is only personal? Can one person transmit their reality to another? Can we transcend our personalities and touch something more true? And does Q'uo have a preferred perspective on truth? They warn us first that language is a blunt instrument for this work, words being tools made for conquering decisions in the physical world. With that apology, they begin.

The first level, they say, is apparent reality, the world of consensus, of life as it is. And they give it an image I have not been able to forget. This manifestation, intricate and rich as it is, is but the onion skin skimming the surface of an infinite well of being. The skin is tough and resistant to puncture, they say, yet quite thin. And the entity with a sharp needle of selfhood simply pierces it, and moves into the depths of that ocean which is being, which is consciousness. Half of what we carry around, they suggest, is simple sense impression, and the other half is construction upon it, built by what the instrument calls world opinion.

But here is the generous turn. The everyday and ordinary surface, they say, holds every tool necessary for utter realization. There is enough information lying like litter about every doorpost in the ordinary of things. Most seekers prefer not to work with the ordinary, but to seek what underlies or overshadows it, drawn by the fascination of the depths. And Q'uo honors both paths. The mystic who delves into the deep mind, and the one who sees the sacramental in the ordinary, like dust in a sunbeam or leaves in wind. Both are dealing with illusion, they remind us. All is illusion except the one great original Thought which is Love. If there is a you which is seeking, that you is an illusion. We are illusion. All that can speak is illusion and distortion.

That sounds bleak until you hear what they build on it. Through the densities, they say, the seeking soul familiarizes itself with progressively denser illusions, illusions more filled with light and more articulate of truth. Until at last, the entity that has balanced love and wisdom turns away from manifestation and releases all personality, not so that a seeker may know the Truth, but that it may be it. I love that distinction. Not to know it. To be it.

And then the most practical counsel in the session, about whether we should try to hand our reality to someone else. Q'uo says the searching is an entirely private matter. Each entity's journey is unique. It is not a mistake to offer your vision when asked, but there is an innate respect they encourage for the free will of others. The respect for another's viewpoint may well cause you to listen rather than to improve the other's thinking, for that entity may have much to offer you. When questions are asked, give everything. When they are not, practice the truly listening ear. It is far better, they say, than proselytizing.

I want to give you two smaller images they tuck into the session, because they are the kind of thing you can use on an ordinary Tuesday. The first is about seeking in the deep mind. The truth comes into consciousness more like a scent, they say. An aroma is detected and the nose follows that scent to the bubbling pot. Seeking in the metaphysical realm is of that nature. You simply must follow your intuition, which is the olfactory organ of the metaphysical universe. The second is about intensity. The more serious and caught up one gets in pursuit of the perfect ideal, the more knots one ties in one's own mind. So let intensity be balanced by what the instrument calls the light touch.

And they close with a sentence that gathers the whole evening. This illusory dream world, this twilight, is the absolute best environment possible for learning what it is to be aware and what it is to love and be loved. This world and no other. So do not despise the onion skin. It is thin, and it is tough, and it is yours to pierce. And on the other side of it, the infinite well is waiting, exactly as deep as you are willing to go.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Truth Between Us
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the truth between us.

This session comes from a March afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is about one of the tenderest problems in human life. How do you communicate honestly when the people you are talking to see the world so differently? What about white lies, when the absolute truth would hurt? And how does Q'uo manage it with us? Their answer is wise about words, and wiser about what lies underneath words.

They begin with a warning that sets the tone. When one attempts to communicate the truth, they say, one can be sure that if the matter has substance, the full truth shall not be revealed. All efforts to define or capture pure truth are what the instrument would call quixotic, errands of the soul doomed to a noble and worthwhile attempt and failure. You can approach truth asymptotically, from many angles, but you cannot arrive at it in time and space. I find that oddly comforting. It takes the pressure off every conversation you have ever fumbled.

To show what better communication looks like, they turn to the one known as Jesus, who did not speak plainly but offered little stories with the character of riddles, parables containing self-contradictory notions. One might infer, they say, that this entity considered the feeling behind a parable the carrier of truer communication than the specific words themselves. And the effort succeeded, they suggest, not only because of the speaker or the cleverness of the stories, but because of the relationship between the speaker and the material. This was an entity who knew itself, and that self-knowledge is the hidden foundation of all honest speech. Before the mouth opens, they say, a significant portion of what is to come has already been ratified or nullified by the being of the person communicating.

And then the sentence I want to underline for you. Pure truth lies always in the area between any two entities rather than in the one or in the other. Even if they agree, still, the truth itself cannot be captured. That is our title tonight, and it reframes every difficult conversation. You are not delivering truth like a package. You are meeting someone in the space between you, and something true can happen there, or not, depending on the honesty of the meeting.

Language itself gets a careful, almost affectionate analysis. It was built, they say, for the day-to-day transactions of people with people. What to order, what errands to run, what schedule to keep. For that, it is strong enough. But when entities awaken and begin to hunger for something that is not the bread and butter of life, something all the sweeter for being impractical, the deeper truth, the wider perspective, the ground of being, then words start to slip and go false under the weight. The truest communication, they say, tends to happen between two seekers who recognize each other as comrades and can listen with a light and free heart, not asking words to bear much, but allowing words to wash over and touch upon the felt and present truth.

The hardest case, they admit, is between one who has awakened and one who still sleeps, where the attempt to persuade, no matter how gently done, creates friction. Their counsel is beautiful. Do not shove. Use the light touch. If a truth can be shared in a humorous or light-hearted way that charms and disarms the hearer, the inroads may be made with the listener all unaware of the gift received. Be playful, even a little silly, so that the thought leaves a taste behind and can be revisited later.

And then the closing image, which I think is the real answer to the whole question. The greatest single communication which an entity ever makes, they say, is the look, the stature, the beingness, the way the seeker is. Your bodies, your beings, these that you dress and wash and feed and tend, these are your wisdoms. Your inherent vibratory expression communicates more deeply than you shall ever know. For the truth, as it becomes purer, is that which we are. And that is far beyond words.

So tonight, if there is something true you have been trying to say and the words keep failing, take heart. The words were never going to carry it alone. Tend to the being who speaks them. Meet the other in the space between. And trust that what you are, quietly, over time, is saying everything.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mind of God
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mind of God.

This session comes from an April afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and it is almost entirely questions and answers, the circle firing query after query at Q'uo. What is the mind of God? Does it exist? What was the resurrection body? Was there a light on the mountain of transfiguration? The session ranges widely, and I am going to leave the historical curiosities aside and take you to the two moments where the session catches fire, because those are the moments that will still be warm when you need them.

The first is the question about the mind of God. Q'uo answers on several levels, and the deepest one is disarmingly simple. All that you could name, they say, and all that you might forget to name, and all things whatsoever, remain one thing, and that one is all that there is. You who ask the question are the mind of God. The instrument who channels is the mind of God. Each and every bit of stuff there is, is the mind of the Creator, for the creation is the Creator. And the closest concept they can offer to what you mean by the mind of God is the great original Thought, the Logos, which is Love, containing within itself all unmanifest and manifest creation.

I love the turn they make next, because it hands the whole thing back to you. Within the illusions of the densities, they say, each of you is the mind of God in potentiation. And the work of the densities is clearing away confusion, and in third density that means clearing away each seeker's self-definitions, layer after layer, until each finds within itself the willingness and the instinct to take upon the self the role of that Love, that Logos, that original Thought. Realizing, they add, that within the illusions the only manifestation of this Logos shall come from your words and your hands. Your words. Your hands. That is where the mind of God shows up in this world, or it does not show up at all.

The second moment comes when the questioner, unsatisfied with analogies, asks Q'uo to speak without them, straight to the heart. How are we all one? And Q'uo reaches for the science of the questioner's own schooldays. The illusion is built of what you call atoms, treated as little particles that become things. But no scientist has ever seen mass when gazing at atoms. All that science has found are fields of energy. So the questioner is a field of a certain kind of energy. The instrument is another such field. Each self-conscious person is a complex of vibrations, a signature. And within your density it is impossible to see that there is no separation between the clothes and the body, the body and the seat, the seat and the floor. All these things appear separate. But beyond energy fields, they say, there is no separation.

The senses sense illusion, they say plainly, an illusion your own scientists have penetrated. The energies that seem to separate person from person are dictated by the physical vehicle. And yet there are those who, because of great similarity or great love, can transcend the apparent separation, and such entities have supported and strengthened you all your life. You have felt it. The friend whose mood you knew before a word was spoken. The stranger whose grief moved through you like your own. Those are not metaphors. Those are the fields overlapping, the mind of God recognizing itself.

Near the end of the session there is a quieter exchange I want to include, about the relation of space and time to time and space, and whether the conscious mind lives in one and the subconscious in the other. Q'uo suggests the assumption is largely correct, and adds that the veil of forgetting, which divides the mind, exists only in third density, and only so that the choice of paths can be made. What is necessary for graduation, they say, is not mastery of the deep mind or travel in time and space. It is much simpler, and much harder. That the entity be desirous of serving others in a loving and compassionate manner, more than it desires to serve itself.

So tonight, when you look at your hands, remember what Q'uo said they are for. The mind of God has no other hands in this illusion but yours. No other words but yours. Every act of love you manage today is the original Thought, thinking itself, one more time, in the only medium it has. You.

Thank you for listening.

title: Reaching and Waiting
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: reaching and waiting.

This session comes from an April afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the subject is sexuality, approached not with embarrassment or prurience but with a reverence that is rare in any literature on the topic. The circle asks about the natural expression of male and female sexuality, the archetypal forces behind it, how to work with these energies, and whether the sexual exchange can be a pathway to the unity of Creator and creation. Q'uo answers at length, and I will walk you through it as faithfully as I can.

They begin by refusing to isolate sexuality from the rest of life. The wellspring of your physical vehicles is the sexual activity, they say. The fructifier of inspiration is often the sexual activity. The healer of pain, even deep pain, is often sexual activity. And all the energies of friendship, of people reaching toward people as societies, need to be seated within strong and healthy sexuality to have depth. It is the soil. And then the line that sets the tone for everything. Sexual intercourse is as the Eucharist of red ray, the holy communion of the body. This union recapitulates the oneness of earth and sky, the oneness of male and female, the oneness of reaching and waiting.

Reaching and waiting. That is the archetypal dynamic they describe, and our title tonight. Archetypically, the male reaches with the outstretched hand, and the female awaits the reaching. In truth, they are quick to add, male and female both reach and both await. But as a way of grasping how the energy moves, the image holds. And here is the part I want every seeker to hear. The seeker hungry for wisdom often tries to work on the higher centers, the heart, the throat, the brow, compassion and communication and consciousness, while neglecting the soil. But any plant begins its life within the soil. The sexual identity is as powerful and as completely unique a part of the individual spirit as any other energy. The first holiness is here, where feet meet earth, where spirit meets flesh. Here is the beginning of a good work.

Q'uo is frank about the difficulties, and I appreciate the frankness. Sex is intended to cause great catalyst. It is meant to befuddle, to anger, to grieve, from time to time, for the journey from head to heart must be taught at every level of energy. The male energy reaches, and will always in some measure reach indiscriminately, in fantasy and thought as well as act. The female energy protects, and that healthy protectiveness can degenerate into bitterness and fear. The instrument's own blunt words are quoted, and I will spare you the pejoratives and keep the point. Each side has its characteristic distortion, and each will fail, again and again, to be perfect at this.

And that is where the teaching turns most beautiful. In working with each other, they say, the energy called forgiveness is most important. See the dynamic of sexuality with a merciful gaze. Be quick to forgive. Be willing again and again to attempt to trust. When there is discord at this level, much energy is blocked, and the student who tries to work in the higher centers while the foundation is blocked is building on sand. So work here first, and work here all your life. Then, when male and female wish equally to work together at this level, there is a constant supply of transferred energy, to the male inspiration, to the female vital energy, each giving what each has in abundance.

They close the main teaching with an encouragement I want to pass on exactly as given. See working on sexuality as a holy occupation and part of a holy life. Let it be wonderful and fun. Free the self to rejoice in the beauty of this energy. This is a long process sometimes. However, there is much pleasure in the work. And in the sexual mating between two who grasp the profundity of these energies, they say, there is the possibility of touching intelligent energy itself, and in this fusion the two truly are one. From this rise male and female, blessed, balanced and healed.

So tonight, whatever your situation, partnered or single, active or celibate, the work is the same and it is yours alone to do. Gently part the tangled strands. Let the other's issues stay with the other. Work upon the self, with mercy, with forgiveness, with a willingness to begin again. For this energy lies at the very heart of your individuality, and tending it is tending the root from which everything else in your spiritual life must grow.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Pain of Change
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the pain of change.

This session comes from Easter Sunday in nineteen ninety-five, with spring pushing new green through the ground outside, and the circle asks about resurrection. Not only the ancient story, but the thing itself. Rebirth. The coming into being of a new self. How does it happen in our own lives, and in the world around us? Q'uo begins, as they so often do, in the dark, because the preparation for light is everything.

The beginning of spiritual learning, they say, is always in darkness. This is quite necessary, for much ground must be laid within that darkness. The seed does its first work underground, in the cold, where nothing can be seen. And they draw the parallel to the season itself. Many of your peoples celebrate a resurrection of that which was dead and is now alive, and the placing of that celebration in spring is peculiarly apt, coinciding not with the rhythms of created mankind but with those restless rhythms of moon and tide, of earth and the dark heart of the womb. Now is the time when that which has been in the womb, whether seed or embryo or spirit, has the opportunity to respond to the enlarging of the light.

And then they say the sentence I have been carrying around since I read it. The pain of change feels like a death. The releasing of old opinion feels mortal. And the wound of leaving behind old ways of thought is fell and fatal. There is literal truth in death and resurrection in terms of the spirit. There must be the willingness to die to the old in order for that which is written already upon your heart to become visible, to become illuminated, to be in the light. Even when the old was a rending and separating truth, even when the new is gentler and sweeter, the death of the old is very hard to bear. And we do not wish to quibble, they say, with how hard it is.

I want to pause there, because I think that is the permission many of us need. If you are in the middle of outgrowing a life, a belief, a version of yourself, and it hurts out of all proportion to what is actually happening, Q'uo is telling you that the proportion is correct. It is a death. Treat it like one. Grieve it. Do not rush the burial.

The session turns to the one known as Jesus, who deliberately walked into utter darkness, to Jerusalem, to Golgotha, to a death that for all he could prove had no end. And the key he left, Q'uo says, the key to moving from darkness to light, was given in his words about those who crucified him. Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do. The key to using the light is forgiveness, mercy, charity, love. One may walk into the light and yet not see light, they say. One can move through an entire beautiful day and see no light, walk into one's own season of blossom and yet not blossom, if the heart is closed. Think of the roots in winter, contracted and curled inward, seeking nutriment and not finding it. Then light comes, and the decision is made to let go of all things save the reaching toward that light. There is expansion. There is the opening of the heart with these magic words. I forgive.

There is a lovely, human moment in the middle of the session I have to tell you about. The instrument blocks on a concept she does not personally know, and Q'uo asks the whole circle to re-tune by singing. And they all sing, together, Row, Row, Row Your Boat. Then Q'uo continues, gently, finding another way to say what needed saying. That the enjoyment of the good times has its basis in the enjoyment of the dark times. How precious it is when entities can gaze upon their pain and enter into the darkness without fear, knowing that all is illusion, knowing that both dark and light are useful, knowing that there is no place that the light is not.

And they close with a cosmology that takes my breath away every time. Each time the Creator flings out of its vast potentiality those sparks of being that have become each of you, it receives at the end of that journey such a gift of whole and integrated consciousness that to the infinite riches of creation are added infinite richness more. The gift of that journey is a perfect gift, a gift of love, that which has been reflected from love reflecting at last to love, becoming one again in that sweetness of unity in which all sense is lost.

So tonight, if you are underground, in the dark heart of the womb of whatever is next, do not curse the darkness. It is laying the groundwork. The light is lengthening. And when it comes, the only decision you need to make is the oldest one. Let go of everything, save the reaching toward the light. Say the magic words. I forgive. And rise.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Highway of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the highway of love.

This session comes from an April evening in nineteen ninety-five, and the question comes from travelers in the most literal sense, people writing in from various corners of the planet. How do you be a journeyer? How do you make decisions on the road, outwardly and inwardly? How do you stay open to the inspiration of the moment so that you actually arrive where you are going? Q'uo's answer is one of the most practical and most comforting in the archive.

They begin with the itch. When one has come to the end of a pattern and feels that itch to move, they say, it is salutary both to honor that impulse and to use it as a point of reflection. And the method they recommend is beautifully un-modern. Sit with the awareness of ending. Do not try to figure anything out. Do not break the situation into logical parts. Allow it into the full eyeshot of mind and heart and simply be with it. For the things you need to know in order to be graceful with transformation are learned in the silence that holds the Creator's voice. Perhaps nothing seems to happen, and then comes a dream, or a vision, or you simply wake up knowing what will balance the past and let you walk toward the new horizon.

I love that they do not pretend the road is smooth. In the process of transformation, they say, there is almost always a great deal of sorrow and feelings of loss, for when change comes naturally it simply takes you as destiny will, and it is almost never a completely smooth road from the way that was to the way that has yet to be worked out. And yet they encourage you to have the faith to praise that which is past, every experience that created perhaps much pain and suffering, and to open the heart to that which is, was, and shall be.

The daily practice they recommend is the keeping of silence, the keeping of the listening ear, as part of the ordinary round. In the silence, in the listening, lies the key that unlocks the door of your own wisdom. If you can trust destiny enough to release the attempt to control it, the natural waves of energy moving out from the center of that kindly destiny will gradually take you upon the path and in the direction deeply desired. It is not that your life was predestined, they say, but that certain things were chosen by you, certain patterns, to focus on certain lessons concerning love. No one else has your path. No one else has your lessons. Each pilgrim walking this highway is walking alone in a very deep sense.

And yet, and this is the turn I want you to hold, after meditation the most important resource upon the spiritual path is the company of those who are also seeking. One person cannot give itself the truth, yet the truth is in all, and entities may be instruments through which truth travels to others. You cannot offer yourself enlightenment, but you can become a channel so transparent that love itself shines through you for others to see. And your own poor opinion of yourself, for you are so into self-judgment, has no bearing on how other seekers perceive the light that comes through you. You are simply the bowl in which the precious gift is offered.

There is a line near the end I want to give you as a pocket prayer for the road. If you feel you are moving too fast, or in the wrong direction, stop, take a deep breath, and say to yourself, There are no mistakes. My lessons will come no matter what I do. My service will come no matter what I do. Say it and know it, they say, and then let your hearts be merry and full of praise and thanksgiving, and let your arms reach out to the pilgrims that come your way upon this highway of love.

The questions that follow touch on weather and wind, on whether those we love who have died can hear us when we speak to them, and Q'uo answers gently that the pathways between hearts stay intact, like one portion of a body speaking to another. If you are carrying grief tonight, or missing someone who has gone ahead on the road, let that image hold you. And if the missing feels heavy beyond what images can lift, reach toward the living ones who love you, and do not carry it alone. There is real comfort to be found, and real help, among the fellow travelers still walking beside you.

So tonight, traveler, wherever your crossroads is, honor the itch, sit in the silence, trust the kindly destiny, and keep your arms open for the pilgrims. There are no mistakes. The highway is love, and it runs in both directions, and you are already on it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Beautiful, Terrible Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: beautiful, terrible love.

This session comes from a May evening in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is about the darker side. That part of us that feels unknown and mysterious, sometimes fearful or destructive, angry, jealous, full of rage or doubt. What is it for? Can we become friends with it? Does it have a purpose in our spiritual evolution, or is it simply the enemy? Q'uo answers with a metaphor, a cosmology, and one of the most startling sentences in the archive.

The metaphor first. Imagine, they say, that the Creator goes to sleep, and dreams. And in that dream are peopled all those centers of light we call beings, or souls. In a dream, the instrument feels, all the characters are actually herself, and Q'uo agrees. In the dream you call incarnational life, all the characters are indeed the same. They are the Creator. For it is the Creator's dream you see, and each of you is a distorted fancy teaching the Creator about Itself. The illusion, they say, is intended to be a thick soup of confusion, and they encourage each of you to drink as heartily as you can, with good appetite.

And then the startling sentence. That which you have called the dark side, they say, is the hero, or perhaps we should say the anti-hero, of the play. For of all the characters within, it is the villain that places the soul in the situation into which faith may come and be the deliverer, and hope the handmaiden of that deliverance. I love that line, and I want to turn it over slowly. The darkness in you is not a mistake in the casting. It is the role that makes the story possible. Without the villain, there is nothing for faith to deliver you from, and faith never gets its entrance.

Listen to how they unmake the whole idea of sides. You label the sweet and sunny side of personality as the good side, and the bad-tempered and ugly and mean as the dark side. This is an illusion, they say. That which is truly negative is not those angers or frustrations or sorrows, but rather how the entity chooses consciously to express them. All of those feeling states are equally beautiful to the Creator. They are pure expressions of a self that is universal, and that universal self contains every duality, in every level, in every way that anyone has ever dreamt. How full you are, they say. How complete and whole.

The counsel that follows is precise and practical. You do not have to like your dark side, they say. We do not encourage that. What we encourage is a continuing desire to know the truth, and a constant willingness to separate, when thinking of the self or another, the beingness of a dark impulse from the choices made in expressing it. Ask yourself instead, they say, how shall I choose to express these emotions? For each entity has them all, no matter how pervasive the effort to repress and deny them. Inwardly, forgive and forget, taking only the learning and leaving behind the husk of self that was shed in the learning. And as the self becomes smaller, the inner power of the self shall grow, for with each name which you cease to call yourself, more love may move through that lighter being.

And then Q'uo says the thing that gives this episode its title, and I will give it to you whole. Love is often seen by your people to be a pallid emotion, not romantic, not possessive, and so forth. Yet we say to you that love is a beautiful and terrible thing. Out of love the Creator manifested this illusion. And out of love this illusion must end. Out of love one of your young is conceived, and in great pain oftentimes is given the chance to breathe and to die. But within that theater of incarnational life lies the opportunity in every breath to know the truth and to turn to the one infinite Creator and become one with that love and that light which is divine.

They close with an image I will carry for a long time. When the seeker allows itself time to learn the rhythms of the present dance, incarnational life begins to wake up within the illusion, and the life within pokes its little head out, like a tiny chick emerging from the shell, and says, Remember me. I am you, and I have lived forever, and I will forever live, and I am everything, every emotion, every state of mind, and all of these things are love. All of these things are love. Even the dark ones. Especially the dark ones, for they are the ones that taught you how to choose.

So tonight, do not flinch from the villain in your own play. Honor it. Learn its lines. And then choose, scene by scene, how you will play your part. The audience of one is watching with enormous and unending compassion, and applauding every time you choose love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Strive Without Striving
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: strive without striving.

This session comes from a May afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is one that quietly torments every sincere seeker. What do you do with the gap between your ideals and your actual life? Between the person you mean to be and the person who showed up today? The circle asks for the most efficient way of looking at that difference. Q'uo speaks first, at length, and then a rarer voice closes the session, Oxal, who has something to add that reframes everything.

Q'uo begins with the judging mind itself. It is only natural, they say, that there would be judgment turned toward the self, that distance would be seen between ideal and actual. Yet the truth is neither with the judge nor with the one who refrains from judging, but rather the truth lies ineffably in the present moment. And then they attempt the impossible, to describe that moment. If you can conceive of the present as full of light, full to bursting with all that ever has been or ever will be, this moment of delight, this is the closest we have come to a knowledge of reality. No time, no space, no judgment, but pure white light, a naked manifestation of love.

But here is the catch, and it is a merciful one. The door into this present moment, they say, is locked fast against those who would judge the self or others in such a way as to injure or harm. For a judgment is in many cases an injury, whether inflicted upon the self or upon another. Each within incarnation is a bruised reed, a wounded and fragile living being, and to place the burden of unflinching judgment upon such a precariously alive creature is a cruelty. I want to say that again. To place the burden of unflinching judgment upon such a precariously alive creature is a cruelty. If you have been doing that to yourself, Q'uo is asking you, gently, to stop.

What then, instead of judgment? Praise. Wisdom, they believe, lies not in examining the distance between ideal and actual, but in turning to the light and abandoning judgment for praise of the one infinite Creator. For you are equally praiseworthy, they say, when you have achieved the ideal and when you have utterly failed to achieve the ideal. Equally praiseworthy. Let that land. The scoreboard you have been keeping was never the point. Honor your ideals, they say, and honor yourself as you seek to come close to them. But know that the actual virtue lies in doing what is in front of your face, with gladness, with a single mind, and with a light heart.

There is a poem quoted in the session that I want to pass along, because Q'uo clearly cherishes it. Run the straight race with God's good grace. Lift up thine eyes and seek His face. Lay hold on life and it shall be thy joy and crown eternally. Lift up your eyes. That is the whole instruction. Not down at the scorecard, but up at the face of love.

And then Oxal speaks, briefly, through another instrument, and it is worth the whole session. Oxal says they are ones who have traveled long in the ways of wisdom, using judgment as a tool, refining and refining, until the pathways came full circle and left them with paradox instead of accomplishment. It was compassion that won them access to the worlds they explored. And only when they saw that their wisdoms were so much dust and straw did they turn to those like Ra, who had found a way beyond wisdom to a compassion which is a healing. We ourselves seek this healing, Oxal says. And then the phrase I have chosen for our title. We have begun to learn, they say, to strive without striving.

Q'uo returns to close, and their final words are the ones I want to leave you with tonight. You are loved, they say, not because you have achieved, but because you exist, a child of the infinite Creator. You are enfolded, snuggled, by invisible nurturing arms. Every cell of your body is perfect. Your truth is that all is perfect. There is no striving necessary, for all is well. All that you see and know and do is done upon holy ground. That is the floor beneath the scenery.

So tonight, put down the measuring stick. Lift up your eyes. Do what is in front of you with gladness and a light heart, and strive, if you must strive, without striving. The ground beneath the scenery is holy, and you are standing on it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Passive Learning
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: passive learning.

This session comes from a May afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is beautifully simple. How does learning actually happen for humans? Especially for a seeker of truth, can it happen in a positive way, and can paying attention to it help? Q'uo answers with a model of the mind that I have found genuinely useful, and a defense of the quietest practice there is.

They begin with an image. The being that you are, they say, is like a two-story building with many basements. The top story is consciousness. The first floor is mind, or brain. And the basements, several of them, belong some to the brain and some to consciousness, all to the blending of the two. And the crucial point is that consciousness learns in a different way than the mind learns. The mind learns by accretion of detail, by repetition, by sequence. First one, then two, then three. Touch the hot stove once and the lesson is seated before the recoil finishes. The mind avoids pain, seeks comfort, tries to make sense of randomness, and rebels like a stalled computer when nothing computes.

Consciousness learns differently. It does not learn the facts. It harvests the net results of what the mind goes through. Within consciousness reside what Q'uo calls archetypes of meaning, and the learning of consciousness happens through the harvest of emotion and insight, purified by the fire of experience. Usually, they say, it takes a great deal of experience to affect consciousness at all. The mind is quick and noisy. Consciousness is slow and deep. And here is the image I want you to keep. Consciousness itself is the elephant which many people touch but cannot see. To one who touches the trunk it is a long and snaky thing. To one who touches the ear it is a big flapping thing. There is only one elephant, but there are many places to touch it.

So how do you help the process? Q'uo's answer, as always, is meditation, but they give it a new frame that I love. When the desire to remain silent has been potentiated by action, when you physically sit down and become silent within, a metaprogram immediately and automatically starts. A connection is made with a source outside the capabilities of the mind. The instrument had just discovered electronic mail and the internet, and Q'uo borrows the image. Meditation is like being able to access the internet from your own computer, instantly in touch with global resources. The mind is local. Consciousness is universal. Every time you sit in silence, you have accessed universal mind, racial memory, archetypal structures. There is suddenly no end to the resources available.

And then they give a name to what happens in that silence, and it is our title tonight. One of the circle had asked about passive learning, and Q'uo says yes, this is it. Meditation is passive learning. Tabernacling with the one infinite Creator is passive learning. It is the learning from listening to the voice one cannot hear, which answers questions which one cannot ask. The process cannot be known, and cannot come into consciousness in the local sense, yet the learning is there. And the strength of spirit and will which comes from this learning is helpful.

I find that enormously freeing, because it means the sittings that feel like nothing are not nothing. Q'uo says it directly. Each entity shall, though always feeling that their meditations are no good, yet still experience that balancing and lengthening of the point of view which occurs when one has the universal perspective as opposed to the local perspective. Your meditation does not have to feel good to be working. It only has to happen.

The session closes with a small exchange I want to include, because it is about you. One of the circle describes an image of a blank piece of paper on which he would begin to sketch, as a picture of learning during a life. And Q'uo answers that as you continue seeking, the picture of your journey will become more defined, with color, with breadth of emotion and inspiration, until the colors become more life-filled rather than life-like, with a glow and depth that keeps growing with the seeker. That is what is happening, quietly, every time you sit down and do nothing, on purpose, in the direction of the infinite.

So tonight, if you have been wondering whether your quiet practice is doing anything, Q'uo's answer is yes. The elephant is being touched. The harvest is being gathered. The learning you cannot feel is the deepest learning there is.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Eternal Student
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the eternal student.

This session comes from a September afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, after a summer with no formal meetings, and the question has a delightful cheekiness to it. When we try to be of service to others, are we doing anything other than working on ourselves? Is there any way of serving others except by providing catalyst, which life would provide them anyway? What is our role, really? Q'uo receives the question with evident pleasure, and calls it what it is, a paradox, and a sign. When one runs headlong into a paradox, they say, one has a kind of sign that, yes, this is spiritual work.

Their answer begins with the teacher, because the teacher is the clearest case. Wise is the teacher who waits for the student to ask, they say, for what the teacher essentially is for the student is a kind of catalyst that bears a weight, a heaviness, a bottom, which balances and steadies the point of delivery. When the student perceives a teacher and gives weight to the teacher's words, a stable connection is made. The student opens. The teacher shares carefully. That is the advantage of intending to teach. The disadvantage is expectations, on both sides, which can block teacher and student from noticing all that is actually transpiring. Directions can be missed.

And then Q'uo says the thing I most want you to hear, because it unmakes our whole picture of what teaching is. Within third density it is generally perceived that the teacher teaches a subject. But students are well aware, whether teachers are or not, that a great deal, sometimes a majority, of what a teacher brings is not the subject being taught. Teachers teach first of all by who they are, and how they allow entities to come within their gates of acceptance. The teachers whose teachings affect students most are those who allow the students to learn the teacher as a being, as well as the teaching. For each entity presents a certain complex of vibrations to the world, and those fundamental vibrations are as clearly perceived by a student as the words spoken.

I love that line. As clearly perceived as the words spoken. Every one of us has sat in a classroom, or a meeting, or a kitchen, and learned more from who someone was than from anything they said. Q'uo is telling us that is not a failure of the lesson. It is the lesson. This beingness, this way of living and presenting the self, is a catalyst to the student on a deeper level than the subject matter. And this is each entity's gift to give the world, this way of living that allows the world to see into the self.

So what is the answer to the original question? Are we ever doing anything but working on ourselves? Q'uo's answer is yes, and also, at the deepest level, there is only one self, only one Creator, and all centers of consciousness alike work upon the self, for what is not the self? Both are true. Teaching is possible. You are doing more than teaching yourself. And the one you are teaching is, in the end, yourself. That is the paradox, and paradox is the sign you are doing spiritual work.

The ideal they describe is beautiful, and I will give it to you as a picture to carry. The ideal between teacher and student is a union wherein each shares what each has brought, and the other listens in a way that does not distort, and together there is the plaiting of one strand of thought with another and another, in a rope of new connections and new facets. This is the teaching that gives both new strength, and a continuing desire for more.

And the closing counsel is for all of us, teachers or not. Everything springs from your beingness, they say, so the first career of any seeker is that career of one who seeks to live devotionally throughout a lifetime. In terms of students and teachers, this dedication makes one the eternal student and the eternal teacher. Again, the paradox. Truth is new every day, they say, and there is always the way not yet found, waiting for the one who wishes to sing a new song. Truth is never exhausted, and teachers shall never be unemployed.

So tonight, do not worry about whether you are qualified to teach, or whether your service counts. Tend to your beingness. Live the devotion. The students are already watching, the way students always watch, learning the teacher far more closely than the lesson. And somewhere, in someone else's beingness, you are the student, watching just as closely. The rope is being plaited, strand by strand, and it holds.

Thank you for listening.

title: Disorganized Prayer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: disorganized prayer.

This session comes from a September afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is about two of the most familiar companions in human life. Worry and fear. What is their relation to faith? Can you create faith, or must you wait for it like a gift, like grace? And does worry ever help, by giving us the push to protect ourselves? Q'uo's answer is practical, psychological, and quietly radical, and it contains a definition of worry I have never forgotten.

They begin by refusing to condemn worry outright. The worry and fear that move through the awareness of seekers, they say, is not so much a mistake as that which reacts rather than responds. And in developing faith, the lesson of responding rather than reacting is key. Worry can be foolish and mean nothing, but it can also be wisdom or intuition sensing a real need for concern. The entity who worries the house is not shut properly will check the locks and turn off the lights. Worry gets its bad name, they say, because entities do not ask the central question. Is there anything in this concern that lies within my control? When no avenue of action is open, worry has no function in the outer life. Its function then is inner. It moves you off center, removes your peace, and sets up catalyst. And that, they say, is useful too. It focuses the mind on the point of inner distress.

And then the definition. The question was asked, what can you do instead of worrying? And Q'uo answers, worry is disorganized and random prayer. I want to let that sit. Worry is disorganized and random prayer. The deepest inner dialogue is with the great Self that overarches and undergirds all that is. Worries and fears do register with the infinite One, as cries of distress. But the energy of worrying is tangled and mazed, and the Creator, though always reaching within to comfort, simply cannot move through the tangle that has stopped the inner hearing. So the one who worries may also be one who prays. Same energy. Same reaching. Organized.

Now to faith. Can it be created? Q'uo says faith, when first chosen as a way of living, is nothing more than a leap into space. Faith creates itself in mid-air, when the will of the seeker has been surrendered. That first leap could be nothing more than a conscious decision, a promise to the self. I will live by faith. And each time the seeker finds itself mired in useless cyclical worry, the affirmation may be repeated. I will live by faith. Sooner or later, they say, the repetition breeds a new and positive habit of mind, and there comes a moment when the seeker skips the usual worry and is inspired spontaneously to affirm it. That moment of peace, they say, is as precious as your rare metals, and should be stored carefully in a special part of the memory, that memory that lies just behind the surface of things.

I love the honesty of what follows. Faith does become a habit, they say, and in pleasant seasons you may rest in the peace which passes understanding. But in the natural cycle of light and dark, there will be times when there is no comfort and no spontaneous feeling of faith. Then the wise seeker is content to live upon the bare memory of those glad times when the spirit was high and faith flowed like water. These memories are true, they say, and they are as the talisman that protects the entity suffering through change, even though no sense of faith remains. Keep the talismans. You will need them. That is what they are for.

And the practices that connect the deep faith to the conscious mind are the simple ones. Regular meditation, for in the silence connections from the deep mind are being made and information is flowing. And the encouragement within the self of praise and thanksgiving, for all things, large and small. Prayer, praise and thanksgiving, they say, are three resources that strengthen the connection to faith. Not complicated. Not secret. Just repeated.

So tonight, the next time you catch yourself worrying, try hearing it differently. Underneath the tangle is a prayer trying to get out. Untie one knot. Turn the worry into a question you can act on, or turn it into a prayer you can release. Say the small promise. I will live by faith. Say it until you mean it. Say it until you do not have to say it anymore, because it has become the way you meet the day.

Thank you for listening.

title: Spun of Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: spun of light.

This session comes from a September afternoon in nineteen ninety-five, and the question is about wisdom. What part does wisdom play in the life of a seeker trying to learn compassion and forgiveness and mercy? Can we inform our actions with it? What is wisdom, here, in this density? Q'uo's answer begins by taking the word apart, and ends by putting it back together as something you can hold.

They begin with a provocation. There is a sense, they say, in which wisdom is a term describing an illusion within your density, for the concept of wisdom implies a right or correct way of thinking or acting. And in the spiritual search there is often no correct solution. The tendency of the rational mind to search for correct solutions can sometimes lead the seeker astray. Then they give the image I want you to see. The wisdom of the world is like a housekeeper of the house of light, each kind of thought with its own room, its own shelf, its own closet. The wise man, in the world's eyes, is the one whose house stands before the blast of random circumstance, able to take new information and remodel so the new furniture fits with the old.

It is a fine house, they say, and they do not despise it. A seeker whose worldly house of logic is untended shall have unnecessary difficulties. But it reaches to the limits of the spiritual walk and not beyond them. For in the world of spirit there is a far colder kind of wisdom. It is the wisdom of one who gazes upon illusion and is able to see through the illusion to the mystery. And here is the line that stopped me cold. The spiritual wise man is first the world's fool. That ability to gaze at the richness and fullness of life and see its vanity is infinite, is the beginning of spiritual wisdom. To see the feast and know it is a shadow. To hold the prize and feel its lightness. That is where it starts.

So what does spiritual wisdom look like, in practice? Q'uo gives a series of reflections, like faces seen in passing, and I will walk you through them slowly. One reflection is the seeker in inner listening, in meditation or prayer, surrendering the capable worldly mind and taking up instead the silent mystery. One may see wisdom in the one who opens the hand and releases some necessity, letting it go, placing the feet solidly in the mid-air of faith alone. One may see it shining from the face of one who leaves good times and good company to be of service to one who is lost and has asked for aid. One may see it in the one who lays hold of some infinite virtue and stands unafraid, submitting to whatever the world wishes to do. The key to spiritual wisdom, they say, is a kind of seeing.

And then they describe the eyes that do the seeing. Each seeker has a nascent inner vision, the eyes of the spiritual body, wonderfully created, but dormant until the seeker wakes to the spiritual walk. And like all infants, that inner eyesight is at first unfocused and untaught. As it gains experience, it learns that worldly sight can tell lies if it is taken for spiritual sight. The spiritual self looks at a situation where all the things of the world are had in plenty, and sees the imbalances and hungers just below the surface. The spiritual eye sees the riches of the world as poverty, and the naked and vulnerable spirit in all its poverty as riches. To that eye, death and limitation and catastrophe are not necessarily bad things. The riches lie in every circumstance, those perceived as negative perhaps more than those perceived as positive.

Strictly speaking, they say, wisdom is a null word within third density. If it is striven for, the result is only clearer sight, still full of distortion. In a non-relative sense, wisdom is to be embodied rather than contained in the mind. And then the sentence that gathers the whole session. The prelude to spiritual wisdom is surrender. If you burn to be truly wise, they say, then focus upon that burning, that yearning desire. Seek to penetrate the mystery. Ache and reach for the heart of truth. To the extent you have purified that desire, you have embodied wisdom such as it can be in your illusion.

They close with a cosmology in a single breath. Wisdom builds the house of thought within which one may think upon the mystery. Love is the only quality that can fill that form and create out of emptiness all that there is, in its rejoicing, exulting splendor. And beyond all seeking for light and knowledge there lies the golden, living, ever-penetrating fact of love. Your form is spun of light, they say. Your nature of love. Spun of light. Made of love. That is what the wise man finally sees, when the house is in order and the eyes are open. Himself, and everyone, exactly as they are.

Thank you for listening.

title: Desire Without Pride
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: desire without pride.

This is late September of nineteen ninety five, and the question laid before Q'uo is an old one, the kind the great religions have been turning over for centuries. If desire is what ties us to this world, should the seeker drop every desire and let them all go?

Q'uo begins by refusing the simple answer. Desire, they say, is the fuel that runs the engine of your illusion, both the portion which is shadow and that portion which is form. To be a self, set apart from what is not the self, is already to want. You want oxygen, because the blood needs it to live. Nobody would call that unwise. The hunger and thirst for truth, for love, for beauty, these are not mistakes. They are the breath of life itself for the evolving spirit.

But there is something that hides inside our wanting, and it is this that Q'uo spends the evening unpacking. They call it the will, or the self-will, or simply pride. Each of us has felt it, that energy of willing something to be so, or not to be so, of insisting that we know the way things should go. Pride takes a natural desire and puffs it up, the way, in their striking image, a cancer takes over natural cells and multiplies them without stint. Growth is an excellent thing. A tumor is not.

I love that line, because it makes the work so concrete. You do not have to stop desiring. You have to keep an eye on the pride that stirs inside the desiring. When a want comes forward, gaze at it. Is there something in it that insists it is the holder of the keys to righteousness? Little by little, to the increasingly quiet mind, pride becomes easier to spot, and the emotions connected with impure desire become more transparent to the eye and the ear and the heart.

And then Q'uo says something that always stops me. They say that desire is not only human. The Creator Itself is expressing desire, else we, you, and all would not exist. The desire to know the self is that which launched the universe in all of its infinity. Every tiny mote of consciousness in the infinite creation is loved, desired, and manifested because of that desire. So the religions that counsel the total cessation of desire are not exactly wrong. To relinquish desire is to relinquish discomfort, and there is a valid path there. But it is a simplistic solution to a question that has an infinity of paths, all leading to the same one original and central Logos.

Within this density, Q'uo suggests, most of us will not find the path of self-effacement to be the available one. Our work is different. It is to take what is natural and refine it. The desire for friends and companionship can be examined until it is no longer the desire for company that feeds the self, but purely the hope to serve a beloved other self. That is the stripping work, done desire by desire, year after year.

When the questions open up, someone asks about a difficult relationship with a fellow worker, someone who seems to want to serve but whose will keeps getting in the way. Q'uo's answer is gentle and unflinching at once. They say the most important point is that you desire to serve without imposing your will on any, even though another may attempt to impose theirs on you. Hew to the higher road. Cast your bread upon the water, as your holy works put it, and let the outcome be what it is.

Another questioner asks whether pride is the same thing as the ego. Q'uo says the two terms are basically interchangeable, each an illustration of an entity who wishes to impose its own will or desires on those about it, not seeing the larger picture. But they add something worth keeping. The careful attention we turn upon our own inner life, which can look so self-involved, is not itself pride. It is the tempering of steel. The information is used only to temper the character of the seeker, and never to impose that character upon another.

Q'uo closes with an image that has stayed with me. There is a spiritual child within, they say, young and clumsy and awkward, feeling so much love and yearning. Comfort it. Succor it. Cherish it. And when you are faced with what you do not desire, open the hand and say, here is all I feel. Teach me what is the pure desire, and what is the husk and chaff of pride.

So the instruction is not to stop wanting. It is to want cleanly, to let the fire of catalyst burn away the pride of self, and to trust that somewhere in the home of clear and lucid desire, there is peace.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Music Behind the Notes
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the music behind the notes.

The first Sunday of October, nineteen ninety five, finds the group out in the country, with the birds and the trees and the stream running wild, and the question they bring to Q'uo is a tender one. How do you balance the light touch with being a serious student of your own catalyst? What is it about laughter that heals?

Q'uo begins with an image that carries the whole evening. Think of the student learning to play the piano. The beginner does the scales, over and over and over, and it is effortful, heavy work. But as the years of apprenticeship pass, the student begins to hear in a different way, with an expanded awareness of the whole. The true instrumentalist, Q'uo says, plays not the notes but the music.

And this is the seeker exactly. The seeker has a craft to learn, and there are scales that must be played again and again. There are scales which teach the notes of patience. There are scales which teach the notes of devotion. There are exercises that teach the spareness and reserve of true service. To those who feel they are too serious, too solemn, too earnest, Q'uo says this is the stage where the basic work gets done. The earnest self is a lovable, respectable, acceptable self. It is simply the stage where effort is made, and it seems heavy, and lonely, and sometimes empty.

But there comes a moment, for every sincere student, when the soul begins to yearn for something beyond the scales. The universe changes, and it begins to spark into a life that was hitherto unseen, for the soul and the heart are expanding. And the center is no longer only that place in the heart where you opened the door to love. It expands to make a center of the whole creation, with all included and nothing omitted, nothing irrelevant, nothing wrong, but all one shade or shadow or another of infinite love.

So how does the tight, weary, over-serious student find the light touch again? Q'uo offers a question that this instrument was fond of asking. Will this matter in ten thousand years? Most of what disturbs the student will not. And that realization is the key that unlocks the corset of tightness and lets the student expand, opening simply to enjoy the breeze, expanding as a flower in sunlight, turning to the sun.

Then Q'uo describes what is actually happening, energetically, when we laugh. The light touch, they say, is a mixture of the green-ray energy center being full and open, the blue-ray center working in self-expression, and the lower three centers agreeing to lessen or cease their demands. It is not a denial of the lower energies. It is the lower self agreeing to rest for a moment so that the heart can open and speak with the mystery.

Some people have a gift for this. They are the ones who say just the right thing to break the ice. But for most of us, Q'uo says, the skill of asking the self to stop and open to a larger view must be learned as any habit is learned. You oof and grunt and try, and find it hard to do. Continue to oof and grunt, they say. This is good work. At some point your own self will begin to yearn for the stoppage of that earnestness, and will begin to hunger for the music behind the notes of the devotional life.

And here is the part that unhooks the whole trap of self-judgment. You are not repeating your lessons, they say, when the same hard material comes around again and cramps your style. You are learning it at another level of subtlety and profundity. There is no coasting. The Creator and your higher self hope to learn as many depths and resonances of the lessons you came to learn as time permits.

So take the perpendicular route out of the little circle walked by the earnest soul. Take time out for a laugh or a smile, with all compassion for that earnest toiler who truly wishes to learn and to be better, wiser, and more loving than before. Those wishes are reflections of something so precious within you that there are no words for the gemlike quality of this crystalline heart of self that is the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: One Step Further
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: one step further.

This is October of nineteen ninety five, an intensive meditation evening, and the voice speaking is Laitos, one of the quieter members of the Confederation. Tonight is not a night for grand teachings. It is a night for the patient, homely work of learning to channel, and Laitos is working with a new instrument, one known as K, who has only just begun to speak their thoughts aloud.

Laitos begins with encouragement that applies to every beginner at anything, not only channeling. They do not wish to rush any new instrument past the point of confidence, yet they shall always provide the opportunity for a new instrument to continue to expand its abilities. This is true for all instruments, in fact, they say. Even the one who has practiced the art for many years is always being offered concepts of greater scope, greater intricacy, though not, they are careful to add, greater complexity.

Then they turn to the new instrument directly, with the kind of gentle coaching that tells you everything about how the Confederation works. They offer a conditioning vibration, and they remind K that they are happy to adjust it if it is not comfortable. And they give the one instruction that matters most in this art. Refrain from analysis. Speak the concepts that appear within the mind, and do not stand aside to judge them.

When K's turn comes, only a few broken phrases make it through. The recording is ragged with inaudible gaps. And Laitos is delighted. They are very pleased with the progress which K has made since the last session, and they continue to applaud this new instrument's efforts and willingness to take one further step, and to move yet further upon the limb which continues to hold this instrument firmly. I love that image, the limb that holds you even as you step further out on it.

When there are no questions, Laitos does not take it as a failure. They say they are always happy when there are queries, for queries open new avenues of thought. But they are also pleased when there are none, for in that situation they may assume that what was offered has been utilized to its fullest and is ready for further expansion.

At the very end, through K's faltering new contact, comes a message that feels like it was meant for all of us, not only the group in the room. We wish to make known to you that there is progress being made even though you may not feel it at this time. And then the simplest invitation. Take part in the continuing adventure which is the Creator. Rejoice with us, for it is a merry life if you choose it to be.

There is something deeply encouraging about a session where almost nothing is said, and yet everything is said. The work is the work. One more step, taken without analysis, on the limb that holds you firmly.

Thank you for listening.

title: Like the Oak
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: like the oak.

The evening after the session we just heard, Laitos returns to continue working with the new instrument, and this time the teaching widens out from the craft of channeling into the nature of service itself. The image they choose is one of the most beautiful in the whole archive.

Each of you as a vocal instrument, Laitos says, may be likened to the oak, providing a rest, and more, perhaps an inspiration to travelers upon the spiritual journey who come within the reach of your branches. Think of it. The oak begins as modestly as any seed. But it grows into a great spreading tree, and many are the travelers that pass beneath it. On a hot day, after a long journey, a traveler may rest at the base of the trunk, reclining in the shade of the great spreading limbs and leaves. The traveler chooses where to seek shelter. The tree's only job is to be there.

I love that line, because it quietly reframes everything about service. The oak does not provide oranges or apples, Laitos says, but provides shade and rest and a calming effect that is its own to provide. You are not asked to be everything. You are asked to give what you have to give, and to give it freely. This is the essence of the experience, that the desire to serve others is strong, and that there is the ability to hollow oneself out sufficiently to allow concepts and inspiration to move through the instrument in a free and flowing fashion. And your sharing is most efficient when you give away that which you have, to make room for more to follow.

Then comes a question that many spiritual teachers have wrestled with, and Carla asks it plainly, because she is writing a book on channeling. What about the relationship between performing spiritually oriented services and accepting money?

Laitos does not dodge it. To be of the most efficient polarity in the positive sense, they say, one must be willing to give freely enough of the self that one is not concerned whether there be a return for what is given. One seeks to share that which is greater within the self with all those who are equal to the self. This does not mean refusing gifts that are freely given. The salient point is that such gifts are not sought. To give without expectation of return is the essence. To receive freely offered gifts without feeling the necessity to reciprocate points toward the essence of the journey itself.

When Carla presses further and asks how one should decide how much to charge, Laitos can only answer with questions of their own. How much does one value the ability to serve another? If the information which is freely given is heeded or not, is the price the same? How does one put a price and a limit upon that which has no price and is infinite?

Carla laughs and says they sound as confused as anyone, and Laitos, with real humility, agrees that it is a confusing choice to have to make. But the questions they offered are the answer. When you see the universe as portions of one being, then the boundaries between entities, and the systems of dealing fairly with portions of one entity, are illusions that aid each portion to gather experience.

So be the oak. Give the shade that is yours to give. Do not try to be an orchard. And trust that the travelers who need rest will find your branches.

Thank you for listening.

title: Companions on the Way
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: companions on the way.

Mid October of nineteen ninety five. The group has been talking about synchronicity, those uncanny meaningful coincidences, and about how growth seems to quicken when people gather together, whether to talk or to meditate or to worship. They want to know how that works. Q'uo is happy to tell them.

They begin with a supposition they hold as basic. The incarnation, even within this thick illusion, is a magical experience. What wakes entities to the magic is the dawning awareness that the deeper self is not a creature of flesh, blood, sinew, and limitation, but a creature of infinity, eternity, and unity with all that there is. That sense of being other than the illusion is the key that turns the lock.

And then comes the heart of the evening. When entities of like mind seek together, Q'uo says, each is a mirror which shows the Creator to the self and the self to the self. Each face that is seen has the wonderful capacity to surprise us with a side of truth that we had not guessed before. As we gaze into each other's eyes, as we touch each other's hearts, we bloom together, and that blossom is taken away by all. Strength added to strength. Weakness shared with weakness. Love in all things, found and felt in ways that do not harm, but rather support.

Why does synchronicity seem to thicken around groups? Because each individual's path is already synchronous with its own destiny, and when the group joins and shares its thoughts and experiences, the commonality of synchronicities becomes remarkable. The group universalizes each entity's unique path, so that instead of being caught within the biases of the long road that led you here, each remains free of the limitations of self. Each has wisdom that becomes available to all.

And Q'uo does not romanticize it past honesty. For the one who has no spiritually oriented group, the path can still be walked, and will still bear fruit. But companions, they say, make the way merrier and the stones smaller, and certainly the smiles more frequent. The exhaustion each may feel over issues worked upon for longer than can be remembered does not have those same biases where another's troubles are concerned. The fresh ear, the new perspective, this is most helpful.

Then Q'uo says the thing that the whole session has been circling. The service each came to perform is simple to speak of and very difficult to make sense of, for each who came to this place at this time came to aid in lightening the consciousness of your planet. And you do this by being here. Not by doing any particular service, such as healing or channeling, but rather by living. Being is your great gift, and your first occupation. It is the hardest job you shall have within your incarnational experience.
