Here are hearts, they say, that wish for you to be who you most deeply are. Here is a home which one need not be at in order to feel at home. The spirit of a spiritual group is enormously powerful, metaphysically speaking, and no individual is the reason. It is the faith of all who have come to such a place, the knowledge that this is a safe place, that makes the power of such a light center. The entities who dwell here simply keep the doors open. Each of you has brought the magic with you.

They close the teaching with an image that feels like a benediction over the whole project. Person by person by person, a net of gold, that gold being love, faith, the desire for that which is higher and more lovely. And each has gone out into the larger world and touched person by person by person, and so the net spreads.

If you have ever wondered why you light up in certain company, Q'uo would say it is no accident. You are each other's mirrors, and the light you see in the other is your own.

Thank you for listening.

title: Breaking the Shell
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: breaking the shell.

Late October of nineteen ninety five, and the group brings Q'uo two large questions. The first is about the strange blend of destiny and free will, the sense that we planned our lives before we came here, and yet we choose freely once we arrive. The second is about the friction between the peoples of the Earth, and whether all the world's religions and cultures could ever be reconciled in peace.

Q'uo starts at the beginning, with how entities come into being. In third density, fresh from second density's turning toward the light, consciousness wakes up with something it never had before. The inward-turning gaze. The awareness of self. And the lesson of this density is the lesson of finding ways to love and to be loved, not only between one person and another, but between groups of people and other groups.

Then they describe the seeker as a rough diamond, with unpolished edges and no sparkling facets yet, and incarnation as the friction that does the polishing. Some of the abrasive experiences of your illusion seem unlucky and unfortunate, they say, yet it is precisely that friction that does the work of exposing the crystal that sparkles within. The seeker stands as a kind of rough diamond, and through lifetime after lifetime the friction of everyday living works to smooth and refine that crystalline self.

And here is where the preincarnative planning comes in. Before incarnation, Q'uo says, the entity creates the scenario, the screenplay, for its personal movie of life. You choose the cast. You choose who shall play mother, father, spouse, lover, friend, enemy. You make agreements with these entities in the finer worlds. No matter how difficult the relationships seem, this was part of your own choice. It may be hard to believe that you would ask yourself to suffer. But from outside the illusion, they say, it seems like child's play, a good kind of playing at that, to plunge into the sea of confusion and swim about in its waters.

They offer a practice for the hard days. Remind yourself that this is part of the play. If you can find faith within yourself, faith that believes and knows that no matter what occurs you are on track and the deeper goals are being met, perhaps that may soften the harshness of the lessons. It is the outworking of the self's plan for this incarnation that is being experienced.

The second question, about the peoples of the Earth, gets one of Q'uo's most tender answers. Each culture, each religion, each philosophy gives its people an identity, a strength, a pride, a purpose. This enlivens the group, and it is helpful in the individuation process. But that great strength can become a weakness when those within the grouping cannot move beyond its boundaries to see a larger identity shared with others. Then the lines divide, and animosity fuels itself.

Yet within each grouping, Q'uo says, there are seeded those far-seeing individuals who can open up new possibilities by their vision. These are the way-showers. And the work of each culture is like the chick inside the egg, pecking at the shell that it might break free and become a greater being. It is often a painful process. But the great healing power of love aids all in it, for all spring from it.

Near the end, Q'uo asks each listener a question to carry into meditation. You are a vessel, they say, a precious, precious vessel. What shall you hold? What shall you offer? We would not ask you to attempt to develop infinite love. We ask only that you open the self, allow pain to hollow you out, and make yourself a beautiful and transparent instrument through which infinite love can flow.

The shell will break. It always does. The question is only whether you will peck from the inside, or wait to be cracked from the outside.

Thank you for listening.

title: Listening Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: listening within.

The last Sunday of October, nineteen ninety five. The group wants to know about the core self, that foundation being they are trying to reach all their lives, and how to find messages from it in dreams and in the quiet. Q'uo's answer is one of the gentlest meditations on meditation in the whole archive.

They begin by naming the core being of all that exists as the one great original Thought, that unit vibration known as Love. This love, they say, is your essential self. And then they point to the skill that matters most for becoming aware of it. To be transparent is the most apt skill that can be created within your practice. Not to achieve, not to produce, but to become see-through to the surrounding illusion, to experience that lightness of being which belongs to pure spirit.

Those moments do come, they say. The most calm and the most busy of times alike offer windows of opportunity wherein suddenly the illusion crystallizes and shimmers, and the transparency of being can be felt. When these moments occur, find time to give praise and thanks for these experiences of a truth that lies within you.

But Q'uo does not want to talk mostly about that ultimate level, because each density has its purpose, and ours is incarnation. So they turn to the way the core self can be met within this life, and they give it a single word. Listening. Within each entity, they say, there lies a country that is a holy high place. This high place exists within a dark continent of the subconscious mind. Into this place comes the seeker who opens the inner ear, and in this place dwells the Creator in fullness and in mystery. And the silent speech of this mystery is food and drink to the eternal self within.

Your holy work known as the Bible talks of the still, small voice, they remind us. We would characterize this voice as that of the spirit within. And then they say the thing that everyone who has ever sat down to meditate needs to hear. Each condemns the self for not meditating well, and yet we say to you that the attempt is all. Be patient and compassionate when looking at the performance of meditation or silent listening, for the errant thoughts that rush through the calm and silent chamber are just the foolish and shallow personality doing what it does.

Your value, they say, depends not one whit upon your crossing off the items on your list. Rather, your value depends upon your vibration. If you are in love with life, if you embrace the present moment, then your core vibration is expressing at its best, at its most harmonious, at its clearest and most lucid. And this is what people receive from you, louder and more impressively often than what you are doing at the time.

And what is this gift you have to give? This is the part that undoes every spiritual inferiority complex at once. Are you thinking that you are not good enough? This nexus of vibratory patterns, Q'uo says, is that which you came to share with this planet so beloved to each of you. This is the gift you have to give to your fellow beings at this time. Yourself.

You came into this heavy, chemical illusion, they say, because you wanted to fall down and go boom, to be a baby and to learn in the illusion, of the illusion, for the illusion. For within this thick forgetting, the choice to give, the choice to make expressions of love especially in the face of a perceived not-love, is precious. Choices made in the darkness, in the absence of knowledge, go very deep. Never again shall you build the foundation of all that is to come.

So when you are listening, know that you are at your most precious time. Listening within is as the key that unlocks the door to that holy ground which is, in truth, in all places, in all times, and in all things.

Thank you for listening.

title: From Head to Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: from head to heart.

The first Sunday of November, nineteen ninety five. The group is asking about one of the oldest puzzles in spiritual life. Why is it that change and new growth so often seem to come out of confusion, pain, and anger? Why do the hardest feelings so often turn out to be the doorway?

Q'uo begins with the nature of the place. Your third-density Earth experience could be said to be of a certain nature or kind, and basic to that nature is duality. The illusion is rich and redundant in its opposites. And this two-sidedness was prepared for a purpose: the using of individual free will to make choices concerning how each wishes to progress.

Then they turn to fear, and the description is so precise it feels like a hand on your shoulder. The child touches the stove and receives a burn. Thereafter the child sees the stove and still finds it attractive, but the mind and the emotions contract about that seeing and keep the child from hurting itself. Fear is not always the villain. Often fear is wisdom. But quite often, the action of fear is counterproductive. That contracting creates a knot, a tangle of the beingness, so that consciousness is narrowed and straightened and limited unnecessarily.

So Q'uo gives a daily practice. Spend time each day reflecting upon those moments when you felt that contracting which fear invokes. Reflect upon whether you have used fear well in the day, or whether in the events of the day fear has used you. When one is unsure, uncertain, tentative, and holding back cautiously, these contracting feelings create a friction, and this friction makes the seeking so vastly uncomfortable. And since there are so many ways a sensitive consciousness can be hurt, it is no wonder that the experiences of living seem to have much pain in them.

But here is the turn. As you came into this incarnation, you were looking forward to the opportunity to enter into the transforming of the self alchemically with great enthusiasm and gusto. The veil of forgetting was not yet in place, and you saw the incredible opportunity to learn and to serve in the name of love. Like all those who are not in the thick of things, you thought it would be easier than it turned out to be. And the times of suffering are those times which give us the gifts of learning.

Q'uo's summary of the whole journey is one sentence long, and it is worth carrying. Your journey is the journey from the head to the heart, from reason to feeling, from rigid structure to rhythmic and flowing structure, from holding to letting go. And paradoxically, as you allow each strand you hold so tightly to be released, you do become more wise as you release fear.

They do not pretend this is easy, and they do not ask you to pretend either. One can feel like a victim. One can feel the weight of all that has been given up, and drown in the hopes that have not happened, and be deafened by one's doubts. And we say to you, they say, that all this is satisfactory. All this is acceptable. For truly you did not come here to be happy. You did not come here to be satisfied. But rather, you came here to work, and to learn, and to serve.

So they ask you to allow yourself to be foolish. To get to know yourself in all of your impulses and little eccentric ways, with a childlike feeling of exploration. To put your arms around yourself within, and give love and support to that pilgrim soul which sails the seas of life, seeking hungrily, yearningly, constantly for that which beckons.

And they give you a morning practice, a door to knock on each day. Good morning. Today I am with the infinite Creator. Today I am love made visible. Today I am. I am. I am.

Thank you for listening.

title: Rest Where You Are
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: rest where you are.

The group is taking potluck in mid November of nineteen ninety five, letting Q'uo speak on whatever seems most needed. And what comes through is a teaching for the weary, for everyone who has ever felt their spiritual energy run low and wondered if something was wrong with them.

Q'uo begins by looking honestly at the room. The vibrations of this group are heavy, they say, with the weariness that is of the spirit rather than of the body. And this, in a group that is often very high in energy, is worth sitting with, for low seasons have much to offer in the way of learning and in increasing the capacity for personal compassion.

When the seeker experiences low energy, they say, it is experiencing a symptom which points deeply into the structure of the manifested being. Spiritual weariness often signifies a time when incarnative life will seem very difficult. Small matters take on a larger aspect. Any small change triggers catalyst far in excess of what the seeker would usually expect of itself. It is a condition of vulnerability, because weariness sensitizes the perceptive web. Small efforts seem to become major. The mind turns from tasks that would normally be easy, seeing them with the jaundiced eye and the discontented heart of the weary seeker.

But here is the part that reframes it completely. The state of low energy, because it increases sensitivity, offers the opportunity to go more deeply within the self, reaching toward those essences that can be called hope, faith, and charity. Into the weakened web of perception can come the most helpful essences, precisely because the surface defenses are down.

So Q'uo asks each of us to gaze upon the weakened self, not with impatience but with, as far as possible, an undismayed peace of mind. For you have come into this illusion to be affected by it. Yours is not the path of evenness and spiritual perfection. Yours is a path full of dimness, confusion, and perceived difficulty. And then they give the instruction that is the heart of the whole session. Say to the self, peace, be still and stay where you are. Abide. Rest. Release the effort to better or improve your situation. Allow the deep self to open into the consciousness, and allow that essence that is the Creator, that is love itself, to minister unto you.

There is no need to thrash or wrestle, they say. There is no need to give sermons to the self. There is no need, in fact, to alter the state you experience. The need is simply to remember love, for all things shall pass but love. Moods shall come and go. Incarnations bloom, wither, and die. Love remains.

Then comes an image to carry into the low seasons. See the self, the consciousness that dwells deep within, as a kind of tree of life. Or perhaps as a vine, for the vine itself, root and branch, is the Creator, and you, each, are a branch off of that vine. By your own free will you graft other things onto that vine, and some grafts take beautifully and some turn sour and bitter. And when the mouth is bitter with the taste of despair, it is difficult to remember that the basic vine is love, and that one needs only to travel back down to the roots to ground the self in the Creator.

In times of difficulty, Q'uo says, goading oneself toward enthusiasm is not their suggestion. Rather, come into a relationship with the momentary self in which that self that is suffering is seen as a child, a child that you can take within the embrace of your own heart and rock and comfort and strengthen. Open the doors of your attention to love, and let that love dwell, beaming and radiating, until that child within is permeated and completely saturated with that love that dwells so perfectly at the center of your being.

Peace, they remind us, is not the removal of all that is not peaceful. Peace within is the fruit of regular, repeated, consistent willingness to experience the self as the self and to regard it with love. Be patient in that work. Be quiet when you try to judge. Remember, and refrain.

Thank you for listening.

title: Dance with the Force
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: dance with the force.

We are in the middle of a remarkable weekend in November of nineteen ninety five, a series of dialogues between Aaron, the Buddhist teacher who speaks through Barbara, and Q'uo, speaking through Carla. The topic the group has chosen is living the devotional life, and the honesty in the room is striking. People are confessing that they take themselves too seriously, that they are angry with themselves for failing again and again, that they get the two by four between the eyes and still do not learn.

Q'uo opens with something worth sitting with. Each seeker sincerely wishes nothing more than to find truth in the self, in the environment, in the thoughts, and in each other. And within the classroom of earthly life, the questions are far, far more important than the answers. The desire, the emotions of yearning and hope, are in themselves more highly to be regarded than any knowledge that can be expressed in words.

Then Aaron takes the microphone, and they reframe the whole subject in a single sentence. Simply to incarnate is a devotional act. It takes tremendous love and courage to move into incarnation. To live the devotional life is not to be rid of fear, but to offer even that fear as part of the devotion, to learn that everything is an expression of the divine, so that the love is found within the fear, for fear is merely a distortion of love.

They offer an image. Be a fish with them, twenty yards down under water. Feel the heaviness, the darkness below. Look up and see the light, the sun seen dimly through water and atmosphere. Now emerge from the water, and at those last inches, suddenly, ah, there it is, the sun. This act of looking through the surface is akin to the spiritual awakening each of you has experienced. But even then, they say, you are seeing at a distance. Then you must go into the heart of the sun. I will be burned up, destroyed, you say. Yes, the small self cannot exist there except as concept. And what do you find? One has to laugh, because you find that you have always been there, that you have never left, that the rest was all illusion.

The practical question is what to do with the ego, the small self that keeps getting in the way. And Aaron is blunt. The doing is not to wage war with the ego, which solidifies the illusion. The work is to bring even the ego self into the divine. You cannot transcend ego until you accept ego. The work is to embrace the ego self so that it becomes transparent, seen as a serviceable tool of the incarnation, worn as a cloak, with no identity in it.

They give the image of the box. Set yourself down inside a closed carton. That is your relative reality. Now poke up the lid with a finger, and raise your head just enough to peer out. Aha. There are a thousand, no, a million, no, ten million or far more cartons which beings inhabit, and around them this infinite space which we call ultimate reality. You can never leave ultimate reality, and so you can never cease living the devotional life.

Q'uo adds the part about self-judgment that so many seekers need. Why is the self so often not an object of devotion? Perhaps because the seeker hears its own thoughts and flinches at the dark side. But you are a whole and completed entity. The illusion presents the night and the day, the dark side and the light side, as the entire globe of your Earth turns again and again. Do not flinch away from the portion of your human nature you perceive as dark.

Q'uo closes the evening with a practice for bedtime, and it is one of the loveliest passages in the archive. As you lay your frail barque of flesh down between the soft, cool sheets of your bed, think on all your attributes and shower them with your affection. Ah, sweet feet and legs that have carried me where I chose to go this day. Ah, dear back, strong, bent under the burdens of the day. Kindly stomach, hard-working heart, sweet tongue spouting such folly. Ah, dear, dear pride, lovely vanity, elegant sloth. Do not fear these attributes. They are yours to command. They are precious, precious gifts.

And then Aaron teaches the pushing hands exercise from Tai Chi. When life pushes at you, you have two choices. Push back, or learn to dance with that force, to absorb it, and when the force releases itself, to take it back. Soften around the resistance, make space for it, and you become able to dance with that which pushes at you, be it internal or external.

The devotional life is not the war against yourself. It is the dance with everything, including yourself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Overflowing Sink
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the overflowing sink.

The morning after the session we just heard, Aaron continues the Aaron and Q'uo dialogues, and they begin with an exercise that everyone in the room will remember for years. Walk into a bathroom with me, they say. Turn on the faucet and watch the water fill the sink. Suddenly it threatens to overflow, and the faucet will not turn off. It turns in only one direction. Quick, gather towels. Mop up the water. Feel the tension building in you. Me against this water. This, they say, is the relative human.

Now I walk into the bathroom, they continue, and pull the plug. Whoosh. The water goes down the drain. Feel the tension relax. Life constantly hands you its barrage of overflowing sinks, of problems to be solved, and your energy contracts into a self that will handle those problems. This, my dear ones, is not devotion. This is control. This is fear.

And here is the subtlety that makes the teaching cut so deep. Even if that sink was above your neighbor's living room, and your desire to stop the water was so no harm would come to your neighbor, if you are meeting the issue with that contraction of fear, you are perpetuating an old pattern which believes the ego self must be in control. In the moment when you symbolically pull the plug, you shift tracks from the fear track to the love track. You come back into harmony. The universe is not throwing mud on you to make you feel small.

If the universe does fling mud on you, Aaron says, in some way you have invited participation in that experience, because the soul sought the experience, sought it because there was a higher area of learning it sought. So the work is not to mop faster. It is to stop, release the tension of the old patterns, and come back to the spacious perspective. Pull the plug, or open the heart, or whatever is appropriate. Nothing against me. To do this over and over and over is to live the devotional life.

Q'uo follows with a practice for the moments of self-judgment that visit every seeker. Visualize the Creator's hand downstretched, open, palm upward, that hand being as tall as you. Into that palm, give the gifts of your humanity. Here is the thing not done. Here is the thing done in error. Here, envy and pride, all the sorry gifts of the undisciplined self. Now look upon these bits of colored stone. To you they were gray, ugly, broken pieces of self, fit only for the trash. Look now and see the beautiful colors of these shards of a life, blessed, accepted, and transfigured by the love of the infinite One.

The conversation turns to a painful and practical matter. One of the group is living with a partner whose anger lands on her as hurt, and she asks how to be with it. Q'uo is honest first. It is appropriate to hurt when negative emotions are directed upon your head. To the spirit it is an opportunity to respond rather than react, to allow the self to feel mourning, grieving, returning anger, every iota of reaction, and at the same time to decide to create a response that bears feeling from the heart.

Aaron adds what the teaching needs to be complete. Among those who value offering their energy lovingly, there is a popular misconception that when you are abused you must be a doormat to that abuse. There is a time to speak your own truth, not from fear which defends in the same pattern, but from a loving place to both of you which says, this is enough. Like a loving parent who picks up the screaming two-year-old and holds it, preventing further damage, lovingly, until its energy has quieted. You have a right to your own processes, but you do not have the right to pour the energy of those processes on me in hurtful ways.

If you are listening to this and you are living with real harm in your own home, please hear this as love speaking. Reaching for real-world help is not a failure of devotion. It is devotion in its most practical form, the refusal to let harm keep circulating.

Q'uo closes the session with a sentence to carry. You cannot overspend the love that comes through you. The task lies in allowing the self to become transparent, so that the love flowing through creates that glow that recreates the face of the earth. You tremble on the brink of miracles. Lift high your hopes and live by faith.

Thank you for listening.

title: Wade into Forgiveness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: wade into forgiveness.

The evening session of the Aaron and Q'uo dialogues turns to the largest subject of the weekend, and Aaron opens it with a sentence that reframes a lifetime of effort. To live the devotional life is to learn how to forgive. Forgiveness cuts karma, dissolves it entirely.

But what is karma, in this teaching? Not the story of what someone did to you. At the place where that karma was formed, Aaron says, we find always an energy contraction. The karma is not about one person doing this to me. It is about the way the self solidifies around the story of it, the misunderstanding that says I must angrily confront or be a doormat. To release that blame and anger is to forgive. And forgiveness, they insist, is a process and not an event.

They liken it to entering a cold lake on the first hot day of spring. The air is warm and gives rise to the desire to swim, but when that toe touches the water, it is still frigid from the winter's ice. In just such a way, the heart may still be frigid from winter's ice. Kindness does not ask you to go to the end of the dock and leap in. Wade in slowly. If it feels good, go in. At the point where the feet are numb and there is discomfort, it is time to get out and wait until the water may be warmer. Tomorrow the heart may have thawed just a bit more.

To consider the possibility of forgiveness is to touch the deepest hurt places in the self with an honesty which acknowledges the wish to enact pain in return for pain, and the enormity of the desire to be safe. And it is not enough to acknowledge these forces, but one must do so without judgment. The process of forgiveness begins with the self.

Then Aaron leads the group in a forgiveness meditation, and I want to carry its shape to you, because it is built to be practiced. Bring to heart and mind the image of one whom you love and who loves you. Ask forgiveness for the ways you have hurt this one, intentionally or not. It was my fear speaking. Then turn it around, and offer forgiveness for the ways this one has hurt you. Feel the wall come down between you. And then turn to someone harder to forgive, which is the self. Say your own name to yourself, and bring into the heart what has seemed difficult to forgive. I love you. I hear you. I forgive you.

If you are working through real hurt, including harm done to you by another person, go gently with this practice, and do not walk it alone if the water is too cold. A trusted counselor, a support group, a friend who listens well, these are not detours from the spiritual path. They are part of it.

Q'uo adds the teaching about the foundation, and it is one every intense seeker needs to hear. There is a very real danger, they say, to those who go overboard with spiritual disciplines. The most common mistake of the spiritual seeker is to rush into the higher energy centers without maintaining the health and balance of the lower energies. It is as if the owner of a house with cracks in its foundation set about building another story onto the house. The foundation not being secure, the entire structure might end up in pieces.

So where is the foundation built? Not in the spectacular moments. In the small things of every day. The chop wood and carry water of life, the chores, the repeated tasks, hold the most potential as training wheels for the seeker learning to ride the bicycle of devotional life. The world does not value the laborer who washes dishes. But if the seeker who does the dishes has remembrance of the holy nature of all life, it shall be lightening the consciousness of the planet as it lovingly cleanses, rinses, and appreciates each dish.

One who can see the holy in the homely has the greater life than one whose accomplishments are brilliant to the world but whose personal orientation toward the humble side of life is just to get it done. And Aaron adds the quiet agreement of their own tradition. The darkness is not your foe. It is your teacher.

Wade in slowly. Tend the foundation. The water will warm.

Thank you for listening.

title: God Bless This Mess
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: god bless this mess.

The final morning of the Aaron and Q'uo dialogues, November of nineteen ninety five, and the weekend's teaching comes to rest in the most ordinary places imaginable. Q'uo begins with a sentence that quietly dismantles every spiritual fantasy of escape. The life of devotion is lived where you are, or not at all.

There are relatively easy spiritual practices, they say, such as meditation and prayer and the sharing of worship in groups such as this. And there are relatively difficult spiritual practices, such as standing in the checkout line at the grocer's and scrubbing the toilet bowl. It is a common hope someday to retire to a pleasant and secluded place where finally you can devote yourself to worship. But we suggest to you that the life of devotion is lived now, wherever you may be. It is the confidence and focus within that turns bare earth into holy ground, blazing with the incandescent light of love.

Each mistake, each error, each missed opportunity, they say, is a gift to the infinite One just as much as each moment when you judge yourself to be on the beam. Clumsy or graceful, awkward or flowing, your spirit is utterly beloved. May you play together like otters, they say. May you be merry with each other.

The conversation turns to pride, the shadow that follows every glimpse of the light. When you discover your own angel nature, how do you not become clothed in pride? Aaron answers with the simplicity of long experience. To be clothed in pride is just to be clothed in pride, just as to feel anger arise is just to feel anger arise. You do not need to act upon it, nor to get rid of it. Only to note, here is pride. Pride is part of that which wants to be somebody, to be safe and in control. And when you embrace the fearful self that does not feel safe, the circumstances that gave rise to pride begin to diminish.

Q'uo offers an image for the long road. View the self as a rough, huge planetoid with deep ridges and valleys, and the influences of the cosmos beaming down in a refining fire, slowly smoothing those mountains of pride. In the fullness of time, those ridges shall be smooth, until at last the mantle of rock shall be polished away, and the immense jewel that your consciousness is shall emerge and become as the sun. Do not hurry toward that destiny, they say. Enjoy your crust of imperfections. They shall not harm your spirit, but only give it the catalyst that your consciousness seeks.

And Aaron tells a story about the teacher Gurdjieff, who once paid a rude and difficult man to return to his community, because, as he put it, the man was the yeast for the bread. Child, Aaron says, this yearning for perfection in you, this self-striving to become what it already is, the fears, the patterns of reactivity, all of it, these are the yeast for your bread. The human, they say, is perfect in its imperfection.

Q'uo's final suggestion for the perfectionists among us is a motto to adopt. God bless this mess. And when the group shares a dream of being made to dive into a trough of slop and emerging into a white room among robed teachers, Aaron laughs in recognition. The dream, they say, is as perfect an illustration of the process of incarnation as they have ever heard. Only when you move through the messiness of incarnation, the messiness of a body and emotions, do you emerge into the angel that you are.

Aaron closes the weekend by teaching the practice of Tonglen, the giving and receiving. Breathe in the light and send it out to where there is suffering. Then breathe in the suffering itself, a heavy black mass, and release it upward to the divine. You do not need to carry it. You are merely the vehicle through whom it passes.

May all beings everywhere love and be loved. May all beings know the infinite spaciousness and joy of the forgiving heart. May all beings follow this path of letting go into the deepest truth of their own being, and therein find perfect peace.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dark Days
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dark days.

December of nineteen ninety five. The days are at their shortest, and the group has asked for nothing in particular, only whatever words of inspiration Q'uo has to offer. And what comes is a teaching for the dark season, outer and inner, for everyone who has felt the light go thin and wondered who they were in the dimness.

Q'uo begins by naming what is happening in the room. There is a yearning among all those present for the light that is so absent from the days as the planet moves toward its farthest from the sun. These dark days weigh upon the spirit. Those who have sorrows find the sorrow is greater as the days grow shorter. And there is a spiritual difficulty too. When one is less comfortable, huddled in upon the self, one turns toward the shadows of uncertainty and hesitation. Those energies create the shadow that always follows faith, and that shadow is inextinguishable, for the light that casts that shadow is consciousness itself, and that sun does not go down. And yet in dark days it feels as though the inner sun itself has set.

If you are hearing this in a season when the dark feels heavier than a season, please let this be a small nudge from a friend. There is no shame in saying so out loud, and no shame in reaching for another person, a counselor, a helpline, a friend who will sit with you. The teaching we are about to hear is about the weather of the soul. It is not a substitute for a hand to hold.

All of this, Q'uo says, is as it should be. The doubts and inner discords are not only acceptable but of value. You laid aside your self-knowledge deliberately before this incarnation, because you wished to be affected by the light and the dark. You hoped to serve in the name of love. And each of you is doing all those things. From the standpoint of the work of the spirit, all is well.

Then comes the paradox at the center of the session, and it is one of the strangest and truest things in the archive. The self sees the process of learning about the self as one of digging in and clarifying what it really thinks and feels, adding unto the beingness a higher degree of self-knowledge. And yet the Creator has arranged the learning so that the path to self-knowledge is actually the path of turning the gaze beyond the self, and allowing the falling away of self. That entity who knows itself most deeply is the entity who has given much of the personality away.

They point to the teacher known as Jesus, whose sense of self carried him through a wandering ministry remarkable for the purity of its teaching. And yet when he was asked to describe himself, he said that he who sees me sees not me but the Father. This entity had learned subtraction as well as addition, and he was content to be impersonal and to relinquish much of the earthly personality. Yet there can be no more sure-footed identity than that.

Q'uo does not offer a solution to the paradox of addition and subtraction. Both are good work, in their rhythm and season. They encourage the seeker to flow freely and gladly along with the currents of life which put one in a certain mood or state of receptivity, to trust the intuition of self, and to keep a sense of humor, so that one takes oneself seriously but also finds the light touch.

And then the sentence that the whole session has been building toward. If we were to discuss our own idea of who the entity truly is, we would simply look at the vibration, for each self has a vibratory complex which is as distinctive as your fingerprint. You are, before you can think about who you are. You are not inventing yourself. You are asking yourself to become more than you were.

When Carla asks about a sadness she sensed in the contact, Q'uo answers honestly. The topic itself speaks of beings of light lost, it would seem, in the darkness of the illusion. And this particular aspect of existence has resonance with each in this circle of seeking. The sadness is real. And the love underneath it is real too.

The dark days pass. The sun, the inner one, never actually set.

Thank you for listening.

title: The State of Grace
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the state of grace.

A week before Christmas, nineteen ninety five. The group brings Q'uo a question about grace, and everything they think they know about it. Where does it come from? Is it a gift from outside, or is it always with us? Can we use it consciously, or are we simply caught up in it when it comes?

Q'uo begins by untangling the word itself. One person means one thing by grace, another means something related but different, and the imprecision of language baffles the discussion before it starts. So they offer a more precise way of seeing it. Grace, they say, is a state of mind, a state of mind that is natural to the self-conscious entity who is in balance, whose energies are moving freely and in a balanced manner. On a computer, they say with a wink, grace would be the default setting for being in good form.

Think of what that means. The training of the young entity in your culture develops an attitude geared toward accomplishment, toward fitting in, toward meeting an ever-growing set of standards. And so the growing entity drifts further and further from the feeling of wholeness that comes from the heart outward. Most entities move through the incarnation only becoming aware of grace as something episodic, now here, now there, a visitation that comes and goes.

But in actuality, Q'uo says, those times when grace seems to come near and touch the entity are those times when the individual has been able, involuntarily or consciously, to allow the self to be completely natural, to rest in the center of being and to allow the natural flow of energy. It is as though the self were a receiver that only intermittently worked. The grace was always broadcasting. The receiver was only sometimes tuned.

So how does one tune the receiver? Meditation is always helpful, they say. But they also suggest something quieter and more radical. The conscious attempt to experience thanksgiving when all is going unexceptionally. This is the blessed state so often missed by the spiritual seeker, the state of doing and being that flows throughout a normal day. Within this quiet flow of energy dwell tremendous power, joy, and deep emotion. When the conscious mind turns and gives thanksgiving for this normality, this normal day, this thankful, grateful opening of the heart causes the balance within to strengthen and to normalize.

I love that line, because it reverses the usual spiritual ambition. We are always looking for the peak, the breakthrough, the extraordinary Tuesday. And Q'uo is pointing at the ordinary Tuesday and saying, there. That is the one you keep missing.

And then they say the thing that lifts the whole teaching off the page. Each of you has the pure and perfect light within. Each of you dwells in a state of grace at a very deep level, at all times, in all places whatsoever. The illusion in which you dwell was designed not to give you the experience of balance, but to give you the feeling of imbalance and confusion, so that the self would have material against which to push and from which to learn. The imbalance is the classroom. The grace is the floor it stands on.

When the questions open, someone asks about the journey of the soul itself, and whether the soul comes out of the Creator fully formed. Q'uo's answer fits the evening perfectly. The process begins with total unity, moves into seeming separation, to the point of seeming complete separation in third density, and then begins the movement back into unity. The essence of each soul, at its heart, is mystery. There is energy. There is intelligence. There is infinity. There is unity.

So grace is not a prize for the good days. It is the natural poise underneath every day, the Garden of Eden you were born into and never actually left. The work is not to earn it. The work is to stop leaving it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Passing Scene
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the passing scene.

January of nineteen ninety six, and the group has given Q'uo an open floor, permission to speak on whatever seems most worth saying. And Q'uo goes straight to the heart of everything they came to share. Open the doors of your attention, they say, and behold the present moment.

The body you enjoy and the world you live in, they say, is a passing thing. In time it was created, and in time it shall disappear, changed into that which was not. Yet there is that which was before the worlds were made and which shall be long after your sun has gone nova. There are many words for this inalterable reality from which all things spring. Among those words, they say, we choose love.

Within your essence, unchanged and unchangeable, resides this vibration. This is your true self. That true self peeks up into the passing days like the tip of a great iceberg, barely clearing the water, yet being a mighty mass below the surface. Indeed, all that your peoples tend to think of as their identity, all were created and will cease to be.

How does one find this present moment? Not by grasping, because within time the attempt to grasp the present moment is constantly doomed to failure. Your mind and the illusion itself were created so that things would occur in an order. In the eternal present moment, all things exist simultaneously. That which is, is. And in this fullness of being resides the peace that is so eagerly sought by those who weary of the passing scene.

Q'uo suggests the practice of regular contemplation or meditation, for within silence there is the key that unlocks the doors of attention. And into that sanctum of the open heart, silent and listening, there resides the Creator whose name is Love. The voice which speaks in silence is that which gives life and peace. It does not give wisdom, exactly. It works little by little to open the heart to the presence of love.

And there are other doors into the same room. If you gaze into another's eyes, truly looking into those remarkable depths, you may see the Creator. Even if you look in the mirror at your own eyes and look into them, you shall see that which you do not recognize as personal, for you carry within you a consciousness which is love. It is a matter of uncovering and recognizing that which has always been there, that presence which is closer than your breathing, more intimate than your hands and your feet. It is that which abides.

When the questions come, someone asks about the ebb and flow of meditation itself, the reluctance that creeps in, the practice that begins to flag. Q'uo answers with the image of tempering metal. The continuing beyond confusion, beyond distraction, beyond the difficulties, is like the tempering of the metal in a tool that gives it strength, burnishing it that it might shine brightly. When your focus falters in meditation and must be returned with patience and love to the one point, that very returning is the work. To persevere and persevere and persevere is perhaps the most common and at times most difficult portion of any seeker's journey.

If the journey were always easy, they say, then the pearl of great price would be much devalued. So continue as you are, with faith, with forgiveness, with acceptance. And know that you are not alone, even when you feel great isolation, for there are those who walk with you and rejoice at your every step.

The passing scene will keep passing. The love underneath it was here before it, and it will be here after. Find the center for just a moment in each day, and the heart changes, and so the eyes change.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Two Covenants
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the two covenants.

Late January of nineteen ninety six, and the group brings Q'uo one of the most loaded questions in the archive, a question about Yahweh, the Mars entities, the old covenant of law, and why the teacher known as Jesus seemed to replace it with a covenant of love. Q'uo answers the way they always answer the large questions, by refusing to treat history as only history.

Your question concerns history, they say. And yet this history is also a mythology, and the one function is as important as the other. Because of these coincidences of meaning and value, it takes a careful and subtle intelligence to find one's true way through the bylanes of cultural detail and distortion. That which has to do with the relationship of consciousness with the Creator will always fly before any gust of wind that attempts to chase it. And the more words that are thrown at it, the faster it will flee.

What follows is best heard as the archive understands itself, an interpretive telling rather than a claim about the past. There was, in this telling, an entity called Yahweh who sought to aid a struggling people, and whose plan to improve the physical vehicle caused greater distortion than it prevented. The mistake is made, Q'uo says. There it is. One cannot go back. One simply learns and moves forward. This kind of situation occurs at all levels of consciousness.

And then, in this telling, came the second influence, one that took the same name and the same frequency of light, but with ever-increasing distortions toward belligerency. Its gift was the law in all its detail, the proclamations and taboos and schedules of sacrifice. And Q'uo names exactly what the law offered. The hunger which many among your peoples have had revolves around knowing what is right. Through the structure they knew what was right. The tendency was to enunciate finer and finer points of law until all possible actions were covered, and the entities within the system were safe.

Look upon your present world scene, Q'uo says, and see the entities about you looking for a way to be safe. Look upon your leaders who wish to prohibit freedom in order to guarantee safety. The spirit of that old covenant is strong, and it survives.

But there is another promise, and another logic. In the testament of the one known as Jesus, the place of the law is simply turned upon its head. Man was not made for the Sabbath, but the Sabbath for man. The direction to love the one infinite Creator and to love each other self as the self is not a detailed, closed, or encapsulated direction. It is specifically open-ended. There is never an end to love. There is never the need to return to the old prescriptions and old taboos.

These are not either or situations, Q'uo says, but either or processes. And as each student works upon its personal polarity, perhaps it will aid the student to ponder these two kinds of promises, these two kinds of ways of thinking, when the way seems unclear. One path is rational and linear. It holds, it insists, it is aggressive. The other does not hold, does not insist, is not aggressive. And that second spirit, they remind us, was before the one known as Jesus, and exists, as the other does, within each entity. For each of you is the universe. You are looking out at a world that is actually interior.

They close with a sentence to keep beside the bed. The attempt to nail down a history replete with metaphysical subject matter shall always be unending and full of gaps where there is no logic, there are no words, there is no road, there is no structure. Not that there is no structure. Just that there is, beyond all structure, love.

Two promises. One asks you to memorize the rules. The other asks you to love without end. The choice, as always, is yours.

Thank you for listening.

title: Learning to Receive
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: learning to receive.

Early February of nineteen ninety six. The question this week is one that will sound familiar to anyone who has ever tried to live a life of service. Is it possible that it is as hard for service-to-others people to accept the love offerings of others as it is to give? Many of us rush to reciprocate the moment someone helps us, because we want to be sure we give more than we receive. What we really want to do, we say, is to give.

Q'uo smiles at this, in their way, and reaches for Don's old hundred and eighty degree rule. If something feels right to the wisdom of the world, it very probably points the other way. Receiving the love offerings of others, they say, is the greatest gift you can give, and it is won by giving in service to others. When you reach the point at which there is no difference between receiving and giving absolute and unreserved love, then shall you be ready to learn the ways of wisdom.

Until then, we must learn these lessons that seem so opposite. How to serve others. How to accept service from others. Yet are you not looking in a mirror when you gaze upon another? Is that entity not looking at the Creator when it gazes back at you? Is this not the essence of your being?

Then Q'uo looks at the values of the culture, where the emphasis is always upon that which this instrument calls the green energy of money, some having more and some having less. Needless to say, they say, this is an illusion, for all things belong to the one infinite Creator, and as you give and as you receive, you are simply moving the energy around.

And here comes the sentence that this instrument was fond of saying, and that Q'uo endorses wholeheartedly. Keep the energy flowing. Don't resist. When it is time to accept love, learn, my children, to say thank you with an open heart and a clear mind. The reciprocity is in accepting love without reservation, or any evasion that would create an invulnerability between you and the other self.

Similarly, when you give, give wholeheartedly, and you shall experience that event as if you were being fed by heavenly food. You see, it is not money, or places, or times, or any event or object whatever that is given or received, for what is actually occurring is this. You are a thought. That thought is love unreserved, complete, utter, and whole. All you give is love. All you receive is love. The rest is masks, symbols, and placeholders.

So gird your loins to accept with joy when it is time to accept, and to give with equal joy when it is time to give, and know that what you give, you give to yourself, and what you receive is what you have given away. All is balanced in the one infinite Moment which is all that there is in reality.

The session closes with a questioner who feels that a great gift has been given, a new beginning, almost as if starting all over in thinking. And Q'uo's answer belongs to all of us at every threshold. It is said among your peoples that each day is a new beginning, and indeed this is so, yet some beginnings are larger than others. For one who begins a new journey, there is love. For one who ends a long journey, there is love. For one who feels confusion in the midst of what seems like a difficult journey, there is love.

To be able to accept that which is in one's incarnation at the time of the experience is love revealed. And sometimes the most loving thing you can do is simply open your hands and let yourself be given to.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Real Seniority
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the real seniority.

February of nineteen ninety six. The group wants to understand the phrase that floats through the Confederation material, the seniority by vibration, the idea that some entities have priority in choosing their next incarnation. What does that priority mean, and how could it be fair?

Q'uo begins where fairness is found, at the beginning. All who have incarnated on this planet in third density have incarnated in full equality with each other. The difference does not lie in status, and it does not lie in who is ahead or behind. Seniority by vibration, they say, is simply a recognition that there are those entities who have reached a certain level in their ability to carry the love of the infinite Creator in their beings, and who are thus able to accept an intensified challenge in their incarnational patterns.

Think of it this way. When the choice is made to participate in planetary consciousness work, entities who have the vibration that indicates a balance that will allow them to take up the more difficult incarnations may choose first, because they can carry the heavier weight of work. It has nothing to do with the outside appearance of the entity. It has nothing to do with worldly success. One could be senior by vibration and sit in a prison cell, or in a hospital bed, and still carry that seniority without any outer sign at all.

Then Q'uo says something that reframes every frustration anyone has ever felt with their own circumstances. There are those, they say, who specifically request and then accept difficult incarnations as part of the balancing of their learning. And then they describe a pattern that will feel painfully familiar. The more one works, the greater the seeming limitation may become. There is a feeling of moving not so much in circles as in an ever-decreasing spiral, wherein one works and works and becomes less and less able to do what one wishes to do.

But then they hold up the other side of it. There are those whose restrictions from within are as difficult as those from without. One may be free of worldly restrictions and yet be a prisoner within one's own mind. So which is freer, the one in the prison cell who has found inner peace, or the one in the mansion who is a slave to appetite and ambition?

The closing teaching of the evening is about where the senior entity actually lives. The senior entity, Q'uo says, has moved past the outer form and rests in the present moment. Not in the past, where the regrets live. Not in the future, where the anxieties live. In the present moment, where the infinite Creator dwells. For the entity who has learned to live in the present moment has learned the only lesson this density was built to teach.

And when a questioner asks about the one called Hatonn, the beloved teacher who worked so closely with this group in the early years, Q'uo speaks of him with the warmth of a friend. He is one whose love for this planet runs very deep, one who has continued to work with the light of this world long after his own cycle moved on. He reminds us that the teachers too are pilgrims, and that the seniority we keep asking about is not a rank they hold, but a weight of love they are willing to carry.

So if you have ever felt your life grow narrower instead of wider, as though the more you tried, the less you could do, consider that you may not be failing at all. You may be carrying exactly the weight you asked to carry. And the only question that matters is the one this session keeps returning to. Can you rest in this moment, and let the love that is here be enough?

Thank you for listening.

title: The Red Root
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the red root.

Our final session in this wave takes us to February of nineteen ninety six, and the group wants to know about something most spiritual people try to skip over. The red ray, the first energy center, the basic life energy that so many seekers associate only with sexuality and then quietly apologize for. Q'uo's answer is a celebration of embodiment, and it is a good place to land.

The question begins with the observation that there seem to be more lessons to be learned on this planet in the red ray than in any other. Why is that? And Q'uo answers by widening the meaning of the red ray until it includes everything we share with the simplest living things. The red ray is not only sexuality. It is the primal energy of life itself, the energy of the blood, the breath, the food taken in and transformed. It is the life force that pulses through every plant and animal and person on your planet.

Before there can be any spiritual work at all, they say, there must be the body, and the body must be alive, and for the body to be alive there must be the circulation of the red-ray energy. The seeker who ignores this foundation and rushes upward is like the owner of a house with cracks in its foundation building another story anyway. We heard that image last session too. The archive keeps returning to it, because it matters that much.

Then Q'uo says something that will surprise anyone who has ever thought of spiritual life as the opposite of physical life. Rejoice in the body, they say. Rejoice in the breath that moves without your asking. Rejoice in the blood that carries its burden. Rejoice in the food that becomes you. The body is a garment, and you are the one who wears it, and the garment deserves your gratitude and your care.

And yet they are careful about what the body is and is not. The consciousness within the body is far deeper and more abiding than the body itself. When the incarnation ends, the garment is laid aside, and the consciousness moves on, clothed in new forms as the lessons require. The body is precious, and it is temporary. Both are true at once. That is the paradox of the red root, that you are asked to love what you cannot keep.

The group asks how this energy can be balanced and used, and Q'uo's answer is beautifully ordinary. The balancing of the red ray is accomplished in the simple acts of living. In eating with attention. In sleeping well. In moving the body as it was made to move. In honoring the drives and appetites without either worshipping them or warring against them. The red ray does not ask to be transcended. It asks to be respected.

There is a quiet theology underneath all of this, and it is worth naming. Your body is not the enemy of your spirit. Your appetites are not evidence against you. The energy that wakes you in the morning and carries you through the day is the same energy, refined and refined again, that will one day let you know love itself. Every ray begins at the root.

So the next time you are tempted to treat the body as a problem to be solved, remember this session. Eat your food. Breathe your breath. Move through your day. And know that the ground you stand on is holy, because it is alive.

Thank you for listening.

title: Truth Is Embodied
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: truth is embodied.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, a circle of questions and answers, and it keeps circling one great knot: the difference between knowing a thing and being it.

A seeker in the group asks about those flooded, semi-lucid states that come when you meet new fellow travelers, a buzzing fullness of energy in the middle of an ordinary day. And Q'uo, the voice the group was channeling, answers gently. When a seeker moves into a place where it feels spiritual power, that power sets up a resonance within the seeker too. And sometimes, when two people meet with a real dynamic between them, the energy moves back and forth between them, an open circuit that stays open as long as it is useful to both. I love how practical they are about it. If the feeling ever seems too intense to be useful, they say, simply return to the meditative state and ask your own guidance to steady the flow. It is not the place of this energy to lead you. It is your place to receive it, and to shape it.

Then the seeker asks something even lovelier. He has noticed that the answers in these sessions seem to be woven around the unspoken lives of the people in the room. He once had a question he never said aloud, and it was answered anyway. Q'uo's explanation is beautiful. They do not offer words, usually. They offer concepts, and the channeler clothes them in words of her own choosing, drawing on her own memory for examples. But deeper than that, they answer what lies beneath the words. They do not read minds, they say. A mind is not a book. But they sense the gradations of desire. And desire, when it has a direction to it, is what they call the call. Like a radio set to one number on the dial, they pick up the broadcast aimed at their range. I find that so tender. The unspoken is not unheard.

And where does the information come from, in those flooded states, those flashes of other lives, those streams of knowing that seem to pour in? Here Q'uo gives an image I will carry with me for a long time. Picture a starfish, they say, reaching out with every arm to touch the sandy floor of the sea, in every direction at once. Your consciousness is like that. It reaches out on one level, and then on the next, and then on the next, so that there are universes within universes within universes dwelling inside you. The easiest level to touch is the high subconscious, the one that feeds your dreams. Below it lie deeper levels, the racial memory carried in the body itself, inner guides in the darker parts of mind, the mind of the archetypes, and finally the ground of it all, which is the Creator Itself. It is as though within the mind there lie temples, they say, whose doors are carefully guarded, and persistent seeking begins to slip keys into the locks.

But the heart of this session, the part they keep returning to, is this. The truth cannot be learned. It can only be embodied. You can pile fact upon fact and build a brilliant intellectual house for truth, and it will still not be the thing itself. The journey, they say, is a journey from head to heart. What you give to spirit is not your conclusions but your basic vibration, your way of perceiving. And I find that both humbling and freeing. You do not have to be brilliant. You have to be honest in your heart.

Someone asks how to discipline the heart so that it shows the truth that is already in there. And Q'uo answers with colors. Picture anger, they say, not anger at something, but the pure color and texture of the emotion itself. Picture love, joy, grief. These deep feelings are truths. The trouble is that we almost never meet them pure. They come wrapped in old moral judgments and reservations. But the seeker can learn to look at what is being felt, as it is being felt, and slowly loosen the coloration, the bars that hold the emotion in one fixed shape. Grief, for instance, can move from being a rending, tearing thing into something purer, a channel of itself. The emotion does not change. Your hold on it changes. Two steps forward, one step back. That is the work.

There is a small, playful ending I want to leave you with. One of the group members, warmed by all of this, says it would be wonderful to hold hands and run from star to star and jump all over the place. And Q'uo answers, with such tenderness, that they will meet him as he dreams, and explore.

The mind has its temples and its starfish arms, and the heart has its one small door. What you cannot learn, you may yet become.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Legs of Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: two legs of light.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group came with one burning question: what is the shadow, the dark side of the self, and how should we relate to it?

The answer Q'uo gives is not what the seeker expected. Each seeker, they say, comes to a point of choosing a path, and the hope is always the same, to become light itself, to dismiss the dark. And they say, plainly, that this hope does not bear fruit. The light and the dark are two sides of one coin, and that coin is the seeker. You cannot leave one whit of yourself behind. The graduation they speak of is not a shedding. It is a walking of the stairs of light with your dark side firmly integrated into the self that walks.

And then they give the image that carries the whole session. When the spirit finds its legs, they say, one leg is the light, and one is the dark. Together they make one shape, and that shape is identical to the infinite Creator. So the shadow is to be related to as a leg you stand on. As the musculature, the connective tissue, the power and the strength that let the seeker stand fast through times of difficulty and woe. The will itself is part of the shadow self. The will animates and vivifies all those bright ideals the light part of you loves to dream. The dark side is what persists until everything has been accomplished. Listen to how they put it. That which feels so heavy is also what grounds you, and sustains you, and makes you secure.

I love the next image even more. If your shadow could be objectified, what animal would it be? To the uninformed eye, Q'uo suggests, the dark side looks like a dangerous wolf, ready to tear apart everything the seeker treasures. But to a more informed eye, that wolf has become half wolf and half dog, and well trained. The shadow holds tremendous, infinite vitality. It blesses the seeker with night, and the night is like an eggshell around the newborn spirit, velvet, soft, and black as midnight. Evolution happens inside that dark. So their advice is simple and almost domestic. Tame the wolf. Train the dog. Love the faithful companion the way a master loves a servant who has never left your side.

They are careful to add that this darkness is not an absence. When someone asks whether darkness is just the lack of awareness of the Creator, they correct him gently. No, they say. They were speaking of the fertile blackness of night, the place where spirit is born.

Someone else asks about a different kind of drying up. When he first joined the group, he was full of questions. Now the desire to ask has faded, and he wonders if something is wrong. And Q'uo answers with a rowboat. When you first climb into the boat, they say, you row fast, desperate to reach the far shore. After a while the strokes stop being new. You have rowed all over the lake, and the scenery is familiar. And then, just when the questions are growing fewer, something happens. A critical mass within. You realize you have no oars, there is no shore, and faith alone will move the boat you sit in. How can one ask questions of the ocean? The man answers that it is a joy to know they sit in the rowboat with him. And Q'uo says, you and I, we are bubbles upon the sea.

As the session closes, they ask each listener to feel for the balance point within, the place that holds the illusion of light and dark in calm and peaceful equilibrium. And they leave the circle with these words, which I want to leave with you. Each entity is fragile. Each life is tender. Be tender with each other.

You were never asked to saw off one of your legs. You were asked to learn to walk.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Awaits
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love awaits.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group took pot luck, no set question, just an open evening. What came through was one of the tenderest discourses in this whole season of the archive, on the practice of remembrance.

Q'uo begins by admitting something striking. They are error prone, they say, as are you. Their experience is illusion. Their thoughts are about the illusion. And yet, beneath all of that, there is one thing that binds every seeker and every voice together. The nature of each of you. Because each of you, and each of them, is the same Self, wearing a different mask of forgetting.

They notice something funny and sad about seekers. Even those who know clearly and lucidly that all is illusion still get knocked sideways by it. The desire to figure it out creates its own insecurity, and the digging goes deeper. Do we truly know what our illusion is, they ask? We want to move beyond self, and yet we have not moved beyond self. And here is the turn that undoes me. What we are moving toward, through all this seeking, is self. That great Self that is the Creator. Moving up the ladder can feel like learning more things to hold on to, but it is really more like things falling away. Everything you can hold on to will fail you. The only thing that does not fail is love itself.

And then they say the line that gives this episode its name. Love remains, they say. It passes every test, and it waits for the weary to finish the current round of tests and questions, wonderings and murmurings. It waits patiently, with all the love, literally, in the world. Your Self awaits you between each word, between each breath, between each bone in your body, between each synapse in your nerves and brain. Love awaits.

They ask you to picture it. Are you in the desert? Love will find you there and hover about you with living water, waiting for you to open the door to the present moment. Are you in the garden, the oasis, where blessings abound? Then love is everywhere, and it is easy to forget that the bright feelings of good times are not the deep tide of the heart. It is easy, when everything is lovely, to wander away from the holy of holies and just play in the garden. Love calls to itself from within the good times and the bad, and it remains the same in both. It can only be glimpsed fitfully. But those moments of inner awareness, those flashes of wholeness, are enough. More than enough to exalt and strengthen and inspire.

Their practice is almost embarrassingly simple. Move into remembrance as often as you can think of it. Ask yourself to remember, to give thanks, to give praise. Sharpen that desire day by day, and it builds a rhythm of evolution all its own. Because the part of you deep enough to remember, moment by moment, is the self you are yearning toward. The slightly more aware self. The one opening, and opening, into the infinite depths of love.

The second half of the evening belongs to Carla, the channeler herself, who asks the kind of question only a tired servant would ask. She has been wondering if she is just massaging her own ego with all this channeling. Has everything not been covered by now? And Q'uo answers with such grace. Yes, many topics have been covered, they say. There are many ways to approach love. But the heart of this work is not the information. The heart is the blending itself, the seeking of love and the sharing of love, the birthing of love that did not exist before you sat down together. The treasure, they tell her, is the time together.

She asks whether silent meditation and channeled meditation are equal ways of sharing the presence of love. And they say, in effect, that each is full of love, and the choice is yours. Some hearts are reached through the doorway of the mind. Some are reached in silence, straight to the foundation of being. Try each, they say, and trust your own appreciation.

And when she admits she has mostly kept channeling because the people around her still want it, they do not scold her. They say the most helpful words often come through an instrument that had little desire to be one that day, but answered a call. You answer the call of others. We answer your call. This is the way of service. I love that line. You do not have to feel ready. You only have to answer.

Between each breath, between each word, love is waiting for you to remember it is there.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Imperfect Witness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the imperfect witness.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question is a practical one. How does the balancing process work? Should we just be spontaneous, or should we consciously bring light into each situation? How do we become good mirrors for each other?

Q'uo starts with two assumptions, and I want to lay them out carefully, because everything else follows. First, that there is a center to things, a sense to be made of the universe, even though that sense is alive and cannot be pinned down like a butterfly in a collector's case. The moment you stop it, it stops being living. The whole holds every pair of opposites in a dynamic balance. Second, that it is the business of humankind to experience, and to bear witness to that experience. Not to be perfect. Not to hunger after perfection. What is precious, they say, is the depth and quality of perception. The seeker of truth is like the witness that makes the fallen tree make a sound.

Listen to how they put it. What the infinite Creator treasures is not the polished conclusion of the scholar, but the diamond in the rough of the person as she is, bearing witness to the catalyst that struck her. It is not important to create perfect responses. It is important to let the most deeply felt truth of your being thrive.

Then comes the elephant. Q'uo asks you to imagine standing so close to an elephant that all you can see is a patch of dark, leathery skin. That is one truth. Now rise up, as if in a helicopter, a few feet back, and you see the whole animal. That truth does not deny the first one. It adds to it. Rise further, and the elephant is a small dot among the dwelling places of your peoples. Further still, a planet spinning in space with clockwork precision. Further still, empty space and stars. Each view is true, and each is larger. This, they say, is what balancing is. Not a new opinion. A larger point of view. A view that has pulled back from the previous one.

They are honest about the social part too. When you treat someone with compassion and kindness beyond what you actually feel inside, they congratulate you. That is a polarizing, positive choice. But if you do not take that unbalanced action back inside yourself afterward and balance it, assimilate it, it will drain you, because you will have spoken a lie. The wound needs attending. The soldier at the line of battle takes incoming fire, and the wounded self needs healing. And healing happens, they say, when the seeker opens the self, imperfections and all, to the largest perspective. The largest perspective is love. In love, the opposites are reconciled.

Here is the reversal I did not expect. We tend to think spiritual evolution is a building process, higher and higher, more wisdom, more understanding. Q'uo says it is the opposite. As the seeker evolves, the seeker becomes more able to release the self, to let go, to surrender the part that wants to be perfect, or better, or wiser.

They describe the old balancing exercise the group already knew. Review the day. Notice where you were swayed, positively or negatively. Feel each point, intensify it, hold it, and let the mind place what was felt within the whole range of that feeling and its opposite. It reconnects the distorted self with the truer self that contains the entire range of every emotion. And the key, they say, is the remembrance of the larger viewpoint. The balance you are after is not an intellectual balance between two concepts. Wisdom is not the project of your density. There is a great deal of wisdom in seeking the center of feeling which is absolute.

And they insist on one more tool, which I adore. A sense of humor. It takes the sting out of difficult experiences, not by denying pain, but by seeing the pain of living in its larger context of sorrow and joy.

Near the end they pause the whole circle for a moment of silence, and ask everyone to hold the heart as a glowing ball of perfectly white light, dwelling within the darkness of flesh, like the sacrament on the altar of a cathedral. This perfect light cannot be brought into the illusion, they say. But it can be witnessed, imperfectly, by every heart. Love abides within each. Light dwells in the very heart of each. This is your truth. All else is language.

The way to be a witness to the light, they say, is to live today. Hopes for tomorrow and regrets about yesterday have their uses, but they do not help you bear witness. By the time an impulse has been edited into a presentable expression, it bears witness to the editor, not the truth. So go ahead and edit yourself. Such is the way of service. But then let the self heal. Spend time just letting go, releasing the pains and the joys alike to the infinite One. These are the harvests the Creator desires.

Just as you are, you are loved. Each moment is a moment of choice. Each moment is infinite.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Tapes We Play
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the tapes we play.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group brought a question every one of us has lived. What are these tapes, these behavior patterns that play in the mind whenever something happens? Where do they come from? How do we recognize them? And can they be changed?

Q'uo begins with a picture of who we are, and it is worth holding on to. You are, they say, a second-density physical vehicle, an instinctual animal body with a life of its own, carrying a consciousness that is a citizen of the universe and a child of the infinite Creator. The naked ape carrying truth, love, and infinite values. In the world, but not of it. That split is the whole stage on which the tapes get made.

Because here is how a tape gets recorded. The consciousness inside the infant is mature, they say. It has a fair degree of crystallization already. But the infant body is helpless, utterly dependent, unable to speak its thoughts. And so the very young mind, which experiences its caregivers as titanic, god-like providers, begins storing information about what kept it alive. It perceives dangers where none exist. It misses the real sources of difficulty. Triggers get laid down into thought and speech patterns, and the second-density mind files it all away, keeping survival data at the ready. These are your tapes. They were recorded by a very young entity doing its best to survive, and they have been playing ever since.

Now, Q'uo offers two completely different ways of working with them, and both are worth hearing. The first way works at the level of the mind itself. It is exacting, intellectual, painstaking work. You start by noticing the trigger, the specific thing that starts the tape. Over time you build intelligence about each crystallization.
