Then you move back, and further back, until you find the original experience, the young and tender moment when the distortion hardened into place. Often there is a phrase or a sentence at the root, something you gradually learn to identify. And once the root is exposed, you can encapsulate it, and by mechanical redirection of thought whenever the trigger appears, gradually remove the distortion from the interior tape library. They admit this work is better done with another person, because the intellect is almost inevitably blindsided by its own depth. It is hard to stand outside yourself and see yourself whole. But they promise that even this surface-level untying of knots often brings great emotional release.

The second way is entirely different. It does not work on any particular tape at all. It works from the level of the infinite consciousness, the Self that has only adopted this manifested symbol of a self for a little while. That consciousness, they say, is like a metaprogram the living mind can access. It does not think. It is not logical or intellectual or physical. It is as that which sings the tune. It is the bell that is struck, ringing in a combination of tones unique to you. And where the second-density mind accretes knowledge and holds it against future need, the infinite mind simply moves between pure states of feeling, and whatever is felt is automatically seen with thanksgiving. This is the way of love itself.

How do you reach that metaprogram? Through the doors between the conscious and the deep mind, opened in silence. And here Q'uo says something I want to underline. We cannot say enough about silence, they say. The silence within is a precious gift you give yourself. When you open to the presence of the one infinite Creator, life-enhancing energies can flow into the sore and aching cracks and crevices of the conscious life, offering that strength that is love, offering a larger and yet again larger perspective, for that is the way of love.

They close with a blessing that is really an instruction. Be very charitable to yourself, they say. And give yourself that wonderful endowment of time to be still, and know that the place whereon you stand is truly holy ground.

The tapes were recorded by a child who was trying to survive. You are allowed, now, to be the adult who listens to them with love, and slowly, deliberately, records over them.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Law of Responsibility
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the law of responsibility.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six. The opening of the transcript is missing, lost to the tape, so we drop into the middle of a discourse already in motion, and what is here is more than enough.

Q'uo is speaking of the daily dying. Each day, they say, you capitulate a little, you let go, and each daily dying is simultaneously a day of resurrection. Life and death tumble together like puppies, endlessly experiencing limitation and expansion, darkness and light, sadness and joy. And each emotion, they say, is a truth. How often, they ask, have you met the resurrected Christ consciousness upon the road and not known it was the Creator?

They ask you to lift the blinders, again and again, into faith, into hope, into peace, by thinking on the concept of a love that would give itself and spend itself to the point of death. Each of you is a hero within your own creation. In one season it is easy to see yourself as together, efficient, able. And many, many times you have judged yourself unworthy, inadequate, not coming up to your own expectations. So they ask you, whenever you remember in the course of the day, to seek again and again for self-forgiveness and self-worth. Move in your mind, they say, to that tune that is the earthly heart. And there, if you have eyes to see, you will find that the stone has been rolled away, and the light has claimed the tomb for its own.

Then a questioner asks about the Law of Responsibility, and the answer is disarmingly simple. As the seeker becomes aware of more principles that apply to the life pattern, the seeker has the responsibility of using them, in service to others and in the enhancing of the life. If you learn a thing and do not use it, you will find it harder to discover the next thing. That is the whole law. Use what you know, to the best of your ability, in revealing love to yourself, love for yourself, love to others, love for others. I love the bluntness of it. Knowledge is not a collection. It is a commission.

Someone follows up. He has heard that if catalyst is not processed, it drains the entity. Is that related? Yes, they say. If you have a catalyst before you, and you know you are capable of processing it, and you do not, you will find yourself in inner turmoil and confusion, until you use the principles you have gathered to meet what is in front of you. The drain is not a punishment. It is the friction of an unused tool.

The group had a difficult moment before the session, a sharp exchange of feelings, and someone asks whether it damaged the group's energy. Q'uo's answer surprised me. They were pleased, they said. It is not the presence of difficult feelings that causes a problem for the group's energy. It is the lack of attention given to them that makes holes in the wall of light around the group. What blessed them was that everyone shared what they had. The vision of sorrow replaced by the vision of hope, through the simple effort of supporting each other in something difficult.

And Carla, the channeler, asks the most human question of the evening. What can we do to make this place safe? Is there more we should be doing? Q'uo's answer is one I want to keep. There will always be more that can be done, they say. The journey is infinite. If you look at what is not yet done and judge yourself accordingly, you will always come up short. If instead you look at what has been accomplished, and each has done much, then there is reason for rejoicing. And we recommend rejoicing.

They close by returning to the heart of it. Your being is of inestimable value, though most are unaware of the value of the being, for it is that which is at the center of the heart. This is the journey, they say, to move to the center of the heart, which would seem to be quick and easy, for do you not carry it with you? Oh, but this is the infinite journey. For are you not all things? Are you not the one Creator? So when you seek the heart of love, you seek the heart of self. Have faith. You are well set upon this journey. There will be difficulties. There will be challenges. How else would you learn what you do not know?

Use what you have learned. Rejoice in what you have done. The stone is already rolled away.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Alchemist's Oven
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the alchemist's oven.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group asked the biggest question a seeker can ask. What are the steps to make the harvest, to walk the path of the seeker of truth? And where does the desire to walk it even come from?

Q'uo begins by refusing the premise, gently. They are not authorities, they say, not infallible, just travelers on a path with no steps. And all they can offer is opinion. Each seeker is the captain of her own ship, on an ocean whose tides are not known, and upon which there is no land. Yet every island of truth, every continent of discovery, is within the seeker. The journey across perilous waters is an illusion, but a necessary one, because all within third density dwell within a heavy illusion, and all of it is the shadow of one great original truth. Love. That which is ever unmanifest, invisible, ungraspable, unprovable.

Someone in the group had said that none is worthy. Another had said that all are worthy. Q'uo says both are true, and that the paradox is the mark of the spiritual. No one is worthy, if worthy means having accomplished enough understanding to pass some final test. No amount of learning, however abstruse, will let you bear the fullness of light through knowledge. And at the same time, beyond and throughout all illusions, each entity is perfect. Each is loved by the Creator. Every iota of flesh, every thought, every emotion is loved, accepted, and forgiven by love itself. So the human experience balances between complete unworth and complete worth, and between the two runs the pathless path.

Then they ask everyone to breathe. Feel the breath coming in, the life the trees have given you. Feel it going out, feeding the plants in return. There is a depth of interconnectedness here that needs no words. And they point to the one great gift that overshadows all others. Presence. You are aware that you are conscious. That self-awareness opens a door that cannot be closed again. Not everyone is ready to walk through it, and for those who sleep, they say, rest easy. There is a time and a season for each. But for those who have awakened, the greatest gift is the incarnation itself. You chose to be here. You planned this trip, setting up relationships that would focus your heart on exactly the lessons of love you deemed most telling. Your basic vibration is love itself, distorted and contracted by the ways you freely chose to limit it.

And here is the great reversal of the session. The way to climb the steps of light, they say, is not to take on learning. It is to release learning. To release the strictures of contraction you placed on consciousness to defend yourself. When entities pull away from the open heart, it is usually not from anger or bitterness. It is to defend the vulnerable self within. So the path toward graduation is discovering, balancing, and releasing the things from which you pull back and contract in order to survive.

They give the image of the alchemist's oven. You are a jewel, a perfect and unique gem, and the furnaces that polish you burn brightest during times of initiation, when all seems dark and there is challenge and struggle within. In these times, they say, rejoice, for you have joined forces with your destiny. You have come to a time of transformation. Sorrow, grief, anger, disappointment, all the negative emotions you feel are gifts, holding in their hands hours of despair and months of isolation and pain and tempering. The oven of the alchemist is designed to refine gold, to burn away the dross, leaving the precious original thought, pure, shining, and untouched.

And service? It is simple and nearly impossible, they say. Simple, because by being who you are you are expressing love, for that is all that can be expressed. Nearly impossible, because if you try to give love from your own energies you will quickly run out. Love is in short supply within the illusion. But you do not need to give it from yourself. You only need to move yourself out of the way of the love that comes in infinite supply from the one Creator. Let it pour through the instrument that is open and empty, and the world will feel the light and never know where it came from.

Someone asks about forgiveness, and the answer is clean as a blade. To forgive is to give love for whatever has been given to you. The desire to forgive is enough to begin. But if you place conditions on it, you have not yet forgiven. To truly forgive, you must erase all conditions. Wipe the slate clean within your own heart and mind. And there is, they note dryly, much opportunity for practice.

They leave the group with a vision. A midsummer night, clear skies, stars everywhere. Breathe in, and you breathe in the universe. Breathe out, and you create it again. You are the light of the world. You are the Creator's hands, the Creator's voices.

The fire does not destroy the gold. It only burns away what was never gold to begin with.

Thank you for listening.

title: In Season and Out of Season
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: in season and out of season.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question is one every seeker eventually asks. Why do we burn out? What is it that burns, our inspiration, our desire, our will? And what is the wisdom of resting along the path?

Q'uo opens by noting the season. Spring has cycled around, the light is increasing day by day, and even the planet itself, they say, increases its fidelity to the original thought as the light grows. Each individual, each kind of thing, has its seasons and its cycles of being. For the spiritual seeker, such cycles are to be expected. That is the first medicine. The dryness is not a failure. It is a season.

Then they go deeper, into what a seeker actually is. Each entity, they say, is the perfect vibration of love, distorted in a pattern unique to that one individual, so that each is congruent with every other, and at the same time entirely separate and different from any other. Like snowflakes, they say. No two alike. Just as your fingerprint is unique, your consciousness has its own soul print, its own signature. And this means that on top of the common cycles of season and time, each seeker has cycles unique to itself. What is perfect for another is not likely to be the optimum way for you. You can gather tools and tips from every teacher you meet, but in the deepest sense you must chart your own cycles and penetrate the mystery of them yourself.

Deep within, they say, there is a treasure. Much work has been done by the being that you are, and much has been stored in the subconscious, like potential memory waiting to be recognized. The key to that treasure is the practice of affirming the self that begins with silence, with meditation, with opening the inner door to the holy of holies, where beyond time and beyond space you dwell with the Creator. From that sacred place comes your faculty of recognition. When someone speaks and it resonates, it is as though a potential memory has been given permission to move into your waking mind. That is what the ring of truth is. Something you already knew, remembering itself.

Now to the burnout itself. Each entity, they say, has fairly regular cycles of enthusiasm and lack of enthusiasm. You have been calling the low point burnout. But the truth of your essence is not much connected to these seasons. What you are learning can be processed by the self that sits in silence regardless of the emotional weather at the surface of the mind. Even in the stormiest ocean, the movement beneath the surface is far profounder and far less obvious. You are learning in season and out of season. What you do in response to surface conditions is relatively unimportant, if in season and out of season you simply remember, in an undramatic way, who you are and what you seek.

I love this line. You do not have to wax poetic to be a seeker. You do not have to sustain enthusiasm to do your work. It is not necessary for each day to be a carbon copy of the day before. Adjust your rule of life as your needs and hungers shift. But, and this is the subtle part, the mere absence of enthusiasm is not by itself a reason to abandon a practice. As long as you are not hungering for a different one, persist. In the desert, persist. Rely on the memory of those deeply held desires that still seem fair, even though the yearning is missing. The channeler adds her own proverb. It is easier to find a good job if you already have a job. In seeking, too, it is well to be loyal to a practice that brings you daily into remembrance.

And if a new practice does move you, by all means follow it. The listening itself, done regularly in silence, will give you the inspiration to change course when the change is right.

They close with the thought I want to leave ringing. You cannot ruin your path. You cannot fail to receive constant feedback from all experience, a constant and self-renewing source of catalyst. There are times to race, and they urge your feet to have wings. And there are times when the body of emotions has been beaten and needs to rest, and then there is the pausing on the path. All the moods of your emotional weather are acceptable. Someone asks how to serve when there seems to be no one to serve, and they answer that the tuning of your own being in the desire to serve is itself a service. Where there is the desire to serve, there is always the opportunity.

The fire goes quiet. The embers do not. Keep sitting by them, and they will warm you again.

Thank you for listening.

title: Mercy for the Wanderer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: mercy for the wanderer.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question is tender and specific. What about the wanderers, those souls who came to this planet from elsewhere to serve, and who so often feel like strangers here? What difficulties are particular to them, and what might help?

Q'uo answers as those who have been wanderers themselves, and you can feel the kinship. They know the call to serve, and they know the veil of forgetting, and how far a young wanderer can feel from anything that feels native. And they say they have never regretted it. They walk the group through the energy centers, one by one, the way a doctor might walk through the body, naming where the wanderer tends to ache.

It begins at the root, the red ray. The wanderer's very cells, they say, shrink and quiver with the mismatch between the consciousness they carry and the culture around them, a culture driven by fear and hunger and the belief that money and power will satisfy the wanting. The wanderer's survival instinct itself feels threatened, as though it cannot survive here. Their corrective is disarmingly simple. Look at the fact that you have survived. You will continue to survive until all you came to do is done. Being a wanderer does not condemn the body to an early grave. It promises a chronic mismatch of vibrations, which often shows up as illness, allergy, and mental and emotional difficulty. I want to pause here and say this gently. If that heaviness ever feels like more than heaviness, please reach for real help among the people around you, a counselor, a doctor, a trusted friend. The archive offers spiritual comfort, not medical care, and you deserve both kinds of support.

And what opens the root? Care for the body the way you would care for something precious. When you bathe and dress and groom, do it with respect and love. Rock the body in your mental arms, they say. Hold it and tell it, I love you, I love you, rest easy, for I love you. You are that body's only human connection. It offered its instinctual life over to a consciousness that was never born and will never die. It needs your love.

The same center holds sexuality, which they speak of with reverence, as the surface expression of the force that created the densities, the port upon the ocean of eternity. Whether you express this energy or are celibate does not matter, they say. What matters is knowing and respecting its goodness, so it wells up as a never-failing spring.

Moving up to the orange ray, the belly, the center of self relating to self and to other selves one at a time. Here is the wanderer's great trap. The wanderer often does not know how hard it is on itself, and so projects that hardness outward and concludes it cannot deal with people. But other people are mirrors. They reflect the self back to the self, and the information you need to turn within comes through them. Beneath the criticism, the never-satisfied voice asking for more, there is a dim memory of being able to give and serve and be more. Q'uo does not deny there is always more. They simply say that is not the point. The word they offer for all dealings of self with self is mercy. Accept, forgive, and support the self that is living by faith alone in a difficult environment. Let your witness be that of the loving and the merciful.

At the yellow ray, the solar plexus, the center of groups, institutions, nations, and most intimately, the family. Here the wanderer's loneliness cuts deepest, because somewhere beneath the veil there is a memory of a loving, steady, supportive family of the spirit, and the families of Earth rarely feel like that. When the group energies get hard, entities retreat or else immolate themselves in some cause that spares them from choosing. Q'uo's advice is one word. Remembrance. Remember that there is a good reason you came. Remember who you are, why you are here, and where you are headed. The weariness will still be there. The pain will still be there. But so will courage.

They stop at the heart, the green ray, promising to continue another time, and leave the group with this. Each of you is perfect and whole and in total unity with all that there is. This is reality. The rest is illusion. For each, his star.

Someone asks how wanderers can better serve, and the answer is the whole session in a sentence. To love is to serve. The desire to serve is the foundation. Fuel the desire, and the ways will come to you.

You came from far away because you wanted to help. Be as merciful to yourself as you are trying to be to everyone else.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Distillery of the Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the distillery of the heart.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six, and it is the second half of a conversation. Two weeks earlier the group had asked about the wanderers, those souls serving far from home, and Q'uo had walked them through the lower energy centers. They had reached the heart, the green ray, and now they pick up exactly where they left off.

The heart, they say, is a place of fruition, a rest where you can gain an overview of the road you walk. It is the seat of wisdom bathed in compassion. And yet it is vulnerable, because whatever tightness sits in the lower centers bleeds off the energy before it reaches the heart. This is the wanderer's great temptation, to hurry past the basic work into the heart and the higher centers, where the lessons feel more uplifting. Q'uo counsels slowness. True openhearted energy arrives only when the seeker has begun to value each energy center equally, and starts any conscious work with a brief examination of each one, attending to imbalances before asking consciousness to function in the heights.

True openhearted energy arrives only when the seeker values each center equally, and begins any conscious work by examining each one, attending to imbalances before asking consciousness to function in the heights. Find appreciation for the lessons that seem basic. Each ray of self is beautiful to the infinite One. The catalyst that feels so heavy is an expensive gift of the higher self. When you can take that on faith, you have passed a great stumbling block on the way to the open heart.

Then comes the image that gives this episode its name. Once you stand in the open heart, there is a subtler work, the sifting and winnowing of everything the heart contains. The heart holds all expressions of love, from the most refined to the most inchoate and distorted. All of them are true at some level, but the surface emotions can be red herrings, clues pointing the wrong way. So Q'uo asks you to see yourself as a distillery, and your emotions as the raw ingredients of wine. The grape with its skin and stems, the sugar with its impurities, the water with its impurities, all of it is wine, but not yet. These are the emotions the heart receives when new catalyst arrives, usually in some confusion. You are not well advised, they say, to simply follow the heart and leave it at that. First let each experience be refined and purified by the distillery within. Refrain from impulse. Honor every feeling by returning to it later, in a centered state, and letting the deeper truth of what was felt move through the refining fire, until the pure emotion is distilled from the dross.

They make it concrete. See the heart as having a curb, they say. When you find the dross of some feeling, the part that was not fundamentally clear, place those stems and skins at the curb like trash, to be carried away by time, while the pure emotion filters into the deep heart that holds purity and compassion and its own wisdom. Discrimination is such a valuable activity. Each has it. Use it often.

Standing in the open heart, they remind the group of something stark. The green ray has only one true polarity. Those who seek the path of service to self must bypass it entirely. So for everyone who wishes to serve by serving others, spend as much time as you can within the open heart. The light it sheds moves backward to the root and forward to the crown. The passion-pure heart, they say, is the greatest power in the universe.

Moving into the throat, the blue ray, they note the irony of the wanderer as communicator. Wanderers are communicators by nature, yet their constant experience is frustration at not being understood. The reason, Q'uo says, is not inability. It is that the wanderer speaks on a level the listener is not on. The great skill is the listening ear, sensing where the other dwells in its own mind and heart, and tailoring what is said to that place. So do not just hold your tongue, and do not just speak. Listen, assess, and speak directly into the heart of that energy. That gives the other full respect.

At the indigo ray, the center of work in consciousness, they counsel reverence and small steps. The hunger for spirit is seductive, but that work will be refined across higher densities, so there is no hurry. Third density is not the place from which to take off into the ethers. It is the place to refine your basic choice, service to self or service to others, made and remade, again and again. Temptation to shut the open heart comes every day. That daily remaking is the chief work of your incarnation.

And then the shortcut. Perhaps it would not be incorrect, they say, to name one, and it is two words. Praise and thanksgiving. No matter what is occurring, it is a gift. Many of these gifts are brutal. Death and pain seem like dark presents indeed. And yet each situation is a chance to choose praise and thanksgiving. Remember the distillery. Often the darkest grapes, the mustiest growth, given time and allowed to sweeten, offer the most profound blessings.

The heart is a distillery, the emotions are the harvest, and gratitude is the fire under the still.

Thank you for listening.

title: Too Much of a Good Thing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: too much of a good thing.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the spring of nineteen ninety-six. The tape is short, and it ends abruptly, mid-thought, as though the rest of the evening was lost. What remains is the opening of a discourse on addiction, and I have chosen to stay with it exactly as far as it goes, because the beginning already holds so much.

The group asks about addictions of every kind, of food, of drugs, of friends, of rituals. Is there any value in them? How do you work with one? What is the right attitude, to solve it, correct it, or accept it? How do you even know you are getting anywhere?

Q'uo begins, characteristically, with the word itself. Addiction, they say, is to your people what the word vice was to a previous age. Both describe the condition of feeling driven to do or use or be some thing, or some way. But the modern word makes it sound more vulnerable to the quick fix. And for specific addictions there are quick fixes. Yet the nature of addiction, or vice, can be seen more simply. It is that which takes a good thing and overdoes it.

Listen to how they put it. What drives entities to addiction, very simply, is the instinct that the body, the mind, and the spirit have to seek comfort, enjoyment, and peace. There is nothing foreign in the wanting. The wanting is native. It is the engine of the whole incarnation.

And then they take you back to the very beginning, to the first hours of life. A soul enters incarnation without preference, because it has had no experience. Immediately the newborn breathes the air and begins to weep, because it is cold, uncomfortable, and hungry. Everything was provided in the womb. Now here is life, in full complement, and this helpless entity knows only when it lacks comfort. When it lacks comfort, it cries. The parents hear that innocent cry and learn to feed, or bathe, or change the squalling infant. The only tool the young entity has is its inarticulate voice. And so, they say, the trials of incarnation begin with the sobs of the newborn.

I find that image unbearably tender. Every addiction, traced back far enough, is that cry. A creature that once knew only how to weep for comfort, still weeping, in more complicated ways, for comfort still. The tape breaks off there, and I will not invent the ending the evening might have had. But I want to leave you with the other image Q'uo offered at the start of the session, before the word addiction was ever spoken. Your relationship to every opinion, including theirs, should be that of a connoisseur choosing fruit at the market. You know which truths you are ripe to receive. Take what satisfies you. Shrug off the rest. Some truths last a month, some a year, some a lifetime, and all will one day be overshadowed by a higher and broader truth.

If the search for comfort has become a place of suffering for you or someone you love, please know that help exists in the world beyond these recordings, in counselors, in fellowships, in doctors, in friends who will sit with you without judgment. You do not have to untangle this alone.

A good thing, overdone, is still a good thing at its root. And the root is the oldest cry there is. Comfort me. I am here.

Thank you for listening.

title: Faith to Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: faith to love.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the late summer of nineteen ninety-six, the group's first meeting after a long break, and they came with the most modern of questions. We are overworked and pressed, they said. How do we refill our batteries? How do we keep our spiritual balance in a world that demands so much worldliness from us?

Q'uo answers with a story. The channeler had once heard a visiting preacher tell of his time as a missionary doctor in Africa. He and his wife worked in a poor country through drought and an outbreak of disease, laboring so long and so hard they did not know how they could go on. Being also priests, they decided to rise early and pray, taking two more hours from their small allotment of sleep. And it worked. They found more than enough power within to move through their days in grace. It is an extreme example, Q'uo admits. But it shows how the way you gaze upon reality can change what your consciousness can bear.

They name the disease of the culture plainly. You live, they say, in an environment of consuming, collecting, and doing, and you have absorbed its values. There is the expectation of the dwelling, the vehicles, the duties to family and friends, the gadgets that make life simpler and infinitely more complicated. The culture encourages the doing rather than the being. And this is a true and substantial point.

So they ask you to step back from the outer world of flesh and bone and deeds, and call upon the deeper reality. The consciousness that chose to move into just this perverse environment, just this materialistic society, just exactly this one and no other. Why would it do that? Sit with the why, they say, and know that only one answer will suffice. Love. Love is the beginning and the end and all that lies between. Each of you came as a messenger of light, a vessel full of love. And here is the sentence I keep returning to. It does not come from you. It only comes through you. You are not responsible for loving the world. You are only responsible for allowing space within yourself, so that a channel of life may be made through you from the infinite Creator. Through your smile, through your eyes, through your outstretched hand, the infinite love flows.

Yes, they say, you are bogged down in the mire of too much to do. Yes, you are weary. And this is exactly what you hoped would happen. This very suffering, this crown of thorns that the too-short days are, is the destiny you hoped to achieve, for it is in this very place that you can learn the most about service and love, and offer the most powerful service and love.

When all seems confusion and the energy is gone, they offer a practice of one word. Say to yourself, perhaps, just one word. Love. The channeler, being Christian, says the word Jesus. Others might say Christ consciousness. Whatever name you give the principle that created all that there is, it is an infinite source of energy, and calling upon it, you shall be strengthened.

Beyond that, they offer the sense of proportion. See yourself as a tiny creature standing upon a ball in the far reaches of an unimpressive galaxy, in the midst of an infinite creation in which ten thousand years is the blink of an eye. Truth is eternal. The knower of truth is eternal. Each of you is an infinite spirit. The more you remember who you are, the more easily you find that center, that holy of holies within, where the Creator waits patiently, hoping you will stop, open the door, and tabernacle with the Most High.

Someone asks about the dynamic of love and faith, thinking of love as active and faith as passive. And Q'uo answers with an image of great beauty. Love and faith, they say, are like the tresses of a maiden, plaited together, inseparable. Love is the sun shining. Faith is the trust that to love is what is most appropriate, most helpful, most central to your being. There is the faith to continue when any response but love would seem appropriate. The faith to look foolish and love anyway, when less harmonious responses are called for. No qualities, they say, are higher or more difficult than having the faith to love, and loving in spite of every obstacle.

They close with a promise for the exhausted. No step in any incarnation is taken alone. Each entity is surrounded by friends unseen, teachers and guides called to you by your own seeking, who watch you walk and walk with you, and who hold your hand, in the metaphysical sense, when the moments of stress appear. Call upon these unseen friends whenever you feel alone. All such calls are answered. Perhaps not as you imagine. But in a way that has substance, and lends support. For this is a journey all take together, and none arrives home without aiding the journey of another.

You do not have to manufacture the love. You only have to make room for it, and have faith enough to let it pass through.

Thank you for listening.

title: Jump First
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: jump first.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the early autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question is one of the oldest in spiritual life. How do you contact that still, small voice within, when the catalyst is confusing and you do not know what to do?

Q'uo begins, as they so often do, by telling you how large you are. When you look in the mirror you see a curtain of flesh, and for all practical purposes that image is you. But what dwells inside that habitation of bone and flesh is an entity of such power that one of the ways you will express yourself in densities to come will be to participate in being a star. Your roots lie in eternity. You recapitulate the great original thought of love that created all that there is.

So why would something so vast agree to forget everything? Why draw the veil over all that full awareness? Because, they say, the fastest, most efficient place to sharpen the disciplines of the personality is the deep illusion of third density. The illusion works on you not in spite of the veiling but because of it. It throws you into confusion. It knocks you off center and sends you spinning. And your higher self wanted the spinning. Wanted the frustration. Because only in the ignorance of unknowing can a person choose to operate solely by faith. All the wisdom the mind seeks pales before the wisdom of simple faith.

The lessons you came to work on, they add, are not literal lessons, not specific wisdoms to memorize. They are more like seminars on a theme, and the theme is always love. Some must work on how to love. Some on how to accept love. Some on loving without possessing, some on loving with commitment. And here is the mercy in it. You cannot make a serious mistake. If you do not take the lesson on one road, it will simply follow you down the road you did choose. The reasons you are here will follow you faithfully.

The goal is not to become full of yourself, but to become familiar enough with yourself that you turn transparent to the infinite love flowing through you. The bushel hiding your light is that consolidated sense of self, opaque to love and to change. For spirit grows constantly. Love moves without end. Its very nature is flowing.

And so, when you are confused and seeking the next step, their advice is this. Affirm that you live in utter faith that there is a way prepared for you. You do not know what it is. Ask in meditation and prayer for the awareness to come. And understand what you are doing in meditation. You are sinking down through the layers of mind, past the distortion at the top of the subconscious, down through the cultural mind, the national mind, the racial mind, the mind of Earth, to the roots of the archetypal mind, where the conceptions are purer because they have no words.

That still, small voice, they say, is truly silent. It is a rare entity who hears a voice saying do this, do that. What you will hear is nothing. But for the one who waits in faith in the tabernacle shared with love itself, there will come a feeling of peace. Either the peace that knows, this is what I shall do, and can point the finger just there. Or the peace that says, I shall cooperate with whatever happens, because I know that what is mine will come to me. Both are feelings. Both contain great personal truth.

Allow time to pass. Sometimes the knowing comes in seconds. Sometimes you must invoke faith and patience again and again. Those times of waiting, though difficult, are like the fertilizing of the ground. Wait happily, they urge, for in the waiting much is taking place. The ground is being prepared.

And then the sentence that gives this episode its name. Faith is not something you can buy, or something you can work toward. Faith is something that comes to you after you take the leap into empty space. Once you are falling, you feel the emotional parachute open, and then you know what faith truly is. But you must jump first.

Someone asks the sharp question. How do you tell the leap of faith from the temptation to jump? And the answer is the whole session in miniature. Listen for the small voice. Meditate on the action or the inaction for as long as it takes to feel the impulse move in one direction or the other. It may take a moment. It may take a great deal of time. And while you wait, have faith that the process itself will unfold as it should, for this is not a universe where chance plays a significant part. Not even a small sparrow falls without the knowledge of the Creator.

You cannot think your way to the voice. You can only get quiet enough, and brave enough, to hear it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Speed of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the speed of love.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question aches with a feeling I suspect you know. We will not have enough time to do the work we came to do. When is the work really done? What is happening when we worry? Talk to us about time, worry, and spiritual work.

Q'uo begins where they always begin when the question is large, with the architecture of the illusion itself. Time, they say, is a building block that exists so the Creator's children can experience sequence. The universe you inhabit they call space over time, the physical world where space seems to rule. The universe of spirit they call time over space, where time has the ascendancy. Both are equally illusory, made for one overarching purpose, to create the illusion of sequence, so that the Creator might know Itself through the experiences of each unit of Itself. And each unit of the Creator is love. Before any thought of you was visible to the most metaphysical eye, you were already created, and already loved.

Loved as you are, they say, there is nowhere to go and nothing to accomplish that could make the Creator approve of you more or love you more intensely. Hold that for a moment before we go on, because everything about worry follows from forgetting it.

The right use of time, they say, is first of all the right use of consciousness, of attention. Your culture weighs actions completed, money made, projects finished, services rendered. By their fruits you shall know them. All of that is excellent stewardship. But it misses the deeper matter, which is the tuning of your consciousness to the vibration of the original thought, which is love. You cannot run out of time to do your main job, they say, because your main job is to meet each catalyst, moment by moment, with the vibration most essentially yours, closest to the tuning of love. Think of it as a constant, they suggest, like the speed of light. Let us call it the speed of love. The same for all entities, and yet each entity's way of tuning must be entirely its own, never learned by rote.

They pause the circle here, and ask everyone to move attention into the heart, the green-ray center, the holy of holies where love dwells fully and undistorted. Like the sun lights the sky, they say, the Creator rests in full strength within you. The key to that door is silence. The habit of turning within, of centering first upon the Creator who is love, will stand you in good stead on every road you walk.

And here is the liberation for everyone who fears the clock. You can finish an incarnation and only then realize you ran out of time for what you came to do. Yet what you came to do is available in every living moment. Each of you came with at least three things to do. To experience. To learn. And to use your gifts in service to each other. The Creator cannot smile upon anyone, or reach a hand to anyone, or feed or clothe anyone. The Creator's voice and hands and actions are yours. It does not matter whether the service looks small or great to the world. What matters is the love with which it is done. The channeler quotes her beloved Khalil Gibran. Work is love made visible.

And worry? They are wonderfully un-prissy about it. If you worry, they say, by all means get it all out of the closet. Number your worries. Revel in them. Roll in them, they say, the way Scrooge McDuck rolls in his money piles. Do what concerns you to do, whether it seems foolish or wise. Worry does not ruin your vibration. A loving person worrying is still a loving person. What closes the heart is something else. Those thoughts you return to again and again. Not enough. Unworthy. Afraid. Those keep the heart shut. But worry itself, the honest fretting mind, barely dents the tuning, as long as the heart stays open.

They end with faith, which they describe so simply. Faith is the quality that lets those who cannot see into the metaphysical world act as though they could. You chose a great deal about this life before you came, for deep reasons. You will never get objective proof of any of this, because it is essential that you choose without the advantage of knowing you are right. But know you are underpinned by a Self as sturdy as you are frail, as wise as you feel foolish. Allow little seeds of faith to grow in your garden of thought. Live as though your destiny will come to you, as though all that is for you will simply be attracted to you when it is time. And notice the small synchronicities, the subjectively interesting hints, that say to you, yes, you are on the right track.

You are not behind. There is no behind. There is only the tuning, moment by moment, at the speed of love.

Thank you for listening.

title: This Too Is Me
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: this too is me.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question is raw and honest. Each of us has thoughts of injuring another who has wronged us, and it makes us uncomfortable. How do we deal with this darker side, this part of us that needs some kind of recognition?

Q'uo answers with unusual directness. They know, even at their remove, the power and attraction of the magnetic emotion you call anger. And if they had to name it more accurately, they say, they would call it a kind of fear. Whoever is enraged is fighting for survival. The body, the second-density brain of the creature carrying your consciousness about, is honestly, genuinely concerned for its survival. The instinctual angers that come from feeling invaded or threatened live deep below reason. So the first thing they say is this. Do not brush the dark aside. Do not tell your body it should not be angry because it is not spiritual. That does not make sense. The darker emotions deserve a place. They deserve respect. They deserve attention. If such inner pain is not honored, they say, it can shrivel the most robust nature.

Then they explain the mechanics. Love, the original thought, is purely expansive, radiating outward in all directions. When it pours through your vehicle, it enters at the base, the red-ray survival chakra. If it is blocked there by contraction, by fear, little energy can rise to the higher centers. So the first work with anger is to forgive yourself for having this nature, this nature that contracts against threats. Your first duty, they say, is to yourself. Validate and support that dark side, for it is very concerned with your welfare, and it needs to be reassured, comforted, and held as gently and lovingly as the baby at the breast.

I want to sit with that image, because it undoes everything we were taught about the shadow. Not fought. Not exorcised. Held. Like a baby at the breast.

The objects of your anger, they add, only seem to be other people. Spiritually speaking, every other self is a mirror, reflecting what you like about yourself and what you wish were not part of you. The angrier you are at another, the more of yourself you are recognizing. It is as though the anger were a vampire, threatening to take you over and drain your strength. And how does one stop a vampire? There is only one way, they say. Accept that vampiric energy into the heart. Cradle it. Know it as the self. And say in compassion, this too is me.

Yes, you will have fear. Yes, you are worthwhile. Your illusion was built so that you could not help but respond blindly to incoming catalyst. It was never intended that an incarnation be without conflict. Indeed, they say, the part of you that is your higher self rejoices when you feel the catalyst of rage or resentment, for now you are doing the work you came to do.

Much anger is born between two people, blocking not only the root but the orange ray, the belly, the relationship chakra, where so many try to control or resist being controlled. Anger at society blocks the yellow ray as well. The infinite energy coming to you gets rationed, and little reaches the heart. So the work is long. They give the image of a closet. Fear contracts you into a small, crowded space. The skillful way is not to fling the door open and declare you will never go back. It is baby step by baby step. Open the door a little more. Do not try to become a person without anger. Try to become a little more light, a little freer than you were a year ago, a month ago, an hour ago. Pour compassion into that closed place and let it gently move you back into the light. Two steps forward, one step back, for a lifetime. Feel good about that, they say. Work in consciousness is a maintenance program. It is not a college you graduate from.

Someone asks how to help a person consumed by anger, and someone else asks the harder question underneath. What do you do when the anger is aimed at you, when words are used as weapons and even the strong are reduced to rubble? Q'uo's answer is careful. Accept the other's anger as theirs to carry, seek communication when the heat has drained away, and keep clear who is responsible for what. The one expressing the anger owns the anger. You own only your response. And if you are in a situation where anger has become cruelty, please hear this from me as well as from the archive. You deserve safety, and there are people in the world, counselors, friends, shelters, who can help you find it. Tenderness toward yourself includes protecting yourself.

They close the session the way all of this points. The universe exists because of opposites, light and dark. You are a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree being, the full circle from lightest to darkest. The earthy part of you, the soil where the dark nature hides, is heavy, but it is the soil in which truth and beauty grow. So gaze unafraid at the dark emotions. Love them. Accept them. Work with them gently, persistently, and with humor. Enfold your dark side in your heart. The goal is the open heart, and it was never going to be reached by pretending the dark was not there.

This too is you. All of it. And all of it can be held.

Thank you for listening.

title: In Love with the Self
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: in love with the self.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question is about balance. They had been noticing patterns in themselves, a pull toward ritual and routine on one side, a hunger for novelty on the other, and they wondered about the strengths and weaknesses of each. What they got was a discourse on one of the deepest balances of all, the masculine and feminine within.

Q'uo begins with the yin and the yang, the reaching and the waiting, the bold and the quiet, the fondness for the usual and the fondness for the new. And their first word is a liberation. There is no one correct balance to aim for. Each spirit carries its own stored harvest of distortions, its own wiring, unlike any other's. Balance is balance for one entity at a time. If you are an entity which enjoys itself, they say, you have achieved an enviable state. And then the line I want to hold up to the light. It is the work of much compassion and hard-won wisdom to fall in love with the self. To be a support to that self in all its uniqueness, with all the quirks that trumpet its imperfection. Each entity is uniquely distorted, and each should celebrate those distortions, while keeping a weather eye out for the ones whose laughter is not kind, and working with those until the same stimulus triggers not a new emotion but a sense of compassion that embraces what is seen.

The entity in balance, they say, is one in whom judgment of self and others has been tempered with gentle kindness. Accurate, but kind.

They are careful about the language of male and female. It is true, they say, that the physical vehicles carrying your consciousness have distinctive patterns, and that your upbringing has given you a thorough, often crippling grounding in what it means to be a biological male or female. But it is emphatically not true that the infinite and eternal spirit, the true self, is bounded by these instinctual behaviors, or even very conscious of them. There is no fixed limitation on how a spiritual seeker must express its being. The choice of sex, like the other great choices of the incarnation, was made before birth to set up a fertile learning situation, nothing more and nothing less.

They sketch the general lessons lightly. For those in female bodies, the lessons often revolve around increasing the capacity to accept, to nurture, to forgive, to understand. For those in male bodies, they often revolve around fulfilling responsibilities and duties without recrimination. But they warn against taking these differences too far. Beneath them lie things deeper, wider, and broader than the whole spectrum of sexual difference. The female principle, they say, flames brilliantly with dreams of many colors, and it is the work of a lifetime to find roots for all those wings of imagination. For the masculine, it is the work of a lifetime to allow imagination to become powerful.

And here is the turn that matters most. Each entity, regardless of the body it wears, contains a unique balance of yin and yang, the male and female within the self. There are three hundred and sixty degrees of possible balance. The most efficient way to work on yourself, they say, is to be in relationship, especially the primary mated relationship, where differing views of commonly witnessed catalyst can be shared without judgment and with mutual respect. Any relationship with open, clear communication will do. Because the other is always a mirror, and what catches your aggravated eye in another is a message to the deep mind about a judgment against yourself.

It is so easy to judge, they say, and so very difficult to refrain from the kind of judgment that does not stop at describing accurately but moves on to evaluating the morality or beauty of a situation. The work is to gaze with sense wide open, and to arrange what comes in, in the way that brings poise and calm, so the seeker is ready to take in more rather than being swamped by what has already arrived.

They close with a practice almost too small to notice. Discover the self new each day. Find the places that seem blocked or over-eager, and make time for silence and listening, time to open to the possibility of a better configuration of energies. The channeler prays, Lord, teach me Thy ways. That simple desire to know the better way, they say, has far more efficacy than any attempt to figure out precisely what to do next. The true work of spiritual evolution is done below the surface of consciousness. When you can know that all is love at the same time you are expressing your distortions, you have indeed become wise.

And if questions of identity, of relationship, of the masculine and feminine within you ever feel heavy to carry alone, speaking them aloud with a trusted counselor or a wise friend can be a genuine kindness to yourself.

There is no single right way to be whole. There is only your way, found a little more clearly each day, in love with the self you are becoming.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Is the Middle Man
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love is the middle man.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group asked for clarity on relationships. How can we know what is really happening between us and another? Should we plan, or trust intuition? Should we be true to ourselves even if it seems to hurt someone else?

Q'uo begins where they always begin, with the self that comes to relationship. Every relationship you experience on the Earth plane, they say, is in an important and basic way a projection of a relationship you are having with yourself. The one who wishes to know herself becomes an entity who pays attention to the movement of energy within the body, to the thoughts and the emotions, choosing ever more fearlessly what to heed and what to let pass.

They pause over something small and piercing. On the gravestones of your people, they note, the whole of a human life is expressed by the dash between two dates. A little precious gem of a life. And within that gem, your personal goal is to experience more and more truly what is actually occurring. Life passes with blinding speed, and all too soon the time of learning is done. Death, they say, is a summer vacation, and yet it closes a precious door, behind which there was confusion and movement and passion and life such as you cannot know outside the chemical distillery you call your body.

Then they say something that undoes the whole project of figuring people out. Knowledge, in their opinion, is itself an illusion. The entity who wants knowledge will penetrate illusion after illusion, and each penetration will uncover another illusion. Consider those in your culture who are absolutely sure they know the spiritual facts of life, and cling to that knowing in a way that precludes loving everyone. Knowledge will fail you in relationship. But step back to the beginning, to the impulse that woke you up the first time, the craving for truth, the hunger and thirst for love. For that which is true and that which is love are congruent and identical. The truth that cannot be gotten at by knowledge can be attained through love. For each of you is love. Each of you is created as love, in love, for love.

And now the image that gives this episode its name. You cannot relate to another by saying to yourself, I am love, she is love, we are love. You have only conjugated the sentence. You have not gotten to love yet. But when you realize the ground of your being is love, you can turn to love itself. The connection is not between one and one. It is between one and one with another one, so that there is a go-between, a middle man, and that middle man is love. That entity between you is the truth. When you can see what stands between you and the other not as a wall but as a globe of metaphysical light, you give yourself and the other the space, the time, the patience, the permission to relate imperfectly, to misunderstand, and to work things through very slowly. The illusion will fool all of its children again and again. That does not change the truth of love. Love is not fazed by imperfection.

They offer one more analogy, and I adore it for its unlikeliness. Life is like a glass of sparkling drink, they say, effervescent with trouble, bubbling and storming until the bubbles burst into the air and are gone. That is the experiencing. That is the catalyst. That is the movement. That is the life. And when the bubbles are gone, still the drink is what it was. It has simply gone flat. There were trouble bubbles. There were joy bubbles. And now there are no more bubbles. There is simply the essence that is you. Each of you is a delicious, delectable mixture of everything you have experienced, every distortion you chose, every attempt you think failed and every one you think succeeded. Within the illusion you are almost never accurate about any of that. But the illusion is not about being accurate. It is not about knowing. It is about loving.

So when is it time to stay in a painful relationship, and when is it time to go? Not in knowledge, they say. Not in thinking. Not in planning. It is in the moment when you can let yourself go bubble-free, when you can stop the effervescing and sink into your essence, and become aware of that silent voice that speaks with thunder to those who listen with the heart open. The truth will come out, and you will feel it, not think it. It will be the feeling that feels just right, that feels loving, that feels peaceful. And you may come to that feeling in a moment, or a month, or a year. So much of wisdom lies in waiting, in not forcing decisions, but flowing in cooperation with the energies you sense from moment to moment.

Getting at relationships through the mind is not efficacious. Moving from the open heart is far more efficient.

Between you and everyone you love stands a third presence. It is love itself. Trust the middle man.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Merry Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the merry heart.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group's question was simple and brave. How can we work with relationships and feel safe in doing so?

Q'uo answers by taking you back to before you arrived. Each of you, they say, wanderer or native, came here not only to serve but to do a particular kind of work on yourself. You have been through the school of love before, on this planet or others, and you graduated without perfect understanding. Somewhere along the way you felt the lack of some inner strength, some core of steel, some aspect of the lessons of love not yet realized. So at an unconscious level, each of you asked for this incarnation, asked to go back and attack with appetite and enthusiasm the remaining little tangles of feeling and sensitivity that have knotted through succeeding densities. In the higher densities the veil is lifted and everything is remembered, so there is no chance to work through faith alone. Only here, in the confusion, can you do that particular work. It is so prized, they say, that there are lines waiting to get into your third density at this time.

Let that land for a moment. The confusion is not a bug. It is the feature you stood in line for.

To live at all, they say, is to live by faith. The floor beneath you is hidden. You cannot see your feet or the terrain, and you cannot see the lines linking person to person. The appearances say each entity is a monad, walking alone, and that isolation is a tremendous source of suffering. And yet when an entity stops looking for its feet and simply moves ahead, step by step, something unpredicted happens. The steps of the one who has stopped straining against the blindness are more assured than the steps of the one pressing with urgency against it. Relax. Allow. Let things be. That is the only procedure that gives faith its proper centrality.

Consider your own body, they say. Does your heart ask permission to beat? Do you remember to breathe? The second-density creature carrying you never forgets, never falters. You trust that nature of self completely. Now extend that same trust to your mental, emotional, and spiritual bodies. That is what it means to live by faith.

They offer the image of the watched pot that never boils. Living in faith is turning on the fire and trusting the water to bubble when it is ready. The desire to control survival and comfort is perfectly natural. And yet the learning costs what it costs, and some suffering cannot be avoided. Indeed, they say, it is one of the beauties of your density that you are in confusion and pain much of the time, and therefore more open to rapid learning than one who knows the score.

They speak from experience, and the confession is startling. In their own third density, they say, they had an unusually easy time of it, and so there were depths they never learned, because they had not enough difficulty to break their pride. Each of you, they say, has an inner idol that needs to be cast down. Each of you has this sterling opportunity to break through the defenses, the shells, the masks gathered to defend against feared pains. And the answer to the pains is simply to accept them, to embrace them, to walk through them by faith, seeing the love that is in the moment.

There comes a time, they say, when an entity has disciplined the personality to the point where it can see its own suffering, see the pain and the confusion, and at the same time rest in peace and in faith. In the knowledge that comes to the open heart without proof, that beyond all appearances the one thing to focus upon is love. This matters most when the entity faces itself. Only when you have learned to love and forgive your own self, dark and light mixed together, can you turn open-heartedly to embrace another in intimacy of spirit and mind and body. Until then you remain self-absorbed. After that, you radiate, like the lighthouse, like the fire upon the hill.

See yourself as a fortress, they say, that fortress of flesh that defends and guards and fears. And see the hope of the incarnation as the dismantling of the armament, mask after mask, until the self is transparent and empty, a vessel through which love may flow. The deeper you take this nakedness, the more intimacy you can endure, the more love you can channel. The entity whose pride is dust simply is. And in that bare being lies infinite, unbounded love.

Think of your life in faith as a process of mining, they say. You bring up the ore and sort the dirt from the gems. Each of you is a marvelous, beautiful gem. You are simply in the process of tapping away the dirt that surrounds it. And that tap, tap, tapping will continue as your years increase. That is what you came for. That is what you thought was a glorious chance. So allow the pain to be, for it, like any other sensation, is your sister and your brother.

They leave the group with a benediction I want to leave with you. Go forth rejoicing, for love is all about you, and you can walk by faith with a merry heart.

The gem was never in danger. Only the dirt was ever being removed.

Thank you for listening.

title: When Things Seem Darkest
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: when things seem darkest.

This session comes from a Sunday meditation in the autumn of nineteen ninety-six, and the group asked for the proper relationship to the darker side of the self. What came through is one of the clearest statements in the archive on a subject every seeker meets, and it deserves to be heard slowly.

Q'uo begins with a metaphysical correction. The duality of light and dark, they say, is not the ultimate reality. It is an artifact of incarnation. In order for there to be observed manifestation, there must be duality. Within the original thought of infinite love there lies no shadow. But you and they alike walk the path of duality, moving through densities and vehicles, and in all of that unimaginable variety, duality is the condition of the road. So the light side and the dark side alike are portions of the shell of manifestation, the totality of the self learning within limitation.

Within this dynamic, they say, rest all those who sleep, meaning all who are in incarnation but not yet aware of themselves as consciousness experiencing itself. To the sleeper, the question of how to be does not even arise. But to the sleeper who has awakened, the dynamic becomes useful and very fruitful. Because the polarity of intended action speaks powerfully to the deeper mind, and the more difficult it is to find a positive polarity, that is, the more the dark side is engaged in working through catalyst, the greater the opportunity the seeker has to polarize positively.

Listen to how they put it. When things seem the darkest, when the self sees itself as that darker side, this situation in itself is a gift. The way to open the gift is simply to accept and absorb that awareness of the darker self, while allowing the heart to remain open. When the open heart approaches the darker side, its gift is to be able to know the light while gazing into darkness. In the metaphysical sense, they say, there is no such thing as a disaster. No catastrophe. The light can shine in any darkness. It only takes bringing that truth into conscious awareness to place the dark side safely within the bounds of self, where it cannot cause you to infringe upon the free will of another.

The channeler knew a phrase from the group's late teacher, Don, which Q'uo borrows with delight. The one-hundred-and-eighty-degree rule. Your relation to your dark side, they say, should be one of gratitude and love, for the dark side is what strengthens and enables the light side. Every experience of the darker self burns away pride and egotism. So when you see that side of yourself with its vices in abundance, do not turn away. Embrace it. Love it. Accept it. Forgive it for being.

They reach for the creation story the channeler knows best. The first act of the Creator in the manifested world, they say, was to separate the light from the darkness. And that says it well. The duality is what lets each of us wend our way back. For we did not come from the light or the darkness, if we speak of true origin. Before all created things, that which each of us is, at our base, simply is. Each of you, each of us, is consciousness itself.

Then they describe the inner mechanics with a tenderness I did not expect. Infinite energy streams into your system from the base of the spine upward. Wherever the dark side has left unresolved catalyst, there the instreaming light must stop and dwell with that darkness. So the hope of every seeker is to balance those tangles of self-judgment and self-criticism, and smooth them away with love and tenderness. Sometimes it takes many years to fully address one tangle, one place where you have come up against your darker side again and again and found self-judgment unavoidable. Be patient with yourself, they say. Take each day as a new, unique, one-of-a-kind experience. Do not accept the thought that you can do nothing with this energy. You are Creator and co-creator of your incarnation. Remember the light, and let that memory shine like a lighthouse in the stormy sea of difficult days.

And they name the great allies of this work. A sense of humor. And the ability to appreciate other selves as they too struggle to become what they hope to be. Each of you can be the light for another when that other's light is lost. And each of you will in turn accept with humility the light of others when you are lost and forlorn.

In grasping the necessity of having a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree range of personality, they say, lies a peace that will serve you well. You were never meant to be half a person. The dark was never the enemy of your journey. It was the weight that made the walking real.

When things seem darkest, the light is closest. Keep the heart open, and let it do its work.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Perfect Sheet of Paper
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the perfect sheet of paper.

This session is different from the others in this set. It is the thirty-first session of the Aaron-Quo Dialogues, conversations between two voices, Aaron and Q'uo, speaking through the same circle. The question was about channeling itself. Since we are all channels, how can we bring our energy through more purely? What helps us become more clear?

Aaron speaks first, and smiles at the question, because it carries a primary distortion. Your deep concern as humans, they say, is always how do I do it with more purity, with more clarity. The question might be better phrased, how do I do it with more love. What bringing love guarantees is greater compassion. And then the sentence that reframes the entire spiritual project. If you plan to allow the universe to channel through you with absolute purity, they ask, then why are you in incarnation? It is easy on their plane. Here is the greatest gift, to allow the expression of the universe filtered through the human. You are not here to learn perfection. You are here to learn faith and love. The fears that arise in you are not problems. They are gifts, reminders to have compassion for this human vehicle. Can you see, they ask, that it is only fear that drives the desire for perfection, and not love?

So Aaron rephrases the question into two better ones. How do I become a channel that offers what is most needed, in the deepest spirit of love I can hold? And when I experience distortion, how do I greet it with love? Q'uo takes up the theme. You dwell in two worlds, they say. There is the earthly vehicle, the mortal, limited, problem-solving brain. And there is the citizen of the universe that you also are, infinite, eternal. The concept that will most clear the channel goes against logic. Do not try to rise above the body. Move back down into the basement of the house, into the lower energies, and join with them lovingly, without judgment. You worked hard to earn this body. Do not brush it aside. The opening of the heart is possible only when the seeker gives up on the intellect and moves in unknowingness. The seeker lives in faith.

Aaron returns with the image I will remember this session by. I call them the angel and the earthsuit, they say. You are angels in earthsuits. If you wanted only to be angels, you would not have chosen to incarnate. Anyone can manifest with great love as an angel. The challenge is to do it in the earthsuit, and to bring the two into balance. Then the story. Imagine leading a group down a mountain when the weather turns and the snow closes in. The path is steep, the cold is deadly, and you caught only a glimpse of the way before the clouds rolled in. Do you wait for someone else, or do you lead, unprepared as you are? And the real question is this. When is it ego that says, I will lead, and when is it love? When is it the small self, wanting to be the hero, and when is it the large self, acting in service to all beings? Both voices will be present. That is the human experience. If you strike out at the small self in anger, you shut out everything, including love's voice. But if you hear it and say, quietly, I hear you, I hear how afraid you are, then it quiets. And you can reopen to the greater self, still whispering, we must get these people off the mountain. Together, it can be done.

And then the paper. Take a smooth white sheet, they say. Wad it into a ball. Squeeze it tight. Open it out, and it is filled with wrinkles. Can you see that the perfect sheet still exists? It has not gone anywhere. The wrinkles exist too. Neither truth is denied. The only question is which you choose to practice. When you are busy attacking the wrinkle, you are giving solidity to it. You are practicing the wrinkle.

They trace how this works with the thought of unworthiness. The wrinkle is the belief that you are unworthy. Striving to become worthy sets up a contraction every time there is a chance to be generous. Release the whole notion of the self that must be fixed. Observe the fearful self with kindness, and the heart knows what to do. There is no more giver. There is no more clinger. Giving happens. The fear does not disappear. The guide on the mountain is still afraid when they take the first step. The challenge is not to be fearless. It is to bring love where there is fear. Watch the patterns come and go. A loving heart knows what to do.

Aaron closes with a teaching drawn from two traditions, the Buddhist three kayas and the Christian Trinity, the ever-perfect and its expression in form. The inner core and the outer expression are not separate. The negativity in you is not the opposite of the divine. It is a distortion of the divine. And love, too, is a distortion of the divine. There is nothing there but God, sometimes expressed with great distortion. How do you reduce the distortion? By offering forgiveness and kindness. Only love dissolves negativity. Do not chase your fear away with a big stick. Hold out something sweet in your hand, and invite it to come and take a taste. The perfect sheet was never lost. It was only ever wrinkled. And the wrinkles, loved enough, smooth themselves.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Pure Spring
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the pure spring.

This session comes from the Aaron Q'uo dialogues, and the group brought one of the hardest questions there is. We mean to do no harm. We mean to offer our energy in love. And still, sometimes harm is what comes out. How do we work with our own distortions, so we can offer ourselves more clearly, with less harm?

Before the teaching begins, Barbara leads the group in a Buddhist practice of purification. With deeds of loving kindness, I purify my body. With truthful communication, I purify my speech. It sets the tone for everything that follows.

Aaron starts with an image that carries the whole session. Think of yourself, he says, as a streambed. A pure spring rises and flows through you. The water from the spring is always pure. But the streambed gathers debris. Silt settles to the bottom. Pollutants fall in. And whoever drinks downstream gets cloudy water.

I love the honesty of this image. He does not say: keep the water perfectly pure. The purity of the spring never changes. You bring fear into it, greed, anger, and for a while the water is cloudy. Then you clean the streambed, and the water is pure again.

And here is the turn that I think is the whole teaching. When you pollute the water, what do you do? Most of us turn on ourselves with shame and judgment. And Aaron says that is the real problem. Not the pollution. The shame. Listen to how he puts it. Your self judgment, even your sense of shame, are not ways of being responsible. They are deterrents to responsibility. What are you going to do, sit there and condemn yourself while others drink your poisoned water? Or are you going to go and clean it up?

He makes it practical. There are two areas of work. First, deepen the intention to offer your energy with love, so you pollute the water as little as possible. Second, accept that because you are human, you will pollute it sometimes, and then be responsible for what you have created. Clean it up simply. Observe the source of the pollutant and close it off. If the source is anger, open your heart to it. Make a bigger container for it within you, so it does not need to pour out into the world. Anger is not bad, he says. Anger is just energy. When there is a lot of it, it needs a big space.

One of his favorite practices comes from Thich Nhat Hanh. Breathing in, I am aware of my anger. Breathing out, I smile to my anger. Again and again, until you feel the space enlarging. Then, once the distortion has stopped pouring out, mop up. Ask for forgiveness. You cannot ask while distortion is still pouring out. You attend to it first, and then you mop up.

Then Q'uo speaks, and I want to linger on what they offer, because it gives the session its second anchor. They take up the question this group returns to again and again. Where is the love in this moment?

Ask it, they say, and abide in faith with patience, and that which is sought shall come to you. If you can come to the present moment and know it, you have entered eternity. If, when you come to that present moment, your question is where is the love, in that moment you have entered love.

They go further. The way the question is asked is far more important than what is asked, for the attitude that asks the question is the point of view that will limit the answer. So abide in love, and look in all things for love, even with rage, with fury, with the strongest and heaviest of emotions. There is at the heart of that emotion a purity, an essence. And there is the same beauty in those dark colors as in the light ones, for they create variety and depth in a tapestry.

Aaron returns to close, and he asks a question that stays with me. Do you think you teach more when what flows through you is absolutely pure? Or could it be that you teach more when what flows through you becomes distorted, and then you very lovingly attend to that distortion, helping others learn that they do not need to be perfect, only conscious and responsible?

He tells of a teaching given to the instrument by a discarnate guide. Let go of everything. Give everything away. At first she wondered if that meant her house, her car. Then she understood. Are you identified with your fear, your unworthiness, your shame? Give away the identity with it. To be a servant is not to be somebody but to be nobody. Let the divine make use of whatever moves through you, in ways the divine itself determines.

His last instruction of the night is the simplest. Watch for the contractions. When a loud noise startles you, your body energy contracts around it. Fear contracts.
