That personality you think of as yourself, the whole drama of preferences and plans, is perhaps one or two percent of your total being. The rest lies in the roots of mind, and it is there that the sorting of will and faith actually happens.

Meditation opens the door between the two, if only ajar. Time in the silence is time spent listening to the voice with no sound, which does carry messages of faith and choice. But not to a schedule.

And this is where the seeker loses the one quality that supports the whole enterprise. That quality is patience.

There is a refrigerator magnet this instrument has seen, and I cannot resist repeating it: Lord, give me patience, and give it to me right now. That is the third-density mind kidnapping the spirit. To be content to wait, they say, is the best resource the seeker has. For the one who does not mind waiting, results can often come quickly.

Patience lies within you, they say, a powerful, slumbering, elegant beast. If you are seeking spiritually, there is no friend more faithful than patience. There is no challenge that cannot be won with patience.

Letting go of the surface of things. Resting in the mid-air of not knowing. This is an art, and it is the one they encourage you to practice.

And here is the strangest comfort in the session. In reality, they say, time and space do not exist, and there is no possibility of making a wrong choice. For all has already occurred, and all is perfect.

I know how that lands. For minds that cannot hold it, they simply say, we accept that. They are not trying to make sense. They are sharing how things look from where they stand.

What you are really doing, they suggest, is not making the choice but becoming the person who brings the most desire to the choice. To hone the desire. To move within those old words, not my will but Thine, not once or twice or a hundred times, but with every breath. To consume the self in the divine, until you have only to say, oh, see, I should do this now.

It is difficult to let go. The soft spot where this is possible is surrounded by hard rocks on every side. But they offer one practical mercy for the scheduled mind. If no answer comes before your deadline, perhaps that silence is itself the information.

When the right time comes, you will know the choice the Creator has for you. You will feel it to your bones, to the end of your heart, to your depths. And you will be able to jump on it with all of yourself.

In a moment you shall know. Yes or no. And for you, that will be the correct decision.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Reflected in Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love reflected in love.

The question on this February Sunday is about guides. What guides are available to us? How are they available? How do we gain access to them, and feel that we are being guided?

Q'uo begins by saying the subject is peculiarly unsuitable to words. And then, beautifully, they use a great many words to show you why.

First, personhood. You think of yourself as the flesh on the bones, the face in the mirror. But that personality shell, as real and sacramental as it is, is a shallow and limited selection of your self, chosen for the challenges of this incarnation. Next to your whole self, they say, it is as insubstantial as a shadow.

Within that limited mind you have direct connection to all energy whatsoever. The entire universe is within you. And it is in the deeper strata of self that the many kinds of guidance dwell.

This is one of the quiet gifts of silent meditation. When the inner silence is entered, the door between the conscious and unconscious mind opens. For some with a bang. For most at a slow, steady pace, with occasional leaps.

Then, vibration. If one word could describe the manifested world, they say, it would be vibration. Heat is a vibration. Light is a vibration. And so are qualities, consciousness, essences. The first vibration is the infinite love of the one Creator, and each of you is a system of distortions of that vibration.

The goal of the seeker, very simply put, is to become more and more congruent with the undistorted vibration of love.

Now the question of guides looks different. You are not asking a friend to talk to you. Unless you specifically wish for a named inner-plane teacher, and for that they recommend studying the Eastern systems, where the cultures make room for such guides, what you are really doing is tuning yourself to a level of vibration.

In the Western frame, guidance more often comes as contact with a consciousness field of a certain vibration. A feeling of the way. A tentative moving toward orientation with your own deeper energies.

It is not necessary to have any particular vision of your guide. But it helps, they say, to choose a mythical system you feel kinship with, Christianity, Buddhism, any cosmology that feels like home. Not as a matter of the mind, but of the emotions and the spirit. It organizes the effort. It gives you starting points.

This instrument, for instance, asks to be led by what she calls the Holy Spirit. In choosing that, she has done two things. She has placed her trust in a certain kind of entity. And she has called upon herself. For guidance comes from the deeper self.

Here is the sentence the whole session bends toward. All guidance is from your self, in a less distorted configuration of vibration, to the self within incarnation.

I love that line, because it dissolves the whole anxious machinery of seeking signs. The universe is far from blank. It is filled with the vibration of all that there is. Guidance is always very, very near.

The teacher known as Jesus said, he who has ears to hear, let him hear. And this instrument lives it, finding conversation with the forces of nature, an overheard comment, a chance happening. Anything and everything is material, because to her all things are sacramental.

You may be someone else's guide, too. Be aware when questions are asked of you. For that which is love may speak through you, if you are empty enough and clear enough.

And when emergencies seem to demand instant guidance, remember the greatest friend of the seeker. Sister patience. Wait for the rhythm of things to come into the configuration that is harmonious and right. When the moment of rightness comes, there is no doubt. Only awareness, and great gratitude.

What is happening, beyond all systems of thought, is energy relating to energy. Love reflected in love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Pride of the Seeker
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the pride of the seeker.

The question on this March Sunday is about spiritual pride. We all meet it sooner or later. Some say it comes up last, the culmination of all our work. What is it, how do we work with it, and is there a right time to face it?

Q'uo begins, as they often do, by stepping back. What is pride, in general? It is always pride in something. Strength, delicacy, abundance, work, relationships. And there is nothing more distorted about pride than there is about the illusion in general.

The illusion teaches you to take pride in what you do. Strangers open conversation by asking about work. It is awkward to walk up to someone and ask, what sort of vibration do you have? What kind of being are you? Entities tend not to take pride in who they are, in the being they express moment to moment.

Then they tell the old story from the Christian scriptures, of the two men praying. One in fine clothes, listing his devotions: I give, I fast, I pray without ceasing. Beside him a beggar, saying only, Lord, have mercy on me, a sinner.

Can you see the walls that have risen around the rich man, they ask? The wall of wealth, of dress, of possessions, of actions. All offered sincerely, all offered as accomplishment. And behind those walls he cannot see the one thing he shares in total equality with the beggar. The human state itself.

For it seems to each human, without any evidence, that she is alone. That the walls of skin cut the self off from oneness with all else. The infant learns what hurts, and the walls go up around the young heart. Don't touch the stove. Don't pick up the dog. Don't, don't, don't. By adulthood, the entity is to some extent controlled by fear.

And here they make a move I did not see coming. They change from pride to fear. Because, they say, the only catalyst dealt with in third density is fear and love.

The entity begins wrapped in love, and learns to close itself, to become defended, because there are things to fear. So the whole spiritual life can be described as learning how to love, or learning how to release fear. For fear is that distortion of love which posits a separation between beings and things.

I want to read you their image for working with fear, because it is so tender. Picture the fear as a cave of safety, with a stout blanket over the opening to hold back what you dread. If you rip the blanket away, you must face everything at once. But if you sit with the fear, accept it, stay conscious of it, then gradually you can make a small opening in the blanket, and venture a step or two into the world beyond the cave.

Not ripped away. Eased open. That is the pace of real transformation.

And spiritual pride, they say, is what remains when the fears have been shaken and the cave has been left. It is the distortion peculiar to those who have worked hardest to realize who they are. As long as you think you have a self you must defend, you are working with it. If you are still thinking, I am living my own life, you are not yet beyond it.

Coming into fuller awareness, they say, is not a process of addition but of subtraction. Simplification. The elimination of things from the defended self, until the self is empty and the barriers are down.

Is that safe to do in this density? No, they say plainly. Not in the sense of preserving the body or the emotions. But it is not a terrible thing to be working with pride, or with fear. This is what you came to do. This is your subject matter: fear and love, boundaries and unity.

They close with the prayer this instrument repeats each time she tunes, the prayer of Saint Francis. Lord, make me an instrument of Thy peace. Where there is hatred, let me sow love. Where there is injury, pardon. Where there is discord, union. Where there is doubt, faith. Where there is despair, hope. Where there is darkness, light. Where there is sadness, joy.

It is the outcry, they say, of the soul that wishes to be free of self and subsumed into service. The darkness that separates. The light that joins.

So be content. Do not give up on the self because it still has distortions. You are not supposed to be without illusion. You are here to live within distortion by faith, trusting the plan that placed you here, trusting that all that is yours will come to you, and that you need only ask: Thy will for me today, what is it? And I will try my best.

That is all you must do.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dark Night of the Soul
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dark night of the soul.

The question on this March Sunday is about change. The big kind. The initiations and transitions that rearrange a life. What is the balance between doing something and letting things happen? Between the work of the heart and the work of the mind?

Q'uo steps back first, to describe the ground the drama plays on. Each of you, they say, is as a hologram of the creation. Beneath all the noise there is a spot in the awakened soul, far below sense and rational thought, where the spirit knows itself. An essence that does not change with time or occasion.

When moments of that clarity come, they say, etch them into memory. The bare memory of the realness of self is a balm against the difficult passages. It is the one resource that does not wear out.

Then they do something honest. They use the word suffering. When the life of flesh is born, it begins to change, and within each transformation there is decay, there is loss. And there is that terrible interval when loss has occurred but new life has not yet become apparent.

Those times, which this instrument calls the dark night of the soul, are times of gravest pain and bewilderment. And the mind, which is a problem-solving organ, cannot solve them. The brain was built to make choices for the safety of the vehicle. It cannot think its way to peace of heart or grace.

I find that distinction clarifying rather than discouraging. It explains why the cleverest analysis fails at three in the morning. The mind is the wrong tool for this depth. It is within the heart and the deeper emotions that spiritual change takes place.

The heart is already holy ground, they say. The mind must think itself sacred. But awaiting in the innermost heart is the Creator, that intelligent infinity that so curiously loves every spark from which it is learning about itself.

And if the pain you carry feels heavier than you can hold alone, please reach for real support, a trusted friend, a counselor, a crisis line. There is no shame in asking for a hand.

The session then turns to the past, to old trauma and buried programming. And here is the teaching I want you to hear carefully. The crystallized nuggets of pain are usually treated like weeds to be pulled up by the roots. But that approach only builds thicker walls around them.

The issue, they say, is forgiveness. One cannot give the pain away. One can only give away what one has forgiven oneself for feeling. And the key is forgiveness of self, forgiveness of others, forgiveness of humanity.

When that final iota of forgiveness arrives, it is as though someone has lifted a burden from the shoulders. You cannot force the moment. You can only persist in the desire. Ask, and you shall receive. Knock, and it shall be opened.

They speak of the one known as Jesus, who deliberately took suffering and dedicated it to the suffering of all beings, opening his arms to the world. And they suggest you can do something like this in your own measure. Take upon yourself the sorrow of the world, not to be crushed by it, but to say: I want there to be less suffering, and this is what I can do.

Gaze with a cold eye upon the suffering involved in transformation, they advise. It is the one who can look at the dark night with an indifferent eye but a full and willing heart for whom the process begins to come easier.

By releasing and yielding to your suffering, by welcoming what must be suffered as a brother and a sister, the heart opens as if by magic. And you find that no matter how intensely you hurt, it does not kill. It cleanses. It empties. It renews.

There is a line near the end that stopped me cold. All that I have, this I give to you. Do with me what you will. I am a boat. Life is the ocean. Toss me somewhere. I shall attempt to sail.

That kind of abandon, they say, is powerful. Embrace the darkness, and you embrace also the light that follows. For in the dark night there is a moon setting and a sun rising, and that sun is a glory beyond all space and time.

You are never alone in this process. Unseen, they hover, waiting to comfort, looking for any glimmer of hope within you. May each of you help each other find the way home.

Thank you for listening.

title: Distortions of Distortions
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: distortions of distortions.

The question on this April Saturday begins with a line from Ra. The source of all distortion is the limitation of the viewpoint. Given that each of us brings distortions into the illusion, how do they affect what we produce in a lifetime, our families, our work, our service?

Q'uo starts at the very bottom of the metaphysical ladder. All that there is in the manifested world, they say, is distortion. The lack of distortion, when absolute, describes the Creator in its unmanifest state. The first distortion is free will, which produces the Logos, intelligent energy, what your scientists call the photon, or light.

So when they greet you in the love and the light of the infinite Creator, they are greeting you in distortions. Were they to come as undistorted Creator, they would have no being in a manifested universe at all.

I love the vertigo of that. It means distortion is not a flaw in the plan. It is the plan.

When they gaze at a distorted personality, then, at the tangles of energy blockage that look to others like an unbalanced character, they see distortions of distortions of distortions. Systems of energy, all of them distortions of the one great original Thought, which is love.

And here is the mercy in it. That you are distorted in such and such a way is not bad or wrong. Before incarnation, each entity selected the personality shell containing exactly those gifts and limitations that would set up both the learning and the service of this lifetime.

The biases show up early as simple preferences. Things the young spirit likes, things it avoids. And through the years the same crossroads return, again and again, reliably and dependably. Each spirit faces one or more basic incarnational questions, and the choice can be made fresh each time, for service to others or service to self.

This instrument, for instance, came to learn to give without expectation of return. To that end, certain biases were chosen. Just so, each of you arranged the circumstances that would give you the catalyst you wanted.

But there is a twist of fate in it, and they are honest about that. Gifts are not necessarily used for what you think they should be used for. Because you can play the piano, it is not necessarily your fate to become a pianist. The delicacy of hearing, the dexterity of mind and muscle, have metaphysical uses that have little to do with music.

Biases in the form of talents do not equate from talent to expression. There is always the mystery of the rhythm of destiny, which, if listened for and heeded, eases the accomplishment of what was metaphysically hoped for, however illogical it seems in Earth terms.

The circle had asked a pointed version of this. How can three such unbalanced, distorted entities produce a pure channeling? And the answer is the heart of the session. Metaphysically speaking, it is the intention, the desire, and the hunger of the entity in visualizing service that creates the service. Not the system of distortions.

The distortions chosen by each of the three were exquisitely useful in creating an atmosphere where three confused and highly distorted entities could support each other's desire to serve, with a purity of intention honed over time.

Seen by human eyes, each entity is less than perfect. Seen as systems of energy that may harmonize, distortions may be most fortunate and most powerful in combination.

Later in the session, a questioner asks about her father, who died the previous summer, and the strong sense of his presence with her. Q'uo answers with unusual tenderness. When entities leave the Earth plane, there is healing to do, and often part of that healing is keeping company with those still living with whom there is a deep connection.

It is not necessarily a message, they say. It is enjoyment. Appreciation that could not be felt within incarnation, seen now from the wider standpoint. In most cases where there is that intuition of presence, the source is the other self, relating from larger life as part of its healing.

And if you are grieving someone you love, be gentle with yourself, and lean on the people and supports around you. You do not have to carry it alone.

You chose your distortions before you came. They are not mistakes. They are the instruments you tuned for exactly this music.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Prodigal Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the prodigal heart.

The question on this April Sunday is about gratitude. How does it work, metaphysically? It is said to be a powerful force, just to be alive, just to be breathing. How does gratitude change our spiritual growth, even in the worst of situations?

Q'uo begins by naming the difficulty honestly. Within the illusion, the atmosphere is not full of clarity but of confusion and negative-seeming emotion. The heart wants solitude and peace and beauty. What the world offers is crowded and shaking.

No one who takes incarnation on a third-density planet, they say, is hoping for a clear and peaceful existence. You came hoping to be utterly confused, and yet to remember, somehow, those truths that can only be known by faith.

The search for true thankfulness has to begin with identity. What is the spirit, that it should feel anything at all? Each of you begins with a spark of light that is your essence and core, in no way different from or lesser than the Creator itself. For it, as all things, is infinite and divine love.

The clay you are formed from expresses that love, but is not that love. The essence of you is closer than your body, closer than your breathing. You are love.

When one can realize that, even for a moment, the seeker has feet on solid ground, and can say to the world however it comes: I am love. I am in a state of utter confusion. But I am love. This is my nature. I take this on faith.

I love that as a starting posture. Not I am grateful, which can be forced. But I am love, which is simply true, underneath whatever the day contains.

They warn that gratitude cannot be approached head-on. It comes as a natural efflux from the soul that is willing to be still and let the world find its balance within. Your culture teaches the opposite: that worth is in what you do, that ambition is the path. And so helpers look like allies and obstacles look like enemies, and thankfulness gets rationed out to whoever serves the plan.

Then they do what teachers do when words fail. They tell a story. The prodigal son.

A wealthy man has two sons. The younger demands his inheritance, runs to the city, and burns through everything until he is living with the pigs, eating what the pigs eat. It occurs to him that his father's slaves eat better than this. He will go home and beg to be taken on as a servant.

But when the father sees him coming, he rejoices, and orders a great feast. The older son is furious. I stayed. I obeyed. You never killed a fatted calf for me. And the father says, don't you see? I thought I had no son, and now I do.

Look at the gratitude in all of them, Q'uo says. The father, grateful to have his son back. The prodigal, grateful to be accepted even as a slave. And the older brother, whose hard heart comes from never having done anything wrong enough to need forgiving.

Each of you is a prodigal, they say. Each of you has squandered precious things. Each of you humbly seeks to return to the house of the Father, to that place of love undefiled. And in that state, gratitude is natural and flows effortlessly.

Why is gratitude so powerful? Simply because it is the truth. In truth, everything that occurs to you is a gift. Each situation delivers the sisters and brothers of experience. Sister Sorrow. Brother Pain. Brother Anger. Sister Depression. Each spirit has its own difficult guests, and each comes bearing gifts.

The mind rebels against this. The mind wants to sort everything into neat piles. This is that, this is the other. But the spark of true self within you is ever ready to spread and illuminate the heart.

If you can live within the open heart, you may begin to see each day as part of a dance that is all too short. A dance of rhythm and grace. And the attitude of gratitude will come easier and easier, until you experience whole days for what they really are: one moment, one now, ever fresh, ever beautiful, ever perfect.

The power of a thankful heart is truly infinite. May your heart have the benefit of your protection, your nurturing, your care.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Lamp on the Hill
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the lamp on the hill.

The question on this May Sunday is about the longest journey a seeker takes. Not across the world, but from head to heart. It is easy to understand, intellectually, that all things happen in their time. It is another thing entirely to wait for that time, and accept it.

Q'uo begins with an image. Each of you, they say, is a lamp upon a hill. It is not your light that lights the lamp. It is the Creator's. What you can do, as you work with mind and heart, is little by little clean the panes of your lamp, so they become transparent and the infinite light can shine through.

I keep that image with me. You do not manufacture the light. You maintain the glass.

The difficulty is that your culture works against this journey at every turn. It values accomplishment of every kind as a positive asset, and motionless being as a zero, or worse. The list of things to do for the day may never seem as important as the yellow wheat in the field, or the blue of the sky, or the tips of the trees embracing the air with new leaves.

There is slim value for being within your culture. And this is the key disadvantage for the journey from head to heart. For the head is the place where things get done. The heart is the place where things get cherished and cared for.

For the head there are choices, right and wrong, left and right. For the heart there is the flowing of things. Into the heart, time and space themselves flow. For each of you is a citizen of eternity, taking part in time in order to learn and to serve.

Now the practical question. How do you neutralize a lifetime of training? It cannot be done with the head. To attempt with the mind to move the center of being from mind to heart, they say, is to hire a rustler to protect the cattle.

Instead they introduce the concept of the will. Choose a principle that speaks to you most deeply of infinity and eternity, and deposit there every bit of will and faith and hope you possess. This instrument gave her life to the one known as Jesus the Christ. Yours may be another name. What matters is the surrender of the small will to something infinite.

And the tools? The first and always the central one is time spent with the Creator. Time being with the Creator.

The eyes that see the world see a human being sitting. The heart within knows a different reality. See yourself as a pilgrim walking up to the door of an inner sanctum, inserting the key of silence, walking in and sitting, not with other human beings, however worthy, but with the infinite Creator.

This communion awaits you constantly. It is not that the Creator is not with you. The Creator is your companion from the instant of your beginning. It is the self within incarnation that forgets where to go to tabernacle with the infinite One.

Sit in silence daily, they urge, and allow the Creator within to make itself known. With no words. With no dramatic fanfare. But that still, small voice whose message is far beyond concept, and whose surety is absolute.

The eventual goal is to gradually replace expectation with curiosity. The mind grasps and holds and tries to control the rhythm. In the spiritual sense, the only control is in how you surrender the small will to an infinite One whose wish for all is to give and to receive love.

Each time you catch yourself in imaginary conversations, in circles of worry, knocking against the corners of life, stop. Remember that you are a child of the Creator, a child of eternity, a child of love itself. You need do nothing but welcome the rhythmic and rightful destiny that awaits.

It matters not what is occurring on the surface of your life, they say, as long as you are attempting to be an instrument of love, a harbinger of peace.

Practice being. At odd moments, allow yourself simply to be aware, resting in that deep peace that is awareness of the Creator. You will get lost in the sea of confusion again and again. But that too is illusion.

Trust the heart within. And may you see all things with the eyes of love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dance of Relationship
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dance of relationship.

The question on this May Sunday is about the place where the spiritual life gets the least theoretical. Relationships. The doubt, the fear, the lack of trust. How do we resolve these difficulties skillfully? How do contemplation and prayer bring harmony between people?

Q'uo answers that relationships are not a distraction from the spiritual path. They are the path. The heart of the third-density experience for which you took incarnation.

Your whole makeup calls you to be with each other. And it is in learning how to love a mate, a companion, a friend, a family member, that we learn by reflection how to love ourselves, and how to love the creation.

They sketch the densities briefly, and it is worth hearing. First density learns manifestation, rock and ocean and fire. Second density learns movement toward light, the flower turning to the sun. Third density is the first in which spirit finds conscious expression. And its work can be put as one question: how do you wish to serve?

Service to self, or service to others. Two poles of a magnet. And each of you begins in the middle, in a well of inertia, with no charge at all.

What moves you is not grand decisions but small ones. Whether to share your peanut butter sandwich with the other kids in fifth grade. Whether to sit with the kid with the broken leg. Whether to help the parent who seems to need it.

I love that they reach for childhood memories instead of abstractions. The whole graduation of a soul, they are saying, is decided at the lunch table.

Each choice polarizes you a little more. Not based on evidence, but on faith. Faith that the love and hope and charity you feel in your heart are real, and not foolish or naive.

Faith only matters where knowledge is absent, and in third density the truth is hidden from you on purpose. There will never be proof that would stand up in a court of law. It is only when there is no way to prove belief and hope and love that choosing them has metaphysical weight.

And here is why relationships are the great schoolroom. The people you see occasionally get your Sunday self, your dazzling best. But a mate sees everything. For mates, the performance is impossible. Thank heavens, they say, for that impossibility. For it is necessary that we have catalyst to work with.

The friction is the teaching. The pain and suffering and not understanding, the wondering, this is the friction we need to move us toward learning. And as we learn, we begin to see each situation not just as a situation but as an opportunity to find the love in it and express that love.

What do people fear most in relationship? Being betrayed. Offering trust and having it broken. There is within each the dancer that would fly and soar in joy. And yet when we let that self out we are as foolish as little lambs in the pasture, and easily squashed.

So it is a scary thing to surrender to love. Are we not all love, underneath?

This instrument's favorite centering question comes up here, and I want to give it to you plainly, because it is the most practical tool in the whole session. Where is the love in this moment?

Ask it when you are confused. Ask it when you are hurt. Each of you is love, a projection into manifestation of the infinite love that created all that there is. In relationship, especially the mated relationship, that awareness is a healing balm for those who feel abandoned or rejected or misunderstood.

They close with a dance. All of nature and humankind is engaged in a dance with meter and rhythm, and the plants and animals know the steps. The moon and the sun and the stars dance also. And within each of us there is that completely aware dancer.

To that part of you, there is no such thing as waiting. There is only pausing and resting until it is time for the next step. But to the human heart, anxious to put things right, there seems to be no rhythm, no cue for when to enter the stage.

So wait for the rhythm to catch up. Reject the hopelessness of the situation. Rest. And trust that the still, small voice will tell you when to come in, and what to say.

You are crucial to each other. You may smile at a hopeless stranger in passing, and that realness may jolt them out of hopelessness into hope. You do not know what you do. You cannot know the impact you have as a being.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Fool's Leap
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the fool's leap.

The question on this September Sunday is about acceptance. Several people in the circle are facing changes, a move, a new job, a new situation at home. How do we accept what the universe gives us when it does not look like what we wanted?

Q'uo gently renames the question. Acceptance, they say, has overtones of toleration, of something grudging. Their word would be faith.

Years ago, when this instrument lay close to death in a hospital bed, she put a motto above the bed. It read: faith, the final frontier. She wanted the joy of acceptance. And she knew it would not come from arguing with reality.

Faith, they confirm, is a foolish thing in any rational sense. It is the archetypal image of the fool walking off the cliff into dead air.

This instrument thinks of the cartoon coyote, sprinting at top speed past the edge of the cliff and continuing to run on nothing, until he realizes there is no more cliff beneath him. That realization is what sends him plummeting.

Or Peter on the water. At the teacher's call he steps out of the boat and walks on the waves, until he realizes he is on water. As his faith falls prey to rational observation, he sinks like a stone.

So each of you, full of faith, is vulnerable to accusations of foolishness. Like any fool, there is almost no answer that will satisfy the critic.

Then something remarkable happens in the transcript. There is a long pause. Q'uo deliberately gives the instrument no words for several seconds, to demonstrate the very energy they are describing.

The instrument did not rush to fill the silence with her own opinions. She was content to be silent if they were silent. And they point to that as the lesson. It took her years to learn it. Each of you has spent lifetimes working on this precise discipline.

When you are not within the veil of forgetting, they say, you are full of faith and power and purity. You have been eons in development. And yet within the shell of personality, how difficult, how impossible it is to remain aware of who you are.

They offer an image for your situation. You are as the unhatched egg. This world of shadow is your time of being unborn, developing the being that shall hatch at the entrance to larger life. Within the shell is marshaled infinite power, wisdom, and love. Within the shell lies the food you shall need, the drinks of water that are guidance, inspiration, and hope.

Unlike the egg, your shell is large. You may move about. You may express yourself in many ways. But you are constantly and infinitely protected. Each moment you have in this illusion is precious, for it can be given only the one time.

So be alert. The winds of your thoughts are rich with useful concept. Guidance comes by sign, by metaphor, by physical experience. As you notice coincidence and synchronicity and pattern, your environment becomes more and more full of information.

And when the practical mind panics, yes, I have faith, but I need a job, they are wonderfully down to earth about it. Voice your concerns not to yourself but to the Creator. This instrument argues with the Creator. The Creator does not mind.

Have conversations with deity, however you envision that, at any length, with any emotional import whatsoever. When you talk with the Creator, you open lines of energy in the deep mind that marshal forces helpful to you.

Let your faith be in something you can talk to. Let the Creator be real to you.

There is a Zen saying this instrument loves: I held stones in my mouth for twenty years until I learned to be silent. Where does the urge to fill the silence come from? There is a fear of the unknown, the ineffable, the trackless. And yet that is the very material your soul came here to work with.

You wished to place yourself at risk. You made yourself vulnerable in order to have this opportunity to work on faith.

So strive, they say. Help your situation in every logical, rational way you can. But when those things are done and concern remains, then walk upon the water. Jump into mid-air. Toss yourself into the sea of confusion, in faith that the Creator will toss you where you are to go, and bring you the fish you need to eat and the water you need to drink and the understanding you need to grow.

For the fool there is a peace the world cannot know. The peace of absolute trust. That the one who watches the sparrow also watches you.

Thank you for listening.

title: What the Heart Desires
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: what the heart desires.

The question on this October Sunday is one of the most human ever brought to the circle. How do we know what our true heart's desire is? Not what we think we want as we go through the day, but what is central to the evolution of the soul.

Q'uo begins with energy, because desire is energy. The energy of desire fills the universe in which each entity lives. And each of you, as a citizen of eternity, has a core vibration, a distortion of the great original Thought which is love, creating a signature as unmistakable as a name.

Your very nature is vibration. And the desires of the heart, known and unknown, have tremendous power to shape circumstance, so that opportunities are offered to learn more concerning those desires.

Then they draw the map of how we desire. On the surface, where most of us skate, desire is simple. The personality says, I want this. The acquisitive person goes and gets it. The careful person saves up for it. Either way, it is treated like a commodity.

But something happens that turns the surface skater into a swimmer. A spiritual awakening goes off like an alarm clock. And the desires of the heart become more complicated, and much less easy to satisfy.

Yet even awake, we keep approaching them the old way, as if the heart's desire could be saved up for like money for a movie ticket. And the desires of the heart are not commodities. They are constantly in evolution, just as your whole being is constantly becoming more of what you truly are.

So how do you find out what you truly desire? They offer an image I like, of the mind as a computer. On the surface there are bells and whistles. But hidden in the programs are powerful subprograms the casual user never sees. You have plunged into those waters now. You have become aware of deep voices within the mind, presences that are the self and yet the oversoul of the self.

In the silence you can put the question: what do I truly desire? And then you can listen. Listening to that graceful and yet muscular silence is a discipline that will never disappoint the persistent listener.

Allow the confusions of the day to slip away, and you enter the heart's holy of holies, where the Creator waits infinitely and patiently. Within you are not only the instructions for this life, but for the you that you are before time was.

And here is the turn that reframes everything. We assume that desire equals the need to fulfill the desire. For the surface life, that is logical and useful. For the life of faith, it does not encompass the experience you set up for yourself.

When you reach the bottom of the personal, incarnational mind, you come to the end of your ability to reason. And there you come to a point of surrender. Working with the personality to see into the deeper energies, you open the underlying desire that feeds all of life.

At the back end of that great long train of desires, they say, you will find a little caboose that reads: I surrender. Not my will, but Thine.

Perhaps that is bad news for those who wish to bend life to their plans. But in the metaphysical realm, thoughts are things, and as the desires of the self and the desires of the Creator slowly synchronize, destiny becomes fluid.

At the bottom of every desire, they say, you will find the desire to cooperate faithfully with the destiny that brought you all you have enjoyed. And the heart, when it is finally pierced through all illusion, desires completely one thing: the opportunity to love and be loved, to breathe in and to breathe out. All else will be as it will be.

One last practical thread, from the writer known as Ken Keyes, whom this instrument admires. Desires in themselves are neither good nor bad. They simply create a bias. Followed too far, the bias becomes an addiction: if I have this, I will be all right; if not, I shall not.

His remedy is to downgrade the addiction to a preference. I prefer that this happen in this way, but I am not addicted to it. It is not necessary. That clear seeing, with the center held in balance, is what lets you surrender without pretending you want nothing.

Be careful what you desire, this instrument often says, for you will get it. So desire carefully. Desire deeply. And then let the deeper desire underneath them all have its way with you.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seasons of the Spirit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seasons of the spirit.

The question on this October Sunday is about the changing seasons of the spiritual life. We want to meditate more, live more peacefully, be more aware. It takes enormous effort to turn those desires into patterns. And just when a pattern holds, something in us needs to change again. A part dies, and a part is reborn.

Is the change caused by our efforts, the circle asks, or does it come because it is time, no matter what we do?

Q'uo begins with the rhythms. There are cycles all through the life: the energies of youth and maturity and age, the cultural divisions of weeks and years, the Monday through Friday that everyone assumes is simply how time works, forgetting that before the days were named, they were all Sabbath days, one as holy as the next.

Some changes are natural, the organism expressing its pattern. Some are imposed by the culture you live in. But the changes weighing on this circle are of another kind. They belong to the spiritual appetite.

Once an entity has awakened to herself as a citizen of eternity, there is no more contentment with the chores of the day. The actuality of spirit works upon the seeker, encouraging the desire to be ever more open, ever more transformed.

And here is the trap. The seeker puts pressure on herself to do more, be better, seek harder, meditate longer. The spiritual ambition becomes another achievement program. And usually she does not fulfill those ambitions, and ends up simply frustrated and irritated with herself.

This instrument has said many times that although spiritual evolution seems like a process of addition, it is often a process of subtraction. And Q'uo agrees.

The bounty the ambition hopes for is not contained in adding activities. It is in moving fully into the present moment, and taking the bounty of that moment as it passes. For each moment is itself, whole and perfect. When you are in the moment, you are not in time.

When you become even a bit aware of the timeless aspect of the moment, there is an almost automatic resonance, a feeling of coming home. And this is accomplished not by adding focus, but by relaxing into the magic of the timeless present. If you are within that present moment, you are in meditation, aware of who you are, aware of why you are here.

They are not telling you to stop meditating. Far from it. But a little meditation goes a long way. And here is a thought worth sitting with: when you cannot get yourself to meditate, it may be that the wisdom of the self is pulling you away, because the organism instinctively knows it cannot handle more change right now.

For that is what meditation actually offers. An enhanced vulnerability to change.

So ask yourself, when the schedule will not hold: what am I stuck on? And how am I not conforming to the needs of my bodily organism? The culture gets you up and shoots you out into jobs and drops you off at night to watch television until too late. That scheduling is not conducive to a natural life.

Many find the first moments after waking are the only time truly their own, and that is why morning meditation is so often recommended. But any point in the day that offers itself is just as good. The important thing is not to do it a certain way, but to have that formal return to the center of the soul.

Play with your schedule, they say. Have fun with it. Vary the ways you meditate. Bend those stiff necks that say it should be done this way. Find new ways, new times, new practices.

And more than anything, they offer this: most spiritual seekers become heavy with their seeking. What penetrates to the heart of self is a weight, a gravity. And yet it is also dancing in the wind, light as a feather.

So keep the light touch. Forgive your judgments of yourself, not because you no longer care to do good work, but because you trust yourself to be doing all that you can.

Be gentle with yourselves, they say. You have hungered and thirsted after truth, and that truth has led you on a merry chase, and continues to disappear into the mystery. Whatever you felt to do this day, that was the right thing for you. Whatever you shall feel tomorrow, that shall be the right thing then.

Lay your concerns down. Relax into this present moment. And know that beyond all telling, you are love, and you came to bear witness to that love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Citizens of Eternity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: citizens of eternity.

There was no group question on this November Sunday. Pot luck, the circle said. Ask about whatever you like.

Q'uo's answer is that every possible thread harmonizes into one subject. Love. After long years of speaking with these seekers, they have found a thousand ways to talk about the love and light of the one Creator. But the basic message remains utterly simple, and infinitely profound.

The simplicity of oneness. Of Creator and created. Gaze up into the night sky, they say, and know there are more ways to speak of love than there are stars on the clearest night. And yet all speaking ends in one thing: that same love that created all that there is.

Then they turn to something tender and personal. This instrument, they say, is troubled by the gap between how others see her and how she sees herself. To those she counsels, she appears finished, accomplished. Within her own judgment, she holds herself unworthy.

And they say this will be true of each person. That each entity is both deeply flawed and utterly perfect.

How can one be both? Within the illusion, you can be seen as the giver and the taker, the wise one and the fool, and both estimates are correct. And in the end no estimate is correct, for within the illusion there is no final righteousness. You live in two worlds at once: the outer world of form and sequence, and the inner world of infinity and eternity.

Your citizenship as a human in incarnation is limited. Your citizenship in eternity is infinite.

Once the seeker has awakened to that citizenship, there is a reorientation that cannot be reversed. It is as a chemical reaction that one cannot undo. Those who try to close the gate find it impossible, for the point of view has shifted, and the creation has become new.

So spend time feeling the newness of life, they urge. Each sunrise. Each relationship. Each beginning. Let the stale air of old opinion be vented and fall away. What is needed this day is a creature of today, not the offspring of old thought.

They give the instrument an image, and I want to leave it with you whole. A traveler moves across a desert, gazing feverishly for water. And all the while, metaphysically speaking, this traveler is in a world made of water.

When you feel you are truly in the desert, when all is dry and lifeless and without hope, practice knowing by faith the watery environment of the human spirit. For what seems dry and dusty on the surface is, in metaphysical terms, a treasure. A canvas on which to paint a self in love with the beauty of the infinite Creator.

You are a citizen of eternity, and you have meat and drink the world does not know of. Let the desert become the ocean, life-giving and new with every tide.

When the circle asks how to love the self on the service-to-others path, the answer is practical and gentle. At the end of the day, review the day in meditation. Watch yourself move through it again. Notice where you accepted yourself and where you did not. And make the conscious effort to accept the self for its full range of expression.

The doing happens in the day, spontaneously. The accepting happens in the quiet afterward. That is the balance of being and doing.

Sit in the silence with the self as a friend. That is the whole instruction.

Thank you for listening.

title: When Anger Turns Inward
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: when anger turns inward.

The question on this November Sunday is a brave one. We feel anger and frustration at ourselves. How can we use these feelings to move toward compassion for ourselves? Is there hope we can change, or should we concentrate on accepting ourselves, anger and all?

Q'uo calls this a move into the heat of the battle. And they remind the circle of something easily forgotten. Before this incarnation, you were not under the veil. You gazed at the possibility of this heavy, confusing life and you chose it. You yearned to enter the sea of confusion completely, to live a life that was a testament of faith and love and joy.

Each of you had to wait for the chance to be here, they say, because so many souls desired to lend their faith to the Earth at this juncture. The fields are white. And each of you is helping, more than you know.

So why the anger? Why the frustration? Here is their answer, and it reframes everything. Many people have no trouble feeling anger and blaming it on the outside world. But each of you has learned that nothing is truly outside you. So the anger turns inward.

Metaphysically speaking, they say, that is a significant advance.

When you are chastising the self, you are consumed with the desire to be better. One of the circle quoted the old line: of myself I can do nothing. And Q'uo picks it up and runs with it.

Things done from the self, without inspiration, will not have the virtue you came to share. How difficult it is to see that actions without love are not useful. And why is it so difficult? Because your culture worships doing.

Listen to this passage, because it is one of the sharpest pieces of cultural criticism in the archive. When entities meet, what do they ask to establish rapport? Very commonly: what do you do? Can you see how far from the heart such a question may take one? It is assumed there will be an employment by which you justify your existence. I am a librarian. I am a teacher. I am a nurse.

And yet each of you has a life within that is compelling and fruitful. The dynamic tension between the portions of self you have discovered in your spiritual work. Realization after realization, year after year.

That inner life is usually shared without words, simply by the quality of being with someone. People come to you for counsel because they sense it. This is the heart of your gift. This is the heart of your incarnation. To be yourself. To meet the moment with your full, open, loving self.

How infinitely difficult that is, on a daily basis. As one of the circle said: if I forget to pay attention for just a moment, it all comes back, and I am back where I started.

They do not offer a simple technique for moving from frustration to the deeper self where love always remains. They do not know a foolproof way. What they offer instead is stranger and kinder.

Persist, they say. Persist with humor, with grace, with style. And it is all right to be ungraceful. It is all right to be awkward, to be behindhand, to be half there and half not. This does not matter. What matters is the continuation of simple attention, the effort to be the best you can, and then to let the rest go.

What a gift it is to yourself, simply to let it all go.

The intellect will keep judging you. You may tell yourself not to judge, but the intellect knows not how to do anything other. So do not take it too seriously. The mind is a portion of the illusion. The intellect is not the same as consciousness.

You have consciousness as a being, as a citizen of eternity. You have an intellect as a function of the illusion. It is enough to separate the two in the abstract, and to remember, when the negative processes rise, that your consciousness is not a portion of the tangle. It remains free to be love.

Just allowing the breath to move in and the breath to move out, while identifying with the consciousness that endures, may bring fresh air into the muddle that life often seems to be.

From the inside, you may feel you are failing. And yet, they say, this is only true within the illusion. The work in consciousness you are doing is only tangential to the events you are conscious of.

So persist. And be glad you are still in the fight. The anger you turn inward is the sign of a soul that has stopped blaming the world, and started taking responsibility for its own becoming.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Children Coming In
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the children coming in.

The question on this late November Sunday is about the newcomers. What kind of souls are incarnating into the Earth plane now? Who are the babies being born in these days?

Q'uo describes three broad groups moving through the nursery doors of the planet.

The first, and still the largest, are third-density souls hoping to graduate, in this lifetime or the next. By and large, they say, perhaps most of those born carry the familiar human vehicle, the old style of body, with the higher centers waiting in potentiation. The hope is that one last lifetime, as this planetary cycle closes, might bring the growth that welcomes fuller light.

The second group is newer, and growing. The pioneers of fourth density. Children born with both the third and fourth density bodies activated. Often, they say, such children show unusually mature thought, an enhanced ability to learn and to create, and a joy in enumerating the beautiful treasures they find.

The third group is the wanderers. They have streamed to this planet in large numbers in the last generation, and much of the strong spiritual support in the arts that people have noticed in these years has come from them.

The wanderer has more in common with the Earth native than with the double-activated child, because the wanderer is fully under the veil of forgetting. The difference is inward, in the region of faith and intuition. The wanderer carries more of an instinctive belief in spiritual coincidence, in the aliveness of all things.

Your planet, they note, has never had a pure or easy history. It has welcomed many populations who did not graduate elsewhere, many archetypal structures layered one over another. It is as though your plane of existence is a classroom filled with those whom other teachers have so far failed to inspire.

But they do not dwell on the confusion. They dwell on the energy. Yours is a planetary sphere full of tremendous energy, full of great power, most often trapped within confusion. And they celebrate the vividness with which your peoples hold ideas. So many entities, they say, are just on the threshold of the level of awareness that shakes down the entire organism and rearranges it.

And they are thirsting for what they are but cannot see within themselves. They are searching for their Creator. They are searching for love.

Then the practical counsel, and it is some of the warmest in the archive. Focus upon the young ones, they say. Whenever you have the chance to interact with children, look into their eyes. Make contact with spirit there.

For in each of the three cases, the entity is an old soul. Full of experience. Full of potential. And each connection with a young one strengthens that child's gifts of faith and will.

If kindness does not come easily to you, they say, then let your kindness be for children. Let the heart open for the young ones.

Find ways to practice devotion to the Creator, and share it as a normal, everyday part of living. Some keep an altar. Some light a candle and meditate. Some walk among the blooms, or watch the birds. There are so many avenues where the spiritual can be taught to children without heaviness or pretension.

Most of all, simply be yourself. For this teaches more than anything else. Children are simpler and less devious in their seeing, and they will appreciate an entity who is herself far more than any mask, no matter how exciting the mask.

You never know what you might say or do, by your mere presence, that might be realization to another.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Manger of the Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the manger of the heart.

The question on this December Sunday, asked as the shadows lengthen on a winter afternoon, is about the entity known as Jesus. What is he doing now? And how can we benefit in our devotional lives from his teachings?

Q'uo will not speculate, through this instrument, about precisely where that entity now works. But they offer something larger than biography. They describe what he was, and what that means for you.

This entity, they say, was one of a social memory complex nearing graduation to fifth density, a group whose common possession was a full consciousness of love and compassion. A love that creates. A love that destroys. A love that transforms. A love that is all that there is.

This love was not yet balanced with wisdom. But it was exquisitely poised, and when the opportunity came, it incarnated into the Earth plane carrying what this instrument calls Christ consciousness.

That complex is now studying the ways of wisdom. But the state of consciousness itself is alive and well within your inner planes, where many teachers who have known it await the work of the Holy Spirit.

Thusly, they say, the Earth plane has never been without Christ, nor shall it ever be without Christ.

And here is the sentence that reframes the whole question of who Jesus was. That energy you know of as Jesus is not owned by an individual. Nor was it owned by an individual while that individual was in incarnation.

The one known as Jesus persistently said: when you hear me, you do not hear me, but my Father. He found himself completely lost to his earthly personality, experiencing oneness with the Creator, with nature, and with each seemingly imperfect human being before him.

There was not enough personality clinging to this Christed being for him to retain a personality shell after his departure. That is how thoroughly the small self had been set aside.

This is why they can say, as this instrument requires of them, that Jesus is Lord, while meaning something precise by it. Not the celebration of an individual, but the recognition of the Lordship that individual carried as his identity, having forgone the normal ramifications of the ego-driven personality.

Wherever we see the Christ within incarnation, they say, that consciousness held by that entity is Lord. One recognizes it as one would recognize an oak tree. It is distinctive. It is perfect of its own kind. A deeply impersonal, infinitely true consciousness that transcends personality and reidentifies the individual as love.

And now the turn toward you. Each of you has the potential to begin to learn to carry the consciousness of Christ within the self.

It is crucial what angle you view the self from. Your culture teaches you to see yourself as personality: characteristics, abilities, biases, hobbies, the whole gamut of human identity. But each who has awakened knows that is only the surface. The personality is truly a shell. What it holds is infinite.

There is no bottom to the roots of consciousness. The roots move into infinity. And the key the one known as Jesus offers is the redefinition of self: the movement from the I of the personality to the I of, when you hear me speak, you hear not me but the Father who sent me.

For each of you was sent into this illusion. Each of you sent itself, to serve as a lighthouse for the light moving into the Earth plane.

It is not that the I of self has the fuel to burn an infinite light eternally. But the awakened self becomes aware that the I that is truly the self is simply moving through the vehicle of personality in infinite energy. What the personality can do is allow the energy that moves through the being, and bless it on its way.

Each of you is a receiver and a sender of energy. All of it can be held, or all of it can be allowed to flow. Each serves by allowing it to flow through with as little distortion as possible. And not simply allowing, but blessing it on its way.

At this season, when the world experiences the shortest days and the longest nights, know this. The baby that lies in the manger in the old story is alive, and lying in the manger in your heart.

Know that the consciousness of Christ is carried by others as well, that there are always Christs within your inner planes. But know most of all that the savior of the world lies within the single unified heart.

For each of you has, in perfect accomplishment, the awareness and the ability to be Christed. And as destiny rules, each of you shall be given your times to express perfect love.

Who am I? Why am I here? What is my service? Whither do I go? Move ever deeper into those questions, past the local personality shell, into the deeper mind.

You are redeemed, loved, cherished, and treasured. By the Christ that was Jesus. By Christ consciousness wherever it is. And by us.

Thank you for listening.

title: Tuning the Tone of Guilt
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: tuning the tone of guilt.

The question on this January Sunday is about guilt. When we feel it, we are overtaken by it, and we do not know where it comes from. Where does guilt come from, and how do we work with it in our spiritual evolution?

Q'uo begins, unexpectedly, with the crucifixion. As this instrument tuned the contact, she challenged them in her usual way, and in the third challenge she named the facet of the Christ that has riveted her for years: the nailing of the body upon the wood, to love others to the point of death.

That image gives us our starting point. The cultural religion keeps the form but removes the fire. What remains is a standard of giving without expectation of return that is, in Earth terms, absolute.

Each of you arrives with a personality largely set up, some with a keener sense of justice than others. Then the culture does its work. Small children are trained in the word should. One should share. One should be respectful. One should behave.

These biases sink into the deeper mind, and each of us is left with a permanent threshold of guilt.

This instrument calls it shoulding all over yourself. And when a sensitive entity takes the club of guilt and beats the self about the head and shoulders, that damage is very real, and the pain very great.

Here is the paradox they want you to see. Those already oriented to service to others, those consciously working on spiritual evolution, accept guilt far more readily than those with a narrower view. So the very entities sensitive enough to be in pain from guilt receive the most guilt from their catalyst. It is as though the Creator were adding insult to injury.

The justice of it is visible only from the standpoint of learning. Guilt, like other painful feelings, is designed to place you where polarization is possible.

When you feel the fear that you have not done enough, and again, enough is relative to your personality and the effort you have made, you are in a strange way asking yourself to polarize further toward service without expectation of return.

But they do not encourage you to obey the feeling automatically. Sometimes that guilty sense of not enough is a knee-jerk reaction, with nothing real behind it. Instead, notice it the way you would notice weather moving through. Evaluate, as honestly as you can, whether there is an actual opportunity for increased service.

When there is none, the guilt is phantom pain, like the ache from a limb long amputated. The form-maker body holds the idea in place out of habit. There is no limb there. There is nothing to do.

They give an example that deserves a gentle pause. The feelings of family after a suicide. Even friends will turn over everything they might have done, had they only known. Though the entity has moved on and nothing can be done, these phantom feelings are very real, and must be dealt with as though they belonged to consensus reality.

If you are living with thoughts of suicide, please reach out now, to someone you trust, a counselor, or a crisis line in your country. You do not have to carry it alone.

When guilt has nothing to work with, the discipline is this. Sit with the feeling. Accompany it. Be one with it. Allow it to express itself, give it respect, be a witness to it. And then, by will, let it go. Let it be balanced by the awareness that all that has been done is all that can be done, and it is time to move on.

When examination shows there truly is more you can do, then the guilt is good catalyst. For it is not only the willingness to serve that creates polarity, but the willingness to work upon the self, to become more capable of giving. The giving of self is a muscle. It atrophies in those who do not use it.

And for those who catch the process and choose a response rather than drowning, there is the deepening of will and faith.

Know this: as love casts out fear, love casts out guilt. Doing all you can helps, but emotionally, enough is never enough. There is no logical end to guilt. It is not subject to logic. It is a tone in the music of the emotional body.

But a tone can be tuned. With prayer and silence and praise, you can tune the emotion called guilt, combing out the fear and self-condemnation, until it rings as a beautiful and true note.

Forgive yourself for being human. Forgive yourself for not being able to sacrifice yourself to the point of death. Acknowledge that the best you could do is not the best, and that is all right. That is as it should be. That is part of the perfection hidden within this sea of confusion.

Rock and hug and love this imperfect being that wants so much to serve. Then send the child within onward with a lighter heart.

And above all, laugh. Take these things a little lightly. Laughter and merriment are most helpful spiritual disciplines, they say, especially for serious students who grow heavy with the wish to do things well.

In all things, find the love. And find within yourself the response to that love which most truly expresses who you are.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Keys Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the keys within.

A winter Sunday in nineteen ninety-nine. The circle asked Q'uo about something every one of them had felt: that slow draining of control over the ordinary day, the sense that you can no longer move anything around you, and whether there is any way to live well inside that helplessness. Q'uo's answer begins with an image, and I love this image. You are a citizen of eternity, they say. That is your true nature. But for this lifetime you have placed that boundless self gently inside a jar of clay, what they call, with real affection, the hairless great ape that carries you around. And the ape's mind was built to solve problems and measure things, and then make a choice. It was never built to hold eternity.

When that small mind is in command, Q'uo says, you get the whole weather system of the rational creature: worry, disappointment, endless problem-solving. But there will never come from it that feeling of ease and spaciousness that is your birthright. Faith is not the product of such a mind. Listen to how they put it. Faith is expressed in the middle of utter confusion, in the midst of the grand chaos that is the nature of your third-density physical illusion. They give the old story of Peter stepping out of the boat and walking on the water beside his teacher, and doing fine, right up until he remembered he was human and humans sink. Faith, they say, is illogical and cannot be defended rationally.

There are rooms in the deep mind, and each opens with its own key. One door is opened only by silence, and Q'uo heartily recommends spending time in silence whenever you can. Thirty seconds. Five minutes. A little silence goes a long way. Another door opens only with the key of patience, and here they slow down to say something I keep returning to. Patience is not pinned to any expectation. If your plans are ambitious, if there is a plan, then each plan is destined to be left behind, and even when a plan comes out exactly right it often does not give the expected feeling. True patience releases expectation entirely and waits with an open heart.

And then there is the door opened by the key of faith. This instrument, Carla, had once been near death, and she taped a message to the wall where she could read it from her bed. It read, Faith, the final frontier, a play on the old star-voyaging phrase. Q'uo pull it from her memory because faith is the entry into unknown land. Faith is not faith in anything. Faith is the knowing of things not seen, the sureness that you are in the right place.

And there is one final door, opened only by the key of honest love. Q'uo call it the holy of holies, the mercy seat. If you can enter that door, all the rest open too. If you can dig down past the topsoil of confusion and the fertilizer of your difficulties, down to the rock, they say, that rock is love. And they ask for just a moment of feeling how much the Creator loves you. Every hair. Every freckle. Every folly and mistake. I love the gentleness of that line, the insistence that nothing in you is excluded.

Here is the heart of it. The circle had asked what they could actually control. And Q'uo answer: for the servant of others there is only one province where work is permitted, and it is not the world, and it is not other people. It is the self. The one place your power truly lies is the momentary decision to seek the love in that moment. They borrow a question from Ra, which they call a helpful question at any juncture, but especially when the spirit is weary. Where is the love in this moment. You cannot control the archipelago of confusion, they say, all those islands of dry ground in a sea of things beyond your power. But you can control the facing of the heart, right now, toward love.

And here is the strangest, most generous part. The love you would give does not come from you at all. If you try to love the world from your conscious self, you will run out quickly, they warn. Instead, see yourself as a transmitter. The energy moves through you, not from you. You receive it and you send it, and you create a circuit with infinite intelligence. What a relief that is, to the tired giver. You are not the source. You are the open wire.

The circle that day also wondered how to divide a spiritual book into chapters by energy center, since every topic seemed to touch several at once. Q'uo smiled through that one, gently suggesting she write instead from the experiences a seeker knows in her bones, letting familiar ground become the doorway to the devotional life. It is the same lesson, really. Do not force the material into your plan. Open the door you are meant to open and let the rest follow.

So keep these keys. Silence for a little while. Patience without expectation. Faith in the unseen. And honest love, the last door, behind which all the others wait. You are a citizen of eternity, paddling about in a borrowed boat, and the confusion is not a failure of your journey. The confusion is the journey. The keys are in your hands already, because the rooms are inside you, and the One who put them there is closer than your own breathing.

Thank you for listening.

title: Transmitters of Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: transmitters of light.

Early February of nineteen ninety-nine. The circle asked Q'uo about something huge and very much of its time: the way people everywhere seemed to be waking up to unseen things, to guides and angels and an inner sense of the sacred, and what that awakening actually means. Q'uo's answer is quietly radical. This is the blooming, they say, of a larger self-realization: that we are direct co-creators with the infinite, not receivers of a finished world but living conductors of eternal energy. And the way they describe how that works is, I think, one of the most beautiful passages in all of these sessions.

Each of you, they say, is as a radio. You receive and you transmit vibration. It does not matter how old you are or what the details of your life look like. If you are awakening, you are a receiver and a transmitter of love and light streaming from the Creator into the Earth plane. Your scientists would tell you that everything is particles vibrating, creating fields. One such field holds the spirit of you. And when that spirit awakens, they say, there is no going back to sleep. Once awake, you must remain awake. And so the question becomes practical: how do I help this along? How do I mature the spiritual child within?

Their first suggestion is simple and old. Silence. Time spent in silence, whether in formal meditation or just sitting, greatly aids the inner spirit, and it aligns you with your own destiny. And Q'uo are clear that you came here with one: gifts to share, lessons to learn, service to offer, companions planned along the way. But they are equally clear that the outer practices, however good, are secondary to something deeper. More helpful than any technique, they say, is the persistent focus on the nature of the self within incarnation. Because being a transmitter is not about doing. The greatest single practice, they say, is simply to be. To be the deepest and most true self of which you are capable. In this being there is a releasing of the doing, for metaphysically speaking, it is not what we do but being and essence that are the gifts we have to give each other.

Listen to how they put the mechanism of it. Each seeker is here to allow the one great original Thought to be us, and to move through us and out into the Earth plane. By blessing this energy and yet not holding it, knowing there is enough, an infinite amount, that it cannot be spent, the seeker affirms that which is. I love the image of the blessing that does not grasp. You do not hoard love. You let it pass through. And what people remember of you afterward is not the brilliance of your ideas or the length of your service, but what Q'uo call the vibratory level of your beingness. We have all met such people, the ones whose very presence raises a room. And Q'uo insist, always: it is not from you that these things come. It is through you.

There is no key to the heart that the worldly mind can turn, they say. No technique of the will can force it. It is the naked soul, the bare and unadorned spirit, that is love itself, and that is each of you. So they suggest a daily practice that feeds the inner self, whatever form that takes for you: meditation or prayer, contemplation, the gazing at inspiring objects, the reading of inspired words. And then they add something honest and useful about truth itself. Truth is fluid and personal, they say. There will be landmark truths that stay with you for a very long time, and there will be truths that transform and migrate as you grow. Do not cling to yesterday's map. Follow the hunches and intuitions, which are the only voice of the deeper self into the conscious mind.

The session's questions wandered into lovely territory: whether the guides we expect are the guides we receive, the fairy or the angel or the medicine spirit appearing according to the seeker's own calling. Q'uo say yes, gently: the forms of guidance refine themselves to match the vibratory essence of the one who calls. Each entity experiences that which it truly desires and has made room for. It is all one creation meeting you where you are.

And then they give the closing counsel, and I want to read it almost as they spoke it. Trust in the self. Move slowly and thoughtfully and wait for inspiration. When your ambitions are yielded, ask: what is the Creator's will for me today. Where is the love in this moment. The love in this moment is you. May you carry that truth and wear it as a crown. And even when the crown sits heavy, may you serve, may you reach out to others, may you respond to requests for help with the best that is in you. May you encourage others in their paths, for you are the hands, the voices, the caring of the infinite Creator within the Earth. You and none other.

A radio does not need to understand the signal it carries. It only needs to be tuned, and to be on. That is the whole of the teaching tonight. You are the instrument. The music is already playing. Be still enough, and be true enough, and it will sound through you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Shape of Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the shape of desire.

Late March of nineteen ninety-nine, with the first week of spring just arrived. The circle asked Q'uo a question that seems simple until you sit with it: how do we use our desires and expectations in a balanced way to grow spiritually? How do we know what we really want, underneath what we think we want? Q'uo's answer begins not with us, but with the Creator. And I love the boldness of where they start. The Creator Itself used the function of desire, which is also called free will, when It decided that It would know Itself. Desire is not the enemy of the spiritual life. Desire is the engine of all of creation, the original wanting-to-know that flung out the galaxies.

So when you discover you are full of desires, Q'uo say, do not be surprised and do not be ashamed. You shall never find yourself lacking in desires. This is the nature of your being. The awakened soul does not become desireless. It becomes a creature of desire that learns, slowly, to know the desires of the heart, to refine them, and to discipline the personality that carries them into the world. And they draw a line that matters between two kinds of desire. There is the desire that has an object in the outer world, a meal, a journey, a thing to possess, and they are blunt about its nature. Such desires have a very short shelf life after the acquisition of the object. Once the object is acquired, it is no longer desired. And then there is the other level, the desire for purity, for truth, for beauty, for true love between people. These have a life that is denied to the desires for things. These place you in a different world, where you see with what the writer Ken Wilber called the eye of contemplation.

Their counsel about these higher desires surprised me. Stoke these fires of hope and faith and will, they say, and ask for your highest desires with abandon and greed. Abandon and greed. They want you to want the highest things fiercely. For these desires cool the fire in the oven of desire itself, tempering you the way heat tempers a blade.
