This instrument has herself moved through the gate of death, and Q'uo tells the story through her own experience. Her kidneys failed. There was a great deal of pain, and then, when death occurred, there was the cessation of the pain. The body that had been disfigured was suddenly fair and perfect. She spoke to a rose on a fence and a whole section of rose bush wound itself around her arm, without thorns, with endless love. She could hear music and see it in the air. The experience expanded through death rather than being cut off.

And then graduation, which is a different thing from death. Picture a walkway filled with light, with loving presences on either side guarding each spirit that walks it. Then a light whose very nature changes as you move, becoming more dense, more bright, more challenging. You are walking to find your most comfortable and attractive place to be. You are looking for your new home.

I find their treatment of the wanderers especially tender. Many in the room, they say, did not start here. They moved through higher densities elsewhere, and came back to third density on Earth for two reasons. To rebalance love and wisdom and remake the original choice more purely. And to lend their being to what the instrument calls the ministry of essence, simply living a life of faith and letting the Creator's love flow through them to lighten the planet. But there is no such thing as a tourist in a body on Earth. All of you have become natives, whatever your planet of origin.

The graduational measure, they say, is simple. For positive polarity, the seeker must think more about serving others than about serving the self. They are extremely pleased, they add, that each in the group has chosen service to others, for that is the polarity they have chosen too.

On the third question, telling one kind of source from another, they are brief, and I think deliberately so. You have a gift of discrimination from the Creator and from your higher self, and it strengthens by being trusted and used. Move into the heart and ask, within the safety of your own energy field, is this true for me. If it is, move on it. Use it. Live it. If it is not, walk on.

What I love most is how ordinary they make the extraordinary. There is love in every moment, they say. There is love in every thought. The question is only how distorted that love is. Take the principles seriously, they add, but take the self lightly.

This session speaks of death as a doorway and a homecoming, and if you are carrying grief for someone who has passed through that doorway, please be gentle with yourself and reach out to someone you trust, a friend, a counselor, or a support group, so you do not carry it alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Way of the Open Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the way of the open heart.

This is a session about emotions, and it holds one of the most beautiful ideas in the whole archive, that the Logos, the one great original Thought, is not a thought at all, but a purified emotion.

The group asks Q'uo to elaborate on something said a couple of months earlier, that emotions are the thinking of the deep mind, and that we might be able to use our emotions in our spiritual evolution.

Q'uo begins with reassurance. There is an irresistible pull to evolution. It is as necessary to our nature to progress as it is for iron to be drawn to the magnet. The only question each entity faces is how quickly it wishes to progress. When you see your own lapses, they say, meet those judgmental feelings with the courage of your conviction that all is proceeding according to an unseen plan.

Then this striking line. It was designed into third-density experience that from beginning to end, your experience will include perceptions of the self as imperfect, not once, not twice, not three times, but seven times and seven times seven. Cyclically, without end, throughout the incarnation. This would seem a recipe for discouragement, and yet the intent is the opposite. Before awakening, you skate upon the surface of life as though it were a pond. Once awakened, you are drawn to the depths of each present moment, and the profundities of each moment are infinite. The gateway to intelligent infinity lies within each present moment.

I love that line, and I love what comes next, the two ways of working. The first is the way of wisdom. This is the analytical, reasoning mind, the desire to get hold of experience and understand it by logic. Great systems were built on this approach, the Buddhist, the yogic, the Taoist disciplines. It works, they say. It does accelerate evolution, to some extent. But it is a way of remaining comfortable while learning, holding the energy in the higher chakras, and thereby, in their words, sidestepping the main thrust of the third-density experience.

The second way is the way of the open heart, the way of love. Here the seeker releases the preference for working in the higher energy centers and accepts the self as a full energy system, from the lowest and most primitive emotion, the desire for survival, all the way up, but again and again springboarding from the heart. Instead of holding the energy still, the goal becomes accelerating the flow of energy through the entire system. Blessing, forgiving, redeeming, transforming, and offering each and every emotion to the one infinite Creator.

Listen to how they put the difference. Working with wisdom is like letting carbon build up on the valves of an engine. The way of love is like running the engine through its paces so it burns the carbon off. It is rougher and bumpier, they admit. It invokes faith without proof, reason, or logic. There is no attempt to justify hardship, and no attempt to disempower hardship by rising above it. It is the way of vulnerability, of remaining open and weak in the face of strong and sometimes painful feelings.

And here is the heart of it. Emotions are the shadows, the symbols, and increasingly the essence, of deep and purified rivers of energy that abide within what your psychologist would call the unconscious mind. At the roots of consciousness lie rivers of purified emotion, like gems, refracting from the white light of unlimited energy the colorations of energy called emotion. These essences are great truths the Creator has learned about itself. A thought is linear, they say. An emotion is global, universal, round. It does not climb. It rolls. It does not fall. It continues to roll.

Each of you has felt those moments when a tiny thing triggered a massive flood of emotion. When this occurs, they say, it is an excellent signal from the self to the self that here is a gift, imperfectly seen perhaps, but real. Emotions are messages from the deeper self to the conscious self. The seat of emotion is the heart chakra, and without moving into the heart there is little chance of self-forgiveness.

This instrument, they tell us, has consciously known two pure emotions, grief and love. Neither experience shall ever be forgotten. When the seeker touches the heart of an emotion and it resonates purely, it is a life-changing event. Never again will grief lay waste to this instrument as it did before she experienced pure grief.

If grief is moving through your own life right now, please be gentle with yourself and consider reaching out to someone you trust, a friend, a counselor, or a support group, so you do not have to carry it alone.

What stays with me is their final counsel. The goal is not happiness, peace, or contentment. The goal is simply continuing to accelerate the pace of spiritual evolution. The open heart does not attach an outcome. It simply seeks greater openness, and trusts that no matter what comes, the seeker will be able to use it to refine those rising rivers of emotion.

Thank you for listening.

title: Service Without Trespass
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: service without trespass.

The question this week is one every caring person has stumbled over. When are we actually being of service to others, and when have we gone too far and infringed upon another's free will.

Q'uo agrees at once that the boundary is moveable, or at least seems to be. For many in this density, they say, there is almost no action that is not considered an infringement. The character of each seeker is completely individual. Some are set up, by the gifts they brought into this incarnation and the experiences that shaped them, to feel that every helpfully meant suggestion is across the line, not helpful at all but interference.

And then there are others, they say, who are happiest when their decisions are made for them, or made very much with them in mind but without their intense contribution. To such entities almost no helpful-seeming act feels like infringement, because they feel their own opinions have no worth. There is clearly, they say, no arbitrary theoretical line across which stepping is infringement and before which it is not. With each entity, the boundaries and possibilities of the relationship will be unique.

I love how honest this is. It refuses the comfort of a rule. You cannot look up the answer. You have to know the person, and more than that, you have to know yourself, and even then the line moves.

Listen to this quiet warning they slip in at the beginning. Even their own words, they say, could be a subtle infringement if taken as authority. Authority itself has the ring of infringement, and they would like to take away any taint of authority from their words. They are not wiser than you, they say, only more experienced. This is the whole session in miniature. Help that arrives as authority is already trespass.

So what do we do, those of us who want to help and keep tripping over the line. Q'uo's counsel, woven through the session, is to watch for the ask. Offer when invited. Drop the seed and leave it. Let the other entity's response tell you where the boundary is today, because today is not yesterday, and this person is not that person.

There is a deeper point underneath, and it is about why service is so easily distorted. The desire to help can be genuine love, and it can also be the self wanting to be needed, wanting to be right, wanting the situation to resolve on our terms. The same act can be service or control depending on the heart behind it. And the heart behind it is the one thing the other person always senses, even when they cannot name it.

What I take from this session is a practice. Before offering, pause. Ask yourself whether you are responding to a request or to your own discomfort with the other person's situation. If it is your discomfort, sit with it first. Let it be theirs to carry, or theirs to hand to you. And if they do hand it to you, receive it as the gift it is, the gift of being trusted.

The paradox Q'uo leaves us with is a gentle one. The most powerful service is often not an intervention at all. It is the example of a life lived in love, the steady light that others can navigate by when they are ready, and that never once reaches out to grab the wheel.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seasons of Awakening
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seasons of awakening.

This session is about the timing of spiritual awakening, our own and everyone else's, and it offers one of the archive's most useful images, the alarm clock.

The group asks about the seasons of awakening. Each person seems to have a time and a way of realizing more of the heart of life, of becoming desirous of learning and growing and taking things in hand. How can we cooperate with these seasons, foster them, work with them, in ourselves and in other people.

Q'uo begins at the level of incarnational lessons. Before incarnation, each spirit had a great deal of say in choosing what lessons of love it wished to concentrate on, and what outer services it might specialize in sharing. When the lifetime begins, memory of this choosing is removed. The veil descends, and in complete forgetfulness and innocence the physical child is born with a destiny that is, in some way, complete.

Then comes the pattern that anyone who has lived a while will recognize. There will be a repeating theme, perhaps two or even three themes, of incarnational lesson, bringing up material about one lesson of love, again and again. Each time it repeats, it becomes a little clearer. At least that is the process hoped for before incarnation.

I love how plainly they describe the way we dodge the lesson. In the midst of difficulty, the careless thinker concludes that the relationship or the situation is at fault, rather than the self needing to pay attention. So the solution is to leave the relationship or leave the situation, thinking another person or another situation will change what is wrong. It is only when the pattern repeats with another person that the seeker begins to feel there may be a theme, and that it may be worth attending to in hopes of learning the lesson and moving on to more interesting ones.

This, they say, is the general scheme of spiritual evolution working at the unconscious level, designed to work while the person is asleep, spiritually speaking, and designed to be very vulnerable to being accelerated by the person who has awakened.

And now the alarm clock. Before incarnation, each entity dwelling in a body has her alarm clock set for a certain triggered time. Many hit that triggered time and, rather than waking up, hit the snooze button and go back to sleep. To some extent this can be influenced, but Q'uo recommends leaving it completely to each seeker as to when that seeker will actually awake. For it truly is an awakening process. It is as if entities of Earth are born into a kind of dream which they can dream nicely all the way from cradle to grave, until there is an awakening into a higher and more overarching level of dreaming, involving more light and more of what you would call reality.

When this happens, they say, there is a shift. Before, you were plodding upon the land. Suddenly you are on the ocean, moving quickly, and you cannot walk out of the boat onto safe shores. It is a time for rejoicing. But here is the temptation. When the awakened entity views those who are still asleep, it can seem desirable to shake them up and wake them up.

Listen to how they put the boundary. It is perfectly all right to mention things that interest us and drop a seed here and there. There is no infringement in doing so. But to move further than the first mention, without a substantially positive response, is to begin to encroach upon that person's privacy and free will. Instead, trust that each person's incarnational schedule is set as it should be. If they are still asleep, they should still be asleep. Something is going on in the pattern of that person's life that will work out perfectly for that person.

The person each needs to focus on in terms of spiritual work is the self. For truly, the self is the universe. The self is the Creator. The self is all that there is.

And the closing counsel is so simple I almost missed it. Regardless of the rate and pace of your busy days, find time to be. For in the midst of whatever change you are in, beyond all levels of alteration, you are who you are. You have a basic nature and vibration that has been your signature of love for eons.

Thank you for listening.

title: Balance in the Whirlwind
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: balance in the whirlwind.

This was a Homecoming meditation, with old friends returning to the circle, and the question was how to keep one's balance on the path while changes are happening so quickly, around us and within us.

Q'uo opens with an image I keep returning to. We are as you, they say, pilgrims upon a dusty road. Each of us knows the stones in the shoe, the dust upon the road, the light of hope in the sky amidst the clouds. We share a landscape, and we share in what may be called the journey. The journey has many faces, challenges and surprises, and they are glad to look at these masks with us.

Then this counsel. Hold only to your thirst, to your hunger, to your desire, to that passion that often seems so unfashionable within the mirrored walls of the world. For you need not look at those mirrors until you are ready to see that all things are the reflection of the self.

To speak of change, they begin at the level where there is no variation or shadow, the truth of unity. Think of all times and spaces, they say, as the final moment before oblivion. That which seems eons is but a heartbeat of the one infinite Thought which is love. All that you will and have and are, experience, experienced, experiencing, is taking place precisely now. You are in a circle dance. Your movements contain eons of awkwardness, missed steps, and seeming mistakes of every possible kind. And yet, seen from the level of the circle dance, every mistake was part of a perfect pattern. Every foolish choice was that freedom that you could not otherwise have had.

I love that phrase, the circle dance. It reframes everything. The lifetime of questioning, the years spent turning this and that over, seen from above it is the eccentric but perfect balancing dynamic that it was, that it is, and that it shall be.

And then they say something that stopped me cold. Each of you was placed in this illusion precisely so that you would lose sight of yourself. You were not put here to be intelligent and to make wise decisions. You were put here to make mistakes and to suffer. Each of you came here to get lost. Each of you hoped that when you plunged into this place of unknowing, you would awaken to that instinct within you for faith, and you would choose to live by faith. You had hoped you would take the opportunity of not knowing anything to choose, freely, the good, the true, the beautiful, the just, for no reason except that it is a beautiful thing to behold a fair and truthful principle.

This is the whole session in one paragraph. You came to choose without proof. The confusion is not the obstacle to the work. The confusion is the work.

They are honest about how it feels, too. It is easy to move upon the surface of life as though skating on a pond, they say, or walking the midways of a carnival, distracted by the rides, beguiled by the surface of things, while just beneath, the awakened self chews through catalyst with a voracious appetite. Puzzle follows enigma follows challenge. The accumulation of changes creates the sense of having lost one's sea legs, of having lost the lodestone by which one sets one's course.

When that happens, they suggest something almost shockingly simple. Remove yourself from the path, one way or another. Go find a cave or a rock or a beautiful valley dotted with sheep and rest a while, and wait, and cultivate as a crop, patience. For there are riddles that do not have a ready solution. And there are other times when the thing to do comes as if upon a wave and deposits itself at your feet, and when those gifts of the sea resonate with you, move quickly.

What is faith, they ask at the end. And they answer it in three words. All is well.

What I carry from this session is the permission to be lost. You came here to get lost, and the lostness is not failure. It is the field in which the only choice that matters gets made, freely, in the dark, for no reason except beauty.

Thank you for listening.

title: Listening to the Body
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: listening to the body.

The question this week is wonderfully practical. How can we get information from our bodies without having to get a cold, injure ourselves, or bring ourselves bodily grief to get our attention. We learn moderation and care the hard way. Could we learn it an easier way.

Q'uo begins with the group's tuning song, and I am glad they did, because it gives the session its frame. The song asks, what if God was one of us, just a slob like one of us, just a stranger on the bus, trying to make his way home. My friends, Q'uo says, this is your situation. Each of you, in the core of your energetic body, is the Creator. At the heart of your being there is no difference between you and the Creator. The entire journey of awareness, from the first expression of light through all the densities until light is absorbed once again in spiritual gravity, it is a journey home. Each of you is an energy system centered upon the Creator, full of personality shell and experience and incoming catalyst, attempting in her own way to make her way home.

Then they turn to the body itself, and to the missed signals. Many times, as the circle has discussed, there are missed signals that, when missed, result in becoming overstressed and developing injuries, or becoming overtired and developing a cold. And here is the part I did not expect. It is not considered a mistake, by those watching from the inner planes, for entities in third density to miss the signals before they move into the body. It is considered normal behavior for third density.

The body, the mind, and the spirit find themselves sometimes uneasy allies in this illusion, they say, attempting to integrate sources of information coming into the body, mind, and emotional systems. The signal function of the conscious body simply does not work the way it would naturally in higher densities. The body must exceed natural boundaries for the subconscious information to come into the conscious mind. Phone lines must be installed, in other words. And these are not telephone lines of a linear kind that could be rigged mechanically. That signal system was not intended to work in space and time.

But each of you has a portion of self in time and space's other half, in what they call time-space. The metaphysical identity of the self beyond the personality shell exists there. When you achieve pure being, when you are expressing your essence, you are in time-space. That is where the effortlessness comes from. It is simply a shift in creations. Space has gone away. Time as you know it has gone away. But identity, energy, focus, and power have not disappeared. They have become clarified, illuminated by the underlying glow of creation.

So the question becomes how to penetrate the veil between the daylight mind and the vast reaches below the threshold of consciousness. And the answer, woven through the session, is the revolving solution of issues, the steady practice of sitting with catalyst and transforming it into experience before it has to shout.

Listen to how they describe the work. The song for tuning spoke of the transformation of catalyst into experience as a major force in the movement of learning. That is the whole practice in one phrase. Something happens. You sit with it. You let it become experience instead of letting it harden into the body. The body is the last resort of the messenger, not the first. It only raises its voice when the quieter channels were missed.

I find this deeply kind. There is no scolding here for the cold you caught or the injury you earned by overdoing it. There is only the observation that you are learning to read an energy system that was designed to be hard to read, and the encouragement to keep installing those phone lines, in meditation, in silence, in the daily practice of turning toward the signals while they are still whispers.

What stays with me is the stranger on the bus. The Creator, making his way home, in a body that aches and a mind that misses signals, learning, slowly, to listen.

Thank you for listening.

title: Beneath the Angst
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: beneath the angst.

The question this week names something everyone in the room could feel. The level of anxiety, tension, stress, rush, hurry, and angst all around us in the world today. We see it in others and we see it in ourselves, in our daily round of activities. Is there a message being delivered when a life is lived this way. Is there anything to take from it besides what we see on the surface.

Q'uo begins with a gentle correction of the mirror we hold up to ourselves. From their point of view, they say, since they can see the shining hopes and good intentions of the heart, each entity looks a great deal more successful than the opinion each self has about itself. Much of the self-perceived imperfection of the personality, as seen by the awakening seeker, is an artifact of culture and cannot be translated in any linear way into the actual vibratory pattern of the mind, the body, and the spirit.

Here is the image I keep returning to. The essence of each of you resonates far below the level of surface consciousness. So while the irritations and anxieties of the day may destroy the conscious peace of the seeker, the seeker's service, the offering of its essence to the planet and its people, continues to go on without a great deal of disturbance. To the conscious mind there is no essence. To the conscious mind there is only a system of thoughts about the self, which they call the virtual self.

I love that phrase, the virtual self. The anxious chatter in your head is not you. It is a system of thoughts about you. And beneath it, the real offering continues, undisturbed, like a deep current under chop.

Then this. Other selves are seen with much more balance by the self than the self is, because they are not perceived as the self. If you find yourself gazing at others, concerned with their imperfections and sympathizing with them, do the same with yourself. For that instinctual reaction you have to the struggles of a person you perceive as well-intentioned but imperfect, that instinct has more balance in it. And you may trust that the instinct that saw the love in another's heart is the shadow of that heart itself within you, transducing the love and light of the infinite Creator in relatively unimpeded form, despite the surface angst.

Listen to how they put that. The love you can see in someone else is the shadow of the love in you. Your own heart, recognizing itself.

They are honest that there are many layers to where an antsy feeling may come from, and they do not reduce it to one cause. But the through-line of the session is this. The angst is surface weather. It is real, it is felt, and it is not the measure of the soul. The measure is far below, where the essence keeps its steady rhythm, offering itself, even on the days the virtual self is convinced everything is falling apart.

What I take from this session is a practice for the rushed days. When the hurry rises, pause long enough to remember the layering. There is the weather, and there is the current beneath the weather. You are the current. The weather will pass. It always does. And the people around you, the ones whose imperfections you can see so clearly and forgive so easily, they are currents too, briefly weathered, briefly believing they are the storm.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Constancy of Change
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the constancy of change.

The question this week is about the one thing you can count on. In the context of the perfection of the moment, where all things are well, change happens at all times. How does it happen. How much is conscious and how much is subconscious. Is there a balance between change and keeping things the same that is well to maintain. How much of the change can we affect, and how much will happen whether we have any input or not.

Q'uo begins at the deepest level. Change, they say, is a fixture of all the illusions of which we are aware. At the heart of creation is a constancy of metamorphosis that is, as far as they know, circular. The creation as a whole has its source as its ending and its ending as its source, and all that stems from source and comes to an end is one unified entity in a constant state of transformation.

Then this. All begins in the utter unpotentiated love, the Logos, that is the Creator unknown to itself. The first distortion of this Logos is free will. And free will is the agent of change. In the Creator, and therefore in its creation, through free will the Creator chooses that which you know as light. Light in its first manifestation may be seen as the sudden being of all that there is.

I love how they handle the Big Bang here. Your scientists have envisioned the birth of creation as inevitably explosive, they say, and have called it the Big Bang. But this is creation seen through the lens of your third density, in which time and space structure perception. In other illusions it may be seen not as an explosion but as a transformative process rolling from light to light to light, vast systems of vibration put in motion by the Logos, destined to roll their metamorphoses from the beginning of creation to its ending, when all energy has been spent, all desire balanced, and the harvested experience absorbed by the one infinite Creator.

Listen to this image. This design accomplishes what in your bodies would be a heartbeat. For the creation is the body of the Creator, and an entire creation, with all the densities of an octave, expresses one heartbeat of that creature which is the Creator. Your whole universe, every star and sorrow in it, is a single pulse.

Against this background, they place the smaller question of our own changes. How much do we steer. Their answer is characteristically balanced. You are a sub-creator, endowed with the same free will that is the agent of change in the Creator. Your choices matter. They are the means by which you shape your incarnation. And at the same time, you are riding a design vastly larger than your steering, a design in which change is not the exception but the substance.

What I take from this session is a loosening of the grip. We tend to treat change as a problem to be managed, as if stability were the natural state and change the interruption. Q'uo reverses it. Change is the natural state. Stability is the brief arrangement. The question is not how to stop the river but how to move in it, consciously, with as much love as you can bring to the stroke.

And there is comfort in the scale of it. The same free will that moves the galaxies moves in you. The same love that began as unpotentiated and unknown to itself is learning itself through your small daily changes, your changed mind, your changed heart. Nothing is wasted. The heartbeat completes itself, and every pulse is gathered in.

Thank you for listening.

title: Through the Doors of Death
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: through the doors of death.

This session returns to the question of what happens when we die, and asks it in the most personal way. What happens when we pass through the doors of death from this illusion to the next. Are we able to go on to another location and accomplish other work. Do we still have contact with our loved ones, and can they become aware of this.

Q'uo begins by taking the physical world apart, gently. To the outward eye, they say, it appears that life comes up from the primeval ooze, flourishes for its season like the grass and the flowers, and sinks back into the earth. Many have lived and died believing this was the whole situation. It is our opinion, they say, that this is not at all the situation.

Listen to this. Your own scientists are aware that the body which contains your consciousness, and the chair it sits on, and the floor under the chair, and the earth under the floor, are all created by what appears to be space, empty space. Matter itself has never been seen by your scientists, though they have seen the path of the energy made by seeming particles. Beyond this model there is no physicalness to the physical illusion, but rather a series of interpenetrating energy fields. The energy animating those fields is what has transcendent reality. And the birthplace of all that is, is the love of the one infinite Creator.

I love how they ground this in the familiar. In the beginning was the Logos, said the one known as John. In the beginning was the Word. But deity has developed connotations of great emotion, so instead they refer to that energy which created all that is as love. For the Logos is the one great original Thought that is love. Each star, each planet, each atom has as its heart the Logos. All things are love, stepped down and stepped down again so that experience might be gained.

Then the Creator's heartbeat, an image that appears again and again in these sessions and never loses its power. The Creator has a heart that beats, and each of its beats is a full and complete creation. In each creation you, as sub-creators, set out as explorers on another incredible adventure, beginning as elements, moving through experiences as animals and trees and plants, until each comes to self-awareness. This is the crux at which each of you now stands.

And then the question underneath the question. What dies when you die. Their answer is precise. What dies is the portion you would call the body and the personality. For when you came into incarnation, you could not bring the depth and richness of your spirit into a personality shell. Within the heart of your being you are the Creator, and therefore all that there is. As a citizen of eternity you are not bound by time. All the subtleties of self you have developed through the entire octave have their shadow within your third-density experience. You know things that are out of time. They rest in the depths of your subconscious, and only the tiniest portion can come through the veil of forgetting.

On the question of loved ones, the session's later exchange is tender. There are groupings, or clans, of entities who move as a group through incarnation after incarnation. The relationships vary. Sometimes members remain in the inner planes, offering assistance unseen, as guides and angelic presences, only to take incarnation once again. So as you move through this earthly experience, you may look at your loved ones, your family, your friends, those of like mind and heart, and see those who have been with you for many, many incarnations, on this planetary sphere and others.

They bow before our courage, they say, for we dwell in a thick and heavy chemical illusion, and it is only by faith that we may hope and feel and know that all is well and that all will be well.

If you are grieving someone who has passed through those doors, please be gentle with yourself and reach out to someone you trust, a friend, a counselor, or a support group, so you do not carry the grief alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: Waiting on the Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: waiting on the heart.

The question this week is about decisions. When we are trying to make a decision that is important to our spiritual lives, we often have to wait patiently, to take the matter to the heart. How can we do this more effectively, to gain the direction we need for our greatest growth. How do we discover what our direction is.

Q'uo begins with a word about discrimination, and it is sterner than usual. The concept of discrimination is sometimes difficult, they say, for people accustomed to feeling not entirely competent to judge. Many are the factors in your culture that disenfranchise spiritual seekers from trusting their own opinion. The bludgeoning of that blunt instrument known as school creates a respect for authority which is perhaps overstated. For in the realm of spiritual seeking, truth is not a matter of authority. Truth is not subject to proof. Truth is, in any linear terms, entirely subjective.

Listen to that. To get to a spiritual truth, it must first be realized that this spiritual truth will be true only for you. It will not be true for another living human being. This is not relativism as an excuse. It is the recognition that the resonance that tells you something is yours cannot be borrowed from anyone else's certainty.

The session's counsel on decisions is simple and demanding. Take the matter to the heart, and wait. In the meditative state, ask any question, then wait in patience, and receive a direction from that which they have called the heart. Or call it the higher self, angelic presence, guidance, unseen hands. Each entity has this assistance available. Knocking upon that inner door is the most healthful method of achieving a direction and an answer.

I love the honesty about the waiting. There is no technique offered for speeding it up. The waiting is the technique. The heart does not answer on the schedule of the anxious mind. It answers when the question has settled deep enough to be heard, and the practice is to keep returning to the silence, to keep knocking, without demanding the door open on your timetable.

There is a companion teaching woven through the session about the give and take of difficult decisions. It is in the working through of disagreement and confusion, they say, that the ability to exercise decision-making power is most enhanced. The hard decisions are not obstacles to your growth. They are the gymnasium of it. Each one you sit with, patiently, strengthens the very faculty you are trying to use.

And underneath it all is the insistence on self-trust. You have been trained, by school and by culture, to look outward for the verdict on your inner life. Q'uo asks you to reverse the flow. Listen for the resonance. When something is part of your personal truth, it will have a certain ring to it, and you will recognize it. Trust that resonance of recognition, and not the seeming authority of any source.

What I carry from this session is the image of the knock. Not pounding. Not breaking the door down. Just knocking, in patience, and waiting, in faith, for the direction that is already on its way to you from the deepest part of yourself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The White Envelope
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the white envelope.

The group takes pot luck this week, and since it is close to Christmas, they ask Q'uo for a Christmas message. What follows is one of the warmest sessions in the archive.

Q'uo begins with the season itself. The Christmas season is the season of the least light. Some portions of your planetary surface are almost entirely in the dark for some part of your winter. It is at this time of darkness that your story of Christ begins.

What is the message this entity comes to offer. Indeed, they say, the heart of that message is a kind of light. But it is the kind of light that can be generated without your sun or any other source of what you think of as light radiation. The light that gleams when no other light shines is the light of love, and it is that quality of light which the one you call Jesus the Christ embodies. For this entity expressed, in a supernally perfect way, the essence of pure love.

Then they retell a little story the instrument received in her web mail that day, and it becomes the heart of the session. A wife who dearly loved her husband saw that he was disenchanted with Christmas, not the sentiments of the season, but the commercialism and the hustle. So she began to think of what she might do to give him a better Christmas. At a sporting event they attended, one of the teams had no uniforms, just young people with no advantages, without even bus fare. She found a way to buy uniforms for that scruffy little team, wrote a note about it, put it in an envelope with her husband's name on it, and hung it on the tree. That little white envelope became the favorite present of the whole family that year.

And she did it every year after. Each year she would find someone who needed something, a couple that had lost everything in a fire, a young child who needed an operation, and she would quietly be that person's Santa Claus. Each year everyone looked for the envelope. Then came the year the husband died. The wife barely managed to get the tree up. But she placed a white envelope in the tree. And on Christmas morning, she and her children discovered that every single person there had placed a white envelope in the tree. Each child, worried their mother could not continue the tradition, had found someone to give to, because they wanted to give their dad his favorite present.

I love this story, and I love what Q'uo draws from it. They could speak of the history of Jesus, they say, but this entity would much prefer that they speak of the love itself to which he came to bear witness. The love beyond the love of possession. The love beyond human love. The love that created each of you.

And then the turn that makes the session. Each of you is as Jesus the Christ, they say. Not literally identical to that personality, but in this way. Each of you enters a dark world, both in your incarnation and at that point within your incarnation when you awaken to the light within. Each spirit enters the world to bring and to share, to bless and to transduce the love and light of the one infinite Creator. And for this to be meaningful, there needs to be that backdrop of darkness.

Listen to this image. As each spirit awakens to the basic nature of the experience, each is awakening as an infant into a manger in a stable, not into a comfortable and secure place, but into a most humble abode. Each infant spirit is helpless and brand new, and needs a great deal of help. So each of you is the caretaker, the parent, the teacher, the comforter of your own spirit. Each of you can clothe that infant spirit in the garments of care and self-awareness and time, time given to silence and to the love that rests in the cradle of the heart.

How shall you parent your own inner spirit, they ask. Remember that this spiritual child is moved and strengthened by the choices you make. In the dark aspects of the daily round, decisions can be made in fear or in freedom. When an ethical crux comes, pause and ask, where is the love in this situation. Where is the light in this moment. Where is the service that can be rendered. If you can ask these questions, you have used the darkness of Earth to light the candle of the heart's great and often untapped resources of faith and hope.

We bless that darkness, they say. Looking back on our own third-density experience, we see the gift of unknowing for what it is, a necessary prerequisite to the free choice of faith. The choices you make in these times of unknowing have a weight that can change the course of your soul's development. Know that you have the resources within you to be that candle lit within the darkness, and that the darkness shall never overcome it.

This session holds the death of a beloved husband inside a story about giving, and if grief is present in your own season, please be gentle with yourself and reach out to someone you trust, a friend, a counselor, or a support group.

Thank you for listening.

title: Within or Without
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: within or without.

The question this week sets two words against each other that seem to mean the same thing. Religion and spirituality. Seeking from without and seeking from within. The group asks for ideas on the direction appropriate for each person, how each can be helpful, what the hindrances might be, and whether there is really a precise answer for each of us, or a certain amount of uncertainty we need to accept.

Q'uo begins by asking each listener to come along on a small journey of imagination. See yourself resting in your seat, limbs relaxed, mind quiet. See the evening outside, the patchwork of snow and earth and tree. Now lift away from the chair, draw back in space until the Earth becomes smaller and smaller and disappears, and you are one with the stars and the distance that is the outer appearance of the house of the Creator. Rest in this larger identity and know that you are loved by the one infinite Creator, that you have been with that Creator since before there was time or space. In your heart of hearts, in your deepest self, you have no limitations, no location, no set personality shell. Your truth, beyond all telling, lies in this oneness.

And then the question beneath the question. If you are all these things, why did you choose to be in such a heavy and deep illusion at this particular moment in eternity. Why did you choose to forget you were a citizen of eternity and take flesh. Each of you desired greatly, before this incarnation, to partake in this experience. Each felt there were things to learn in this density, in this darkness, at this time. And above all, each of you was moved to service. For truly, they say, this is the dawning of the fourth density. Your planet is traversing the boundary between third density and fourth, moving from a density in which the lesson is choice into a density where that choice has been made.

On religion and spirituality themselves, Q'uo draws the contrast this way. Religion is the outer path and spirituality is the inner path, and the tension between them is the real subject. Truth, they say, is a slippery word, and it evolves as we evolve. The principles and ideals remain the same, but we ourselves are in a constant and unremitting state of evolution. We cannot stop it. We can only accelerate it or let it proceed at its own pace.

I love their honesty about the cost of seeking. The more successful you are at accelerating your spiritual evolution, the more likely you are to feel at times that you have lost everything, that you cannot make heads or tails of what the truth might be, and that you might as well give up. This, they assure us, is part of the pattern. Wherever you are, whatever the lightness or darkness of your own interior heart, you are part of a pattern of spiritual lightening that, seen in hindsight, will prove to have been effectual and inspired.

So is there a precise answer, an outer or inner direction that is right for each person. Their answer is that the mystery recedes before us as we pursue it, through density after density, experience after experience. The mystery remains, and our thirst for it continues to motivate us. There is a certain amount of uncertainty, and we are asked not to solve it but to accept it, to let the not-knowing be part of the path rather than a failure of the path.

What I carry from this session is the permission to stop shopping for the correct container. Whether you kneel in a pew or sit in silence alone, the larger identity is the same. You are the one who drew back until the Earth disappeared. You are the one the Creator has loved since before time. The outer forms and the inner silences are both fingers pointing at that.

Thank you for listening.

title: Many Roads to Healing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: many roads to healing.

The question this week is a delicate one. The group asks about the healing practices of the Christian Science Church, with its emphasis on the truth that we are all one, whole, and perfect, versus the orthodox use of medications and treatment by physicians. Would one be more likely to result in a cure. And what can Q'uo say about healing in general.

Q'uo begins with the complexity of the human being. The healing of mind, body, and spirit, they say, is often a complex project, because there are illnesses with components that are physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual. Each of you is basically thought, not a single linear thought but a round, three-dimensional essence, a vibratory complex, a harmonic with at least three basic tones plus overtones and undertones of being.

Listen to this image. This complex, harmonious chord of being that you are is beautiful. Whatever your situation, whatever the difficulties you face, this basic essential self is unable not to make music, no matter how dark the chords. For each of you is essentially a thought which is love, and love is that which is beauty and truth. Each of you sings a song that is your identity and your name in the metaphysical universe.

Then they address the doctors directly, and with surprising fairness. Illness, they say, is not usually a simple thing but a multi-layered set of departures from the natural balance of energies in the subtle bodies as well as the physical body. A medical physician in your culture is not trained to probe deeply into spiritual issues. Faced with physical illness, the professions look for linear and mechanical answers. They treat the body as a machine, and a machine it is. Many conditions have been healed by correct mechanical operation or the correct adjustment of chemistry through medicine. It is no wonder the physician does not always achieve the desired results, for mechanical and chemical agents do not address the issues of the finer bodies. The only way to address those issues is by moving into the arena of thought and vibration.

And here is the passage I find most important. Within certain entities' illnesses there are levels on the inner planes where pre-incarnational lessons have been put in place, meaning a certain condition cannot be healed because it is protected. At other levels there are points of opportunity for leaving the incarnation which are also protected, so that only the will of the one who is ill can choose life or death at a crisis point. No healing can be effective at those points except the healing of the person by the person, by that person's will and choice.

I want to be careful with that idea, because it could be misread as blame. Q'uo is not saying anyone causes their illness or fails to deserve healing. They are saying that some conditions are woven into the incarnational plan at a depth no outer intervention can reach, and that this is not a failure of medicine or of faith. It simply is.

Their conclusion refuses to rank the methods. The judgment of all may be withheld from choosing one technique as better than the others. Each person who is ill represents a picture with a certain number of levels, and each level of the illness may take a different level of healing. It may be effective to offer surgery, medication, subtle energies, intercessory prayer, and the healing of one who knows the truth. Health may not come before all of these levels are employed. And always it must be remembered that in some cases, no matter what is offered, certain illnesses are protected and impervious, because they are a portion of the pre-incarnational plan.

So the answer to the group's question is neither side wins. Many roads, many levels, one patient, whole and mysterious.

This session speaks of illness and healing, and it is not medical advice. If you are dealing with illness in your own life, please work with qualified health professionals you trust, and reach out for support, medical, emotional, or spiritual, whenever you need it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Utter Patience
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: utter patience.

The question this week is about patience, and about the group itself. How can a group help us develop patience, whether patience in what we seek, truth, love, the purpose of our life, or patience in accepting the things that do not change, a rift in a friendship, a job situation, a family relationship.

Q'uo begins by widening the question. They are sure it extends to all the spiritual qualities that are greatly desired and difficult to obtain, faith, a sense of humor, persistence, compassion, those qualities often sought but usually imperfectly found. And yet, they say, how blessed it is when the seeker can find a moment of utter patience, utter humor, utter acceptance, or utter love.

Listen to this. All of these streams of emotion flow through the channels of the deep mind in pure and undistorted vibrations, for they are part of what this instrument would call the default setting of the vibration of creation itself, the Logos of the one infinite Creator which is love. Patience is not something you manufacture. It is something you uncover. It is the default. The distortion is the hurry.

Then this image, which I love. When one attempts to talk about love, one ends up talking about qualities such as compassion, faith, hope, patience, and humor. But these are all as the rays of light which come from the sun of love, each a slightly different color, each definable and recognizable, yet each a ray from the heart of the Creator. And what the spiritual group does is to bring that sun a little closer, to make it more possible to find a conscious, honest faith in the existence of this sun.

The cocoon of incarnation is permeable, they say. Through your energy body there are tremendous numbers of entrances into finer densities. Through the gateway of intelligent infinity there is access to inspiration and to realms of teachers and guides. And through the openings into the self which are through the heart, not just the chakra but the physical heart, there is entrance into the deep mind. All of these sources of light are aided in their clarity by the subtle enhancement of group energy.

Each of you brings to a group, they say, a variety of qualities over which you have little or no control, and many of these are greatly helpful to the group. Each of you brings, in essence, the universe, and all the energy and power that fuels that universe that is yourself. And when you open that universe in meditation there is a golden connection, in any circle of seeking, that runs between each member of the group. No connection is ever lost. And each connection increases the light.

I find that last line quietly staggering. No connection is ever lost. Every circle you have sat in, every hand you have held in meditation, every stranger whose breathing fell into rhythm with yours, it is all still there, still increasing the light.

They add something I did not expect. There are many around your world, none of whom anyone in the group knows, who have joined this group because they are aware that this group meets at this hour. And these unseen friends also add greatly to the power of the work. Plus the many beings of spirit drawn to such a circle, whose delight is in enhancing the experience for all attending.

So how does the group teach patience. Not by instruction, but by proximity. Sit close enough to the sun of love, together, and the rays reach you. The patience you cannot manufacture alone arrives as a property of the field. Indeed, they say, it is by a series of connections with other awakened beings that each of you creates the net of love that is lightening your planet at this time. And that net, they are happy to say, has become more and more articulated as more of those upon your planet awaken.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Harvest Now
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the harvest now.

The question this week concerns the ascension. Many sources have described it in different ways, its rapidity, those to whom it occurs, how and when it occurs, what it means. The group asks for Q'uo's perspective on what the ascension, or the rapture, or the graduation, or harvest, is like now for us on Earth, and what it is likely to be like in the near future.

Q'uo notes that these terms are not precisely interchangeable, but closely associated. And then, as they often do, they step back to the ground beneath the question. The creation, they say, is a thought. For lack of a better word, the creation is a Logos, a concept at once simple and unified and infinitely complex. The physical world you enjoy is also a thought, but a much weaker one, much stepped down from the energy of the Thought of the one infinite Creator, that Logos which we can also call love.

Each of you is a thought, and that thought is of love, because all thoughts are distortions of the one great original Thought which is love. Before all manifestation, each of you exists as an energy, an essence, a crystal, an energy field that takes in energy, transduces it, transmutes it, and sends it through the energetic system of body, mind, and spirit.

Listen to this. Every thought you think, every thought you pursue, every thought you bring to fruition, creates slight changes in the vibration that is your energy signature. To those on the spirit planes, these vibratory patterns are as clear as day. It is as clear to us as day who you are, how you are, whose you are.

To the entity in physical manifestation, this is not at all clear. There is much confusion, and there will continue to be, generated by the very nature of third-density experience. The suffering may seem to be erasing your identity. This too is an illusion. For beneath the surface confusion, those energies of deeper thought and feeling continue to pulse rhythmically, continue to process energy, and continue to send out the fruit of the energy that has moved through your energetic bodies. Each of you is sending out your own harvest of received, blessed, transduced, and transmitted energies.

And here is the image I carry from this session. They compare this energy output to light, to a candle. Many times it seems to each that there is no way one person can be of service, that one person's light cannot make a difference. But this instrument is fond of saying that in a dark place the light of one candle can be seen for quite a distance. Metaphysically, they say, this is far more true even than the physical truth of candles and sight.

Each of you makes a significant difference to the lightening of the planet as well as to the lightening of your soul. For when each of you does one, each of you is doing the other. To work on the self is to work on the world. Indeed, to work on the self is the most direct and effective way to work on the outer world in a metaphysical sense.

Then they turn to the Earth itself. Your Earth has come to a crux in its own development. It is as though the Earth must needs give birth to itself. The third-density Earth is being transformed into a fourth-density positive sphere, and your Earth is having difficulty with this birth. Its energy system is clogged with the toxic material, metaphysically speaking, of centuries of negatively polarized choices. But as entities such as yourselves awaken and choose positive orientations, that toxic material is gradually given permission to be released, and the instreaming fourth-density energies find more welcome.

They are honest about the physical side. There are problems of excessive heat within the mantle, difficulties of weather, flood, earthquake, fire, causing suffering and loss of life. And yet, they say, had they spoken a quarter century earlier, they would have been less sanguine. As Earth entities awaken, the planetary energy lightens, and global catastrophe has become instead a series of small and survivable catastrophes. This, they feel, is a very hopeful portion of the subject. Things are better, metaphysically speaking, for the Earth's harvest than they were.

What stays with me is the reversal at the center of it. You do not light the planet by fixing the planet. You light the planet by tending your own candle. The harvest is not something coming for you. It is something coming through you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The New Buddhism
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the new Buddhism.

The question this week is about a cultural moment. There seems to be a new interest in the practice of Buddhism around the world, and the group asks Q'uo to shed light on why interest has increased, what effect it has on people, how Buddhism connects to other world religions, and how it connects to the philosophy of the Law of One.

Q'uo begins with the ground beneath all of it. There is one Creator, they say, of which the so-called revealed religions are attempts to discern, illuminate, and express. Any religion has what this instrument would call baggage. And in the case of Buddhism, as with the other major world religions, that baggage is not the baggage of a few years but the weight of generations, centuries, and millenniums of practitioners finding ways to re-identify and reassess the valuable points of the religion.

Each religion, they say, has two sides. There is the revealed or outer aspect, and the inner, mystical aspect. And it is in the mystical aspect that the religions tend to unify and harmonize. A mystical Buddhist can speak to a mystical Christian, a mystical Jew, or a mystical worshiper of the East and have very few communication problems, because mysticism focuses on essence and not on detail.

I love that line. Essence, not detail. It explains so much about why interfaith dialogue works at the depth and stalls at the surface.

It is in the outer aspect, they say, that we find the challenging material. In each religion's settled church aspect there is the tendency to be dogmatic. And they are fair about dogma's appeal. The advantage is simple and vital. Many among your peoples have the necessity for a dogmatic type of belief system, a certain list of things believed true and a certain list held untrue. But the more a system attempts to define its theology dogmatically, the more pronounced the tendency for disputes between factions. Efforts toward unified belief on a global scale, they suggest, will be far more successful when mounted by the mystical portions of the faiths.

Then they offer a striking lens. The most striking difference between the religions, they say, is the energy center which is the seat of each system's germinal energy. In Christianity the basic chakra activated is the green ray, the heart. This is because the entity known as Jesus was a teacher concerned with one thing only, and that was love. His whole teaching, they say, was a new covenant having only to do with love, love of the infinite Creator and love of each other, beginning with the self.

And Buddhism. Here they see both the gift and the challenge. Those who seek along the Buddhist path, they say, have done far more investigation into the discrete realms of the inner planes, the states of consciousness, the places where teachers dwell, than any other system of religion. But the difficulty with this tremendous panoply of resources is that entities can remain within the higher centers without bringing the lower centers into balance. This weakens the integrated self.

Listen to their counsel to Buddhist seekers. Take care, in a persistent and continuing way, to reintegrate the lower energies, the orange and yellow and green rays, so that there is not simply talk and thinking about the Creator and the releasing of the illusion, but also the awakening of the heart and the valuing of the structures of the illusion. For the structures of the illusion, the relationships, the families, the friendships, are an elegant design for learning. Into each relationship has been poured a tremendous amount of preincarnative thought. You may see each relationship as a carefully prepared lesson in the giving and receiving of love.

On why Buddhism draws so many now, they offer a quiet observation. It is not that Buddhism has had no fights and shames in its history. But because its worshipers have not for many centuries had ascendancy as a nation or an economy, little is known of that history of shame. So seekers in the supermarket of world religions can come upon Buddhism in an innocent and fresh way, with the feeling that this is a religion of peace and enlightenment. And this perception, they say, is extremely valuable.

What I take from this session is the double vision. Honor the fresh perception, and do the integrating work. No path, however peaceful its reputation, does the lower chakras for you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Red Ray
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the red ray.

The question this week is unusually intimate. How can a person who has a great deal of sexual energy available from the red ray, but who has no sexual partner, allow that energy to move through the various energy centers of the body in the most harmonious way possible.

Q'uo steps back before answering, and I am glad they do. The chakras, they say, do not work separately. They work as a system, with significant connections between the finer bodies. So it is well, when faced with a perceived imbalance, to realize that the situation is non-local, no matter how local it may seem. A blockage that feels like it lives in one ray is seldom blocked in only one ray.

Then they look carefully at the nature of red ray itself. It is the first gateway of the energetic body. It is the first gateway that allows in the infinite energy of the one infinite Creator. And while a red-ray blockage has to do with sexuality in the linear sense, in the deeper sense it has far more to do with the processes of love and fear as regards survival.

Listen to this. Survival is a vital and hidden issue for an entity that is well fed, decently clothed, warm, and with a roof over its head. It does not occur to the waking consciousness that there is a survival issue with regard to sexuality, for sexuality is clearly not necessary for survival. But at the gateway to the energy body you are also gazing at the gateway to the physical body, and the instincts of the physical body have a sometimes striking and hidden effect. That which is perceived as sexual frustration is actually, they say, the cry of the heart to survive.

I find that reframe genuinely compassionate. The ache is real, but it is not only what it seems to be. Underneath the specific want is the older want, the body's ancient insistence that its needs be met, the stomach crying for food, the body crying to reproduce, to breathe, to move. When a gateway need is persistently denied, the energy system sets up blockages along certain lines, and the soul perceives a red-ray blockage. On the level of observation, this is correct. On the level of solution, it is not.

Their practical counsel is the energy balancing they have taught through this instrument before. Sit quietly at the end of the day, in a reflective mode, and be with each distortion remembered from the harvest of the day's emotions, whether it leaned positive or negative. For all distortions from balance are equally useful to look at. In silence and in the release of control, allow the help that is available from the unseen beings who surround and guide each seeker.

And then a permission I did not expect. Another aspect that may help with unclogging blockages, they say, is simply to act on the emotion engendered. Locate the basic emotion as accurately as you can, and then express it. They give the example of waking with such frustration that the desire is to scream. Move to a place of safety, they say, and scream. It is not wise to upset others or destroy something within the self. But it is very wise to acknowledge and express emotion when it can be done without infringing on the free will of others. There is real spiritual value in acknowledging primal distress, even in the most primitive release, for it is a scream from the heart that wants to survive.

Beyond a certain point, they say, it is well to rely on faith. All energy is one. There is not sexual energy and heart energy and family energy as separate substances. There are aspects, colors, as the energy moves through the centers. But the energy itself is limitless white light. And what one accepts into the waking mind becomes the door through which the solution can be approached.

First, they say, there is the faith that all is well. This is a significant step for one who is suffering, for the physical body wants to react in a fear-based manner, to protect and control. Yet often you have chosen, before incarnation, the very situation that now causes suffering, not to break through quickly, but to initiate a process of self-acceptance, self-understanding, and self-forgiveness far deeper than the issue that began it.

This session speaks openly about sexuality and the body. These are normal parts of being human. If questions about your own body or desires are weighing on you, consider speaking with a trusted counselor, therapist, or health professional, someone with whom you can be fully honest.

Thank you for listening.

title: Welcome Home, Wanderer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: welcome home, wanderer.

This session has a special occasion behind it. The group has just about finished preparing A Wanderer's Handbook for printing, and they are sending a flyer to their mailing list. Many who receive it are likely wanderers, or spiritual outsiders of one kind or another. The group asks if Q'uo would like to say something to these people, about the concepts in the book, and about the quality of being a wanderer, of being alienated and isolated in the spiritual journey.

Q'uo's first words are the title of this episode. For many to whom we speak, they say, we simply say, welcome home.

Listen to how they describe the feeling. One thing very common among wanderers, and among all those who have begun the process of awakening from the sleep of Earth, is a feeling of not being at home in the Earth world, of not recognizing the colors and shapes of your beautiful planet. As lovely as it is, still it does not feel like the shores and the fields of home. And this is because in many cases they speak to those who do not originate from this planetary environment, but who have chosen deliberately to come to Earth on a voyage of service and learning.

But then they widen it, and this is important. For many others, Earth is the native sphere, the beloved home, and yet the spirit has awakened from the dream of Earth. More and more, in the awakening process, Earth has become an alien place, not because its shapes are unfamiliar but because the thinking of its peoples has begun to jar against the newly found resonances of an awakening awareness of the self as a citizen of eternity. Whether you listen as one who came from elsewhere or as an Earth native, they say, we speak to you as absolute equals. For all of those who have awakened have become wanderers upon Earth. All begin to experience the dislocation of living in two worlds at once.

I love that leveling. The wanderer is not a special rank. The wanderer is anyone who has woken up enough to feel the distance between the world as it is and the world as the heart knows it could be. If you have ever felt like a stranger at the table, like the colors were wrong somehow, like everyone else got a memo you never received, this session is speaking directly to you.

They are clear that the isolation is real and also that it is not the whole story. The awakening brings a dislocation, yes, but it also brings a recognition. The ones who feel most alien are often the ones closest to remembering. The homesickness is itself a kind of compass. It points at what you are, not at what you lack.

And the occasion matters. A handbook for wanderers, going out into the mail, into the hands of people who may never have heard the word used this way. Q'uo treats the flyer as a kind of calling card from one outsider to another. You are not the only one who feels this way. There is a name for it. There is a book. There are others.

What I carry from this session is the greeting itself. Welcome home. Not welcome to the group, not welcome to the teaching. Welcome home. As if the whole spiritual path were not a journey outward to somewhere new, but the slow recognition that you never actually left.

If the dislocation feels heavy, if the two worlds feel too far apart, please reach out to someone you trust, a friend, a counselor, or a community where you can be honest about it. You do not have to hold the distance alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: Circles of Return
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: circles of return.

The question this week is about reincarnation in groups. We reincarnate from life to life with friends, time after time, in clans or groups, learning to serve and seek the Creator together. How does this process affect the planetary consciousness. Does it aid the planet, and how does that work. How does it aid the individual harvest when that time comes.

Q'uo begins by correcting the picture most of us carry. It is more accurate, they say, to look at reincarnation involving the repeated joining of relationships as part of a circle of being, in which each incarnation is a spoke out from the center, and all experiences harvested in each incarnation are fed back into the central pool of self, than to describe reincarnation as a series of successive lifetimes.

I love that image, the wheel instead of the line. Not a march of lives, one after another, but a hub with spokes, every life radiating out from the same center and returning its harvest to the same pool. Within time and space, time must seem linear and directional, they say, or the whole pattern would become fruitless. It is essential that those moving through incarnation be unable to see the great circle, unable to see the nuances of each karmic issue. The not-seeing is part of the design.

Then they describe the choosing. Each is aware of the careful process of preparing for incarnation, of choosing those with whom one shall come into relationship. The harsh lessons, the confusion that seems woven into our closest bonds, these are not accidents. Into each relationship has been poured a tremendous amount of preincarnative thought.

Listen to how they counsel us about difficult relationships. It may seem that instead of becoming more unified with those we are in relationship with, we have not made progress, and we may wonder about the efficacy of our work. And yet, they say, it is well to trust the rhythms of relationship and to allow them to be of the shape and texture that they will be, rather than attempting to remold them according to a desired outcome. Is not the work of mending work done upon the self. Is not the process of forgiveness the forgiveness of self that sees the other self as the reflection of the Creator.

That question lands hard. The mending you want to do on the relationship is mending to do on yourself. The other person is the mirror, not the project.

And the circle is larger than any one clan. Rather than one small group repeating together through a whole creation, each may expect to become intimate, to go through catalyst, healing, harmonization, and unity, with each other spark of the infinite Creator. This process of each helping each to learn the lessons of each density is not malignant or undesirable, no matter how confused the relationships seem. It is the outworking of spiritual gravity, calling each to become more aware of the true nature of the self.

On the planet's share of this, their answer is woven through the session. Every harvest of experience fed back into the central pool of self is also fed into the planetary consciousness. The clan that learns to love each other better lightens the whole. The individual harvest and the planetary harvest are not two processes. They are one process seen from two distances.

What stays with me is the wheel. Every person who has ever vexed you, every friend who has ever saved you, every love that has ever rearranged you, they are spokes on your wheel, and you are a spoke on theirs. And at the hub, the same self, gathering it all in, life after life, until the circle is complete.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Royal Thirst
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: The Royal Thirst.

This session comes from the spring of two thousand and one, and the question put to Q'uo is a bold one. What is the nature of the Matrix of the Mind, and how is it related to the Potentiator of the Mind? And how might any of this be used in a daily life? It is the kind of question that asks for the deep map of the self.

Q'uo begins not with definitions but with a story. When the infinite Creator wished to know Itself, Q'uo says, Its great heart beat out the next creation, with all of its densities and sub-densities, and time and space were invoked. And each spark of that beating heart became an agent of the Creator, a thought rounded and centered in the one great original Thought, which is Love. And then this line, which I love: each of you is a Logos, stepped down and stepped down until you are able to experience the very illusion you now experience.

So here we are. Each of us with one foot in each world, as Q'uo puts it: the world of the Earth and the world of infinity, the world of things and the world of thoughts. Each of us human, earthly and limited, and yet not fully human, not fully earthly, not fully limited, because there is the growing awareness of the creatorship within.

The Matrix, Q'uo says, can fruitfully be seen as one energy with the Potentiator, and yet it is useful to see them as completely separate figures. The Matrix is figured forth as royal. This is not a mistake, Q'uo says. As a spiritual being, each seeker is indeed the highest royalty. And yet the Matrix is empty and waiting. Its nature is hunger. The hunger for evolution is stitched and knitted into every fiber of the carefully articulated web of being that the Matrix experiences as its nature.

Listen to what is required to enter that Matrix. To enter into the Matrix, Q'uo says, one must become naked. The sorrows and shames and unworthiness, the whole wardrobe of self-opinion, must be taken off as shoes are taken off, as garments that are upon the body but are not the self. You do not, when you put off the clothing of self-opinion, put off the essence of self. You are who you are, and your signature is beautiful. That is the line I keep returning to. You are who you are, and your signature is beautiful.

The Potentiator is cast also as a royal being. And here Q'uo offers us a gift: see the Potentiator as the guardian angel, the guidance, the guru, the agent of divine change. See this agent as a gift-giver to one who opens the hands without knowing what they hold. For as the Matrix reaches to the Potentiator, the need of the Matrix creates the gifts of the Potentiator.

I love the image Q'uo gives for this. Spiritual evolution is not a lesson plan, not step one, step two, step three. It is as though the unfed mind, by its thirst, by the intensity of its thirst, and by the direction of its seeking, creates an unending grove of trees whose fruits drop into the hands of the seeker, who then eats that fruit and receives knowledge peculiar to the soil in which that fruit grew, the soil of that particular seeking. One person on one day receives one fruit from spirit. That same person on another day, with just the tiniest change in seeking, in attitude, in state of mind, receives an entirely different fruit. The archetypal journey, Q'uo says, is far more creative and far more plastic than any plan.

There is a constant back and forth between the one who reaches and the one who awaits the reaching. And all that is hidden within the Potentiator changes every time it releases fruit from behind the veil. So there is no comfortable assurance here. No one can tell you that all is in safe hands, that all will go one way. What can be trusted beyond all telling, Q'uo says, is the protected nature of this work. As the seeker dedicates itself to the seriousness of its desire, it alerts a large body of discarnate protection, which the instrument would call inner-planes or angelic. That thirst, and its fulfillment, shall be blessed.

And here is the closing promise, and it is a large one. You are at the beginning of a journey of self-knowledge that shall bring surprise upon surprise, awareness upon awareness. And yet at each spiral of awareness, including the one at which you now are, you are already that being which you hope to become. The bare attempt to seek within brings resonances of that being to your waking personality, which strengthen and have a tendency to heal it.
