The past can inform you about yourself, Q'uo says. Memory can tell you where your strengths and weaknesses have been. But do not be harsh with yourself when you stumble. The more you rest in trust and faith, the more room you give coincidence to work for you. And the stronger your belief that all is well, the more quickly patterns will smooth out and reveal that, indeed, all is well.

Thank you for listening.

title: The She-Wolf Runs With You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: The She-Wolf Runs With You.

The tenth of February, two thousand and two. The question to Q'uo is about the shadow self. That darker side of ourselves that we occasionally explore but which is mostly a mystery. What can we do to get to know our shadow selves, to accept our darker side, and become whole?

Q'uo begins with the symbol in the instrument's mind labeled pop culture: the yin and yang, the circle with the S-shaped curve, one graceful arch black and the other white, the black having a white dot and the white having a black dot. One can see the white from the black, Q'uo says. And they create a spherical being. This is the three-hundred-and-sixty-degree being we have been talking about.

It is the glory and the pain of humanity, Q'uo says, to express and experience two paths for the price of one. This density is unusual even for later densities in the strength of the apparent wide chasm between the forces of light and the forces of darkness. And there has been a concerted effort by many to conceive of this as a war, and the light workers of the world as warriors fighting dark forces.

When one is in balance, Q'uo says, one sees and allows the enjoyment of the radiation of beauty, the truth, and the very obvious unity of the positive that is thick in the air in daily life, in all sorts of nooks and crannies that are seldom even seen because the creation is so rich in its gifts. And yet the creation is rich also in challenges. And the challenge is in seeing the dark side without its masks, or with a more understanding choice of masks for the dark side.

And then the image that stays with me. Is not the she-wolf a terrible hunter, greatly feared by its prey? And do you not desire to have the she-wolf run with you? She is a murderer. You can think about each and every aspect of the dark side of the self: the self that feels self-pity, the self that feels jealousy, greed, murder, and many more that are more subtle and lie within the heart.

To come into an acceptance of the she-wolf that runs with you. To come into an acceptance of the liar whose dazzling footsteps dance one out of trouble. The instrument herself, Q'uo says, has certainly experienced the feelings of a murderer when a loved one was apparently struck and perhaps killed. There is no length of time between the sight of someone that needs defense in the mind of the perceiver and the feelings of murder. And it is a pure, clean, crisp and powerful emotion, not unlike anger but with deadly intent. Would any say that this instrument had an unintegrated murderer within her? No. And yet in her inner thoughts she does indeed have a murderer alive and well and living in the hospitality of the temple of the body, the mind, and her spirit.

And so each contains all that there is. And when that dark side of self is seen as an asset by the self, when the she-wolf bares its fangs and seems to come at one as a predator that wants to tear out the heart, that is when you embrace that she-wolf and know that that is your powerful, brave heart that is capable of anything but that chooses to be your she-wolf, to be your totem, to be your seeker of truth that prowls in dreams and comes back with news of elsewhere.

All of those aspects of the dark side that seem so grimy, Q'uo says, are actually no grimier than what passes from the bowels of your body. Is food fair and excrement foul? It may seem so, yet both are necessary, and the intake and the outgo are equally necessary, and the bowel is just as necessary an organ as the tongue. Both are valued equally by the body. And whether dark or seemingly light, both are affected not by the literal nature of their seeming function but by the emotion that powers them.

This instrument has found helpful, and uses to this day, a prayer, Q'uo says. And they speak the prayer of Saint Francis in full. Lord, make us instruments of thy peace. Where there is hatred, let us sow love. Where there is injury, pardon. Where there is discord, union. Where there is doubt, faith. Where there is despair, hope. Where there is darkness, light. Where there is sadness, joy. O divine master, teach us to seek not so much to be loved as to love, to be understood as to understand, to be consoled as to console. For it is in pardoning that we are pardoned. It is in giving that we receive. And it is in dying that we rise to eternal life.

Blessed are those moments when you despair and think you will never understand, Q'uo says. Because at that point, when you can pinpoint something about the thinking process with which you might quarrel, something can actually be improved. Watch the thoughts. Watch the comments you make to yourself about those thoughts. The voices that are needed, they say, are the voices of silence. Not our words, not the words of your parents, not the words of any perceived guardian or authority can give you that which is beyond words: the presence of the one infinite Creator whose nature is absolute love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Stars in Orbit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: Two Stars in Orbit.

The twenty-fourth of February, two thousand and two. The question this week is about communication. Real communication. It is hard enough to be honest and speak clearly to another person about what you are thinking and feeling. How can a person also engage the heart, so that the intellectual communication shared is not just words?

Q'uo finds it a provocative subject, one with many subtleties. And they begin by saying that communication is a far more multi-dimensional process than the words alone would suggest. When they speak words through the instrument, they are usually offering concepts which do not come in the shape of words, but have that quality of infinity which rounds the two-dimensional into the third, the fourth, the fifth and the sixth dimensions. So that the same words coming into the field of twelve different entities will mean twelve different very complex sets of things.

It is helpful, Q'uo says, to step back and look at who is communicating. As you sit in your chair you would seem to be a fairly well-defined physical object. You weigh so much, you have so much mass, a certain color of hair, a certain color of eyes. You present a fairly simplified picture of a finite entity. Yet in truth, within your finite bounds, each of you contains the heavens and the earth and all that in them is. Each of you is all that there is, and all that there is resides within you.

How shall that star which is you shine in such a way as to communicate to that star which is shining back at you?

Within this image lies the question of energy fields, Q'uo says, and how they attract or repel each other. Some entities will be helped and pulled together by the forces that will naturally drive other entities apart, because each entity has a certain quality of vibration which carries a certain charge. It is simply a matter of each person having a very discernible, clear signature of being that expresses far below the level of self-awareness. You put out a very clear signal, each of you. There is only one of you. There is only one of each of you, and each of you is precious and unique and quite necessary.

The goal of communication often seems to be to come to a resolution, to effect a change, to get things done. And Q'uo suggests something quietly subversive. There are times when the goal of communication is not so much to obtain the desired result, but simply to express the dynamic that is occurring. Not with a drive to find a solution, but in the spirit of clarification, so that between two entities who differ there comes into being a growing understanding of that fuller nature of that other self that lies behind the seemingly flat surface of a disagreement.

You expect communication to behave like a chemical interaction, Q'uo says: a vector, a direction, an arrow from one to two to three to four. Information received and processed, work done, decisions made. And sometimes two entities accomplish these things with very little effort, and those are blessed times. But in the communications that have gone awry, the assumption is always that the goal of a conversation would be to come to a conclusion. And Q'uo suggests that this is not always the most helpful model. Sometimes what matters is that each who attempts to communicate simply express the emotions, the mental structures, and the spiritual considerations that have injected themselves into the matter.

And then Q'uo gives us the image I want to carry. It is tempting, even seductive, to enter the list of communication as if it were a medieval jousting match, with the communicators loading up their armor and getting on their destriers and heading toward each other with a shield in one hand and a lance in the other, to get their ideas across and, of course, knock that person off of their steed and win at the list of communication. This is not a model Q'uo encourages.

They encourage instead the model that realizes right and wrong have only a limited amount of energy, whereas truth and love are equal in their energies. What is being communicated is the tip of an iceberg. And when the skillful person hears what is communicated, that person is willing to open awareness to take in not simply the point of the iceberg showing above water, not simply the words, but is willing to open to the unseen presence of all that is below the waterline: all that is unsaid, all that fills out the substance of an opinion or a feeling. So that each can see the other as a positive source of information and support, even when there seem to be huge discrepancies in opinion and ample evidence suggesting the impossibility of a happy conclusion.

It is not necessary to have a happy ending in order to have good communication, Q'uo says. These dynamics are dynamics of illusion. That which is valuable is the spirit within each of the parties who communicate.

And all of the things in your life are placeholders for things of the spirit, Q'uo reminds us. All things are alive. All things are ready to tell you their story. There are wonderful, powerful spiritual energies just waiting for channels through which they may run, be blessed, and come into the power and ownership of the Earth.

Two stars in orbit. Not two lances in a joust. Remember the signature. Respect the unsaid. Let the communication be the clarification, not the conquest.

Thank you for listening.

title: Roots in Heaven
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: Roots in Heaven.

The seventh of March, two thousand and two. A special meditation. The group has spent the afternoon in a meeting about how to make the Law of One information available to more people. Many ideas have been exchanged. They ask Q'uo for a response: what is the value of this effort, and what is the likelihood of its success?

Q'uo begins with simple joy. Joy that entities who so dearly wished before incarnation to come together in the grand collaboration have come to the moment of realizing just a bit of that wonderful, peaceful awareness of the lightness and worth of the ideals about which they have been speaking. They confirm that this is a good plan for such efforts, for within your density at this time there is indeed an increasing transparency, and fourth density is as close as your breathing. It is truly said that heaven is near at hand.

It is necessary only to claim that awareness, Q'uo says, in order to begin, as the one known as K has said, to participate in an alternate reality: a reality of concept, intent and desire.

And then Q'uo gives the principle that governs all such work. Remember, they say, the truth of the energy flow concerning metaphysical law. It is not that which is of this world. Rather, it is as if one planted a tree with the roots in heaven and the branches touching the Earth: through people, through works of art, through every channel of living energy that has been created by thought, whether it be the original Thought of unconditional love which is the infinite Creator, or whether it be that which is produced by the co-Creator that each of you is.

A tree planted upside down. Roots in heaven, branches touching the Earth. I love that Q'uo reaches for this image when the question is about planning and outreach and logistics. The linear details matter, but they are not the source of the life.

In the metaphysical world, chariots are your thoughts, Q'uo says. That which you create which goes forth in the metaphysical world is created because of your desire, your will, your faith. And so when it comes to the details and the planning of that linear nature, remember that the energy of the spiritual world is coming very reliably down the trunk of the Tree of Life and into its branches, which are each of you. As above, so below is one of this entity's favorite sayings. There is a shape hoped for by the plastic and progressing thought processes of each of those who are collaborating within a given project, and each is a channel, receiving guidance concerning the collaboration.

So Q'uo asks that we trust and consult guidance as plans are made, in addition to using the very sound linear and intellectual processes of analysis in the creative conception. Both. Not one or the other.

And then this, which I think is the most important line in the session. Each should realize the sacredness of the life surrounding such an effort. For the life must support the work. If the attempt is made to merge the world of thought and the world of commercial ventures or business, remember that the energy that is within the reach of each who offers needs to be respected, and its path allowed to remain clear.

The life must support the work. The messenger's own being is part of the message. Burnout, grasping, compromise: these are not merely practical problems. They are breaks in the very channel through which the work flows.

Beyond all considerations, Q'uo says, the chief lessons of the enterprise have always to do with accepting love from others and giving love to others without pride, vanity or feelings of unworthiness. The work that each of you does in truly entering into the energies of each of you will create creative pathways that will link in a more telepathic or whole-concept level, so that the synergy of energy fields becomes consciously validated, freeing those energy exchanges to take place at an enhanced rate.

There is also a great deal of unseen, hidden work possible during communication which creates far better collaboration, Q'uo says. Conscious acceptance of the ideal of a spiritual community, where each is nurtured by each, is helpful for communicators. For each of you has the ability to comfort and feed others by the attitude with which you greet your compatriots, and all of those about you have that same ability to function as support, encouragement and humor for you.

I find something tender in this session. A small group of people, sitting around a table, wondering whether their plans to share something they love will amount to anything. And Q'uo's answer is not a business plan. It is a cosmology. Plant the tree upside down. Let the roots drink from heaven. Trust the guidance coming down the trunk. Keep the life clean enough to carry it. And accept love from each other along the way, without pride, without vanity, without feelings of unworthiness.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Still Small Voice
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the still small voice.

It was a Sunday meditation in March of two thousand and two, and the group had noticed something. People were dealing with old issues they had shelved for years. New ones were popping up overnight. There seemed to be an unusual amount of fuel available for spiritual growth. They asked Q'uo if the perception was real, and if so, what to do with all that energy.

Q'uo's answer, I think, is both a confirmation and a gentle warning. Yes, they said, there is more energy available. Your planet has entered the dawn of fourth density, the density of love and understanding, and in that environment guidance is closer and stronger. But the guidance answers to the call you send out. Q'uo compared it to a radio. You are the listener, tuning the dial of the self. Whatever signal you put out has the potential of an enormously enlarged response.

The next decade, they said, would be the end of the end of the old age, not the beginning of the end. And in that time there would be increasing transparency between desire and guidance, so that help, once it is asked for, can be squared and squared again. For those who seek to purify their emotions and see into the heart of their desires, there will be miracles occurring, peace becoming possible within the heart, helpful coincidences, evidence of unseen hands at work. But the same energy answers fear too. Those who read the new energy as power that cannot be controlled will find more confusion, more misguidance, more opportunities for negative catalyst. Not because the energy is bad, but because the call was fearful. The radio plays the station you tuned.

And here is the line that steadied me: guidance does not have to do with your catalyst. It has to do with you. The painful events, the difficult people, those are the curriculum, the friction that teaches. Guidance is the mechanism that helps you look at your own thoughts and your own responses, and take the longer view. Listen to how they put it: guidance helps an entity "take a longer point of view and see into interior patterns that are not necessarily obvious upon the surface."

Then Q'uo said something I did not expect, and I have been sitting with it all week. You need to be tough, they said. Tough enough to listen to guidance and still make your own conclusion. That was the actual word from Carla's own guide, spoken in her private meditation: you are now able to listen to our words because you are tough, and have become tough enough to listen, and yet make your own conclusion. The mature listener, it turns out, is not the obedient one. The mature listener is the one who can hold a voice of guidance beside her own judgment and let both speak.

Later in the session someone asked what to do when a desire to help a family member blows up in your face. The surface says failure. Q'uo said, look again. All experience is in motion. What looks like failure today may be the first movement of growth. Ancient energies being expressed. Parts being assigned for a play that is not finished yet. There has been movement, they said. Growth comes in many packages. Do not ever feel that failure is all that is possible to determine from a situation in which anger has played a large part.

And Carla, the instrument herself, brought a worry that night. She had been receiving inner promptings that called her a prophet of Mary, of Sophia, and she was afraid of painting herself into a corner of ego. I love Q'uo's response, because it is so sane. Those energies are open-ended, they said. You know how to challenge them. Return to your North Star. And to her deeper question, whether it is because she is a Christian woman that the rays come to her shaped as Christ, the simple confirmation: yes, that is so. She does not need to take it literally. The mystery can be invited without being made into a mission.

So what is the practice, if you want to work with this amplified guidance? Q'uo kept it simple. Turn concern into prayer. When the emotion you feel is not the emotion of your true heart, turn it into prayer for another, and trust that even silent prayer has a real effect, because what one person knows can pass to another without words. It usually comes, they said, in a still, small voice of silence. That is the title I gave tonight's episode, and I cannot improve on it.

Tune the radio. Be tough enough to keep your own conclusion. And when you worry, pray. The help is closer than it has ever been.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Cannot Fail
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you cannot fail.

The question that spring Sunday was about service. If we want to serve, is there a danger of distorting it, of being proud of our service, of doing it in public so that it feeds the ego? The group wanted to know the optimum way to be of service to others without activating the ego along the way.

Q'uo began not with rules but with the foundation, and I want to give you the image exactly as they gave it, because it is worth closing your eyes for. They showed the instrument a blank, black night sky, without even stars. Not darkness as emptiness, but darkness as fullness upon fullness of light, a field of energy without any visual cue, without any proof of its existence or its identity. That, they said, is the foundation stone of each incarnational self. You are a gathering from fullness into fullness, formed without sight, without vision, out of energy itself, and that energy is love.

You chose, they said, very carefully, the attributes and limitations and gifts you carry in this life, from a vast array of distortions within a soul self that has been formed through many, many experiences. Your value to the Creator is precisely in those irregularities, eccentricities, and inconsistencies that make you just the personality you are. I love that line. The very things you apologize for are the instrument.

And then the sentence that became tonight's title. In terms of pleasing the infinite Creator, and in terms of fulfilling your hopes of serving, you cannot fail. For all that you do informs the one great original Thought in a way that no other spark in the infinite universe can. Each of you is precious and beloved by the Creator. When the doubts of self-worth rise, they said, move to that place of safety and rest that the instrument calls Gilead, and feel the balm of the Creator's love. For truly, in the Creator's eyes, you can do no wrong.

Q'uo then described the kind of seeker who comes to this work. There is a surface to consensus reality, they said, like a glass floor you cannot see. Many move from infancy to the grave without once falling through into the great reaches of deeper consciousness, never leaving the comfortable shallowness that allows almost complete control. But that was never a possibility for this circle. You seek not the surface but the water world beneath it, a world of smooth, rhythmic gliding.

And the way energy moves through water became their great image of service. Push water from behind, and it does not travel from here to there. It passes its force to the next drop, to the next, so that something that occurred off the coast of Japan can eventually express itself upon the shores of California. Study water, they said, to see how entities come together in their patterns, how service may not show where you expect it but arrive at a distant shore, long after the wave you began has traveled. There is a demand we put on service, that it be quantifiable, measurable, visible. Release that tension. The joy of service is in the doing, not in the result you are permitted to see.

Then came the turn that surprised me. Let us shift to another gear, they said, and look at being and doing. Some of service does have to do with doing, and they praised every kindness freely given from the heart. But always, the truer and deeper elements of service have to do with your being. It does not matter, in terms of the worth of service, what that service is. Some services may seem more noble than others. And yet all service is equal. What ennobles service is the love with which it is offered. That love can be held within the heart, withheld, or released. And judging yourself against a picture of service held in the mind, they said, is only a mind game.

Someone asked about a good day he had had, a day of unusual patience and peace, and wanted to know how to bottle the magic and get the feeling back. I want you to hear this answer slowly. To be, and to accept yourself as you are, they said, is the quickest road to attaining those goals you desire. And when you do achieve a success, do not feel overly glad, for to become attached to one expression or another is to place small stumbling blocks in your own way. It is a balancing act, my friends. On the one hand, you have a journey to make. On the other hand, you are the Creator, all is truly well, and there is no need for anything. That is the paradox in which each of you moves.

So the optimum service, the answer to the question, turns out not to be a technique at all. It is a posture. Rest in who you are. Offer from the heart. Release the judgment of how you are doing. And let the ripples go where they go, the way water does.

Thank you for listening.

title: Coming Home to the Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: coming home to the heart.

The question that April Sunday was the one every seeker carries into the grocery store, the office, the traffic jam. Each of us has had moments of accessing the energy of compassion, prolonged experiences that let us know it is real. The group wanted to know how opening the heart is actually accomplished by those of us who live here in third density, still behind the veil of forgetting, trying to discover our unity with all things while living the daily round of activities.

Q'uo stepped back from the question entirely, and took the group with them to the beginnings of creation. The Creator, they said, burst forth in an infinite number of sparks, each containing the stuff of the Creator in holographic form, each sent out to collect information. You are beings of light, beings of love, beings of infinity, citizens of an eternal universe that expresses itself in illusion upon illusion upon illusion. And the Creator's only hope for you is that you be yourself, and explore what the self is in an ever more profound sense. In cameo, in small, you are the microcosm of which the Creator is the macrocosm.

And here is the teaching I keep returning to. Each of you came specifically to be thrown off balance, to be confused, puzzled, foolish and wrong. You knew before incarnation that the great opportunity of the illusion is that spirit cannot be seen or proven here. You are not here to be masters of the illusion. You are here to be confused, and in the scramble and the struggle, the aura you brought in, with the gems of creatorship hidden in it, goes through the refining fire of your Earth, and your emotions stabilize and deepen and purify themselves through the hard-won experience of it all. That friction creates great beauty.

So what is the secret of finding your way back to the open heart? Q'uo said there is one, and it is buried in every religion, which is why they encouraged each person to play with the religious and mythical images that pierce their own heart. For Carla it is Jesus Christ. For you it may be something else. Whatever your image of unconditional and sacrificial love, the secret is to know in the deepest part of your soul that who you really are is the Creator, so that moving into the open heart is a matter of coming home.

There is a home within your heart, they said, that the instrument calls the sanctuary, the holy of holies, the inner temple of self. You might picture it as a room locked against casual visitors, even against yourself. The key that unlocks the door is silence. The momentary stopping of the inner voice. Once there, you are in a tabernacle with the Creator, and you may sit and rest, or even, as Carla often does, picture yourself crawling into the lap of the Creator and resting against that comfortable, strong breast. The Creator is waiting in every moment of every day, hoping and rejoicing when you come home.

And then the teaching that became tonight's title. You do not need to strive for unconditional love, because at the very center of the self, the truth of the self is this same shining, unconditional love. When all else is released, this is your nature. This is your essence. And your outer personality becomes as a pane of glass, clear and transparent, able to let the light shine through.

Then the session turned practical, and I want to give you the two instructions as plainly as they were given. First, re-experience the ordinary things of the day as if all were new, because they are full of light. Each day is a brand new gift, a brand new life, a new opportunity to find the most creative ways to love. The joy of it is in the doing, not in the results. Others will reap the seeds you sow with your being this day.

And second, and I think this is the harder one: retain the energies to give to the self the love you hope to give to others, and do that before you attempt to give to others. It is as though each of you wishes to beautify the lives of others while leaving at home that self within that is as the neglected child. In Carla's holy works the direction is to love others as you love the self. It is important to love the self. It is not selfish. It is work that will probably need to be kept up day after day, ministering to yourself with the same joy that you minister to others.

There were questions at the end about envisioning a road into fourth density, and Q'uo gave the group the image of the Fool from the tarot, walking off the cliff and suspended in midair. It is foolish to seek to love all beings, they said. It is foolish to move intuitively in a world where reason wrests its reward from all. And yet, is it not foolish to love the Creator that you have not yet met? Yes, you build a road. It is a road made of things not of this world, the principles and qualities at the center of the heart of a Creator of love.

When the image of the self is the dancer instead of the bumbler, they said, then even falling down is part of the dance. Cherish and protect your sweet essence of self. Each of you truly is a child of the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mountaintop Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mountaintop within.

The group had just come from a workshop, and the question they brought on that May Sunday was the one that follows every mountaintop. How do we keep the excitement alive? How do we remember who we are, what we came to do, when the daily round of activities swallows the weekend whole? Is there a process we could accelerate or harmonize with, so the freshness does not fade?

Q'uo began with the state itself. It is never to be predicted, they said, how it will occur, under what circumstances, through what combination of effort or ritual. It is almost as if one emerges into it from a fog, a fog you did not see, a fog you did not know you were in until suddenly the mist clears and the sun shines, and all is made perfect, and quite perfect. This is a true state. It is not the same as happiness, which, as it comes, guarantees its own departure. This is a state that can remain through tragedy and times of personal difficulty. This is the temple within that no power of life or death can destroy.

And yet the experience most of us have is of coming into that temple and going out, being in that state and then abruptly abandoned on the shores of consensus reality. So Q'uo spoke of the simple, hard work. Persistence in a daily practice. The instrument's rule of life: a lit candle at the altar within, time spent in silence, opening the heart to tabernacle with the one infinite Creator that always awaits within the tabernacle of your own heart. The joy that lurks within the center of your being is invited by silence. It is a playful energy. It is full of light and full of dance, and each of you was intended to be a dancer through this illusion.

I love the image they gave of who we were, before we came. Each of you, upon the brink of incarnation, gazed at what was to come and thought, this will be so much fun. This will be so simple. How could I possibly forget any of the truths I know, simply by being born into this illusion? I will remember. I will remember. And then the air of Earth hits the face, and all of a sudden you are a helpless infant, dependent upon others for every need. Almost guaranteed, in childhood, come the repeated times when the feeling of panic and distress becomes overwhelming, and those biases are carried on the back like a burden until they are once again named and greeted and faced and embraced and loved and forgiven and placed within the heart to be healed, and then part of the strength of the entity that has come through many waters.

There was a thread in this session about community that moved me. The freshness of love, they said, is what spiritual communities are most excellent at maintaining in their members. And it is a matter of people, not institutions. In groups that gather in homes, unofficial and spontaneous, the likelihood of fresh energy is higher, because the only reason to come is the sense of a spiritual family that together may seek more efficiently than each alone. Each time you reconnect with those beloved strangers, part of your energy of being, another golden strand is laid within the net of love that surrounds the Earth, and it is glowing brighter every day.

And then the central teaching, the one I want to leave in your hands. Each of you has one central service in common, and that is the ministry of essence. The primary task is simply to be yourself. It always seems as though one must do something in order to be of service, and yet, as Q'uo has said many times, it is in how you are within yourself that you serve in the greatest capacity, since each of you is as the crystal that transmutes and sends forth the light that is received from the infinite Creator. When your heart is open and the light is flowing through you and you feel transparent to that energy, then the most beautiful light moves into that grid that the instrument sometimes calls the Christ grid, and which others have called the grid of unconditional love. Each of you is doing tremendous work for those who shall come after you, sowing seeds of light and seeds of love whose blossoms you shall not see, for you shall move on.

Do not be discouraged if your light is not accepted. That which is upon the surface is an illusion. The energetic work that you do is as it is. It is only necessary that you do the work, that you keep body, mind, and spirit in enough balance that energy may flow through. Be steadfast in those situations which do not seem full of love. Allow yourself to be the love that is brought to that meeting, to that moment, to that situation. And if you are flagging, and weary, reach out and allow someone to give to you that which you have so often given to others.

Know that your memories of the mountaintop times are perfect, that they are valid, that they are the truth of you. And know that in honoring that memory, in remembering those times, you allow yourself to rise once again to that mountaintop where all is well and all people are one.

Thank you for listening.

title: Where the Love Is
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: where the love is.

This was a private session, mid-May, with a question that had two prongs, both about the same hunger. The questioner wanted to know how to deal with the catalyst in her marriage, how to be of service and love there rather than adding to the difficulty. And she wanted to know how to read the strange guidance of her life, the quickening pulse, the synchronicities that happen all the time but whose meaning escapes her, the dreams she records many times a week but cannot interpret.

Q'uo began with a sweeping assumption, and I want you to sit with it the way they asked her to. All is one. The mate is the projection of the self into the face of another self, both entities being the Creator. Many entities chose to make commitments precisely for the efficiency of this mirroring. And then the sentence that turns the whole session around: the catalyst is the prize, not the problem, of the relationship. For it is in working with the catalyst of the self as projected onto the other self that the entity comes face to face with the refining fire of realization that this, too, is a part of me.

It is not possible to remove the shadow from the self, they said, for each contains the seeds of all things. If the self is all things, then it is also in part a shadow self, a darker, richer-hued, more difficult to comprehend part of the self. Wherever the fear is, there the catalyst will be rich upon the ground and ripe for the plucking. So it is not a skillful goal to wish never to be a catalyst for another, because that would suggest catalyst is unfortunate. What is truly unfortunate, they said, is that which never changes.

The practical question then becomes: how does one become a place of emotional safety for another, so that even within a disagreement, even within the tangles of personality, there is trust enough for each to feel comfortable misbehaving and apologizing and discussing with utter honesty those things which lack between the two? Q'uo offered the image of the pearl, the result of the irritation of sand within the oyster. Without the refining fire of seeming difficulties, the pearl, which is each of you, would never be polished into its complete and perfect beauty.

And then the practice, the one sentence I want you to carry. When the moment comes to respond to catalyst, let that response answer the question: where is the love in this moment? Beneath every difficulty that tangles two upon the soul level lies a unity, a oneness, more the truth of the relationship than any structure of description that lives in words rather than in the open heart which knows that it loves, though it knows not, perhaps, how to respond. See the relationship as an opportunity to be in love with the Creator, to tend to an angel that is in your care. Beneath the questions of this kind of love or that kind flows the current of friendship, companionship, and that wonderful ease that comes to those who truly and unguardedly love.

The second prong, the synchronicities and the dreams, got an answer I did not expect. Do not bear down too hard on understanding each message, they said. The magic lies within the feelings that synchronicities and dreams create and rouse within the self. These emotions are precious things, and through the incarnation each is working to purify, beautify, and make more truthful those expressions of pure being that emotions are. So ask the self: how do I feel? What color is this emotion? What part of myself does this seem to figure for? In dreams, every figure, every detail, every process is the self. There is no need to seek far for who these characters are, for they are all the self, symbols chosen because they are the closest construction the subconscious can find to create a precise shade of feeling.

And there was one more image, given near the end, that I have not been able to put down. Each of you is as the stained glass of a rich and beautiful design. All the colors within the window that is you are your very own. No one else has selected the way you move energy through your energy body. And this means you are creating a constant tapestry of color and music that is the personal signature of yourself. Your own knowing that you are on the right track, those silver flecks and quickenings she described, those are the signature becoming audible.

So the session's double question had one answer after all. Allow yourself to be ever more truly and deeply yourself. In that comfort of self, bless and welcome the infinite energy of the one Creator as it flows through. And when you stumble, move as a dancer even when you fall. Let there be the light touch, and let the self be merry.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Net of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the net of love.

That May Sunday the question was wide open. We have heard that the planetary vibration is changing, the group said, that each individual is going through a spiritual change as well. What can we do to facilitate this change, to help with these vibrations of love? And what, they asked, is the service Q'uo would most desire?

Q'uo's answer began with a metaphor that made me laugh and then made me sit very still. It is the time for growing the grass, they said, not for growing the trees. There are many trees on your planet, and it is the time for the grass. The trees, the teachers, are there to make sure the grass grows, but the trees cannot make the grass grow. The grass is everything else that grows on your planet. All of that which is humble, unassuming, seemingly without the knowledge of anything of spirituality or metaphysics, that is the grass, and it is the time for the grass to grow.

Those who are not consciously seeking are not lost, they said. The light of each is moving into the Earth itself, and it is all growing together into a bright and ever-more-glowing grid of light that is crisscrossing your planet and forming the framework of fourth density. The planet herself is going through the birthing of fourth density, and each is going through the birthing of the new life that comes with the marriage of self and self. Like a marriage, it is messy and awkward at times, and like all birth, it is an experience of intense pain and intense joy, the joy of knowing that out of the pain something beautiful is coming.

Then came the sentence I want to set in the center of this episode. Each of you is a master. Q'uo said it plainly, twice, with the gentleness of friends speaking to friends. You have come to your present location and your present time for the purpose of fulfilling that which the deeper self has chosen. It is not necessary to know what that deeper self is or what it intends, only to know that there is a plan and that you are in it, in just the way that has been set up for you. No one is in the wrong place. No one is an exception to the plan. The most useful word for this is not mastery but trust.

Someone asked about the second strand of DNA coming online, and Q'uo responded with candor I appreciated. That is a term of your own science that the instrument does not grasp well enough for us to give you a linear and specific answer, they said. But the concept is sound enough. The energy body is beginning to open and awaken, and what is becoming more and more true is the interconnection among you, the golden threads that reach from soul to soul to soul. As energies rise, those who seek truth will become more aware of their power, and also more aware that power is not of the ego but of the heart.

And then they answered the question about their own service, the service Q'uo most desires, and I want you to hear the tenderness in it. There are those in your world whose service is wisdom. Others offer spiritual strength. Others, like this instrument, have become able to be channels of light and love. But we, said Q'uo, would claim no such particular service. What we offer is an experience of unconditional love, in fellowship, in companionship, in the sharing of the path as a fellow sojourner. We can be no more to you than your friends.

There is a practice here, and it is deceptively small. We would encourage each, when meditating, to set up within the self the image of a little watchtower, a little lighthouse, whose beacon is simply unconditional love. And ask yourself, whenever you see a light to be lit or a heart to be healed: how can I most fully serve in this situation? For you are a lighthouse for others, not knowing who may be in need of light.

I want to close with the image that made the whole room laugh, because it holds everything we have said. Someone asked about scrubbing toilets, and Q'uo said, yes, scrubbing the toilet is an energy which may be used in many ways. It may be seen as drudgery. It may be seen as work to be sloughed through. Or it may be seen as the most healing of energies, the energy which heals through serving, because there is nothing that expresses more totally the ability to serve as healer than the desire to do those jobs which no one wants to do. Whoever does such service from the heart is expressing her essential mastership.

The grass grows. The net of love brightens. The lighthouse stands. That is the work.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Leap of Faith
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the leap of faith.

The questioner came to this private session tired. She had been a dedicated seeker for a long time, and she found it difficult to love, difficult to relate, difficult to feel unconditional love, and difficult to feel her spiritual connection. She asked Q'uo for guidance. And their answer, I think, is one of the most compassionate things in the whole archive.

They began by naming the loneliness of awakening exactly as it is. The spiritual awakening, they said, is like an awakening in the desert. At first there is nothing but desert. The world seems harsh, without oasis, without love. The seeker has opened and asked and prayed for help, and it seems as though the desert winds have answered with more and more wind, more and more dust, more and more emptiness. It takes the self a very long time to realize that this desert is not as it seems, that in fact there is water beneath the sands.

The work itself, they said, is simple, which is not the same as easy. The questioner is seeking a more open heart. What is needed is the practice of self-forgiveness, of self-acceptance, of learning to find the self lovable at last. This is a great work, they said. Perhaps it is the only work. And the energy body works against the self when the self condemns and criticizes itself. When you feel low and discouraged about your ability to love, this does not help you. You are taking energy from your heart and spending it on the self as critic.

Then came the teaching about faith, and I want you to hear it in Q'uo's own rhythm. The leap of faith is one which is made into thin air, they said. It takes the courage to simply leap into the midair, trusting that there is something which will uphold the leap, even though the self has never before experienced that which upholds faith. And we know you have a sense of humor about this. And so you have. They reminded her of the cartoon coyote that walks off the cliff and hangs suspended for a moment before dropping, and of Peter, walking on the water toward the Christ, upheld not by his feet but by his faith, until he remembered to be afraid, and sank.

Faith, they said, is a leap into thin air that works only when the self believes there is something real enough to walk upon, when there is in fact only air and no visible support. The truth is that it always works. The support is invisible. The support has always been there, ready to uphold every entity that reaches out its foot in midair and stands upon the breath of the Creator. The only thing that does not work is looking down. Peter did not sink because the water would not hold him. He sank because he remembered he was afraid.

There is a practical thread running through this session that I want to pull out for you. When the questioner asked about retaining energy, Q'uo said something precise. Before the incarnation, the seeker knows she has much to do, and she has planned for much to be done. Once within the incarnation, the self has the opportunity to be that which it desires to be and to do that which it desires to do, but only as the energy allows, and the energy is extremely limited. Retain the energies for the self first. Be able to be selfish for the self in terms of taking time for rest, contemplation, reflection, and the breathing in and out of the silence. Then, when those resources have been renewed, look out into the world and ask: what would love do here?

I should mention that the questioner also asked about physical weariness and illness, and while the spiritual teaching about exhaustion is beautiful, this is a moment for honesty. Spiritual insight is not a diagnosis, and a tired body deserves real-world care. If you are living with unexplained fatigue or illness, please walk with your doctors and healers alongside any inner work.

The session closed with the most delicate image. Q'uo showed the instrument a light bulb, and inside it a closed loop of fire, burning not outward but inward, a fire that lit from within. There is love already within, they said. It is the love that lights the self from within. There is no need to go elsewhere for love. The love is within. But the fire needs tending. Feed that which is within the self with good thoughts, with good deeds, with the intention of love, and the fire will burn brighter and stronger and more purely, until the fire of the self becomes the true and pure flame of the Creator.

The desert has water beneath it. The air will hold you. Step out.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dance Anyway
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dance anyway.

The group had been receiving messages through the internet about frightening prophecies of catastrophe, and they asked Q'uo for perspective. Are these visions real? Should we prepare? The answer they got was not what they expected, and it has aged into something much larger than the question that prompted it.

Q'uo began by saying plainly that it is very difficult to make good, accurate predictions from the inner planes. Not because the beings who speak are insincere, but because prophecy concerns the flow of events in which each soul is involved in a way that is simply too complex to map. Every prediction, they said, no matter how inspired, is almost always wrong in some important respect. Not necessarily false in essence. Just wrong in detail, wrong in timing, wrong in the way the human mind reads the symbols it has been given.

And there is a deeper reason for this unreliability. Each soul, before incarnation, made its own rough plan for its life, a plan that includes choices about when and how to leave this life. So it is impossible to separate the predictions given to one entity from the plans of all the entities involved in those events. The prophecies are not describing a fixed future. They are describing a field of possibilities, colored by the expectations of everyone who hears them.

But then Q'uo said the thing I will carry with me, the thing that makes this session worth your time tonight. There is a catastrophe facing each entity that is absolutely certain, they said. The catalyst of leaving this life behind. Each will face death. Each will face the letting go of everything known. In that sense, the doomsayers are right that a great change is coming. It is just that the change is personal, and it is certain for every one of us, and it does not need a prophet to announce it.

So the question becomes not how to prepare for the world ending, but how to live with the world ending, daily, in the only way we ever actually meet it. And here is Q'uo's answer, and I love it for its plainness. Choose the thread of love. There are two threads running through every moment, they said: the thread of fear and the thread of love. You cannot serve both. When you hear frightening news, ask which thread you are feeding. Fear contracts. Love expands. Choose the thread that leads to the heart, and you will never be lost, no matter what happens in the outer world.

There was a practical teaching in this session about the mixed life we are living now, with third density not yet gone and fourth density already dawning. The instrument's own practice, given to her by her guidance, was to begin each morning in silence, to sit with the Creator before the day begins, and to carry that center with her. In a time of transition, they said, the entities who will do best are those who have a practice, however small, that reminds them daily of who they are.

And then the ending that gave this episode its title. Someone in the group asked what to do with all this, with the prophecies, the uncertainty, the weight of it. Q'uo's answer was almost mischievous. Dance, they said. Play. Do the things that make the heart sing. The serious business of the spiritual life is not seriousness. The most powerful response to fear is not a better plan. It is joy.

I keep thinking about that. The world of the prophecies never arrived. The catastrophe that did arrive, for each of us, was personal, as they said it would be. And the instruction holds in both cases. Do not feed the fear. Tend the morning silence. Choose the thread of love. And no matter what the messages say is coming, dance anyway.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Onion of Beauty
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the onion of beauty.

The question that June evening was about beauty, but really it was about relationship. The group was exploring how men and women perceive each other, what happens when physical attraction and spiritual connection meet, and whether desire itself is a failure. Q'uo answered with one of the most complete teachings in the archive on how a human being actually meets beauty, center by center, layer by layer. It became tonight's title.

They asked us to imagine beauty as an onion, and to peel it slowly, from the outside in. The outer skin is the red ray, the instinctual body, and here Q'uo was wonderfully blunt. Physical attraction is an animal instinct. It is hardwired. It is the body's way of recognizing a potential mate, and there is no shame in the mechanism itself. The attraction of the eye, the response of the body, these belong to the second-density creature we also are, and they function whether the spirit approves or not. An entity can be committed, faithful, and spiritually devoted, and still notice beauty. The noticing is not the failing.

But the onion has deeper layers, and each one changes what beauty is. Move inward to the orange ray, and beauty becomes personal, tangled with the self's own story. Here is where the real work happens, because this is the center where we meet our own wounds, our own hungers, our own unexamined needs, and project them onto the other. So many relationships stumble here, not because the beauty was false, but because the self looking at it was not yet known to itself.

Move deeper still, to the yellow ray, and beauty becomes social, tribal, cultural. This is the beauty of the family, the clan, the shared story, the patina that forms on a relationship the longer two people walk together. A face you have loved for twenty years carries a beauty no stranger's face can carry, because it is layered with memory, with shared laughter, with the look that says we have been through this before, together.

And then the green ray, the heart, where beauty stops being about the other at all and becomes about the seeing itself. Q'uo quoted the poet Keats here, "truth is beauty, and beauty is truth," and they meant it literally. When the heart is open, the beholder and the beheld are not two. There is a German phrase the instrument loved, ding an sich, the thing in itself, and Q'uo used it to describe this moment: you do not see the surface of the person. You see the thing itself, the soul, shining through the personality the way light shines through stained glass.

Deeper still lie the blue and indigo centers, where beauty becomes communication and then pure knowing, the recognition of the other self as the self. At this depth, they said, the question of attraction dissolves, because there is no other to be attracted to. There is only the one infinite Creator, meeting itself in a new face.

I want to be honest about something. This teaching touches the body, and desire, and the tender places where people carry shame, and I do not want to leave that unspoken. If this evening's talk of bodies and longing has stirred tender feelings in you, consider sharing them with someone you trust in your waking life, a friend, a counselor, anyone who listens kindly.

The practical teaching at the end of the session was the balancing meditation, the daily practice of sitting with the experiences of the day and letting each one find its center. And there was one more image I have kept. Q'uo said that each person is a beautiful being, and that the work of the seeker is to learn to see it, layer by layer, until the seeing itself becomes the love. The onion has no core. Peel it all the way down and what you find is not a center but a fragrance, everywhere at once.

So do not condemn the eye for noticing. Teach it, instead, to look deeper. That is the whole curriculum, and it is the work of a lifetime.

Thank you for listening.

title: When Love Cannot Reach
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: when love cannot reach.

This was a private session, on the fourth of July, and the question was about a relationship that had become a labyrinth. The questioner had met a man, V, through an internet dating service, and what began as companionship had turned strange and tangled. She asked Q'uo what was happening between them, on every level, and how she could untangle herself without doing harm.

Q'uo's answer was given in the language of the metaphysics she had asked for, and I am going to translate it into plain speech, because the teaching underneath is one many people need. This was, they said, a meeting arranged before birth, and not a comfortable one. The two had been entangled across lifetimes, and the pattern between them was old. In this life he had come with a deep distortion, a wound around love itself, and his way of reaching for connection had become reaching for control. She had come with the complementary wound: the belief that if she loved purely enough, she could heal him.

I want to say this carefully, because it matters. Q'uo described a dynamic in which one partner feeds on the other's energy, in which the connection feels fated and intense and impossible to leave, and in which the loving partner keeps pouring light into a vessel that cannot hold it. They spoke of it in terms of polarity and energy transfer, but the human shape of it is familiar. One person gives and gives. The other takes and takes. And the giver calls it love.

Here is the teaching, and it is blunt. You cannot heal another person by loving them. Love is not a tool for fixing someone. Q'uo told her, in essence, that the service she could offer this man was not her energy, not her body, not her endless patience. It was her absence. By withdrawing her energy, by refusing to participate in the pattern, she would give him the only thing that could actually help him: the silence in which he might finally meet himself.

Before I go further, I need to pause, because this teaching touches a place where real people are hurting right now. If a relationship of your own feels tangled and frightening in the way this one was, you do not have to carry it alone. Please reach out to someone you trust, a counselor, a friend, or a crisis line in your area. Insight is good. Safety is better, and it comes first.

The practical guidance Q'uo gave her was specific and, I think, wise. Retain your energy for yourself. They told her to stop sending him light, to stop praying for his transformation, to stop doing the inner work on his behalf. Instead, turn all of that care inward. Build the silence. Sing the sacred songs, the ones that belong to you, not the ones you sang for him. Fill your own vessel first, and let the pattern starve for lack of fuel.

There is a subtlety here that I do not want to lose. Withdrawing is not punishment. It is not revenge. Q'uo was clear that she should release him with love, genuinely wishing him well, and then turn her face toward her own life. The entanglement ends not with a battle but with a quiet closing of the door, and the understanding that some souls have agreed to teach each other precisely by being impossible for each other.

The session also touched on why such meetings feel so fated, and the answer is worth hearing. Before incarnation, we make agreements. We choose our teachers. And some of our teachers come disguised as lovers, as friends, as the people we cannot stop thinking about. The lesson is never in fixing them. The lesson is in what their presence reveals about us: the places where we abandon ourselves, the belief that our worth is measured by our ability to save someone.

If you are in a labyrinth like this one, hear the teaching at its simplest. Stop pouring. Come home to yourself. Sing your own song. The love you were spending on someone who could not receive it is needed, urgently, by the one person who can: you.

Thank you for listening.

title: Pain as Fertilizer
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: pain as fertilizer.

The questioner came to this August session with a direct question. What is the spiritual meaning of pain and suffering? She wanted to understand why it exists, what it does, and how a seeker is meant to meet it. Q'uo's answer is one of the most complete teachings on suffering in the archive, and it begins in a place you might not expect.

They began with the mind. Pain and suffering, they said, are first of all experiences of the mind. The mind that is not balanced will pass its unprocessed catalyst to the body, and the body will express what the mind could not. This is not blame. It is mechanics. The body is the faithful servant of the mind's unfinished business, and illness and pain are often the body's way of saying: there is something here you have not yet looked at.

But Q'uo was quick to add what the teaching is not. It is not that the sufferer did something wrong. It is not that pain is punishment, or that the one in pain has failed spiritually. Suffering is the friction of a soul learning. And then they gave the image that became tonight's title. Pain, they said, is as the fertilizer in the garden of the soul. No one plants fertilizer for its own sake. No one celebrates the smell of it. But nothing grows tall without it. The experiences we would never choose are the ones that break up the hard soil.

There is a passage in this session where Q'uo quotes the teachings of Ra on the balancing of the self, and I want to give you the heart of it. Each experience of pain is an opportunity to balance, to find the love in the moment, to see the Creator in the suffering. The one who suffers and still turns toward love has done the great work. Not because the suffering was good, but because the turning was.

The session also took up the question of happiness, and here Q'uo said something I have been turning over for weeks. Happiness is not an objective. It is not the goal of the spiritual life, and chasing it as a goal is one of the great confusions of the seeker. What the great teachers point to is not happiness but something steadier: a state of being that can hold both joy and sorrow without breaking. They spoke of the one the world knows as a teacher of compassion, who describes not happiness but bliss, a quiet radiance that remains when the storm has passed through and the sky is clear again.

And then the teaching on fear, which runs underneath everything Q'uo says about suffering. Fear, they said, contracts the consciousness. It narrows the field of what can be seen, until the sufferer can see nothing but the pain. Love does the opposite. Love expands. The work of meeting suffering is the work of refusing to let fear have the last word about what an experience means. This does not make the pain smaller. It makes the self larger than the pain.

I need to pause here, because this teaching walks a fine line, and I want to walk it honestly. The idea that suffering can be fertilizer is a spiritual truth, not a treatment plan. If you are living with pain, please keep your doctors and healers close, and let real human care walk beside you while you do the inner work.

The practical teaching at the end was the daily practice of silence and balancing, the sitting with the self that lets the unprocessed catalyst be processed before the body has to carry it. And there was one more sentence I want to leave with you, because it reframes the whole subject. The Creator, they said, did not make a mistake in including suffering in the design. The design was made for souls who wanted the full curriculum, the hard soil and the fertilizer and all. You signed up for the garden, not just the harvest.

So if you are in pain tonight, hear this. You have not failed. The soil is being broken. Something is being prepared to grow. And the turning toward love, even now, especially now, is the whole of the work.

Thank you for listening.

title: Breathing In Thanks
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: breathing in thanks.

The question on that September Sunday was simple, and the answer remade it. What is gratitude, really? Not the polite kind, not the thank-you note kind, but the spiritual kind. What does it do, and how does one live inside it? Q'uo's answer begins by turning the question around.

Gratitude, they said, is not a response to good things happening. It is a way of being. Most people practice gratitude backwards: something good happens, and then they feel thankful. But the gratitude Q'uo describes flows the other direction. It is the stance of the self toward existence itself, taken before anything happens, and held regardless of what happens. It is not thanks for the gift. It is the recognition that existence is the gift.

And then they gave the practice, and it is so simple you could miss it. Breathe in thanks. Breathe out praise. That is the whole instruction. With each inhalation, receive the moment as a gift you did nothing to earn. With each exhalation, return praise to the Creator, not for any particular outcome, but for the sheer fact of being alive to breathe at all. The breath becomes a prayer that never stops, a conversation carried on beneath all the other conversations of the day.

Q'uo used the image of a cut flower to show what happens when we forget this. A flower cut from its stem still looks like a flower for a while. It still has its color, its shape. But it is no longer receiving. It is living on stored life, and it withers. The self that moves through the day without gratitude is like that flower: still functioning, still beautiful, but cut off from the source. The breath of thanks is what keeps the stem connected.

There was a thread in this session about the ten thousand things, the old phrase for the whole teeming world, and Q'uo said that each of them is singing. The song of the creation is going on whether or not anyone is listening. Gratitude is what tunes the ear. And here is the line I keep coming back to: each of you has a song that no one else has ever sung. Your life, your particular way of moving through the world, is an original composition. Gratitude is how you learn to hear your own song while you are singing it.

The session also touched on something the group had been discussing, the idea of harvest, of spiritual polarity, of whether one is positively or negatively oriented. And Q'uo said something that cut through a great deal of anxiety. The harvest is not a test you pass by achieving the right thoughts. It is the natural result of a life lived in love. Gratitude, practiced as a way of being, does the work on its own. You do not need to measure your polarity. You need only to keep breathing thanks, and let the rest take care of itself.

I want to add a practical note, because this teaching is so simple it invites a misunderstanding. Breathing in thanks does not mean pretending everything is fine. It does not mean being thankful for suffering, or performing cheerfulness when the heart is broken. Q'uo was clear that gratitude includes the whole of experience. You can breathe in thanks for the breath itself while still grieving what the day has brought. The thanks is not for the circumstance. It is for the aliveness in which the circumstance is happening.

So tonight, wherever you are, try it. One breath. In: thanks. Out: praise. Not for anything in particular. Just for this, this moment, this being here. Do it again. And notice what happens to the room you are sitting in, to the weight of the day, to the flower on its stem.

The song is already playing. Gratitude is how you join it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Sphere of Balance
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the sphere of balance.

The question that September Sunday was about balance. How does one stay balanced in a world that keeps tipping? The group wanted something practical, something they could actually do when the day runs sideways. Q'uo's answer began by quietly dismantling the question.

Balance, they said, is not what you think it is. Most of us picture a scale, two pans, and the work of keeping them level. Or we picture walking a tightrope, and the terror of falling off. Q'uo offered a different image entirely. Balance is a sphere. A ball. Something that rolls, that bounces, that wobbles and rights itself, that can be dropped and picked up again. You do not achieve a sphere. You inhabit it. And when it rolls away from you, you do not panic. You go and pick it up.

I love this image because it removes the moral judgment from losing your footing. In the scale model, imbalance is failure. In the sphere model, imbalance is just motion. The ball is supposed to roll. Your job is not to freeze it in place but to stay in relationship with it, to keep coming back, to keep picking it up with a light hand.

The session moved through the prayers that people actually use when they are skidding. Q'uo spoke of the prayer attributed to Saint Francis, the one that asks to be made an instrument of peace, and of the simple prayer of the fellowship of those recovering from addiction: the request for the serenity to accept what cannot be changed, the courage to change what can, and the wisdom to know the difference. These prayers work, they said, not because of their words but because of their posture. Each one is a way of saying: I cannot steer this skid, so I will stop trying to steer and start trying to be present.

That is the practical teaching, and I want to give it to you plainly. When you are skidding, do not steer. The instinct, when life loses traction, is to grip harder, to think faster, to fix it all at once. Q'uo says the opposite. Relax the grip. Let the vehicle go where it is going for a moment. And in that moment of not steering, turn toward the one thing that is always available: the heart. Love the skid. Love the dark patch you are sliding across. There is a line from the session I have written on a card: see the dark, and love it with your light. Not fix it. Not flee it. Love it.

There was a thread about taking the self lightly that I want to pull out, because it is the secret ingredient. The entities who stay balanced, they said, are not the ones who never fall. They are the ones who can laugh at the falling. Solemnity is heavy, and heavy things do not roll well. Take yourself lightly. Let the sphere bounce. The Creator, they reminded the group, has a sense of humor about all of this, and you are allowed to share it.

The session also touched on the harvest, on what all this balancing is for, and Q'uo said something that simplifies everything. The harvest is not a thought. It is not a doctrine you master or a test you pass. It is a pure emotion, the steady state of the open heart. All the work of balance, all the picking up of the sphere, is just the slow training of the heart to stay open, whatever the road is doing underneath it.

So tonight, if you feel off balance, try the image. You are not on a tightrope. You are holding a ball. It has rolled away before. It will roll away again. Your only job is the gentle one: go pick it up, take yourself lightly, and keep rolling with it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Let Yourself Be Poetry
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: let yourself be poetry.

The question that October Sunday was about the voice inside the head. The group had been noticing how much of their suffering came not from events but from the running commentary on events, the old sentences on repeat. They asked Q'uo about self-image, about the words we say to ourselves, and about how to change the inner climate.

Q'uo began with a simple and devastating observation. Most of the sentences you say to yourself are not yours. They are inherited. They are the voices of parents, teachers, churches, cultures, absorbed in childhood and replayed ever since as if they were your own thoughts. The seeker who wants to change the inner life has to start by noticing this: the critic in your head has someone else's accent.

And then the teaching that became tonight's title. You are the author of the legend you live inside. Q'uo said that each entity is constantly writing the story of the self, choosing the words, setting the tone, deciding whether the protagonist is a hero, a fool, a victim, or a dancer. The events of your life are largely not up to you. But the telling of them is. And the telling is what you actually live inside.

They gave the group a practice so small it sounds like nothing, and I think it might be everything. Change the verbs. When you catch yourself saying you are bumbling through the day, try saying you are dancing through it. When the inner voice says you are failing, try saying you are learning. This is not positive thinking as decoration. It is authorship. The words you use about yourself are spells, cast daily, and they shape the energy body as surely as food shapes the physical one.

There was a wonderful moment in the session when someone asked about the difference between walking and dancing, and Q'uo ran with it. Walking is what you do to get somewhere. Dancing is what you do when the getting there is not the point. The spiritual life, they said, is a matter of turning the walk into a dance, of bringing the same attention to an ordinary Tuesday that you would bring to a ceremony. The dishes, the commute, the waiting in line: these are not interruptions of the spiritual life. They are the material of it, waiting to be danced.

The session also took up the question of play, and here I want to quote the spirit of what was said, because the transcript is long and the point is short. The Creator made a universe for joy. Solemnity has its place, but the seeker who cannot play has mistaken the map for the territory. Sing. Make things. Be silly on purpose. The heart opens faster through play than through effort, because play is the native language of the part of you that remembers who you are.

I should add a gentle note here, because this teaching about the inner voice touches a tender place. Learning to speak kindly to yourself is beautiful work, and it is also real work. If the voice inside your head feels cruel in a way you cannot soften alone, please consider bringing it to someone who can help, a counselor, a trusted friend, a professional. You deserve a kinder narrator, and sometimes we need help installing one.

Q'uo closed this thread with an image I have carried all week. Picture yourself as a legend in your own mind, they said, not with arrogance but with authorship. You are the poet of your own life. The events will keep coming, the old sentences will keep trying to replay, but the pen is in your hand. Write the next line kindly. Let yourself be poetry.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gnostic Instinct
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gnostic instinct.

The question that October Sunday was about religion. Not faith, but religion: the institutions, the hierarchies, the rules. The group wanted to know what Q'uo thought about the difference between the living spiritual impulse and the structures built around it, and whether organized religion helps or hinders the seeker.

Q'uo began by honoring the impulse itself. The religious instinct, they said, is real and universal. Every culture reaches for the sacred. The trouble begins not with the reaching but with what happens next, when the living experience hardens into an institution, and the institution begins to serve itself instead of the seekers who built it.

They described the pattern with unusual frankness. A teacher appears, someone with a genuine open heart, and people gather. Then the second generation arrives, the organizers, and they begin to codify: these are the beliefs, these are the practices, this is who is in and who is out. Then comes the third stage, the priestly class, those whose position depends on being the intermediaries between the seeker and the sacred. And at that point, they said, the institution has a vested interest in your not finding out that you never needed an intermediary at all.

The word Q'uo kept returning to was gnostic, from the old word for knowing. The gnostic instinct is the direct knowing, the personal encounter with the sacred that needs no permission. Every religion begins as someone's gnostic experience. Every religion ends, if it is not careful, as a system for managing other people's gnostic experiences. The seeker's work is to keep returning to the source: your own heart, your own silence, your own direct meeting with the mystery.

There was a thread in this session about rules, and I want to give you Q'uo's distinction, because it is razor sharp. There are rules that protect love, and there are rules that replace love. The first kind says: do not harm, be honest, show up for each other. The second kind says: believe this, perform that, obey us. The seeker can feel the difference in the body. One kind of rule makes the heart larger. The other makes it smaller. Trust the largeness.

Q'uo also spoke about the teachers themselves, and here the compassion in the session deepened. The founders of the great traditions, they said, were not trying to start religions. They were trying to describe what had happened to them. The distortion came later, from followers who loved the teacher so much they froze his words into law. If you want to honor a teacher, they said, do not worship the description. Have the experience.

I want to handle one more thread with care. The session touched on the ways religious authority has been misused, on the wounding that happens when power wears sacred clothing, and I will not repeat the details here. But I will say what Q'uo said underneath the details: no institution, however holy its language, has the right to your conscience. If you have been harmed in a religious setting, that harm is real, and it deserves real care. Consider bringing it to someone you trust, a counselor, a friend outside the system, anyone who will believe you.

The closing teaching was simple, and it is the one I want to leave in your hands. Religion at its best is a trellis, and the living vine is your own seeking. A trellis can help a vine grow upward. But the trellis is not the vine, and a trellis that strangles the vine has forgotten its purpose. Keep the gnostic instinct alive. Meet the sacred yourself. Let the institutions serve the seeking, and never the other way around.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Three Levels of Catalyst
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the three levels of catalyst.

The question that November Sunday was about catalyst itself, the spiritual word for everything that provokes us, everything that triggers a reaction, everything we would rather not deal with.
