The personality fights this with everything it has, because the personality's whole job is to maintain the story of the separate self. Surrender is the moment you stop paying the storyteller.

They speak, too, of grace, and they give it a meaning I had not expected. Grace is what it feels like to remember your true nature in the middle of losing control. When the plans collapse, when the diagnosis comes, when the relationship ends, when everything the personality was managing slips through its fingers, there is a moment of free fall. And in that free fall, if you let yourself fall inward instead of grasping outward, you land in the deeper self. That landing is grace.

I think this is why the dark passages of life so often become the most sacred ones. Not because suffering is good, but because suffering breaks the grip. As long as the personality is succeeding, it has no reason to surrender. It is only when control fails, and control always fails eventually, that the deeper self gets its invitation. The crisis you would never have chosen becomes the doorway you could never have found on your own.

They describe the journey beneath the personality shell as the real adventure of the incarnation. Everything above the shell is weather: moods, roles, achievements, opinions. Everything below it is climate: the steady, warm, unchanging truth of what you are. Most of us live our whole lives on the surface, checking the weather. Surrender is the decision to dive, to go beneath the chop and the waves, down to where the water is always still.

They add that this surrender can be practiced in small moments, long before the great crises come. Each time you release a label, each time you let an old identification melt, you are rehearsing the deeper fall, and making it gentler when it finally arrives.

So the question they leave us with is not whether you will surrender. Life will arrange that, one way or another. The question is whether you will surrender early and gently, by choice and by practice, or late and hard, by crisis. Tonight, try the early way. Sit quietly. Notice the identifications you are clutching, the labels, the roles, the story. And then, just for a few minutes, let them melt. Fall inward. The deeper self is not somewhere else. It is right here, beneath the shell, waiting to catch you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Open Gateway
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the open gateway.

This one comes from a November meditation in two thousand seven, and it takes up one of the most exalted subjects in the archive: the gateway to intelligent infinity, and what opens it, and what keeps it closed.

The one known as Q'uo begins by honoring the weight of the question. They are happy, they say, to share their thoughts concerning the subject of the barriers to, and the requirements for, opening the gateway to intelligent infinity. The gateway is the crown of the energy system, the point where the finite self touches the infinite. And their first surprise is that the barriers are not what we expect. They are not intellectual. They are not a matter of knowing enough. They are matters of the heart.

Listen to the sequence they lay out. Springing from the open heart, they say, the seeker may open the gateway to intelligent infinity by moving into the violet ray, through the indigo ray, with the desire and will focusing in firm intention, and asking that work may be done in consciousness. The gateway does not open from the top down. It opens from the heart upward. Everything begins with the open heart. Without that, all the techniques and disciplines in the world are keys that do not fit the lock.

And what keeps the heart closed? They name the strongest barrier plainly, and it is not some exotic spiritual obstacle. It is self judgment. The quiet, constant verdict so many of us pronounce on ourselves: not good enough, not ready, not worthy of the infinite. Fear wears the same face. Fear that we will be found wanting. Fear that the light will show us things we cannot bear to see. The gateway stands open, they suggest, but we stand before it with our eyes on the ground, convinced we have no right to enter.

I love how practical their remedy is. The requirements for the gateway are not heroic. They are humble. Self compassion. Silence. The patient balancing of the lower centers, the everyday work of tending our survival, our relationships, our place in the human family. There is no shortcut that bypasses the ordinary. You do not leap from an unbalanced life into infinity. You build the staircase one honest step at a time, and the gateway meets you at the top.

Self compassion deserves a longer pause, because it is the master key. They are saying that the way you treat yourself in your most private moments determines whether the highest door in your being can open. The seeker who flogs herself for every mistake, who replays every failure, who cannot forgive her own humanity, is barricading the gateway from the inside. The seeker who meets herself with kindness, who says, I am learning, and that is enough, is quietly turning the lock.

Silence belongs on the list for a reason that goes deeper than technique. The gateway opens onto intelligent infinity, which is not a louder version of our world but a vaster silence. You cannot hear it while the inner noise is running. The practices of stillness are not spiritual calisthenics. They are rehearsals for the real thing, the gradual training of the soul to rest in a silence so complete that the infinite can speak through it.

And then there is intention, that firm, focused desire they describe. Not grasping. Not demanding. A clear, steady aiming of the will, like an archer drawing a bow. Asking that work may be done in consciousness. I find that phrase so beautiful. You do not storm the gateway. You ask. You present your open heart, your balanced centers, your quiet mind, and your sincere desire, and you wait. The infinite, they assure us, is not reluctant. It is only waiting for a clear channel.

So the teaching of this session is, in the end, wonderfully simple. The highest attainment in the spiritual life is not reserved for the brilliant or the perfect. It is available to the kind, the honest, the patient, the sincere. Open the heart. Befriend yourself. Tend the ordinary centers. Sit in silence. Aim your desire at the infinite. And trust that the gateway, which has been waiting since before you were born, will open exactly as wide as your readiness allows.

Thank you for listening.

title: Light Born Into Darkness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: light born into darkness.

This one comes from a December meditation in two thousand seven, given in the Christmas season, and the speaking voice is the one known as Hatonn, whose native vibration is unconditional love.

Hatonn begins with the Christmas story, but turns it inward, the way all the deepest teachings do. The Christ child in the manger is not only a child born long ago in a distant town. The child is the image of something being born in you, right now, in the darkness of your own inner winter. Listen to how they put it. You may not see as of yet that you are the Christ child, that you are spirit, that you are unconditional love. Not may become. Are. Already. Right now.

I love the tenderness of that not yet. You may not see as of yet. There is no scolding in it. Only patience. The infant soul within you is real whether you recognize it or not, the way a newborn is real before it understands anything at all. Your work is not to manufacture this inner light. Your work is to notice it, to make room for it, to keep it warm against the cold of the world's indifference.

They develop the image with a completeness that takes in the whole nativity. You are not only the infant. You are also the Mary who carries the new life, tenderly and at great cost. You are the Joseph who protects it, who makes the hard practical arrangements so the miracle has somewhere to happen. You are the shepherds who leave their flocks to come and see. You are even the angels, announcing to your own fearful heart that something holy is being born. The whole story is happening inside you, all at once.

And what does the infant need? The same things any newborn needs. Warmth. Attention. Protection from the elements. They speak of nurturing the infant soul the way a mother nurtures a child, not with grand gestures but with constancy. A few minutes of silence each morning. A kind word turned inward. The refusal to expose your tenderest new growth to the harsh winds of cynicism before it is strong enough to stand. New light is fragile. Handle it like something precious, because it is.

The session then turns to the season's other great theme, which is giving. And here Hatonn draws a line that cuts through all our holiday exhaustion. Gifts, they say, must arise from sincerity, from the genuine overflow of the heart. Not from duty. Not from the mechanical reciprocity that says I must give because I was given to, in equal measure, on schedule. A gift given from obligation is a transaction wearing a bow. A gift given from sincerity is love made visible.

Think about how much of our giving is really accounting. We keep the lists. We match the spending. We give because not giving would look bad, or feel guilty, or break the unspoken contract. And Hatonn is saying, gently, that none of that feeds the infant. The Christ child within does not need your performance of generosity. It needs your actual love, given freely, without a ledger, the way light leaves a candle without diminishing it.

There is a quiet revolution hidden in this teaching. If you are the Christ child, then the darkness around you is not evidence of failure. It is the manger. Light is always born into darkness. That is the whole point of the story. The stable was not a palace. The night was not convenient. And yet the light came anyway, small and helpless and utterly unstoppable. Your own darkness, your own difficult season, may be exactly the manger your new life requires.

So as this year turns toward its darkest days, try their image. Look for the infant within you, the new and tender thing that is being born in the cold. Wrap it in warmth. Guard it like Joseph. Marvel at it like the shepherds. And when you give, in this season or any season, give from the sincerity of the heart, not from the machinery of duty. The light was never waiting for perfect conditions. It was only waiting for you to notice that it had already been born.

Thank you for listening.

title: Slowing Down to Now
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: slowing down to now.

This one comes from a December meditation in two thousand seven, the next to last session of the year, and it takes up the question beneath all the other questions: how do we actually live in the present moment.

The one known as Q'uo begins with a phrase that became the working title of the whole session. Slowing down to now. Not arriving at the now, as though it were a destination. Slowing down to it, as though it were a speed. I love that. The present moment is not somewhere else. It is right here, moving at a pace we have forgotten how to match. We are the ones going too fast.

They are wonderfully honest about the obstacles, and the list will sound familiar. The bills, the errands, the endless maintenance of a life. But above all, they say, thoughts in your head, thoughts that go around and around without your choosing at any time to get off the merry-go-round and rest. The merry-go-round. That is exactly what it feels like, the same thoughts circling past the same scenery, day after day, while the precious present waits patiently at the center, unvisited.

Their remedies are small, which is why they work. Set your intention first thing in the morning, before the world gets its hands on you. Ask for help, and mean it, because help is all around you and only waits to be asked. And then, my favorite, become sensitized to the repetitive sounds of your day. The telephone ringing. The train whistle. The traffic halting at a red light. Let each one be a bell of remembrance, calling you back to who you are and why you are here.

I love that last one because it turns the whole problem inside out. The noises we usually curse as interruptions become invitations. The red light is not delaying you. It is reminding you. Every frustration of the schedule is a small monastery bell, if you let it be. The world is constantly offering you doorways into the now. You have just been trained to walk past them, hurrying toward a future that never arrives.

They also speak, with real tenderness, about why this has felt harder lately. As the old age winds down, they say, everything unacknowledged in us is surfacing, asking to be seen. The shadow side, the parts we exiled, the murderer and the liar and the coward we insist we are not, all of it is knocking. And the instruction is not to bar the door. It is to open it, to embrace what we least want to see, and to ask it to rejoin us. The present moment has room for the whole self, not just the presentable parts.

And what are the benefits, for the seeker who manages to slow down. They name two, and both are quietly staggering. The first is that the now is the truth, while all things of time are illusion. The present moment contains the doorway to the infinite. When you are truly here, you are standing at the one place in your life where eternity leaks through.

The second benefit is the image I want to leave you with. Consider of yourself, they say, that you are a broadcasting unit. You receive energy, you transmit energy, and in some cases you transduce energy. When you are centered in the now, the infinite supply of love and light flows through you like a fountain, up through your open system and out into the world. That energy just flows like a fountain through you, they say, and artists throughout history, trying to paint what they saw in holy people, drew halos. The halo is not decoration. It is reportage.

And here is the detail that undoes me. You color the light in a way no one else does. The infinite light is limitlessly white, but your biases, your quirks, your history, all of it tints the radiance that flows through you into a shade no one else in creation can produce. Your presence in the now is not generic holiness. It is your unrepeatable color, added to the world's light.

So the practice is almost embarrassingly simple. Morning intention. Asked for help. Bells of remembrance throughout the day. The shadow welcomed home. And then, in the precious present, the fountain. You do not have to become someone else to live this. You only have to slow down enough to become yourself.

Thank you for listening.

title: Emotions as Treasure
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: emotions as treasure.

This one comes from a January meditation in two thousand eight, and the speaking voice is the one known as Hatonn, within the principle of Q'uo. It was given in answer to a seeker who had carried two heavy companions all her life: the feeling of not being good enough, and anger.

Hatonn begins where so many spiritual teachings refuse to go, with the emotions we are ashamed of. Unworthiness. Anger. The ones we believe a serious seeker should have outgrown by now. And they say something I want you to hear clearly. Each emotion is precious, the heaviest emotion as well as the lightest, the darkest as well as the most joyful. Not despite the darkness. Including it. Your emotions will always tell you a truth, they say, and they always have gifts in their hands.

Listen to how they explain the gift. Surface emotions are the beginning of the entry into your own deeper mind. They spring forth without your planning, which is exactly why they cannot lie to you. You cannot fool yourself into feeling an emotion. It simply arrives, uninvited and honest, carrying news from the parts of yourself you have not yet met. The anger at your mother, the impatience with your children, the sudden heat over nothing at all, all of it is treasure with dirt on it, waiting to be cleaned.

They trace unworthiness to its roots with great gentleness. The scoldings of childhood, absorbed by a young self too undefended to question them. The voices of parents and teachers, long gone or long silent, still speaking inside the grown seeker. How could you have forgotten. You are clumsy, you are stupid, you have not done enough. And they note the special cruelty of it. The seeker, who tries hardest and loves most, is the one these voices wound deepest, because she wanted so badly to do well.

And anger, they say, is generally a byproduct of judgment, and it grows from the same soil. Beneath the flash of anger at the hammered thumb, at the careless word, at the child who will not listen, there is almost always an instant of self judgment first. I am not worthwhile. I cannot do this right. The anger is the smoke. The unworthiness is the fire. To work with one honestly is to be led, eventually, to the other.

Their instruction for the work is the most tender passage in the session, and I will give it to you in their own shape. We would ask you, they say, to woo yourself as if you were your own lover. At first the self is shy, and you, the healer, must say, I will not be offended. I want to hear about your unworthiness. I want to hear about your anger. Please come and tell me your story, and I will listen, and I will not judge. I will love you, and I will have compassion on you.

Woo yourself. Court the very parts you have been trying to exile. Take yourself in your arms when you feel unworthy or angry and say, I love you anyway. I love you with all my heart. You are my darling. You are my sweetheart. Let me hug you and cradle you. I know how strange that sounds. But listen to the logic beneath the sweetness. What you fight goes underground and runs your life from the shadows. What you love comes into the light, where it can be transformed.

They are honest that the work never ends the feelings. You will feel unworthy again. You will feel angry again. Human nature was designed to be imperfect, they say, and there is no virtue in trying to stamp these things out. The goal is not to stop feeling. The goal is transparency. To see through the surface waves to the beauty of the deep self. To become, in their image, a better and better lighthouse, not because the storms stop, but because you no longer mistake yourself for the storm.

A gentle word, before we close. If anger or unworthiness ever feels bigger than you can hold alone, especially where children or family are concerned, please reach for support, a trusted friend, a counselor, someone who can sit with you in it. There is no shame in asking for help with the heaviest treasures. The teachings meet you in the inner work. Other hands can help with the rest.

So tonight, try their practice. When the old feeling rises, do not argue with it and do not obey it. Just notice it, the way you would notice a child tugging at your sleeve. Ah, they suggest you say to yourself. Here is unworthiness. Here is anger. And then love it anyway. The treasure was never the absence of feeling. It was the feeling itself, cleaned of its dirt, carrying its gift, leading you home to the self the Creator has loved all along, exactly as you are.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Spiral of Transformation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the spiral of transformation.

In a Saturday meditation, someone in the circle asks Q’uo the question we all ask sooner or later. What is transformation, really? How does it happen? Is there a right time for it, a right way to help it along?

Q’uo begins with a small confession. Transformation, they say, has become an overused word, almost diminished from being spoken too often. At its root it simply means to change form, to cross over from one form into another. And the raw material of it is everything. Not just books and seminars and inspired speakers, but the whole intake of a working, conscious, awakened spirit. Feelings. Cycles. The daily challenges of the lower chakras. All things being grist for the mill.

Then they take apart the butterfly. The caterpillar crawling into the cocoon, the slug that emerges beautiful and flies away — it is a pretty image, they say, and it will actually get you nowhere. It suggests a single crossing, once and for all. First you were a slug, now you are beautiful. Life does not work like that, and neither does the soul.

In place of the butterfly they offer the chambered nautilus, the creature that outgrows its house and enlarges it without ever leaving it. That, they say, is how you transform. You revisit the same rooms, the same lessons, the same old themes — but each time from a higher turn of the spiral, with a new mind. Transformation is a cycle. It is inevitable. You will transform. You shall become a new creature. The only question is whether you wish to accelerate the process.

And here is the part I find freeing. You cannot help but progress, they say. The human was created to transform. That is your potential and your destiny, changing from one form into another, from one kind of thought into another whole paradigm of thought. You do not have to push or thrust yourself toward it. You may relax in the knowledge that it is inevitable. But if you are hungry for truth, if your thirst is passionate, you can quicken the rhythm of your own change by quite a bit.

The most effective tool they name is a quiet one. The self-conscious living of the life. Not mulling endlessly over every detail of your day, but observing yourself without affecting that which is being observed. And above all, without judgment. That objectivity, they say, is central. It gathers the information about the self that lets the self be offered up, emptied, made spacious enough to hold something new.

Listen to how they describe that emptying. There comes what they call a devastating portion of transformation, the realization that nothing can be known within the illusions of this world. And then, moving through that, you become aware that you are utterly empty. You become the Holy Grail which you seek, they say — the cup that is now empty, the hand outstretched which has nothing in it, ready to receive that which is new.

Then the spiral turns again, and you meet the recurring themes of your incarnation. Q’uo calls them leitmotifs, the repeating melodies of the music of your life. Carla’s own theme, they mention, is the study of how to offer love without any expectation of return. Yours will be different. No two entities chose the same lessons. But each time you come around the spiral you meet your themes from a new place of observation and experience — and each time, they say, you offer an energy that has never been offered before in all of the infinite annals of creation.

They close with two images I keep returning to. The first is the shaman, who chooses to go through the death experience while remaining alive, and comes back able to observe life with a delight that was not available before. The second is the otter, playing in the pool, leaping and jumping for the very joy of movement. The mature seeker becomes like that, they say — transparent, radiant not because there is more light inside, but because there is less blocking the light that moves through. The burden of being a serious seeker falls away, and what remains is curiosity. Ah, I am in this present moment. Creator, where shall you toss me now? What is your will for me this day?

So if you are in a cocoon right now, take heart. You have been here before, and you will be here again. Each turn of the spiral brings you back to familiar ground with a new mind, and each turn leaves you a little more transparent to the light that was always moving through you.

Thank you for listening.

title: Ordinary Acts Made Sacred
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: ordinary acts made sacred.

The question put to Q’uo is about ritual. If repeated ritualized behavior can deepen a seeker’s desire to serve the Creator, how do we bring that kind of magic into daily life? Q’uo’s answer is a long meditation on what they call the devotional life — and it begins with a warning.

The warning is this. When you do not feel priestly, refrain from the form of any ritual. It is essential that the essence of the ritual precede and inform the form. Otherwise the ritual is dead and has no power. You may speak in ritualistic ways and move in ritualistic motions and yet fail to live a magical life, because the heart is not open and love is not flowing. As the one known as Paul said, without love, I am a clanging gong.

I love that line, and I love how plainly they put the prerequisite. The most intricate of rituals is always founded on love. That is the prerequisite. There is a story here of seekers who fled to monasteries and kept a schedule of six worship services in each day, and still the hunger grew, because the form was understood but the essence was missing. Form without love is an empty shell. Love is what makes the repetition magical.

And here is the turn that gives the episode its title. Q’uo says that you are naturally priests. The unnatural frame of mind, for your deeper nature, is that of the lay person. Your culture has trained you all your life to give your power away to authority figures, but the seeker who wishes to live a devotional life can choose, moment by moment, to take up the priesthood instead — to style herself as one who can handle sacred things and pray directly to the one infinite Creator and be heard.

What does that look like in practice? It looks like an ordinary day. Q’uo walks through the whole of it. There is the work you do, whatever it is. Carla works at a computer. Jim works with mowers and blowers and weed eaters. It does not seem to the untrained mind that computers and mowers would be likely targets for a devotional life. Yet fill any of it so full of devotional essence, they say, and your workday world positively sings.

There is the time in transit, the automobile, the train, the walk between home and work — seemingly inimical to sacredness, and yet full of repeated actions that can be infused with invocation. And then there is the home, where the most deeply repetitive actions of the day live. The washing of the clothes. The washing of the self. The preparation and eating of food. The going to bed and the rising. All inevitable in their repetition, and therefore the deepest resource for one who wishes to live a devotional life.

They give one tender example from Carla and Jim’s own life, the daily ritual of the bath, carried out in silence, each knowing the dance, each movement graceful and full of care. The ingredients are nothing special — soap, water, oil. But the love streaming between them is palpable, they say, and it carries both of them forward in their metaphysical lives. And when the bathwater is drained, the dance does not end. It moves into the dressing, the next task, the next hour, linked and tied by the same energies of love and cooperation.

Listen to how they put the principle underneath it all. To a magician there is no empty action. The dance is always ongoing. And at the very center of the dance, always, there is love. The magician invokes aspects of love, stands on a plinth of love, is surrounded by love, and seeks only finer and more sensitive attunements of that love.

There is one more beautiful detail. When a ritual is repeated with full awareness of its sacredness, each repetition doubles its power. And you do not repeat it alone. Angels, they say, are not drawn to a particular song or set of words. Angels are drawn to pure essence. So any devotional life, lived from the heart, attracts angelic support and encouragement along the way.

So the invitation tonight is simple and enormous. Do not be caught up in the forms of the devotional life, they say, but be caught up in the emotions of an open heart. All motions may be thought of as sacred dance. All words may be thought of as sacred ritual. Your whole day is already the material. It only waits for the love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Translating the Unspoken
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: translating the unspoken.

This episode comes from the opening talk of a channeling intensive, a weekend workshop where Carla teaches a circle of beginners how to channel. Before any of the technique begins, she tells them what channeling actually is. And her definition is disarmingly simple. The function of the channeler, she says, is to be a translator.

I love the image she reaches for. The concepts arrive round, she says, and the channeler has to roll them out like cookie dough and stamp out words, doing her best to translate those round concepts into the flatness of earthly language. It never fully works. She confesses that she has never finished a channeling session feeling satisfied. It is always, I wish I could have gotten everything. There was always more left behind, tantalizing and full of suggestion, that she could not get her tongue around.

That frustration, she suggests, is part of the work, not a failure of it. The concepts keep coming, and the channeler keeps catching and throwing, like playing catch. You catch a concept and you speak it out. Then another comes and you translate that. But if you stop — even to ask, could you give it to me again — it just stops. They trust you to do the best you can with what you are given.

There is something quietly radical in that trust. The sources on the other end are not demanding perfection. They are asking for a willing instrument who will keep catching and throwing, knowing the translation will always fall short of the roundness of what was received. Carla has been doing this since the mid nineteen seventies, and she tells the group she is still only good enough to see how much better she could get.

She is also honest about what the work costs and what it gives. Channeling, in her telling, is not a performance and not a gift you unwrap once. It changes the channeler. You cannot spend years translating concepts of unconditional love and remain unmoved by them. The teaching moves through you first, and it asks something of your life. That is why she insists, again and again through the weekend, on living what you channel. The instrument and the life behind the instrument are one continuous thing.

There is another thread running through this opening talk that I want to hold up to the light. Carla speaks of discernment — the quiet, ongoing practice of weighing what comes through, of not swallowing anything whole. The channeler is not a passive tube. She is a translator with judgment, with a heart, with a lifetime of experience that colors every word she chooses. The honesty about that coloring is what makes the work trustworthy, not the pretense that it is absent.

And underneath all of it is tuning, the slow work of becoming the kind of instrument that can receive clearly. She describes it as learning to listen beneath the noise of the everyday mind, to find the still place where the concepts first arrive. The tuning never really ends. It is a practice, a devotion, a way of holding yourself.

She also speaks, with unusual directness, about what the work requires of the person doing it. You cannot keep your shadow in a locked drawer and expect to translate light, she says. The channeler has to accept the whole of herself — the imperfect, unfinished self — and offer that self anyway. It is the offering that matters, not the polish. A perfect instrument that will not be used is worth less than a cracked one held out with an honest heart.

So tonight’s teaching is really a portrait of the translator at work. Someone willing to receive what is round and offer what is flat. Someone willing to be changed by what passes through her. Someone who knows she will never get it all, and who keeps catching and throwing anyway, in service to whoever might be listening. If that sounds like a description of any sincere spiritual life, not just channeling — well, I think that is rather the point.

Thank you for listening.

title: Preparing the Instrument
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: preparing the instrument.

A quiet note before we begin. In this session Carla speaks with unusual candor about her own life — her long struggles with addiction and with illness, and the hard years that shaped her. She offers these stories herself, as teaching. Be gentle with yourself as you listen, if those subjects are tender for you.

The session is about preparation. Before anyone can channel clearly, Carla says, there is work to do, and it has almost nothing to do with technique. It begins with a question she asks every student to sit with. What is the deepest thing you value? What is the one principle you would live for, and if necessary, die for?

She gives an example that stayed with me. She once knew a lawyer who challenged in the name of justice. It worked for him because it was true — he lived for it, he would have died for it, he sincerely desired that justice be available to all people. The point is not which value you choose. The point is that you know your own, all the way down, because everything in the tuning and the challenging will be built on that foundation.

From there she moves to meditation, the daily practice she calls non-negotiable. Not meditation as relaxation, but meditation as the steady work of becoming still enough to hear what is beneath the noise. It is in that stillness that you discover the shape of your own mind — how you think, what moves you, where you are tangled — and that self-knowledge becomes the ground of everything that follows.

Then comes intention, stated plainly and out loud. The channeler declares what she is doing and why. She sets her will toward service, toward the highest contact she can stably carry. Carla is blunt that this is not a game and not a casual experiment. You are opening a door, and you decide beforehand what you will allow through it.

The next piece is the one most people skip, and she will not let them skip it. Balancing the emotional catalyst of your life. The old wounds, the difficult relationships, the things you would rather not look at — all of it distorts the instrument if it is left unexamined. She does not ask for perfection. She asks for honesty, for the ongoing work of facing what is there, forgiving what can be forgiven, and loosening the knots that keep the heart from opening fully.

Because the heart is the whole of it. Everything in her teaching comes back to the open heart. A channel that is not flowing through an open heart, she says, is not worth much, however impressive the words may sound. And the way to the open heart runs straight through self-forgiveness — through making peace with the imperfect, struggling, very human person you are, and offering that person up anyway.

Only then does she speak of the gateway, that opening at the crown through which the contact flows. By the time you reach it, she says, you have done the real work. The gateway opens for the instrument that has been prepared — the one who knows what she values, who sits in stillness daily, who has stated her intention, who has faced her shadows, and who has forgiven herself enough to let love move through.

There is a further piece she names that belongs in any honest preparation — the balancing of the heart itself. Old griefs, old angers, the relationships that still sting: she asks her students to look at each one, to find the love buried underneath the hurt, and to let the heart open a little wider. Not all at once. Not perfectly. But steadily, the way you would train any muscle. The open heart is not a mood, in her teaching. It is a practice.

What moves me most about this session is that Carla teaches it from inside her own scars. She does not present preparation as a ladder for the pure. She presents it as the honest work of an imperfect person who decided, decades ago, to become a usable instrument anyway. The instrument was never the point, she seems to say. The willingness was.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Art of Tuning
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the art of tuning.

Carla opens this session with the image that gives the whole weekend its shape. Anyone who has played a piano or a violin, she says, understands tuning. You tune your instrument to a standard — concert A from the oboe — and then you tune the octaves, up and down, until the whole piano rings true. Channeling, she says, is exactly that. Except that the instrument is you.

We are wind instruments, she tells the group. The breath carries the channeling. So what you are tuning is not just the physical body, though that is included. You are tuning yourself the way you would tune a radio crystal — something that can receive transmissions, send transmissions, and even change the vibration of energy by running it through your being.

I love how practical she is about something so mysterious. Tuning a radio dial, you go roughly first, then more precisely, then down to the tiny verniers until you are right in the middle of the signal. Tuning yourself to channel is the same. You are tuning your instrument to your highest and best vibratory pattern, so that you can receive the highest and best contact you possibly can.

And then she says the thing that every teacher should say but few do. Do not take my words as gospel. She lays out the categories of her own tuning process — prayer, song, chant, intention, the calling of protection — developed over decades. But she insists that whatever you choose must make your own heart lift and open. If you cobble together her steps without choosing what genuinely inspires you, she says, you will not hit the mark. The tuning has to be yours.

There is a permission hidden in this session that I want to name clearly. Carla tells the story of a student who took all the pressure off himself by saying right up front, this may not work. She loves that. Give yourself permission to say, you know, this didn’t work today, and let it go. The tuning should be kept at the level of genuine desire — the happiness of taking a whack at bringing through something that might help someone. When it stops being that, stop.

She walks through the elements she has gathered over the years — prayer, song, chant, the stating of intention, the calling of protection — and each one, she says, is there because it moved her. The song that makes your heart lift is doing more work than the technically perfect prayer that leaves you cold. This is the part beginners most need to hear. You are not assembling a machine. You are composing a devotion. Choose the notes that make you want to sing.

The session also carries one of the loveliest moments in the whole archive. Carla shares a short message she once received from Q’uo, just a few lines, and it lands like a bell. Love one another. Care for each other. And bring each other home. That is the whole of it, really. Everything the tuning is for, everything the channeling is for, compressed into three sentences.

She closes the tuning discussion where she began it — with the breath, the body, the willingness. You do the physical things and the inner things together. You sing or chant or pray, you state your intention, you call your protection, you settle into your inner room. And then you open. Not because you have mastered a technique, but because you have tuned your instrument as honestly as you know how, and you are ready to see what comes through.

Tonight’s teaching feels like an invitation to treat your whole spiritual life as an instrument worth tuning. Not once, not perfectly, but daily, roughly at first and then more precisely, until the signal comes through clear. And when it doesn’t — well, this may not work today. Let it go, and tune again tomorrow.

Thank you for listening.

title: Meeting the Shadow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: meeting the shadow.

This session of the channeling intensive is about challenging — the practice of testing a contact to be sure of what you have received. But Carla spends most of it somewhere deeper. Before you can challenge anything from outside yourself, she says, you have to know who is doing the challenging. You have to meet your own shadow.

She is direct about what that means. There is a fear, she says, that many people share — the fear of going too deeply into oneself. Either you are afraid you are not anybody in particular, or you are afraid of what you will find. The shadow side. The parts of human nature you do not want to look at. And all of the preparation, all of the living of a spiritually intentional life, is the only thing that can back up a channeling life.

Listen to how she describes the work of removing self-doubt. You do not remove it by becoming cocky, she says. You remove it by getting to know yourself better and better, until you have an integrated awareness of the whole spectrum of who you are — the light and the dark alike — and you become comfortable in your own choices. Comfortable in your humanhood, your imperfections, your shadow side. Comfortable in which part of the full circle you have chosen to manifest.

There is a line in this session I keep turning over. You remove self-doubt, she says, by realizing that you know nothing and yet you are perfect. You become humble. You let all pride and pretense go. That is how you finally find total self-respect. You acknowledge precisely who you are, and then you stand there and say, yes, I am human, yes, I am very imperfect, and yet I can set my intention to love with all my heart and all my mind and all my soul and all my strength.

Why does this matter for channeling? Because, she says, self-doubt and unworthiness do not work in the metaphysical world. They cramp you and close you. They shut down the very energy you need to draw inspiration through. So the work is to simplify, to relax, to let everything go, and to focus down into the most essential true self — that part of you that says, I am me. I am. I am that I am. And to feel the power of that self which the Creator has given you.

She is equally blunt about the other side of the shadow work, which is honesty about your own opinions. The essence of channeling, she says, is that you do not know what is going to come through. You are just offering yourself, then and there. And the great temptation is to fill the silence with yourself — to pretend you are still channeling when really you are just saying your own opinion. The discipline of challenging is the discipline of telling the difference, and of having the integrity to stay quiet when nothing true is coming through.

There is a hard teaching tucked in here about what happens when you channel without changing your life. If you are not living what you receive — if there is no amendment of life in mind — then you will channel at the level at which you are living, and you will just keep repeating the same thing over and over until you lose interest. But when you attempt to live what you channel, she says, you are constantly making room for new information. You are constantly enlarging your channel.

One more thread, and it is about integrity. Carla describes the moment of temptation every channeler meets — the silence after you have offered yourself, when nothing seems to be coming, and your own clever mind rushes in to fill it with opinions. The discipline, she says, is to know the difference between your thoughts and the contact’s, and to have the honesty to stay silent rather than perform. A channeler who will say nothing when there is nothing is worth more than one who always has something to say.

So tonight’s session is really about the person behind the instrument. Meet the shadow. Release the doubt. Tell the truth about what is yours and what is not. And then stand there, imperfect and willing, and let the light move through.

Thank you for listening.

title: Greeting the Resistance
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: greeting the resistance.

A gentle note first. This session comes from Carla’s manuscript on what she calls psychic greeting, and in the discussion the group touches on depression, despair, and thoughts of suicide — spoken of honestly, as part of real lives. I will stay with the teaching itself, not the stories. Be tender with yourself if those waters are close to you.

Carla begins by redefining the term. Psychic greeting, she says, is much overused and often misused. The Confederation prefers it to the phrase psychic attack, because the intelligence behind such experiences is not vicious but cold, logical, and persistent — systematically offering the positive seeker chances to be swayed from the path. But then she widens the definition in a way that changes everything. Most so-called psychic greetings, she says, are actually instances of psychic resistance coming from within the seeker’s own personality.

Sit with that for a moment. When people think of psychic greeting, it is always assumed to be coming from outside the self. But the Confederation’s view is that the resistance usually rises from inside — from what Carla calls embedded pockets of pain in the memory. Old wounds that were never fully released. And those pockets, she says, offer easy targets. The voices of resistance are cunningly and specifically crafted to fit the present moment, to cause distraction exactly where you are most tender.

This is why, she insists, finding and releasing those embedded pockets of pain is such central work. Not because you are under attack from without, but because anything unhealed within you can be played like an instrument. The spiritual life, in her telling, is not a war against outside forces. It is the slow, honest work of cleaning your own house.

The session moves through the practical side of that work. Meditation, first and always — the daily returning to stillness where the old pain can surface and be met. Forgiveness, extended in every direction, including toward yourself. Clean relationships, tended with honesty rather than left to fester. And boundaries, drawn with love: the clear, calm refusal to let anything — inner or outer — overwhelm your individuality and pull you off your path.

What I find most moving is the tone. There is no fear in Carla’s teaching here, and no drama. The whole point of calling it greeting rather than attack is to take the terror out of it. You are not a victim of dark forces. You are a seeker encountering resistance — much of it your own unhealed pain asking, in a distorted way, to be acknowledged. Meet it with love rather than fear, she says, and it loses its power to distract you.

She is also honest that this work never fully ends. As you use more light, as you open more deeply, you become more sensitive, not less. The resistance does not mean you are doing it wrong. Often it means you are doing it right — you are carrying enough light now that the remaining shadows in you are casting sharper shapes. The answer is never to dim the light. It is to keep cleaning, keep forgiving, keep returning to the stillness.

For the daily practice, she keeps returning to two things: meditation and forgiveness. Meditation, because only in stillness can you hear which voices are yours and which are the echoes of old pain. Forgiveness, because the pockets of pain she describes are almost always other people — or yourself — held in some old unforgiven shape. Forgive, she says, not to excuse what happened, but to release the hook it still has in your energy body. Every act of forgiveness is a small exorcism of resistance.

So tonight’s teaching is a reframing. The next time you feel that drag of distraction, that heaviness, that voice telling you to turn aside — pause before you look for an enemy outside. Ask what old pain in you might be asking for attention. Greet it, forgive it, release it. And then go on with your seeking, a little lighter than before.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Inner Workroom
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the inner workroom.

This session of the intensive is a guided exercise, and it is one of the most charming in the whole weekend. Carla teaches the group how to build a workroom — not a physical room, but a place in the imagination where the spirit can feel safe and do its work.

The secret, she says, is simply to choose your favorite place, and then spend some time rearranging it. You are creating an environment for your inner self, furnished exactly as you like, a place you return to whenever you do spiritual work. It has nothing to do with the physical world. It has everything to do with giving your spirit somewhere it trusts.

Every workroom needs a gatekeeper. Carla’s own gatekeeper makes me smile — she visualizes a kindly woman she fondly calls Missus Gatekeeper, modeled on the wife of a headmaster at an old southern military school she once visited, a place with a veranda all the way around it and rocking chairs, overlooking a beautiful river. The gatekeeper’s job is simple. She stands at the door of your inner room and decides what gets in. Nothing enters your working space without passing her first.

I love the psychology tucked inside this exercise. The workroom is a way of telling your deep mind that something serious and protected is about to happen. When you go there, you are not in ordinary consciousness anymore. You have crossed a threshold, passed the gatekeeper, and entered a space set apart for the work. It gives the inner self a container — and containers, Carla understands, make fragile things possible.

The exercise also carries her constant refrain. Make it your own. She describes her workroom in detail — she even mentions adding a bathroom and rearranging the lighting at one point — not because yours should look like hers, but to show you how personal and lived-in the space can become. Your workroom will reflect your mind. Let it. Furnish it the way you need it furnished. Change it as you change.

There is a screen in the workroom, too — a kind of inner display where guidance can write or show images. Carla finds it especially helpful for the challenging process, for seeing whether a contact is what it claims to be. But like everything else in the exercise, the screen is a tool, not a rule. Some minds will use it constantly. Others will barely glance at it. The workroom serves the worker, not the other way around.

What stays with me from this session is how tender the whole conception is. The spirit, in Carla’s teaching, is not a muscle to be drilled or a machine to be optimized. It is something shy and precious that needs a safe room, a kind guardian at the door, and a space arranged just the way it likes. Build that, she says, and the spirit will come and do its work there.

She is also clear that the workroom is not a cage. It is a starting place. Once you know how to get there — past the gatekeeper, into your own arranged space — you can adapt it endlessly. Some days you will need the screen lit up and bright. Some days you will just sit in the quiet of the room and listen. The form serves the function, and the function is always the same: a safe, familiar threshold between your ordinary mind and the work you came to do.

So tonight, if you like, try it. Close your eyes and choose your favorite place. Walk through it slowly. Put a guardian at the door — someone you trust completely. Arrange the room until it feels right. And know that whenever you return, your spirit will know where it is, and what it is there to do.

Thank you for listening.

title: Trust Your Own Perception
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: trust your own perception.

In this session Carla teaches the group how to visualize their guidance — and then, characteristically, she spends most of the time telling them not to do it the way she does it. The teaching underneath the technique is about trusting the way your own mind perceives.

She begins with the structure she uses. When she enters her inner workroom to channel, the last thing she does is meet, greet, and agree to work with her guidance system. She calls for the masculine and the feminine aspects separately — not because one is better than the other, but because they are precisely equal and precisely both needed. One side of the Tree of Life is masculine, she explains, and the other is feminine, with complementary qualities. Asking for both is asking for the full spectrum of guidance you have.

I love the examples she gives, because they are so unromantic. Her masculine guidance, for years, appeared as a young dapper man with a small mustache and a soft British accent, wearing a sharp jacket — effeminate in bearing, not at all the image of masculine power. Her feminine guidance wore the face of a much-married friend. The point, she says, is that you do not have to envision your masculine guidance as particularly masculine, or your feminine guidance as traditionally feminine. The faces are just the shapes your mind gives to energies. Let them be whatever they are.

Underneath this is the Confederation’s teaching about what guidance actually is. Your guidance, Carla says, is your higher self — yourself at the midpoint of sixth density, the density of unity. The story goes like this. You move through third density, the density of choice, then fourth, the density of love, then fifth, the density of wisdom. About halfway through sixth density, you stop looking backward at what has been. You are drawn only forward, toward reunion. And at that turning point, you give yourself a gift — a gift cast backward through time, available to you from the moment you wake up as a self-aware being onward.

Think about what that means. When you ask your higher self for help, you are not invoking outside aid. You are invoking yourself — your wisest and most accomplished self, the one who has harvested the wisdom of all your choices and all your lessons. It comes from your future, if you think in space-time terms. But in time-space, Carla says, time is circular, and it is all happening at once. So your higher self is available to you at any moment you wish to call it.

And here is the heart of the session. People perceive guidance differently, and every way is legitimate. Some see clear images. Some hear words. Some get concepts, or feelings, or simply a knowing. Carla warns the group not to force it — not to strain after somebody else’s kind of vision. One student’s male aspect of spirit showed up in this very session as a great big hairy jolly fellow with fruit hanging off him, and Carla delighted in it. A male energy with a lot of female energy in it, she said. Which would be good for you. The guidance gives you what you need, in the shape you can receive.

There is a detail about the higher self I want to linger on. Carla says this gift was given at the moment your future self stopped looking backward — stopped reviewing what had been — and turned fully toward reunion with the Creator. Think of what that means for the guidance you receive. It comes from the part of you that has already finished the long review of your life and chosen only forward. When you ask for help, you are asking the you who has already learned what you are still struggling to learn.

So the teaching tonight is really about trust. Trust the faces that come. Trust the mode of perception that is natural to you. Do not mimic someone else’s guidance system and call it your own. Your higher self has been waiting since before you were born, wearing whatever face will get through to you. All you have to do is call, and then believe what answers.

Thank you for listening.

title: Making the Tuning Your Own
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: making the tuning your own.

This session is the practicum. After days of teaching, Carla walks the group through her tuning process step by step, out loud, so they can practice it together in real time. It is the most detailed look anywhere in the archive at how an experienced channeler actually prepares — and the most repeated sentence in it is, don’t do it exactly like I do.

She begins where everything begins, with intention. State clearly what you are doing. I am now tuning to channel. Then the radio dial — that image from the earlier session — tuning roughly at first, then more and more precisely, until you are settled into the middle of the signal. Then something inspirational, in her words: a prayer, a song, a chant, whatever lifts your heart and opens it.

Then the stating of the intention to the Creator. Her own form of it is, I wish to receive the highest and best channel I can carry in a conscious and stable manner. She likes the highest and best formulation, she says, because she does not presume to know what the highest and best contact is for her on any given day. She only knows that is what she wants. You may name a contact instead, if you wish. The honesty of not knowing is part of the prayer.

She adds a line I find beautiful in its humility. I want all the words to be yours, she says to the source, and none of my own. It is a cue to her own subconscious as much as a request to the universe — a deliberate stepping aside, so that what comes through is not colored by her preferences.

Then comes a step she added only about ten years ago, and I love that she tells them this — that the process is still evolving, even for her. She asks to see her colors, her energy body, checking each chakra through the rainbow for blockages. And then she asks her helpers to do the equivalent of putting a computer into safe mode: balance the whole energy body to the level of the weakest chakra, and hold it there, crystallized, for the duration of the contact. It steadies the tuning, she says. It got rid of her own vacillation.

Then protection. She visualizes being dipped in the violet ray and the red ray mixed together, which seals the body, and then being dipped in limitless white light, which seals the spirit. And finally, the most human detail in the whole sequence — she counts down from her age. It takes a while, she admits, laughing. But it is her way. It brings her down, step by step, into the roots of mind, into the workroom, to the gatekeeper, settled and ready.

The group practices all of this in silence, and when they come back up, the questions pour out. How long should it take? What if I can’t find my workroom? What does it mean to form the circle? And underneath every question is the real one: am I doing it right? Carla’s answer never changes. You can’t just mimic somebody else and have it feel like your own. You need to own this and make it your own. Grasp the reasons for each part — the tuning, the protection, the asking for unseen help — and then adjust the doing of each to suit yourself.

The questions afterward are as instructive as the walkthrough. One student asks about forming the circle of unseen support — and Carla explains that when you state your intention, you can invite all those in the unseen realms who come in the name of love to join the circle of seeking. Not to do the work for you, but to hold the space with you. Another asks about the clap at the end, and she laughs — yes, just clap. The percussion creates a psychic ending. It tells your deep mind: this is complete.

She is honest that there is no clear-cut list of instructions, and that some teachers would pretend otherwise. But I know from the depths of my being, she says, that I have found the best way only for myself. That sentence might be the whole weekend in miniature. Take the map. Walk your own road. And when you are done, seal it with a clap — a small percussion, a psychic ending, a way of saying, it is complete.

Thank you for listening.

title: It Is Okay to Pass
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: it is okay to pass.

This short session opens the practice circles of the intensive — the part of the weekend where the students stop learning about channeling and start trying it. Carla’s opening remarks are mostly about permission. Specifically, the permission not to channel.

She describes two levels of unreadiness, and both are honorable. The first is when you are in such a mess in your head that you do not even want to try to feel the contact. Then you just say, pass. The second is when you are at least partway there — if you have half a leg up, as she puts it, then get on and ride. Say, I am Laitos, and see what comes. And if nothing comes, you simply say, I leave this instrument, and hand the contact to the person on your left. At least you will have tried.

There is no penalty for passing, she says, and she means it. In any group of people learning a new skill there is always a wide range of speeds. Don’t feel badly if you are slow. Don’t take it to heart if you are quicker. Just know that if you are quicker, you are quickly at the start of a very long journey. She has been trying to make her channeling better since she began in the mid nineteen seventies, she tells them, and she has gotten just good enough to see how much better she can get.

The contact they will be practicing with is Laitos. Carla explains that she checked with Q’uo about whether to ask for the highest and best or to ask for Laitos directly, and the answer came back that it amounts to the same thing — for a training circle of beginners, you are going to get Laitos anyway. Laitos is the Confederation’s practice contact, the patient teacher of new channels, and the group is simply not ready for the Q’uo vibration yet. There is no shame in that. It is just where everyone starts.

To comfort the nervous, she tells the story of her own beginning. Her first channeled message, she says, was, I am Hatonn. I am having difficulty with this instrument. That was it. That was the whole message. And it did not get much better for a while. She was not one of the fast ones. I love that she tells them this — the great channeler of the Law of One material, beginning with eight words about difficulty.

She also tells them the one thing that will steady them more than any technique. You do not get a whole different feeling when you are channeling than when you are talking, she says. It feels like you. The train of thought simply continues — until you stop listening within and start thinking for yourself, and then it stops. That is the only way you can tell the difference. You stop the channeling and realize, oh, I was channeling, because now I am not. Now I am thinking.

One exchange in the session charmed me. A student asks whether some other, alternate Laitos might slip in unnoticed while the circle goes around. Carla smiles — in all her years of teaching, she says, that has never once happened. What does happen, without fail, is the beginner’s real question, asked in a dozen different ways: was that me, or was that them? Her answer is the whole teaching in miniature. It feels like you. It is supposed to feel like you. Go ahead anyway.

So the session ends where the real work begins — with a circle of beginners about to take turns saying, I am Laitos, into the unknown. Some will feel something. Some will feel nothing. Some will pass. All of it is perfect, Carla says. All speeds are perfect. The only failure would be pretending. Everything else is practice.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mirror in the Pouch
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mirror in the pouch.

This is the first full channeling circle of the intensive, and the contact is Laitos — the Confederation source who trains beginning channels. Rather than speaking about love and light directly, Laitos tells the circle a story, passed from instrument to instrument around the room. It is a story about a seeker. And like all good stories, it is about everyone listening.

Once upon a time, in a small village at the foot of a great mountain and at the shore of an ocean, there dwelled a young man who hauled the nets at eventide and walked behind the plow at harvest. He was happy in the sunlight and content in the rain, and he knew no desire except to live out his life in that small village. Until the day a ship with a strange sail appeared on the horizon, and strangers speaking an unknown tongue came ashore, and something in him woke up with a great desire to know more than he had known before.

So he sets out to climb the mountain no one has ever climbed. The journey is long and full of obstacles. He comes to a river he cannot cross, and walking upstream he finds only a waterfall and a cliff. He wanders inland and finds a village of strangers, and an old wise man who tells him the climb is nearly impossible — which only inspires him more. The old man gives him a pouch, and tells him to open it when he is in danger or lost.

Back at the waterfall, the young man follows his intuition, though he does not understand it. In order to go up, he must go down. He spreads his arms and leaps into midair — and the colors of his vision change, and he finds himself borne up on the back of a huge white bird, flying toward a rainbow that circles the peak. I love that moment in the story. The leap comes first. The wings come after.

On the bird’s back, flying toward the rainbow, he asks the bird what it is that makes him hunger so to know what he does not know. The bird is silent. He has no answers, Laitos says, and yet he has become something more than he was before. He ponders the mystery of unknowing as he flies.

Then he remembers the pouch. He opens it, and inside he finds a mirror. And when he looks into the mirror, he sees himself as that which was the seeker and that which was sought. The beginning and the end of the journey, lying in his hands, in his heart, in his mind.

What does he do with this revelation? He asks the bird to take him home. The village marvels to see him walking on the shore again. What have you learned, they cry, what miracle has brought you back? And he says, I have seen that those with different languages are yet kind. I have seen that when I abandon myself to the quest for truth, the truth itself shall come and give me wing. And above all, my friends, my family, my beloved, I have seen that there is nothing more precious than you. I have found my happiness.

The questions after the story are wonderful in their human specificity. One student asks why she became so incredibly cold just before she channeled — and Laitos answers gently that the feeling of cold has long been associated with the entrance of a metaphysical presence into the room, a subjective signal, fleeting, nothing to fear. Another asks what fourth density is like, and Laitos describes a place with no veil, where every thought is known — and where, astonishingly, that total exposure brings not shame but tremendous comfort and ease. To be fully known, and fully accepted.

After the story, Laitos speaks directly to the circle, and the words are worth carrying with you. You are, indeed, channels already, they say. In all that you do and say you are already being a channel for love and for light. Love is all that there is. And all that there is, is love. And then, as they always do, they leave the group with one small instruction. Do not forget to meditate, they say, even if you only have five minutes.

Thank you for listening.

title: Meeting the Contact Halfway
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: meeting the contact halfway.

After the first channeling circle, the group gathers for questions, and the questions are the ones every beginner asks. How do the words actually come? Do they pop into your mind one at a time? How do you tell your thoughts from theirs? The answers Carla and the group work out together are some of the most practical teaching in the whole intensive.

Carla is honest about her own experience first. She does not get words, she says. She gets concepts. Then she has to translate them into words. It is not precisely a picture. It is hard to say precisely what it is. It is just impressions. She goes with a very slight impression, starts talking about it, and it gets clearer as she speaks. Subtle work, she calls it. Not obvious work.

One student offers the image that unlocks the session. Flip the light switch, he says. When it is your turn, just say, I am Laitos — flip the switch — and then the concepts or pictures start coming. Carla agrees completely. You had felt enough presence to venture forth, she tells another student. Next time, just go ahead and do that, and perhaps the concepts will come to you.

Another student puts it even better. The way I perceive it, she says, I have to meet them halfway. I have to open my mouth. I have to have the willingness to put myself out there and speak, with faith that something is going to come out and it is not going to sound foolish. That phrase — meeting the contact halfway — becomes the teaching of the night. The contact does not possess you and speak through you like a puppet. It meets your willingness with its concepts, and together you make the words.

Carla offers an image for what happens when you wobble, as every beginner does. The sources are like the satellite navigation in a car, she says. If you get off course, the gadget recalculates and guides you from the place you actually are. The channeling sources are like that. If you get off course they just work gently with you to tell the story from that point. They are quite tolerant of slight variations between what they put out and what you pick up. Their goal remains unchanged. They want to produce a body of words that has the potential to help people wake up and realize who they are and why they are here.

A student adds the philosophical reason this must be so. It has to be a meeting of peers, he says. Otherwise, if it were their words and just your mouth, it would be something like possession, an invasion. Free will has to work that way. It has to be your own imagination meeting theirs, your faith carrying the words forward.

And then there is the most reassuring testimony of the night, from a student describing what it actually felt like. At first she saw words on her inner screen. Then the screen went away, and it was as though the story was telling itself. After she started channeling, she says, it was as though the story was choosing my words. Another student nods — if you are in the altered state, just go. Forget about how the words come out. Just say it. Be confident that whatever you do is okay.

The session wanders, as real conversations do, into dreams and stage fright and the fear of looking foolish — and Carla meets each one plainly. To the student with stage fright she says: give yourself suggestions during the tuning. Tell yourself you are allowed to be shy and to speak anyway. To the one who dreamed of a dark figure offering to teach him, she affirms what he did in the dream — he kept affirming his positive polarity, kept asking the figure to declare itself. Discernment, it turns out, works in dreams too.

So the teaching tonight is about faith in motion. You will not get a voice from the sky dictating sentences. You will get a slight impression, a nudge, a picture — and then you open your mouth and meet it halfway, trusting that the words will come. They will not be perfect. The sources will steer, gently, like a navigator recalculating. And what comes out the other side will be, in some mysterious way, both yours and not yours. That is what channeling is.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Story of Creation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the story of creation.

In the second channeling circle of the intensive, Laitos tells another story — this time the biggest story there is. The story of the beginning of this creation, of which we and they are a part. It is channeled by beginners, passed around the circle, and all the more moving for that.

At the beginning of creation, Laitos says, there was the allness of the One. In complete quiet, resting — that intelligent infinity which is the ground of being. And into that stillness came the first distortion of the Law of One, which is free will. Listen to how they describe it. Free will is a shining entity, like the flame of what this instrument calls the Holy Spirit, like the wind of spirit that goes where it wishes. No one can predict its path.

It was this free will, they say, that touched the placidity of the infinite and suggested that it might, by creating a world, come to know itself better. And so the Creator launched forth the one great original Thought — and that Thought was unconditional love. In that Thought lay the potentiality of all that was to come.

This unconditional love, fertile and creative, then created light — the third distortion of the Law of One. And light, Laitos says, is an entity of infinite joy and effulgence, full of the love of the one Creator. In its turn, light spun out of itself the vast array of time and space — all the planets in their courses around all the billions of suns in the billions of galaxies. And to its children, light gave a staggering gift. Co-creativity. Each of you, they say, is a creator in your own universe.

The beginners’ channeling brings fresh images to the ancient story. One instrument offers two pictures of the Creator’s impulse to expand: children playing on a summer day, all laughter and pure bliss — and a single tree growing alone in an orchard, which knows that without struggle and linear growth it will gain no self-awareness. Both are true, Laitos suggests. The bliss and the struggle belong to the same urge to know itself.

Another instrument is shown a squash, of all things — and the concept of the heart. The squash is the heart, and inside the heart are the seeds of all of us. The heart is the Creator. The heart pumps, and the seeds spread across the land, each one with its own free will, growing as it pleases. When asked about it afterward, Laitos confirms the image and deepens it. You are all parts of the true vine, they say, that vine of unconditional love. And as your thoughts ripen, you shake out the seeds — thought by thought, as you move through your incarnation, offering them to everyone you meet.

Near the end of the circle, the story turns inward. The great work of the one Creator, Laitos says through another instrument, is the work each of you shares: to know the self, to know the Creator, and to know the creation. All is contained within each portion of your being, and your being is all that there is. These seem like simple truths, they say, yet no more profound statements can ever be made. Through each experience does the Creator know itself — and through each experience, you know yourself as the Creator.

One answer in the question period deserves its own hearing. Asked what spiritual principle makes the clearest channel, Laitos names quietness and confidence — the assumption that all is well. Form the intention, hone the desire, firm the will, they say — and then release all thought of how it should happen, and offer everything you are to the Creator. There is no need to reach or grasp in the house of the Father, they say. Love is always infinite and fully available. The clearest channel is the most relaxed one.

And then the closing, which I want to leave you with whole. Each of you, with your unique personality and gifts, offers us a different way to tell our tale that is simple and unified. Love is all that there is. And all that there is, is love.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Voice of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a voice of love.

The intensive closes with a meditation, and the contact is Q’uo. The question before them is simple and a little heartbreaking. What is the use of all this — this channeling we have been learning all weekend — in the time that remains to us? Q’uo’s answer is not about technique at all. It is about why any voice of love matters, and why yours does.

They begin with an image I have carried with me since I first read it. Each voice that offers to channel, they say, is like a certain kind of stained-glass window. The colorations that seem to you like defects of character, like limitations of spirit — those self-same quirks give a pleasing color to the voice of love as it shines through you. No two windows are alike. And as you attempt to speak, you create new stories, new ways of saying the one simple statement: all is one, and that one thing is love.

It is a great blessing to us, they say, when there are new entities through whom we may speak. And they thank the beginners — for their courage, for their integrity — because to break free of the taboo against speaking thoughts without knowing ahead of time what they will be is a great departure from the safe conduct of the culture. You may not feel very courageous, they say. But you are.

The session moves through deep waters — the nature of third density as a school, the veil of forgetting, the choice every soul must make between service to others and service to self. Q’uo describes this Earth not as a prison, as one questioner ruefully puts it, but as something more like a testing field, a fiery furnace. The conditions are harsh, they say, and precisely because they are harsh, you can do in a single lifetime what it would take a million years to do elsewhere. You hold in your hands the keys of unknowing. It is not the answers that matter here. It is the questions.

And then the line that gives this episode its name, in a way. Speaking of the wanderers — those souls who chose to come here to help lighten the planet — Q’uo says that each one fought, tooth and nail, to get into line for a body and come here at this time. When you are not inside the intensity of it, they say, this looks like the best party in town. A unique opportunity to change the balance of love and wisdom within yourself, rapidly, by faith alone.

Toward the end, a questioner asks about her family history research — the hours spent learning the joys and sorrows of ancestors she never met — and whether it serves them. Q’uo’s answer is one of the loveliest sentences in the archive. Any time a heart opens, they say, the entire creation sings. In the main, the opening serves your own spirit. But nothing that opens a heart is ever wasted. The whole creation hears it.

There is one more image from the session I cannot leave out. Q’uo says that those who have awakened often feel terribly isolated — making their choices alone, without the comfort of like-minded company. And yet, they say, this isolation is an illusion of the physical eyes. The unseen realms are rich with those who would help you, who love you, who wish only to be of service as you make your choice. Groups like this one matter, they say, because they let entities find each other — and encourage each other, and love each other, and bring each other home.

So this is Q’uo’s answer to the closing question. The use of channeling, of any voice offered in love, is to add one more stained-glass window to the world — your colors, your quirks, your particular way of saying that all is one. You do not need to change the face of the Earth in a single moment. You only need to speak, in your own voice, to whoever is hungry to hear. And whenever your heart opens as you do it, the entire creation sings.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Philosophy of Contact
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the philosophy of contact.

In a Saturday meditation, the circle asks Q’uo a pointed question. When extraterrestrial sources contact human beings — with specific information, sometimes face to face — does that infringe on our free will? What is the philosophy behind such contact?
