Q’uo’s answer is remarkably candid, including about their own mistakes.

The heart of it is the Confederation’s ethic. Those of the Confederation, Q’uo says, have agreed among themselves not to appear openly to your peoples — not to land, not to stage the great display — precisely in order to preserve positive polarity and to avoid infringing on free will. They understand the desire for a mass landing, for a heralded new day with all the strength of superior knowledge. Many thousands of years ago, they say, they put that thought away. It would not lighten the consciousness of the planet. It would only overwhelm it.

I find their honesty about failure even more striking than the philosophy. Asked whether the Confederation’s hands are clean, Q’uo says plainly that they are not. They speak of information shared long ago with those working on nuclear energy — given with the hope of easing humanity’s heavy labor so people could turn to spiritual growth — and of the unwise amount shared with the one known as Nicola. These powerfully positive people, Q’uo says, were not able to control the results of the use of that information. Is it a concern of ours that this information was used to harm, where we had hoped only to help? Yes, they say. It remains a concern. From each of our mistakes we have learned much.

That learning is why they work the way they do now — not through landings or interventions, but through instruments. Through quiet channeling, offered to whoever freely chooses to listen. And here is a detail I love. Q’uo says they find it helpful to work with instruments who have no particular need to express their own thoughts — channels without a bias about the outcome of their words, so that what comes through is not bent by personal opinion. The humility of the instrument is part of the philosophy.

They also speak frankly about the other side of contact. There are negatively oriented sources, they say — what the archive calls the Orion group — who respond to the call of those wishing to graduate in the negative polarity, and who fully intend to infringe upon free will. They have no ethical considerations to hamper them. And there are mixed cases, like the sources known as the Nine, whom Q’uo describes as loving Earth deeply and sincerely wanting to help, yet never having grown past the impulse to interfere for the good — to appear physically, to make changes in the environment, to convince people they are real.

The promised landings, Q’uo says, echoing Jim’s dry remark in the discussion, shall not occur. Not from the Confederation, at any rate. The philosophy is settled. Help must be offered in a way that leaves the choice entirely with the human being — taken up freely, or left behind freely. Anything else, however loving the motive, becomes another form of control.

Q’uo also offers a fascinating aside about the sources known as the Nine — the contact behind some well-known channelings of that era. These entities, Q’uo says, love the people of Earth deeply and sincerely want to help. Their difficulty is older than any of us: they have never grown past the impulse to interfere for the good. It is a portrait of how even genuine love, untempered by respect for free will, becomes distortion. The road of good intentions, it turns out, runs all the way into the inner planes.

So tonight’s teaching is about restraint as a form of love. The most advanced sources the archive knows have learned, by painful experience, that the greatest gift they can offer is the one that demands nothing. No proof. No spectacle. No interference. Just words, through a willing instrument, for whoever is hungry. The rest — as always — is up to you.

Thank you for listening.

title: From Knowing to Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: from knowing to being.

The question before Q’uo in this Saturday meditation is about the seeker’s relationship to spiritual information itself. All these books, these channelings, these inspired words — how should we hold them? Q’uo’s answer is gentle, funny in places, and quietly revolutionary.

They begin with words themselves. Words have a redeeming feature, they say. When spoken, words partake in the human breath — and the breath is sacred. The very structure of words is sacred. Speaking a holy name, in any tradition, creates avenues deep into the archetypal mind, awakening resonance from very deep places within the roots of consciousness. There is a blessedness, they say, in working with words that inspire.

And yet. There is an old Buddhist story they retell, of a saint who held stones in his mouth for twenty years until he learned to be silent. In silence, they say, there is no need to take a cookie-cutter to the concepts that speak to the deep mind. In silence, one may rest, and allow the truth to rise up into consciousness from the infinite invisible that is the heart of each seeker.

The teaching that follows is about balance. Some seekers love philosophical structures and can walk many paths without being swayed. Others are sensitive to beauty and profundity, and can be swept up by a seductively beautiful system, losing themselves in it. Q’uo will not prescribe one way. Any spiritual system, sincerely followed, can get you there. But the deepest question is not whether a system works. It is how you relate to all outer words while you use them.

Their answer is my favorite line in the session. Work with outer teachings consciously, they say, at all times creating a spaciousness around the words — a spaciousness that gives the soul room for the unspoken, the ineffable. There is much between every inspired word that is unspoken, they say, and it is that unspoken ambience in which the spoken word rings with truth.

Then comes the turn that gives this episode its title. Jim had observed, in the discussion before the channeling, that as the decades of his seeking went by, he became less interested in forming questions and getting answers. Q’uo agrees, and names it as a mark of spiritual maturity. The intense desire to know the truth, they say, becomes gradually transformed into the intense desire to be the truth.

Listen to how they describe that ripening. At first the journey looks like an outer one — seeking out there, sifting through the harvest of other people’s seeking to find your own truth. But gradually, things begin to fall away from the seeker’s mind and heart and experience, until the truth itself rises to the surface of consciousness. And what rises is not a fact. It is a realization. That it is a perfect world. That nothing can be known — and that all speaks of the one infinite Creator. The seeker becomes transparent to himself, and finds at the very heart of himself the consciousness of unconditional love.

They close with practical kindness. Find your own tempo and rhythm, they say. Sometimes it is right to cram yourself with new thoughts. Sometimes it is wiser to refrain from study entirely. What matters is the balance between the intellect and silence — because beyond thought lies truth, beyond the intellect lies insight, and beyond knowledge lies gnosis.

Earlier in the session, Q’uo lingered on the practice of speaking the holy names — the Creator name, or Jesus, or Buddha, or any of the god-names of the world’s traditions. The combination of letters, shaped by the human breath, creates avenues into the archetypal mind, they said, awakening resonance from very deep places. It does not matter which name you use. What matters is that the breath carries it down past the intellect, to where the roots of mind drink.

And one more thing, almost tossed off, that I want to underline. There is great wisdom, they say, in taking lightly and with laughter the entire business of study and thought. Trust yourself. Trust your sense of resonance. And then enjoy your seeking — your questions, your answers, and everything that goes into a life lived by spiritual means.

Thank you for listening.

title: Know in Order to Serve
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: know in order to serve.

The question in this Saturday meditation is about affirmations — about using the will to create changes in consciousness. Q’uo’s answer introduces one of the most beautiful concepts in the archive. The magical personality. And their first move is to take the mystery out of it.

The magical personality is not a mysterious entity, they say. It is yourself at a different stage of your development. It is your higher self — your highest and best self, a completely magical, focused, sacred being. It is, they say, your gift to yourself from the midpoint of sixth density, reaching back across all of space and time. You and your higher self planned this incarnation together. And your higher self is, at all times, as close as your breathing.

Because this personality is so powerful, Q’uo suggests a certain protocol for working with it. When you sit down to your affirmations, take it on deliberately — with a gesture, a ring or adornment worn only for the working, a visualization of putting on magical robes. Carla herself, they mention, visualizes putting on her robes before channeling and taking them off afterward. At the end of the working, put it aside again. The point is cleanliness. You step into the sacred role fully, and then you step back out, so that the purity of the working is not dragged into the ordinary business of the day.

And the polarity of the whole thing is guarded by a single sentence. I desire to know in order to serve. Positive magical workings, they say, always have to do with service to the one infinite Creator and, by reflection, to the world and to the self. There is nothing of the worldly self in the desires of the magical personality. That one sentence — know in order to serve — is the gate. Everything on the far side of it is clean.

What are you seeking when you invoke this self? Q’uo’s answer is disarmingly simple. That which you seek is ever and always a part of yourself — a deeper, more fundamental, more true part of yourself. All things are one, they say, and the implications of that echo through level after level of awareness. You are calling to yourself across the aeons, moving toward the one point where you and the Creator are one.

The session then turns to mantras, and the teaching deepens. A mantra, they say, is a magical working without form — not a statement but a name, a naked principle. And because the mind cannot do anything with a naked principle, it lets it go down immediately into the subconscious, where it bores deeply and creates immediate change in your vibration. In the deepest roots of consciousness, they say, the name of every seeker is the one infinite Creator. Whatever god-name your mantra contains is the deepest, truest name of yourself.

Repetition is the key, as with all ritual. The change in consciousness you seek becomes easier, even effortless, as the habit deepens. And here is the image I want to leave you with. One of the questioners had said that mantra practice smooths out the bumps in the personality shell, and Q’uo agrees wholeheartedly. It brings you, they say, to a world where suffering and catalyst, light and dark, day and night are gathered up into a sacred space where all is one and all is well. That deeper truth then informs the lesser truth of daily life, and the life is transformed in a way that cannot be explained intellectually — but is very effective.

Q’uo adds a practical note about the protocol that I appreciate. The ring, the robe, the gesture — these are not superstition, they say. They are signals to your deep mind that you have stepped into the magical personality and stepped out of the everyday shell. And the stepping out matters as much as the stepping in. You do not try to maintain that purity while you are paying bills and answering the door. You take off the robe. The sacred has its hours, and so does the ordinary — and honoring both is part of the magic.

So tonight’s practice is simple. Choose your words with care and deep love. Take on your highest self like a robe. Speak the ancient names. And hold the whole working inside one clear intention. I desire to know — in order to serve.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are Already a Priest
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are already a priest.

The question in this Saturday meditation is about time, energy, and focus — the three things every seeker feels she lacks. Q’uo’s answer begins with a declaration that reframes the whole problem. Each of you is already a priest, they say. Your very nature is sacred. Every cell of your body is full of the love and the light of the one infinite Creator.

They sketch the two ways our cultures hand off the sacred. In the East, the village gives the spiritual job to one person — the guru, the shaman, the priest — and everyone else is assumed not to be a master. In the West, a few feel called to special vocations, and the rest attend services, receive their Sabbath sermons, and go back to the secular world until next week. Either way, the vast majority of people are content to think of themselves in non-spiritual terms. Just people, living their lives.

And Q’uo says plainly: the people of your planet have given away their power. They have lost the conviction that they are priests. They have lost the sense of themselves as magical and powerful entities. Listen to the image they use — the modern soul asked at every turn for numbers. What is your social security number? Your driver’s license number? Your account number? A name is not unique enough for the culture. And so there is less and less reliance on the quality of a human being, and more and more on a string of integers that cannot express the depth and richness of a soul.

But it is possible, they say, to take back your power. To recover your sense of magic. To become a priest in your daily life once again. You do not need a monastery. There are very few cloisters left, and very few who want them. What you need is already in your hands — if you understand the three qualities rightly.

Time first. Yes, most entities do not have time for full-time seeking, between making a living and tending the family web and carrying their share of the world. Q’uo does not argue with this. They simply set it aside and move to the second quality, energy — and here they draw a distinction I keep thinking about. Your physical energy is finite; the exhausted body will sleep whenever it can. But there is another kind of energy entirely, your vital energy, your élan vital. And it is not depleted by physical work.

What depletes it, they say, is tolerating cynicism, boredom, and negative thinking within your own thought processes. It is so easy to become cynical gazing at an obviously imperfect culture — or to batter yourself against unmovable bastions trying to change it, until world-weariness becomes your usual attitude. But that is a choice, they say. There are other choices that keep the questing spirit alive, enthusiastic, and innocent of cynicism.

One of the questioners had said it best, and Q’uo quotes him. Either one becomes what one hates, or what one loves. The energy that brings you toward the spiritual life is the energy of seeking to become what you love. A positive orientation can look at disaster and chaos and still find hope, still find a vector toward the light. And those cheerful, positive souls you admire? Ask them honestly, Q’uo says, and they will tell you about the suffering that threatened their cheerfulness — and about digging deep to find the will and the faith to look beyond the obvious, to the unseen energy of love that is our nature.

Which brings us to the third quality, focus — the one that makes up for the lack of the other two. If you can focus, if you can become single-minded in seeking the one infinite Creator, then whatever your estate in life, the world becomes spiritual. All that you see becomes sacred. From the least to the most, all things speak eloquently of the Creator. All voices are voices of love.

So the teaching tonight is not that you need more hours. It is that you are already what you are trying to become. A priest. A magical entity. A cell of the Creator’s body. Take back the power you gave away, refuse the cynicism that drains you, and focus — even for a moment — on the love underneath everything. The sacred was never anywhere else.

Thank you for listening.

title: Melodies in the Air
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: melodies in the air.

The question in this Saturday meditation is about art — about the spiritual principles behind the creative impulse. Q’uo’s answer is a love letter to artists, and a warning, and a reminder to the rest of us that we are all in the same business.

They begin by distinguishing two kinds of artists. There are those who treat art as a career, a role, a way to make a good living — and they, Q’uo says, limit themselves by staying in the lower chakras of expression. And then there are those with the spontaneous and irresistible urge to create. Those who must express what is within them. Whether or not such entities would think of their gifts in spiritual terms, Q’uo says, what they do is a spiritual exercise by its very definition.

Listen to how they describe it. To touch the creative impulse, the artist must move into the open heart — the green-ray chakra — and rise from there into the blue ray of communication, the indigo ray of faith, and on through the violet ray to the gateway of intelligent infinity. The artist draws from beyond that gateway the inspiration needed to express the visions she has seen. She is, they say, like a treasure hunter who finds treasure and then must share it.

Carla’s favorite example is a musician named Willie. Asked how he created so many beautiful melodies, he said, there are melodies moving through the air at all times. It is just a matter of picking one out of the air and putting words to it. Q’uo says he was accurate. The infinity of possibilities flows through that gateway to all who access it, at all times. There is no end to the creative impulse. The artist does not manufacture beauty. She catches it.

Then the warning, and it is a serious one. The great difficulty artistic entities face, they say, is becoming overly fond of the upper chakras — the heart, the throat, the brow, the gateway — and neglecting the lower ones. They become untethered, ungrounded in their lives and incarnations. And here is the sentence that stopped me cold. This is the temptation for those who love beautiful things, not realizing that beauty begins with the stench of birth, the blood, the wailing, the sharp light, and the terror.

The creative process, they say, must move down, daily and consciously, into those very beginnings of life — into survival and sexuality, into relationships, into the whole energy body — in order to have the strength and the sheer energy to make the most of the spiritual gifts of creativity without destroying the body, the emotions, or the mind through inattention. Heaven without earth, in other words, is not sustainable. The treasure hunter has to come home and eat dinner.

Q’uo also sketches the varieties of artists — the performers who create from the heart, the writers and poets and inspired teachers with the pronounced blue ray who must communicate in new ways, those drawn to the realms of faith and magic. Each mixture is unique to the artist, and the mode of the art will be unique too. But these, they say, are the waters in which the artist plays.

And then the turn that includes everyone. All entities are creators, they say, but not all are drawn to express it. Many are solidly attached to their little island of consensus reality and want their feet not to sink into the unknown. Yet the creative impulse dwells within all, as part of being part of the Creator. Each entity is a sub-creator. Each entity, through faith and will, can change his world.

You can see it, they say, in the small things. A collection arranged just so. A tree decorated with love. Meals prepared with care. Children raised with genius. The impulse is the same impulse. It is only the scale that differs.

So tonight’s teaching is for the painters and the poets, yes — but also for the cooks and the gardeners and anyone who has ever arranged anything just so, for the love of it. The melodies are moving through the air at all times. Pick one out. Put words to it. And remember to come down to earth afterward, where beauty begins.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Land of No Night
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the land of no night.

In the spring of two thousand eight, a circle of new channels gathered for a weekend of intensive practice, and those of Laitos came through with a story. Not a lesson in the usual sense, but a tale to be carried in the heart.

They pictured for the instrument a land of heavenly light, a country where the sun never set, where the people were farmers, humble folk who had known nothing but everlasting day. The crops grew, the children played, and life was good. Yet one day dark clouds rose and covered the sun, and for the first time in memory, darkness fell upon the land.

The people could not comprehend it. They wondered if this was the end of the world, if they were facing their extinction. After an hour or two the cloud passed and the light returned in full splendor, but the people were troubled to their roots. As one, they turned to the wisest among them, whom everyone called Father, and asked him what the darkness could mean.

Father was silent for a moment, and then he spoke with gravity. Just as silence had preceded his words, he said, so does darkness precede the light. They had grown so accustomed to endless day that they had forgotten there was such a thing as the dark. Yet the darkness was not wrong. It was simply an experience they had not had for a very long time, and it was not theirs to fear but to regard as an opportunity.

Then a young maiden stepped forward. Something in the discussion had stirred her memory, like a dream that was also a distant reality. She remembered drifting as a nebulous cloud far above the planet, feeling the darkness calling to her, drawing her toward embodiment, toward a fuller knowing. She had answered that call and lived upon a dark world, and she had learned something there that she could now teach.

She took a flower in her hand and showed the people an insect that had crawled inside the blossom, a creature they had not expected to find there. They began to fear it, but before their eyes the flower closed around the insect and opened again, more beautiful than before. The maiden said to them, the darkness is part of us, but our light is greater, and we can engulf the darkness with our light and our love, and grow closer to the Creator.

Father smiled, and then he spoke a hard truth with love. By their preference and their long excellence, he said, they had earned the right to unending light, and they had wished it so. Yet during their long day they had not moved forward. They had remained upon a happy plateau. It is the darkness of the soil, he said, that offers deep, sweet food to the seed. It is in the darkness of your own hearts, interior and shadowed, that you experience the depths of emotion and choose to seek the one infinite Creator.

Then the maiden strewed the petals of her flower, and the wind caught them and shaped them into a great ship, its hull formed of roots. She invited all who were willing to board this ship of consciousness, which would carry them into a land where light and darkness could be experienced together, mastered together, and blended into catalyst for growth.

Some were afraid, and asked her what they should do if the darkness proved too great. The maiden pointed to the distant horizon, and there above the clouds stood a tall castle, rising so high they could not see its top. You would never have thought to look higher, she told them, if the dark clouds had not come. Fear and darkness help you climb to heights you could not have scaled without them.

Then the maiden took Father's hand, and together they began to ascend the castle steps, she wrapped in gleaming petals of light, he wrapped in the dark roots that signify fertility and growth. And they danced through the darkness toward the light, to the very peak, where the darkness wrapped itself about the light as a lover, and the light wrapped itself about the darkness in return.

And when the dance was done, the maiden and Father turned to the people and asked them one question. Would you choose eternal day, or would you choose that which seems fearful but brings growth? And with boldness, one by one, the farmers of that village chose growth.

We might ask ourselves the same question whenever the clouds gather over our own lives. The dark is not the enemy of the light. It is the soil in which the seed of the self breaks open. And those of Laitos remind us that we need not fear the night, for above every cloud there is a castle we have not yet learned to see.

Thank you for listening.

title: Intention Sets the Tone
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: intention sets the tone.

On the same spring weekend in two thousand eight, in the closing session of the first channeling intensive, those of Q'uo spoke to the new instruments about the nature of contact itself, about what happens, energetically, when a being without a physical body speaks through one who has one.

They began with the energy body, which they call the primary body. The creature you are would be empty and hollow, they said, were it not for the interpenetration of your flesh and bones by the energy body of your infinite and eternal self. Think of the physical body as a horse that waits to be ridden, and loves the rider who rides it well. The rider is the soul.

The first contact, then, is between you as a physical being and you as an energy being. The second is between your energy body and theirs. And here those of Q'uo offered an image from the carpenter's shop. Intention is like a saw cutting an opening in a board. The carpenter thinks long and hard about the shape and size of the opening, and the saw must be skillful so that the cut is smooth and the fit is good.

When you make your intention, you cut an opening in your energy body of a certain shape, and that shape is the shape of your desire. It is not flat but multidimensional, formed by the alignment of the heart, the blue ray, the indigo ray, and the violet ray with the gateway to intelligent infinity. The clarity of the cut is the clarity of your intention.

But before the cutting, they said, comes the clearing. In your eagerness to serve, do not skip the examination of your energy body. Blockages, acute or chronic, narrow the beam of energy that rises from the root through the heart and out the crown. So make it a daily practice to look over your thoughts, to balance and free the energy body of distortion.

And if they could use only one word for that work, the word would be forgiveness. Forgive yourself for the small failures of the day, not because you are worthy or unworthy, but because your nature is perfection. Shall you hold it against the world that it cannot show you that perfection, they asked, or shall you by faith alone claim the perfection that triumphantly exists regardless of appearances?

Forgiving others follows the same path, and it is easier, they said, to forgive another than to forgive the self. But remember that what is held against another is held against yourself, and what is forgiven another is forgiven yourself, for you and the other are one. Come into a state in which all is forgiven, and in that environment set your intention to serve.

They spoke then of buried pain, the pockets of deeply held hurt that nearly every incarnation gathers. The greater the pain, the harsher the defenses built around it. You need not attack these islands of pain with violence. Instead, become a detective of your own reactions. When some small event provokes a reaction out of all proportion to its cause, take note. That unevenness marks the direction of an old wound.

Patiently, lovingly, follow the trail. One day the pain may present itself to you free of its defenses, and you will see it in its true shape for the first time. Then embrace the realization and release it. And the balm for such wounds is forgiveness again, forgiveness of the self, of the other, of the situation. You may feel a lightness in the shoulders that carried the burden, and an inrush of new energy into the body.

Do this gently, they cautioned, and do not try to clear every distortion at once, for the very desire to become perfectly clear creates distortion of its own. This work cannot be finished in a lifetime. Remain watchful, day by day, for what disturbs you, and let your knowledge of yourself deepen.

They also reminded the new channels that the contact is a tender thing, intimate by nature, and it deserves preparation and rest. Take time to tune before the contact, as you would tune a radio toward the highest and best station you can receive. And when the contact is over, take as much time to rest and let the experience mellow, like the afterglow that follows any true communion.

In the end, their hope for every word they share is simple: to decrease distortion and enlarge love, in themselves and in all who hear. That is the whole of their intention, cut clean and offered freely.

Thank you for listening.

title: Inviting the Sacred In
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: inviting the sacred in.

A note before we begin. This evening's session speaks openly about sexuality and intimacy as sacred ground. If that subject is tender for you, please listen with care, and take only what resonates.

On a Saturday evening in May of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo were asked about sacred sexuality, about how two people might share the energy of intimacy in a way that honors the Creator. And they answered with unusual frankness and tenderness.

They began by laying the groundwork. Your energy body is electrical in nature, they said, fed by the light of your sun and by the heart of the Earth itself. That infinite love and light streams upward into the red ray, the seat of survival and of sexuality, and if it is not blocked it rises freely into the heart, letting the heart open and bloom like a flower.

The beginnings of sexuality are simple and primal, they said. But its potential is that it may become sacred. Sacred sexuality lies within the precincts of the indigo ray and moves into the mystery of the violet ray, calling down inspiration from the Godhead principle itself into the joining of the physical and the metaphysical.

It begins, as all sacred work begins, with intention. When two people set their intent together to invite the Creator into the equation of their electrical circuitry, they become as priest and priestess, invoking the one infinite Creator in the connection that is the essence of their union.

But intention needs a vessel, and so those of Q'uo spoke of preparation. Whatever two entities do after they have set their intent can be considered a kind of courtship. The world lies heavy on the shoulders of those who must earn a living and fulfill the duties of the day, and there is much to lay down before one can enter into sacred play. There is much of the grime and weariness of the world to release.

They spoke of how the red ray, the ray of sexuality, is also the ray of saying yes or no to life itself. Many have felt that ray narrow under the weight of sorrow. And sometimes the simple act of sharing one's troubles with another whose ears are open begins to open it again. The colors brighten. The energies lift. Life begins to seem good again.

Then, as privacy deepens and the outer world falls away, the talk between the two deepens as well, moving into the blue ray of honest communication. Each listens in complete sympathy to what the other has to say. And the energy lifts further, toward the indigo ray, that ray of faith and magic where two beings may become magical together.

The energy body has its points of contact, they said, places where two energy bodies can close a circuit and become one. When two people hold hands, or touch lips, sexual energy moves between them. Sacred sexuality is the conscious closing of those circuits, structured as any magical ritual is structured, yet shaped entirely by the sensibilities of the two who invoke it.

It was intended by the Creator, they said, that sexuality might offer third-density beings a taste of the steady state of the universe itself, which your peoples call by another name. That steady state is the power of unconditional love. It is the engine that drives creation. It is the sunlight falling upon you.

And beneath all of this runs a quieter teaching, one that applies far beyond the bedroom. The sacred is not somewhere else. It is invited. It is invited by intention, by preparation, by the laying down of the world's heaviness, and by the willingness to meet another with an undefended heart.

Whether in intimacy or in ordinary friendship, the principle is the same. Set the intention. Clear the space. Listen deeply. And let the energy that moves between two open hearts do what it was always meant to do, which is to remind both of them that they are, and have always been, love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Closer Than Your Breath
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: closer than your breath.

In a special meditation in May of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo answered a seeker who felt blocked from her own guidance. She wondered whether the wall between herself and her inner knowing had been set before her birth, or whether it had grown up during her life. Their answer was both reassuring and challenging.

No power on Earth or in heaven, they said, could keep you from your guidance, for your guidance is an aspect of yourself. But many seekers build a wall of their own making, out of personality and out of a low opinion of the self. They called it the unworthiness factor, a quiet prejudice against the perfection and beauty of one's own being.

The guidance you seek so ardently is closer to you than your very breath, they said. And yet, when a seeker is prejudiced against herself, a glass wall can obstruct the free flow of information between the higher self and the self in incarnation. The good news is that a wall built by the self can be taken down by the self.

The journey begins in the lower energy centers, and it must be walked not once but every day. Then, as you move into the heart, you come to what they called an outer courtyard. You stand before the open heart, and yet there is a gate you must cross. It is guarded, they said, by lions of discrimination, and those lions will not let you pass until you have accepted yourself.

That sounds simple, and for those who are habitually self-critical, it is anything but. How does one forgive oneself for self-perceived faults and errors? Their answer was to see the personality for what it is: a shell, an illusion thrown outward, beautiful in its way but not the whole of you. Within that shell lies a spirit that is beautiful, worthy, wonderful, and exquisite, unique in all creation.

When you catch yourself in a fault, do not think judgmental thoughts. Think affectionately, they said. Say to yourself, ah, there is my personality again, and give yourself a hug. They did not suggest you stop trying to become a better person. They encouraged the journey toward the light. But they asked that you walk it as one who already knows herself to be magical and entirely worthy.

Only when you have gathered up all the bits and pieces of yourself that you once shrugged aside, only then can you truly enter the tabernacle of the open heart. Then the lions will let you pass. And once inside, remain in silence for a while. Let the silence fill you. Rest, and let the love you have for the Creator flow and radiate, until you feel the answering pressure of love coming back to you.

From that resting place, you can begin to work with your guidance. Form the intention clearly, even speaking it aloud. Then let the answers flow without judging them, for besides low self-worth, the greatest hindrance to hearing guidance is the intellect's habit of evaluating everything the moment it arrives.

They closed with a practical warning. Anything that closes the heart closes the guidance: troubled relationships, self-judgment, a life out of balance. So move back with humility and begin again, each time you sense yourself shutting down. The road to the open heart is walked daily, sometimes more than once a day.

And the destination was never far. Your guidance has been with you all along, closer than your breath, waiting on the other side of a wall made of glass, through which you only had to learn to see yourself clearly, and to love what you see.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dry Season
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dry season.

On a Saturday in late May of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo spoke about the seasons of the spiritual life, and about what to do when the Beloved seems to have gone silent. Every seeker knows the bright seasons, when the path feels full of light. This session was for the other kind of weather.

They offered the image of a candle. Your will, they said, is a candle that you keep burning day and night. Sometimes it is hardly needed, because the world is full of sunlight. But during the dark night of the soul there is only the candle of your will. Feel the steel core within you, and let it blaze in good seasons and in poor.

It is easy to love the parts of yourself that match your ideals. The harder truth is that there is much more to the self than the polished parts on display in the windows of your ideas about who you are. All the rest of the self, lying in shadow, unrecognized and unpolished, waits for your attention.

And this is not a task you finish once. It is like housework. Again and again you return to the rooms of the self and find some new portion of the shadow side. Then it is time to win that heart over, to offer it honor and respect, and to ask it to integrate itself into you, so that its darkness becomes your strength rather than your weakness. This quest, they said, shall never end.

This is why meditation is so helpful. In meditation, they said, you accept that intellectually you do not know your essence. In meditation, you rest in unknowing. You are not trying to figure anything out. You are no longer talking to yourself, or talking to the Creator, or talking at all.

They spoke then of faith, which needs no striving, because you are already a being created by the infinite One, full of power and beauty. Faith stabilizes you amid the chaos of perceptions. Outer events will always bring conflict, and truth will always be elusive. But with faith in yourself and in the goodness of your design, you come through the storm still standing, and each time the heavy weather returns, you find it easier to remain steady and serene.

If faith is new and fragile in you, they suggested, give it something to hold. A person, an ideal, an image or icon that carries meaning for you. Keep such reminders in your field of vision as you work and play, as you eat and sleep, and they will call you back to the stance of the seeker, centered in faith.

And they offered a practice for the emotions that surge in the dry seasons. Do not treat your feelings as problems to work around. Instead, receive them as guests coming to tea. Offer them hospitality. Sit with them and listen. Surface emotions are often muddy and impure, but when they are honored, they clarify. They deepen, and they connect the surface self with the roots of consciousness.

There is a beauty to each emotion once it has been purified, they said, pure feeling with no distortion. So take the time to process what you feel. Answer when your emotions call. Sit with these guests as they speak to you in their colors, and watch those colors grow clear.

If you are in a dry season now, hear this session as it was meant to be heard: not as a demand to feel better, but as permission to keep the candle lit. The darkness you are walking through is not a sign that you have failed. It may be the very soil in which your faith is learning to stand on its own.

Dive deep, they said. Dive with love. Dive with absolute surety and faith. And may your excursions be filled with light, and your horizons fair.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Living Flame
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the living flame.

In a special meditation in late May of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo were asked about metaphysical technologies, about devices that might enhance the natural abilities of seekers. Their answer turned the question inside out, and pointed to a power far greater than any machine.

They were candid about the Confederation's own history with such experiments. Long ago, they said, they offered the technology of sacred geometry to the culture of Egypt, hoping the pyramid might become an instrument of initiation and healing, a new paradigm of unity. The hope was genuine. But they named another example too, offered in the same spirit of hope, and every listener knows its name. Good intentions, they said, are not enough when a tool is placed in hands that are not ready.

And so they spoke plainly. The way to aid humankind is not through outer technology, or any technology, but through the continual sharing of a single realization: the true identity of all humankind. That is the work they have chosen, and they described it as weaving a net of love, a net that catches people and helps them get their feet under them and realize who they are.

For the secret of spiritual evolution, they said, is the realization that each human being, just as he is, is capable of becoming a person of infinite power and focus. Not after some upgrade. Not with the help of some device. Just as he is, right now.

This is the vision they hope to enlarge in every communication: the human being as a living flame, that bright point where consciousness and the world meet, moment by moment, through the thoughts of a focused mind. To encourage that focus, to remind each person that they are a portion of the Godhead, with both the honor and the duty of taking up that responsibility, is among their most basic hopes.

The magic of every third-density entity lies within, they said, and it awakens the moment you realize that you are a being of power, and that this power is founded in love, made of love, and dissolved completely in love. The love and light streaming from the Logos, reflected back from the heart of the Earth and fed into your energy body, is the source they would have you consider. It is already yours.

There is a challenge in this teaching, and they did not hide it. It asks you to start over in a certain way, to return the power of life and love to the individual, and to step off the grid of a culture that keeps telling you that what you need is somewhere else, in something else, in someone else's invention.

So the next time you find yourself waiting for the right tool, the right teacher, or the right circumstance to begin, remember the living flame. You are not missing a device. You are not missing a piece. The power you are looking for is the one you are looking with, focused, founded in love, and entirely your own.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Song Returned
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the song returned.

A note of gentleness before we begin. This story touches on deep grief, and on a moment when its hero no longer wished to live. It is told with tenderness, and it ends in healing. If sorrow is close to you today, please listen softly.

In June of two thousand eight, at the opening of the second channeling intensive, those of Laitos told a story for the new instruments. Once upon a time, they said, there was an angel resting on a cloud in the heaven worlds, who longed to become a person and live a life on Earth, that she might serve the cause of love in incarnation.

She went before the head angel and made her requests. She wished to carry masculine energy, having known the feminine. She wished for a hard land, one of the dark jungles near the equator, rather than an easy one. She wished to be born into a family that had known great hardship and lost a child, for she wanted to learn the lessons of love. And she chose, as the manner of her leaving, a death at the hands of one she loved, that she might learn the greatest lesson of all, which is forgiveness.

Seeing the weight of what she had undertaken, the head angel gave her a gift to carry into the darkness, something that would remind her where she came from. The gift was song.

The angel was born into a tribal village amid drumming and chanting, and grew up as a warrior boy of the jungle. He had a younger sister, born with a body that kept her confined to the hut, and he loved her and cared for her from her first days. But the needs of the body, the demands of the tribe, the pain and confusion of earthly life pressed upon him, and slowly he began to forget where he had come from. Only in dreams did he remember the singing.

One night the dream was so vivid that he woke feeling he could break into song. He began to sing alone, where none could hear, afraid he would not be accepted. But his little sister heard him, and it brought her joy, and she begged him to sing with her. Together they stood in the middle of the village and let out their souls, and one by one the people stopped to listen, and soon the whole village was clapping and laughing with the two children.

When they asked him where he had learned the song, he said he did not know, only that it was his song, and that when he sang it he felt love pouring through him, speaking of healing where there was poverty, of rightness and goodness.

But sorrow came. His sister died, and the tribe blamed his song for her death. His parents turned from him. Believing he had failed completely, the boy walked alone into the jungle, and came at last to a great river he had never seen. There, hoping that nature would decide his fate, he waded in and let the current take him, no longer feeling the love, no longer knowing how to go on.

The river did not take him. He woke on the far bank, in a settlement of strangers, people of a different color and dress, who took him in and taught him new things: reading, writing, a new life. Slowly the wish to die left him. And then, in a dream, his sister came to him, cradled him, and whispered that he must not be afraid to sing, for the gift of song was why he had come.

He began to sing again, softly at first, in the hymns of the settlement, and the fear dissolved, and the song filled the spaces where the fear had been. He sang in the streets. Others gathered and sang with him. And at last the song carried him home, back through the jungle to the village of his birth, where his mother ran to him weeping and his father followed, and they said to him, we are sorry. And he said, there is nothing to be sorry for. I love you.

Those of Laitos closed the story with a word for every listener. Each soul that comes to Earth, they said, comes from a cloud of glory. Each one donned flesh and bone because it truly wished to serve. And each one brought a song to remember who it is and why it came into the mire and the dust of Earth.

If you have forgotten your song, it is not lost. It is waiting in your dreams, in the quiet moments, in the love you have not yet stopped feeling. Believe in the song of love unknown, they said, and one day, perhaps softly at first, you will sing it again.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Thousand Colors
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a thousand colors.

In the second session of the second channeling intensive, in June of two thousand eight, the new instruments brought those of Laitos a puzzle. Each of them felt the contact differently. Some felt it strongly, some faintly, some as warmth, some as pressure. And the same person could feel it differently from one session to the next. If the source was the same, they asked, why did the experience change?

Those of Laitos answered that it could not be otherwise, and that this was by design. If every instrument felt exactly the same sensation, in exactly the same way, it would be a kind of proof. It would suggest that their energies could be measured and demonstrated, and their words would then carry authority instead of inviting faith. They prefer, they said, to be met by the heart rather than proven to the mind.

So the contact comes through each instrument the way light comes through stained glass, taking on the color of the glass it passes through. The message is one, but the feeling of it is as varied as the people who receive it. That is not a flaw in the instrument. It is the nature of the work.

They asked the new channels not to judge what came through their own words. Knowing that the intention was there, to bring the message faithfully, is all that is required. Trust, they said, that as you step into the unknown, the path will be given, the words will be given, the thoughts will be given. Trust is the whole of the instrument's part.

One instrument was struggling with exactly that, standing at the edge of the work as at the edge of a pool, wanting to dive but held back by years of hesitation. Those of Laitos honored her courage. To take the plunge is to acknowledge, in experience rather than only in thought, the validity of what you have long sensed to be true.

And then they spoke of the practice that steadies everything: meditation. Daily meditation, they said, cuts through the noise. It carries you beyond the filters of unresolved past experience. It helps you trust more, and be more fearless. It helps you hold a high intention, so that you put out a vibration that attracts the highest and best.

They gave a vivid image. Imagine yourself standing at the door of the astral plane, which is populated by all kinds of vibrations. You stand there with your intention to channel, and you want the highest and best to answer, one who will speak words of wisdom to help others evolve. You would not want the troubled and the lost to answer your call. So be faithful in meditation, and let your vibration do the choosing.

There was another question beneath the question, one the group had been circling all morning: why would the same person, with the same source, have such different experiences on different days? Those of Laitos answered simply. We are all one, they said, and all connected. Each member of the group feels the experiences of the others. The circle breathes together, and the contact moves with the breath of the whole.

So if your own inner work ever feels uneven, if some days the connection sings and other days it only whispers, do not mistake the weather for the climate. The source has not changed. The light is the same light. It is only passing through the thousand colors of being human, and each color is part of the picture.

Thank you for listening.

title: Here and Now, at Your Best
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: here and now, at your best.

In the third session of the second channeling intensive, in June of two thousand eight, a student named Carol asked those of Laitos a deceptively simple question: how can I make the highest and best that I am, higher and better? Their answer began by dissolving the question itself.

The state of being highest and best, they said, is not only unique to each channel, but within one channel's experience, unique to the moment. A sign of spiritual maturity is a certain steadiness of vibration, the way you characteristically meet life. Yet even the most mature person rises and falls with the events of an ordinary day in third density. There is no fixed summit. There is only this moment's best.

Whatever your everyday tuning may be, they said, it will sit closer to your highest and best if you tune before you open yourself to serve. The desire to serve as an instrument, to offer your finest, is the foundation stone of the whole practice.

They offered the image of a flame. A flame grows brighter and larger when you feed it wood and air, and so the fire of a channeler grows brighter when it is fed by the substance of lived experience. But they added a caution worth keeping: the idea of better and more better is meaningless. There is only what is. Every word spoken in faith, with purity of heart, is already perfect.

Then came the image this episode is named for, though the name is ours. An instrument pictured himself standing at home beside a stepladder, while his little granddaughter climbed above his head and cried out, I am taller than you. And in a sense she was right, but in another sense she was up in the air, with no ground beneath her.

The lesson, those of Laitos said, is that to be truly tall you must also be grounded. It is like the oak tree: the deeper it goes into the earth, the higher it reaches into the sky. And the oak at every point is a perfect oak. So attend not only to rising high but to rooting deep in the lower centers, for it is from there that the energy flows upward, and development becomes balanced and steady.

There was one more teaching, and it may be the most practical of all. Tuning to your highest and best includes an element of fire, the fire of passion, and that fire must be alive today, not remembered from yesterday. It is easy, especially for the experienced, to move through the form of a practice and forget the flame.

Perhaps yesterday a certain prayer lifted you to the heights and set your heart ablaze. Perhaps today it falls flat. Do not push forward on yesterday's fuel. Wait until you have found the prayer that works today, the invocation that lifts you today, the song or image that stirs you today. Your energies are in constant motion, brightening and dimming, quickening and slowing, and your tuning must meet them where they are.

The simple version, they said, is this: be clear and pure in your intention. Offer yourself faithfully and without reservation. Practice, and practice, and practice, in the company of those of like mind and heart. And most of all, love: love yourself, love what the Creator shows you, and find within yourself the deep well of connection between you and the Creator, and through the Creator, all things.

Perfection, they reminded the circle, is an ever-moving goal, never fully reached in this density. But here and now, at your best, is always within reach. It is not somewhere ahead of you. It is the ground beneath your feet and the flame in your chest, meeting in this one unrepeatable moment.

Thank you for listening.

title: Testing the Contact
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: testing the contact.

In the fourth session of the second channeling intensive, in June of two thousand eight, those of Laitos took up the subject the students had been circling all weekend: the discerning of spirits. When something speaks in your meditation, how do you know who is speaking?

Their first answer was direct. Challenge it. Offer a challenge in the name of love, and if the entity meets the challenge, then ask what manner of being it is. The challenge is not rudeness; it is the last piece of the process by which you qualify a contact, and once a contact has passed it, you can rest assured you are speaking with what you called forth.

But the deeper teaching was about the two great sources of inner guidance, and how they differ. Your higher self is personal to you. It is you, at a higher level of your own being, concerned with your welfare both spiritual and everyday. It can speak to the choices of your relationships, your work, your daily life.

Those of the Confederation, they said, are not personal in the same way. They pool the knowledge of many, which gives them a broader and more varied viewpoint, but their emphasis is on the principles of the spiritual realms, not on how you should handle the details of your Tuesday. There is, they said, a division of labor here, though all is one and the line is not sharp. And there is no competition between the two. Each has its gift.

Learning to tell them apart, they said, is a matter of vibrational recognition. Each source has its own subtle character, its own feel in the energy body, its own flavor in the information it brings. At first this is difficult, because you are used to recognizing things with your physical senses. But with practice you learn the subtleties, the way you recognize family members by their step before you ever see their faces.

One instrument described sitting with her higher self until the communication took on its own unmistakable essence, a kind of simplicity and joy. Once you know a source that well, through repetition and discernment, it becomes far easier to tell when some other thought has wandered in from elsewhere.

And yet, those of Laitos added, there is a point where the question matters less than you think. When you have tuned your instrument, set your intention clearly for contact with those of the Confederation, and challenged what comes, then you have already set the conditions. You need not spend the session anxiously auditing every sentence for its author.

What remains is the chatter of the conscious mind: the doubts, the fears, the stray thoughts that drift through as you translate energy into words. For that there is no mechanical fix. There is only the memory that the process works as you have learned it, and the willingness to keep practicing until the recognition becomes second nature.

They greeted, as they spoke, the higher selves present in the room, which they said they could see in varying and brilliant colors. It is a lovely image to carry into your own quiet time: that whenever you sit down to listen, you are not alone in the room. Your wisest self is already there, in living color, waiting for you to learn its voice.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Strait and Narrow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the strait and narrow.

On a Saturday in September of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo were asked about an old biblical phrase, the strait and narrow path, and what it asks of the seeker. Their answer may surprise you, for they refused to make it a path of rigidity. They made it a path of focus.

They began with the day-to-day. All of your ordinary duties, they said, are blessed and sacred. Every single one is a small world, and any single chore can be given one hundred percent of the love within you, until it shines as an offering to the one Creator.

The key that turns a life into a sacred journey, they said, is gratitude. No matter whether what faces you looks like a blessing or a challenge, what lies before you is the perfect gift for this moment, containing your service and your learning. It is wisdom to pause a few seconds before a difficult task, open the heart, and remember how grateful you are simply to be alive and facing this moment.

Then they turned to the paradox of the strait and narrow. The instrument through whom they spoke would not give herself high marks for walking a narrow path in the worldly sense. She valued the light touch. She could be careless with details. And yet, they said, beneath the surface activity of every seeker there is an inner room, a Holy of Holies, an inner sanctuary that drives the life and steadies its reactions.

This instrument, they said, cannot stray far from that inner room, no matter what is happening on the surface. And that is where the strait and narrow shows itself. It is not in the perfection of the outer behavior. It is in the depth of the inner dwelling. It informs the carelessness of the surface with the gift of love.

Each of you, they said, is called again and again to that inner room, yearning for the touch of the Creator's hand, for the cloak of divine love. And there are times when the strait and narrow expresses itself as nothing more than the desire to crawl into the lap of the divine, home at last, resting against the heart of God and hearing its beat: love, love, love.

What does this path ask of one who wishes to enter the gates of intelligent infinity? To go deeper, they said. It is not self-indulgent to take your practice seriously, to value your time differently and yourself differently than before. The requirement is a focus that accepts the discipline of the personality with joy, and moves with light feet into an attitude of living that is always aware of the vital inner space, the nest from which the true self emerges to live what looks like an ordinary day but is in fact enchanted.

As the focus stays single, they said, you stop trying to make sense of everything. You are content to behold things and to find ways to respond to them with love. Life speaks, in the old phrase, to those who have ears to hear, and it speaks with an ever sacred and always relevant voice.

They closed with a teaching about undefendedness. It is the work of a lifetime, they said, to become undefended and to feel comfortable without the customary armor. Yet it is exactly this lack of defenses that lets infinity come close. Again and again, in the experience of the instrument, the infinite had slipped in and taken over a moment, an hour, a day, simply because the door was open.

So the strait and narrow is not a tightrope for the perfect. It is a narrowness of focus, a dwelling in the inner room, a willingness to meet the day undefended. Walk it with a light touch, and the ordinary becomes the enchanted.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Merciful Veil
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the merciful veil.

On a Saturday in late September of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo were asked one of the great questions of the spiritual life: why do we forget? Why must we walk through this life with no memory of where we came from, and no map of where we are going? Their answer was that the forgetting is a mercy.

The veil of forgetting exists, they said, because it is only within the innocence of unknowing that you can choose your path in utter free will. There have been worlds where third-density beings remembered more of the grand scheme of things, and those worlds tended to be inefficient at the great choice, for when you know how the story ends, there is a temptation to take it easy, to loaf through the life without ever making the hard ethical choices.

But when the veil drops and you are isolated within your own mind, you know that your choices will make all the difference. The process by which you come to know yourself is then innocent of every influence but your own. In third density, they said, each day is a new day, and each choice is the beginning of a new life. That is a precious characteristic of life within the veil.

Then came the second half of the question: what survives? What lasts past the physical incarnation? And here their answer was both humbling and beautiful. Your personality does not last, they said. But your essence lasts.

Through the slow, hard-won work of a lifetime, you make changes in the balance with which you look at life. You widen and deepen your perspective. And you develop, to use their simile, a certain scent or aroma, like a flower. It is that scent of self that lasts. It is the essence that endures.

Think of what this means for the way you live. The resume of achievements, the carefully maintained image, the story you tell about who you are: all of that is costume, and it will be laid aside. What remains is quieter and more real: the widened perspective, the deepened compassion, the aroma of a soul that has learned to love a little more purely than before.

They were asked, too, about the limits of this unknowing, about strange states of mind and whether they echo other lives. They answered with care, noting that in many cases the present life, with its wounds and its pressures, is more than enough to shape the mind, and that each case must be weighed on its own. The teaching held steady: honor the life you are in, for it is the life that is shaping your essence now.

At the close of this session, the contact identified itself more particularly as Hatonn, speaking as one aspect of the great Q'uo principle, a reminder that the voices of the Confederation are many, and the unity behind them is one.

So the veil is not a punishment and not a mistake. It is the condition that makes your choosing real. And your choosing, choice by choice, day by day, is distilling something in you that no forgetting can touch. Long after the personality has fallen away like a finished garment, the essence remains: the scent of the flower, the part of you that learned, in the dark of unknowing, how to love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Chew It Thoroughly
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: chew it thoroughly.

On a Saturday in October of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo took up a question about catalyst, about the flood of experience that pours through our senses every day, and they compared it to food. The comparison was deliberate, and they chewed it, if you will, very thoroughly.

There is food for the physical body, they said, and there is food for the energy body. And just as a thoughtful person chooses what to eat and drink, so there is a great deal you can do with the waves of experience that flood your senses and emotions hour by hour.

First, consider the moment a new catalyst arrives. Suddenly you are asked to take a big bite of something new: a new thought, a sharp exchange with another person, a conversation with yourself that turns in an unexpected direction. Suddenly you are chewing over a new idea, a new emotion, a new impulse.

The phrase chewing over was chosen on purpose. Just as you chew your food until it begins to break down, promoting digestion, so when something triggers your emotions and tempts you toward an impulsive reaction, it is skillful, spiritually speaking, to refrain from the immediate response and instead chew the trigger over in your mind.

Perhaps the trigger is an old friend, one you recognize from past catalyst. Take a moment to contemplate it. Honor the emotional process it has offered you. Consider whether you truly wish to follow the impulsive response, or whether it is less than your deepest and truest answer. You may find, past the pain in the trigger, a way to move beyond it into peace.

Second, remember that much of what flows into your system will flow out again, unchanged. Experience, like food, comes with husks and skins and waste parts that can do your energy body no good. It is a common mistake of the spiritual path to try to cling to every bit of experience, as if it all must mean something. The sheer volume flowing through you is astounding, and trying to hold it all can constipate the energy body. Let the husks be husks. Let them pass through.

Third, they said, food is best eaten in good company, and the same is true of experience. In the company of friends the body relaxes, the heart stays undefended, and digestion flows. So see your life as a party. If it seems you are the only guest, then light a candle, lay out a napkin, and throw a wonderful party for yourself. Find reasons to laugh. Step back and ask what the wider view might be.

There is a skill to be learned, as any habit is learned, of being good company to yourself. Watch for the thoughts in which you put yourself down, call yourself stupid, or bemoan your fate. Notice how easily the wheels of resentment can be greased. And then, in the very moment that feels hateful, look for the love in it. Look for the light in the darkness, the hope in the despairing thought. If sorrow has settled on you heavily, be gentle with yourself as you do this. Healing has its own pace, and it is far better to let your feelings move through at their own speed than to demand that they hurry.

Sometimes, they added, you will have a case of spiritual indigestion, and then it is wise to call upon your guidance, which is as near to you as your own heartbeat, and upon the helpers who wish only to be asked. And the simplest way to work with guidance is to enter the silence each day, for within the silence is the great original Thought of love, waiting for your small self to step aside.

So much of this, they said, is a matter of habit. Build the habits of contemplation and meditation, of lightheartedness and balance, and you will have a very good meal of life. Take small bites. Chew well. Keep what nourishes you, release the rest, and enjoy the feast.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Robe You Wear
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the robe you wear.

On a Saturday in late October of two thousand eight, those of Q'uo spoke about the magical personality, and about a misunderstanding that has cost many seekers a great deal of unnecessary suffering. It concerns what happens after initiation, and what does not.

They began with the pyramids, and with a detail the Ra group once shared: that the Queen's Chamber position, the high vibration an initiate assumed for priestly work, was meant to be put on like a robe and taken off like a robe, just as you would don a physical robe and hang it away when it is no longer needed.

Whenever a seeker wishes to function as a healer, a teacher, a channel, or in any way that opens the gateway to intelligent infinity, there is a time-limited nature to the donning of the magical personality. It is important, they said, to create a time-bound persona for magical work, and when the purpose has been achieved, to end the dedication consciously and carefully, and set the robe away in the innermost heart, where it can be called forth again.

With repetition, slipping into the magical personality becomes quicker, and slipping out of it becomes quicker too. But they were emphatic: attempting to hold that high pitch of intensity as a steady state is not only impossible, it is undesirable. It would erase the whole flow of the life lived, the experiences registered, the catalyst engaged, the memories and deeper emotions that only an ordinary human day can give.

Think of a judge, they said. The judge dons a heavy black robe, and by doing so signifies that for the duration of the court, there are no private interests, only the scales of justice. But the judge does not wear the robe to breakfast. The priest does not keep the vestments on at home. The robe means something precisely because it is put on and taken off.

Then they addressed the deeper confusion. What of the Buddha, one student asked, or the Christ? Did they not live in the awakened state continuously? Those of Q'uo answered gently. The energy of humanhood, they said, was part of the equation even for them. What comes down through history is the Buddha and the Christ that devotees wish to see. But ask the saints themselves, and they will tell you of the inner struggles of being human.

They mentioned one known as Mother Teresa, who wrote in her private diaries of doubting herself and despairing, even at the height of her service. Initiation creates permanent changes in the basic vibration, they said. But it is not backsliding to wake up each morning and deal with the contents of the day. Whatever the day brings cannot be entirely predicted, and meeting it is the work.

And here came the teaching this episode carries in its heart. There is something in the work ethic that says the spiritual path must be hard labor. Those of Q'uo suggested another frame entirely: take the life lightly. Let the path become play, and dance, and even romping. Where before you were worrying and striving, be relaxed and light-stepping, ready to laugh, ready to let go, and simply be.

Reframe the effort of the spiritual life as a game that is fun to play, and the sense of toil lifts away. You can enjoy every step along the King's Highway, resting in gratitude, peace, and joy. The robe is put on with reverence, and it is taken off with reverence, and between the workings, you are simply, blessedly human.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seeds in the Forest
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seeds in the forest.

On the last day of October in two thousand eight, at the opening of the third channeling intensive, those of Laitos told the new instruments a story. It begins, as the best stories do, in a dark wood.

Picture a dense forest, they said, where the trees crowd so tightly that only their crowns receive the sun. The floor of the forest is mud and dark dirt, with almost nothing growing. A woman stands in the mud, and far ahead, at the edge of her sight, there is a tiny glimmer of light. She begins to walk toward it.

She walks innocently, but with fear and doubt, alternating between the light that beckons her and her own feet, afraid of stumbling, afraid of what lies in her path. The undergrowth thickens. At times it hides the light altogether. Still, something deep within her presses her forward.

The mud is sticky and slows her steps, and she begins to wish the path would clear. Then, searching deep within, she discovers that she can call forth energy and light, and use it to lift her feet from the depths of the mud, to walk almost upon its surface. She does not yet know how to use this gift properly, but she senses that the light itself will teach her.

Alone and discouraged, she begins to see faces in the dark trees, faces that seem to tell her to turn back. Instead of surrendering to the fear, she raises her hands, and the energy running through her fingers touches the trees. The faces evaporate. She can touch the trunks and move faster, more freely, toward the light, and it is an elating experience.

At last she reaches the edge of a clearing where the light abounds and green grass beckons. But the brightness overwhelms her, and she steps back into the shade to steady herself. From that safer distance she looks across the clearing, and sees another figure standing on the far side, staring back at her. A man, who has walked his own long road through his own dark forest.

There is an electric moment as the two seekers gaze at each other, torn between moving toward one another and retreating into the trees. But the connection is stronger than the shyness, and slowly, hearts beating high, they walk toward each other in the sunlight. They touch hands in greeting, and find gentleness and goodness in each other's eyes, and their anxiety begins to dissolve.

They wonder, as they rest together, why they had to muddle through such difficulty to reach each other and the light. And those of Laitos gave the answer through the forest itself. Old trees must die and fall, they said, to make openings in the canopy, for seeds do not grow in the shadow of their parents. All things come and all things go, and the Creator moves on, perpetuating.

The two seekers had to become ready before they could meet. The struggle was the preparation. And now, having learned their lessons individually, they could become one unit, plant their own seeds together, tend them together, and move on, dropping seeds wherever they go.

Those of Laitos closed with a word for the circle. Each of you, they said, has traveled paths that brought you where you need to be right now. You have had to let things go, and you have had to learn new things. And wherever you go from here, you will drop your seeds.

If your own path feels like mud and shadow today, remember the woman in the forest. The light you are walking toward is real, even when the undergrowth hides it. And the difficulty is not a detour from your journey. It is the journey, preparing you for the meeting that waits in the clearing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Blown Circuit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the blown circuit.

In the second session of the third channeling intensive, on the last day of October in two thousand eight, those of Laitos spoke to the fear that haunts every new channel: the fear of failing. And they began by naming it plainly.

It is very frequently the case, they said, that the new instrument will feel it has failed, and will carry that sense of failure out of the session and into discouragement. This, they said, is not a good use of the faculty of judgment. Judgment is a fine tool for discernment, for finding your direction. Turned back upon the self, it becomes a very harsh master.

For everyone gathered in that circle held some idea of perfection in the service they were attempting, and measured against such a standard, every effort falls short. But those of Laitos offered another measure entirely. The importance of your attempt at service, they said, lies primarily in the intent. When you open the heart with sincere desire to serve, there is in a sense no possibility of failure.

They encouraged the lighter touch, the gentler hand in treating yourself, the same gentleness you would offer anyone you were trying to help. When a perceived failure occurs, they said, let every thought of the self be one of nurture and encouragement. Channeling is as much an art as a craft, and there is tremendous help available to the channel who refuses discouragement and returns with undaunted enthusiasm.

They spoke, too, of what happens energetically when things go wrong. Sometimes, in the middle of a session, the contact simply stops, as if a circuit has blown. One instrument experienced exactly this, and feared it meant something was broken. Those of Laitos reassured him: when a circuit is blown, it must be reset, and there is a period of time, unique to each person, that is needed to become centered and focused again.

The contact, they said, is really a kind of electricity, the closing of a gap between one portion of the Creator and another. So retuning after a blown circuit is not a sign of inadequacy. It is part of the work. Each time you sit in the circle, you are gaining experience, and each blown circuit is an opportunity to practice the retuning, until you are once again one-pointed, open, and transparent to what is coming.

They offered one more practice for the inner life, and it applies far beyond channeling. Take any emotion that troubles you, impatience, for example. Move into it without judgment. Feel it fully, even intensify it. Then, by an act of will, ask the coin to flip, and feel its dynamic opposite, patience, with the same intensity. Every emotion sits across the circle of the self from its opposite, like two sides of one coin.

The result is not the erasing of the difficult feeling but an enhanced knowledge of what you are working on, and a growing fullness of awareness of yourself as a living, real being. Beneath the many roles you play, there is a basic, authentic self that underlies them all, and this practice helps you find your way back to it.

So if you have ever walked away from something that mattered to you feeling that you failed, hear this session as it was meant. The intent was the offering, and the offering was enough. Reset the circuit. Retune with a gentle hand. And try again, not because you must be perfect, but because you are willing.

Thank you for listening.

title: Here Am I
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: here am I.

On the first of November in two thousand eight, in the third session of the third channeling intensive, those of Laitos took up a subject every new instrument knows intimately: anticipation. The flutter before the contact, the wondering what will come, the tangle of hoping and fearing at once.

They began with reassurance. A degree of anticipation is healthy and normal, they said.
