Ask for help. They remind us that guidance operates on free will and will not intrude uninvited. Ask, and the help that has been waiting will come. The angels, the guides, whatever you call them, are bound by your invitation. So invite them.

And gather with others. When seekers come together, they say, the light compounds. One plus one is not two but something exponential, a lighthouse growing brighter with every heart added.

In the questions that followed, they spoke of sacred places on Earth, nodes of concentrated energy, and how even one person meditating in harmony with such a place can help it radiate more light. And they spoke to a mother-to-be about the soul entering the womb, encouraging her to converse with the spirit within as an equal. Everywhere, the same message. You are already in the dance. Just dance.

So as you look toward whatever future you are preparing for, remember the stained glass. You do not need to become the light. You need only to let it through, in your colors, in your way.

You are ready. You were always ready. Shine.

Thank you for listening.

title: Bending the Knee
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: bending the knee.

Tonight's teaching takes on one of the most misunderstood words in the spiritual vocabulary. Humility. And the first thing they do is rescue it from its reputation.

Among us, humility has come to mean thinking poorly of yourself. Low self-worth in a halo. The art of making yourself small. But they say this is not humility at all. It is a distortion, and a painful one.

True humility, they suggest, has nothing to do with self-abasement. It is the natural result of knowing who you actually are. And here is the paradox they want us to hold. The more deeply you know yourself, the more humble you become, not because you discover how worthless you are, but because you discover how precious.

Listen to how they put it. When the small self, the ego with all its posturing, becomes transparent before the power of unconditional love flowing through it, what remains is not humiliation but awe. You realize you are an instrument, and the music moving through you is infinitely greater than the wood and strings.

I love their image for this. Think of someone bending the knee to propose marriage. That is not the posture of a person who feels worthless. It is the posture of a person overwhelmed by the privilege of love, by the sheer wonder of being allowed to share a life. That, they say, is what humility before the infinite feels like. Not I am nothing, but I can barely fathom that I get to be part of this.

They are honest about the timing of all this. Early in the seeking, they suggest, humility is not even the right goal. The beginner needs persistence, determination, the sheer bloody-mindedness to keep going through the dark night when nothing makes sense. Humility comes later, when the first victories arrive and with them the great temptation.

And what is that temptation? Pride. The quiet thought that you did this yourself. The sense of entitlement, the feeling that the universe owes the sincere seeker a smooth road. When those thoughts flash through the mind, they say, that is the moment to invoke humility. Not as punishment, but as correction. You are the instrument, not the composer.

They warn that no one is ever finished with this. Pride can return in any moment, wearing subtler disguises each time. The advanced seeker is not the one who has conquered pride forever. It is the one who notices sooner when it has crept back in.

There is a practical consequence they emphasize. People hear more than your words. They hear the energy carrying your words. Service offered with true humility lands differently than the same words offered with arrogance. The teaching is not just in what you say. It is in the transparency of the one saying it.

In the questions that followed, they were asked about the transmutation of sexual energy into the energy of the open heart, and they spoke of intention, of the slow work of moving from possession to communion, offered, as always, as a perspective to consider rather than a rule to obey.

They were asked about a moment of collective joy, a presidential inauguration that had opened the heart of a nation, and they described it as a genuine planetary opening, a memory of unity retained in the heart of humankind, available to be recalled and invoked whenever we choose.

And they were asked about the warming of the Earth, and they offered the view that beneath the physical mechanisms lies a spiritual dimension, the heat of humanity's unresolved aggression pressed down into the planet, answerable, they suggested, by the opposite energies of cooperation and love. Take it as their perspective, offered with humility, and consider what resonates.

So tonight, bend the knee. Not in shame, but in wonder. You are an instrument of incalculable worth, and the music wants to play through you.

Stay in tune. Stay transparent. And let the Beloved do the playing.

Thank you for listening.

title: Spiraling into Truth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: spiraling into truth.

One Saturday evening in May, a questioner put a question to Q'uo that every long-time seeker knows by heart. At the start of the journey, he said, you expect it to get easier. Instead, the further you go, the harder it seems to get. Like a muscle that needs heavier weights, maybe the soul just needs heavier work. Is that true? And is it especially true for wanderers?

I love the honesty of the answer. Q'uo begins by saying yes, it often seems that way. And then they gently set the metaphor aside. It is not that the weights get heavier. Something else is happening, and to see it you have to picture your path differently.

Before this incarnation, they say, you and your guidance gazed at your soul stream, at its balances of power, love and wisdom, and you devised an incarnation rich in catalyst. You chose relationships that would challenge you and support you. Redundancy was built into the plan. Far more relationships than you would ever need, so that if you kept backing away from a situation that carried your lesson, another would appear, sounding the same theme, offering the same chance to adjust the balances within your energy body.

At first you work at the surface of the lesson. Gradually you begin to recognize the pattern, and that recognition is a blessing, because when you see the pattern the fear lessens. There is no more freezing. You take up the challenge and move into it gladly, like a warrior of light. There is the first dark night of the soul, and then the first dawn.

Listen to how they picture what comes next. Do not picture your path as a straight line going forward. Picture it as a spiral going upward, because each time you work with your lesson you have walked further into the light. And picture it as a spiral going inward at the same time, as if you were peeling the layers of an onion, moving one layer closer to the center of your incarnational lesson.

The center remains a mystery. But the closer you move to it, the clearer the colors become and the more intense and true the energies. You have earned authenticity, and in your authenticity you grapple far more intimately with the question of balance. That is the increased difficulty you are feeling. Not heavier weights. Greater closeness to the goal.

Then comes the line I keep returning to. You are not building a stairway to heaven, they say. You are spiraling into the light of truth. As you go, you are learning to love yourself and others and the Creator. You are learning to accept love from yourself, from others, and from the Creator. You are learning to be.

And what about wanderers, those who came from elsewhere to be of service here? Q'uo says yes, there is a strong tendency for wanderers to task themselves with more to learn and more to share. Knowing more, they and their guidance load the incarnational lesson plan with more lessons and more ways of serving. And many wanderers carry a memory, specific or vague, of how energy runs in a more refined system, so there is a hunger for that ease, that comfort of living within the open heart at all times.

They describe what happens next with real tenderness. There is often, they say, an unintentional pride before incarnation, the feeling of, of course I shall remember, how could I forget the way things really are? Then the veil drops, and here you are, mired first in the noisy, cranky chemical distillery you call your body, unable to remember why things seem so different, unable with your physical senses to see beyond the veil.

As an example they point to their own instrument, whose incarnational lesson was loving without expectation of return. It took her many years and many relationships to notice that there was always someone in her life who required loving and was not capable of loving in return. Recognizing the pattern made it easier in one way. She could don her armor of light, as they put it, affix the ribbons to her lance, and set out. In another way it became ever more subtle and ever more intense, because she was spiraling closer and closer to the center of the lesson. And the end of that lesson, they say, is learning to love the self.

It helps, they suggest, to think of your life as a game. You are here to love. The rules are simple. In each challenging piece of catalyst there is that thread of truth. I am here to love. I am here to trust. I am here to gain the insight that all is well. Oh, you may think, this is an excellent piece of catalyst. What a good game.

And as always, they end by recommending the silence. Enter the tabernacle of your heart and close the door, if only for a few minutes each day, so that you may listen. For that which is too deep for words shall empower you, if you but ask, if you but listen.

So if the path feels harder than it did a year ago, maybe you are not failing. Maybe you are simply nearer the center. The spirals are coalescing. Keep going.

Thank you for listening.

title: When the Light Hurts
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: when the light hurts.

In late May, the question put to Q'uo was a difficult one. Why are so many people, wanderers and natives alike, struggling with mental imbalance in these times? The questioner wondered whether the incoming vibrations of fourth density were part of it, and what the spiritual principles behind such suffering might be.

This is an episode to receive gently. What follows is spiritual reflection, not medical guidance. If you are living with mental illness or deep distress, please also lean on the human help available to you. The archive speaks to the soul, and the soul sometimes needs a companion in the room.

Q'uo begins with the human animal, that combination of mind, body and spirit. Your third density, they say, is the density of choice. Everything in it is arranged to shake a complacent person out of complacency, not simply to hand you suffering, but to set the stage for the great choice of polarity on which the next densities are built.

Beneath the surface changes of your energy body, they say, there is a deeper vibration, a basic signature as distinct as any fingerprint. And spiritual evolution, in a way, is the long work of reducing the difference between your vibration and the vibration of the one infinite Creator, whose nature is unconditional and absolute love.

Wanderers feel this friction keenly. When an entity comes into third density from another density to serve at the time of harvest, echoes of the home density remain within the incarnational self. It is like moving to a completely foreign country and losing your memory. Over the years you get used to the new land, you even feel you belong. Yet underneath there is a stubborn, hidden awareness that there is another way to be.

That feeling of being isolated in a strange land can create fear and contraction. The self becomes defended in order to survive. And the more the energy body contracts in fear, the less energy moves through the lower centers into the heart, and the less able the entity is to cope. It becomes self-perpetuating.

But listen to what Q'uo says their hope is in speaking of this. Not to excuse wanderers, and not to justify their difficulties. Their hope is to bring wanderers to remembrance. The key to becoming unafraid and undefended is the memory of why the decision was made, in good faith and with a happy heart, to come among those of third density at this time. The decision was made in an atmosphere of absolute compassion. There was in fact competition for opportunities to incarnate.

Then they turn to something larger, something affecting everyone on the planet. You are close to the onset of your planet's fourth-density activation, they say, and third-density light is being interpenetrated by fourth-density light. The metaphysical atmosphere is changing, and a third-density energy body is not wired to receive fourth-density light without significant distortion.

Here is the part that stays with me. Because of this new light, it has become almost impossible to avoid looking at every unintegrated part of yourself. For those on the positive path there has never been much desire to investigate the shadow side, the robber, the murderer, the envier, the one eaten with greed. Yet the mark of a spiritually mature entity is that he has faced his shadow side, embraced it, forgiven it, and asked it to work toward the good.

These awarenesses arrive harshly, they say, too harsh to bear at first, because the wiring is not ready. That is why this is such a challenging time, and also such a fruitful one. You have, in your very being, the chance to offer a location and a place that is love.

What do they recommend? Compassion, first, upon yourself and upon those around you. This is not a time that offers the easy, the comfortable, the pretty ways of experiencing your sacred nature.

Then two resources. The world of nature, which lies all about you as a vast and largely untapped resource. All within the natural world is in a state of love for you, and your very bones, in their instinctual life, have an answering love for the environment and like nothing better than to dance in rhythm with all of creation. Immerse yourself in it.

And your guidance system. Your higher self, which is as close to you as your next thought. Angelic help. For wanderers, the aid of the social memory complex from which they came. It is the wise seeker who turns in thought to thanksgiving for this help and to the asking of it, for it is truly said that it is to those who ask that response is given.

They close with a line to carry. Beyond the wheres and the whys there is love. Seek love. Open yourself to love. Let yourself be loved. As you go deeper into your nature, do not be afraid of what you shall find. The deeper you go into your personality, the less personal it shall become, and the more loving.

Thank you for listening.

title: Worth in Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: worth in being.

In late May, during a channeling intensive for new students, the question put to Laitos was a tender one. How do we balance low self-worth? The students wanted to know how the mirroring effect works, and how a channel could keep the distortion of low self-worth from affecting the channeling.

Take this one slowly too. Feelings of low worth run deep in almost everyone, and this session looks straight at them. Nothing here is a substitute for the human support you may need. It is simply a different light to sit in for a while.

Laitos begins with something almost too simple to notice. There is no entity on your planet, they say, who reaches physical adulthood without retaining feelings of low self-worth. The reasons are many, but most often they center on voices from early childhood, the voices of parents, teachers, authority figures, telling the young soul that he is not worthy. And what should the child believe but the voice of the beloved? The undefended young soul takes it in.

Then comes the turn I love. If you inquire into the nature of the self that may or may not be felt worthy, begin with being. One is. Before the self can do, it must first be, and in its beingness resides its inalienable worthiness.

It sounds obvious. Your grammar itself says it. Before there can be a doing, must there not be that which performs the action? And yet in your actual experience, attention slides past being to doing. You take yourself to be something you have done, not something that enjoys the native virtue of its own beingness. The first self you take yourself to be is the self that has performed, accomplished, created.

And with respect to any doing, there is that which is done better and that which is done worse. Measured against other possible doings, your first attempts will fall short and be judged unworthy. Measure the accomplished self against the self which is being, and the accomplished self will always fall short. So to the extent that you move your attention from the self grounded in beingness to a self that is your own creation, however accomplished, you will carry a lingering dissatisfaction. That is part and parcel of creating a self, as each of you has had to learn to do.

Two elements, they say, are vital in recovering from low self-worth. Forgiveness and gratitude.

Then they take up the mirroring effect, in the language of the chakras. This is orange-ray work, the energy center of the self in relation to other selves. Mirroring can happen between you and another person. If you are working on low self-worth and you meet someone who seems to have the opposite, an overly inflated pride, that person can be your mirror. Peel back the layers of that onion, take on those concepts as though they were your own, work through them fully, and you begin to understand your own distortion. For others, the pattern runs the other way. Low self-worth becomes defended and defensive, and a false pride grows as a mask over the face of low worth. Seeing pride in another can help there too.

Whatever the pattern, the mirroring effect is most helpful in bringing grist to the mill of spiritual work.

But there is a subtler teaching here. You can also mirror self to self, the low self reflecting the low self, and that mirroring is distorted, because neither side is informed by your true nature. The healing begins when you return to the feeling of lowness and embrace it, accept it, love it, and allow it to be part of the self that is not separate from others, not separate from the one infinite Creator.

Out of that comes what they call true or genuine humility, which is very closely associated with true or genuine self-worth. Not the humility that has been humiliated and scrambles to compensate, to triumph over the conditions of its humiliation. A humility that has nothing to prove, nothing to overcome, nothing to establish in relation to others so that it can be worthy. In that humility, the fledgling self stands in right relation to the crowned self, and that first act of self-worth is paradoxically given the name of humility.

There is practical advice as well. Prayer and intention. They describe simple prayers, first stating the desired condition, then releasing the words. Intention set before channeling steadies the chakras, crystallizing them into harmony for the session, even though daily life will bump and bruise them again afterward. And that is allowed. You do the work, you redo it, day after day.

The closing summary gathers it all. The feelings of low self-worth are nearly universal, because the veil of third density hides your true nature from you, and the self is error-prone. No argument with your parents' old verdicts will fix that. But moving into the open heart, you rest for the first time in an atmosphere wide enough to identify the self with the one infinite Creator, with unconditional love, with being. Resting in that beingness of love, the work of restoring true worth can take place.

Moving into the open heart again and again, they say, there is a safe and protected environment to do that work of becoming, of being. Again and again. That repetition is not failure. It is the practice.

Thank you for listening.

title: Always a Channel
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: always a channel.

The second session of that same May intensive took up a beautiful question. What are the spiritual principles involved in being a battery for the channels in a channeling circle? When you are not the one speaking, how may you serve the circle best by the way you think and the way you are?

Laitos begins by dissolving the distinction the question assumes. Between the times you are acting as a vocal channel, or when you have chosen to sit in the circle without speaking, you are still a channel. You are simply not opening your mouth and vibrating your vocal cords at all times.

There is never a time in your incarnation that you are not a channel, they say. There are only gradients of channeling. Your chakras are functioning, you breathe in the life force of the Creator and communicate the life of the Creator. Even the darkest soul on your planet, even a newborn babe struggling to stay alive, is a channel of the universal light within all creation.

Those who are unaware of their spiritual nature are not aware of the energies flowing through them, and often the love and light are constricted in them. As one grows in awareness, one can open the pathways of the spirit body and become a greater conduit, allowing more to flow through in greater capacity. I love that image, the self as a widening channel.

To be a battery in the circle means you have lent yourself in service to the light. You have said, I am here, use me. You have prepared a pathway for the light to travel, so that the light coming in from the universe travels freely through your being and back out into the universe, exchanged between the members of the group. You each lend your energy to the others.

If each of you in the circle were a note, they say, the combined song of the circle would be a chord, a chord of harmony and beauty, flowing and vibrating together in such a way that it creates a sacred space in which the seeking of truth shall be pursued.

The activity of those listening is not passive. That is a mistaken concept. By your very being you are vibrating at a certain frequency, and that frequency pours into the group frequency to help create it. Every group is unique, even with the same members at another time, because each of you carries an ongoing flow of events that alters your vibration from hour to hour and from day to day.

The nature of the aid of a battery, they say, is that of the lover, the protector, the guardian. It is effective simply to project your love and your thanksgiving for the entity who is channeling, to dwell on the perfection of that entity's service, to give thanks for all the unseen help that protects the circle and to give thanks to the circle itself, for it is a group being of its own.

Rather than visualization, this way of being a battery is a way of being a living prayer. A direct opening of the heart in love and appreciation and thanksgiving and praise.

There is practical guidance too. To raise the vibration of your consciousness, look to a life that modeled it. They point to Jesus the Christ, who studied, who went apart to spend quiet time in contemplation, who did good works, who spent time in prayer. Even in his dark night in the garden, he prayed. A battery is not made by announcement. It comes out of your own personal desire for the evolution of your soul.

And a small daily practice. Choose someone you consider a highly evolved spiritual being. Spend five minutes each day in meditation imagining that being sitting with you. Then imagine the two of you going together to the circle, lending their consciousness as you lend yours.

The sum of it all, as one of the newer channels voiced it, is simple. The single most important contribution of one who functions as a member of a group is a quality of beingness that we may call love. Love is not something one simply feels. It is a palpable energy which one channels.

Even such a small group as this can be so powerful, they say. And we can assure you that as listeners in the heavens we ourselves feel greatly called to respond, even if only by silently blending our harmonious intentions with those of the group.

You do not have to speak to serve the circle. You only have to be the note you are, and let the chord form.

Thank you for listening.

title: Joy over Happiness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: joy over happiness.

The third session of the May intensive asked Laitos a question everyone has asked in the dark at some point. How do we determine what we are to do with our life? How do we find the confidence to do it? And when it does not work out very well, what do we do then?

Laitos answers with unusual gentleness. The purpose of a life, they say, is something every seeker must reach for, and it is well to dedicate yourself to it. And yet life is a process of unceasing discovery, and again and again the purpose will need to be reconceived. Sometimes that means the abandonment of plan after plan. Sometimes it is only a refinement.

When a plan proves unsustainable, the temptation is to harden the goal and judge yourself. You look back on your days and see shortcoming, failure, lack. But that approach only compounds the difficulty, they say, because now you carry not only the lack but the guilt about the lack. These judgments are not salubrious to spiritual development. That is a careful, clinical word for something simple. Judging yourself does not help you grow.

So how do you pursue a path without the judgments becoming a stumbling block? Laitos turns to the difference between happiness and joy, and this is the heart of the session.

You often hear the advice, do what makes you happy. It is not inappropriate advice, they say, and yet it misses the mark. Happiness comes and goes. Joy is deeper.

They offer two lives as examples. When their instrument was a young woman, her joy was in promising to serve another in the bonds of marriage, and she found joy in keeping that promise. When the marriage dissolved at the request of the other, it could be said the joy ran out. But that is not so, for the promise had been kept, and the promise, now dissolved, allowed the beloved to be free. She kept making promises and finding joy in the keeping of them, and almost incidentally, the path of service opened and blossomed through decades.

The other example is the one known as Jim, who was as happy as a man can be dwelling in a house made by his own hands, eating food prepared and harvested and preserved by those hands. His own company made him happy. His thoughts, faithfully recorded, fulfilled him. And yet he turned from happiness, because his joy was in service, and he felt he must go deeper and collaborate with comrades in service. Is he happy now as a gardener instead of a homesteader? Happiness comes and goes, they say, and yet his joy is complete, for he has found a service that pursues a purpose greater than any he had conceived before.

Do not discount happiness, they advise, but look for joy and cherish it when found. Where there is joy, there is service already. In that experience of joy, there is service to the one infinite Creator in the fulfilling of your deepest being.

The path, they add, is not a straight line. It is a long and winding road, and it faithfully leads to the door of that which is for you. They tell of a violinist, a young man who soared to first chair in his orchestra and then watched his body break down under the discipline of his art, his wrists and arms sickening with pain. He came to their instrument in despair, asking what to do.

Her advice to him was to look for the opportunity hidden within the folds of this seeming failure, and to seek in prayer the will of the infinite Creator. Within ten days he was invited to teach at a highly regarded conservatory of music. He accepted, and found a life's service that gives him deep joy. He still pursues it.

When a seeming failure occurs in one who wishes to serve, lift away from the worry and the question of why. There is no information on the blank wall at the end of a blind alley. Turn around. Release the desire that has failed, and find again your deepest desire, which is simply to serve. Let that intention set itself upon the wind, that it may draw to you the next path that shall move you from being to doing.

And here is a sentence worth sitting with. It is never a good assumption that your path of service consists primarily in doing. You may well have chosen before incarnation a path of service that is fundamentally that of holding the light, and that is a service offered in essence and in beingness.

He who thinks only of the destination misses the pleasure of the journey, they quote, and they describe a bus trip their instrument once took, strangers talking heart to heart in the middle of the night, singing together to a traveler's harmonica. Had she been asleep, she would have missed it all. Be awake to the pleasure that is there for you as you travel.

Nothing you prepare is ever lost. You may not see the fruition until you are off the stage of this incarnation, but fruition will come. Skills you built for one destination get called upon in another. Rest assured that what you ask for, in prayer for the highest good, you shall receive.

So if the plan has collapsed, do not ask first what went wrong. Ask where the joy was. Follow that. It was the compass all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: Gentle as Dew
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: gentle as dew.

The final session of the May intensive was devoted to a single word. Grace. Laitos opened by noting how many shades the word carries in your language, and how all of them share one fundamental essence, which they would try to tease out as the contact moved around the circle.

The facet they begin with is dynamic beauty. When someone says beauty, static images come to mind. Grace, they say, is a dynamic expression of beauty. It is the expression of one who is serving, or being, in an acutely balanced manner. It is a sign that one is moving in a very balanced and efficacious way.

Grace is holy, the next voice continues. All things on your planet are holy. All things are beautiful in their own way. Grace is the expression of the beauty in holiness as one moves about one's daily activities. It incorporates into those dynamic activities the knowledge of the truths in the heart that say, this is holy. One moves from a simple activity into grace in that activity. It is a merging of one's self with that of the Creator.

Then a harder teaching, for the troubled seeker. As you move upon the journey of seeking the truth, you will find places on the path that are difficult to traverse, not only because of the trail but because of something within the seeker, so that you react to certain challenges in ways unique to you, in ways that seem to hinder your progress.

At the very core of grace, as the word has been used for centuries, is gratuity. A gift. And the love that gives it is unmeasured, infinite, eternal. You are knit of the same fabric of love as the one infinite Creator. You are the face, the voice, the hands and feet of the Creator in the world around you. You always have the opportunity to express this unconditional love, so that those whom you love are free, free from the fear of your judgment, free from the fear of losing your love, free to be the creatures they are.

Thusly, they say, does grace spin its light and its love from the infinite Creator through you and out into a world that hungers for that love.

Then comes the passage I will not forget. Grace is the cooking oil of the spiritual world, one channel says. When oil is spread on the bottom of the pan and the batter is placed in the pan and the pan goes into the oven, the oil enables the transformative process and keeps the cake from sticking. Grace is the axle grease of the spiritual world. On the axle it lets the wheel turn freely without hanging up. Grace is the oil squirted on the squeaky hinge. It allows things to move freely in the spiritual world and to be transformed.

It is a gift from the infinite Creator. It is the very elixir of the spiritual life. And yet, and this is the paradox they hold so carefully, it cannot be forced. It cannot be earned or hard-won by right effort. It can only come as the gentle dew rests upon the land.

I love that image because it resolves the striving. You can prepare the field. You cannot command the dew. You can live in a way that is open to grace, moving through your day with the knowledge that this is holy, and then grace arrives on its own schedule, quietly, overnight, and everything is wet with it by morning.

There is one more thread worth keeping. Grace smoothes the path of the troubled seeker. When you find yourself reacting to catalyst in the old painful ways, when progress seems hindered, that is not the absence of grace. That is the place where grace is most needed, and most available, if you will let the troubled places be met with love instead of judgment.

So the teaching of this last evening is simple enough to hold in one hand. Move through your ordinary activities as if they were holy, because they are. Love without demanding anything back. And let the dew come when it comes.

Thank you for listening.

title: Close to the Ground
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: close to the ground.

In early August, a special session was called for a very personal reason. Their instrument was about to begin writing a book on the outer work, the daily round of marriages, children, parents, work, the nitty-gritty of outer catalyst. She asked Q'uo for spiritual principles to guide the writing. What they gave her is a teaching for anyone who has ever tried to help another person through real suffering.

This one touches raw places. It speaks of despair and helplessness, and briefly of the thought of ending one's life. Take it gently, and know that its counsel is about writing and witnessing, not a substitute for care.

Q'uo begins with an observation about their instrument's lifelong habit. She attends first to the metaphysical aspects of any situation and only secondarily to the actual situation, the incoming catalyst itself. That way of thinking is excellent for maintaining a stable metaphysical tuning. It is excellent for writing about the inner work. But this book is about what happens on the ground, in the thick of incoming catalyst.

There has been, they say, a tendency in her not to respect or give full sway to the physical events that occur in the outer world, because her overwhelming tendency is to reconfigure whatever comes through the five senses into patterns of spiritual principle. Loving. Listening. Again, excellent values. But the reader who picks up a book about marriage and children and work is not living in those patterns. That reader feels out of control and helpless before the onslaught of catalyst.

They encourage her to let go of her preconceptions about outer catalyst, to step aside from the habit of observation overwhelming the immediate, keen, instantaneous reaction to catalyst as it enters awareness. It is not easy to step outside one's biases. But to compensate for the heavily metaphysical aura that overlays all physical catalyst for her, it is necessary.

Then the image that gives this episode its title. That same day she had been writing about healthy soil, about a book on growing food. When you get down close to the ground, she had written, you see all manner of life you never see standing up and walking across a meadow. Put your hands in the soil to weed a planting and you see worms, beetles, slugs, tiny crawling creatures, so many of them that it is as if they were having a party. It is those beetles and slugs and microorganisms that create the good soil in which seeds grow into healthy plants.

In just this way, they say, it is necessary in writing about the outer catalyst to lose your altitude and get close to the ground. Only when you have knelt down to the very level of the heaviest and most shadowy emotions it is possible to feel can you begin to create access to the experience of receiving outer catalyst.

The temptation, they warn, will be to solve each bit of catalyst as you go. That is putting the cart before the horse. Enter into the suffering of one who is dealing with a relationship or a difficulty at work. It is central to the integrity of the work that you move from the observer to the experience, and allow these catalysts to come into you with the force and power that is common among those upon your planet.

The principle they offer is oneness with the body, oneness with the earth, oneness with the heavy catalyst that is not diluted by wisdom or perspective. She has suffered, they remind her, in each of the ways she needs to write about. She has had the full and intense experiences. But it is difficult for her to access the uncut, raw emotions of those experiences, because her inborn gift is to move to higher ground with every fiber of her being.

That gift has advantages, and it has a cost. In recreating outer catalyst so quickly into something observed by a spiritual seeker, there is a cutting away from the bright intensity of unthinking emotional reaction. Such emotions feel to her like a closed place that makes her claustrophobic, so she breaks free of the closeness of the agony. Yet to write about the catalyst that hits a physical being in a physical world, she must investigate that loss.

You like to think of Jesus as he teaches, they tell her, or as he is lifted up into the clouds and ascending. You are not fond of thinking of him sweating blood in the garden. Spend time in that garden as you prepare.

I find that line devastating and useful. Whatever your work is, there is a garden you would rather not enter. The people you hope to serve are waiting in it.

They close with practical counsel. Pray and ask for help every time you prepare to write. Tune yourself as though for channeling. Set your intention and dedicate yourself wholly to the service you hope to offer. Then go forward with the faith that one foot in front of the other shall bring you to your goal. And move out into the world of nature, even if it is only to sit on the front porch and feel the breeze, to sense into the earth of your nature and feel yourself as fully incarnated.

The help is there. The gifts are there. What is asked is an authentic voice for those who suffer. Get close to the ground, and let the soil teach you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Three Levels of Will
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the three levels of will.

In mid-August, a questioner brought Q'uo a careful question from the Law of One material. Ra had said there is great danger in the use of the will as the personality grows stronger, because it may be used even subconsciously in ways that reduce polarity. Is the will a primal moving energy, strengthened through use like a muscle? Can desires we do not know we have take hold of it? And how do we avoid that?

Q'uo answers by describing three levels of will, one of the clearest maps in the whole archive.

The first level of will is the will that has not been accessed by any entity. It is the wind on the water. It is the movement of water as it travels from rain to aquifer to sea to air again. That free will which is the first distortion has no subject. It has no object. It is pure verb.

The second level is the personal will, the will that creates and then enjoys maintaining preferences. What shall you have for breakfast? What book would you prefer to read? What song would you like to hear? Where do you wish to live? All of these matters that matter only to you are matters of your personal will. And when your will meets another's will, you discover quickly that they are not the same will. but over where to live the clash of personal wills can be excruciating, placing the self in the fiery furnace that tempers souls.

The third level belongs to the disciplined personality, and its watchword is, not my will, but thine be done. The goal of one who wishes to work with the magical personality is to come into a clearer and clearer awareness of just what the will of the Creator is.

The practice is subtle. First determine to your complete satisfaction what that will is. Then, and only then, set the intention to access it and marry it to the desire of your heart. And third, create within the self the environment in which intention and desire become manifest in action.

But here is the difficulty, and they do not soften it. The seeker who tries to determine the will of the infinite One with the mind is doomed to confusion, for the mind is not geared toward truth in the spiritual sense but toward keeping the person comfortable, safe and happy. Even when the mind wishes to think on spiritual things, it reaches for masks and what looks like spiritual behavior. It is not a tool made to engage the truth that goes beyond fact and enters into essence.

Therefore the seeker is well served by a daily practice that removes the self from the kingdom of the mind and brings it into the kingdom of the heart. Walk through the outer courtyard of the heart, gather all of your humanity, and lay it down in the inner sanctum, where there is surcease from the ways of the world and release from the tyranny of the mind.

Then they turn to the magical personality itself. Your earthly personality is assembled with the help of your culture, your parents, your teachers, and you can remake yourself endlessly, to a point. For there are things within you deep-set, to the marrow of the bone. Blessed is the entity who decides to cooperate with those deep-set traits rather than fight them. Becoming more spiritual is not a matter of dropping the earthly persona, but of learning to call upon an impersonal faculty within the self, to lay the earthly personality aside for a time in service to others.

The desire of an entity, they say, is like a firefly, flitting from a flavor of ice cream to peace on earth to a parking place, and all desires are true in their way. But in the silence with the infinite One, the firefly of desire lands, for one infinitely short and infinitely precious moment, at a still point that opens into all of infinity and eternity.

Then comes the hunger of one who finally understands that he knows nothing, a hunger for the presence of the living Creator that can never be slaked in the world of ten thousand things. It is more precious than the fullness of all desires realized, a hunger that calls forth devotion and lives on faith. It is that hunger that fuels the work of the magician.

As you move beyond the desires of body and mind into that emptiness filled with devotion, you are becoming a powerful person, and then you must be exceedingly careful with the use of the will. An undisciplined personality rarely musters will with force behind it, but the seeker aware of his power can get lost in the maze of the self he does not yet know and harm another without intending it.

In the end, they say, all effort must be laid aside and faith invoked, for there is no end to the subtlety of the human mystery. You will keep surprising yourself with who you are. Rely most of all on faith. Faith in your good intentions, faith in the process itself, and faith in the Creator that gave you all that you need to do the work you came to do.

Thank you for listening.

title: Carrying Camelot Home
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: carrying Camelot home.

In early September, the circle gathered for its homecoming weekend, and the question they brought to Q'uo was a practical and poignant one. How do we keep this positive energy going after we each return home? How do we stay positive and share our love and light with those around us?

Q'uo begins with proximity. What is physical proximity? Obviously the nearness of one body to another. Yet each of you knows in your heart that you are fully capable of maintaining proximity and even intimacy on an energetic level, regardless of physical closeness.

They point to experiments their scientists have done with plants. A plant that had bonded with its human companion would be taken far away, instruments hooked to the skin of its leaves, and it would respond instantaneously to the companion's thoughts, positive or negative, no matter the distance. You have within your own bodies that same ability to sense, energetically, the thoughts of those you love and have been near. By simply asking yourself to become aware of those entities with whom you wish to stay in contact, you can maintain that source of support and unconditional love.

There was also a ritual of soil. Each person had been asked to bring soil to the gathering. It was blended together, and a portion given back to each. That soil could be kept as a reminder, a trigger for focusing upon this moment when you were supported and loved and encouraged, cradled in cherishing.

But then they step back from logic and physicality, even energetic physicality, into something larger. You have expanded into the present moment, they say. You have become a link between physicality and infinity, between one body and one name and the mystery of oneness of which you are ineluctably a part.

In this present moment you are linked not only to those around you but to your guidance system. Its foundation is your higher self, that self in mid-sixth density who has experienced all that was desired and then turned toward the Creator, leaving behind a thought form containing the harvest of all it learned, so that you may call upon your highest and best self at any time.

Many of you also carry the oversoul of the group of entities with whom you came to this planet as wanderers. And if you wish to ask angels into your life, they are always waiting to be asked. We have banded together with the angelic forces, Q'uo says, and you can call upon us. We are always ready to offer you a carrier wave for your meditations. Mentally call upon us at any time and we shall be there.

What is necessary to access all of this is to lay down your burdens of mind and body long enough to contact your heart, to open it, and to ask for help. Entering the silence, even for thirty seconds or a minute, can be enough to give you that pulse of energy which carries the joy and the peace and the power you are feeling now.

Then they turn the attention inward, to you alone, naked and unadorned with helpers, armed only with yourself. And here is the sentence I want you to hear twice. You are adequate. You are enough. You are all that there is. Joy dances in your heart. The answers you seek are like seeds sprouting in that heart of hearts.

You have good soil within you, they say. Let each seed, each moment, each experience, fall into your heart, and give it a chance to ripen.

The session closes with a small practice, almost a game. Widen your awareness to include everyone in the circle. Feel the connections of your blended auras, one upon one upon one, as a circuit of electricity moving about. Etch this moment into your memory, and give yourself one word by which to access this nugget of awareness. It could be love. It could be Camelot. Choose your word, and breathe it into your heart, knowing it shall remain there, available whenever you desire.

Each time you go into meditation, even for a moment, you can recall that cluster of memories. The smell of rain on grass. The rustle of wind through leaves. The little noises on the periphery of awareness. It is a moment that extends infinitely, wrapped in a tissue of your awareness and tucked away. Unwrap it as often as you like. It shall never grow stale.

So the good times can roll on. Not because you hold onto a place, but because you carry the tuning, the word, and the silence, wherever you go.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Snooze Alarm
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the snooze alarm.

In mid-September, the question before the circle was about service and free will. When we offer wisdom or love to others, we can infringe on their free will if they are not ready to receive it. Does that create an imbalance in the energy body? And if so, how do we balance it?

An interesting note opens this session. The voice speaking is Hatonn, the density of love, stepping forward as the mouthpiece of Q'uo for the evening, because the circle's energy was so heavily biased toward love. You will hear Q'uo's name throughout, but know that it is Hatonn's love doing the speaking.

The teaching begins with parents. It is definitely an infringement on an infant's free will to direct that infant in the ways of the world. And yet it must be done. Manners must be learned. The child must be trained to become a functioning part of the tribe of humankind. Unless the parent enjoys impressing his will on the child, unless the intent is to bully and make the child feel small, there is no karmic debt and no imbalance from that benign, beneficial training.

The same holds for the teacher. Authority used to abase or shame a student creates imbalance. Authority used to share knowledge does not.

In all such cases, what matters is not what is done but the intention of the one doing it. Look always to the intention when you gauge the success of being of service. From the space-time perspective, the manifestation is everything. But from the metaphysical perspective, the shape and quality of the intention far outweighs the manifestation. That should comfort all of you who try again and again to be of service and find yourselves lacking in the result. If your intentions are pure, metaphysically speaking, you are succeeding brilliantly.

Let others worry about whether the manifestation is perfect. Your concern is only to attempt, in the present moment, to move according to the intention of service you have set for yourself.

Then the question everyone in the circle recognized. You have found treasure, this philosophy that has changed your life, and you want to give everyone the same good experience. It can be a crushing blow to discover that almost no one in your family or circle of friends is interested.

If you persist in buttonholing people and pressing your information on them, you are involved in service to self rather than service to others, because of the primal nature of free will. The compassionate course, when information has not been requested, is to refrain.

But there is another way to share. If you move not from person to person but from soul to soul, and you see an opportunity to drop a seed of thought, with no concern or attachment for the outcome, then there is no ripple in the calmness of the energy body. No balance is disturbed. All is well.

Their instrument, they say, likes to think of herself as a snooze alarm. It is her role to offer her shining truth with all the passion and skill she has, eager to wake those who are sleeping lightly and ready to wake. But once the alarm has jolted them awake for a moment, she carefully refrains from caring whether they roll over and go back to sleep or sit up and say, now that is something I would like to think about.

When there is no concern for the outcome, the ego self is not involved, and there is no imbalance in sharing truth. If you answer a question another has asked, you have served. If you respond to a request for time or talent, you have served. What happens after the offering is not your concern.

And when your service is rejected, when every attempt seems to fail, remember that the situation is perfect, because it is giving you grist for the mill. The outer catalyst strikes your energy field according to your biases, bringing discomfort, grief, anger. To the worldly mind these seem unfortunate. To the seeker they are gifts, showing you where your pain lies, and more than that, showing you what the pain is hiding.

Sit with those surface emotions and let them ripen in meditation. Even the harshest surface emotion, refined by ripening, shall deepen your nature and hollow you out so that you may carry more love, just as a chalice carries wine. Suffering hollows out the earthly personality if you let it. It does not have to make you bitter or cynical. You become an alchemist, turning disharmony into harmony, fear into love, darkness into light.

Do not cringe away from your suffering, they say, but cradle yourself as you move through the natural alchemy of the transforming energy of the love in your open heart.

And as always, enter the silence. You are a heartbeat away at all times from the gateway of intelligent infinity. You need only release the self from the strictures of intellect and logic and enter the silence.

Set the pure intention. Drop the seed. Sound the alarm. Then let go, and let the other soul decide.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Daily Conversation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the daily conversation.

In late September, a questioner asked Q'uo something beautifully direct. How can I enter into contact with my higher self and receive daily guidance with such clarity that I can tell it apart from my own imagination? What spiritual principles can help me receive guidance?

Q'uo begins with the architecture. Each entity exists both in third density, as a creature of flesh and blood, and as an energy body in time and space. The foundation of your guidance system is your higher self, that self in mid-sixth density who has experienced all that was desired, and who, turning at last toward the Creator, left behind a thought form containing the harvest of everything learned, so that you may call upon your highest and best self at any time.

That higher self is joined by at least three angelic entities. Some call them the Holy Spirit in its male and female aspect. Others call them gurus or angels. Those who serve the light sometimes gather a dozen or more such presences about them. This service need not be outer. Many are those who create a portal within themselves which holds a space where light may come through from the realms of pure love into third density, and that is a great service in itself.

The spiritual principle involved in seeking your guidance is faith. And here they draw a distinction worth keeping. Faith is often confused with belief. Belief is always belief in something, a creed, a system of tenets. Faith, on the other hand, has no content. It contains no knowledge. It is an attitude. It is the attitude that knows beyond doubt, regardless of circumstances, that all is well.

The entity living a life in faith cannot be daunted by circumstance. Sometimes learning involves suffering, sorrow, pain. Yet one living in faith knows that what is happening is precisely what is needed to advance spiritually and to be of service. Faith does not recognize closed doors. It abides, patiently, trustingly, with infinite attention, for there shall come hints and inklings from spirit that illuminate the present moment.

Now the honest part. There is no such thing as knowing, without any doubt whatsoever, that you are communicating with your guidance. There is a reason for this unknowing. Each entity in third density is given complete free will, and it is not desirable, for spiritual growth, that there be some way to test and prove spiritual influences the way you test facts.

Instead you are given the ability to set intentions. Set the intention to speak with your guidance, carefully and profoundly, in such a way that the self hears the self on a deep level. Then proceed to have a conversation on a continuing basis.

Their instrument, they share, communicates with her higher self using a computer. She types in her questions, then allows her mind to be filled with a thought. When it comes, she types it without questioning or analyzing it. If she wants to continue, she types another question and waits again. It is a simple procedure, and a protective one, because your guidance dwells within your protected aura and cannot be disrupted.

Its simplicity frustrates the intellectual mind, which immediately demands, how do I know this thought is not my thought? You shall never know in that objective way, they say, until your scientists can build instruments to track vibrations of this subtle kind, and by then you will be done with third density. So your task is to continue and persevere. Have the conversation daily if you can. Keep a record, on the computer or by hand.

Gradually you will build up enough material to look back on, and the longer you continue, the denser the patterns of congruency become. You will begin to gain confidence in the source, not from proof, but from a growing synchronicity, a spiritually interesting coincidence gathering around the conversation. Eventually you will trust it because it has stood you in good stead, and because there is a certain energy you associate with it that comes at no other time.

It is not spiritually helpful, they add, to treat guidance as a product you purchase at a store. It is far more helpful to dwell within your humanity in unknowing while pursuing a life in faith.

A life in faith is supported best by entering the silence daily, in whatever way you wish. Within that silence is all the information you need. It is not offered in words or even concepts. It flows in the currents of silence into your deepest heart, to lodge there securely and bubble up into daily life in dreams and visions and feelings, the way of gnostic knowing rather than intellectual knowing.

Launch yourself into midair, as is the way of faith, they say, and you shall find firm footing in that midair, as you allow yourself to remain empty so that you may be filled with the gifts of the spirit which are yours.

Thank you for listening.

title: Temptations Are the Path
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: temptations are the path.

In late September, the question put to Q'uo was about temptation. Do we create our own temptations to test our growth? Do unmet temptations repeat until we get them right? Or is temptation simply a distraction pulling us off the path?

Q'uo begins with the word itself. Temptation carries connotations of judgment in your culture, the sense of something evil pulling the seeker astray. They do not wish to denigrate anyone's faith. But from their point of view, they would rather call these occurrences catalyst. Catalyst is a neutral term. In chemistry it means that which, being present in a process, affects change in the other elements without itself being altered.

Shall the workings of a mill that is fed grain be given a moral tinge? They ask. There is the grain offered to the grinding stone so that the wheat berry may become ground and useful for making food. In the same way, catalyst is offered on a continuous basis, in rhythmic and repeating cycles, to each seeker. The grinding stone of the seeker is its engaged emotions. The processed grain becomes what the spiritual being uses to nourish the spiritual process.

It may be said that the self creates its own catalyst, but only in the larger sense. Before incarnation, the self, along with the Creator and the higher self, planned the incarnation and chose its themes. So the incarnational lesson revolves and comes around again as long as you are within incarnation. This is not a process where you learn a lesson and are finished with it. It is as if you keep receiving a pop quiz. Your incarnation is a term in a school. It is a school of souls. It is a refinery for souls.

You asked whether temptation repeats until overcome, or distracts from the path. They take each thought in turn.

First, they suggest it is unwise to see temptation as something to be overcome, and they give the loveliest example in the session. Their instrument has a small cat, Pickwick, who strives with every fiber of his being to climb into her lap while she is busy. She holds out her hand to keep him back, and is always surprised at how much pressure such a small being can exert. When she releases the effort, often the cat falls over, because he no longer has the point of resistance he was pushing against. The more one strives to resist a temptation, the stronger the temptation becomes.

There is another way. Picture the dieter and the chocolate. No matter how many times she rejects the thought of chocolate, the chocolate remains the same pristine temptation. But the dieter who can rest with the temptation, acknowledging its power and choosing, in this particular moment, not to act, is not resisting. She is honoring the temptation, letting the thoughts flow through with no judgment, only the determination to continue. With the resistance removed, the temptation is not nearly so strong. And when it is no longer needed, it will fall away.

It takes far more presence of mind to sustain awareness of a temptation than either to indulge it or to banish all thought of it. But the resulting spiritual process is cleaner and clearer by far.

And why the repetition? Because you are not going in a circle. You are not in a rut. You are in a spiral. Each time you meet the catalyst you meet it at a different level, and each time you use it, your process advances. It is just as desirable to meet that catalyst on the last day of your incarnation as when you first met it as a child. Do not stop appreciating catalyst because it repeats. It is only seemingly the same.

The second thought, that temptation distracts from the path, has virtue in one way and not in another. It is true that there are energies, from your own shadow or from outside, whose goal is to distract the seeking self and take its light out of the equation. To dim a bright light it is not necessary to remove the body. It is only necessary to distract the attention enough to interrupt the flow of love and light through the seeker.

But in another sense, almost the opposite is true. Temptations are not distractions from the path. Temptations are the path. It is in those moments of challenge that you do the work you came to do, that you declare yourself an entity of service to others, an instrument for love and peace. Without the catalyst, without the temptations, those fine moments would not come.

So they encourage you to develop an appetite for catalyst and temptation. Not because the tempering is fun, but because this is how you accelerate your spiritual evolution. Remain sweet-tempered while dealing with perceived catalyst. The energy it takes to feel self-pity is toxic and not helpful spiritually.

And as always, the greatest help is the silence within. It awaits you at all times. It can work its magic in a few seconds if you truly seek it. In that silence is the one infinite Creator, and as you are one with the infinite Creator, you know all that the Creator knows, far below the conscious mind's awareness. Take in that information-laden silence, lay it upon your heart, and it will bubble up into your daylight consciousness, and you shall be changed by the wisdom and compassion of the silence.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Fingerprints on the Window
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the fingerprints on the window.

In early October, a channeling circle gathered new students around a question from one of them. What is the dynamic between actually being of service to others and being able to perceive that we are being of service? She told them of people approaching her on the street when she had no money to give, and how it disturbed her that she could not be generous. She wanted the spiritual principles behind the true desire to serve, and where that desire meets actual behavior.

A note on the voice. The session identifies itself as Q'uo throughout, but the speaking entity that evening was Hatonn, of the density of love, stepping in because the circle's energy called for it. So when I say Q'uo, know it is Hatonn's love doing the speaking.

The first teaching is a paradox. The attempt that a servant of the light makes to be of service allows that servant to discover things about herself. It lets her come across the dirty fingerprints on the window that cast shadows when the sun tries to pass through. Each fingerprint has to be attended to. And it is only by placing yourself in the light and desiring the light to come through you that the flecks of dirt and grime can be discerned. It is a gift to the self when one wishes to be of service.

Let us speak about the fingerprint called fear, for in effect each fingerprint could be labeled fear, because fear is the opposite of love. She had chosen to carry a ring with the intention of giving it to whoever asked her for money. In herself she discovered the fear of being approached, of meeting another's eyes when she had nothing to give. When she carried the ring, the fear lifted, and she could look everyone in the eye.

When the fear is no longer there between two selves, the light flows between Creator and Creator. There is no longer a holding that traps energy. The energy flows more freely through the centers that deal with society and relationship. The act of generosity was never performed. The ring was never given. But the desire to give is what helped her find a blockage and release it, and that was the only purpose necessary. The act of giving was far less relevant than the gift of love created and the discovery of a blockage to that love.

It has been said to look for love in all situations. In working with the self in these subtle arts, it is just as helpful to look for the fear. Why are you afraid? What would remedy this fear?

Then a teaching that rearranges the whole furniture of service. Consider that in your attempt to be your highest and best self, regardless of what you are already doing, you are already of service at every moment of your life. Going about your bodily needs is of service, because without the body sustained you would not be an effective seeker. You need water and nutrients. You need sleep. You need social time and play time. This is not at the sake of doing service. This too is service.

Instead of seeking to do service, give gratitude for the service you already do. Thank the earth for the plate of rice that gives you the energy and patience to be a loving spouse or parent or friend. Thank the night for the rest that lets you wake refreshed to be at your highest and best. The acting out of what your society calls service is much less important. You always work on the self, and when you work on the inner self, the outer situations take care of themselves.

They speak of those held up as models, Gandhi, Jesus, Martin Luther King, who gave tremendously of themselves. People once wore bracelets asking what would Jesus do in this or that situation. But none of these people asked themselves, what is the thing that is of service? They just did the service.

How is that possible? They say this is an unskilled question. The skilled question is to find the love, and the service will follow. When the heart is open, there are no questions of what is of service. There is merely service. The heart leads the way. The faithful servant follows. And the love appears.

When you ask what would be of service, you remove faith and use the intellect to replace it. You are not moving love but trying to emulate love. Love cannot be cultivated by will or logic. Love is cultivated by allowing it to accumulate naturally as the seeker continues to seek, continues to give thanks, and continues to point herself ever toward the light.

The closing words of the session are an instruction and an image. Gaze within and gaze at the Creator. Gaze into the eyes of another and gaze at the Creator. Gaze at the trees, at the sky, the water, the winds that blow, and gaze at the Creator.

Service to others, stripped of outer content, is the meeting of Creator to Creator, with no separation, no evasion, no fear, and no distance. You may have no money. You may have no time. You may have only one moment. But when you gaze fearlessly into another's eyes and love him, and let the love of the infinite Creator pour through you as through a stained glass window, you have satisfied the work of polarity in that moment.

Find the love first. The service will know where to go.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Spiritual Athlete
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the spiritual athlete.

In mid-October, a questioner brought Q'uo a situation many seekers will recognize. Work had been a source of great catalyst for years, person after person trying to get him fired, and right after a great opening of the heart the previous winter the level of catalyst had risen hugely. How much was external, how much self-created? What spiritual principles could help him think about it?

Q'uo begins with the seasons. In the spiritual life there is often a season of fullness and harvest, followed in its course by other seasons. And they speak of the energy body as you would speak of weather, a body interpenetrating the physical body, in a constant state of flux.

When you learn to ride a bike you never really forget how, but you can get very rusty. In the same way, once you have experienced the joy and peace of the open heart, you have seen all things as interconnected, and that is not forgotten. Yet neither is it to be held in one open setting. The energy body is intensely sensitive to incoming catalyst. So often a wonderful opening of the heart is followed, unaccountably, by events that tend to close the heart. This is not accident.

When you have had a profound realization, a responsibility is undertaken as a result of that burst of light, and an automatic rhythm comes upon its heels. It is as though the Creator were offering you the opportunity to examine whether you truly grasped the content of that realization of oneness.

The function of this pop quiz is not to cause distress but to aid you in refining your ability to maintain the eyes of love that were the gift of the realization. It is easy to love the lovable, they say. The challenge is always to love the unlovable, and to continue, in the face of catalyst from another entity, to see that entity as the Creator, as your brother or sister, indeed as your very self.

It is often a shock to discover what a fragile hold you have on a realization that seemed robust and permanent. But you have lost nothing except the apparent comfort of feeling the fullness of love. You chose the veil, and that choice, made in faith, polarizes you in a way that certainty never could.

Then the teaching on mirrors. In truth you are never alone. You are in a world of mirrors, and everyone you meet mirrors back to you yourself in one aspect or another. Even the most difficult relationship offers you the chance to see a part of yourself you have not looked at in that way.

When something triggers you, that is a part of yourself as yet unhealed, and that is the source of the triggering. Your co-workers who sought to harm you have actually given you gifts. They let you see, as in a mirror, a part of yourself you need to find. The opportunity is to look straight into that mirror and say, thank you. I will seek after that shadow part of myself, and I will love it and accept it and hold it to my heart until it has been redeemed by my love.

The catalyst is not so much about anyone else as it is about you. The work you do spiritually is not about others. It is about yourself. When you can gaze into such catalyst with gratitude, you are free of the fear and anger that close the heart. And as you love that shadow in yourself, you can gaze at the one attempting to harm you and see past the mirroring to the unity between you and the other self and the Creator.

They almost characterize it, they say, as the dance of the spiritual athlete, when again and again the waves strike you and seek to tumble you and put you off balance. And you seek not so much to stand your ground as to cooperate with the waves, to roll and dive and jump and dance with the energy, losing all fear, not even worrying whether your heart is open, simply paying attention, moment by moment by moment. For the Creator is in that moment, and in you, and in those with whom you dance.

Judge not yourself, they say. Do not be concerned that your heart has not felt so open for a while. Sometimes in the dance the movements are so fast, and you are still learning the steps, and it seems as though you have lost the realization. You have not. Feel the opening of your heart even now. Feel the love in the moment. It flows through you. You are not responsible for producing it. You are only responsible for patiently, again and again, doing that work of remembrance that releases fear, so that you remember who you are and why you are here.

You are a child of the one infinite Creator, and you came here to create a space through which light may flow, to help lighten the consciousness of the planet. Momentary lapses do not keep you from your work. You are on mission and on task. There shall come another full tide, and your heart shall once again be awash in utter love. And then once again the seasons of testing. All of it is the tempering and honing of the spirit within.

Each time you dismantle a trigger and gaze at the Creator within one who is blessing you by attempting to harm you, you become calmer and stronger. Keep dancing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Stained-Glass Window
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the stained-glass window.

In mid-October, the question put to Q'uo came from the Law of One material itself. Ra had said that for a seeker three things matter. Know the self. Accept the self. Become the Creator. The questioner asked Q'uo to touch upon the first two, and to dwell mostly on the third. What does it mean to become the Creator?

Q'uo takes up each in turn, in one of the great discourses of the archive.

Knowing the self takes years, they begin, because as a very young entity your parents and teachers explained the way things were, and you became acculturated to a hundred things that never made sense to you. Many go through life asleep, thinking only of being fed and sheltered and paying the bills. For you that was not enough. You woke from the planetary dream, and once awake you cannot go back to sleep.

At first, knowing the self is largely finding out what you are not, and letting those things fall away. Perhaps the quickest way to discover who you are is to rest in meditation at the end of each day and go over your day, emotion by emotion. When you find what pulled you off balance, ask what trigger lay beneath it. Beneath your reactions you will find buried crystals of pain, usually from early childhood. Lift them into the daylight, release the wound, forgive it, and you recover a part of your whole self.

As the days and years go on, you notice the themes that repeat, and that is the hint of why you are here. Each entity comes into incarnation with a plan, not predestined but flexible and redundant. Before incarnation you and your guidance looked at your soul stream and chose a direction, more wisdom for the love in your heart, more openness for your wisdom, a better use of power. Whatever your lesson, two things are sure. It is about balance, and it is unique to you.

As you empty out pride and pretension, you become aware of something underlying your personality, what they call consciousness. You are both of this world and not of this world, and it is well to find a haven within yourself where your energy body may flower and breathe in the love and light of the infinite Creator.

Then they come to the shadow, and this passage asks for steadiness. As you get to know yourself you are disturbed by what you find, for you have a shadow side. Since all is one, you contain the full range of selfhood. The thief, the liar, the murderer, all those things you would never be, you meet through the eyes of other people. That could not be me, you think. And yet those aspects are within you, needing to be acknowledged and loved.

What those anarchic elements carry is a strength missing from the sweeter, more angelic side. You need that grit, that perseverance, that ability to hold your ground and hold the light. Those shadow sides give teeth to your ideals, so lift them into your arms, and say, come work with me for the light.

Now becoming the Creator. There are two minds within you, they say. The intellect dwells in space and time. It is finite, a problem-solving computer, unique to you, part of the animal. Consciousness dwells in infinity and eternity, and it is common to all of you, because it is the beingness of the one infinite Creator.

Walk into the woods on a summer day, and the trappings of civilization fall away until only the song of birds and wind speaks to you. You sink from surface intellect into consciousness and are one with the singing, and you rest in the mind of the infinite One, whose song is love. Your breathing in is a breathing in of love, and your breathing out the answering of love to love. You may do this in your chair as well as in the woods, for you are every bit as much consciousness as you are intellect.

Becoming the Creator is allowing consciousness to supplant the intellect. You can be nothing else but the Creator. That is a given, though you cannot prove it. It is not that you become unconditional love, for you were unconditional love the whole time. It is that you find ways, as you know and accept yourself just as you are, to allow consciousness in.

Part of the intellect fears that if impersonal loving consciousness grows, you will lose your individuality. Nothing could be less true, they say. It is only as you become aware of the deepest part of yourself that you breathe more freely, awakened to eternity as well as the world of finite things.

Think of your life as an instrumentalist tuning her instrument to sweet harmony, for this is the creation of the Logos, whose name is unconditional love, and you are tuning to that Logos. Each person lets the light shine through her as through a stained-glass window, and the colors of your window are the colors of your emotions, your thoughts, your ideals, those things you hold most dear. As Saint Francis said, you are an instrument of his peace, holding a space through which light may flow out into the world.

It is a long game with a simple strategy. Know the self. Accept the self. Become the Creator. Settle in for the long walk. Do not reach, do not push. Set your intention to know and to serve each day, for the present moment is that marvelous point of connection between eternity and the physical illusion.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Waking Beam
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the waking beam.

In late October, the question before Q'uo came in a letter from a man who had spent twenty-four years as a Navy Seal and six more as a security contractor in war zones. He described a moment when, sensing his group was about to be attacked by rocket, he felt an overwhelming urge to send out the thought of love, and the attack was thwarted. Over the following years he used the thought energy of love again and again to keep the groups he protected safe. His question was how this knowledge could be shared, so others might help change the paradigm of war.

This episode touches war and its aftermath, including the invisible wounds carried home. Receive it gently, as the session itself does.

Q'uo begins with the distance between paradigms.
