There is a substantial distance between the paradigm of the warrior or protector and the paradigm that has become crystal clear to this man, at whose center is the concept of those on both sides as equally valuable. They note, quietly, that the theories of warfare systematically undervalue even the lives of those on one's own side, treating them as less important than the mission. The energy fueling the desire for a new paradigm of protection is substantial.

A second difficulty. Many in third density are deeply asleep in the planetary dream, in a comfortable numbness that has replaced the early yearnings for truth. At the soul level each of your brothers and sisters is a part of the Godhead principle, a citizen of eternity, fully aware far below consciousness that they are one with the Creator. At the conscious level many have no belief in the power of love. That is not a tragedy, they say. There is no time limit on spiritual evolution. Progress is inevitable.

The challenge, for this man and for all who serve the light, is to share in such a powerful way that it triggers what their instrument calls the snooze alarm, not only by what is said but by the energy carried, which flows out into the world as a lighthouse that others may recognize from afar and be drawn toward.

Words are the first level of sharing, and they honor his book as a real tool. Words can only go so far. Compared to the awareness of love, words are poor indeed. Yet many entities are at a tipping point right now where just the right word at the right time shall create the change in consciousness that wakes one up, and having awakened, they cannot go back to sleep.

But he hopes for something more direct, an apprehension of the power of unconditional love, offered without infringing free will. Q'uo names the older ways. Gurus retreat from words and sit in silence, so followers may sit in their train and share the energy of meditation. Shamans take students into the wilderness, lead them close to death, so they may become fully aware of death and then rise to become fully aware of life. Both use essences rather than words, and both have merit.

What must be awakened, they say, is desire. That desire will be fueled by belief. His own experience with the Archangel Michael operated beyond space and time, and his challenge is to make its full impact accessible, so that those who would not believe become convinced in a subjective way. To shift a paradigm drastically, it is necessary to create a hunger for the new paradigm.

The love he touched is not the flabby, weak word your culture uses. It is the love that created all that there is. Jesus, in his teaching, often altered awareness radically by healing the ill, the blind, the lame. When faced with the miraculous, the dream of earth falls away and all things become possible. The challenge is to create moments that strip away the torpor of careless unbelief. Believe with no doubts in the validity of what you wish to do, and keep a constant, unremitting request for aid.

What he has set before himself requires allowing the self to be empty, so that the chalice of flesh that is his earthly temple may be filled with the power of the living Creator each and every day. Let not your intention grow old or stale, but set it anew as each sun rises and each sun sets. Speak to the daytime and the nighttime your desire to serve.

A magician, in the white magical tradition, is one who develops the art of creating changes in consciousness at will. That is what he hopes to teach. It is not an insurmountable challenge, though it is a substantial one.

As you ask for help, concepts shall come. Trust them. Let new ways and strategies roll around in your mind untagged and unordered, tumbling together like puppies at play. Allow rather than force your strategy to unfold. You are asking of yourself something illogical and paradoxical, and those two elements almost guarantee you are on the right track, spiritually speaking.

And know that at any gathering you offer, you have a tremendous arsenal of resources in the unseen realms. Your own guidance. The guidance systems of those present. Oversoul energies. The archangels, who until requested in space and time cannot offer their help, and who are in their own way warriors for the light. Call them, use them, give thanks.

You do not change the paradigm of war by arguing with it. You become the lighthouse, and let the sleeping recognize the light.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Road to Nowhere
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the road to nowhere.

In late October, a new cycle of channeling intensives began, and Laitos tried something different. Instead of a question, they told a story, passing the contact from channel to channel around the circle, each new voice picking up the thread. Storytelling, they said, is a good way for new instruments to recognize the contact, for in a story there is no possibility of error. It bends as each entity adds to it, like a river that cannot go straight because of the needs of the water.

So be bold when your turn comes, they told the students. Speak what comes into your mind without evaluating it.

And so they begin. Once upon a time there was a family that lived near a road. There were many superstitions about this road, for it was not a road to another town, nor to a lake or a mountaintop. Entities who took it were often not seen for many years, and when they returned they were changed. The light in their eyes was different, the smile on their lips deeper. They would not explain where the road had taken them, only that it was powerful and positive.

Energy seemed to thrum along the road, invisible but palpable. And a little boy, more and more, was drawn to it. With his parents' permission, he packed his knapsack and started off on a magical journey.

When the sun rose the boy moved up the road with no fear, only a great curiosity and longing. The farther he went from home, the more he felt as if he were becoming more at home. All was familiar, seen through different eyes that were also his own.

Along the path he met a young girl about his age, coming down to the road. She glowed with the intensity of the surroundings. They greeted each other, the road brightened, his knapsack shimmered with light, and a feeling of love overwhelmed him.

Days followed days. In the evenings the boy would reflect on what he had seen, and he ate less and drank less, because he was alive and living off the air and sun. He began to see the world through his own eyes, no longer the eyes of his parents.

In a forest at nightfall they found a small cave, and inside an old man, resting, with a smile on his face and a glow of light in his eyes. He bade them sit and told them many things, yet not speaking as they had known speaking. The more he told, the more they knew in their hearts that it was true, that they had known it forever and were learning it, it seemed, for the first time.

As the knowledge passed, their hearts began to open, and the boy and the girl recognized this supposed stranger, and recognized each other, no longer strangers from different peoples, but friends who had known each other before their births.

As this realization came, the cave and the fire and the trees seemed to break away and melt, as though reality itself were re-contextualizing itself. What they had supposed real and solid no longer seemed so real and solid, but pliable and knowable in a profound way. And the old man stood, crooked his finger, and bade them follow him deeper into the cave, into the darkness.

Deeper in, the cave opened into a beautiful forest. The children danced and played between the trees, joyful, and it became clear they had been there before. They made a game of anticipating what would come at the next turn of the path, and it came naturally to them.

The boy began to see the cave as a midpoint of the journey. It continued until moments became a lifetime of bliss and knowing, and he walked on, wishing to see the world through new eyes.

At last the two felt the desire to return home, to share what they had learned, and the desire seemed to bring them almost immediately to familiar ground. They walked into the village looking upon the people with astonishment, as though recognizing them, but dimly.

Questions came thick and fast. What did you see? Where did you go? But they had few words, only the joy of moving through a glowing world in which every rock and every tree had a special energy which, when entered, told its own story.

They did not say much. They smiled with smiles so full of joy and wisdom that many thought, perhaps one day I too shall walk upon this road that goes to no town nor shore nor mountaintop, and see what I can see.

Laitos closed by thanking the students for their tuning and their desire to serve, and for helping share with the world the possibility that there is a paradigm of love that can supersede a paradigm of fear, a paradigm of unity that can supersede a paradigm of separation.

A story told by many voices, bending like a river, about a road that goes nowhere and everywhere. Perhaps one day you too shall walk upon it, and see what you can see.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Light Suitcase
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the light suitcase.

In early November, a channeling circle gathered with new students, and Q'uo offered them an image I have not been able to put down since. The life of one who has awakened to spirit, they said, is upheld and closed about with a web of love and support. And each of you has prepared carefully for this incarnation. Out of a nearly infinite array of previous incarnations, you have packed a very light suitcase.

In it you packed the relationships in which you agreed to take part, for your mutual aid, one to the other. You packed just the gifts you need to offer, that which you wish to give in this incarnation among your fellow humans in this tribe of earth. And you packed into that overnight bag some challenges, limitations and fail-safe measures that, when activated, shall recall your mind to the service at hand.

You are surrounded, they continue, with many unseen helpers. Your guidance system, your higher self. Inner masters, angels, those who vibrate in a way congruent with your desire to serve. Some in the group had attracted nature spirits and devas, powerful primal energies of the earth who appreciated their harmony. All of these unseen energies love you to an extent almost impossible to imagine.

Then the image deepens. Take that suitcase to your destination, the body you inhabit, the home you inhabit. It is like going to a friend's house. You packed what you needed, what comforted you. But what is at your friend's house? An entire house, and loved ones around you upon whom you can depend. Your higher self and your guides and the nature spirits that dwell around you. When you abide in their house they wish to be good hosts. And while you stay, when you show appreciation and gratitude for their welcome, they are most happy to give you what you most need. None of you are alone in this journey.

You do not have to pack the towels. They are in the bathroom for you to use. You do not need food, for your hosts will provide it. The more closely you come into companionship with those around you, the more their home becomes your home and their things become your things, until you no longer have to ask for a glass of water. You can simply go to the kitchen and get your own. They think nothing of it. You think nothing of it.

Let us speak about gratitude, they say. The lack of gratitude is a measure of separation. It is an ego-filled dependence that says, I will take care of myself. I have packed everything I need and I need nothing from you. And your hosts agree. They feel they need not supply anything, if that is your wish.

But when you drop the ego and say, thank you for having me in your home, I appreciate your sharing with me what you have, a connection is built between you and those forces. The stronger the connection, the greater the gratitude, and the more a oneness is formed between you and those unseen forces.

That which you need is always present in your life. It is as simple as looking about yourself and reaching out and taking what you need, in a way that is not prideful but that acknowledges the light. The instrument felt, as these words came through, an extreme closeness, as if space had condensed and everything outside her were pressed up against her skin. That collapsing of space illustrates the closeness in which what you need is so near it is almost a part of you, with no separation between you and the thing upon which you depend.

It sounds trite to say it once again, they admit, but the truth is that all is one. And the Creator serves the Creator. When the Creator within the person knows that the inner self is one with the rest of the outer self, then that which is needed is already a part of the self.

I love the humility of this image. You did not come here self-sufficient, carrying everything. You came light, on purpose, trusting the hosts. The challenges in your bag are not punishments. They are fail-safe measures, little alarms meant to recall your mind to the service at hand when you drift.

And the love around you is not the measured, conditional, insipid love you are used to in daily life, stepped down and stepped down from mate to child to friend to a favorite dish. They speak of essences and entities who have never departed from the unconditional and vastly creative love of the infinite Creator. That is the household you are staying in.

So travel light. Say thank you. Walk into the kitchen of the universe like you belong there, because you do. What you need is already within reach.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Power of Mercy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the power of mercy.

In late November, the question put to Q'uo was about power, and especially about the power of women. In our culture, the questioner said, the acquisition and use of power by women is often discouraged from childhood onward. What is the most appropriate use of one's power, in protecting the self and in serving others?

Q'uo begins by sorting out what power means. There is physical power, strength in the arm. In the metaphysical world the connotations remain, but the hammer is the hammer of focus, the sword is the sword of intention, the weight is the weight of desire. Metaphysical power is the ability of the focused and disciplined personality to set and keep an intention and to do work in consciousness.

Between those lies a third kind, emotional and social, the sticky complicated power of influence, of pressing one's will on others. When most people think of power they think of this kind. But Q'uo sets it aside. The right use of power, as they mean it, is not about the halls of economic and political decision making.

Then they tell a deep history. Third density is the density of choice, where the great apes who began it with instinctual ways have attempted, over thousands of years, to become human. Many, they say, have never fully become human, but rested with second-density values. The defense of the clan. The gathering of resources. Protection from threat.

To be human is to become self-aware, to behold within the self that ethically motivated being into whose fragile temporary home infinity and eternity have been poured, so that each self-aware human is a fully formed spark of the one infinite Creator.

What followed on earth was a ruinous, repetitive series of empires, in which the male principle of aggression, protection and control built empire after empire, and each, uninformed by the female principle, crushed itself under its own weight. Against that background, the feminine principle, which would balance the aggression, was feared and controlled and placed under the heel of the male. Your planet at this time, they say, is heavily overbalanced toward the masculine principle, and desperately in need of balance.

But listen carefully, because they are not speaking of literal men and women. They are speaking of two energies which, cooperating fully, create the balanced and perfected human. It is not only men who need the feminine principle. Biological women need it too, upheld and validated and honored.

To live the Law of One is to live a fully human, fully balanced life, valuing both wisdom and love, looking always for that point of balance where ethical choices enlarge unconditional love. The feminine principle looks for ways to cooperate, to collaborate, to move in harmony and rhythm, to sustain an environment which does no harm but only serves to improve and balance relationships.

How do you promote that spirit within your own being? It begins, they suggest, with the way you treat yourself. The feminine principle is not a judgmental principle. It is a loving and merciful principle. And the first overbalancing of male energy any awakening human will find is that point of judgment within the self when a self-perceived error occurs.

How do you handle yourself when you err? Are you judgmental? Do you say, what a fool I am, I can never get this right, I should be ashamed? If so, you are reacting in an overbalanced male way. It is easy to judge. It is far more difficult to forgive. Yet is there anything to forgive when a child adds two plus two and gets five? It is a matter of correcting the error next time.

Begin by using your power to forgive, to begin again, to let go of the need to judge, the need to force correction. As you forgive yourself, you gain the power that comes with mercy. As you see yourself as a whole person, greater than the sum of your mistakes, there comes a feeling of dignity and self-respect. You are no longer judging yourself on your behavior. You are judging yourself on your intentions and your basic nature.

As you become self-forgiven, whether biological male or female, there awakens within you a self-perception that includes true power, for you know you have the power to understand and forgive. And when those about you impinge upon you in hurtful ways, you have the power to stand on your self-forgiven feet, gaze at them at the soul level, and forgive them. For they know not what they do.

And so your world begins to be self-forgiven. And your power grows. Your power to love, your power to forgive, your power to exercise patience and understanding. The definition of magical power is the power to create changes in consciousness at will. Each time you tune into that feeling of self-forgiveness, you change the vibration of your entire energy body, and you change the vibration of the planet.

You have tremendous help in this, they add. Your guidance system is nearer than your hands or your heart. As you vibrate in a certain frequency you draw to yourself unseen companions who vibrate at that frequency, angels and inner masters standing at your back like a backdrop of light. Lean into that help. Ask for it.

The Creator's name in some circles is I Am. How shall you serve? That is the challenge given to those in the density of choice. May you choose with your deepest heart to become you.

Power, rightly used, is mercy. Begin with yourself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Bloom Within Eternity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the bloom within eternity.

In late November, the last session in this set, the question put to Q'uo reached for the largest frame of all. As the seeker integrates what it learns from previous lives and from this one, it becomes more and more as it is, and as it is, it is the one infinite Creator. So as we become the Creator, do we give up our identity? Is it something we will miss? And since living as the Creator seems to have more to do with being than with doing, how does the seeker move along that upward spiraling line of evolution? What is gained? What is lost? And how is it done?

Q'uo answers by holding two scales at once. There is the little life of one incarnation, and there is the life of the soul stream, which lives a larger life within eternity, moving through all the densities of experience. Never doubt, they say, that you are infinite and eternal. Yes, you are sparks of the Creator, and yes, you are the Creator.

If all things are one, why are entities unique? These paradoxes are only the beginning, they say. When you speak of becoming the Creator you dwell in a land of paradox and mystery, where logic shall not necessarily be of aid. Yet if you abandon the intellect entirely and rest only on faith, you rob yourself of all the hard-won advantages of being an incarnated human being.

So they suggest neither pure logic nor pure faith, but an awareness of your strange situation. You are a stranger in a strange land, and a native of it, in a body of bone and muscle. In a million small ways physicality reminds you of limitation.

And yet, contained within this web of limitation and pain and suffering, there lies what one member of the circle had drawn that evening as the sorcerer's stone of now. A now which echoes from the little life to the soul stream to the one infinite Creator.

Without your physicality, without your location in space and time, without the tremendous sacrifices your soul stream makes to project itself into this bound illusion, you would not have the capacity to hold open the potentiated space in which the Logos of absolute love can channel down into form. Within the tiny boundaries of a little life and a seemingly limited personality, you hold the Creator's highest hope for knowing itself. The power of your position is astounding.

It is well that an entity awakening to its larger self has no idea of the power it carries. For you are in a way like puppies, and you must grow into your feet and your ears and your tail. As you grow from a spiritually immature thinker to a seeker increasingly awake, your puppy feet begin to take hold.

Some seekers gather more and more detail from memories of previous incarnations, reasoning that more detail will bring more knowledge of the self. Others find moments out of time that come without warning, in which the sense of self becomes resonant and clear with almost no intellectual content, a path of direct apprehension and intuition. There are paths too numerous to mention, but the importance of any path fades before the awareness of the potential of your humanity. You are all that there is.

What do you gain as you become more aware of how it feels to be you? You gain freedom and peace. You have no need to defend, no need to protect, no need to explain. You are. And who and what you are is a creature of such beauty and worth that no words can hold it. Each of you is a bloom within eternity, exquisitely unique, not only in this little life but as a soul stream of infinite experience. And that infinity, that Creator-ness unique to you, is the gift you give to the infinite One. It is beyond price.

What do you lose? In a way, a great deal. As you become comfortable with your deepest self beyond distortion, distortions fall away. Do you value yourself because you are good at telling jokes? Perhaps that quirk falls away. It is as though you asked an old person what he had lost by growing old. He could say, I have lost my looks, my teeth, my ability to go hours without rest. Or he could say, I have lost my fears, my worries, my anger, my prejudice, my self-imposed limitations. If you value your distortions, you shall feel the loss of much as you grow closer to the frequency of the one infinite Creator, which is love.

What is gain and what is loss, when you are gazing at the opportunity in one small life to hold a channel that connects particularity to the infinite, to be hollowed out and emptied of the details of gifts and personality, so that your life may be lit from within by love?

And how is it done? Each moment of your life is a moment in which the potential for being is held before you like a gift. Shall you take it in this moment? You may be distracted, but another moment shall come immediately, and then another. There is no moment in your third-density life that is not utterly full of the opportunity to know the self, to accept the self, and to become the Creator.

So do you lose your identity in becoming the Creator? You lose the distortions. What remains is more you than you have ever been. A bloom, opening, within eternity.

Thank you for listening.

title: Embracing the Wolf
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: embracing the wolf.

This session comes from a December gathering of people learning to channel, a circle of new instruments asking Q'uo a question that gets at the heart of every seeker's life. They ask, in essence, when something on the path stands before you and says go no further, a darkness, an opposition, a dread, what is it, and how do you answer it.

I love how honestly Q'uo begins. They speak of the desire to follow a spiritual path wholeheartedly, and how often, in childhood, we learned that desire was risky business. One discovers that to follow a desire would be unacceptable, and so one learns to build into the very structure of desire a resistance to it. The desire does not die. It goes underground. It finds secret and subterranean ways to express itself. And here is the line I keep returning to. This, they say, is energy of the Creator and is never, never to be despised. Yet so often that is precisely its fate. It is despised even by the one to whom it most closely belongs.

Sometimes, they say, a pocket of rejected desire grows so strong it seems to acquire a life of its own. It turns on the one whose desire it is, in forms that beggar the imagination. Dreams. Shadows. The monsters of the night. And listen to how they put the first step. Recognize that all such energy is your own, is the energy of the Creator, is real, and is ultimately capable of being reintegrated.

Then a second instrument takes up the image of the mountain. The shadows of the mountain that were not hit with the sun begin to appear around the climax of the mountain. You see crags and pinnacles arising out of the darkness around you and you say, what is this that has appeared at my side. It is not part of me. But go deeper into the mountain, and you realize each of these rocks and crevices is part of the same mountain. They are part of self. The snows fall on the entirety of the mountain alike.

I find that so tender. The snow does not choose which part of the mountain is worthy. It falls on all of it. And Q'uo says the monsters in the night exist, they are very real in their impact, and yet they are merely empty perceptions of the mind, holding no real form. The fear is real. The form is not.

The practical teaching lands in the middle of the session. When you are faced with such visions, essences, and distractions, cease movement. They use the image of a swimmer in deep water. Stop thrashing toward a shore you cannot see. Float. Let yourself be borne by whatever current you are in. And when the effort to extract yourself has ceased, when you are empty and unresisting, ask to find the love in that moment. They even suggest the question itself as a mantra. Where is the love in this moment.

There is a reason this works, they say. It is the glory and the truth of each seeker that the love in that moment is himself. To open the self amid challenge to the awareness of love is to open the self to the universe that is love. And then comes the passage that gave this episode its title. One allows love to flood the self, they say, so that one is marinated in love, drenched, permeated and filled with love. And from that point of perception it becomes the act of simplicity itself to love the unlovable, to embrace the wolf that bites.

But Q'uo does not leave it at love alone. The other half of the journey, they say, is to build that armor of light about yourself with as much fervor as the love sent from the heart. Love opens you. The armor of light gives the opened self a safe haven. Both are needed, the open heart and the protected vessel, the seeker who tempers himself like a blade in fire.

They close with a reminder that the temptation to give up the journey when opposition comes is normal. There is no shame in feeling disheartened. It is simply part of the tempering. And eventually, each seeker will find that there is great benefit in sharing heartfelt love with each portion of the creation, including those portions that seem negative, especially in the interaction with the self.

Tonight's teaching is a hard one and a gentle one at once. Whatever stands before you saying go no further may be the very part of you that most needs to be met with love. Cease the thrashing. Ask where the love is in the moment. And let the snow fall on the whole mountain.

Thank you for listening.

title: Becoming the Magician
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: becoming the magician.

The question this December evening reaches back to Ra. The seeker, Ra suggested, may become the magician, one who creates changes in consciousness at will. The group wonders about the weight of that. If you can change consciousness by choice, what does that ask of you, and how do you keep your balance, body and mind and spirit, while you do it.

Q'uo begins by stepping back to look at the environment. Your density is the density of choice, a heavily polarized place. And into it you came by choice. There is a long line of those who wish to be present at this time, they say, and you earned your place by the seniority of your vibration. You are here with entitlement, to choose what you will and to will what you choose. I find that bracing. Not a burden laid on you, but a seat you earned.

Then they define the flame. Each of you carries within you a flame that burns true and bright in any circumstances of life. You brought it when you entered the body, and it will still be burning when the body is dropped, without a single lapse of consciousness. What is that flame, they ask, and answer simply. We will call it your will. You are, each of you, a very young and inexperienced Creator. And your will is the will of the Creator. So the question is not really what you are allowed to want. It is what kind of Creator you wish to be, and what kind of creation you wish to create.

The group guessed that the magician's burden is the responsibility to use this power in service to others. Q'uo says, in a way, but that is not broadly enough stated. The real burden is knowing your own will. When you awaken to the extent of your personal power, you become aware of the burden you shall bear. And they are careful here. We are not saying use your power as someone has told you that you should use it. We are not saying use your power as we say. You are undertaking the profound responsibility of knowing what your will is.

There is a small story tucked into the session that I love. Carla, the instrument, is riding in a car to a restaurant. There is no parking place. The driver circles the block, and as they return, a car pulls out of the closest spot and they slide right in. And Carla thinks to herself, have I used my will rightly in praying for this parking place. How unspiritual a thing to pray for. Yet Q'uo's response is gentle. What shall you pray for. You are here legitimately, with entitlement, to choose what you will, to fulfill the desires that you wish to fulfill, until you are satisfied that you have gleaned everything from this environment that you can.

As for balance, they refuse the static image. Anyone who has ridden a horse or a motorcycle knows, they say, that balance is not only your balance, but the balance of the animal beneath you and the conditions of the road. It is not a static thing. It is freely flowing and always developing and changing. And for the spiritual seeker, balance is fundamentally this. That each of the chakras of your energy body lies open, so that each may accept and allow through it the full power of the love and the light of the one infinite Creator, streaming infinitely and eternally.

You do not need to become a magician to graduate, they add. You need only an open heart, and the choice of how to serve. But each of you wants more, they say. Each of you wishes to pull down inspiration through the gateway of intelligent infinity. So the fertile question for each day is simply this. Is this moment one in which I wish to change consciousness. And if so, how shall I apply my will.

The session ends with an image of quiet grandeur. If you choose the magical life, they say, there are orders upon orders of angelic hosts that move into the orbit of those who vibrate in ways congruent with them. Whether you wish to heal, to teach, to create in poetry and music and dance, or to become a self-aware beingness in all situations, many presences wish to aid you. And then the caution that undoes all literalness. Loosen yourself from the literal meaning of these words. A parent is all of these for her child. The dancer, the singer, the teacher, and the one whose radiance keeps the child safe and happy and open. Do not be fooled by what things look like in the outer world. Not all teachers teach. Not all dancers dance. Not all singers sing. Only you know what kind of magician you want to be.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Wheel of Emotions
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the wheel of emotions.

The question comes on the day after Christmas, and it is about the feelings we are taught to be ashamed of. Jealousy. Anger. Doubt. Greed. If love and fear are the great opposites, the group asks, are all the other emotions some mixture of the two. And is there any positive use for these supposedly negative emotions.

Q'uo begins by defending the emotions, and I find their defense moving. Among your people, they say, emotions are often unappreciated and dishonored by those who would live a spiritually oriented life. From our perspective, however, the emotions that you feel are gifts of enormous worth. Whereas the mind moves from thought to thought, governed by logic, the heart moves from emotion to emotion, with no intellectual component whatsoever. For emotions are those gifts of the heart that stem from the very depths and roots of your consciousness.

Then they give an image that reframes everything. In the roots of consciousness, the emotions can be mapped, much as the waterways of a continent can be mapped. There are rivers of emotion of every kind, the positive ones you name joy and bliss, and the ones you call negative, greed and gluttony and lust. Yet each emotion flows from its most distorted manifestation, through a succession of removals of distortion, until at last they all empty into the same ocean. The ocean they call the Logos, or unconditional love, or bliss. Every river reaches the sea. Even this one. Even that one.

Carla had been trying to measure emotions on a yardstick, a ratio of love to fear, and Q'uo gently sets the yardstick down. That attempt, they say, compresses the three hundred sixty degrees of emotion into a two-dimensional straight line. The model they offer instead is a color wheel. Emotions as complementary colors, arranged in a full circle around a center, and the center is unconditional love.

Listen to how they read jealousy on that wheel. The object which has inspired one's jealousy is greatly loved. Therefore the jealousy has love at its heart, yet tinged by the fear of the loss of that love. The energy of the love becomes quite different from the original free and easy feeling. I think that is one of the most compassionate sentences in the whole archive. Jealousy is love, afraid of losing what it loves. What if we met our own jealousy that way. Not as a shameful thing, but as love wearing a frightened face.

They suggest a practice for living with all of this. The clearest way to approach emotion, day to day, would be to remain transparent and unattached to the outcome of one's objects of desire. Not to suppress the feeling, not to obey it blindly, but to let it move through without gripping the result.

And they return to the balancing exercise they have taught for years. Find each trigger that moved you this day from balance to imbalance. Look at the process by which you were pulled off center. Then allow the seemingly opposite emotion to come, as a complementary color would be seen across the color wheel. You lessen distortion within yourself by encouraging equal respect given to both the seemingly negative and the seemingly positive. It is subtle work, they say, but it is the work you are here to do.

The session ends with a sentence I want to leave ringing. Every emotion has its place. The surface of emotions is only the beginning of them. And the promise underneath it all, that all emotions, once they have been purified, work in harmony to create of you a human being. Trust your emotions, they say, to help you learn who you are. And as you relate to others, trust the emotions in them that resonate with your own, in terms of dealing with each entity at the soul level. Your jealousy and another's jealousy carry the same energy. Your love and another's love of a certain frequency carry the same energy. It is emotions rather than thoughts which unite your people.

They are not the obstacle to the spiritual life. They are the raw material of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Desert Blooms
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the desert blooms.

This is a channeling circle session, a gathering of new instruments, and the question they bring is one of the most quietly desperate questions a seeker can ask. When all your inner work seems to leave no mark on the outer world, when you labor on yourself and nothing appears to change, is the work still worth doing. Are you still of service.

Q'uo answers with a single sustained image, and it carries the whole session. Beneath the surf of your own surface of self-perceived distortion, they say, you are the sun.

Let me slow down for that, because the teaching builds on it. Perception, they say, does not necessarily speak truth. If your attitude becomes distorted by fear or self-doubt, that too has a self-perpetuating quality, and it will seem to the self that the self moves only more and more into error, and that this error is the truth of the self. Your creation is a creation of vibration. And beneath the surf, beneath the chop on the surface, you are the sun. The clouds obscure the manifestation of sunlight, they say, but not its essence. A cloudy day does not switch the sun off. Your doubt works the same way.

Then the central claim, stated plainly. Being, radiance of being, and inner work are prior to and superior to outer work, because they are that from which blooming emanates. Essence will always have more power than manifestation, just as mystery will always speak more truth than facts and logic. Your essential vibration will bloom as it must when it is ripe, they say, whether it is seen even by you or whether it is not.

There is a hymn woven into the session, and I want to give it to you the way Q'uo gives it. Mine is the sunlight, mine is the morning, born of the one light Eden saw play. Yours is the vibration of the Logos, they say. Yours is the vibration of the sun. Let your light shine. Or perhaps, they amend, allow yourself to become transparent to the light that shines through all, illuminating all, articulating all, expressing all. Not striving to shine. Becoming see-through to the light that is already shining.

There is a practice tucked into the session for the days when the clouds will not part. Unguarded moments show beauty to the self, they say. Snatches of music and melody heard within the folds of the mystery itself tell your truth to you. Someone in the circle spoke of gazing into the mirror, into one's own eyes, and seeing the Creator. It is a matter of catching oneself past one's guard, they say, and in that unguarded moment, allowing that which is to be as it is. You do not have to achieve the sunshine. You only have to be caught off guard long enough to notice it was there all along.

And then the question that names this episode. Why did you come to this desert to bloom. You came because it was the desert and blooming was needed. Bloom upon bloom, light upon light, all hidden, all unseen, and yet towering and illuming the shadows of manifestation. I love the audacity of that. The hiddenness is not a failure of the work. The hiddenness is the work.

They ask whether you could do this without incarnation, and answer no. You would not have the right to make changes in the consciousness of this tribe of humankind. You yearned for the opportunity to become unseen, to plunge into the earth of your flesh, and to let spirit have a place in this desert. A harvest is called by the very rhythms of creation, and you are the workers in that harvest. You are the place the light may shine.

The closing line is the one I keep underlining. Let your light shine so that all those that see you see you not, but only love. Not your personality. Not your achievements. Only love, passing through. That is the answer to the circle's question. The inner work is not a preparation for service. It is the service.

Thank you for listening.

title: Carrying the Light Home
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: carrying the light home.

The question this January evening is about what happens after the circle breaks. When people of like mind gather and share with open hearts, the group says, a lot of light and energy is generated. How do you carry that with you when you leave. How do you take it into an ordinary Tuesday. And what does it have to do with the dawning of a new age.

Q'uo begins with the physics of the gathering itself, and it is vivid. Each of you is powered not only by a physical body but by an energy body, and as you rest in the circle, each of your auras blends with the auras on either side of you. It is as if you all hooked yourselves up to a great big battery, each of you being a battery for each other. They describe an enormous dome of light over the dwelling, reaching into the heavens, built as soon as the group started talking at the door. I find that consoling. The sacred space does not begin when the meditation starts. It begins when friends arrive.

Then they turn to the larger moment. The third-density light is waning, they say, soon to be setting, so that there may come the dawning of new light, a new morning, the density of love and understanding. And in the waning, more and more fourth-density light interpenetrates your world, carrying an enormous amount of truth. This is why, they say, each of you is gathering up the shadow side of yourself that you had neglected. You are all things. If you are all one, then you contain all that there is in that unity. And many are the distortions of love brought about by fear. So this is the time to cultivate fearlessness, and to leap into faith.

Their image of the transition itself is one of the most beautiful in the archive. You shall walk into the sunlight, they say, and it shall become fuller by exquisitely, carefully nuanced grades of density. And as you walk into the fuller light, it shall cease being third density and begin being fourth density. And yet you still may walk on. You may walk on until the light becomes too full and is uncomfortable to you. Then that is where you shall stop, and that is where you shall stay. No judgment from outside. Only your own preferences, met by light.

But the heart of the session, the answer to the group's actual question, comes with a nativity image I cannot improve on. You have within you a manger, they say. And in that manger lies love itself. You are in a position to come into the stable of your own heart and take up that infant self that is your maturing soul. You have the capacity to cradle, nourish, and nurture that child within. And the Creator, they say, is nearer to you than your breath, closer to you than your very bones.

What they ask you to carry into your daily life is not a technique but a way of seeing. See with eyes of love. When you see with eyes of love, then you are seeing whomever you look at as a soul. You are not looking at their behavior. You are looking at their essential being. This does not mean going foolish or blind, they add. Keep your boundaries. Keep your discernment. But in addition to all the normal movements of personality and intellect, carry the love and the light. You do not create the light, they say. You carry a space through which the infinite love and light of the one Creator may flow.

And the parting charge is simple enough to fit in a pocket. Carry the intention to love the Creator, and to love all those whom you meet as though they were yourself. You carry within you not only fourth density but all densities, all that is in manifestation, all that can be imagined. You are very young gods, they say, with much to burn away in the furnace of everyday life. But the gems are real. Go collect them.

Thank you for listening.

title: As Many Ways to Pray
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: as many ways to pray.

The question this January evening is about prayer, and it is asked with unusual honesty. What makes a prayer effective. Is it better to focus on one person or a group. Does the intention matter, the emotions, the visualization. And underneath it all, the deepest question. If all is one and all is well, if the one we pray for is the Creator, whole and perfect, do they need prayer at all.

Q'uo comes at it from several angles, beginning with the energy body. They walk up the chakras the way you would climb a ladder. Red at the root, orange in the belly, yellow in the solar plexus, and then the green-ray heart, the first center that, when opened, lets the seeker work with the higher energies. The violet ray is your signature, they say, your vibration, known to them in a far deeper way than your name. And above it, the gateway to intelligent infinity, through which the one who prays moves from the world of space and time into the world of time and space.

Their picture of the healer is one I want to linger on. The healer is a kind of instrument, they say. All the healer needs to do is set the intention to offer itself as an instrument for healing, and the healing then moves through. It is not the healer's hands doing anything. It is the energy moving through the healer. They contrast this with what they call yellow-ray healing, where the will has not moved through the open heart, where the healer pushes the gift into the patient. That works, they say, as long as the energy is fresh, but like any finite energy, it fails after a time. The model they recommend is the healer as that instrument which sings the melody of the spirit.

They hold up Saint Francis as the pattern for the teacher and the channel too. Lord, make me an instrument of thy peace. If there is any ego involved in the reaching, they say, it will fail. The chakras opened to the heart, the heart open, the intention set, the gateway opens, and what was called for comes down and does its work.

Then they turn to the question of method, and here the teaching opens wide. The Creator does not speak in words, they say. It is that still, small voice. His silence is thunder. And in that silence is all the information that is infinite. For some, resting in silence is all that is needed. For others, there is the gift of visualization, holding each entity in thought and seeing them well and in the light. For others, a hymn or a chant rises unbidden, directed at the crystallized place of pain the prayer hopes to dissolve. For others, there is the need to talk it out, to journal, question and answer, the way the author of Conversations with God did. For one who needs the words, they say, those words are very helpful, more helpful than all the silence in the world.

And then the sentence that settles the whole inquiry. There are as many ways to pray as there are people who seek to join in union with the one infinite Creator. We would assure you that there are no mistakes. If there is an intention to pray, however you choose to pray will be an effective way for you to pray.

A follow-up asks whether prayer is meant to reveal the self to the self, and Q'uo's answer is a small masterpiece of spiritual psychology. For some, they say, the self is full, so full there is no room for further understanding. For such entities the path of prayer is the path of releasing the fullness of self, letting all that self-definition fall away, so that the self becomes a chalice, empty at last and able to receive the truth. For others, bound in suffering and doubt, the chalice is already empty and ready. For them it is precious to open the self in passive prayer, to float as the candle flame floats above the candle. Either way, the self is revealed to the self, and the revealing is the prayer.

Thank you for listening.

title: Ready as You Are
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: ready as you are.

This is a channeling circle session, and the question is one of the bravest I have heard in this archive. At what point along the seeker's path, the group asks, may he turn his full attention to the Creator and say, I am ready as I am. As flawed and distorted as I may be, I ask that you use me as your instrument. And what qualities of attitude should accompany that statement.

Q'uo is visibly moved. The sweetness and earnestness of this query is very moving to us, they say. And their answer begins with a gentle overturning. Doubt not that that which you seek is there. You do not become ready by perfecting yourself into readiness. You become ready the moment the hunger and thirst ripen into bloom. Now is the time.

But they are honest about what follows the asking. What passes through you, they say, even when you attempt to serve to the uttermost, will bear the mark of an imperfection which is your own. You will have to come to own it as your own. The Creator sees you always, is with you always, and will never turn a blind eye to your heart's desires. So you need not fear that in your imperfection you might not make the grade. For by asking this question, they say, you have in turn answered this very question. Seeking the Creator and being the Creator. This is the epitome of service.

Then they offer what aids the instrument's life. Three things. First, be ready to lose everything that you understand as familiar and normal. When you ask the Creator to come into your life in power and in grace, you are releasing yourself from any definition of yourself which you previously had. What shall be required of you is unknown. Carla, the instrument, has had the experience many times, they say, of things falling away from her, things she thought were deep parts of herself. Be willing to let self-definition go, to let it flow, let it be, and you shall discover that next layer within you that is more real, more essential, and closer to the Creator's selfhood.

Second, they encourage what they call bloody-minded, stubborn perseverance. There is a story in the session about a high school baseball coach whose best advice was three words. Never give up. You shall face challenge after challenge whether or not you dedicate yourself, they say, but when you dedicate yourself, the challenges cut to the bone. There are many times when it makes no sense not to give up, when any rational person would give up. And we ask you to leap into faith with abandon, with joy, with laughter, and with rock-steady determination not to give up. Remember the words, all is well, and all will be well.

Third, abandon all pretense and pride, for they are those things which narrow and limit you. Let humility wrap its sweet tendrils around all of those sentences that begin I am or I should. And instead ask, what wilt thou have me do, for I am your instrument. What song would you have me sing with my life.

I love that they end not with a technique but with a song. You do not audition for the Creator with your perfection. You offer the flawed instrument you are, and the flaws become part of the music. The question the circle asked, when may I say I am ready as I am, is answered by the asking itself. If you are asking, you are ready.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Nexus of Two Worlds
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the nexus of two worlds.

The question this February evening arrives from a listener in Tennessee, and it is a philosopher's question. How do intelligent infinity and intelligent energy correlate to the terms spirit and consciousness. Four words we use loosely, and the group wants to know what Q'uo means by each.

The answer is one of the clearest cosmological statements in the archive, so let me lay it out the way Q'uo lays it. Consciousness, they say, is that field which carries the one original Thought of love. Our consciousness and your consciousness are one. From that field, every particle and iota of matter, every mote of light, carries the same consciousness. They give Carla the image of an infinite jigsaw puzzle. You fit in just a certain way into the integrity and wholeness of the one infinite Creator. Infinite, and yet every piece has its place.

Spirit, as they use the term, is that portion of consciousness which is not manifest in your world. You may apprehend it as the voice of your conscience, your higher self, your guidance. Or as the energy that comes to you from the trees, the animals, the wind, the earth, fire, and water. Spirit is consciousness, unmanifest, reaching toward you.

Then the two terms from Ra. Intelligent infinity, they say, could be linked with consciousness, in that intelligent infinity is the Creator in its latent state. The state the Creator enjoys before it asks itself, who am I, and decides of its own free will to bring into being a creation of parts of itself that will give it information about who it is. Latent. Unasked. Whole.

Once that free will works upon the mystery, the field created is called the Logos, the one Thought, and that Thought is love. Thusly, every iota of the infinite creation is love. And intelligent energy is love acted upon by free will to make the manifest creation. Its nature is light. Love is the thought. Light is the thought made manifest. When they greet you in the love and in the light, they are greeting you in the name and essence of all that there is.

And then the sentence that makes this session more than a vocabulary lesson. You, each of you, are that center, that nexus, that combines space and time and the physical reality, and time and space and the unseen worlds. It is not for the animals to do this, they say. It is not for the wind and the water, fire and earth. It is for that miracle of self-awareness that you are, to hold, in one fragile yet eternal shape, all that there is in the temporal world and all that there is in infinity and eternity.

I find that staggering and oddly consoling. You are the place where the manifest and the unmanifest meet. It is into your instrument that the Creator's infinite energy of love and light can flow, they say. It is from your open heart that that same love and light may be blessed by you and allowed to move into the creation around you. You are not a bystander in the cosmos. You are the crossing point.

So to hold the four words once more. Consciousness is the field. Spirit is the unmanifest portion of it, reaching in. Intelligent infinity is the Creator before the question. Intelligent energy is love, set in motion by free will, becoming light, becoming worlds. And you are the nexus where they all touch.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Witness Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the witness within.

The question this February evening is about the mind's power over truth. Various mystical teachings, the group says, posit a ground-level essential self, untouched by the wayward thoughts of the conscious mind. If that is so, what power do our surface thoughts have, both to reveal and to obscure truth. And which matters more, the content of our thoughts, or our attachment to them.

Q'uo begins with a small story about the tuning song the group sang before the session. Someone sang Somewhere Over the Rainbow and got the lyrics wrong, but caught the feeling and the vibration the songwriter intended. It is not that your thoughts are not important, they say. They are. But it is an artifact of your cultural indoctrination that you value the thoughts of your intellect at the expense of the thoughts of your heart, which come to you in intuitions, emotions, feelings, and insights. If you stay completely within the intellect, you are caught in the ceaseless round of relativity. The thoughts may be bright as jewels and crafted with precision. Yet without love, they do not ring true. They do not show you flashes of the Creator within.

Then the horse and rider. The problem with the intellect, especially in your culture, they say, is that you either ride it and enjoy the ride, or you are ridden by it and a slave to it. The intellect needs to be in harness with the mind of your heart, that energy within you that is stayed on love. And when the heart sends up grief and anger and fear instead of love, they do not say to suppress it. Persist in paying attention to your feelings, they say. Honor them, allow them their sway, and you will find you can let them go down into the refining fire that purifies even the darkest feelings, until you are as supple with your feelings as you are with your thoughts.

Their practical image is the driver with the reins. Become silent, so that neither intellect nor feelings are being stimulated but you are simply being. The silence resets and refreshes both. And do not pull hard on the reins. A light but firm hand is what they recommend, so that not only do your thoughts not carry you away, but your feelings do not carry you away either. You are in the driver's seat, moderating, paying attention to all that occurs inwardly as you go.

Then the heart of the session, and one of the great sentences of this archive. You are not your thoughts, nor are you your feelings. You are the entity, part of the Godhead principle, who is witnessing these thoughts and feelings, and who, from these thoughts and feelings, develops desires. Everything you think and feel is grist for the mill, they say, grist for the mill of your witness, grist for the mill of your choices. Good. Useful. But to be attached to a thought or a feeling is to allow that thought or feeling to ride you. The rider becomes the ridden.

As for the ground of being the group asked about, yes, they say, there is one, and for each of you it is the same. The ground of being is that one great original Thought, the Logos, which has created all that there is in the seen worlds and the unseen worlds as well. Another word for that Logos is love. You cannot be other than love. There is no other essence within the creation. When at last you come to the essence of yourself and feel the heart of you, it is a heart full of love.

I love the way they close the loop. Why the deep illusion, then. Why can we not simply know we are love. Were you to experience yourself as just like each other, they say, there would be no point in the manifested worlds. You are an explorer, gathering information with mind and heart, following your desires, and learning who the Creator is by learning who you are. The thoughts are the equipment. The witness is the traveler. Do not confuse the two.

Thank you for listening.

title: Out of Control, In Tune
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: out of control, in tune.

This is a channeling circle session, and the question is about the unconscious. What is the connection between drive, psychic energy, and the unconscious mind. And is there anything we can do to protect ourselves when dreams, or problems, rise up from the deep and spill into the conscious day.

Q'uo begins with a sentence that stops you cold. One wishes often to control one's experience. And surely there is nothing less possible than to control one's experience, if one wishes to be a seeker and to grow. The genius of living in an illusion in which one cannot see what is occurring on the vast and cosmic level, they say, is that when one is out of control and in the murk, the mysteries and paradoxes of everyday life sharpen one's experiences greatly. One is out of control. One will remain out of control. And being out of control, one can experience the glory, even the majesty, of primal experience.

I find that strangely liberating. The spiritual life is not a project of getting control. It is a project of learning what to do while out of control. And what you can do, they say, comes down to two elements. That which involves the waking consciousness, and that which involves sleep.

For the waking day, they offer the image of tuning. The experience of waking life is a dance in which the music must be heard before one can react to it. It is a spontaneous dance. Yet if one has set one's intention for the day, one is entering the dance from a vibratory level which has been chosen by the seeker. You do not choreograph the day. You tune the instrument, and then you dance.

And when the tuning slips, as it will, there are ways to restore it. Very brief ones, they say, such as naming the name of that which represents love to you, or calling upon love itself. And longer ones, meditation, prayer, the intoning of chants, working with nature, remembering certain key phrases that restore tuning because of their beauty. There are an infinite number of ways, they say. They all require setting your intention, and then, without judging or being disturbed by the movement away from the desired tuning, working to come into remembrance.

Then sleep, which they describe as a journey into completely uncharted waters. Moving closer to that threshold between the conscious mind and the geology and geography of the archetypal mind, with its water system of emotions and its various watersheds. Before that journey, they say, you may hedge yourself about with aid, from angelic sources, from the inner planes, from your guidance and your essential self, simply by asking for help. Setting the intention to rely upon that help creates a foundation for the dream life.

They also speak of becoming aware within the dream itself. The simple remembrance that this is a dream, they say, is very helpful in reducing the pain of what occurs in the dream world. Causing the image of the self within the dream to move, even the movement of an arm or the opening and closing of an eye, is very powerful. Above all, set the intention to use dreamtime for service to the one infinite Creator and the radiation of light. Then the self, known and unknown, arranges itself to maximize what dreaming can teach.

The session's closing counsel is the one I carry with me. Remembering that all that occurs in experience, waking or sleeping, is some distortion of love, gives you the path back to love itself. And you are, above all, creatures of love. The dream that frightens you, the mood that ambushes you, the day that will not be controlled, all of it is love in a strange costume. Tune the instrument. Name the name. And dance.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Dogma of Service
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no dogma of service.

The question this March evening begins with a quote from Ra. It is not desirable or helpful, Ra said, for an entity by itself to control thought processes or impulses, except where they may result in actions not consonant with the Law of One. The group wants to understand the paradox underneath. If all things are one, how can any action not be consonant with the Law of One. And where is the line.

Q'uo calls it one of the knottiest issues there is, and they refuse to resolve it with a rulebook. In our humble opinion, they say, questions of what is service to others and what is service to self are endlessly subjective. One cannot create a dogma or a creed of service to others. In the history of your planet, attempts to do so have always failed. They recite the commandments, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not commit adultery, and then deliver the line that undoes them. As soon as you raise a temple of truth or a pillar of rule, rightness, or righteousness, you simply beg for that exception that proves the rule, that anomaly that undoes the pillar of truth.

What binds you in unity, they say, is not anything the senses can meet. It is your source, your ending, and your essence. Your source is love, the great original Thought. You are sparks of the Godhead, and your connections with one another, even a touch of auras for an instant, last forever. You store and expend energy. A light within you moves ceaselessly through your energy body and back to the one infinite Creator. And you color that light with your intentions. Your power to intensify the light passing through you stems from your growing awareness that you have a will, and that you can use that will to set your intention and create the universe that you wish to create.

So how do you choose, moment to moment, without a creed. They offer two ways. The first is the way of devotion. Focus intensely and persistently upon the Creator, hungering and thirsting for the Creator, and when you come to a choice point, cry out, lead me, Lord. The spirit is quick to answer the call, they say, and angels flock to one who seeks not the kingdom of this world but the will of the Father. In the session, the instrument even sings it. Lead me, Lord, lead me in thy righteousness. Make thy way known before my face.

The second way is for those to whom devotion is a dry and arid desert. The way of the mind and the heart. Ask yourself, analyzing this moment, where is the service. Where is the love. And then engage the heart again. Where in this choice does my heart open. What choice makes me feel energy moving through my heart. Am I increasing unity. Am I increasing love. Am I offering consolation, support, sympathy. Am I listening. All of these, they say, are ways of saying, am I opening my heart.

And the image they leave you with is a small defiant candle. It is almost as if there was a tide of judgment in the world that wants to put out the light, that wants to make differences that judge people, that wants to make people not okay. And against that rising tide of darkness stands the candle, the frail, feeble, flickering candle of the love that is moving through your heart at this time. Yet all of the darkness in the world cannot put out the light in your heart. So this little light of yours, you can let it shine, without fear that by loving instead of judging you shall be diminished.

As for Ra's original line, Q'uo clarifies the level it was spoken on. At the level of choice of polarity, the very first rule is free will. Your rights as a spiritual entity under the Law of One end at the tip of your nose, the end of your fingers and your teeth. It does not infringe upon others to think what you will. To think thoughts of three hundred sixty degrees is part of exploring who you are. The line is drawn not at thought, but at infringement. No dogma. Only the open heart, and the question it keeps asking. Where is the love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Gaze at Chaos, Respond in Peace
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: gaze at chaos, respond in peace.

The question this September morning is about the turning of an age. The group is thinking about the winter solstice of twenty twelve, the date so many teachings pointed to, and they ask what they can do now, in the time remaining, to help themselves and their loved ones and their planet make the transition as harmoniously as possible.

Q'uo answers with the most domestic image imaginable, and I think that is the point. Preparing for the shift of the ages, they say, is like preparing for a holiday feast. There is the feeling of needing to prepare, to cook the food, to bake the turkey, to make the cranberry sauce, to set the table. Buy the presents. Wear the special clothes. Plan where everyone shall sleep. All of these elements, they say, are part of a useful attitude. Do not sneer at the ordinary preparations. The sacred has always arrived through the kitchen door.

Then the teaching underneath the image. You are saying goodbye, they say, to the yellow-ray density, the density of choice. And the shift is a shift in the center of gravity of your thinking. From wondering whether you should get a new appliance or toy, to wondering how you shall marshal the resources so that all who are alive and bear the human genome have enough. From duty to your family and your nation, to concern for all humanity. It is the difference between the legalistic mind and the open heart.

Which raises the question they ask outright. What is enough. You have lived in a culture, they say, that suspects that word is null and void, that you will never have enough. It is ironic that many of those who have a great deal of money are consumed with making more and stashing it away, and finding a safe place to survive. One of the best gifts you can give yourself at this time, they say, is to release thoughts of making sure you can survive.

They are practical about it, not reckless. Keep extra water, they say, against a power outage. Plan, indeed. But if someone comes to your door hungry, take half the peanut butter sandwich that is all you have left and share it, for that entity is you, and you are he. Do not concern yourselves with tomorrow. In the Lord's Prayer, the request is to have enough for today. Give us this day our daily bread. Tomorrow you may pray that prayer again.

Then the passage that names this episode. Your gift at this time, they say, is to gaze at the chaos and respond in peace. To gaze at the hostility, and respond in compassion. To listen to those whom your intellect would call idiots take over the public airwaves, and respond with a smile. You are not the boss of anyone. You do not have to correct anyone. Let the world wag. Look to your inner tuning.

And they name the one word they had not yet used, the perfect gift for such a time. Forgiveness. What have you not forgiven yourself for today, they ask. Find the time to sit with yourself until you are self-forgiven. Because you need to gather all of yourself into your heart, and that includes those parts you have called the shadow side. You are your own savior in this, they say. Not because you are alone, but because no one else can do the gathering for you.

The session closes with a school metaphor I love. You came into this incarnation to learn, and your semester hours have stacked up. Nobody is only taking twelve hours. Everyone is going for fifteen, eighteen, some are working on twenty-one. Do not demand of yourself that you achieve anything measurable, they say. It is the keys to unknowing that will serve you in these latter hours, not the keys of knowing. Find your joy. Find your laughter. Find that place within you that loves yourself, and accept yourself, because that makes of you a co-creator that will love others and accept others.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dance of Synchronicity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dance of synchronicity.

The question this September evening is about those moments when life seems to wink at you. A book falls open to the page you needed. A stranger says the sentence you were thinking. A song on the radio answers a question you had not asked aloud. The group wants to know how synchronicity works, and whether there are guides or angels arranging it, or whether it is something that happens inside us when we are ready to see it.

Q'uo begins where they so often begin, a few steps back. All things are one, they say. You dwell in a completely unified and interactive universe. Within your everyday consensus reality it is counterintuitive to say that you are part of all you see, and that all whom you see act as a hall of mirrors for you. Yet it is so. All of nature, the elements, the plants and animals, the air you breathe and the water you drink, are dancing in rhythm. And you are either part of that dance or you have not yet awakened to the true state in which you actually dwell.

They describe the awakening the way a biography might. One day you realize that what you thought was your consciousness was a mix of politics and social training and enculturation. You step out of the box. You read until you burn out, meditate until you make yourself crazy. And slowly you begin to dwell in silence, that silence in which you are able to hear the still, small voice that speaks to your heart of hearts. You realize the walk you are walking is not a physical road. In Carla's mystical Christianity, they say, it is the King's Highway, and it is walked not in space and time but in the unseen worlds of time and space. That is where you, as a citizen of eternity, have never stopped dwelling.

There is a wonderful phrase for the chattering mind. The monkey mind, Carla calls it, the biocomputer you were born with, that excellent choice maker and that slave driver. When you let that mind rest, consciousness, which unlike your brain is common to all, lets you think differently, see differently, understand differently. Silence, they say, is the key that opens the door to understanding.

Then the leap. Why would any rational being leave the solid earth of what can be proven and leap into the abyss of the mysterious and paradoxical. Because that is where spiritual growth takes place. They picture the old maps with their warning, here be dragons. There are indeed mighty denizens of the abyss of midair, they say, yet they are those which not only guard the treasures of love and understanding, but guard you, each of you, as you seek along the King's Highway.

And here is how synchronicity works, in their telling. Once you have taken the leap into faith, you set into motion a different set of rules. You are awake, vibrant, magical, dancing with the energies around you. And your thoughts change their behavior. When you have a thought, they say, it doesn't simply roll around in your head and go clunk like a gutter ball at the bowling alley. The thought moves out into the dance. And that which wants to respond to that thought begins to find ways to enter into your reality. Entities meet. A song on the radio says, yes, that thought you were thinking just then is very good, keep that up. Your totem might show up. The tree you were drawn to, the bird that speaks to you, finds a way to appear in your reality to underscore a train of thought.

They add a practical courtesy. Remember to thank the unseen guidance, your higher self, your angels, those ministering beings attracted to you by your vibration. Ask them every day for their help and thank them for being with you. That frees them, they say, to enter more fully into offering you synchronicities.

And the last counsel is about proof. You will find, they say, that when things are truly oriented to the spiritual there is no way of proving it that people will believe. It is useless to try. There is no other entity you have to convince. What you are attempting to do is orient yourself, once you have left the box, in a larger and more puzzling universe. So pay attention to the synchronicities you can. They are there to help you build your subjective awareness of the truth. Once you begin to treat them as valid, they will come thick and fast, almost more than you can remember at the end of the day.

Thank you for listening.

title: Free Will, Love, Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: free will, love, light.

The question this September evening is the largest one this archive ever asks. Give us, the group says, a synopsis of the development of the creation, from before the first distortion all the way through the third. And tell us about the divine masculine and the divine feminine, where those two polarities first appeared, and how they split.

Q'uo begins before the beginning, with the only thing that is not a distortion. Unity. You and we are one. The tribe of humankind is one. The only thing in creation is the Creator, and each of you is a spark of that infinite Creator. You shall always be you, they say, through all the octaves. You shall take upon yourself sex, appearance, gifts, and limitations. And the challenge of third density is moving from chaos into mystery, from the scrabbling to know and own and have, into the relaxation of allowing yourself to be who you are.

I love their image of the seeker here. You are deep-sea divers, they say. You are not satisfied to skitter across the ocean of life like a dragonfly. You dive deep, and eventually you pierce the veil of otherness and begin to feel the threads of commonality that lie behind the shapes of judgment.

Then the three distortions, laid out like rungs. The first distortion is free will. It was by choosing, by free will, to know itself, that the Creator created the creation. His curiosity is endless, they say, and his sense of play and artistry equally infinite. It was a long time and many creations before the Creator tried the experiment of offering total free will to the sparks, and yet this is your situation. Your free will is paramount. The other person's free will is also paramount, which means your rights stop behind your teeth and at the end of your nose.

The second distortion is the Logos. When you open the Bible to the Gospel of John, they say, it begins with the Logos. In the beginning was the Word. The Greek for that Word is Logos. In the beginning was the Logos. The Logos was with God and the Logos was God. The Creator set its intention to know itself, and so were born the infinite billions of galaxies. Yet all things are distortions of love. The challenge is always to find the love, to see through the chaos that surrounds confused entities' relationships, whether between two people or between nation-states.

The third distortion is light. And it is only at this point, far down the chain, that manifestation occurs. Manifestation is slow in coming, they say. Much must be accomplished first. Yet you live in a world of manifestations, and so you are always climbing what Carla calls Jacob's ladder, only you are climbing it down, into the depths of your own heart. And there the Creator lies, beyond all manifestation, beyond all images, ready to heal, ready to nurture, ready to love.

That nurturing image becomes the bridge to the masculine and feminine. They are frank about the surface level. One biological sex is given the ocean of life, they say, and becomes a priestess who can conceive and bear a child. There is innate in women a certain inner power, and an absolute access to mother love, the love that is above and beyond all loves. Men tend to be larger, more directed to protect and serve. Yet both are challenged by the same ideal, which is to use their power rightly. And they do not flinch from the shadow. The male sex is aware of the inner power of women and is somewhat challenged by it, they say, and the instinct of a bully is not to harmonize but to control. It is a sorry mess your societies have made of the possibility of dancing together in utter harmony.

But the deeper teaching is not about bodies at all. When does polarity begin, they ask, and answer, in third density, the only density where nothing can be known, where the veil of forgetting falls.
