Every sincere attempt to love is registered in the deep ledgers of the soul. The attempt that misses its mark still changes the one who attempted it. You are learning the art of love, and no apprentice masters an art without spoiled canvases.

The teaching closes with a widening. Service, Q'uo said, is not something you do in addition to your life. It is what your life is. Every breath is an opportunity. Every encounter is an assignment. Every moment of kindness, seen or unseen, remembered or forgotten, is a thread in a great weaving whose pattern you will only see from the other side.

So be the stove. Tend your inner fire. Shine in the dark without needing to be seen shining. The service of being is the foundation of the service of doing, and the world needs your warmth more than it needs your worry.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Tone Poem Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the tone poem within.

The circle asked about the energy centers, the chakras, and the one they call Q'uo answered not with a diagram but with music. Think of your energy system as an instrument, they said. Each center is a string, and together they play the tone poem of your being. The question is not whether the instrument is perfect. The question is whether you are listening to it.

Q'uo walked up the scale from the root. The red ray, at the base of the spine, is your relationship with the earth, with survival, with the simple fact of being alive in a body. When it is clear, you feel safe in the world. When it is blocked, everything above it wobbles, because you cannot build a steady tower on a shaking foundation.

Above it, the orange ray, in the lower belly, is your relationship with yourself and others, one to one. How you feel about your body. How you meet another person honestly. This is where so many of the old hurts live, the rejections and embarrassments that taught you to armor yourself. Q'uo was gentle here. The armoring once protected you. It is all right to thank it and lay it down.

Then the yellow ray, at the solar plexus, the center of the self in the group. Family, tribe, society, all the places where you learned who you are allowed to be. Then the green ray, the heart, the great central sun of the system, where love flows outward without keeping accounts. Then the blue ray, the throat, where truth finds its voice. Then the indigo ray, the brow, the seat of the magical personality, where you see with the inner eye. And at the crown, the violet ray, the flower that opens to the infinite.

It is a beautiful map, and Q'uo immediately warned against using it as a ladder to climb. Do not chase the heights, they said. Do not try to live in the crown while the root is crying out. The most common mistake of the earnest seeker is to reach for the upper centers, for visions and powers and cosmic consciousness, while the lower centers remain blocked and aching. The instrument cannot play its high notes truly if its low strings are broken.

Instead, work from where you are. Q'uo's instruction was simple: attend to the disturbance that is given to you today. If your survival fears are loud, work with the red ray. If your relationships ache, work with the orange. If you feel invisible in the group, work with the yellow. The energy system is intelligent. It shows you, each day, exactly which string needs tuning. Trust the showing.

And here is the word of grace that runs through the session like a refrain. Do not feel that you have failed if there is coloration to your light. Your light will have color. It will have shadow. It will be, on any given day, a mixture of clarity and confusion, of openness and armoring. That is not failure. That is being human. The tone poem of your being is not meant to be a single pure note. It is meant to be rich, complex, and utterly yours.

Q'uo closed with the practice itself. Each day, sit with yourself. Run your attention slowly up the instrument, from root to crown, and simply notice. Where is the tightness? Where is the ease? Where does the breath catch? Do not judge what you find. Just listen. Attention is itself a form of love, and the centers respond to love the way a garden responds to sun.

You are an instrument, my friends. You are a tone poem, still being written. Tune the string that asks for tuning today, and let the music be what it is.

Thank you for listening.

title: How to Carry Your Cross
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: how to carry your cross.

If you are listening in a season when life feels impossibly heavy, this session is for you. The circle asked about suffering, about the times when catalyst comes not as a gentle teacher but as a crushing weight, and the one they call Q'uo answered with a tenderness that has steadied many seekers in dark hours.

Q'uo began with the image in the title. Each of us, they said, has a cross to carry. Not as punishment. Not as a cosmic mistake. The heaviness you feel is, in a deep sense, the work you came here to do. You did not incarnate for the easy stretches. You came for the hard parts, because the hard parts are where the soul grows fastest. The weight is not a sign that you have failed. It is a sign that you are in the arena.

But how, the circle asked, do you carry it without being crushed? Q'uo's answer was disarmingly simple. One act of acceptance at a time. Not the whole cross at once. Not the whole future. Just this moment, just this weight, just this breath. Accept what is in front of you, and then accept the next thing, and the next. The cross is carried the way a mountain is climbed: one step, and then another.

Q'uo spoke of what happens inside us when the weight comes. We armor ourselves. We build a shell around the heart to keep the pain out. They described it as an orange-ray armoring, a hardening of the emotional body that once served as protection but now serves as prison. The armor keeps the pain from getting in, but it also keeps love from getting out. And slowly, the armored heart forgets how to feel at all.

The way through is not to tear the armor off all at once. It is to let the heart do what hearts do when they are given safety: reveal what has been stored. Q'uo said that as you do your inner work, old hurts will surface, griefs you thought were finished, fears you thought were outgrown. This is not regression. This is the heart cleaning house. Each stored hurt that rises into the light and is met with acceptance is a stone lifted from the cross you carry.

There is a line from the session that deserves to be held close. This is precisely the work you have incarnated to do. Not despite the heaviness but through it. The soul does not grow by avoiding the weight. It grows by learning to carry it with an open heart, until the carrying itself becomes a form of love.

Q'uo was honest about the cost. There will be days when acceptance feels impossible, when the cross feels too heavy for one more step. On those days, they said, be gentle with yourself. Rest. Ask for help, from friends, from guides, from the Creator. You were never meant to carry it alone. The whole creation is rooting for you, and help is nearer than you think.

And there is a promise, quiet but certain. The weight changes you. The one who carries the cross with acceptance does not stay the same person who picked it up. Something is tempered in the carrying. Something becomes stronger, kinder, more transparent to love. The cross you carry today is shaping the being you are becoming.

So if the weight is heavy tonight, hear this: you are doing the work. One act of acceptance at a time. One breath, one step, one moment of willingness. The mountain is climbed this way. The cross is carried this way. And you are not carrying it alone.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Organ of Acceptance
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the organ of acceptance.

The circle asked about the heart, and the one they call Q'uo began by drawing a distinction that changes how you think about thinking itself. There is the mind of the world, they said, the busy, clever, anxious mind that plans and worries and argues. And there is the mind of the heart. They are not the same organ, and they do not speak the same language.

The mind of the world speaks in judgments. Good and bad. Right and wrong. Success and failure. It sorts everything it meets into boxes, and it is very proud of its boxes. The mind of the heart speaks in acceptance. It does not sort. It receives. Q'uo called the heart the organ of acceptance, and the phrase is worth sitting with. An organ has a function. The heart's function is not to judge the world but to welcome it.

But most of us, Q'uo said, cannot hear the heart's language, because the heart is buried. They offered an image: picture the true self as an embryo, small and tender and new, and picture it surrounded by a thick crust. That crust is made of everything you have not wanted to feel. Old griefs. Old shames. Old furies. Every emotion you postponed, every tear you swallowed, every wound you decided to deal with later. Later never came, and the crust grew thicker.

Here is the hard truth Q'uo would not soften. Postponed feelings do not disappear. They remain, stored in the body, stored in the energy system, waiting. And they wait with infinite patience, because they know that someday you will have to feel them. The crust around the heart is not made of stone. It is made of unfelt feeling. And the only way through it is feeling.

This is why the spiritual path so often gets harder before it gets easier. As you open, as you meditate, as you sincerely seek, the crust begins to crack, and what comes up is not bliss but backlog. Grief you forgot you carried. Anger at people long gone. Shame about things that were never your fault. Q'uo said this is not a sign of failure. It is a sign that the heart is finally strong enough to do its work.

Q'uo spoke of faith in a way that belongs in this session. Faith, they said, is the foolish expectation that within anguish there may yet be found joy. Not the expectation that anguish will be explained away, or that it was never real, but that joy can coexist with it, can be found inside it, like a seed inside the winter ground. This is not optimism. It is deeper than optimism. It is the heart's native knowing, speaking in its own language.

The heart, Q'uo reminded the circle, is a muscle. And like any muscle, it grows stronger with exercise. Every act of acceptance is a repetition. Every time you receive a difficult feeling without flinching, every time you welcome a difficult person without closing, every time you say yes to what is instead of demanding what should be, the heart grows more capable. You are not waiting for a bigger heart. You are building one.

They closed with a practice. Relax the body, they said. Begin with the body, because the crust lives there as tension. Breathe into the tight places. Soften the jaw, the shoulders, the belly. And as the body softens, let the heart soften with it. Do not try to feel anything in particular. Just make room. The heart knows what to do with room. It has been waiting, patient as the embryo, for the crust to thin enough for its voice to be heard.

The mind of the world will keep shouting its judgments. Let it shout. Beneath the noise, the organ of acceptance is doing its quiet work, receiving everything, rejecting nothing, turning the whole of your life into material for love.

Thank you for listening.

title: Strengthening the Will
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: strengthening the will.

The circle asked about the will, and the one they call Q'uo began with a definition that reframes the whole subject. The will, they said, is desire purified. Not desire destroyed. Not desire denied. Desire clarified, refined, burned clean of everything that is not truly yours, until what remains is a steady flame pointing at what your heart most deeply wants.

Most of us, Q'uo said, do not have a weak will. We have a scattered will. We want a dozen contradictory things at once. We want rest and achievement, freedom and security, change and comfort. The will cannot serve a dozen masters. It spends itself in the tug of war and has nothing left for the march. Strengthening the will begins not with effort but with honesty: what do you actually want? Beneath the shoulds and the fashions and the fears, what does your heart desire?

Q'uo offered the image of a muscle. The will grows stronger the way a muscle grows stronger: by being used. Each time you choose in the direction of your heart's desire, especially when it would be easier not to, the will grows a fraction stronger. Each small kept promise to yourself is a repetition. The seeker who meditates for five minutes when they said they would is doing will-training. The seeker who speaks the true sentence when the easy sentence was available is doing will-training. It is all exercise.

But there is an enemy, and Q'uo named it plainly: doubt. Doubt is the acid that dissolves the will. Not the honest questioning that seeks truth, but the corrosive whisper that says your desire is foolish, your path is hopeless, you are not the kind of person who gets what they want. Every time you entertain that whisper, the will weakens. Every time you answer it with steady action, the will strengthens. You do not need to feel confident to act with will. You need only to act.

The session took an interesting turn when the circle asked about the company of others. Q'uo said the will is contagious. When you sit with seekers whose wills are strong and clear, your own will is strengthened by resonance. This is one of the hidden functions of spiritual community. You borrow each other's steadiness until your own is built. And the reverse is true as well, which is why Q'uo counseled care about whose doubt you let into your inner room.

Q'uo also warned about the shadow of the strong will. There is a kind of will that succeeds in the world by overriding everything in its path, that achieves its goals by force and calls it strength. This is not the will Q'uo is describing. The overbearing will gets what it wants and loses what it is. The purified will is different. It is strong the way water is strong: persistent, clear, impossible to stop, but never cruel.

The purified will has a quality Q'uo kept returning to: it radiates. The person whose desire has been clarified does not need to persuade anyone. Their very presence is an argument. Like the sun, which does not lecture the planets on orbiting but simply shines, the strong-willed servant of love teaches by example. Others see the steadiness and remember their own.

The teaching closes with a promise and a practice. The promise: will and desire, rightly understood, converge. At the end of the path they are not two things but one, the flame and the fuel indistinguishable. The practice: today, find one small thing your heart truly wants, and do it. Not the grand gesture. The small kept promise. The will is built in inches, and every inch is yours forever.

Desire, purified, becomes will. Will, exercised, becomes strength. Strength, surrendered to love, becomes light.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Stranger at the Door
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the stranger at the door.

The circle gathered in a season when multitudes were fleeing war and seeking shelter, when the news was full of strangers at borders and fear in the headlines. They asked the one they call Q'uo how to meet such a moment. Q'uo's answer went deeper than policy, deeper than opinion, all the way down to the heart itself.

They called it the great examination of the heart. Every age brings one, they said. Ours arrives in the form of a question: can your heart open to those you call strangers? Not to the familiar, not to the tribe, not to those who look and speak as you do. To the stranger. The one who fled with nothing. The one whose customs unsettle you. The one your fear wants to turn away. This, Q'uo said, is the test of the open heart, and it is being administered now.

Q'uo was blunt about the alternative. Negativity begets negativity, they said. Judgment begets judgment. The heart that closes against the stranger does not stay the same size. It shrinks. Fear is a contracting force. Every act of rejection makes the next rejection easier, until the heart is a small hard stone that can love only its own reflection. This is the real danger of the fearful age: not what the strangers will do to us, but what our fear will do to us.

But the teaching did not stop at the border. Q'uo turned the examination inward, to the strangers inside us. Within every psyche, they said, there are voices that have been exiled, parts of the self that learned to dwell in the shadows. The shameful parts. The angry parts. The parts that do not fit the story we tell about who we are. We treat our inner strangers the way frightened nations treat outer ones: with rejection, with walls, with denial.

And here Q'uo offered one of the most healing images in the whole session. Those exiled voices, they said, are voices in anguish, and voices in anguish are voices in need of love. The shadow self does not need to be defeated. It needs to be welcomed home. Imagine saying to the darkest part of yourself: I am more than I ever imagined I could be. And hearing it answer: I am you. The stranger at the door of your heart is yourself, asking to come in.

The circle asked what a seeker should actually do when the world's suffering fills the news and the heart feels helpless. Q'uo's answer was practical. Send light, they said. In meditation, in prayer, in the quiet moments, direct love toward the places of suffering. This is not empty gesture. Love is a real energy, and it goes where it is sent. And then, with eyes open, watch for the opportunities that come to you in your own life: the chance to welcome, to shelter, to feed, to befriend. The great examination is administered in small rooms.

Q'uo closed with a vision of where all of this leads. Every voice, they said, will eventually join the choir. The angry voices. The frightened voices. The exiled and the exilers. No one is left out of the harmony forever. The dissonance of this age is real, but it is not final. It is the sound of a choir still warming up, still finding its pitch. The music is coming.

So tonight, consider the stranger. The one at the border and the one in the mirror. Open the door a fraction wider than fear wants you to. The examination of the heart is not graded on perfection. It is graded on willingness. And every willing heart makes the choir a little more complete.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Stray Smile
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the stray smile.

The circle asked about service, and how to know whether our efforts to help are truly helping. The one they call Q'uo began with a sentence that settles the anxious heart: where there is love, there is no mistake in service.

They started with motivation, the hidden engine of every act of giving. Look closely, Q'uo said, and you will find that your motives are rarely pure. They are many-hued, a mixture of genuine caring and less noble impulses: the wish to be seen as good, the hope of gratitude, the quiet fear of being useless. This is not a scandal. It is the human condition. Every act of service is an attempt to integrate all the scattered motives of the self into something whole.

The danger, Q'uo said, is not the mixed motives. The danger is what happens when service is rejected. Picture it. You offer your best, from the heart, and the other person does not want it. They turn away. They criticize. They misunderstand. And something in you recoils. If you do not want what I offer, the wounded self says, then I will offer nothing at all. So there. Q'uo named this moment with great tenderness, because it is the moment when service stops being about the other and starts being about the self.

But the rejection, they said, is also a gift. It is an invitation to look inward, to examine the offering and ask what was really in it. Sometimes the other person was picking up on something you could not see: a subtle pressure, a hidden agenda, a need to be needed riding along inside the gift. The rejected service becomes a mirror. Look into it honestly, and you will learn more about love than a hundred successful offerings could teach.

Q'uo offered a caution here that every sincere seeker needs. Do not turn the mirror into a weapon against yourself. The too-quick habit of harsh self-judgment is counterproductive. You are as much a part of the creation as those you serve, and as worthy of gentleness. When you find the mixed motives, when you see the dross among the gold, do not condemn yourself. You are learning. Consider yourself as a child, Q'uo said. You would not harshly judge a child for an unartful attempt to be friendly, for a clumsy opening of a fledgling heart. Grant yourself the same grace.

The session spoke of judgment in a way worth keeping. There is a skill the servant of love must develop, and Q'uo called it by its right name: discernment. Not the harsh judgment that condemns self or other, but the clear seeing that notices when an offering is unlikely to be received, when restraint is kinder than insistence, when the other needs space more than they need your help. Love without discernment can blunder. Discernment without love can wound. The servant needs both.

And then, near the end, Q'uo said the thing this episode is named for. Do not underestimate the significance of the stray smile, the gentle touch, the gratuitous act of approval. We imagine service as grand gestures, but the energies of the self respond more to the small things than we realize. A smile given freely. A hand on a shoulder. A word of genuine appreciation, offered for no reason. These are not decorations on the real work. They are the real work.

The teaching closes where it began. Where there is love, there is no mistake in service. Your motives will be mixed. Your offerings will sometimes be refused. You will be clumsy, and you will learn. Keep offering. Keep examining. Keep being gentle with the child who is learning to love.

And do not forget the stray smile. It travels farther than you will ever know.

Thank you for listening.

title: Wishing Them Well
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: wishing them well.

It is the first session of a new year, and the question before the circle reaches back to something Ra once said: that our society seems dedicated to the most stubborn desire for distraction, anonymity, and sleep. What does that mean, the circle asks. And why is the appetite for comfort and distraction so strong here?

Q'uo begins with a picture of this planet as a classroom many have visited before. This world, they say, is populated by a great many souls who have already had their third-density experience elsewhere, and who did not complete their lessons there. So they came here, across vast reaches of time and space, to try again. Many cultures, religions, and nations were built around aims that have little to do with the spiritual journey: ambition, money, fame, position, acceptance. This is what is valued, Q'uo says. This is what is practiced. It is no wonder that those who wake up feel frustrated at how many do not wish to wake.

I love the honesty of what follows. The spiritual journey, Q'uo says, is not always comfortable. These are the very questions that unsettle us: why am I here, what is this life for. Most people push them aside, because they make comfort uncomfortable. And there will be times when the catalyst is misapplied or missed entirely. But catalyst has no end. It will come again and again and again, until it is processed in some fashion, or the seeker grows numb and drifts back toward sleep.

Your path within this illusion, they say, is the most difficult path you will ever travel, because only here is the veil of forgetting so thick that it is not obvious you are part of the One Creator. But that same thickness makes this the place where the smallest penetration of the veil yields the greatest progress. It takes effort, conscious effort, inspiration, motivation, persistence. And if you exercise these qualities, they come back to you tenfold, a hundredfold. Cast your bread upon the waters, and it returns to enrich you and enliven you.

So what should the seeker do about those who sleep? Be not overly concerned, Q'uo answers. This is the line the whole evening rests on. Be not overly concerned with those who sleep, with those who are distracted, with those who seem anonymous. Give to them what you can. Give to them that which is asked. Serve as best you can, and go on your way wishing them well. That is all you can do. That is all any can do.

And for the seeker's own dark moments, there is the still, small voice inside. Listen to this voice, Q'uo says, for it is your greatest ally. Around it gather all the other assistances: friends, synchronicities, dreams, people you meet by apparent chance on the street. What is required from you is persistence and passion. What you seek, you shall find. It does not distract from your seeking to enjoy the daily round of things: music, dance, the company of friends, the rituals and birthdays. If the love and the light of the One Creator are first in your heart, all the rest is added to you.

Then comes a question that tests everything the evening has said. How do you see the One Creator in the one who does terrible violence? Take that one, Q'uo answers, and look beneath the surface. Look at how that entity was molded by forces beyond its control until it became a victim of the same violence it inflicts. Can you not feel great compassion and sorrow for a being that has no room for love or light within its own mind, within its own life? Every entity you meet, and every entity you will never meet, is the One Creator. Some are more challenging than others. But the Creator waits in the inner sanctum for the silent seeking of each, and there is enough time for all to find it.

However long the journey, it will have an end, and the Creator will be discovered within, and seen not only as the self but as every other self. This is why this time is so valuable. This illusion was not meant to be easy. It was meant to challenge, so that those who came here could learn the great lesson of finding the Creator within, and choosing to spend that finding in service to others.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Unimpeded Flow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the unimpeded flow.

Tonight's question returns to something Ra once said about the heart of evolution. Technique, Ra said, is not the heart. The heart is unity, love, light, and joy. But there was one phrase the circle wanted to understand better: smoothly activated. What does it mean for the mind, the body, and the spirit to become smoothly activated? And what does joy have to do with it?

Q'uo begins with the long view. Each of you, they say, has lived through many incarnations in this illusion, and many who are wanderers have lived through many more in other densities besides. Each incarnation has its purpose: to learn two or three or perhaps four major lessons. When incarnation after incarnation goes well, you accumulate a reservoir of knowledge to draw on, consciously or unconsciously. The entire creation lies at your feet, awaiting your discovery of it, and each life teaches you a few more of its infinite nuances.

And here is where the machinery of it comes in. Each day, Q'uo says, you receive a gift from the One Creator: intelligent energy, or the energy of intelligence, which enters through your feet and lower energy centers and moves upward through your system. When there are blockages, the flow is bumpy. It is not smooth, not continuous. The unlearned lesson, the unprocessed catalyst, leaves its mark as a constriction in the energy body. This is the body's way of telling the student there is more work to do.

Sometimes it takes many incarnations to unblock a single center. The process is slow. But when the mind, the body, and the spirit have each learned to process catalyst cleanly, then what was experience becomes reliable guidance, and the energy begins to flow without impediment. This, Q'uo says, is what it means to be smoothly activated. It is a rare thing in third density. Yet there is a threshold of smoothness that opens the indigo-ray center, and with it comes the quality you may call joy.

Joy, in this teaching, is not a mood. It is an inner signal. It is the subconscious mind telling the conscious mind that all is, indeed, well. From time to time, when you have the sense that an incarnation's goals are unfolding as they should, joy rises up unbidden. It is the sense of unity beginning to color your whole experience. All is indeed well at all times, Q'uo says, but within this illusion, that is not often experienced as a truth. Joy is the moment when you taste it.

And if the seeker who has touched this joy can balance the indigo ray with the lower centers, something further becomes possible. The experience can be released as a shuttle through the violet ray, and the entity knows the fully experienced presence of the One Infinite Creator, with its attendant joy and feeling. This is the enlightenment experience, they say, called by many names across your traditions. And such a being, they note, seldom wishes to leave the illusion afterward. More often it wishes to return and be with those of its kind, to share what it has found.

I find that detail quietly devastating in the best way. The highest attainment described here does not end in departure. It ends in return. The unimpeded flow, once it moves from the base all the way through to the crown, turns the being back toward others. The energy that found no blockage in the self now moves outward as service.

So to be smoothly activated is not to be finished. It is to be, at last, a clear channel. The energy of the Creator enters at the feet and rises unhindered, and what pours out the other end is not ecstasy kept for oneself. It is love, given away. Joy is the signal that the way is open. Service is what you do with the open way.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Harvest Begun
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the harvest begun.

This session resumes after a long quiet, and the first questions are the ones readers abroad have been asking: where are we in the transition from third density to fourth, the event the Confederation calls the harvest? And how will that transition show up in ordinary, everyday life?

Q'uo answers plainly: in one sense, the harvest has begun. The fourth-density energies are already interpenetrating this planet, in both its inner and outer dimensions. What remains unknown is not whether the harvest will complete, but when, and how many will be ready. That depends on the free will of billions, and free will, Q'uo says, is the most difficult thing in creation to predict. There are ancient forces working against it, and yet they shall fail, they say, for their day is short, and the light shall shine, and the harvest shall be complete.

Then comes a teaching about how harvest actually grows. You may know the concept of the doubling. When there is one who seeks, that is the cornerstone. When there are two who seek successfully, there is the doubling, and the third continues to double, and so on, until a critical mass is reached for the planetary population. Groups like this circle, gathering to seek together, are doing more work than their own individual destiny. They are aiding the planet itself in its aspiration to a fourth-density future, an ambiance of love in which the veil of consciousness will, little by little, fall away.

There is a tender moment of honesty in the middle of this. Some, Q'uo says, will not make the harvest, and the total is likely to be substantial. This is said with sorrow. Those who must repeat third density, perhaps for the second or third time, can feel despair at the prospect. And yet advancement can happen quickly, and the guides who watch the process are attuned to every glimmer of hope. Every soul who has participated in this planetary experience carries a portion of the secret of creation itself, and has the promise of bringing the Creator information that can be got in no other way. That is why it matters to aid every last soul whose yearning merits hope.

What is this planet's destiny, then? Q'uo says plainly that Earth stands at a crossroad, and that the largest number crossing the threshold will be of the positive vibration. This planet, they say, will be a fourth-density positive planet. There will be a certain number harvested in the negative sense, and they will find their further evolution on other planets. But what makes this planet unique, they say, is what its people have been through: an up close and personal experience of transmuting negative energies into positive manifestation. Those who have done this work will carry a strength, an insight, a vibratory character that other planets will gladly receive.

And the wanderers, those souls who came from elsewhere to incarnate here, have a double purpose. One is to raise the number who might meaningfully aspire to be harvested. The other is almost as important: to help preserve and carry forward the best of this planet's cultures, so that when fourth density comes into full flower, it grows on soil that has been prepared. The transition will be dramatic, they say, as the difference between night and day in many institutions. But there must also be a reach back into the past, a continuity, so that this planet's particular pattern of development flowers in its fullness.

When you gather together in groups such as this, Q'uo tells the circle, you are commended to the effort of giving birth to the earth that has not yet been but is very soon to come. All compassionate love shall find not only its day, but its cycle upon this planet. And this planet shall be as bright as a star in the heavens of a new creation.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Two That are One
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the two that are one.

Tonight the circle brings one of the oldest questions in the archive. If we are individual portions of the Creator, imbued with free will, how do we reconcile that with the idea that the crystallized seeker performs the Creator's will? Is there a line between my will and the will of the Creator? Or is the line itself the illusion?

Q'uo begins before the beginning, with the Logoi, the great stars of consciousness that first individuated out of intelligent infinity. Each Logos was free to create further extensions of itself, planets revolving in relationship, and upon those planets, the small consciousnesses of earth, wind, fire, and water, each imbued with the freedom of will. From that first investment of free will, the whole creation unfolds: an infinite universe of beings, each exercising free will to discover more and more the nature of the One creation.

Then comes the turn that reframes the entire question. Consider the spiral of light, Q'uo says, and ask yourself: who is it that spirals upward, and to whom does the spiral tend? The answer in both instances is that it is you. It is you whose seeking enlivens the spiral with its intention and desire, and it is you who receives this intention as a gift. You are constituted, they say, as both the whence and the whither. You are both the created and the Creator.

As the created, you bear that which is your own, and you may call this your will. But as the Creator, you participate in infinity, and infinity has intrinsically no limit that one would call a specific will. Here is where the difficulty lives for the seeker: what of my desire to evolve belongs to mere creatureliness, and what belongs to that which calls to me? We have no perfectly clear conception of the destination, Q'uo admits, and so we cannot perfectly say what the Creator's will in itself might be. But we can watch our own desires. Desire upon desire issues in more desire, until at last a distinction emerges: some desires express our beingness more eloquently, more inclusively, than others. And joy arises when will learns to converge with other strands of will it finds in its proximity.

Follow that convergence far enough, they suggest, and you arrive at a thought of a will that would embrace all possible wills. That thought, they say, one may call the Creator's will, or creative will itself. There is in desire itself an instinctual striving for unity. Love may enjoy the name of this unity at the point at which desire has found its direction. One looks into the eyes of the beloved, and what does one see but the Creator looking back? This, Q'uo says, is the golden moment. To the best of our ability to state the matter, this is the purpose of the creation: that the Creator be given the opportunity to gaze upon itself from a point of view that seems not originally present to the self.

A seeker in the circle offers a metaphor: creation is a kind of daydream of infinity, where each part within the dream is invested with free will and ends the dream when it is ready. Q'uo finds it apt, with one refinement. This is not a dream that fades with the morning. Each portion of creation moves in rhythm, expending its given energies on its journey of seeking the One Creator, and then blending its individuality back into the One. And each entity which moves beyond third density has, in some fashion, made the trade: the small will given back to do the will of the Creator.

And why the dream at all? Perhaps, the circle suggests, the infinity is whole and complete and cannot be enhanced, so the creation is mere play. Q'uo gently disagrees. The Creator, they say, hoped it could be enhanced, for this is the great desire of free will within the Creator and within all its portions: to know what free will can produce. If there were no creation, and only intelligent infinity remained, unwilling to do more than be, perhaps it would be infinitely bored. But being playful and curious and intelligent, the Creator made the game, the play, the many storylines, and thus the Creator would learn.

The will of the Creator and the will of the creature, Q'uo concludes, are from the standpoint of the creation ultimately not just two, but one. Not just one, but two. No answer to this mystery can be completely satisfactory. And then the final line, which I think about often: paradoxically, is there any other will to exercise? Thus all does begin and end in mystery.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Precarious Bridge
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the precarious bridge.

Tonight's speaker is Hatonn, the Confederation source whose specialty is love itself. The question before the circle is one that troubles every sincere seeker: if people experience the catalyst they need for their own growth, chosen before incarnation, is it right to try to relieve their suffering? Where is the line between letting someone learn their lessons and stepping in to help?

Hatonn begins gently. When you look upon those who suffer, and you are conscious of pre-incarnative choices, you know there is a reason for such suffering. Perhaps the entity wishes to learn endurance. Perhaps strength. Perhaps to empathize with others who suffer, so that it might partake in the strengthening of inner resolve to continue forward into the light in spite of the pain. This is true. And yet it is only half the picture.

For there is also the suffering that is not your own, and it is a different country. You have learned over a lifetime to deal with your personal pain, but to be confronted with the pain of another can leave you without any of the resources you have developed. It is particularly heartbreaking, Hatonn says, to gaze upon the suffering of another when you feel you cannot do anything about it, when you cannot take the full burden upon yourself as you might wish to do. All you can do is look on in sympathy and compassion, and open your heart in such a way that if an opportunity to serve should appear, you are at the ready.

This readiness, though, is where the discernment begins. It is deceptive to feel you are called to serve where no actual service can be meaningfully offered. You can attempt to serve in a way that feels to the other like you are forcing yourself upon them. Religions and healing professions alike have devised remedies and applied them with great certainty, only to discover that these protocols reflected more the expectations of the one who desired to serve than the need of the one served. And when the suffering soul is at its wit's end, it will grasp at any straw, and the straws prove of little avail.

Under these conditions, Hatonn says, it is easy to swing to the other extreme and say: perhaps the suffering is needed after all, perhaps it is precisely what the doctor ordered. That too is an overreaction. So the seeker is torn between too much of what one already knows and too little of what one cannot possibly know. And this, Hatonn says, is the dilemma of all who have sought to help throughout the whole length and breadth of creation from time immemorial. We too find it difficult to discern where help might best be offered.

What then is the seeker to do? Take a small step back, Hatonn suggests, and ask whether there are resources in the innermost heart, previously unknown, that bubble up to the surface in tender places where the heartstrings are tugged. For it has been our experience, says he, that love is the greatest gift one may give. And the act of opening the heart in love does not automatically override all suffering. What it does is allow one who wishes to serve to share in that suffering, to let a little bit of that suffering become one's own, to absorb this tidbit of chaos and let the pain have its sway in an alternate frame of reference.

One finds at that moment, Hatonn says, that love itself is not what one thought it was, but more. That within the heart of love there is to be found a resource resonant with the deepest sorrow, a resource in relation to which the deepest sorrow may find its joy. This is one of the most beautiful sentences in the evening's teaching. Love is not the absence of sorrow. Love is the resource in which sorrow finds its joy.

Two cautions follow. First, know the limits of your capacity to absorb the pain of another without being overwhelmed. Second, never abrogate the free will of the other. If the other does not wish to share that suffering which you would so gladly absorb, that too must be respected, allowed to follow its own course to the conclusion that feels right to the one whose suffering it is.

And if your gift is refused, do not recoil in hurt or anger or despair. If that happens, Hatonn says, it is a sign that you have overstepped the mark, however good your intention. Intention is not set once for all time. It must be continually revisited. The bridge you build to another is a most precarious bridge, here today and gone tomorrow. What works for the young no longer works for the old. What works for some does not work for others. Sometimes you are asked for something today that tomorrow will be thrown back in anger in your face. The challenge is to find a place within the desire to serve that is sufficient unto itself, so that you do not take rejection too much to heart.

Sometimes you reach out, and sometimes you do well to withdraw. The going forth and the withdrawing are part of a rhythm. And in the same rhythm, learn the other side of the coin: to have the humility to allow yourself to be the one who is helped. The helper and the helped are one energy, changing hands.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Greater Act of Wisdom
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the greater act of wisdom.

Tonight's question comes from a seeker in Moscow, and it goes to the heart of the seeker's path. Can wisdom suppress the opening of the green-ray energy center, the heart? Ra says love and wisdom are two sides of the same coin. But Ra also says that on the negative path, wisdom is gathered far earlier than on the positive path. So which is it? Does wisdom help the heart open, or hold it shut?

Q'uo begins with the world we live in. Your mechanized, computerized, digitized society, they say, requires you to move at increasing speeds, physical, mental, and emotional, speeds that seem to demand the omitting of what becomes extraneous detail. Like the listening heart's attention to another's needs. Against that backdrop, the question of whether wisdom impedes love becomes very practical indeed.

There is a kind of wisdom that is essential: the discernment of intentions. In this illusion you cannot see another's intention self-evidently, so you develop powers of judgment about communications and offerings. But here is the trap. The wisest among you may be deceived, Q'uo says, because the criteria you use to sort good intention from bad can be easily mimicked. And there is a deeper trap still. The self-protective filtering you develop, which seems like the better part of wisdom, is the very mechanism that can block your access to open-hearted communication.

And so the opening of the heart presents itself as a great act of folly. It seems like foolishness to open the heart, because when you do, you are vulnerable. Another may cause you pain. Another may reject the love you offer. And when the heart has been hurt, it recoils, and the next opening becomes that much harder. Q'uo offers an image I will not forget: the heart is like the springtime flower opening on the first days of bright sunshine, tentative, testing the air for a hint of frost. But the flower must open to fulfill its destiny, even without knowing what the day will bring. When it finally sees that its glory lies in being fully opened, even if this glory subjects it to the possibility of damage, then it realizes the destiny that is uniquely its own.

We cannot tell you, Q'uo says plainly, that you will be safe in every effort you make to engage others from a standpoint of love. We cannot say your offering will be accepted. You may find that those you sought to love will not love you in return. You have a saying, they note, that it is better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all, and this is true, but its truth does not neglect the fact that to have loved and lost is to have lost indeed.

So judgment has its place. Sound judgment is never to be despised. It is possible, to quote another of your sayings, to throw your pearls before swine. But here is the turn the whole evening has been building toward: perfect wisdom, Q'uo says, would counsel that no risk ever be taken. Perfect wisdom would counsel that the odds militate against the fruition of open-hearted interaction. And yet, if perfect wisdom always prevailed, the spiritual sustenance which is the very lifeblood of soul would be denied. Folly is not the same thing as love, but in a world defined too much by wisdom, it can seem folly to love at all. Therefore, it is indeed the greater act of wisdom to allow wisdom itself to be curtailed in the face of love.

Every offering of love is a risk. A risk can seem unwise. But life itself is a chance, and love is its main chance. And those who have become wise with the passing of years must realize in the end that the greatest gift life has to offer is the gift that surpasses understanding, the gift that puts one in relation to the mystery of being. It is a mystery that perpetually confounds the understanding. It is a mystery that cannot be made the subject of any wisdom.

The session closes with a question about the numbers: what does the fifty-one percent mean, the measure of service to others that makes harvest possible? Is it quantity of thoughts and deeds, or strength of intention? Q'uo answers that it is the intention behind the expenditure of energies that is measured. And when the circle asks whether simple kindness and compassion, simple concern and care for others, would meet the requirement, the answer is yes. That would indeed meet the requirement. Though Q'uo adds, quietly, that such simple kindness is difficult to find upon your planet. Perhaps that is the evening's real challenge. The bar is not high. It is just rare.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Dance and the Rest
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the dance and the rest.

Tonight the circle brings a question that will sound familiar to many seekers. Our lives are increasingly busy, often to the point of feeling profoundly overwhelmed. How do we find the time and space to work upon ourselves, so that we may become whole enough to offer ourselves in service to others?

Q'uo begins with something practical. Look at your schedule of energy expenditures, they say, and find one or two places in each day where there is extra time and opportunity and desire to focus within. Take a survey, a temperature, of your spiritual progress for the day. The beginning of the day is excellent for this. After the nourishing silence of meditation, take some of that inspiration and focus it upon the hours ahead, looking for ways to refocus yourself upon what is truly important: the seeking of truth, the finding of the One, the serving of all.

And then the sentence I want to hold up to the light. Perhaps, Q'uo says, this is the way to make up for the time that you do not have: by increasing the focus that you do have. If you feel frazzled by your tasks, take a few deep breaths, close your eyes for a few moments, and refresh your inner field of vision so that your outer field of vision is refreshed too. If the time is truly so short that nothing worthwhile seems possible, then use your refocused conscious intention to open your heart and share what is there, so that everything you do in your daily round is marinated in this loving vibration. Marinated in this loving vibration. What you cannot give in quantity, give in saturation.

The second instrument takes the question deeper, into the interior obstacles. When you set about opening your heart, you will find residues of old catalyst still lodged within you, like impediments to the energy you would gladly dedicate in service. Opening these old wounds to let them come forth can be very real pain. And you face challenges not only of your own making but of those around you, at a time when repressed energies are being loosed right and left. It is easy to feel overwhelmed and without resources.

Begin, then, with a simple point: you are all things. You are the One Infinite Creator in one of its infinite faces, and as such you have the full resources of that Creator upon which to draw. The deepest of these resources has a simple name, and that name is love. Turn your attention to the disturbed energy, the seemingly unprocessable catalyst, and begin by recognizing that it is you, and the disturbance is also you, and that it is asking to be loved.

By loving that little bit of energy which presents itself to you as unlovable, you subtly begin a process by which catalyst is moved to a higher level. And here Q'uo names a corner of the heart most seekers will recognize: the remoter corner where the heart is not fully available to you, not fully open to your experience, somewhat numb. Numbness of the heart is a common experience at this stage of development, and a difficult one to address. The slightest provocation can thrust the seeker back into a state where the energy to continue seems gone. But encouragement can be found, hope can be found, support can be found, such that the impossible begins to seem just a little bit possible. And the first break in a wall that has held for many a long season can begin a process by which the wall crumbles, and energies of a freer nature come through.

There is one more act required, and it is easily missed. A trauma, Q'uo says, is an event so overwhelming that it presents too much catalyst to be taken in at its inception. To process it, you must also forgive yourself for not having been able to process it the first time. There is a second element overlaid upon the first, and it must be part of the processing too. Be forgiving toward the part of you that could not bear it then.

And when the work is too much for one day, step back. This will not be work that is done in a day. Each here has volunteered to take on a certain portion of the processing of the planetary energies, and that is ambitious work. There will be periods in which you must withdraw long enough to regenerate your strength, to recollect yourself, to recreate yourself, so that you have again the strength and the joy for the undertaking. See yourself as a participant in a dance which at some points is quite energetic, but which allows its participants to recede into a quieter mode for a portion of the dance. And during those periods of rest, practice one simple exercise: non-judgment. Let the waters of the earth speak to you. Let the fragrance of the air surround you. Let the warmth of the sun warm your bones.

The simplicity of the open heart, Q'uo says, is the most difficult work you are called upon to do. And yet it is only allowing. That which needs to be allowed, even when it comes with a tincture of pain, needs only to be accepted, needs only to be allowed a part in the drama which is your life. Each here is a work in progress. Let the dance have its quiet measures too.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Out of Time
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love out of time.

Tonight the circle wants to understand the metaphysics of love itself. Ra has said that love is the great healer of distortions, and that love is the great protector. But how, metaphysically speaking, does love do these things? And why does our experience of time seem to change when we vibrate closer to love? Is something merging in us, the way it merges in higher densities?

Q'uo begins with an image of love as a carrier wave. When this circle gathers in love, they say, the love reaches out into the heavens and gives us a kind of carrier wave into your dimension, that we may perform our service. Love, they suggest, is a transdimensional kind of energy, able to cross thresholds of light that otherwise hold firm. Before they go further, consider what this implies: love is not merely a feeling that happens inside a person. It is the medium by which different orders of reality touch each other.

Love precedes the distinctions that make individual experience possible, Q'uo says. In the experience you enjoy, love can be seen as an activity in which you engage: you love another, you feel loved by another. But the roots of that activity lie prior to time and space having arisen at all. Love is the characteristic which most clearly defines the one original thought within the One Creator. And so love itself can be seen as a kind of transport from one domain to another.

Then comes the passage about time that stopped me cold. Reflect, Q'uo says, on the eons upon eons you undergo through your incarnational cycles, moving from one density to the next and to the next. There is a sense, grounded in the nature of love itself, in which all of these vast eons of time are, in fact, as of one instant. All time is always all together. Your present experience, in which the sense of remove from the original thought is about as strong as it will ever be, is the product of the veil of forgetting. The first effect of forgetting is the loss of the sense of who you are as a being connected in love to the whole.

That forgetting, they say, has been useful in ways no unveiled realm could offer. Before the veiling was discovered as a possibility, there was no concept of serving exclusively the self, because the residual awareness of connection made complete separation unfelt. What has been learned under the veil, about the Creator, about creation, about love itself, could have been learned no other way. And the forgetting is why, for you, the experience of love generally involves overcoming a feeling of being unloved. You are relearning what you once knew without trying.

What you call time and space, the realm where unity is more prevalent, is where those who have ventured into the focused work of physical incarnation go for respite and restoration. And here is the part that answers the circle's question about the strangeness of time in moments of love. When you are in your garden, or feeling love for a person, or deep in meditation, and you sense a spaciousness, an openness, you are touching the metaphysical. In those moments the intellectual barrier that separates you from the inner qualities of the spiritual world is removed, and you stand, briefly, where time is all together.

A gardener in the circle asks about the plants themselves. The second density, Q'uo answers, is as aware of love as is the third, though able to express it only in limited ways. As you tend your plants, the planting, the weeding, the tilling, and send them your love, they are aware of it on a very basic level. They connect the reception of love with your presence, and they shine it back forth in their flowers and their fruits. Love moves down the densities as faithfully as it moves up them.

In the higher densities, Q'uo adds, these experiences will be more common and easier to obtain, for there the veil is gone, and the unity of all creation is plainly seen. But the veil has given you something the higher densities cannot easily get: a reason to move from perfection into new expressions of yourself. Love as healer, love as protector, love as the transport between worlds, and underneath it all, the single instant in which every eon is happening at once. Perhaps that is why a moment of real love feels timeless. It is.

Thank you for listening.

title: Becoming the Author
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: becoming the author.

Tonight the circle holds two schools of thought up to the light and asks which is true. One school says spiritual growth comes through the suffering we go through, that suffering should be embraced and not avoided, and that faith and patience should be bolstered as the catalyst runs its course. The other says our experiences come from our thinking and feeling, and that it is our duty to create better conditions for ourselves, to change what we do not like by concentrated and focused thought. Both cannot be fully right. Can they both be partly right?

Q'uo answers that there is indeed a difference between acceptance and self-activation in relation to catalyst. But they suggest the two are sides of a single process, and that process is the very reason you incarnated. This is the key to the whole evening. Acceptance is not the opposite of creating your life. It is the first half of it.

Acceptance must come first, because the catalyst you are given is indeed that which you face. A significant portion of the failure to process catalyst, Q'uo says, is that the catalyst is deemed inaccessible from the start. One resists what is given, and this is catalyst gone awry. But acceptance does not mean passivity. The more consciously you participate in relating yourself to your catalyst, the more that catalyst begins to resonate to the inner harmonics of your being, and thereby the more you become author of your own catalyst.

Catalyst comes very often in harsh forms, Q'uo admits, in forms that suggest no immediate way forward, that look for all the world like something about which there is nothing to do but accept what is given and suffer through it. And they will not deny that there are days and days upon days when creation shows a somber face to the seeker, and the intrepid seeker can but put one foot in front of the other, day after laborious day. If you are confused, that too is something upon which you may reflect. As surely as the day follows the night, there is significance lurking even in the most scattered and confusing kinds of experience. Even confusion has a kind of unity to it.

What is it about this pain, you might ask yourself? What is it about this circumstance in which I have felt myself torn out of my zone of comfort, thrust into a world that seems unwelcoming, faced with faces glaring back in hostility or judgment, while I seem to have few resources at the ready? Even this situation has its integrity. Even a situation such as this bears a secret message. The situation is asking something of you, and the asking is the gift.

And here is the sentence I want every seeker to carry: catalyst that is allowed its play in such a way that it inspires you to response is catalyst that is properly received, and you should not despise your inspirations. Do not despise the restlessness, the anger, the urge to change things. The inspiration to respond is the signal that the catalyst is working. Acceptance lets the catalyst in. Self-activation is what the catalyst was for.

That is the nature of catalyst, Q'uo says, and it is a very significant portion of the reason you incarnated: to undergo catalyst in the strongest possible sense, and to meet it with only a fraction of your whole being, a distorted fraction at that. What you are working on at any point is something of your being you have determined is not quite yet in balance. And while your reactions may seem overbalanced, even that is part of the work.

So the two schools are reconciled. Embrace what is given, because it is given. And then create, because you are the creator. Acceptance and self-activation are not rivals. They are the inhale and the exhale of a single process, and the process is you, becoming the author of your own catalyst, one response at a time.

A note of care, before we close. This session also touches on grief for loved ones who have passed, and on addiction. Q'uo speaks of the departed as remaining in contact, their ties of love unbroken by the transition. And of addiction they say it is a kind of crutch taken up when difficult catalyst has not yet yielded understanding, and that facing it straightforwardly, with the counsel of those who know the path, is the way through. These are tender subjects. Take them gently, and take them at your own pace.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Most Eloquent Mystery
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the most eloquent mystery.

It is the Homecoming gathering, and the question is as simple as it is demanding. The Confederation sources stress the importance of seeing the love in the moment, any moment. But how? Can you suggest approaches for making a positive identification of love when it is not readily apparent?

Q'uo begins with a discipline for the day. The more difficult it is to find the love, they say, the more positively polarized you become in every situation in which you do perceive it. Begin your day, then, in conscious remembrance that this is your purpose: to seek love, to find love, to give love, to be love. Whether by prayer, meditation, or reading something inspirational, begin the day that lies before you by remembering what the day is for.

But a question rises behind the question, and the second instrument takes it up. Why, in a creation of love, should there need to be an effort made to love? The answer reaches back to the architecture of creation itself. There are three great distortions, Q'uo says. The first is free will. The second is love. The third is light. Love follows upon free will, because once an infinite number of sparks are created, each with its own will, there is already the distortion toward not being the Creator, and with it the need to return. Love is the return.

Yet there is another sense of love, prior even to love as the second distortion. It is the quality of the One Creator conceived as completely undistorted, unhampered, undifferentiated, unseparated from itself. This quality is mystery. Mystery characterizes the Creator in its undistorted self. And this mystery resonates down through every distortion, every facet, every iota of the creation. It is available to be participated in. And to our experience, Q'uo says, limited though it may be, love is always the most eloquent, the most searching, and the most fulfilling way of participating in the one central mystery of the creation.

I want to sit with that for a moment. Of all the ways to meet the mystery at the center of things, love is the most eloquent. Not understanding. Not mastery. Love. When you love your neighbor, when you love yourself, when you love the entirety of the creation with all the shortcomings you perceive in it, with all the difficult people you know, with all the flaws you can easily see in yourself, then you have the greatest gift to give the Creator that the Creator could ever want. The Creator becomes known to the Creator, just as when you love someone, that someone becomes known to you in a deeper way than they ever could be if the carrier wave of that relating were anything else.

And then the teaching turns to the hardest case, the one the evening's question was really about. To love those that seem to you to be unlovable is strangely enough an even greater gift. For when you find in yourself that resonance of love that can reach out to that which does not solicit it, but rather seems to reject it, you have inched toward a wholeness of your being, toward a realization of your own being as unified. And every such experience of loving the unlovable, every such experience of unifying the un-unified, is an experience of the Creator finding its lost love returning home.

The Creator finding its lost love returning home. That is what happens, they are saying, in the checkout line, in the difficult conversation, in the moment when love is least apparent and you choose it anyway. The struggle of your daily affairs is simply the effort to move love from diminished capacity into fuller capacity, into deeper realization. No knowing will ever exhaust the mystery. It is truly an inexhaustible source. And that inexhaustibility is something you may sense in a small way in your own experiences of love: that however much you love, there is always more love to be found.

The session's later questions turn to honesty as a catalyst, to intuition, to the habits that hold seekers back. Q'uo's counsel is steady throughout: engage honestly and stay with the exchange until it is complete; trust the still, small voice beneath the veil; and when a pattern has you in its grip, face it straightforwardly and seek the counsel of those who know the way. Every day on this planet is an opportunity to find harmony where there was disharmony, peace where there was unrest, wholeness where there was brokenness. That, they say, is more important than anything else on your list for the day.

Thank you for listening.

title: Rigged in Your Favor
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: rigged in your favor.

Tonight's question opens with a line paraphrased from the poet Rumi: live life as if everything is rigged in your favor. The Confederation seems to echo the same thought, especially about catalyst. In the earlier phases of development, catalyst is offered to the self by the Logos, but as the entity grows more conscious, catalyst is eventually created entirely by the self, for the self. Can you speak to this notion that the universe is working not against us, but always for us? And how do we use that understanding to take responsibility for our own creation?

Q'uo answers with a question of their own, and it is the oldest question there is. Who am I? It is easy to answer, they say, that you are a spark of the One Infinite Creator, an eternal soul working its way back to the source. And this is emphatically true. But that truth, known only abstractly, has not reached into the root of your being, and that root lies very deep within you, and very deeply concealed. A good portion of your spiritual journey is the work of letting that truth descend from the head into the root.

Much of what you call yourself, they continue, is a construction. From childhood onward you have built a sense of self, a sustainable vehicle for moving through the world and relating to others. Q'uo calls this your envelope of being. It has tender shoots and vulnerable appendages, easily damaged by the harsh winds of catalyst, so the envelope serves as a membrane, letting the outside in and the inside out in a measured to-and-fro. It is well to have it. They do not advise tearing it down prematurely. One of the ways to keep the atmosphere within it healthy is the company you keep: friends, associates, fellow seekers.

But then there is the harsher catalyst, the kind that shakes your entire sense of who you are to the very foundations and leaves you feeling completely at the mercy of external events, with no freedom of movement at all. These forms, Q'uo says, are far more common in your illusion than the gentle kind. And this is where the Rumi line is tested. Can you look at all the catalyst you encounter as weighted in your favor, as tending toward your development, your profit, your well-being?

Yes, they say, but with a refinement. The you in that formulation must always be allowed to remain in question. Again and again you will find you must release that portion of your sense of who you are that resists the catalyst on offer. And this is not easy work. The self you have imagined yourself to be must very often be abandoned as no longer sustainable in the face of the catalyst you have no choice but to confront. The envelope must sometimes be torn so that something truer can breathe.

So it is well, Q'uo says, to regard the world in its totality as tending, broadly speaking, in the same direction as your spiritual development tends. And it is well to keep this vision firmly in mind: that the story which will be told of your whole spiritual life, spanning many, many incarnations from density to density, is a story which has a happy ending. It is a story which blends, in a beauty beyond your ability to imagine, with all other stories. Keep that vision. But know also that you are on a journey of very long duration, with many paths and byways, and the happy ending does not spare you the walking of them.

I find this to be one of the most practical teachings in the archive. It does not ask you to pretend the harsh catalyst is pleasant. It asks you to hold two things at once: the clear-eyed recognition that some catalyst will shake you to your foundations, and the settled trust that the whole of it is weighted in the direction of your becoming. The universe is not neutral toward you. It is for you. Not for your comfort, but for your development. And the development is certain, even when the path is not.

You are blessed ones, Q'uo tells the circle at the close. With this thought, they leave the instrument: the thought that everything, in the end, is rigged in favor of your becoming who you already are.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Paradox of Seeking
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the paradox of seeking.

Tonight the circle asks about the seeker's relationship with the Creator. The Confederation speaks of the self as the Creator, and of greater awareness coming from that realization. And yet some of the greatest mystics belonged to traditions that teach an external, even personified Creator. Ra themselves speak of a yearning between the individual self and the Creator. Is it beneficial, or even necessary, to hold an objective, external perception of the Creator while seeking in third density?

Q'uo does not resolve the paradox. They deepen it. To seek by the path of service to others, they begin, seems to suggest you serve a being other than yourself. And yet all are one, and all are in the One Creator. This they affirm as true. Still, they say, it makes sense to place your seeking as if there were an other to serve. There, in a nutshell, is the paradox of seeking. For you are the Creator, as we have said, but you are also a portion of the Creator for whom it makes sense to say that you seek. And in seeking, you seek to become, and in becoming, you become other than what you were. And yet this otherness which you become is not ultimately other than the self which you already are.

Consider how you relate to your friends, they suggest. Those that you love, if they sorrow, do you not sorrow with them? If they rejoice, do you not rejoice with them? When you are with them in a true and open-hearted way, the boundaries between self and self diminish. A strange phenomenon takes place when the heart begins to open: the self is enlarged by including the other self within itself, not to dominate it, but to participate in the adventure of selfhood. At the point of intersection, there is a larger self.

Broaden this step by step, Q'uo says, including ever larger groupings and ever larger frames of reference, and one way of thinking of the Creator is as the broadest conceivable inclusion of all selves in the creation. To be sure, that thought leaps over a large experiential chasm, for the intervening steps are many and long. And that is exactly why it makes perfect sense, while the long seeking is underway, to fashion an image or a concept as the terminus of the seeking. There is nothing wrong, they say, with putting the name Creator to it, or God, or Allah, or Brahma, or whatever name has meaning for you. The external Creator is not an error. It is a waystation the heart builds for itself on a very long road.

And here is the line the evening turns on: the Creator thus can rightly be said to reach for the Creator within each and every creature. That drama is reiterated infinitely, level upon level, as step by step the Creator finds its way back to itself in the person of the creature. Every finding in the process of seeking, they say, leads you back to a deeper portion of the self where the Creator already is resonant. Yes, it makes sense to seek the Creator. And seeking seems to suggest you are not identical with what you seek. And yet every finding returns you to the self.

There is a caution woven through this. Some seekers conclude that what lies within is still grasped by a self that separates itself from all else in creation. That is a real trajectory, Q'uo acknowledges, and it can carry a seeker beyond this density. But it is the path of the open heart, the path in which otherness dissolves again and again into shared being, that they commend. We are both tethered to the same source, they say, and it is our joy to experience your joy as our own, our sorrow to experience your sorrow as our own. That dissolving of otherness in shared being is the pathway of the open heart.

So is the external Creator necessary? Q'uo's answer is characteristically both. Fashion the image. Use the name. Let the yearning have its object. And know that every step toward that object is a step further into the self where the object already waits. The paradox is not a problem to be solved. It is the shape of the road.

Thank you for listening.

title: Both Teacher and Student
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: both teacher and student.

Tonight the circle brings a question about the Earth herself. Ra once described those of us in third density as parents of that which is in the womb, the Earth, and said that in those days the delivery was not going smoothly. We also think of the Earth as our mother, giving us everything, including our bodies. So which is it? Are we her children, or is she ours? And how does our own evolution ease her transition into fourth density?

Q'uo's answer is: both. Yes, they say, all of you are both teacher and student to your Mother Earth, who is both teacher and child to you. And this is true, they add, throughout the One Creation, upon every planet that bears intelligent life. The relationship is not a hierarchy. It is a reciprocity. She mothers you into incarnation, and you, by your seeking, midwife her into her next density.

There is a riddle at the heart of this reciprocity, and Q'uo names it plainly: each moment contains love. Part of the great riddle of your existence is to find love in all moments. It is easy in most moments, they acknowledge. Some moments seem to contain none at all. And if it seems to you that there is no love in a moment you are experiencing, perhaps it is your opportunity to offer your love to that moment. Not to preach, not to convert. We do not ask you to become evangelists, they say. We ask you to simply radiate that which is the heart of your being. For in each heart there beats the rhythm of love, the revelation of light, the truth of unity.

Seek the Creator within yourself and within all other selves, in whatever form has meaning for you. This is the service you render to the birthing Earth. If your desire and intention is to aid her in her birthing of that fourth-density being which is you and many others, then you may see the opportunity to share love in any amount, in any form, with any entity, at any time. The circle you sit in is itself part of this work. Seeds are planted by each entity within all, Q'uo says, so that there is the possibility of your becoming more than you were before you came here today.

And the painful things? The traumas that sweep the planet, the suffering of peoples driven from their homes, the anguish of those discriminated against for their race or sex or beliefs? These too, Q'uo says, may be seen as labor pains. Each time there is pain or anguish of this nature, you may see it as equivalent to a labor pain in the birthing of the new Earth. That does not make the pain less real, or less worthy of your compassion. It places it inside a larger story: the story of something being born.

There is also, they say, a crystalline grid of energy about the planet, a network of portals through which the intelligent energy of your sun moves and is enhanced, especially now, in this time of transition. Those who are open to love and understanding may share those qualities with those about them, particularly in meditation. And these portals also serve those who are moving through the transition you call dying, into the larger life. The planet's energy body and your own are not separate systems. They are one system, breathing together.

I keep returning to the central image: teacher and student, parent and child, each of us to the Earth and the Earth to each of us. It dissolves the last hierarchy. You are not above this planet, managing it. You are not below it, merely carried by it. You are in the delivery room together, and the delivery is each other.

Thank you for listening.

title: Infinite Worth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: infinite worth.

It is a special meditation, and the question is one of the most human ever brought to the circle. What is the role of self-worth on the seeker's path? What are we worthy of? What does it mean to have infinite worth? And what do we do with the obstacle of self-doubt?

Q'uo begins with laughter. So, as you look upon yourself in the larger sense of your origins, of your destiny, of your choices to be here, you are indeed beings of infinite worth. I laugh, they say, because it is so obvious to us. We do not see the boundaries that are helpful to you and yet difficult for you. We have sympathy. We too have traveled this trail.

The difficulty, they explain, is structural. You are behind a veil that shields you from a true understanding of who you are. And for all the world it seems that who you will become must be based on what you have done.
