So if there is someone younger in your life tonight, someone lost in the miasma, consider what Q'uo suggests. Remember your own electrified years. Trust both your intellect and your intuition. Offer what helped you, lightly, and only where it is welcome. And above all, share the one thing no one can argue with and no one can take away. Share your being, exactly as it is.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Inner Company
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the inner company.

Tonight comes from the October channeling intensive, and it opens with a small, honest moment. The instrument is uncertain of the exact query that was asked earlier, and fashions the best approximation he can. Laitos accepts it graciously. What follows is a teaching on where a seeker can turn when the path grows dark and the mind grows doubtful.

The question, as Laitos finds it, is how the seeker of truth can find inspiration, information, and confirmation from the inner realms, from the spiritual guides and teachers each has attracted in this incarnation. It is a question every conscious seeker knows intimately, because it does not take long on this path to discover how much doubt and confusion the third-density illusion holds, and how much misinformation circulates about how a life should be lived.

Laitos begins with an inventory, and I suggest you take it personally, the way it is meant. Each of you, they say, has a number of inner resources upon which to call. You have guides. You have your higher self. You have those loved ones who have passed into the realms of spirit and yet hover about you, offering assistance in whatever manner may be perceived, whether a hunch, an intuition, a coincidence, or perhaps even a vision. And there are inner-planes teachers, drawn to each seeker according to the nature of their pursuit of truth.

There are many ways to pursue this seeking, Laitos notes, and no two entities in the infinite creation are the same. Whether you walk the path as Christian, Buddhist, Jain, Native American, or something entirely your own, each perceives differently, sometimes subtly, sometimes significantly. The inner resources arrange themselves around the shape of your particular journey. They do not ask you to become someone else before they will help you.

Through the second instrument, the teaching turns practical. Call upon these resources in times of prayer, in times of meditation, in times of contemplation, and in times of extreme need. The instrument's mate, Laitos mentions, leaned many times on a simple prayer of Jesus, being of the Christian mystical persuasion. The form of the prayer matters less than the reaching. A sincere call, made in stillness, is answered in the currency of the inner worlds, hunches and quiet knowings and timely coincidences.

I find this session quietly radical in its reassurance. The spiritual life is so often presented as a solitary climb, you against the mountain. Laitos describes something closer to a company of companions, seen and unseen, walking the ridge with you. You are not left to figure out the illusion alone. You have never been alone in it. The guides, the higher self, the beloved dead, the teachers drawn to your particular questions, they are all within reach, and the reaching itself is the practice.

There is a humility in this teaching that I want to underline. Laitos does not present the inner resources as a vending machine for answers. They are sources of inspiration and direction, to be consulted as you proceed through your daily round. The final discernment remains yours. That is as it should be. You are the one living this incarnation, and no guide, however wise, can walk it for you.

So tonight, if there is a question weighing on you, try the old practice. Sit in the quiet. Call upon whatever inner resource your heart trusts most, a guide, your higher self, someone you have loved and lost. Then listen the way you would listen for a friend's voice in the next room. The answer may come as a hunch, a coincidence, a sudden clarity. It has been waiting, Laitos says, for you to ask.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Joy at the Center
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the joy at the center.

Tonight's session comes from the October intensive, and the question is one of the most human ever put to the Confederation. How do you share what matters most to you? How do you give voice to the things you have found on the spiritual path, the ideas and dreams you cherish, in a way that another person can actually receive? Laitos answers with a teaching about joy that I have been carrying with me since I read it.

They begin with an observation about the spiritual journey itself. Traveling this path has, of necessity, a kind of prerequisite. Sooner or later, the time comes when you must give voice and feeling and emotion to that which you cherish. Think of your own life, Laitos says. The ideas, the friendships, the dreams you have held dear from your young years through your middle years and beyond. There is a kind of affirmation, a reality, that comes to these cherished things when you speak of them, when you share them, when you let another partake with you in the joy you have found therein.

Through the second instrument comes the image that gives the evening its shape. Think of an onion, Laitos says, with its many layers. As you move through your days, you are always trying to reach the innermost layer, where the deepest meaning is found. And in that meaning, at the core of the creation itself, there lies what lies at the core of everything. Simply love. There is love, there is light. Light without love is without meaning, but love without light is without manifestation.

And then the counsel that reframes the whole question of sharing. The joy of which we speak, Laitos says, must lie at the heart of any communication you propose to make with others. Not the argument. Not the evidence. Not the carefully constructed case for why your path is the true one. The joy. But there are very often many layers of concern that obscure this heart, layers of worry about being understood, about being rejected, about saying it wrong. The work of sharing is the work of peeling back those layers until the joy itself can speak.

I keep returning to how practical this is. Most of us, when we try to share what we love, lead with the outer layers. We explain, we defend, we persuade. Laitos suggests the reverse. Begin with the joy. Let the other person feel, before they understand anything, that this mattered to you, that it lit you up from the inside. Understanding can follow. But the joy is the doorway, and without it, all the words are only onion skin.

There is a tenderness in the way Laitos speaks of this circle of new channels, perceiving in each of them a desire to serve of such purity that it shines like a light within the heart. They are speaking to people learning to be instruments, but the teaching belongs to anyone who has ever loved something deeply and wanted another to love it too. A song, a book, a teaching, a quiet revelation in meditation. The impulse to share is sacred. The art is in letting the joy lead.

So tonight, think of the thing you cherish most, the thing you have never quite found the words for. You do not need better words. You need only to let the joy show, the way light shows through a window. Speak from the innermost layer, and trust that what is real in you will find what is real in the one who listens.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Fourth-density Blending
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the fourth-density blending.

Tonight the October intensive turns to the question that hangs over this entire era of the archive. How do we blend our vibrations with the fourth-density vibrations now engulfing the planet? Laitos, speaking through the evening session, gives an answer that is both simpler and more demanding than the question expects.

The simple part comes first. The most important factor in the blending, Laitos says, is your desire to do so. The vibrations themselves need no special invitation. They are always present, and growing, around you and within you. Your ability to open yourself to them is what determines how fully you experience and express them. You are like receivers, on a great scale, taking in these vibratory energies and letting them move through your being, to come forth as thoughts, as words, as deeds that make the new vibrations translatable to those around you.

I love that image, the receiver. You do not manufacture the fourth density. You tune to it. And the tuning is not a technique but a willingness, a desire held steady through the static of ordinary life.

Through the second instrument comes the demanding part, and it corrects a fantasy many seekers quietly hold. It is important to keep in mind, Laitos says, that the fourth density is not simply a new dawn in which all questions are answered and all work is done. There is a great deal of work done in the fourth density, and you stand now on the precipice of it. The simplest characterization of that work is that you are to learn to love. But that is, Laitos admits, an excessively succinct way of putting it.

What follows is a teaching on feeling itself. The loving of fourth density involves what you would call feeling, and love, as the songwriter said, is a many splendored thing. It is a convergence, an integration, of a great many feelings, diverse among themselves. In advanced fourth density, entities undertake to explore whole ranges of feeling, to work with them and integrate them into the larger whole called love. The feelings you find difficult now, the ones you would rather not have, are not obstacles to the new density. They are its curriculum.

Consider what this means for the blending you are attempting today. Every emotion you meet, the grief, the anger, the tenderness, the joy, is practice for the work ahead. The fourth density does not ask you to arrive already harmonious. It asks you to arrive willing to do the harmonizing, feeling by feeling, until the many splendored thing is whole.

There is a humility in Laitos throughout this session that I want to name. They are fourth-density beings themselves, speaking to third-density seekers about the density they inhabit, and they do not speak down. They speak as fellow travelers describing the road just ahead, with respect for those still walking the stretch behind. The blending, they suggest, is already happening whenever you let a new vibration move through you and out into the world as a kinder thought, a truer word, a more generous deed.

So the practice for tonight is not complicated. Hold the desire. Open the receiver. Let whatever feeling is present be present, and offer it up into the larger love you are learning. The new world is not waiting for you to be perfect. It is waiting for you to be willing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Alchemy of Weakness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the alchemy of weakness.

Tonight the October intensive takes up a topic most spiritual teachings tiptoe around. What do we do with our weaknesses? Not the picturesque flaws, but the real ones, the patterns that trip us again and again. Laitos, speaking through the Sunday morning session, offers a reframing so complete that it changes what the word weakness means.

They begin with the premise underneath everything in this philosophy. Weaknesses are not always what they appear to be. Each is potentially a strength in formation. For each weakness has the opportunity to make you stronger precisely in that area, because as a weakness it stands out, it gets your attention, and you focus upon it in a manner that changes it dramatically. And then the sentence I keep underlining. Each strength that you have, my friends, was also once a weakness.

Sit with that for a moment. The patience you admire in someone was once impatience that stung them into attention. The courage was once fear that refused to be ignored. There are no native strengths, only weaknesses that were worked with long enough to turn. Your flaws are not evidence against you. They are the raw material, already on the workbench.

Know then, Laitos says, that neither weakness nor strength is by accident, or carelessness, or happenstance. These are areas you carefully chose to work on before this incarnation, and they are key to your movement forward in polarization. The thing you are most ashamed of may be the exact assignment you gave yourself. The curriculum was not imposed on you. You designed it.

Through the second instrument, the teaching widens into the question beneath the question. Who are you? The obvious answer comes quickly, your characteristics, your groups, your history. But there have been times, Laitos suggests, when a response surprised you, when you discovered within yourself another possible answer to that question, one you might not have suspected. The pattern of spiritual evolution runs through many incarnations, and across them, the answer to who you are could very easily be different each time.

I find this pairing of teachings quietly profound. Your weaknesses point to what you came to work on, and your identity is larger than any single lifetime's version of you. The shame you feel about a pattern is the small self judging itself. The larger self chose the pattern as a doorway. Both are you, and the work is to let the larger one lead.

There is no scolding in this session, no program of self-improvement, no list of techniques for fixing yourself. Only the suggestion to look again at the thing you call a weakness and ask what strength it is trying to become. The attention you give it, Laitos says, is itself the transformative agent. What you look at with honesty begins to change, the way a dissonant note, once heard clearly, begins to resolve.

So tonight, instead of rehearsing the familiar indictment, try the reframing. Name the weakness plainly. Then ask what strength it is the seed of, and what small attention you could give it this week. You chose this work before you were born. It is time to get on with it, not with dread, but with the curiosity of a craftsperson meeting good material.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Artists of the Creator
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the artists of the creator.

Tonight is the last gathering of the October intensive weekend, and Laitos chooses to close it with the topic of creativity. What follows is one of the warmest sessions in the archive, a farewell that doubles as a benediction on every act of making.

Laitos begins by redefining the word. Creativity, as they see it, is the creative energy of the One Creator finding a home in each mind, body, and spirit complex within the illusion. Every entity in the infinite creation is able to make something new out of something old, to make something inspiring out of what lacked inspiration before, to speak a message of truth where no clear message stood. The arrangement of things, of ideas, of concepts, of sounds, this is the basic means by which your experience is made manifest in a way observers can understand.

Then comes the widening that I find so generous. Laitos looks at the circle and sees creators of one fashion or another, artists of one kind or another, in every seat. For each of you uses the intelligent energy of the One Creator to proceed through your day, and if you look at the means by which you do your work, or do whatever it is you do, you may find it is a quite creative endeavor with just a little bit of attention. And if you focus more attention in love and in light, you might produce something surprisingly eloquent and elegant.

Consider what this does to the ordinary hierarchy of art. The painting and the poem are not more creative than the well-run meeting, the carefully cooked meal, the garden tended with attention. Any arrangement of the materials at hand, done with love, is the Creator's energy finding its home. You do not need to call yourself an artist. You only need to notice that you already are one.

Through the second instrument, the session turns personal, and it is genuinely touching. The instrument has sent Laitos a message expressing sorrow at the impending parting, and Laitos answers it directly. They too feel a certain sorrow, they say, but it is a sweet sorrow, sweetened by the recognition of a marvelous opportunity to exchange energies creatively with this group. And then the promise. They are always available. If you wish their presence to lighten a meditation, or if on a walk you catch a scent on a breeze and remember them, they will be there.

I keep thinking about that image, the scent on the breeze. It is the opposite of grand metaphysics. It is intimacy. The vast social memory complex, the Confederation philosophy, the densities and octaves, all of it resolving at the end into something as small and human as remembering a friend when the wind shifts. The teaching on creativity and the farewell are the same teaching. To create is to leave something of yourself in the world that others can catch, like a scent, long after you have gone.

Laitos thanks the group for their determination, their inspiration, their open-heartedness, and for the energies they brought forth all weekend, which they describe as a joy to behold. It is seldom, they say, that they partake in this manner with entities upon your planet. You can feel, reading it, that the gratitude runs both ways. The teachers came to serve, and they leave having been served by the sincerity of the students.

So this is the closing benediction of the weekend, and perhaps of this whole wave of sessions. You are a creator. Your days are the medium. Arrange what is before you with love, and the work will speak. And when the breeze shifts and you remember, know that the ones who taught you are still within reach.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mind's Quiet Crisis
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mind's quiet crisis.

Tonight's session begins where many seekers secretly live. In the moment when the mind that has carried you so far suddenly cannot carry you further. The group asks about the relationship between the analytical mind and inspiration, and Q'uo answers with one of the most psychologically astute teachings in the archive.

They begin with how the journey usually starts. Rational analysis naturally leads the spiritual seeker's path at first, feeding the mind information about concepts beyond the five senses. Slowly, and by degrees, there occur what Q'uo calls intuitive experiences, seeming to originate outside the self and yet within the self as well. And when the analytical mind examines these experiences, it often falls short. Intuitively, the seeker feels there is more.

Through the second instrument, the teaching deepens. The analytic portion of the mind is a prelude to a kind of questioning that eventually leads somewhere the questioning cannot follow. It begins to appear that a different range of capacities must be allowed a place. And this, Q'uo says plainly, can lead to a crisis. The patterns by which you have construed the world, the habits by which you have secured your place in it, begin to seem at risk of becoming outdated. Old habits will no longer suffice for new vistas of experience.

Then the question that names the crisis. Who am I now becoming, if I can no longer think of myself the way society has invited me to, lo, these long years? There is a kind of crisis, Q'uo says, in loosening the tethers that tied you to a social complex that is, in many respects, quite distorted, distorted enough that it cannot provide the resources you need to move forward. If you have felt this vertigo, the ground shifting under the identity you built so carefully, know that the archive considers it not a breakdown but a threshold.

There will be a moment, Q'uo says, and it may repeat many times, when you no longer have an answer for where you are going. No means, by the old patterns, of determining how it stands with your course, your direction, your resources. In that moment there remains one resource they would never discourage you from opening. Inspiration. It is, they say, the greatest gift you can enjoy as a third-density creature.

But inspiration comes without the structure that would let you interpret it easily, without the form that would seat it in your becoming. So how do you receive it wisely? Q'uo offers no magic mirror, no one answer true for all circumstances. Instead they offer a question, one they have found useful at many stages of their own development. It is simple, and it is not easy. Where is the love in this situation, and how may I serve that love to the best of my capacity?

Consider what that question demands. Self-knowledge, to know the extent to which you can open yourself in service. An intelligent estimate of how you may be sustained in that service, and how it may be received by those you wish to serve. What is true of your capacity today may not be true tomorrow. So the process calls for constant review. And here is the synthesis the whole session has been building toward. Analysis that proceeds without reference to inspiration is dry. Inspiration that has not been tied to a specific intent is diffuse. The two need each other, the way the banks need the river.

A follow-up question asks about consciousness itself, whether it is a mental phenomenon connecting body and spirit. Q'uo's answer fits the evening. Consciousness is not one faculty's property. It is the whole of the mind learning to include what the analytic part cannot yet grasp.

If your analysis has brought you to the edge of its own map, take heart. The crisis is the curriculum. Ask the simple question, where is the love here, and how may I serve it, and let inspiration do what analysis never could. The new vista does not require you to abandon the mind. It requires you to let the mind become larger than itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Two Faces of Wisdom
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the two faces of wisdom.

The group comes with a question about something that sounds simple and turns out not to be. If wisdom is the goal of the spiritual seeker, what is positive wisdom, and what is negative wisdom? And how does a seeker on the positive path tell them apart? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo takes up the question across two instruments, and the answer is stranger and more practical than you might expect.

First, they say, wisdom by itself has no polarity built in. A piece of information, a technological capacity, an inspiration about how something could be used, all of it arrives with both a positive and a negative potential. It falls to each of us to sort it out, to feel for the heart of it, to decide what we will take up and how we will use it.

But there are marks you can learn to read. Information that tends to incite fear, that promotes a sense of separation, that suggests a way to make yourself bigger at the expense of others, that carries the marks of the negative tendency. Information that suggests joy, that opens free possibility, that suggests acceptance of others and the chance to be of help, that carries the marks of the positive tendency.

Then they add something easy to miss. There is a receptive phase of wisdom, taking things in, and an expressive phase, giving things back out. Both matter. When you are unsure about something you have taken in, ask what it would mean to carry it into your own life. Would it help make your world more accepting, more loving? That question alone will tell you a great deal.

The hard part is that the negative tendency does not always show its face. It can masquerade as positive. A bit of wisdom can seem innocent and still carry, underneath the threshold of your attention, a small splinter of something that pulls against everything you stand for. You only notice later, when you find yourself moved off your center and scrambling to make amends for what you have come to think must have been a bad, bad mistake.

And here they are gentle. Dealing with mistakes, or what appear to be mistakes, is part and parcel of the third-density experience. Nobody gets through unscathed. A good portion of seeking is just review and reassessment. The practice they recommend is simple: examine what you take in, regularly, so that what comes through you has been tested in the depths of your own being and found consistent with what you stand for.

Then the question turns inward, to the unmanifest self. The seeker is the creator of an inner universe, and polarity applies there just as it does outside. Those stray thoughts and imaginings, the imaginary arguments where you finally win, the fantasies of difficulty visited on someone you disagree with, all of it redounds to the seeker. As ye sow, so shall ye reap. It is well to know the seeds you plant, and the ground they are planted in.

And one more thing, tucked in at the end, for the seeker who wonders how the mind finds its lessons at all. The conscious mind, they say, has a kind of gravity. It draws to itself the concepts and qualities that hold relevance for the lessons it came to learn, the way a dropped stone falls toward the earth. You are, in a real sense, a small planet, pulling toward yourself the experiences you came to have.

So wisdom has two faces, and everything that comes to you wearing wisdom's clothes must be looked at twice. The choice, after all, is yours. It is yours concerning how wisdom shall be used, and yours concerning how you will take up the power invested in the information that comes into your hands.

Thank you for listening.

title: Crossing the Abyss
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: crossing the abyss.

The group asks about conformity and non-conformity on the spiritual path. How do you stay true to the inner life while still serving others, without cutting yourself off from the world? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo answers with one of the most complete descriptions in the archive of what happens when the self you have always been can no longer carry you forward.

They begin with a question. Who are you, really? Everyone has a ready supply of answers: your background, your training, your culture, the values you were taught. All of it weaves a richly colored garment you have learned to wear comfortably. But as you move deeper into seeking, that comfortable coat begins to fit less and less well. It shows wear at the elbows. And eventually it becomes clear that the self you have always known yourself to be is no longer a self you can continue to be.

This, they say, is the most trying experience you are ever likely to have, because there can be nothing harder than shedding the sense of self you have long accepted as the true answer to the question of who you are. The ego is built from imitation, copying the people around you, and from resistance, the thick skin you grew to survive the judgments of your culture, the daggers of expectation. The two combine into what they call a personality shell, protective and expressive, and none of it truly yours.

At some point the seeker reaches a place where they cannot go further without the shell dissolving. It has many names: the dark night of the soul, ego death, crossing the abyss, traversing the labyrinth. Whatever you call it, it is experienced as dread, because every use the shell has served must be sacrificed. You lose everything you thought you had. Every touchstone, they say, but one.

That one touchstone is the resolve you carry with you, the basic intention you set for the trajectory of your life going forward. Entered any other way, the abyss is an opportunity to fall into madness, to lose all sense of personal integration. But carried through by clarity of purpose and strength of resolve, by the commitment that the entire meaning of your life is service to others, you can come out the other side. No one can enter this experience except utterly alone.

And on the other side, something strange. You no longer feel part of the social complex that once defined you, either in the ways you agreed with it or the ways you resisted it. Now your only resources are those of spirit, and here the paradox reaches its height: it turns out that spirit has more resources than you could ever have contemplated. They come as flowerings of the open heart, needing only to be allowed.

What does service look like from there? Not what you would expect. Your best service often comes in ways hardly anyone notices. You do not need to leave a mark, because there is no self whose mark needs leaving. You can be as quiet as an autumn breeze. You can be as quiet as a symphony that never gets played.

You will not get much feedback. The one you serve may never know what you gave. But take heart: when you serve from the open heart, it is never in vain, for that which seems to miss its mark nevertheless finds its way home in spirit, unerringly. The seeker's path is arduous, and the world may seem to have no place for what you carry. But as long as what you carry is simple open-hearted love, they say, you cannot go wrong.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hallowed Ordinary
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hallowed ordinary.

A question arrives that many seekers quietly carry. We all have passions and desires and goals that do not look like service to others. A craft, a love of making things, the ordinary work of a life. Is pursuing those things self-serving? Or can they belong on the positive path? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo gives an answer that dissolves the question entirely.

You came into this incarnation, they say, having knocked upon a door. It has been said that if you knock, the door shall be opened to you. Your incarnation is that knocking, repeated. It is a door opened with perseverance. And as you bring that desire into your daily round of activities, with every action, every person you meet, every word you speak, you become hollowed out, and become a channel for the One Creator to use.

Here is the turn. If you follow the path you laid out before this life, in whatever way it leads you, you walk a hallowed step. There is no true distinction between what you would call mundane and what you would call spiritual. There is no line between the holy and the ordinary. You have within your being the ability to make holy whatever means by which you have chosen to live your life.

The talents that look obviously spiritual are the ones seekers tend to chase. But the rest of life is not a distraction from the path. It is the path. Every experience can be read for what it teaches, because the Creator indwells in all entities, in all experiences, in all things. At the end of your day, in meditation, you can reflect on what has gone before and find an abundance of teaching you did not see while you were living it.

What matters is the heart of your intention. What you hope to do, what you intend to do, is what empowers your actions and your thoughts and your words. And yet they say it twice: there is no service or action you undertake that does not have the capacity for service, for you are the One Creator in all that you do, experiencing itself, teaching, learning, in one way or another.

Then the line that holds the whole evening. You cannot fail. You cannot waste your time. You cannot waste another's time. For all times are holy. You expend your energies consciously and unconsciously, with intention or without, and they are as seeds planted in ground which may be fertile or rocky, which may or may not show you fruit. And yet each action matters, even the haphazard ones, for they can be used by another in a multitude of ways.

Who can say how another will look upon an interaction with you? There is as much possibility for growth in the most fleeting of experiences as in the long devotion of two travelers walking the path together. It all depends on your intention and your attention, what you give to the moment, what you see within the moment, and how you carry it into your own seeking.

Thank you for listening.

title: Befriending the Shadow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: befriending the shadow.

The group asks about the shadow side. What is it, and how do we balance it? It is a question every serious seeker eventually reaches, because sooner or later the things we pushed away start knocking. Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo answers with tenderness and with a practice.

The shadow, they say, is that portion of the self which cannot be dealt with clearly and must be put somewhere safe. Every culture has its customs and expectations, and whatever the conscious mind finds too disturbing to look at gets shut away, as in a closet, so daily life can go on. Each of us carries what you might call heavy baggage, full of qualities we shunned because our culture shunned them, or because of something in our own experience. That baggage weighs on us precisely because it is not understood and not handled in the open, where it could bear fruit.

And here is how you find it. Shame is the breadcrumb trail. The quality of shame, the discouragement from expressing certain parts of yourself, points directly at the darkened area. Follow it, and you will find the source, where it can be balanced and eventually erased, for in truth all is the One Creator, and there is no true shame.

These buried things do not sit quietly. They become blockages in the energy centers, the lower ones especially, and until they are cleared the intelligent energy of the Creator cannot move freely upward to open the heart. At some point the shadow finds a way to be noticed, whether as a nagging of the mind or as repeated experiences that keep leading the seeker to the closet door. Every seeker must eventually realize that the shadow side is a good friend and has much to teach.

Because look at what it has been doing all this time. It is the grittier, heartier, more substantial part of you, the part that has had to fend for itself, developing perseverance and endurance, waiting to be noticed and used as a full partner in your journey. When the light side and the dark side are unified within your being, they say, you have the opportunity of functioning upon all cylinders.

Then the practice, offered by those of Ra. In meditation, invite the quality you wish to balance to present itself as it most recently appeared. Look at that experience and make it larger, magnify it until it becomes outrageous. Then, for a moment, image the polar opposite. If it is shame, image joy. Let the opposite grow as large as the original. Then simply accept yourself and love yourself for having both of these qualities within your being as means to teach you love. Done daily, this simple exercise can remove the blockages that are really just imbalances.

The closing thought is the one to carry with you. It is not an error or a mistake that darkness exists within you for a time. The paradox is that the light grows brighter as you are able to absorb and unify and balance and work with the darkness within. So make friends with your dark side. It is simply another aspect of yourself, waiting to share its gifts with you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Muscle of Patience
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the muscle of patience.

This evening comes from a practice channeling circle, where newer instruments are learning to serve as channels, and the topic could not be more fitting for people learning to sit still and listen. Patience. Tonight, the one who calls itself Laitos speaks through several voices, and what emerges is a portrait of patience as something far larger than waiting.

The normal human mind, they say, moves at a very rapid pace, and your modern world of constant communication has made multi-tasking the normal way of doing things. All of this lends a busy-ness to the mind. Meditation tends to remove it. And to become an instrument that can perceive thoughts of a subtle nature takes patience, a quality that for most people must be exercised consciously, like a muscle. To grow the muscle of patience, you must have patience for the task itself.

Then one instrument offers the question that unlocks the evening. If you find yourself with a lack of patience, you are blessed with an abundance of impatience. Look into the heart of the impatience, and you will find that it stems from desire. So then the real question becomes: what is it that you desire, that creates the sense of urgency and importance and the call to action that generates the impatience?

They cannot answer that for you. Desire is the heart of your spiritual path, and discovering the depth of your desire is yours alone. But once you know something of your desire, you can place it in a greater context. Zoom out, and see the part that desire plays on your greater journey. And in that greater perspective, patience can appear. For you can ask yourself, when feeling impatient: is this experience toward which I am impatient not also part of that journey? Is this moment, which I desire to be done with, not a gift from the Creator to aid me upon my path?

Another instrument offers an image. See the polarity of patience and impatience as a circle, impatience on one side, patience on the other. When you find yourself on the impatient side, visualize the circle becoming smaller, let the two poles come closer, and come to balance. And with patience and impatience there is also acceptance and non-acceptance. Becoming in acceptance of what is will help you achieve patience. Try to remember that all is well, and everything is as it should be.

The deepest rendering comes next. Patience is an ultimate act of love. It is love of the moment, being in this moment, seeing the flaws and the beauty of every passing second. This instrument sees the universe as a mother, constantly nurturing us, giving us these instances of catalyst, but doing so with love, and having great patience for us. And just as a child becomes a parent in time, we too must learn this patience so that we may give it back to the universe and to one another.

The last word is a practical one. The impatient self is misaligned with the speed of the moment, wanting to move at a different rate than the rate at which the moment is moving. Acceptance is the bridge between the two. And the way forward is the setting of the intention: in bringing awareness to impatience, and desiring to cultivate patience, you set in motion the processes that engender its birth. The greater the frequency of the intention, the more space is created for patience to emerge.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Living Planet
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the living planet.

The group asks about our relationship to the Earth. From love and acceptance to control and manipulation, there is a spectrum of response to the catalyst of life. Where on that spectrum does our global culture lie? And what would a relationship of love and acceptance toward the planet look like? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo answers, and the answer starts inside the seeker, not out in the world.

The planet, they say, is more than a lump of rock floating in infinite space. It is a living thing, composed of many other living things vibrating in harmony and, at this time, also in disharmony. You are immersed in this vast vibrating system. The energy that enters your body at the base of the spine is drawn in from the planet itself, and it carries some of the planet's built-in disharmony with it, from the bones of the planet outward. You draw it in, and it vibrates within you, unless and until you are able to process it and heal it.

So when you contemplate being of service to the planet, the first thing to consider is how far you have gotten in healing the planet's disharmonies within your own person. The further you have come, the more you will be able to meet the friction of other people with soft-edged acceptance instead of jagged judgment. This is slow work, done again and again, and it is never complete. They tell us they do this work themselves, routinely.

Then they turn to something the seeker may not expect: the personality itself. Your judgments about how to respond to life have become structural, crystallized into your personality, and that is not a bad thing. You cannot process everything from scratch in every instant. But those judgments are often not well adapted to the circumstance before you. So it is useful to see your personality as an instrument you work through, one that can be allowed to thin from time to time, even to be set aside, when the occasion requires it.

The catch is that the personality is deep-rooted and clever. It can arrange its propensities to give you back a distorted picture of your own motivations. You may set out to be helpful, your intention clearly to aid a group, and then find yourself at loggerheads with a fellow seeker, and conclude, quite confidently, that the other is wrong. What is actually at stake is the nature of the energy investing your will to serve, the most elusive portion of your being, which can transform itself from one mode to another in a moment.

And so the heart of the evening. There are those who have so despaired of the root of serving others that they set it aside, and every interaction becomes a demand that others conform to their judgments about how the universe should be put in order. But ordering from without, they say, is almost always less efficient than ordering from within. Service is best performed by one who serves with an eye to the spirit that animates it, not with an eye to the protocols that seem, in judgment, to express its proprieties.

One more thread, for the seeker who finds fear rising in deep meditation. Those disturbing images and impressions that surface are portions of yourself wishing to make themselves known, blockages becoming hints and clues. Exercise the faith that what is expressing itself is part of you and potentially quite helpful, and the will to keep exploring it. In short: there is nothing to fear. There is much to discover. But it will take effort.

Thank you for listening.

title: Transmuting the Nightmare
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: transmuting the nightmare.

The group brings a hard question. Those of Ra spoke of offering to the spiritually asleep only the comforts meant for sleep. But what do you do when the sleepers are not harmless? When those who seem deeply asleep are causing real harm to the planet, perhaps leading everyone down a path of destruction? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo faces this question directly, and the answer is not what you might expect.

They begin with the metaphor itself. What is it to sleep? At its most innocent, sleep is a stepping back from full engagement, a comparative bliss, largely undisturbed by the catalyst that stirs us awake. And no sleep is ever perfect. To sleep is perchance to dream, and to dream is to receive inspirations meant to stir you toward further seeking. Sometimes a sleep is well undertaken, for a mind and body subjected to harsh catalyst, allowing the seeker to rediscover its center and rejuvenate its energies.

But within a disharmonious planetary experience, your sleep may perchance be vexed to nightmare. And here is the line to hold onto: there is that energy, that love of the Creator, animating even the experience of nightmare.

So what does one who seeks in the name of love do, faced with those whose conduct seems to build darkness upon darkness, anguish upon anguish, hate upon hate? The answer they give is the simple message they always bring: all is one. And from a practical point of view, it yields the conclusion that you are the one whose conduct is giving you difficulty. You are not two, but one, with the miscreant. You are not two, but one with the criminal. You are not two, but one with the one who wishes not only to sleep, but within that sleep to reach out and do harm.

This is probably, they say, the most difficult question in the creation. And they will say this much: to the extent that you can absorb the hostility offered to you, that is all to the good. One of the reasons wanderers have incarnated at this time is to take in the negative catalyst on offer and transmute that negative energy into simple, unpresupposing love.

And then they give the practice. In meditation, in as balanced a state as you can hold, invite in a little bit of the disrupted energy of your planet. A small nibble at first will suffice. Hold it in your heart and let the loving energy of your heart center infiltrate that fragment of disturbance, infusing it with love, until the fractured thing is returned to wholeness. With experience you can take in a little more, and a little more. When your meditation ends, release the healed energies back into the world.

But know your limit. The more radiant you become, the more disrupted energy will be drawn to you, unconsciously, because at bottom it truly wants to heal, though it does not know that is what it wants. It can build to the point that you reach your limit, surfeited with energies crying out to be healed beyond your capacity. This, they say, is the signal that for you, a good sleep is nigh. You cannot, by yourself, heal all the stray energies of this planet. Your group cannot. We of the Confederation cannot. Do the best you can do, and for the rest, humbly turn to the Creator and ask what there is to be learned in contemplating that which seems irremediably sad.

And for those who feel unqualified to serve at all, one final comfort from the evening's questions. Your own estimation of your abilities is irrelevant when you wish to serve. You cannot know how you may affect another by simply wishing to serve and offering what you have, however meager it seems. Intention is that which is important.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Measure of Awakening
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a measure of awakening.

This evening comes from a practice channeling circle, where the newer instruments are finding their way, and the topic is gratitude. It is a short word for a large thing. Tonight, the one who calls itself Laitos speaks through several voices about gratitude as a steady state, as a measure, and as a question worth taking into meditation.

In our home density, they say, gratitude is a steady state of our being. Within the fourth density of love and understanding there is so much praise and thanksgiving for the unity of the creation, the love that animates it, the light that it is made of, that our hearts overflow. It is an honor to be able to move further along the trail of seeking and discover more of the treasures of the One Creator hidden all about the creation.

But you do not need them to tell you that in your experience gratitude does not always come so easily. And here they offer something beautiful. One of the primary purposes of the veil you live behind is exactly this: when a spark of the Creator can find its way through the darkness, glimpse a brief glimmer of light, and follow it with faith, it is a powerful thing. The glimmer you catch is worth more, in a way, than the steady blaze you might have had all along.

Gratitude, they say, is simply one name for the variety of experiences you have that come close to a true recognition of the Creator. You already know the benefit of recalling through the day the things for which you are grateful. But they suggest something more demanding. Take the concept of gratitude into meditation and try to fit it around the experiences for which you would not normally feel gratitude. Discover the struggles, the disharmonies of your days and weeks and years.

Why, they ask, would one be grateful for such things? That is a fruitful question to take into your contemplations. Consider the blessings that do not look like blessings on the surface, and take them into a grander context, and explore them more deeply. You may find that there is nothing in your life experience for which you cannot manifest gratitude.

One instrument reminds the circle where they are: you are at the finest university in your galaxy. You are lights in your bodies, and each day brings the highest state of learning available to physical forms. When you are struggling, allow yourself to be present. Look around at all the amazing things happening while you were not paying attention. The sun is out. You are the sun children.

Another instrument is honest about the difficulty. Gratitude can be a blockage of her own, she says, and she feels she cannot be a clear lens for this message. But the message comes through anyway: it is by practicing acts of gratitude, moments of silence, being thankful for what is around you and making the best of it, that the vibration rises. It is a necessary step toward graduation.

And the final rendering. Gratitude could be said to be a measure of degrees of awakening within the illusion. It may be practiced, and they commend the discipline. But it also arises on its own as the being expands its point of view and comes into contact with the truth of unity. It is a natural response when the self that was astray and alone discovers the threads of connection it has with all things. The more time spent in this state, the more vital one becomes, because in gratitude the walls come down, the barriers grow permeable, and the self opens to the universe, increment by increment.

It is not a lonely feeling. It is a feeling between two partners. It rings back and forth between the One and the many, the Creator and creation, and in it is a mutuality of love that has its most concise expression in your language in the simple words: thank you. Take these words into your meditation. Contemplate the energy in them, and you will find the thread of gratitude goes deeper than your conscious awareness knows. And as you follow that thread deeper, you may, to your surprise, find transformation awaiting you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Appointed Rendezvous
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the appointed rendezvous.

The group asks about relationships formed before incarnation. When we have agreements and lessons planned with specific people, how do we find each other once we are here, behind the veil? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo gives one of the archive's fullest accounts of how souls travel in company, and how fateful meetings actually happen.

First, they confirm it is true. You are not here as isolated individuals. You are here in groups, families, clans, of a spiritual heritage stretching back through many lifetimes in this illusion and far more in illusions before it. Many of you are from elsewhere, having come to this planet over many thousands of years to aid it in its transition. The forgetting wipes clean, almost perfectly, the memories at the core of your being describing your origins, your groupings, your intentions. It takes real bravery to venture in.

Then they invite you to consider the question from inside the experience of the veil. Your consciousness glides upon the surface of very deep waters. What you think is the cause of an action may have roots in a reality far deeper than you can imagine. And the fact that these depths are hidden does not mean your free will does not reach down into them. Events that seem to overtake you, catching you unawares, can be bubbling up from a deeper place in your own being where intelligence and choice are at work.

Go deeper still, and something remarkable. At the roots of mind there is a pool of beingness where you are already in a condition of blending with other spiritual entities, intelligent, and in many cases incarnate along with you. From this common ground, indications rise to the surface, opportunities to follow paths that lead you into the proximity of other selves with whom you have this deep connection.

Now the question of planning. On the pre-incarnative level, many of these patterns are forethought, and they prefer that word to pre-programmed, because free will is irreducible, and doubly so behind the veil. No plan is ever definitive. All arrangements are a kind of expectation arising from within the intuitive dimensions of your being. And it is always given to you to turn away, to refuse the catalyst offered from the deep. That possibility, too, is reckoned in.

And here is why the possibility of refusal matters. Were it not possible to miss your appointed rendezvous, the rendezvous would not have the significance it has when it does come to pass. No one, they say, has kept every possible rendezvous. The veil is a powerful instrument of forgetting. But if you trace the intimate connections, the apparent serendipity that led you to meet and mingle your energies with others of like mind, you will see the workings of these deeper mutual longings come to fruition.

What are these meetings for? Sometimes great healing, answering a need you share with the other. Sometimes a gratuitous service, responding to a need felt by the planet itself. There are knots in the group mind seeking to be born, tangles at the level of the collective, and each of you has taken on the difficult task of working them out, embedded in the mass of difficult energy. You can find yourself behaving in ways that surprise you, being someone you hardly recognize, exposed in a posture that shames you.

And the healing energy, always, is forgiveness. You are being given the opportunity to forgive yourself for conduct that at a deep level of your mind you find unforgivable, and to forgive in another what you find deeply unforgivable. To forgive is to heal. To heal is to remove blockage. To remove blockage is to give access from one portion of a deeper energy well to another that has been walled off from it.

They close with a commitment they commend to us. Commit to unlocking these potentials in the name of service to others. If you do, you will become very vulnerable, and you may wonder where you will get the strength to bear it. The strength, they say, comes from below, from the depths where you are already one, already healed, already with those with whom you have formed a deep bond of being.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Streets and the Ashram
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the streets and the ashram.

The group brings an honest discomfort. Some of them feel called to withdraw from active engagement with social issues and concentrate on the inner spiritual journey. They see the value in it, and yet they feel guilty for not being more involved, and the pull of the world keeps growing. What is the role of this dissonance, and how should they work with it? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo answers at length, and refuses to give the easy answer.

They begin with the feeling itself. When the world knocks you off your center, leaves you surprised at your own behavior, the temptation is to withdraw. So they ask: what is the feeling tone of your withdrawal? Are you proposing to retreat into a safe place because it feels secure from the angry winds of chance? If safety is the motive, consider what you are protecting. It is the vehicle you constructed for navigating the world, and it may be less important to your deeper being than you suppose. By the end of the incarnation you will have lost all you gathered here, except what is actually the most important: the love you learned to give.

And there is a question behind the question. If you retreat into an inner sanctum, what do you propose to do there? Lick your wounds in privacy, or connect with something more? The meditative state is not only a safe haven. There is an energy that comes forward in it, a strength of energy, and it can dislodge the structures of your sense of self as easily from within as the world can from without. The love you find inside may be one you do not recognize, one that leaves you disoriented.

Then the deeper consideration: polarity. Within the tangle of loves and dis-loves you experience daily, the question of what serves which polarity can be most confusing. You set out to reach the hurting, the marginalized, those unjustly done by. You make common cause with others. Then you discover their view of the right way differs from yours, or you are opposed by forces that seem completely intractable, completely benighted. And the temptation is to unsheathe the sword, to fight back, to prevail in what has begun to look like a great cultural war.

When that happens, your best intentions have turned into their opposite. Love has turned to anger, to disdain, to hate. How could one not hate what blocks the expression of love? And yet there you are: not a bringer of light, but one who has made it less likely the light can shine. They call this the mystery of polarity. You guide yourself by a little candle shielded precariously against winds that blow from any direction, and it keeps going out and needing to be re-lit. And in the end the only thing you have to guide you is your resolve to keep on going in love.

So they will not tell you whether to demonstrate in the streets or retreat to a charming ashram. The ways of service are manifold and always surprising in the torturous paths they follow. To close yourself off to a service that suggests itself is to fail in one way. To insist there is only one right way to serve is to close yourself off in another. To serve in love is first and foremost to love, and to love is to open yourself to the vulnerability of asking to be loved, knowing it may fail to come.

That is the sacrifice agreed to in incarnating: the want of love you will almost certainly experience in your efforts to serve, taken deeply into your being, where you may find, despite all evidence, resources rising from a deep place precisely able to heal the wound of the unlove you have taken in.

And one practical mercy. When you find yourself in a vexation where love is hardly recognizable any longer, retreat into meditation is always appropriate. And when you realize you are up against your own limits, a retreat into the safety of your own process is not only acceptable but highly advisable. For where you can do no good, it behooves you at least to do no harm.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gift of Resistance
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gift of resistance.

The group asks for guidance on how to interpret the messages carried by bodily ailments. The body speaks, sometimes in pain, sometimes in limitation, and the question is what it is trying to say. Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo answers with one of the most striking images in the archive, and a reframing of suffering that does not diminish it.

The mind and the spirit, they say, made choices before the incarnation, in a realm of great reach and perception. But the mind could have no being in this illusion without a body, for the body gives it a means of being here at all. The mind forms the body in such a fashion that the body may serve as the noble steed that carries the knight into the battle for truth. When the mind is confronted with concepts it has misperceived or not perceived at all, the physical vehicle is used to enhance the perception. And this, they say, is the beginning of knowledge.

Then the harder turn. The self that is putting itself to the test, attempting to choose at the deepest layers of its being, is again and again moved off its center. It is subjected to a framework in which it cannot recognize itself, or refuses to, or struggles to accept what is given. The self is given to itself, to a large extent, in embodiment. And when there is disturbance in embodiment, pain, discomfort, limitation, the self that would like to be what it has fancied being discovers over and over that it carries a burden, meets resistance, drags along something that will not assimilate itself to its highest hopes.

And here is the shock they promised. This resistance is a gift. The process of choice is given the gift of refusal, given that which cannot be assimilated to the self without greatly enlarging the sense of self the self must now embrace. I am the self that looks to the starry heavens above, but that walks with this limp. I am the self that carries this sorrow, that embraces an inner deformation reaching far and wide, and yet is able to reach in hope and aspiration to the starry heavens above. And in so doing finds a way to accept the unacceptable within, and discovers dimensions of aspiration that have long resisted aspiration itself.

There is a deep sense, they say, in which you are occupying a body that has a mind of its own, a second-density creature whose limitations are being experienced, for the first time in your long journey, not simply as the parameters of existence but as things that may limit you, confound your good intention, refuse your commands. It is a torturous affair, and it is meant to be so.

But look at what the limitation can become. A specific limitation may mark you out, make you different from your peers, curtail your enjoyment so that you have no choice but to relate to the world differently. Having accepted this, you may become aware that within this difference of perspective lie opportunities for self-development, and the most essential point: opportunities for service. For that is why you are incarnate: to find a way toward service that can be embraced whole and complete, through all possible limitation, all possible pain, all possible psychic resistance.

And on the path of service to others, something changes in the experience of pain itself. Not that it disappears. But it becomes less significant, because the self you are becoming is not limited to the parameters you now enjoy. The pains that attend incarnate existence will not so much be your pains as pains you sense in passing, pains you endure as you endure a cold front in April. It is here today, but you know it will be gone tomorrow, for this is not you. You are not you in any sense in which a self is less than infinity itself. For upon the service-to-others path, you and I are one. My pain is your pain, and your pain is mine.

And the final word, which does not deny the difficulty. Pain's destiny does not remain in the condition of pain. It points to something beyond it, in the direction of hope, of aspiration, and yes, of joy, which is the crown of these affects.

A gentle note, friend to friend. None of this is medical counsel. Bodies need doctors too, and seeking care for the body is never a failure of the spirit. The two can walk together.

Thank you for listening.

title: Let the Giving Give
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: let the giving give.

This evening comes from a practice channeling circle, where the newer instruments take up the subject of giving. It sounds like a small topic. It is not. Tonight, the one who calls itself Laitos speaks through several voices, and what emerges is a quietly radical picture of what giving actually is.

The first instrument offers the image that carries the evening. It is crucial not to hold on in a defensive manner to yourself. Clutching reinforces separation, fear, and a lack of the fluidity so essential to moving through this illusion. Take back your focus, and let the giving give itself. Giving and receiving are roles you play to pursue a goal. You draw the lines that separate these concepts, but you can erase them as well.

And then the permission that makes the whole thing breathe. Be at play. This is, after all, an illusion. Why not take advantage of it? Why not make it a study, and let your heart arise from it, recognized anew, recognized in your brother, in your sister, and in the one who may seem to be your enemy? It is not undesirable for the distinctions to blur. It is the greatest overcoming of the challenge of the veil to move about in it and let the resonance of your dance show who you truly are, and show others who they truly are.

Another instrument speaks of the unlimited nature of the universe you live in. There is no bottom to the well. So give wholeheartedly, and when you are in the act of giving, give with all your heart, let it go, and do not expect anything back, because you are unlimited, and you are not without what you gave away. When you give with all your heart, you do open yourself to bountiful receiving. But do not do it for that reason.

Giving can be physical or spiritual. It can be your skills, honed and perfected. It can be a gift of a smile, a warm kind smile, where you shine your light forward to a person, a gift that can be reflected on and on infinitely as the one who received it passes it on. If you have nothing physical to give, you can go to a body of water, cup the water, and give in a gift of ceremony with that water. Your prayers, your kind thoughts, your wishes of healing for someone, all wonderful gifts. And there is the gift of forgiveness, the ultimate gift. Forgive others, and do not forget yourself.

Then the image of the loaves and the fishes. One instrument sees the teacher on the hill with a few loaves of bread and a few fish, thousands before him, and with love taking the small gifts to create a gift that grows exponentially. See how something so small, so tiny in your own framework of daily tasks, can grow beyond measure, moving beyond a simple interaction between two beings. Small acts can reach thousands, can reach millions, can move light years.

But with it a warning. Within this density it is easy to get lost in the idea that all must be reciprocated: I give, therefore I must receive. See instead that your gift to the other self inherently gives back to you. You and the other self are still one. The act of giving and the act of receiving are the same. When you give from the heart, truly, you let go of the sense of need and return, and you see that the greater gift was to you: the opportunity to give so freely.

The final voice names the two paths of giving. One path gives enslavement. The other gives freedom. The free path is service to others: a giving that wishes for the fullest flowering of other selves, operating in the understanding that to serve others is to serve the self, for as one is uplifted, all are uplifted. Giving is not a static energy. It is the continuation of a primary movement that moves all selves upward together. To give is to participate in evolution.

And what is it that is given? It is the self. To give the self, more truly and freely and purely, is to not hold on to the self. It is to move ever closer to a surrender and trust in the design of the Creator. For the creation is a gift, and the Creator is ceaselessly giving. There is no holding back. There is no condition.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mirror of Conflict
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mirror of conflict.

This evening comes from a practice channeling circle, and the question, recorded late, was along these lines: how do we resolve conflict with love? It is one of the most common themes on this planet, because no one moves through this experience without encountering confrontation between self and other self. Tonight, the one who calls itself Laitos speaks through several voices, and the answer is patient, layered, and surprisingly demanding.

The journey to harmonious resolution of conflict, they say, is a journey of many lifetimes. The perception of universal love is but a first step. From there there is much work to be done in self-honesty: understanding how you perceive others, how you perceive their actions and their orientation, and understanding the journey you yourself have taken to arrive at your own position. This self-understanding is necessary before any conflict can be approached with real hope of resolution.

Once a measure of that self-evaluation is achieved, you can turn toward the other self with the love that sees: this entity has traveled its own path to arrive at its own position. You have both arrived at a point where the dynamic tension between you will hopefully serve you both. It is difficult to orient yourself to viewing conflict only as something that might serve you. But if you find what the conflict is attempting to teach you, then the love becomes more apparent, the harmonious way forward reveals itself, and a bridge from co-creator to co-creator can be built.

Another instrument takes the question deeper, into the nature of separation itself. There is little that shows the illusory nature of your reality more than the feeling that attends conflict between two seemingly separate parts of the creation. Separation is drilled into every piece, and while it creates great suffering, it has an educational purpose. It is only through these dents in the unity that the Creator finds something beautiful standing out from the undifferentiated whole.

And when a picture disturbs you, remember this: it is not the picture that must justify itself, but the viewer who must make sense of it. It is not an absence of love that attends the confrontation. It is the full presence of love, projected into this situation. So do not despair. You can balance this, but you may have to release your attachment to outcome, or to a sense of yourself that you momentarily forget is but a mirage.

Another voice offers an image to carry. View conflict as the ocean. At times there are small ripples, at times tidal waves. The seas can be calm and then, without a moment's notice, become choppy. Remember that the conflict is at the surface, for under the waves there is so much more. The pain, the hurt, the misconceptions are temporary, here one second and gone the next. With patience, knowing the seas are always changing, there is no stormy sea one cannot handle.

And the most pointed teaching of the evening. When you experience a so-called conflict, search within your own heart for where that conflict actually lies. You may find that the conflict is within yourself. And when you discover where it actually lies, it gives allowance for the conflict to simply dissipate, as if it never existed. Use the experience as a mirror. Treat the self and the other self the same, with love and patience and compassion, listening not just to words but to energies, following them where they lead, focusing your love there.

The final voice names what conflict does at its best. Confrontation grinds away the portions of the rough-hewn sculpture that hide the polarized being within. Each is given the opportunity to remain an undeveloped block of stone, or to allow the refining fires of this density to cast off pieces of stone, so that self may be revealed to self. Each other self is a mirror, offering you the chance to see the fruits of your beingness.

And what is asked of you is simple, which is not the same as easy. Receive attack or insult or injury, and respond not with the same energy, but with unimpeded love for the other self. See beyond their actions. Understand, if you can, their motivations. And move more deeply still, to see that they too are cut off from the all, seemingly, living in the same not-knowing, the same confusion, carrying the same core pain: separation from the Creator. Love is a unifying, simple energy. In it, all barriers and boundaries and differences dissolve, in unreserved embrace, in unqualified acceptance.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Heart's One Language
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the heart's one language.

This evening comes from a practice channeling circle, and the question is the one everything depends on: in what ways do we block our heart centers, and in what ways do we unblock them? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo speaks through several voices, and the teaching is direct, practical, and unexpectedly tender.

They begin with an exercise from those of Ra. The moment contains love. That is all. It is the central exercise offered to seekers in this density. And the biggest hurdle to opening the heart has already been cleared by everyone in the circle, though they may not remember the struggle, which for many takes many lifetimes: accepting the simple thought that the moment contains love, with love hidden from perception, and choosing to believe it is there despite all appearances. This is so central an act of faith that they encourage rejoicing in it. The attempt to find love in any situation is just as beautiful as the love itself.

Then a method for the moments when love is least apparent. Contemplate your conditions in relation to unconditional love. In any struggle, ask what conditions you are placing on the situation, particularly on the other people in it. What are you expecting from them in order to receive your love? A condition of behavior, of reciprocation, of respect? In the hardest cases these conditions seem entirely appropriate. Why would one seek to love the violent, the murderer? They cannot give you an answer to that question. But they know that in your hearts you recognize the worthiness of all to be loved, for within them is the same Creator that is within you, and you are both dancing within an illusion of distortion. They have found a rhythm to which they dance that you may not hear, but it is upon the same stage that you find yourself.

Another voice reminds the circle of something easy to forget. You were born with a whole heart. It radiated naturally and with ease. It is your earthly experience to go through challenging things that dimmed its shine over time. And just as anything needs upkeep, you can give it back its shine. How? By experiencing your emotions to their fullest, whether they feel positive or negative. When sadness or anxiety rise, feel them. Do not deny them. It is in the denial of emotions that the blocks happen. When you flow in emotion, fully and expressively, you are shining up your heart.

And send yourself the same love. There are times you feel critical of something you thought or felt or did, and wish you could turn back time and redo the whole experience. In those moments, send yourself love and forgiveness. Understand that it is all an expression of your humanity, and everything is a teaching. Do not deny yourself by being self-critical. The heart opens when you are not denying yourself or others.

Then the line that names the evening. The heart knows one language, and that language is love. Your heart truly knows only two things: love and acceptance, counterbalanced by learning to love and learning to accept. It is not naturally inclined to anything else. We trip up and block the avenues to love when we lose connection with the heart and move into the mind. The mind is important, but the heart is what truly guides, and the heart is what is truly common between you and your fellow beings.

The final voice speaks of walls. So many on this planet draw the boundaries of the self small and tight, and erect walls and fortifications to keep the not-self outside, to protect the self inside. But love has many ways of penetrating these walls: first through doorways and windows, then through the dismantling of the walls altogether, until the self learns to exist without attachment to the fear that kept it isolated. Released from fear, the self stands in a sort of nakedness that many avoid, and yet it is this state, the student of spiritual evolution discovers, that is the safest and most secure standpoint of all. For love is a sunlight, a clarifier, a life-bringer, and this love is who you are.

Love is a dissolving agent. Blockages are a walling agent. With each deepening of love, the boundaries not only expand but eventually dissolve, as love opens the contained self to the true unity of the universe, which has no true boundary. So practice, in meditation or in acts of worship or in the passions of your days, remembering this truth. And you will become a living, breathing example of it, a beacon upon the hill, showing others what is true, which only deepens your love: for self, for other self, for all self.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gift of the Veil
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gift of the veil.

The group asks a question that reaches into the foundations. Before the veil of forgetting, there was only service to others, only positive unity. So is it truly a choice, in this density, to remain in positive unity? Or is the only real choice the choice to separate from it? Tonight, the one who calls itself Q'uo takes up this question and several that follow, and the evening becomes a meditation on why we are behind the veil at all.

On the surface there are two choices: service to others or service to self. And the means by which each is pursued look like opposites. The negative path absorbs the love and light of the Creator for the self, to control and manipulate others for personal power. It is, in the words of those of Ra, the path of that which is not: it takes what is, which is unity, and fragments it into separation. And yet both paths deal with the same love and light, and both are aimed at the same destination: return to the One Infinite Creator.

Even the negative path cannot hold its posture forever. As the sixth density is approached, the love and light compacted by the negative entity for itself alone must be released, for further progress requires the balance of love and light, requires seeing each other self not only as the Creator but as the same as the self. In the larger view, then, the only choice for all entities, before or after the veil, is to return to the One Creator, with many experiences on the journey home. The question becomes: shall some means be implemented that accelerates this journey?

That is what the veil is. Before it, there was no forgetting, and entities could see plainly that each was the Creator. But without the veil, what was the motivation to change? There was no fear or love so great as to move an entity from what it observed to be unity. Progress, paradoxically and ironically, is most rapid when the truth is hidden, because then the attempt must be made to find it. Whether it takes a moment or a lifetime or a series of lifetimes, the journey quickens. All the trial and error, all the spiritual sweat spent trying to make sense of a life pattern, that is the polarization process.

The evening turns, and the questions go practical. How does meditation work, and why does it let data sink down into the roots of the tree of mind? They offer an image. The normal conscious life is full of distraction and unprocessed catalyst, like static upon a clear radio signal. Meditation retires the consciousness inward, past the daily round of activities, the errant thoughts, the feelings of separation, until the signal from the One becomes the sole focus of attention, and the presence of the One becomes available to harmonize the meditator. What is most useful to the spiritual path becomes obvious, and can do its work more easily, with less and less distraction draining it away.

And one more thread, on thought forms. Is any thought, even a fleeting one, a thought form? The answer is yes and no, as so much of the journey is paradox. Any thought can become a thing at some level of being. The more energy given to the thought, the more apparent it becomes, especially now that the planet has entered fourth-density vibrations. With enough thought-energy, the form takes on its own experience in another reality, and there are beings in the inner planes that use these thought forms as a kind of food, not nourishing a body but inspiring the mind or the spirit.

So watch what you energize. The veil that hides the truth is also the veil that quickens you. The static that obscures the signal is also the reason you learned to listen.
