You may feel judgment arise, resistance, even the desire to inflict pain on the one who inflicted pain on you. Do it anyway. You have been called to heal the heart. And that insincerity, they assure you, will become sincerity. If practiced, it will consume the heart with the fire of love, until the self really does wish the well-being of the other, whatever their actions may be.

There is one more thread worth keeping. The place where enemyship exists, they say, is not within the other. It is in how you perceive the other and your relationship with them. The other may indeed intend harm. But enemyship can only exist within you as a kind of blindness, if you choose to keep your heart closed to that particular aspect of the Creator. And those who inflict pain upon others, they add gently, are often hurting themselves, often coming from moments of feeling hurt, feeling like a victim. See the mirror, they say, but also see the hurt.

Protect the flame of your desire to love, they say. It may take many sessions, many years, many lifetimes. It is not intended to unfold in any precise moment. It is intended to be a journey of the Creator. And the journey has already begun, the moment you wished it had.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Festival of Lights
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the festival of lights.

Tonight begins with a question many seekers know intimately. How does one overcome indecisiveness and stagnation in times when the inspiration to act feels limited? The ones who call themselves Q'uo answer, in part, with a story. And because the story is the teaching, I am going to tell it to you the way they told it, with only the lightest of retellings.

There was once a young, adventurous woman who lived in a village in a valley nestled between beautiful mountains. One day a traveler came and told her of a festival occurring on the other side of the mountain the following day. A Festival of Lights, the most beautiful sight she would ever witness, if she were willing to make the journey.

She felt determined to take up the challenge. The traveler showed her the trails, but warned her it was a full day's journey, and she would need to leave at daybreak. So the next morning she rose with the sun and began, marching with determination, each step bringing her closer. She paid little attention to the nature around her, for there was a promised experience she was determined to arrive at in time.

As the sun began to lower and she feared she might not arrive in time, she came upon a fork in the path. The traveler had not told her which way to go. She decided that making a choice was better than no choice, and took the path to the left, marching on with determination. Not long after, she arrived at another fork, and realized it was the same fork, on the same path.

Well, the result is simple, she said. I must now take the right path. And so she did, and marched with determination. But again, not long after, she arrived at the same fork in the same path.

She stopped in frustration and cried out. Where should I go? What am I to do? It seems that no matter the path I take, I arrive at the same destination. She was deflated and discouraged, and she began to cry. And as she cried, she felt the wind whisper, but she could not understand it. She heard the trees speak to her, and she could not understand. But she saw behind her a sturdy stone, and she sat in contemplation. It was too late to return home. Darkness was approaching. She could not know how to arrive at the festival she so desired to experience.

As she sat on the stone and the sun lowered, the wind kept whispering and the trees kept speaking, and she began to relax into the moment. As it grew darker, she noticed a twinkling within the trees. She began to understand the wind and the trees. They spoke to her of the Festival of Lights. And as she continued to sit and darkness fell, there were more twinkling lights in the trees that danced. She realized there was an entire sky and treeline full of fireflies beginning to offer their light to her.

They swirled and danced. Higher in the sky, the stars themselves began to swirl along with them. She sat for hours witnessing this glorious sight, hypnotized by the amazing orchestra offered to her. Without realizing it, the night had passed, and the sun began to rise again. The wind whispered. The trees spoke. The animals and birds sang. The insects danced for her. And she realized that all along, there was a path outside her perception that was not part of this fork in the road. As the sun rose, she stood and took this path, and was surprised that not soon after, she arrived back at her home village.

She shared with her friends and family and villagers the glorious sight she had seen. She realized that indeed, she had arrived at the Festival of Lights, but it was not as she expected. It was present for her at the moment in which she felt lost.

This, they say, is the answer to indecisiveness. There is no part of the creation, no part of your path, that is not alive with the infinite love and light and glory of the One Infinite Creator. The inspiration you seek for your next step is within every iota of the creation around you. It may not be apparent, and this is intended, for the purpose of your density is perceiving this love when it is not apparent, seeking this light when it is not apparent. Yet you must have faith that it is present.

If you take stock of the present moment and relax into your heart, you may discover that this love is present. Whatever you were supposed to be doing is present within this moment, for there is nothing else that could exist for you. There is no destination to march to. Your destination is now, the eternal now.

They acknowledge the paradox. Even they speak of the soul's progression through the densities, home to the Creator. But they offer a resolution. See that progression as a falling away of expectation, a falling away of the need to arrive somewhere. Instead, a growing realization that what you were seeking is present in this very moment, without any effort needed. Sit upon the stone. Relax. Pay attention to what surrounds you. And the glorious festival that was promised will reveal itself to you, with patience, and with faith that you are where you need to be.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Wisdom of Unmanifested Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the wisdom of unmanifested desire.

Tonight holds many questions, but the thread that ties them together is desire. What happens when you want something with all your heart, you do the inner work, you hold the vision, and it does not come? Are you doing it wrong? Is the teaching of co-creation a lie? Or is something deeper going on? The ones who call themselves Q'uo answer with a teaching about the two wills that live inside you, and it is one of the most clarifying passages in the archive.

They begin with empathy. They understand the appeal of manifestation, especially for one who has lived a life where suffering and struggle have defined the seeking. Learning of the power of thought can feel like being handed the keys to a better life. And many find confirmation in it, for once you learn of the power of thought, you can readily witness its effects upon your reality.

But then the paradox. If each individual contains the infinite power of the Creator, why can you not manifest exactly the circumstances you desire? The answer reaches into the architecture of incarnation itself.

When you incarnated into third density, you chose, of your own free will, to take upon yourself a veil. That veil hides not only your connection with the Creator, but your connection with an essential aspect of yourself, the unconscious mind. While you may consciously know what you desire, there is an entire aspect of your being, far vaster than your conscious awareness, that may have alternative desires. And beyond that, your higher self, your mind, body, and spirit complex totality, still carries the greater desire you chose when you incarnated. Some of your conscious desires are compatible with that greater desire. Some are not.

And this is by design. If you could shape your circumstances to the exact specificity of your wanting, catalyst would fail to do its proper job. You would feel a constant sense of fulfillment, and you would never be caused to seek within a variety of experiences. Within third density there is opportunity for the opposite experiences, and within those experiences an even greater opportunity to learn of your spiritual nature.

For it is not only in the moments when you are happy and fulfilled that you have a connection with the Creator. The Creator is ever present. In each moment, whether your manifestation has come true or has ceased to come true, the Creator is still present. Those situations where the desire has not manifested are just as equally important and valid, for in them you may seek and find the love in that moment, and see the intelligent infinity at play.

Then the line that gives tonight its title. It can be in analyzing these experiences, where the desire has failed to manifest, that you glimpse the deeper part of the self. And once the experience has passed, and you have utilized it for your spiritual growth, you may look back and finally understand that it was the experience that you needed. And because of that, it was the experience that, though you did not realize it, was ultimately what you desired. That ultimate desire is what you carried with you into this incarnation but have forgotten.

The unmanifested desire was not a failure. It was the forgotten desire, keeping its appointment with you.

There is a companion question in the evening about free will in conflict. What happens when your desire requires another person to participate in a certain way, and they do not? The answer is simple and worth keeping. Each entity carries the divine faculty of free will, and it is a natural consequence that one individual's free will may be incompatible with another's. In that conflict, follow the thread deeper, to the greater will underneath, the Creator's will, and you will find the thread leads home.

And the evening opens with a question that belongs at the end of all of this. What is the most important bit of information for soul growth here on Earth? The answer. In your meditations, ask the presence of the One Creator to move through you in ways that present themselves as service to others. Ask for more ability and opportunity to utilize the skills given to you. Ask the Creator, and the Creator shall respond.

So if there is something you wanted that never came, consider the possibility that it was not denied to you. It was rerouted by a wiser part of yourself, toward the experience you actually came here to have. The desire you remember is the smaller one. The desire you forgot is the larger one. And it is still being fulfilled, in ways you are only beginning to see.

Thank you for listening.

title: Where Is Love in This
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: where is love in this.

Tonight's final question is one every seeker eventually has to answer for themselves. When you receive an inner nudge, a dream image, a sudden knowing, a voice in the quiet, how do you sort out what is genuine guidance from what is merely the mind talking to itself? How do you know what to trust? The ones who call themselves Q'uo answer with a test of beautiful simplicity, and it gives tonight its title.

The first step, they say, is evaluating whether this message or this feeling has, as its center, an invocation of love. Is that which I am receiving based in love? Is that which I am receiving inspiring me to love in return? Does this message help me keep my heart open?

If what you receive inspires fear, that does not automatically disqualify it. Fear, they say, is just a reworking of love. But there is something to mine there. The uncomfortable or challenging message is still an opportunity to practice faith, to see the message as a message, to recognize what it brings up in you, and to love it for that opportunity. The question is never only what the message says. It is what the message does to your heart.

While understanding may not be of this density, they say, there is a central truth to spirit that knows, that accepts, that can in some way make sense of all messages, of all information, for all goes back to love. Even the messages that seem inconsequential, even the uncertain ones, are expressions of love in their very formation. The Creator acting as a portion of the creation.

To know whether there is depth to a message is more challenging, and they recommend returning to the evaluation again and again. Ask what it brings up in you. Recognize where love can be brought in, regardless of whether the message arrives in absolute clear love or with some discoloration through the lens of experience. Find the love within it. Be in tune with the sensations in yourself as you receive it.

And then the ultimate radar, as they call it. If you feel that this piece, this experience, this moment has importance to it, if it feeds your soul or speaks to you or even challenges you, if you feel that draw and that magnetism, then that is the value. You establish the value. It is important. Have faith in your discernment. Have faith in your spirit to receive, to understand, to disseminate what the message gives.

The exercises for developing this discernment all come back to one question. Where is love in this? Because there has to be love in this. Where do I feel this coming up in me? And then the patience and the faith that you will receive what you need, the intentional setting of space to explore these nudgings, seeing them as opportunities, trusting the strength and the rightness of yourself. That trust, they say, will illuminate the path toward realizing what is helpful to you on your journey, and what may be lovingly let go of, for it does not serve you.

Earlier in the evening there is a companion teaching about witnessing the suffering of others without taking it on yourself. Suffering, they say, is greatly misunderstood. All entities learn through some degree of suffering, for to suffer is to feel that one is not complete, that one has much to learn. The suffering of others can be utilized as food for growth, for it compels the one who suffers to seek release, and that seeking moves in sympathy with the One Creator. There is no random experience of suffering that does not lead to greater growth and illumination. The observer's work is not to absorb the suffering, but to hold the larger perspective, to see the suffering as the incomplete state on its way toward completion.

Both teachings share the same root. Whether you are sorting an inner message or witnessing an outer pain, the practice is the same. Look for the love. Trust the love. Let the love be the instrument by which you measure everything else.

Where is love in this? Ask it of every message, every moment, every suffering you witness. The answer will not always come in words. But it will come.

Thank you for listening.
